### Added: periodic symmetry operation-inventory diagnostics

Whole-mesh state evidence can now bind the actual Seitz operation inventory
to its group table and full lattice cocycle. It rejects duplicate cosets,
operations that change with k and inconsistent state ownership. Exact
integer/rational checks expose incorrect operations that Gamma-point
orbital panels cannot distinguish. Native source and production gates remain
separate.

### Added: source-owned BIPOLE product-domain composition

A native finite-product source binds independent left/right cell lists and
AO-pair ranges, composing SR, LR and the same-domain zero-mode subtraction.
Tiles outside the declared ranges and changed borrowed inputs are rejected.
Shared-source consumers refuse product-domain inputs. The private source
remains a finite numerical declaration, not a production HF certificate.

### Added: basis-bound physical BIPOLE domain owner

A private owner applies one exact geometric support policy to every ordered
AO quartet, deriving centers from the native basis. Domains are generated on
demand with explicit admission and restartable descriptor ranges, without an
all-quartet cache. Tiny complex-density contractions test SR/LR/zero composition;
production HF traversal and complete Hamiltonian/group certification remain open.

### Fixed: the CFC's step 4 no longer depends on the tetragon diagonal (#779)

Step 3 cuts four edges when a tetrahedron has two corners inside the surface
and two outside, and splits the resulting tetragon into two triangles on its
shorter diagonal -- the paper's own prescription, and a hard comparison that
flips where the diagonals are equal. The quad's total area survives that flip
(0.205850 either side; the whole surface area moves by 1.8e-07), but step 4's
"a third of each triangle to each of its three corners" does not: the same
total lands on the four corners differently and each corner's basis area jumps
by about 0.023 bohr^2. Forty percent of a typical triangulation is tetragon
halves, so this was the largest discrete decision left in the construction.

Step 4 now gives a tetragon's four corners a quarter of the pair's area each.
That is not a departure from the paper but a closer reading of it -- the area
is "equally assigned to the corner points", and the tetragon is the figure step
3 actually produced -- and no diagonal can change it. Measured on water at
0.45 A by scanning the oxygen through a flip: the second difference of the
solvated energy was 125 percent away from its own trend and is now 0.074
percent, and the jump in an area-weighted functional falls by a factor of 1700.
Agreement between the analytic gradient and `cpcm_gradient_fd` on an asymmetric
solute improves from 7.1e-06 to 1.2e-06 Ha/bohr, since the old rule was
kinking the surface the gradient was differentiating. Energies move by under
1e-06 Ha.

The grouping is carried on `IsoSurface.quad_id` through welding (which drops
collapsed triangles) and refinement, and `quad_groups` is the single reader of
it, shared by step 4 and `basis_area_gradients` so the forward rule and its
derivative cannot drift apart. A tetragon whose halves do not share exactly one
diagonal -- which is what welding away a collapsed half leaves behind -- is
returned as two lone triangles rather than mis-grouped.

What remains at a flip is the tetragon's own non-planarity: two flat triangles
spanning four non-coplanar points have slightly different total areas depending
on the diagonal, worth 7e-06 bohr^2 of surface area and 2e-04 bohr^3 of
enclosed volume. That is inherent to representing a curved patch with flat
triangles and shrinks with the grid; removing it would need a
diagonal-independent area formula for the quad, which would no longer agree
with `triangle_areas()` and so with the volume and closure checks.

This supersedes the diagnosis recorded with #770, which attributed the same
9.4 percent defect to the sub-threshold basis-point merge.

### Fixed: the CPCM gradient follows the switching width the run used (#745)

`SolventModel.switching_sigma_bohr` is user-settable and reaches
`build_cavity`, but `CavityTessellation` did not record it, so the gradient's
read of it -- a `getattr` with a 0.5 fallback -- always took the fallback and
differentiated a cavity the run never built. Against a converged
finite-difference reference on water/STO-3G: wrong by 2.2e-04 Ha/bohr at
`switching_sigma_bohr = 0.35`, which is 0.35 percent of the largest component.
The tessellation now carries its width, and the gradient agrees to 1.2e-07.
This closes what v0.13.0 recorded as partially addressed.

The reason it survived is worth recording, because it defeats every cheap
check. A gradient taken with the wrong width is still *self-consistent*: it
satisfies translational invariance to 1e-15 and every other exact identity in
the suite. Only an oracle that rebuilds the energy sees it, so the regression
pays for a full FD and carries a control that mislabels a 0.35-built cavity as
0.5 -- without which it would pass on the broken code too. A cavity that
carries a switching function but not its width is now refused rather than
defaulted.

**Also exposed `SolventModel.switching_drop_threshold`**, because the fix above
is not enough to make a wide switch usable and the remedy was unreachable.
`build_cavity` drops points whose switched weight falls below this fraction of
their raw Lebedev weight; the switching function is smooth across that cutoff
but the discrete point set is not, so a point crossing it steps the energy. At
the default width nothing sits near the cutoff. At
`switching_sigma_bohr = 0.8` a 2.5e-04 bohr displacement moves the point count
from 904 to 905, the local slope reads -0.027 against a trend of +0.016, and no
gradient can match a finite difference across a step in the energy: the
comparison is 2.1e-02 Ha/bohr. With `switching_drop_threshold=0.0` it is
1.2e-07. The option was documented in `build_cavity` all along ("set to 0.0 to
keep every point") but `SolventModel` had no way to reach it, which made the
documented remedy advice nobody could take.

One latent instance of the same defect is closed in passing.
`_electronic_esp_gradient_via_fd` rebuilds the cavity at displaced geometries
and reconstructed only `n_points_per_sphere` from the tessellation, silently
using default radii and width. It is unreachable in production -- the
closed-form ESP gradient replaced it -- so this was never a wrong shipped
number, but it now passes the recorded width and refuses outright when the
reference radii cannot be reproduced, rather than differentiating a different
cavity for whoever re-enables it.

### Added: native streamed physical-product J/K reduction

A private reducer contracts a complete ordered stream of source-owned BIPOLE
panels against an immutable complex density. It enforces common context,
quartet-source and repeated-product consistency, explicit resource caps and
complete finalization without an all-quartet cache. Production HF matching
and full Hamiltonian/group certification remain open.

### Added: the sigma potential can evaluate and differentiate itself (#558)

Direct COSMO-RS feeds a solvent-specific sigma potential back into the
electronic Hamiltonian. Sinnecker, Rajendran, Klamt, Diedenhofen & Neese 2006
(doi:10.1021/jp056016z, the method's original paper) eq. 18-19 make the
solvent operator `V^RS = -sum_t (q_t + q_t^dRS)/|r - r_t|` with the correction
charges solved from `phi_t^dRS = a_t (d mu_S/dq)|_{q_t}`, which with
`sigma = q/a` is `mu_S'(sigma_t)`. That derivative did not exist, and it is the
one piece the feedback needs that the COSMO-RS kernel did not already have.

It is taken from the defining expression rather than from the table.
`SigmaPotential` converged its solvent ensemble and then kept only a tabulation
of itself, so the only available derivative was of a linear interpolant --
piecewise constant, and discontinuous at every grid point. Both constructors
end in the same form, `mu~(sigma) = -logsumexp_j(log w_j - E~(sigma, sigma_j) +
mu~_j)`, so keeping the ensemble makes the potential a function again:
`evaluate` and `derivative` are exact at arbitrary sigma, the latter as a
Boltzmann average of `interaction_energy_dsigma` over solvent partners.
Verified against finite differences to 2e-10 relative. Interpolation is
unchanged and still what `__call__` returns, so no existing COSMO-RS number
moves; the two agree to 2.9e-11 at the grid points and, measured, differ by up
to 9.9e-03 between them, which is why the feedback uses the evaluated form.

**A property of the published functional form is worth knowing before anyone
builds the SCF loop on this.** Klamt's hydrogen-bond term
`E_hb = c_hb max[0, acc - sigma_hb] min[0, don + sigma_hb]` is piecewise linear
in each density, so its derivative steps where a density crosses `+-sigma_hb`.
The sigma potential does not smooth that away: `d mu~/d sigma` is a Boltzmann
average over solvent partners, and every partner's term steps at the *same*
sigma, so the average steps with them. Measured on a bimodal profile, the
derivative jumps by 40.3 across `sigma = sigma_hb` against values of order 70
either side. A Boltzmann average smooths over partners, not over a corner they
share. A Direct COSMO-RS feedback therefore cannot be assumed to converge
smoothly: a segment sitting near a threshold sees a discontinuous potential
from one macro-iteration to the next. The tests separate that jump from mere
steep curvature by halving the sampling interval and checking the change does
not shrink.

### Added: AICCM correlation on the real-Gamma arm, CCSD and DLPNO (#778)

This extends "Added: experimental AICCM correlation from the runner" in the
v0.17.0 section, which shipped `correlation="mp2"` on `variant="four-center"`
only.

`run_periodic_job(method="aiccm", ...)` accepts `correlation="mp2"` on
`variant="four-center"` and `variant="real-gamma"`. The driver is chosen to
match the construction the SCF ran, never to substitute another one, so the
two arms cite different lineages and never share a citation row: the
four-centre arm takes the bare MP2 on the union-and-weight cluster, the
real-Gamma arm the neutral-RI correlation on the neutral fitted torus.
Both consume the reference the front door already converged rather than
building a second one; the real-Gamma adapter keeps the neutral `cderi` its
SCF rode and hands the correlation that same array, so the number reported
is the correlation of the energy printed beside it. `neutral-bloch` refuses
because its reference is the per-k Bloch representation while the drivers
work in real-Gamma supercell space, and names `real-gamma` as the exact
substitute; `chi` refuses as not yet wired; a Kohn-Sham reference refuses
because MP2 needs a Hartree-Fock one. Reported correlation energies are per
unit cell. The bare four-centre drivers form the dense `n_ref_ao**4` AO
tensor, so that arm is a small-cluster tool.

`correlation="ccsd"` is available on the same two arms, closed-shell only.
It is CCSD(T), and the citation key records what the call actually computed:
with the perturbative triples off, the key loses its `(t)` and the reference
list loses the triples paper. An open-shell reference refuses, because
`run_ccm_uccsd` takes no construction selector and so cannot build the
union-and-weight reference. On `variant="real-gamma"` open-shell CCSD does
run, because that same neutral-only driver is the right one for the neutral
fitted-torus reference. `correlation="mp2"` has an open-shell driver on both
arms. Open-shell clusters take the `u` sibling of every citation route
automatically.

`correlation="dlpno-mp2"` and `"dlpno-ccsd"` run on `variant="real-gamma"`,
which is the only arm they can run on: DLPNO screens on a fitted reference
and the bare four-centre operator has no RI decomposition. They ride the same
converged reference and the same fitting as the canonical routes, and at the
default zero truncations they reproduce them to machine precision, so the
truncation thresholds are what buy the scaling. Their citation routes differ
from the canonical ones, because a local-correlation run owes papers a
canonical one does not, and the perturbative triples are recorded per call
there too.

### Fixed: Gamma-CCM CCSD energy semantics were documented wrong

`CCMCCSDResult`'s field comments described its energies as "per reference
cell". They are total finite cyclic-cluster energies, like every other driver
in that package, measured by a clean doubling from a one-cell to a two-cell
torus. This was the same error `CCMMP2Result`, `CCMKSResult` and
`CCMUHFResult` carried. The comments are corrected and carry the numbers; no
computed value changes, and the runner adapters already divided.

### Added: reaching a basis vibe-qc does not bundle

`vibeqc.basis_fetch` renders a basis set from the Basis Set Exchange into a
per-user cache, in the `.g94` plus `.ecp` layout libint and libecpint already
read. The bundled library carries 255 sets; BSE 0.12 catalogues 776, so
roughly 595 were previously unreachable from a stock install.

**It is not a network fetch.** The `basis-set-exchange` distribution ships
the catalogue as package data (~334 MB, 4085 files) and answers with sockets
disabled, so a lookup is a local read. It works on an air-gapped host, and
what you get is pinned by that package's version rather than by what a server
serves; the version is recorded in a provenance file beside every rendered
basis. Because 334 MB is far too much to require of every install, it is the
optional `[bse]` extra, imported lazily: without it the bundled library
behaves exactly as before and unbundled names keep refusing.

**It supplies whole sets and refuses to patch one.** Pass `elements=` and a
record that does not cover all of them is refused with nothing written, so a
half-covering cache entry can never defeat the coverage guard on a later run.
Filling a gap in a bundled basis by grafting BSE blocks for its missing
elements is deliberately not offered: that puts two sources under one basis
name with no reviewed provenance for the join. The def2 beyond-Kr merge did
exactly that once, but as a reviewed operation with a licence entry, not
silently at run time.

**Nothing resolves differently until the caller asks.**
`run_job(..., fetch_from_bse=True)`, or `VIBEQC_FETCH_BSE=1`, is the only way
in; the default is unchanged and an unbundled name still refuses. A bundled
name is a no-op even with the flag on. When a render does happen, vibe-qc
composes a library root carrying the current one *plus* the rendered files
and points libint at that: a superset on purpose, because pointing libint at
the cache alone would hide the bundled library and a run pairing a fetched
orbital basis with a bundled auxiliary would fail on the auxiliary.

A basis that resolves but merely lacks one of the molecule's elements is
**not** a fetch trigger. That stays the coverage guard's refusal.

Each render warns through `warnings`, not the output channel: the basis has
to be resolvable before anything builds a `BasisSet`, which is long before
the job's channel exists, and `output.record` no-ops while none is
installed, so the notice would have been silently dropped. Same constraint
and same answer as `_warn_if_basis_overlay_is_stale`.

**Every run now records where its basis data came from.** The `.system`
manifest gains a `[basis_library]` section: `resolved_root`, the library root
libint actually read, and one `[[basis_library.fetched]]` row per rendered
set carrying the catalogue version, element count and a path to the full
provenance JSON. The root is recorded whether or not anything was fetched,
because vibe-qc prefers a build overlay over the committed library and a
result produced against a stale overlay was previously indistinguishable
from one produced against current data. The section is always emitted, like
`[citations]`, so a consumer branches on `fetched_count` rather than on the
section's absence. Recording is wrapped so provenance can never fail a
calculation.

Every rendered file states that it is not a bundled vibe-qc basis, names the
catalogue version, and keeps BSE's own originating publications. Terms are
the same as the bundled BSE-derived files (`docs/license.md` § 3a). The
roadmap entry that proposed this is corrected in the same commit: its
"pulled on first use" and per-record redistribution-clearance premises no
longer hold.

### Added: the topology search a basis campaign walks (vibe-basis 0.12.0)

`vibe_basis.topology` is M3, the layer that makes the basis *topology* the
search space rather than optimising exponents at a fixed one. That is what
separates this from CRYSTAL23's `OPTBASIS`, and it is the expensive part of a
manual d/f scan.

`BasisTopology` is element-keyed and immutable, with `add_shell`,
`drop_shell` and `split_contraction`; every mutator returns a new topology,
because a search branches and an in-place edit would corrupt a parent that a
sibling candidate still needs. `propose_moves` emits the roadmap's four move
kinds for one angular momentum: `baseline`, `add-high` seeded at a1*r,
`add-low` at an/r, and one `leave-one-out` per shell, with r the local
even-tempered ratio (geometric mean of adjacent ratios, 2.5 when there is
only one exponent to work from). Each move carries the arithmetic that
produced its seed.

`greedy_scan` hill-climbs with the plateau rule, accepting a move only when
it beats the incumbent by strictly more than the threshold and stopping after
two consecutive rounds that do not. An optional beam keeps the roadmap's
width-3 variant available; full enumeration is not offered, because the
candidate count is exponential in the rounds and each candidate costs a
continuous relaxation. `pareto_front` ranks on accuracy, cost and
conditioning together and reports a front rather than a winner, over every
candidate evaluated across all rounds: one beaten on the objective may still
be the one to ship on cost.

Tier 1 throughout, so it never imports `vibeqc`. Candidate evaluation is
injected, and so is the `BasisParametrisation` bridge, since that class is on
the vibe-qc side. `Shell` mirrors `CrystalShell` field for field but is a
separate class, and `to_atom_dict()` emits those exact names so the adapter
is a transcription; declaring the shape rather than sharing it is the lesson
of the duplicated `OptResult`.

**M3's gate has not run.** Scanning Mg-d in MgO and Si-d in SiC needs a full
relaxation per candidate. In particular the part that matters most, that the
scan rediscovers the shipped pob topology when the objective is total energy,
is exactly the part that needs an engine. The 49 tests here are synthetic.

### Fixed: the COSMO FINE Cavity's outward projection is C1 (#770)

Step 6 pushes a segment centre onto its atom's sphere when the area-weighted
mean falls inside, which on a curved surface it always does. The paper states
that as a hard rule, and a hard maximum is C0 but not C1: the segment position's
slope jumps where a centre crosses. The energy is untouched -- it is the
*gradient* that steps, so what this cost was finite-difference second
derivatives. Measured on an asymmetric solute, an area-weighted functional's
slope jumped 0.071 percent across one crossing and now jumps 0.000 percent;
crossings arrive about every 0.025 bohr of displacement per coordinate.

The projection is eased over a band 1e-03 of the sphere radius wide (0.003
bohr) with a softplus. No parameter-free C1 smooth maximum exists, so the width
is a choice, and it is bounded from both sides by measurement rather than
taste: small against the projection depth it eases (0.019 bohr median, so about
six times narrower, and only 51 of 401 segments move by more than 1e-04 bohr
against the hard rule), and wide enough for a finite difference to resolve,
since a band narrower than the step would remove the kink for the derivative
without helping the consumer that needed it. A softplus rather than a spliced
polynomial because it is never below the radius, so no segment is ever placed
inside the sphere it screens. It recovers the paper's rule as the band
vanishes: the solvated energy moves 6.6e-07 Ha at this width, 2.1e-09 at a
tenth of it and nothing at a hundredth.

The projection's chain rule becomes one expression instead of a branch --
`dp'/dg = k (I - u u^T) + sigma u u^T`, with the hard rule as its `sigma -> 0`
and `sigma -> 1` limits -- and the softplus lives in one function that both
directions call, since writing it twice is the hazard behind #546.
`FineCavity.projected` is now a diagnostic rather than a branch selector.

Measuring this turned up a **larger** discontinuity that is not the projection
and is not fixed here: the same functional's slope jumps 9.4 percent at a
displacement where nothing in the construction changes size. It was first
attributed to the sub-threshold basis-point merge, which changes its point
count across the same displacement; disabling the merge outright leaves the
jump unchanged, so that attribution was wrong and is corrected in the handover.
The cause is the marching-tetrahedra tetragon split: a two-versus-two
tetrahedron cuts four edges and the quad is divided on its shorter diagonal,
a hard comparison that flips where the diagonals are equal. The quad's total
area survives the flip, but step 4's per-corner assignment does not, and 40
percent of the triangulation comes from such quads. It is now the largest known
discrete decision left in the construction.

## [v0.17.0] - 2026-09-09 - *Tew's Tern*

### Added: independent physical BIPOLE product supports

The private native LR Gram kernel now accepts separate left/right AO-product
cell lists with complete admission and provenance for both. The shared-cell
API delegates to the same kernel. An exact geometric product builder supplies
the same pair-distance policy used by the SR quartet builder, with bounded
immutable labels. Production HF and complete source integration remain open.

### Added: private physical BIPOLE quartet supports

A bounded geometric builder now enumerates SR quartet images from two
AO-product distance limits and a geometric midpoint limit, using exact
rational interpretations of the supplied binary64 data. Pair-dependent
supports pass ERI-permutation and screw-reanchoring tests, including native
multi-k SR integral comparisons. The rule uses crossed pairs for exchange
without an extra output-pair mask. Production HF, LR and one-electron source
integration remain open; the builder does not authorize symmetry reduction.

### Documentation: historical provenance after the split (#189)

Labelled links to the frozen monorepo as archived, retained their original
URLs, and stopped directing new work into archived handovers. The SKALA
campaign now links its verified moved issue while retaining the old reference.
QVF design notes identify producer and consumer tests in their owning repos.

### Documentation: independent setup and example locations (#189)

Corrected the clone default (`main`) versus installer default (`release`),
removed a stale pending-release claim, and made core calculation archives
and viewer-only samples distinct. Setup and example guides now present the
queue as reusable independently of vibe-qc and link companion manual owners.

### Documentation: shared publishing contract (#189)

Documented subtree ownership, a deliberate copy of the shared Furo CSS with
source provenance, and separate product codename galleries. Core docs deploy
only from `release`; manual main pipelines can no longer overwrite them.

### Added: three-product marketing site (#189)

vibe-qc, vibe-view and vibe-queue have dedicated product pages with independent
installation, documentation and release links. Shared navigation and onboarding
present all three products; marketing routes stay under `/products/`, outside
the companion publisher subtrees.

### Fixed: independent website publishers (#189)

Root marketing deploys preserve `/vibe-view/` and `/vibe-queue/` alongside
the existing protected subtrees, so their independent docs deploys survive
the root rsync cleanup.

### Added: experimental AICCM correlation from the runner

`run_periodic_job(method="aiccm", ...)` accepts `correlation="mp2"` on
`variant="four-center"`. The driver is chosen to match the construction the
SCF ran -- the bare four-centre MP2 on the same cyclic cluster and the same
converged reference -- so the correlation rides the union-and-weight
Hamiltonian that was requested rather than a neutral-RI substitute. The
other three variants refuse instead of quietly returning an SCF-only number,
and a Kohn-Sham reference refuses because MP2 needs a Hartree-Fock one. The
run cites the bare-lineage route rather than the SCF's own row. Reported
correlation energies are per unit cell. The bare drivers form the dense
`n_ref_ao**4` AO tensor, so this is a small-cluster tool.

### Added: Gamma-CCM correlation citation routes

The Γ-CCM MP2 drivers now stamp the citation route they actually built, and
`database.toml` carries the four matching rows. The stamp is per call rather
than a dataclass default because one result class serves two lineages:
`run_ccm_mp2` is the bare four-centre correlation and `run_ccm_ri_mp2` the
neutral-RI one, so a class default would cite the union-and-weight papers for
a neutral fitted-torus number. Guards read the labels out of the source in
both directions, so a stamp without a route and a route nothing stamps both
fail, and the bare and RI rows can no longer collapse into one.

### Added

- Prepared artwork for the six upcoming roadmap milestones, v0.17.0 through
  v1.0.0, with a gallery and generation prompts. Candidate and provisional
  pairings remain separate from the released codename catalog. Schrödinger's
  Llama stands inside an open midnight-blue box with brass trim.

### Added: source-bound zero-mode overlap audit

The private finite BIPOLE source can now compare a supplied HF overlap with
both zero-momentum AO-product factors needed for its exchange subtraction
to take the `S D S` form. The selected-k audit verifies immutable source
inputs, enforces explicit memory/work admission, and records separate
residuals without Hermitization. Its receipt does not certify HF provenance,
probe-charge physics or the full symmetry-reduced correlation operator.

### Added: private HF/correlation long-range bridge

HF long-range J/K now share their unprojected contractions with the private
correlation diagnostics. A private exchange-cache entry point accepts native
integer mesh addresses, preserving third-point transfers without the legacy
Cartesian cache's decimal rounding. Complete complex-density witnesses match
the native finite source and independent Gaussian integrals on tiny shifted
and multiaxis meshes. SCF behavior is unchanged; physical support matching,
the remaining Ewald terms and production symmetry reduction remain open.
### Added: the cohesive objective a basis campaign minimises (vibe-basis 0.11.0)

`vibe_basis.objective` is the L1 layer of the basis-optimisation roadmap's M2:
`CohesiveObjective` scores candidate cohesive energies against a reference with
per-system weights, four losses (RMSD by default, plus MAD, max-|delta| and
Huber), and a deterministic held-out split whose error is reported alongside
the training one. CRYSTAL23's `OPTBASIS` minimises a total energy for one
crystal; this minimises the error of a cohesive energy against an independent
reference, jointly over many systems, and always reports a held-out number.

The module is Tier 1, so it never imports `vibeqc`. References are injected --
`load_pw_reference` parses the `pwref_merged.json` layout but the caller
supplies the path, since Tier 1 cannot reach into vibe-qc's `studies/` tree --
and so are penalties, keeping the `ld_penalty` / `condition_number_penalty`
seam on the Tier-2 side.

A candidate that fails on a system cannot be silently dropped. There is
deliberately no `skip` policy: dropping unconverged systems would make the
objective improve as the basis got worse enough to break them, so the
optimiser would learn to break them. Missing systems are charged against the
training term only, so the held-out split stays a diagnostic. A zero weight is
refused for the same reason. When the ZPE or counterpoise convention is
pinned, a candidate whose flags disagree is refused rather than compared;
left unpinned, every report names what went unchecked.

**M2's gate has not run.** Reproducing the recorded GPAW-pob statistics at
pob-TZVP-REV2 needs 28 periodic cohesive energies, and only the plane-wave
side of that comparison is recorded. The 38 tests here are synthetic and pin
the algebra and the guards, not the physics.

### Added: the cc-pVnZ-PP orbital sets the library was already fitting

The bundled library carried **sixteen** `-PP-RIFIT` auxiliary sets and **zero**
PP orbital sets, so vibe-qc shipped fitting bases for orbital bases the
registry would refuse to load. The 16 orbital sets now ship:
`{,aug-}cc-p{V,wCV}{D,T,Q,5}Z-PP`, 39 elements apiece (Cu-Kr, Y-Xe, Hf-Rn),
fetched from Basis Set Exchange 0.12.

Each BSE record carries its Stuttgart-Köln MCDHF ECP blocks inside the orbital
file; the promotion splits every one into a `.g94` plus a `.ecp` sidecar, so
the per-element ECP decision resolves from shipped data rather than a family
rule. The published core counts are the small-core pattern throughout: 10
electrons on Cu-Kr, 28 on Y-Xe, 60 on Hf-Rn.

**A threshold that contradicted the data.** The `cc-pp` family rule read
`ecp_required_above_z = 30` while no member shipped. Copper is Z=29 and carries
a 10-electron ECP, so on any element the sidecar did not cover, Cu and Zn would
have been called all-electron in a valence basis. Corrected to 28 and pinned
against the shipped core counts.

Registry records give each set its own published RI fit. There is no
`default_jk`: no JK fit is published for the family, and asking for one refuses
rather than borrowing a mismatched fit. The RI fits are narrower than the
orbital sets they belong to (15 elements for `cc-pV*Z-PP-RIFIT`, 21 for
`cc-pwCV*Z-PP-RIFIT`, 8 for `aug-cc-pwCV*Z-PP-RIFIT`), so an RI job on an
element the fit omits is refused by the aux coverage guard naming the element,
not run as a silent partial fit.

All 16 names route the full union of their publications: BSE attributes the
orbital blocks and the ECP blocks to different papers, and both differ per
element, so eight Peterson / Figgen / Metz references were added to the
citation database. `docs/license.md` records the per-element map.

### Added: experimental finite BIPOLE Seitz support audit

The private native finite-source diagnostic now checks exact left/right
AO-product cells and quartet image multisets under one declared four-center
Seitz mapping, including site-dependent reanchoring and duplicate weights.
It reports support mismatches under explicit memory/work caps without wrapping
finite cells onto the k mesh. Supplied mapping metadata is not a geometry or
Hamiltonian certificate; production symmetry-reduced multi-k DLPNO-CCSD(T)
remains gated by HF/source matching and full operator/group validation.

The geometry-bound companion now derives a selected shell quartet's shifts
from native AO Bloch transport, including radial matching and whole shifted
mesh validation. It checks the exact source lattice and budgets both passes;
valid atom/shell mappings can still report non-closed finite supports. AO
transport retains its validated maps for reuse, with orbital-sewing memory
accounting updated for their longer lifetime.

### Added: shared experimental symmetry infrastructure

The internal `vibeqc.symmetry_shared` module supplies bounded native finite
group validation, full integer lattice cocycles, scalar antiunitary block
transport, orbit stabilizers and adjoints, and explicitly named operator and
space diagnostics. Chi finite-torus validation and molecular AO/SALC code
consume the common machinery. Numerical probes preserve backend output
buffers and require a target builder for a different named gauge.

A shared retained-subspace diagnostic now separates metric preservation from
coefficient leakage, preserves complex orbital mixing and scalar time reversal,
and records a bounded, immutable mixing matrix. It works with molecular and
periodic Bloch panel adapters; passing it does not authorize reduction
or select frozen, active, PAO, PNO or TNO spaces.

Retained transports can also be audited against a whole finite group across
named spaces. The diagnostic checks the intermediate-space composition,
scalar antiunitary conjugation and exact rational Bloch factors from full
integer lattice images. It reports inconsistent group laws even when every
individual transport preserves its metric and selected subspace. Molecular
and periodic physical-panel tests cover this additional diagnostic; operator
qualification and production execution remain separate gates.

The periodic state bridge now obtains frozen/occupied/virtual panels, band
masks and exact mesh characters from the immutable native mean-field state.
It preserves native orbital-sewing gates and binds shared evidence to the
actual numerical state and supplied geometry/basis. Whole-group tests use
actual chi RHF snapshots and reject evidence spliced from another state;
this does not authenticate an integral source or enable production reduction.

Molecular AO actions now match exact radial contractions, including reordered
and repeated shell channels. The dormant BIPOLE multipole adapter refuses
unqualified nonidentity reconstruction and converts AO-pair packing at its
native boundary. Production symmetry reduction, analytic gradients and
local-correlation pair skipping remain disabled by these interfaces.
These changes resume archived monorepo issues #717, #753, #760 and #762;
they do not resolve the separate #704/#724 physical-source gates.

### Added: the COSMO FINE Cavity can be built in a molecule-fixed frame

`SolventModel(cavity="fine", fine_frame="molecular")` carries the Klamt &
Diedenhofen 2018 workflow out in the solute's own coordinate system -- the
paper's step 1, which the implementation had skipped -- instead of along the
laboratory axes. The cavity then rotates rigidly with the solute rather than
being rediscretized at every orientation. Measured on water at 0.40 A,
RHF/STO-3G, eps = 78.39, over rotations of 0 to 90 degrees about a generic
axis: the solvated energy varied by 1.0e-05 Ha and now varies by 5.7e-14 Ha,
and the segment set is reproduced to 1.3e-14 bohr instead of changing count
between 235 and 239. An asymmetric solute behaves the same way (1.3e-05 Ha
against 1.7e-13 Ha).

The dominant source was the marching lattice, not the segment directions:
rotating the direction grids alone with the solute left the area spread
unchanged at 5.3e-04 relative.

**The analytic gradient supports it.** A frame that turns with the solute gives
the marching lattice and every segment direction a derivative of their own, and
that contribution is not small: 2.3e+01 of a cavity gradient whose largest
component is 2.9e+01. Rather than rewrite the chain rule for a turning lattice,
`FrameCavityDerivative` reverses the cavity into the frame it was built in --
where the existing chain is exactly valid, because that is where the lattice is
fixed -- and composes it with the frame's own Jacobian.

That gives an exact oracle needing no finite differences: **a molecule in free
space feels no torque**. On the asymmetric solute the lab frame's analytic
gradient carries a net torque of 2.9e-05 Ha, the rotational counterpart of its
orientation-dependent energy; the molecule-fixed frame's is 1.0e-13. Agreement
with `cpcm_gradient_fd` improves from 9.0e-05 to 1.4e-05 Ha/bohr. Translation
invariance is *blind* to the frame term (1.8e-15 with or without it), so the
identity that guarded #729 would not have caught its absence.

Two cases are refused rather than approximated. A linear solute determines no
y-axis, so its azimuth is a discontinuous lab-derived choice with no nuclear
derivative -- and `cpcm_gradient_fd` cannot rescue that one either, since its
displacements cross the same jump. And the frame's two argmax selections tie at
symmetric geometries, water's equilibrium structure included; that tie is
protected, because the two candidate frames are related by a symmetry operation
of the solute and produce the same cavity relabeled, so the energy is smooth
across the crossing (measured even in the displacement to 1e-11 Ha, with the
analytic gradient at the tie matching full-SCF FD to 1.9e-06 Ha/bohr). An
*accidental* tie, with no symmetry relating the two atoms, does jump: measured
5.8e-06 Ha with a 97 percent local slope error, which is the same shape as
#757's assignment defect and about ten times its size. It is pinned by a test
rather than left as a caveat, and it is the reason the default is a maintainer
decision rather than an automatic switch.

**The molecule-fixed frame is now the default**, by maintainer decision: every
`cavity="fine"` energy moves, which is the point -- the old ones depended on
orientation. `fine_frame="lab"` restores the previous behaviour and is the
right choice for a linear solute. A side effect: the resolution guard on
`fine_grid_spacing_ang` fires far less often, because a lab-frame direction
grid meets the surface at an arbitrary angle and can leave a Becke cell holding
a single basis point -- on water the lab frame refuses at 0.44 through 0.65 A
and the molecular frame first at 0.70 A.

The solvation user guide's claim that the analytic gradient does not support
the FINE cavity was stale since #729/#746 and has been corrected in the same
pass. Resumes archived monorepo issue #769.

### Fixed: the COSMO FINE Cavity assigns basis points to atoms smoothly

Step 5 of the Klamt & Diedenhofen 2018 workflow assigns each basis point to the
atom of smallest relative distance by `argmin`. That is discrete, so a point on
a boundary flipped at an infinitesimal displacement and its whole area moved to
the other atom's segment grid: measured on an asymmetric solute, 0.19 bohr^2 at
once, a 6.9 percent error in the local slope of the energy, and a 2.9e-08 Ha
step. Crossings were frequent -- twelve coordinates scanned over +/-6e-03 bohr
found thirty. The energy's slope across one is now smooth to 1.4e-03, fifty
times better, and what remains is the scan's own curvature.

The pair coordinate is the whole design, and two natural choices were built and
rejected on measurements before this one was written. Becke's distance
coordinate with the atomic size adjustment of his appendix A -- the literature
answer, already in the tree for DFT grids -- moves 13 to 16 percent of the
total area between atoms; on water, oxygen loses 29 bohr^2 to the hydrogens. It
is not a smoothing of step 5 but a different rule, because Becke's scheme
assumes a point sits near its own atom while a CFC basis point stands off every
atom by a comparable distance. The tau ratio is faithful but shares every point
with every atom, so the coarsening would cost a factor of the atom count.

What ships measures the offset from the boundary in units of the **marching
spacing**, the one length the construction already carries, and switches with
the compactly supported Stratmann-Scuseria-Frisch function. The area budget
moves 0.9 percent from the hard rule at 0.40 A and 0.33 percent at 0.20 A -- the
smoothing shrinks with the grid, which neither rejected candidate does, so the
fuzzy rule tends to the hard one in the same limit the cavity converges. A
basis point feeds 1.8 atoms on average, falling to 1.4 at 0.20 A. No fitted
parameter: the spacing is already an input and 0.64 is the switch's own
constant.

The analytic gradient carries the new term, verified against finite differences
to 1.3e-08 relative at fixed topology, and the exact translation and zero-torque
identities still hold to 1e-14. `FineCavity` grew the bookkeeping an
overlapping partition needs -- a basis point now supplies a row in more than one
atom's block -- and its area accounting is per (vertex, atom) rather than per
vertex.

Costs about a factor of two in cavity construction and moves every
`cavity="fine"` energy by roughly 7e-06 Ha. The resolution guard on
`fine_grid_spacing_ang` now first fires at 0.70 A rather than 0.44 A, in both
frames, because cells are fed from more basis points.

One limit of #769 is measured and pinned in the same pass, having surfaced
here. A *symmetry-induced* frame tie is invisible in the energy, as #769
established, but not in the gradient: at such a geometry the frame **jumps**
rather than varies, so the chain rule through it is not a route to the energy's
derivative, and the analytic gradient carries a spurious 1.9e-05 Ha/bohr force
along the tie-breaking direction -- in a component symmetry requires to vanish,
and which a converged finite difference puts at 1e-11. Break the tie by any
amount and agreement returns to 4.7e-07 Ha/bohr, better than the lab frame
manages. Averaging the frame Jacobian over the tied atoms was tried and is
wrong: a jump has no two one-sided derivatives to average, and the averaged
Jacobian breaks the exact rotation identity. Resumes archived monorepo issue
#771.

## [v0.16.0] - 2026-09-08 - *Pople's Puffin*

<p class="codename-art">
  <img src="_static/images-codenames/16-vibe-qc-v0.16.0-poples-puffin.png" alt="AI-generated Pople's Puffin codename artwork for vibe-qc v0.16.0">
</p>

### Changed: vibe-qc reads its own QVF, and the viewer no longer shares a schema file (2026-09-08)

Preparation for splitting the monorepo into vibe-qc, vibe-view, vibe-queue
and qvf. Both changes remove a coupling that only worked while the four
components shared one checkout.

**`name_from_qvf` no longer needs vibe-view.** It imported
`vibeview.qvf.QVFReader`, with a fallback to
`vibeqc.output.formats.qvf.QVFReader` -- a class that does not exist, so the
fallback was dead and the function returned
`"(vibe-view not installed; ...)"` whenever the viewer was absent. vibe-qc
writes QVF, so it can read it: the new `vibeqc_naming._qvf_read` opens the
archive, verifies each member against the sha256 the manifest declares, and
returns the structure section. It lives in `vibeqc_naming` rather than
`vibeqc.output.formats` because that package is deliberately importable
without the compiled `_vibeqc_core` extension, and vibe-view itself calls
`name_from_qvf` without vibe-qc built. Validated against the 12-archive qvf
conformance corpus, including the periodic and 2-D slab cases, and it
rejects a tampered archive on digest mismatch. `python/vibeqc/naming/` and
`python/vibeqc_naming/` are parallel copies by design (see
`tests/test_naming_compositional.py`); both are updated.

Naming a periodic system returns `PERIODIC SYSTEM` rather than an empty
string. The underlying gap is separate and pre-existing:
`name_from_atoms_with_lattice` returns an empty name for atoms that name
correctly without a lattice.

**The viewer's schema files are real files, not symlinks.**
`vibe-view/src/vibeview/schema{,_v2}.json` pointed into
`python/vibeqc/output/formats/`, which cannot survive separate repositories
and made `vibe-view/tests/test_qvf_schema_identity.py` compare a symlink
with its own target. They are now byte-identical copies, and that test
checks something real.

**`vibe-view[queue]` is declared.** `vibeview.app` and `vibeview.cli` import
`vq.{listing,fetch,status,submit,overview}` lazily, but `vq` appeared in no
dependency list -- it resolved only because both packages shared a
checkout-local venv. It is not in `[all]`, because the `vibe-queue`
distribution is not published yet.

### Fixed: the SECCM electrostatics read the image records, not the typed cell (issues #444, #348, 2026-09-06/07)

Two defects in the GFN2-SECCM cyclic-cluster route, both of the same shape:
a term that should have been a function of the Wigner-Seitz image inventory
was computed from the home-cell molecule instead.

**The shell gamma now runs on the shared periodic kernel.** Three hand-rolled
Ewald implementations (3-D, 2-D Parry/Heyes, 1-D wire) and their private
assembly loop are replaced by `build_periodic_shell_gamma` driven by the WS
records, the same function and the same Ewald code the Gamma-periodic driver
uses with unit weights. 527 lines out, 176 in.

That kernel carries the neutralising `-pi/(V alpha^2)` background the SECCM
one omitted. The omission was invisible in every shipped number, because it
shifts all elements by one constant and so cancels in the neutral
contractions the SCC consumes -- but it left the individual matrix elements
dependent on the arbitrary Ewald splitting parameter. Across a 3x range of
alpha the shipped kernel now holds `gamma[0, 0] = 0.543268472823` to twelve
digits where the old one ran 0.6347 to 0.5545. Neutral-cell energies are
unchanged.

**3-D `ewald_gamma` is available with a kernel that has a thermodynamic
limit.** The refusal was never a fact about three dimensions: the
Klopman-Ohno remainder's `-eta^2/2R^3` tail with pair-dependent amplitude is
what fails to converge. `gamma_form="elstner"` selects the Elstner 1998
Eq. 17/18 form, whose remainder decays exponentially, and opens the route --
a 2x2x2 rocksalt MgO cluster converges at -4.764409516 Ha per cell. On a
fixed ionic charge pattern the Elstner electrostatic energy per formula unit
moves 4.4e-5 Ha from 64 to 125 cells against the Klopman-Ohno 8.7e-4.

**The anisotropic electrostatics no longer depend on which lattice copy an
atom was typed as (#348).** With the AES channel off, three representatives
of a polar HF chain give bit-identical energies; with the shipped kernel on
they span 1.6e-4 Ha, because its multipole integrals came from the home-cell
molecule. `aes_faithful=True` builds them over the same records as the
overlap and H0 and evaluates the Bannwarth 2019 Eq. 25 energy and Eqs. 39-44
Fock on the resulting atom-resolved cumulative moments; all three
representatives then agree exactly. The two paths cannot be blended, because
the shipped kernel consumes shell-resolved moments and a pair inventory
produces atom-resolved ones.

**The multipole moments are part of the mixed SCC state (#409).** The
shipped loop mixes shell charges and rebuilds the multipole channel from
whatever density falls out, so the moments are never an iterate and
convergence is declared on the charge residual alone. On the faithful path
the reduced state is now `[dq_shell; mu; theta]`, one mixer advances all of
it, and the convergence test is the whole residual. Every mixer then reaches
the same energy to twelve digits -- simple in 129 iterations, Broyden in 25,
DIIS in 23, the Eyert scheme xtb uses in 9 -- where the shipped path's mixers
agree only to about 1e-8. `scc_mixer="newton"` is refused with
`aes_faithful=True` rather than silently degraded, because its
finite-difference Jacobian is defined on the charge subspace.

### Measured: the molecular GFN2 xtb residual, and why the AES default stays put (issues #43, #475, 2026-09-08)

Against live xtb 6.7.1, the faithful anisotropic-electrostatics channel
closes the molecular residual by one to two orders of magnitude on small
polar systems: H2 from -16.497 to +0.051 mHa, NH3 from -5.089 to +0.362,
H2O from +0.601 to +0.138. That confirms the residual is the on-site
DPOL/QPOL term (Bannwarth 2019 Eq. 31) the shipped channel omits.

`aes_faithful` nevertheless remains off by default, because adenine
contradicts the small systems and cannot currently arbitrate: its molecular
SCC reaches **four distinct converged states spanning 29.4 mHa** depending on
the AES model, the auto-stabilisation retry and the mixer -- settings that
should not change the answer. Both results are now pinned as tests.

Two further observations from the same sweep: the third-order term clamps the
molecular SCC step to `min(charge_mixing, 0.1)`, so that option has no effect
above 0.1; and `auto_stabilize` selects a basin rather than accelerating a
solve, moving adenine from -27.5081085 to -27.5014338.

The basin multiplicity is filed as issue #777, which records the four states,
both observations above, and why it blocks #43, #475 and the default move.

Issue #43's recorded +245.7 mHa adenine residual is stale: on the same frame
the shipped path is now -1.86 mHa from xtb, which reproduces the issue's
reference value exactly.

### Changed: the SECCM Wigner-Seitz topology build is vectorised (issue #423, 2026-09-07)

GFN2-SECCM showed a 0.94-1.44x speedup on 20 threads because the dominant
phase was a serial Python build, not the parallel SCC. Profiling put 98.6 %
of that build in one function, which walked every atom pair against a fixed
candidate-label box one candidate at a time -- a solve per pair, a norm and a
matrix-vector product per candidate, and a dataclass allocation per
candidate.

The enumeration is now vectorised over the whole grid. On rocksalt MgO the
build goes from 0.629 to 0.090 s at 16 atoms, 7.06 to 0.87 s at 54, and 69.2
to 5.49 s at 128 -- a 12.6x speedup there, leaving the build at 2 % of wall
where it was the bottleneck before.

The result is bit-identical to the path it replaces: zero differing
classification fields and zero floating-point delta across 3-D cubic, 3-D
skew triclinic, 2-D slab and 1-D chain fixtures. Two last-bit hazards had to
be reproduced exactly to get there, both of which flipped candidates whose
Wigner-Seitz score is exactly 1.0 across the prefilter boundary: `einsum`
reassociating the three-term projection product, and the fact that the
original used two different associations for the same displacement vector --
one for the closest-image distance, another for the classification.

The issue also asks for a benchmark at N ~ 1000 atoms. That size remains out
of reach because the builder retains one classification object per candidate,
so storage is quadratic in the atom count; the tracked benchmark added here
pins the 128-atom build instead, and the remaining work is recorded in
`handovers/HANDOVER_GFN2_PERIODIC_ELECTROSTATICS.md`.

### Fixed: the periodic SCC-DFTB gamma lattice sum converges (issue #425, 2026-09-07)

The periodic and k-point SCC-DFTB gamma summed the bare Klopman-Ohno kernel
by real-space truncation. That is a sum of 1/R, divergent in three
dimensions: charge neutrality should cancel it, but a pair-distance cutoff
gives different pairs different image counts, so each pair keeps a different
divergent constant. It now runs through the shared Ewald-split kernel with
the Elstner 1998 Eq. 17/18 gamma, the maintainer's D1 decision of 2026-08-28.

Both halves are needed. With the Coulomb tail Ewald-summed either way, on
#425's own fixture the Elstner energy is flat at -0.450188859 Ha from a
40-bohr cutoff to 200, while Klopman-Ohno still drifts monotonically from
-0.419 to -0.872 Ha over the same range. The standing xfail is retired and
the test pins both columns.

Moving the energy exposed a latent defect in its derivative: the analytic
gradient still differentiated the old bare sum, 15.6 % off finite differences
on a polar HF cell. It now comes from the same kernel as the energy, and the
gamma form is recorded on the SCF result so the derivative differentiates the
energy that was actually converged -- the provenance discipline the lattice
cutoff already had.

SCC-DFTB-SECCM gains the same `gamma_form` flag plus an `ewald_gamma` route
that sums the Coulomb tail into the kernel instead of adding it separately as
a Madelung embedding. Its 3-D embedding refusal (#211) said "the current Ohno
gamma correction has no thermodynamic limit", which is a statement about the
kernel rather than about three dimensions, so the gate now names the kernel:
a 3x3x3 rocksalt LiH cluster converges with `gamma_form="elstner"` at
-0.400383374 Ha, and Klopman-Ohno is still refused with a message saying what
to pass instead. The SECCM gradient's hand-rolled Klopman-Ohno derivative was
made form-aware in the same change, before it could differentiate a function
the energy no longer used.

Per D1's staging the molecular route gains the flag but keeps Klopman-Ohno
until the measured repin table is accepted; the table is in
`handovers/HANDOVER_GFN2_PERIODIC_ELECTROSTATICS.md`.

Both `gamma_form` and `aes_faithful` default to the shipped behaviour, so
every existing number is bit-for-bit unchanged and molecular-limit parity
with the molecular driver keeps its meaning. Moving those defaults is a
separate, measured repin.

### Fixed: the periodic Gamma GFN2-xTB electrostatics are a real lattice sum (issues #296, #338, #408, #433, 2026-09-06)

The Gamma-point GFN2-xTB driver evaluated its shell gamma and its multipole
electrostatics on the home-cell `g = 0` distance with no lattice sum at all,
so the energy of a crystal depended on which lattice representative each atom
was typed at. The sixth attempt at #296 canonicalised the input coordinates,
which made a relabelling a no-op but left the energy discontinuous at every
cell face. Both are replaced rather than patched.

**A shared translation-covariant kernel.** The new
`semiempirical/core/periodic_gamma.hpp` assembles the second-order matrix as
`Gamma_ij = Phi_Ewald(d_ab) + sum_images w [gamma_ij(r) - 1/r]` over directed
image records `(a, b, shift, weight)`. The Coulomb part is summed by Ewald in
1-D (background-corrected wire), 2-D (Parry/Heyes slab) and 3-D (with the
neutralising background), so it is exactly lattice-periodic in the pair
displacement; the remainder is short-ranged and converges absolutely. The
record abstraction is deliberately the same one the SECCM adapters need,
where the weights are fractional Wigner-Seitz ownership instead of unity.
Verified against the Madelung constants of rocksalt (1.747564594633),
the square lattice (1.615542626713) and the alternating chain (`2 ln 2`).

**The gamma functional form is selectable, and defaults to Elstner in
periodic runs.** `ShellGammaForm::Elstner` is the Elstner et al. 1998 Eq. 17/18
form `1/R - S(tau_a, tau_b, R)` with `tau = 16/5 U`, whose remainder decays
exponentially and therefore has a thermodynamic limit; `KlopmanOhno` is the
GFN2 paper's own kernel, whose `R^-3` remainder does not (the periodic
instance of issue #444). The near-degenerate window `|tau_a - tau_b| <= 0.02
max(tau)` uses the exact series in `delta` through `delta^4`, since the closed
form loses six digits there. Molecular GFN2 is untouched.

**The anisotropic electrostatics are the published model.** The ad-hoc
`gamma^3`/`gamma^5` shell-resolved kernel is replaced by Bannwarth, Ehlert &
Grimme 2019 Eqs. 25-28 on cumulative atomic multipole moments accumulated
over image-resolved overlap and multipole integrals, with the Fock matrix
derived as the exact `dE/dP` about each image's own origin.

**The analytic gradient and all nine stress components now differentiate that
same energy.** Because the Fock matrix is exact, the reduced SCC state is
variational and no response term is required. The former Z-vector correction
is deleted. Against central finite differences: 3.9e-11 Ha/bohr and 2.7e-13
Ha/bohr^3 on a polar 3-D HF cell, 2.2e-09 and 1.2e-10 on a smeared h-BN
monolayer. The stress was previously gated off as 5.3x too large on `xx` and
sign-inverted on `yy`/`zz`; the gradient's 2.4e-3 Ha/bohr residual is gone.
`evaluate_periodic_energy_gradient` no longer central-differences GFN2.

**The SCC state carries the multipole moments.** Mixing shell charges alone
cannot converge a polarisable periodic cell; on MgO the damped simple, Aitken,
CP2K-Broyden and charge-DIIS paths all fail at 2000-3000 iterations while an
Eyert Broyden mixer on the joint `[dq_shell; mu; theta]` state reaches the
cubic-symmetric state in 87 (issue #409). That is now the periodic default.

Periodic runs cite the electrostatics they actually used: Elstner 1998 for the
gamma form and the dimensional Ewald references reach the `.references` and
`.bibtex` files. Multi-k GFN2 remains gated on issue #351, and external xtb
parity is still open, so the route stays experimental.

### Fixed: periodic grid weights use physical point neighborhoods (#772)

Periodic atomic grids now normalize each point over its physical atom-image
neighborhood. Relabelling a home atom by a lattice vector therefore keeps
the same partition, including on skew lattices. The minimum image radius
expands where needed to cover diffuse density through vacuum. Raw grid
points, atomic weights and profile metadata retain their existing layout.
The Python grid, native RKS and periodic Gamma COSX grids share this rule;
home-only molecular COSX uses its matching molecular quadrature.
The default radius remains 10 bohr and must be converged with the grid;
finite-neighborhood boundary sensitivity still requires force step checks.

### Fixed: BIPOLE screening labels identify the active bound (#775)

The BIPOLE SR progress line and current documentation now identify
charge-pair Schwarz screening, matching the active Sun 2023 citation.
Historical QQR records and serialized image-domain policy identifiers
retain their original names. Numerical screening and radius policies are
unchanged.

### Fixed: periodic XC gradients retain custom basis contractions (#776)

Periodic RKS and UKS XC gradients now translate the supplied basis shells
instead of loading each image from the basis name. Custom basis names no
longer abort the native gradient, and optimized contractions supplied under
a bundled basis name remain intact. Fixed-density finite differences cover
LDA, PBE and r2SCAN for both spin treatments and both naming cases.

### Fixed: multi-k GPW and GAPW runs stamp live SCF progress into the .system manifest again (#768, 2026-09-07)

`run_periodic_job` selected the terminal SCF trace row with
`_trace[-1] if isinstance(_trace, list) else _trace`. The restricted multi-k
GPW and GAPW drivers return `scf_trace=tuple(...)`, and a tuple is not a
`list`, so the whole trace was bound as if it were a single row. Neither
following branch matched it, the field dict stayed empty,
`update_progress` was never called, and the manifest carried no `[progress]`
section at all. Silent: no warning, no exception, and the `.out` iteration
table rendered correctly throughout, because the shared renderer normalises
the trace independently.

The affected routes are exactly the two that reach the runner through
`_GapwMultiKRunnerProxy`, whose `__getattr__` forwards `scf_trace` unchanged:
`run_periodic_rks_gpw_multi_k` and `run_periodic_rks_gapw_multi_k`. An
explicit Gamma mesh counts, since a `kpoints=(1,1,1)` RKS request takes the
multi-k driver. Every single-k GPW/GAPW route was already safe, because the
runner-shape adapters rebuild a `list` of `SCFIteration`.

Measured on He / STO-3G / LDA in a 10 bohr cube, same cell for every route:
before the fix `jk_method="gpw"` and `"gapw"` wrote no `[progress]` section
while `"gdf"` wrote `iteration = 2, energy_eh = -2.772172361688382`; after it
all three write the section, and the stamped `iteration`, `energy_eh` and
`gradient_norm` equal the terminal trace row exactly. The GDF energy is
byte-identical across the change, which is the whole blast radius: the block
is telemetry only and touches no SCF quantity.

The selection now accepts any sequence. A result exposing a single row rather
than a sequence still takes the original branch. An AST sweep of the remaining
31 bare `isinstance(x, list)` guards in `python/vibeqc/` found no sibling: each
is fed by `json.loads` or `tomllib`, which never yield tuples, or already
normalises a tuple correctly. Regression:
`tests/test_periodic_runner_gpw_dispatch.py` pins the tuple route, the list
route as a control, and the selection contract itself.

### Fixed: the unreachable QQR citation entry left behind by the charge-pair Schwarz replacement is removed (#773, 2026-09-07)

`tests/test_citation_no_dead_entries.py` was red on `main`:
`maurer_ochsenfeld_qqr_2012` had no `[routes.*]` row and no source reference,
so it could never appear in a references block, `.bibtex` or `.system`
manifest. The issue offered two dispositions, delete or allowlist, and
deferred the choice. A third looked plausible and is wrong, so it is worth
recording why: QQR-style naming still ships in comments, in a run-log string
and in `docs/troubleshooting.md`, which makes it look as though the entry
merely lost a route it should get back.

It should not. The paper introduces QQR as
`|(mu nu|lambda sigma)| ~= Q_mn Q_ls / (R - ext'_mn - ext'_ls)`: a Schwarz
product multiplied by an external MBIE `1/R` separation factor, written with
`~=` and defended in the paper's own title as reliable tightness *instead of*
a rigorous upper bound. `1e10140f8` (#755) deleted that arithmetic wholesale,
because its product-center form omitted angular tails worth ~6.3e-7 Ha at a
1e-12 threshold. What runs behind the unchanged `sr_range_screening` flag is
the opposite object: the rigorous charge-pair Schwarz bound of Sun 2023
Eq. 51, in which separation enters *inside* each Schwarz factor through the
smeared erfc kernel. That bound is already attributed, by
`sun_range_separated_exchange_2023` on `routes.methods."bipole_sr_range"`.
Routing the QQR paper there would credit it for the estimate the project
adopted to replace it, in the references block of every default BIPOLE run.

The entry is therefore deleted, following the house precedent that removed
the Doll and phonopy entries once the shipped method turned out not to be
theirs, and CLAUDE.md section 8, which sends background and survey papers to
the library's `manual-dois.txt` rather than the citation database. No
`_KNOWN_DEAD_ENTRIES` row is added: that list is debt with a named owner and
a wiring plan, and there is nothing here to wire.

Blast radius is zero on rendered output, verified rather than assumed:
`assemble(..., uses_bipole_sr_range=True)` adds exactly one key over the
screening-off assembly, `sun_range_separated_exchange_2023`, and the deleted
key appears in neither. Entry count 441 to 440. The stale QQR prose is a
separate defect and is filed as #775, including one user-facing run-log line.
### Fixed: CFC basis points join segments by Becke partition, so the energy is continuous (#757, 2026-09-07)

Step 6 of the COSMO FINE Cavity assigned each basis point to exactly one
segment by nearest centre, so a point sitting on a boundary flipped at an
infinitesimal displacement and its *whole* area moved to the other segment.
The energy was therefore **discontinuous** in the nuclear coordinates: on an
asymmetric solute, three of 1230 basis points reassigning shifted one segment
weight by 0.333 bohr^2 and the energy by ~6e-7 Ha, and a coordinate scan read
a secant slope of 0.0111 across that boundary against 0.0233 everywhere else
-- a 52 percent error -- with the segment count, projection flags and
triangulated surface all unchanged. Water cannot show this; its symmetry hides
it.

The assignment is now a Becke fuzzy-cell partition (A. D. Becke, *J. Chem.
Phys.* **88**, 2547 (1988), doi:10.1063/1.454033) over the segment centres,
the same construction vibe-qc already uses for DFT molecular grids. Klamt &
Diedenhofen 2018 do not address the discontinuity; their own treatment of
related discrete problems is to avoid differentiating them (COC and
triple-segment area gradients "neglected", exact symmetric coincidences broken
with "a small geometrical noise function", p. 1652).

It adds **no fitted parameter**. Becke's `mu` is a ratio of distances, so the
smoothing width is the spacing between segment centres -- the only length in
the problem -- and `k = 3` is Becke's published order and the existing
`GridOptions.becke_k` default, pinned equal by a test so the cavity and the
DFT grid cannot drift apart. Rows of the weight matrix sum to one exactly, so
the total cavity area is conserved (load-bearing: COSMO-RS sigma profiles read
it) and hence `sum_S dW_S = 0`, which makes the total-area derivative immune
to partition errors.

The slope spread over intervals that do not cross a *different* discrete
boundary is now 1.6e-5, and CFC solvation energies are monotonically
convergent in the grid spacing, which they were not: -0.0052978 (0.28 A),
-0.0052955 (0.30), -0.0052931 (0.32), -0.0052859 (0.35), -0.0052727 (0.40).
The Lebedev cavity is untouched, moving by at most 5.4e-15 against a measured
same-tree run-to-run floor of 1.4e-14.

The gradient was rebuilt rather than patched. The forward-mode
`segment_jacobians` summed over the hard assignment and no longer described
the construction, so it is **removed**; `smooth_coarsening_vjp` plus
`FineCavityDerivative.contract` are the single implementation, reverse-mode
because that is the consumer interface and because the forward `dW/dc` tensor
for one oxygen is 209 MB. Verified by a clean V against full-SCF finite
differences (minimum 1.9e-6 Ha/bohr at h = 2e-3, `err.h` constant on the left
branch and `err/h^2` on the right), the two exact translation invariants, and
exact molecular symmetry: water in the yz-plane now gets a y-force of exactly
zero on oxygen.

**A grid too coarse for the segment grid is now refused.** A Becke cell
supported by a single basis point puts its segment on that point, and two such
cells coincide, making `A` rank-deficient (it is the Gram matrix of the
segments' Gaussians, and two identical Gaussians are one vector): minimum
eigenvalue -1.0e-14 against a norm of 6.6e+03. Merging the pair is not the
fix, since a Gaussian of area `a` is wider than two of area `a/2` and its
self-energy differs by sqrt(2). Spacings coarser than about 0.44 A on water
raise with a message naming resolution as the requirement; the paper's value
is 0.3 A.

Note for anyone verifying CFC derivatives: the Becke partition is stiff,
`err/h^2` around 7e7 for the cavity functionals, so finite differences here
are truncation-limited long before they are roundoff-limited.

Three defects found while verifying this are filed and **not** fixed: #769
(the CFC energy is not rotationally invariant -- 6.0e-6 Ha per degree, larger
than the defect fixed here, because the segment directions are lab-fixed where
the paper's step 1 builds a molecule-fixed frame), #771 (the step-5
basis-point-to-atom assignment is the other hard argmin) and #770 (step 6's
projection is continuous but kinked, 0.02 percent).

### Fixed: CFC segments carry Gaussian charges, so the A matrix is positive definite (#744, 2026-09-07)

`build_A_matrix` on COSMO FINE Cavity segments was **not positive definite**
for roughly one grid spacing in six -- 10 of 29 spacings on water between 0.24
and 0.52 A, worst eigenvalue -8.62. That is not slow convergence: Lange &
Herbert (*J. Chem. Phys.* **133**, 244111 (2010), doi:10.1063/1.3511297)
eq. 2.25 makes positive definiteness of `A` the condition for the polarization
energy to be a *minimum*, so an indefinite `A` means the reaction field can
raise the energy and the apparent charges solve nothing. `run_cpcm_scf`
reported convergence and a negative `e_solv` throughout.

The cause was not the cavity but the kernel. Lange & Herbert state the
dependency plainly (p. 244111-8): the point-charge form `1/r_ij`
"necessitates the use of an alternative switching function, as close approach
of these point charges must be avoided". A Lebedev cavity meets that
precondition through its erf switching function; a CFC has none and cannot
acquire one, being a single closed iso-surface with nothing to switch. Its
segments now carry York-Karplus spherical Gaussians (*J. Phys. Chem. A*
**103**, 11060 (1999), doi:10.1021/jp992097l, eq. 56), so
`A_ij = erf(zeta_ij r_ij)/r_ij` is finite at contact and `A` is the Gram
matrix of normalized densities under the Coulomb inner product -- positive
definite for **any** geometry, making definiteness structural rather than
lucky. Water, same 29 spacings: 0 indefinite.

This introduces **no fitted parameter**. The existing diagonal already implied
a Gaussian width: equating Lange & Herbert's two diagonal forms (Table III and
eq. 4.1) gives `zeta = C_S pi sqrt(2)`, so the defect was that the off-diagonal
was the point-charge limit of a *different* scheme. That bridge is also a
cross-check rather than a definition -- their Lebedev `C_S = 1.104` yields
`zeta = 4.9049` against York & Karplus' Table 1 values of 4.901 to 4.907,
fitted by an entirely different route (exact Born energy of a conductor plus a
uniform surface charge).

Each cavity now declares the representation its construction requires
(`CavityTessellation.charge_representation` is `"point"`,
`FineCavity.charge_representation` is `"gaussian"`) and
`build_cavity_A_matrix` reads it, so a third construction cannot silently
inherit a precondition it does not meet. **The Lebedev path is untouched:** it
keeps the point-charge kernel, its `A` is bit-identical, and end-to-end
energies and gradients move only at the 4e-15 run-to-run floor.

The gradient follows the kernel. The area adjoint gains a term with no
point-charge analogue, since `zeta_ij` depends on the segment areas and so the
*off-diagonal* elements have an area derivative at all; it is
finite-difference-verified directly and guarded against being zeroed. Pairing
the new kernel with the old adjoints left the analytic-vs-FD residual at
5.5e-6 where the correct pairing gives 1.5e-6 -- silent, and still a plausible
gradient.

Recorded without changing: vibe-qc uses the **GEPOL** constant
`C_S = 1.0694` on Lebedev grids where Lange & Herbert Table III gives 1.104
for Lebedev, an implied Gaussian width 3 percent narrow. Changing it would
move every shipped solvation reference, so it is a maintainer decision; pinned
by a test so the next reader sees a deliberate choice.

### Added: the assembled analytic CFC energy gradient (#746, 2026-09-06)

`cpcm_gradient` no longer refuses a FINE cavity. The three cavity terms are
rewritten as adjoint contractions against a shared vector-Jacobian product, so
both constructions go through one interface instead of one of them being a
special case.

The seam is `vibeqc.solvation.cavity_derivative`. Every geometry dependence of
the solvated energy reaches the cavity through exactly two per-segment
quantities, positions and areas -- checked rather than assumed: the only
consumer in `driver.py` is `build_A_matrix(cavity.points, cavity.weights)`. So
a term's derivative factors into the term's half, identical for every cavity,
and the cavity's half. The `A`-matrix adjoints take distinct left and right
vectors (`u^T A v`), which Direct COSMO-RS needs and which the energy
gradient's `q^T A q` cannot distinguish from a bare `2 q_i q_j`.

**A term the #729 derivation was missing.** That work held the marching grid
fixed; `build_fine_cavity` anchored it to `pos.min(axis=0)`, so the grid
followed whichever atom was outermost on each axis. This was
non-differentiable wherever two atoms tie -- water has all three at x = 0 --
and broke translational invariance: the area gradient missed summing to zero
by 0.34 bohr against a largest component of 14.7, with only the argmin atom
wrong. The box is now anchored to the centroid, which is also what Klamt &
Diedenhofen 2018's own step 1 prescribes, so `d(grid)/dR_A = I / n_atoms` for
every atom and a uniform translation of the molecule translates the surface
rigidly. Segment areas are immune to that term (an area is invariant under a
common translation of its vertices) but positions are not.

Verified against full-SCF `cpcm_gradient_fd` on water/STO-3G as a step study
rather than a single step: `err.h` constant on the left branch and `err/h^2`
constant on the right, minimum 1.5e-6 Ha/bohr against a gradient scale of
2.3e-2. Blinding out the box-translation term makes that residual *plateau* at
1.7e-5 -- the #546 signature -- and the net force go from 1e-15 to 4.8e-5. Two
exact invariants now hold with no finite differences at all:
`sum_A dp_S/dR_A = I` at 1.8e-15 and `sum_A dw_S/dR_A = 0` at 6.7e-16.

The Lebedev path is numerically unchanged: the new contraction reproduces a
verbatim copy of the pre-refactor routine to 1.6e-15 relative, and end-to-end
`cpcm_gradient` matches the previous tree to 1.5e-14 against a measured
same-tree run-to-run floor of 1.4e-14.

Partially addresses #745, a latent defect found here: the gradient hard-coded
`switching_sigma_bohr=0.5` while `SolventModel` exposes it, so a run that moved
it differentiated a cavity it never built. It now reads the value off the
cavity; closing #745 needs `CavityTessellation` to carry the field.

### Fixed: basis-name aliases resolve identically in both layers, and def2-SV is registered (#743, 2026-09-08)

`vibeqc.basis_registry.canonical_basis_name` resolved a spelling for
*metadata* while the C++ `basis_data_name` resolved it for the *file* libint
opens, and the two were independent. So `sto3g` was a documented alias that
still failed in `BasisSet`, and Gaussian's `6-31G(d)` had no alias in either.
`basis_data_name` now resolves the same table: `sto3g`, `sto6g`, and the
`(d)` / `(d,p)` polarisation spellings of the Pople sets.

No entry maps `6-311G(d)`, `6-31+G(d)` or `6-311+G(d)`: the library ships no
`6-311g*`, `6-31+g*` or `6-311+g*` file, and pointing at a missing stem would
only relabel the failure.

`tests/test_basis_alias_parity.py` walks the alias table in `registry.toml`,
constructs each spelling, and checks it gives the same basis as its target, so
an alias added on one side without the other fails here rather than drifting.
An unknown name still raises rather than falling back.

**def2-SV is registered as its own family.** The bundled file carries H-Ar
only (18 elements), not H-Kr as the issue said, while def2-SV(P) and its
siblings now reach Rn. It matched no family pattern at all, so it silently had
no defaults and no ECP rule. It is now an all-electron family with that
boundary stated; a heavier atom is refused by the per-element coverage guard
naming the element.

Still open on #743: the cc-pVnZ-PP orbital sets are not bundled, while
**sixteen** of their fitting sets are, so vibe-qc ships auxiliary bases for
orbital bases the registry refuses to load. Measured for whoever takes it: the
BSE records are reachable, carry 39 elements each with their ECP blocks in the
layout `scripts/basisset_dev/split_ecp_g94.py` already parses, and fall under
the same CC-BY-4.0 terms recorded for the def2 heavy blocks.

### Fixed: the periodic SCF-failure diagnostic reports the failure instead of replacing it with an AttributeError (#748, 2026-09-07)

`run_periodic_job`'s non-convergence withdrawal builds a "Terminal check on
the density returned" clause from the last SCF trace row (#116). It read
`_last.delta_e` and `_last.grad_norm` as attributes, which is an
`AttributeError` on the plain-dict rows the GPW / GAPW Python drivers append.
Because the read sits on the *failure* path, every case reaching that branch
reported the same traceback about the diagnostic instead of its own
convergence state: five LiF cases in the 2026-09-07 validation wave were lost
that way, their real cause unknowable from the artifacts.

Most GPW routes are lifted back to `SCFIteration` records by
`periodic_gapw_runner_adapter`, which is why this went unseen. Four are not:
GPW and GAPW multi-k RKS reach the runner through `_GapwMultiKRunnerProxy`,
whose `__getattr__` forwards `scf_trace` verbatim, and Gamma ROHF/ROKS plus
multi-k UKS/ROKS GPW go through passthrough adapters. An explicit Gamma mesh
is one of these: `gpw_use_gamma_branch` excludes RKS, so `kpoints=(1,1,1)`
takes the multi-k driver, which is exactly the shape of the reported LiF
Gamma RKS cases.

The clause is now built by `_terminal_scf_check_clause`, which **cannot
raise**: any unreadable trace degrades to no clause rather than to a
traceback, so the FATAL message always names the real failure. It also stops
mislabelling the residual. Row shape does not determine the physics: on the
GPW / GAPW density loops `grad_norm` holds the density change gated by
`conv_tol_density`, while `periodic_gapw_cpp_host` re-packs genuine
`||[F,DS]||` commutator norms into the same dict shape. The residual is
therefore named `||[F,DS]||` and compared against `conv_tol_grad` only for
record rows, where both are known to hold, and reported under its own field
name with no tolerance claimed otherwise. Record-row wording is byte-identical,
so the BIPOLE pin in `tests/test_periodic_runner_bipole_callsites.py` is
unchanged.

Measured: He / STO-3G / LDA, `jk_method="gpw"`, `kpoints=(1,1,1)`,
`max_iter=1` raised `AttributeError: 'dict' object has no attribute 'delta_e'`
at `periodic_runner.py:13032` before, and now raises the intended
`RuntimeError` carrying `|dE| = 2.772e+00 Ha against conv_tol_energy 1e-07`
and the driver's own residual field. Regression:
`tests/test_periodic_runner_gpw_dispatch.py` (one end-to-end refusal on the
dict route, one unit contract covering record rows, dict rows, tuple traces,
partial rows, and rows that raise on access). The adjacent live-progress
block at `:12809` mis-selects the row on the same tuple traces and is filed
separately as #768.

### Added: bounded scheduler acceptance receipts (#736)

`vq submit --wait-submitted` waits for a durable PBS/SLURM submission ID
and reports staging failures before returning, without waiting for calculation
completion. Arrays share one timeout budget. Timeout and interruption retain
the queued IDs and never replay submission. `--enqueue-only` names the existing
immediate queue-acceptance behavior, which remains the default.

### Fixed: BIPOLE Gilat energy pins enforce absolute tolerances (#708)

The open-shell Gilat regression now disables pytest's default relative
allowance, enforcing the stated 1e-10 Ha energy pin and 1e-12 Ha agreement
with Aufbau. The file joins the BIPOLE test lane while retaining its
verified classification. The bounded Ewald-split energy pins are unchanged.

### Fixed: erfc screening includes angular tails and indexes shell pairs (#755, #21)

BIPOLE short-range J/K screening now bounds angular polynomials and signed
contraction tails with positive Gaussian envelopes. The former distance
attenuation could discard diffuse f-shell contributions above 6e-7 Ha at a
1e-12 screening threshold. Charge-pair and Gaussian-product bounds replace
that estimate; bounded spatial searches visit surviving shell pairs and
retain the direct summation order. Exhaustive traversal remains available
for independent comparisons. The threshold bounds each screened quartet,
not the accumulated error of an entire lattice sum.

The 51 domain tests cover angular tails, signed long contractions, arbitrary
signed densities, sparse/exhaustive equality and thread-count invariance.
A 13-function LiH carrier converged in eight iterations in 279.6 seconds
with two OpenMP workers; its largest erfc build took 49.0 seconds and final
output reused the exact-density confirmation. The six-case performance
campaign and the broader physical-domain/default work remain open.

### Fixed: fold-warning regression includes the terminal evaluation records (#721)

The moderate fold-truncation regression now checks the warning followed by
the existing pending/done exact-density output. The high-drift refusal
still requires the warning alone. No SCF or refusal threshold changed.

### Fixed: unified initial-guess selection and construction (#671, #680, #681, #684, #686, #687, #688, #690, #706, #716, #720, #722, #727, #733)

Initial guesses now use one canonical selector, route-aware AUTO resolution,
exact spin/electron normalization, and preserved restart provenance across SCF
and nested workflows. Periodic AUTO replaces the temporary unset sentinel;
HCORE-only CCM routes resolve AUTO to HCORE and reject explicit unsupported
guesses. ECP atomic guesses use the actual valence basis and pseudopotential.
Output and citations record the effective physical guess. Unsupported
combinations fail before SCF.
