All-electron POB cells retain their charge-only metadata contract without
being mistaken for incomplete ECP operators by guess preflight (#763).
Malformed or reduced-charge records without an operator remain rejected.

### Experimental: common native finite BIPOLE integral composition

A selected multi-k C++ integral source now combines the explicit-image
short-range erfc branch, reciprocal long-range branch and q=0 overlap
subtraction under one immutable source context. Basis/support content checks,
component receipts and enclosing resource admission precede integral
evaluation. Only explicit G0 omission is supported; no HF singularity default
changes and no complete symmetry-reduced DLPNO-CCSD(T) route is enabled.
Added bounded native full-k density recontraction for the experimental
finite BIPOLE source; production symmetry-reduced DLPNO-CCSD(T) remains
unavailable.

### Experimental: exact permutation checks for selected erfc image support

The native multi-k erfc fold can now require that its exact image multiset
preserve all eight real-ERI quartet permutations after home-cell reanchoring.
Repeated-image counts must match; incomplete support is rejected before
integral evaluation. The optional check has explicit work admission and
constant scratch, retains the original summation order, and binds its scoped
receipt to the immutable integral result. It does not enable space-group
reduction or certify a complete BIPOLE Hamiltonian or DLPNO-CCSD(T) route.
### Fixed: the CAS / MR-PT family and OVGF accept an ECP reference (#740, 2026-09-07)

`casci`, `mrci`, `casscf`, `nevpt2`, `caspt2` and `ovgf` refused an ECP
reference. The stated reason for the CAS half was wrong: those routes do not
build their own integrals. They are handed `H.h1e` / `H.h2e` from the same
`build_hamiltonian_mo(..., reference=...)` call the determinant family uses,
so they already carried `T + V_ne(Z_eff) + V_ECP`. The real defect was one
line in the active-space partition, `n_elec_total = molecule.n_electrons()`,
which put the ECP core back into the frozen-core block and asked the solver
for orbitals a valence basis does not have. It now takes `H.nelec`, which the
reference already reduced to the valence count. OVGF had the same defect at
its closed- and open-shell occupied counts and now uses
`effective_electron_count`.

Both refusal sets in `runner.py` are consequently empty: no molecular route
refuses an ECP reference any more.

Measured on H2S / LANL2DZ (18 physical electrons, 10 replaced): CASCI(4e,4o)
reproduces PySCF's CAS with the same ECP to **5.4e-08 Ha**, and NEVPT2,
CASPT2 and MRCI order correctly below it.

**A second, larger defect surfaced while testing this, and is fixed here
too.** `run_job` builds the reference SCF for the CAS and determinant
families internally, through `get_hf_orbital_provider`, which constructed its
own options object and ignored the caller's. An ECP supplied only through
`rhf_options` / `uhf_options`, with no basis sidecar, therefore never reached
the reference and was **silently dropped**: the run completed on a bare-Z
Hamiltonian at the physical electron count. Measured on LiH/STO-3G with a
zero-core model potential, `cisd`, `fci`, `selected_ci` and `casci` returned
byte-identical energies with and without the operator. This predates #740:
the determinant family was un-refused on 2026-09-05, and only the sidecar
half of it worked. `get_hf_orbital_provider` now takes `scf_options=` and all
three reference sites in `runner.py` thread the caller's options, including
the `"uno"` branch an open-shell CAS reference resolves to. The same LiH case
now moves by 1.93 Ha.

Two things this does **not** claim. A CASSCF energy is returned on an ECP
reference, but its analytic nuclear gradient is still unavailable, since that
kernel has no ECP derivative; the runner previously computed that gradient
unconditionally on convergence, which failed the whole energy run, and now
skips it on an ECP reference. Separately, CASSCF sits ~29 mHa from PySCF on
this system *and on an all-electron control*, which is the known basin-
selection defect #712, not an ECP problem.

### Fixed: SCF accelerator citations follow the executed SCF, not the caller's options object (#682, 2026-09-06)

`run_job` materialises `RHFOptions()` when no options object is passed, so an
implicit run and an explicit-`RHFOptions()` run dispatch the same SCF (the
`EDIIS_DIIS` default). The accelerator citation was read from the *caller's*
struct: absent, it fell back to plain DIIS; present, it reported the struct's
default. Two numerically identical H2O / STO-3G runs therefore recorded
different reference sets (implicit: Pulay 1980 + 1982; explicit: plus Kudin
2002 and Garza-Scuseria 2012), the same defect class #657 fixed for ECPs.

Two changes. The C++ SCF drivers (RHF, UHF, RKS, UKS) now record in every
trace row which Fock extrapolation actually reached the SCF
(`SCFIteration.accelerator_step`: 0 none, 1 Pulay DIIS including the
adaptive-depth R_CDIIS / AD_CDIIS policies, 2 KDIIS, 3 EDIIS, 4 ADIIS; the
EDIIS+DIIS and ADIIS+DIIS hybrids record the branch their switch metric
selected). `runner._detect_scf_accelerator` reads the options the runner
actually dispatched (`_scf_options_used`, which also tracks convergence
retries) and refines the switching hybrids by the executed steps: `EDIIS_DIIS`
is credited (Kudin, Scuseria, Cancès 2002; Garza and Scuseria 2012) only when
an EDIIS branch ran, and cites Pulay alone when every applied step was DIIS;
`ADIIS_DIIS` likewise for Hu-Yang 2010. A trace without any applied
extrapolation reports the configured accelerator. ROHF / ROKS routing is
unchanged.

Measured on H2O / STO-3G RHF after the fix (energies unchanged to the last
digit, -74.95994827025959 Ha, 7 iterations): the implicit and the explicit
`RHFOptions()` run both record `accelerator_step` `[0, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1]` (the
hybrid's switch metric never exceeded 0.1 from the SAD guess) and both cite
Pulay 1980 + 1982 only; `DIIS` and the hybrid with the threshold at 1e12 give
the same; the hybrid with the threshold at 0 records `[0, 3, ...]` over 11
iterations and adds Kudin 2002 and Garza-Scuseria 2012; pure `EDIIS` adds
Kudin 2002 alone; `ADIIS` records step 4 and adds Hu-Yang 2010; `KDIIS`
records step 2 and adds Kollmar 1997.

Regression: `tests/test_feature_citation_end_to_end.py` pins implicit-versus-
explicit `.system` accelerator-key equality, the four executed-step cases
(DIIS; hybrid with the switch threshold at 1e12 and at 0; pure EDIIS) against
both the citation set and the recorded steps, and the detector's precedence
rules. `docs/user_guide/citations.md` item 5 states the rule.

### Added: analytic nuclear derivatives of the COSMO FINE cavity (issue #729, 2026-09-06)

Klamt & Diedenhofen 2018 assert that the CFC segment positions and areas are
differentiable, because the pseudo-density is an analytic function of the atom
positions, but give no algebra. `vibeqc.solvation.fine_cavity_gradient` is that
derivation, verified stage by stage against finite differences.

The one non-obvious step is the iso-surface point. It lies on a **fixed** grid
edge, so it has a single degree of freedom, and differentiating the constraint
`PD(p0 + s e; R) = 1` gives

    ds/dR_A = -grad_{R_A} PD / (grad_t PD . e)

The factor `PD` cancels between numerator and denominator, so this holds for
`ln PD` too. The resulting `dt/dR_A = e (ds/dR_A)^T` is **rank one**: when an
atom moves, an iso-surface point can only slide along its own edge. That is
asserted directly, by checking the FD motion has no component off the edge.

Verified against FD: `grad_r PD` and `grad_{R_A} PD` to 1.5e-10 relative to
scale, plus the *exact* translation identity
`sum_A grad_{R_A} PD = -grad_r PD` at 1e-13, which needs no finite differences
at all; `dt_k/dR_A` to 1.2e-9; triangle areas to 4.3e-10; per-vertex areas to
1.1e-9, with the total-area gradient matching to nine significant figures; and
segment areas and positions to 1.5e-9 and 2.7e-9.

**A prerequisite the paper does not mention.** The published workflow places a
vertex by quadratic interpolation along its cut edge, which is approximate:
measured on water, it leaves `|PD - 1|` up to 6.3e-2 (linear interpolation up to
0.48). The derivative comes from differentiating the constraint `PD = 1`, so an
unrefined vertex gives the derivative of a *different* point, and the total-area
gradient came out 0.1 to 1 % wrong -- smoothly and plausibly. Vertices are now
Newton-polished onto the iso-surface along their own edge, reaching
`|PD - 1| ~ 6e-15` in two or three steps and leaving the mesh closed. Also
`refine_iso_vertices` is exposed and on by default.

Three details that cost real debugging and are now pinned:

* Segment **areas** and **positions** sum over *different* groupings. A
  sub-threshold basis point has its area merged into a neighbour but
  contributes no coordinate, so the exact per-basis-point grouping is recorded
  (`FineCavity.area_basis`) rather than reconstructed. A heuristic left
  positions wrong by 1.4e-4; the exact map gives 6e-16.
* Step 6's outward projection is not a corner case: on water it moves about
  **half** the segments, so its derivative
  `delta_{Aa} I + (rho_a/r)(I - u u^T)(dp/dR_A - delta_{Aa} I)` is required,
  not optional.
* `SegmentJacobians.d_position` has two trailing length-three axes meaning
  different things (segment component, atom component). Transposing them is
  silent, so `position_component(atom, cartesian)` exists.

**Superseded (#746, 2026-09-06):** at the time this landed the assembled
energy gradient still refused a FINE cavity, because these were the cavity
derivatives only. #746 assembled it behind a shared cavity-derivative
vector-Jacobian product, so `cpcm_gradient` now works on a CFC. The text below
describes the cavity derivatives themselves, which are unchanged.

### Fixed: full-k periodic DFTB optimization runs at finite temperature and minimises the Mermin free energy (#545, 2026-09-06)

`run_periodic_job(..., kpoints=..., optimize=True, smearing_temperature=kT)` on
DFTB0 / SCC-DFTB refused finite temperature with "zero-temperature only", while
the #434 frontier guard on the same route told users to supply exactly that
temperature: two clear errors in sequence, no way through. The maintainer ruled
on 2026-09-06 that the gate is lifted and the optimizer minimises the Mermin
free energy `F = E - TS`.

Lifting the gate alone would have been wrong: `optimize_periodic_positions`
and `optimize_cell` paired `derivatives.energy` (the internal energy) with a
gradient that, at finite temperature, differentiates `F`, so BFGS would have
minimised one surface with the slopes of another. The optimizer now takes the
potential the derivative result declares (`_minimised_potential`: `F` when
`differentiated_free_energy`, `E` otherwise), the runner threads the resolved
temperature into `opt_energy`, `opt_derivatives` and `opt_cell_derivatives`
and returns `F` from the energy callback, and the derivative result carries
its `smearing_temperature`. `PeriodicSemiempiricalOptimizationResult` gains
`minimised_potential`, `internal_energy`, `free_energy` and
`smearing_temperature` (defaults keep zero-temperature results unchanged), and
the optimized-geometry block prints `F_final` (minimised), `E_final` and
`-TS` when smeared. Physics: Weinert and Davenport, Phys. Rev. B 45, 13709
(1992), Sec. III (the force conjugate to Fermi occupations is `-dF/dR`);
Mermin, Phys. Rev. 137, A1441 (1965).

Measured on the HLi chain fixture (DFTB0, k = (2,1,1), kT = 0.05 Ha): the
optimization converges in 7 steps to `F = -0.5249560807`, `E = -0.3987644425`,
`-TS = -0.1261916381` Ha; at that geometry the kernel gradient matches a
central difference of `F` to 4.0e-9, 8.1e-10 and 2.0e-10 at h = 4e-3, 2e-3 and
5e-4 bohr and differs from the central difference of `E` by 2.45e-6, the
negative control that `grad F` is consumed. Regression:
`tests/test_periodic_runner_semiempirical.py` (a mocked one-temperature
contract test replaces the former rejection test, plus the real-engine
stationarity test above); `docs/user_guide/semiempirical.md` § DFTB periodic
states the contract.

### Fixed: multi-k MOM keeps its occupied subspace through the zero-temperature fill (#725, 2026-09-06)

The maximum overlap method (`use_mom=True` on `run_rhf_periodic_multi_k_ewald3d`
and `run_pbc_bipole_rks`) occupies, at every SCF cycle, the orbitals with the
largest projection onto the previous occupied space instead of the lowest
energies (Gilbert, Besley and Gill, J. Phys. Chem. A 112, 13164 (2008), Sec. 2).
The drivers express that choice by permuting `C(k)` and `eps(k)` so the
selected states lead. Since `a189640bd` (#85) the `T = 0` branch of
`apply_smearing` fills a k-mesh by global energy ordering, so it re-picked the
lowest states from the permuted list and undid the MOM selection; the
fixed-slice guard then refused the run, describing an equal-count case
(verifier's reproducer: `eps = [[0.2, -0.5], [0.3, -0.4]]`, two k points, two
electrons, occupations `[[0, 2], [0, 2]]`, per-k counts `[1, 1]`) as a per-k
count mismatch. MOM had been unusable on every multi-k mesh since.

`apply_smearing` gains a keyword-only `fixed_occupied_subspace=False`. When
`True` at `T = 0` the fill is positional, `occ[:n_occ_each] = 2` at every k,
with `mu` the midpoint of the highest occupied and lowest empty energy under
that partition and no frontier-cut report (the caller chose the subspace,
nothing was cut); with finite smearing it raises, because MOM is a
zero-temperature contract. `closed_shell_periodic_occupations` forwards the
flag and the two MOM drivers pass `use_mom`. Every other caller (GDF, GPW,
GAPW, runner) is untouched and the default fill is byte-identical.
`require_fixed_occupied_subspace` now names a third shape, "occupies states
outside the leading n_occ_each entries", for equal counts that are not the
leading block. Regression:
`tests/test_smearing_package.py` (four `#725` tests) plus one contract test per MOM driver (`test_periodic_rhf_multi_k_ewald.py`, `test_pbc_bipole_multik_ewald_split.py`) pinning `fixed_occupied_subspace=use_mom` at the first occupation call; the
`use_mom` row of `docs/user_guide/initial_guess.md` documents the contract.

### Fixed: the dense AO-batch VV10 regression tests pin the grid they describe, and the coarse VV10 default is covered and documented (#675, 2026-09-06)

`tests/test_vv10.py::test_wb97xv_scf_preserves_pairs_across_ao_batches` and
`test_uks_wb97xv_preserves_spin_chain_rule_across_ao_batches` were red on
`main`. Both describe the dense path (a 6,120-point product grid whose VV10
double sum crosses the 4,096-point AO batch boundary) and pin its energies,
but since `6c96a7c66` the default `GridOptions.vv10_grid_factor` is 3.0, so
they ran VV10 on a 5 x 6 x 12 = 360-point coarse grid: below the batch
boundary, so the premise was never exercised, and 1.66e-4 Ha away from the
pins (measured He / STO-3G / wB97X-V: -2.841764943333874 Ha against the
pinned -2.841931319453023 Ha, identically for RKS and closed-shell UKS).

The two tests now set `vv10_grid_factor = 1.0`, which restores the pinned
energies and XC terms to 1e-15. A new
`test_wb97xv_default_coarse_vv10_grid_is_pinned_and_near_dense` covers the
shipped default: factor 3.0, RKS and UKS pinned at -2.841764943333874 Ha /
E_xc -0.647350682737639 Ha, the coarse shift confined to the XC term and to
the grid-error window (1e-6 < |dE| < 5e-4 Ha), so a silently disabled coarse
grid would fail it. The coarse VV10 grid follows the Vydrov and Van Voorhis
2010 implementation practice (nonlocal term on a coarser grid than the
semilocal functional); it is now documented in the keyword index and the
VV10 tutorial, with `1.0` as the dense reference switch. No kernel change.

### Fixed: vacuum-padded Gamma RIJCOSX drivers evaluate every electrostatic term over the home cell (#707, 2026-09-06)

The one-cell RIJCOSX drivers (`run_periodic_rijcosx_rhf` on a non-tight
cell, and the vacuum-padded RKS/UHF/UKS drivers) build J with the molecular
density-fitting builder, which contains no image-cell electrons. The nuclear
attraction and nuclear repulsion nevertheless summed the image nuclei inside
`LatticeSumOptions.nuclear_cutoff_bohr` (25 bohr default), and the COSX K
summed the image-ket exchange class inside `cutoff_bohr` (15 bohr default).
For a Gamma Bloch orbital that exchange class is the electron's Coulomb
interaction with its own images, whose partner lives in the missing image
part of J. Only the total electrostatic energy of a neutral cell is gauge
invariant (Makov and Payne 1995), so every box shorter than those cutoffs
was over-bound by the uncompensated bare monopole sums.

Measured pre-fix on `5651aaba1`: H atom / STO-3G UHF in a 12-bohr box
converged to -1.6377388584 Ha (32 image protons: -1.8420 Ha in V_ne and
+0.9210 Ha in E_nuc; six image cells in K: +0.5000 Ha) against the exact
molecular UHF -0.46658185 Ha; H2 / STO-3G RHF gave -1.61675811 Ha in a
24-bohr box (-0.5 Ha) and -5.30082663 Ha in a 12-bohr box against the
molecular -1.11671433 Ha. The 50-bohr anchors of the existing tests never
saw the defect because no image cell lies inside either default cutoff.

`_home_cell_electrostatics_lat_opts` now derives two lattice-option clones
for these paths: `nuclear_cutoff_bohr = 0` for V_ne and E_nuc (home-cell
nuclei, ket-image overlap classes kept consistent with S and T) and
`cutoff_bohr = 0` for the COSX builder (home-cell exchange). Post-fix the
H atom lands at -0.46673838 Ha, 9.4e-6 Ha from the molecular RIJCOSX UHF
oracle and 1.6e-4 Ha from exact UHF (the COSX quadrature floor); H2 RHF is
8.2e-5 (12 bohr) and 4.3e-5 Ha (24 bohr) from molecular RHF, the same
box-limit/DF floor as the 50-bohr anchor; RKS PBE0 (H2, 12 bohr) and UKS
PBE0 (H atom, 12 bohr) sit 9.1e-5 and 1.6e-4 Ha from their molecular
oracles. The tight-cell RHF path (periodic GDF J + image-cell COSX K in the
Ewald-3D gauge) is unchanged. Regression:
`tests/test_periodic_rijcosx.py::test_rijcosx_gamma_vacuum_padded_home_cell_electrostatics`;
user guide `periodic_methods.md` § 4.8 documents the home-cell contract.

## [v0.15.162] - 2026-09-06 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Added: `aiccm-ri-mp2` / `aiccm-ri-ccsd` harness routes beside the bare four-centre ones (#719, Task #12, 2026-09-06)

The second half of D-5's answer: harness Task #12 resolved as its **third**
option, so the neutral RI correlation routes land *beside* the bare four-centre
`aiccm-mp2` / `aiccm-ccsd` in `studies/aiccm-2026/run_case.py` rather than
replacing or renaming them. Every published 1-D/2-D bare number stays
reproducible under the name it was published with.

The two are **complementary, not one superseding the other**, which is what
makes the parallel-route choice the right one rather than a courtesy:

* the bare routes are dense (no RI decomposition of the bare ω^sym), so they
  are 1-D/2-D only;
* the neutral RI routes reach 3-D but refuse `dim < 3`, because
  `ccm_neutral_cderi` needs a genuine 3-D reciprocal mesh -- a
  transverse-collapsed one makes the Coulomb kernel a sheet term proportional
  to 1/V instead of 1/r. That refusal is `_reject_transverse_collapse`, and it
  names the 1-D alternative (`periodic.ccm.lowd_scf.run_ccm_rhf_wire`).

The new routes join `_NEUTRAL_POSTHF_RESEARCH_ROUTES` alongside the
`aiccm-dlpno-*` family and are deliberately **not** in
`_GAMMA_CCM_CONSTRUCTION_ROUTES`: they are declared neutral fitted-torus
controls, not union-and-weight Γ-CCM results (ruling R1, D89). `_route_semantics`
reports them as `ccm_approach="not-applicable"`,
`ccm_construction="neutral-fitted-torus-research"`,
`route_role="post-hf-research-route"`, identical to `aiccm-dlpno-mp2`, while
bare `aiccm-mp2` keeps `ccm_approach="gamma-ccm"` /
`ccm_construction="union-and-weight"`.

Measured end to end on LiH rocksalt at `nrep=(1,1,1)`, `ke_cutoff=40`:
`e_hf = -8.330466726683`, `e_correlation = -0.006413130` Ha
(-0.003206565 per atom), with the record stamping `reference_route="direct"`
and the SCF backend it was built on.

### Changed: the A-line RI correlation reference defaults to `reference="direct"` (#719, D-5, 2026-09-06)

**This moves every A-line RI-MP2 and RI-CCSD number produced without an
explicit `reference=`.** `run_ccm_ri_mp2` and `run_ccm_ri_ccsd` defaulted to
`reference="neutral"`, the lean strict-zero-mode SCF. `HANDOVER_D2_EXXDIV.md`
measured that this reference's error grows linearly in the cluster size
(LiH, -1.22 to -29.0 Ha per atom) and concluded `exxdiv="ewald"` is the correct
convention. A standard method cannot ship correlation on a reference measured
to be wrong, so the maintainer took the flip (D-5, 2026-09-05) ahead of the
AICCM correlation arm.

Reproduced on this tree while making the change -- H2 chain, STO-3G, cell
`diag(6, 15, 15)` bohr, `ke_cutoff=40`, both legs riding the **same** neutral
`L` so that only the SCF reference route differs:

| nrep | ΔE_hf (direct − neutral) | per cell | ΔE_corr MP2 | ΔE_corr CCSD |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| (2,1,1) | +0.956443 Ha | 0.478 | +6.088 mHa | +9.981 mHa |
| (3,1,1) | +2.449583 Ha | 0.817 | +6.495 mHa | +11.028 mHa |
| (4,1,1) | +4.070138 Ha | 1.018 | +7.837 mHa | +14.062 mHa |

The reference difference diverges -- roughly 1.5 Ha per added cell, with the
per-cell figure still climbing, so it is not a constant offset that could be
absorbed. Over the same range the correlation itself moves only 6.1 to 7.8 mHa.
The defect is in the strict-zero reference, not in the correlation built on it,
which is what makes flipping the reference the fix rather than a recalibration.

`reference="neutral"` remains selectable and documented; both drivers'
docstrings now carry the measurement instead of the sentence that justified the
old default. No production caller took the default: every default-taking call
site was in `tests/test_ccm_mp2.py`, and each is now explicit about which
reference it means, so the tests pin both routes rather than one by omission. A
new node pins the default itself, since a suite where every call names its
reference would not notice the default being flipped back.

### Added: the FINE cavity is selectable from `run_cpcm_scf` (issue #558, 2026-09-06)

`SolventModel(cavity="fine")` now drives a real calculation on the Klamt &
Diedenhofen 2018 COSMO FINE Cavity; `"lebedev"` remains the default. On
water/STO-3G at eps = 78.39 the two give `E_solv` = -3.85 and -3.35 kcal/mol,
so the default is deliberately unchanged: switching it would move every
solvated energy.

The concern flagged when the cavity landed, that the CFC would need its own
`A`-matrix diagonal, turned out to be unfounded. vibe-qc's diagonal
`1.0694*sqrt(4*pi)/sqrt(w) = 3.7909/sqrt(w)` *is* Klamt 1993 eq. 7b's
`a_uu ~ 3.8 |S_u|^(-1/2)`: the self-energy of a patch of area `w`, which
depends on the segment's area and not on how the tessellation produced it. The
same builder serves both, and the `A` matrix is verified positive definite on
CFC segments.

**The analytic gradient refuses a FINE cavity** rather than returning a wrong
number, *as of this entry* -- see #729 and #746 below, which derived and then
assembled it; `cpcm_gradient` accepts a CFC today. At this point it
differentiated the cavity through two assumptions of the Lebedev construction,
both stated in its own header: segments move rigidly with their parent atom,
and the only other geometry dependence is the Scalmani-Frisch erf switching
function. A CFC has neither, so the result would have been smooth, plausible
and wrong, which is precisely the #546 failure mode.

Also removes a third copy of the cavity-radius formula. It was written out in
`cavity.py` and again in the solvation gradient; both now use one
`cavity.atom_radii_bohr`, so a gradient can no longer see radii that differ
from the ones its energy's cavity was built with.

### Fixed: `method="aiccm"` real-gamma and four-center are reachable with default arguments again (#692, 2026-09-05)

`bbe7b9001` (#666 #667 #668 #671) gave the supercell-Gamma AICCM variants a
guard that refuses every initial guess but `HCORE`, which is the only one their
SCF loops implement. The runner-wide default was `SAD`, so both variants then
failed with **default arguments**:

```
NotImplementedError: run_periodic_job: method='aiccm', variant='four-center'
does not implement initial_guess='SAD'.
```

Half of a documented front door was unreachable without an explicit
`initial_guess`, and eight tests on the #670 arm went red for the same reason:
they exercise the four-centre external-XC route without passing a guess, so the
SAD refusal fired before the guard each one asserts (the order is
`periodic_runner.py:7080` before `:7813` and `:8474`).

The temporary `_INITIAL_GUESS_UNSET` sentinel restored the variant-aware
default. The unified initial-guess framework above supersedes that sentinel
with literal `AUTO` and one capability-aware resolver. AUTO retains `SAD`
on ordinary periodic routes and resolves to `HCORE` for
`variant="real-gamma"` and `variant="four-center"`, with the resolution
printed and recorded. **An explicit `initial_guess="SAD"` on those two
variants still fails before SCF**.

Measured on H2/STO-3G in a 6-bohr cube: both variants now run with default
arguments and return energies bit-identical to their explicit-`HCORE` runs
(`real-gamma` -1.2385562879, `four-center` -1.1167143251); explicit `SAD` still
raises on both; `jk_method="gdf"` with default arguments is unchanged and equal
to its explicit-`SAD` run. `tests/test_xc_external_provider.py` goes from
8 failed / 110 passed to **118 passed**.

Regression: two nodes in `tests/test_periodic_ccm_real_gamma_adapter.py`
pinning that the defaulted run equals the explicit-`HCORE` run, that explicit
`SAD` still raises, and that ordinary periodic AUTO retains the SAD choice.

Nothing released yet. Entries land here as they are merged and are
promoted into a dated version section at the next tag.

### Fixed: accepted-density entropy in multi-k GDF (#705, #728)

Smeared KRHF/KRKS and KUHF/KUKS now compute entropy from the natural
occupations of the density used for the reported energy, including mixed
densities. A terminal canonical refill no longer substitutes its entropy
into the previous density's free energy. Regression checks cover AO-coordinate
invariance, invalid natural occupations, the returned SCF state, and the
existing DIIS/plain free-energy tolerance. Atomic or restart seeds outside
the fermionic occupation interval undergo one Fermi refill of their own
Fock before the counted free-energy iterations.

### Fixed: libint Boys table endpoint overrun (#754)

At exactly `T = 117`, libint's Chebyshev Boys evaluator selected an interval
past the end of its table. This could corrupt periodic GDF short-range
integrals before SCF. The native dependency recipe now sends that endpoint
to libint's existing large-argument evaluator, including when updating an
already-installed dependency. Generated integral kernels are unchanged;
C++ consumers must be rebuilt against the corrected header.


### Fixed: the inline PM7 pair table is MOPAC's, and PM7 parameter metadata reports its Apache-2.0 provenance (issue #440, 2026-09-06)

Independent verification of the 2026-08-28 fix found that the claim "every
shipped PM7 number is copied from `parameters_for_PM7_C.F90`" was true for
the 65 inline element values and false for the pair table: 28 of the 30
inline diatomic `alpb`/`xfac` values (all pairs except H-H) matched neither
MOPAC nor the bundled `pm7_mopac_params.toml` cache (H-C inline
0.950468/0.207259 vs MOPAC 1.038716/0.204582). They had been introduced with
the PM7 method in `d333f5adc` with no source recorded, so under the issue's
tolerance their licence could not be inferred. Maintainer decision
2026-09-06: they do not ship. The inline pair table now carries MOPAC's
values, re-verified against the upstream file and the cache (95/95 inline
values exact), and `tests/test_nddo_parameter_identity.py` pins the inline
tables against the cache by value so the two cannot drift apart again.

The runtime metadata caught up with the inventory at the same time: the PM7
content digests are allowlisted next to PM6's, so `load_pm7_params()` reports
`published:pm7-mopac-inline-v1` and `load_pm7_mopac_params()`
`published:pm7-mopac-full-v1`, both with `license = "Apache-2.0"` and the
Stewart 2013 DOI, instead of a `custom:<sha256>` identity with a blank
licence. These identities describe parameter provenance only; the PM7
Hamiltonian stays gated exactly as before. No PM7 energy exists to move.

### Fixed: OM2 attribution names Dral 2016 Table 2 as the parameter source and Weber & Thiel 2000 as the method paper (issue #272, 2026-09-06)

Independent verification of the 2026-09-02 inventory fix found one false
line: `docs/license.md` and the `omx_params.py` source comments said the OM2
values were "originally Weber & Thiel 2000, Table 2". That paper's Table 2
is an orthogonalization-energy table for H3-, not a parameter table; the OM2
parameters were first published in full in Dral et al. 2016, Table 2, which
is where vibe-qc's values were transcribed from. Maintainer wording
2026-09-06: Dral 2016 Table 2 is the parameter source and Weber & Thiel 2000
is cited for the method. The inventory, the source comments and the cite
block now say exactly that; the runtime metadata (`license = "published
parameter table"`, Dral DOI) was already right and is unchanged, and no
parameter value moved.

Because prose-to-prose pins cannot catch a wrong attribution, the citation
database gained an optional `role` field (`"parameter-source"` /
`"method"`, provenance bookkeeping only, not rendered and not written to the
manifest): Dral 2016 carries `parameter-source`, the Kolb & Thiel 1993,
Weber & Thiel 2000 and Scholten 2003 entries carry `method`, and the OMx
route test asserts that Dral 2016 is the one parameter source on every OMx
route and that the docs no longer name Weber's Table 2.

### Changed: the consumers of the one-electron cell list are list-agnostic; the Ewald-split nuclear family refuses `pair_complete_1e` (#429 stage 2, Family 2, 2026-09-06)

Family 1 made `S`, `T` and the direct `V_ne` ride the pair-complete cell
list behind `LatticeSumOptions.pair_complete_1e`; the two-electron builds
keep the plain `|g|` ball, an exact prefix of it. Every consumer that paired
the two lists index-for-index now reads the ball as a prefix of the longer
list, so the switch runs end to end on the direct-truncated routes. Default
still off; with the switch off every site below is bit-identical (the
consumer suites and the switch-off pins in the new test file say so).

* C++ `run_rhf_periodic` / `run_rks_periodic`: `F(g) = Hcore(g) + F2e(g)`
  is assembled from `Hcore` outward (the outer one-electron cells used to
  be cut back to the two-electron length), the RKS energy and its
  post-loop `J`/`K` decomposition trace the two-electron sets over their
  own length, and the PATOM guess widens its in-field Fock onto `Hcore`'s
  list instead of refusing. MINAO's periodic cross overlap enumerates
  pair-complete under the switch. H2 in a 6-bohr box / STO-3G / 2x2x2 at an
  8-bohr cutoff (7 ball cells, 19 pair-complete): RHF moves from
  -34.655444157536 to -34.655500639285 Ha (5.6e-05, the dropped tail), LDA
  by 8.4e-05; the difference is 6e-07 at 10 bohr and 5e-11 at 15 bohr where
  the lists coincide. PATOM, MINAO and Hückel reach the SAD fixed point to
  1e-14 under the switch.
* Python: `symmetry_integrals_reduced` templates the reduced `S`/`T`
  reconstruction on `one_electron_lattice_cells` (new, the one place the
  list is chosen) and hands the pair cutoff to the explicit builders, so the
  reduced blocks match the full builder to 1e-15 with 57 cells as with 19;
  the BIPOLE symmetric assembly takes its template from the same helper.
  The padded `J`/`K` re-templating zero-fills the pair-complete tail, cell
  moments and the spheropole read the ball as a prefix of a longer density,
  `build_exchange_blocks` aligns the K builder's blocks to the density list
  by cell key, and the multi-k Ewald orbit mapping is built on the K
  builder's own radial list. A 1D BIPOLE H2 chain (direct `V_ne`) runs
  under the switch with 3 versus 5 cells.
* Refusal, not a silent prefix: `compute_nuclear_erfc_lattice`,
  `compute_nuclear_lattice_ewald`, `compute_vsap_lattice` and
  `nuclear_erfc_lattice_gradient_contribution` raise `ValueError` naming the
  switch when it is set. The erfc half and the reciprocal / grid half of
  that split must cover the same term set, and only the erfc half has a
  pair-resolved enumeration; an `Hcore` that kept `T(g)` and `S(g)` on the
  tail cells while `V_ne(g)` is absent there would be a different operator,
  not a tighter truncation (the prototype measured a 2.2e-05 Ha/bohr
  analytic-vs-FD gradient move from widening one half alone). Every 3D
  route that takes `V_ne` from the split (BIPOLE, multi-k Ewald, GDF)
  therefore raises under the switch; moving both halves is the gauge
  decision handed to the route that builds the reciprocal half.
* Measured and recorded so nobody reads the switch as a fix on its own: the
  SCF energy of the direct-truncated C++ route is not invariant to
  re-describing the crystal with an atom moved by a lattice vector even with
  the switch on (H2 box at 8 bohr: -0.536 Ha off, -0.543 Ha on), because the
  two-electron ball and the truncated Coulomb sums carry the same defect and
  the exact one-electron sums stop cancelling part of it. The default flip
  waits for the two-electron family and the Ewald nuclear family.
* Tests: `tests/test_pbc_pair_complete_consumers.py` (15 collected tests: the pinned
  switch-off and switch-on energies, guess fixed points, the refusals, the
  four Python consumers, the reduced-symmetry match, the 1D BIPOLE run).

### Added: pair-complete one-electron lattice enumeration behind `LatticeSumOptions.pair_complete_1e` (#429 stage 2, Family 1, 2026-09-06)

The one-electron `S`, `T` and direct `V_ne` lattice sums select their image
cells by translation length, `|g| <= cutoff_bohr`, where the interaction
they truncate depends on the pair separation `|O_mu - O_nu - g|` (Sharma
and Beylkin, *JCTC* 17, 3916 (2021), Eqs. 17-18). The two differ on any
cell with an intra-cell offset: at the shipped 15-bohr cutoff the Gamma
overlap of LiH rocksalt / def2-SVP moves by 7.2e-01 (an O(1) element) and
MgO / def2-SVP by 8.7e-02 when the same crystal is described with an atom
one lattice vector away, and a Gamma supercell wider than the cutoff
collapses to a free-boundary cluster (stage 1, 3b60a2ca5, refuses that on
the BIPOLE route). The one-electron cell list also grows by about 2.7x
under the correct criterion (MgO at the default: 135 -> 369 cells), and a
family of consumers pairs that list index-for-index with the two-electron
ball, so the sweep's landing rule applies: per consumer family, behind a
guard, with every pin move counted.

* `LatticeSumOptions.pair_complete_1e` (default `False`, bit-identical to
  the historical sums): when set, `compute_{overlap,kinetic,nuclear}_lattice`
  enumerate `{(mu, nu, g) : |O_mu - O_nu - g| <= cutoff_bohr}` -- the ball
  padded by the largest intra-cell shell offset (a plain sphere, so the
  symmetry-orbit machinery keeps a point-group-closed list), each pair
  filtered on its physical separation, parallelised over (cell, bra shell)
  and bit-reproducible -- and the overlap / kinetic / direct-nuclear
  gradient partners differentiate that same set. The explicit-cell builders
  take `pair_cutoff` (0.0 = every pair of every supplied cell, the SYM3b
  contract), `vibeqc.pair_complete_lattice_cells` exposes the enumerated
  list (an exact prefix extension of `direct_lattice_cells`), and
  `overlap_lattice_gradient_contribution` gains `apply_pair_filter` for the
  one caller whose `S` is the all-pairs sum (the Ewald-split `V_ne` G=0
  correction). The switch is threaded through every option passthrough.
* Deliberately not given the pair treatment (measured and reverted in the
  prototype 7d1812152 this is ported from): the Ewald-split nuclear family
  (`compute_nuclear_erfc_lattice`, `compute_vsap_lattice`,
  `compute_nuclear_lattice_ewald`, the FT `V_ne`; filtering one half of a
  split breaks the reconstruction, 2.2e-05 Ha/bohr analytic-vs-FD residual)
  and the cell-resolved multipole moments (the position operator grows with
  `|g|` and the sum is conditionally convergent; widening it moved the H4
  Boys spreads from 3.04 to 91/169 bohr^2).
* Measured with the switch on (`tests/test_periodic_1electron.py`): the
  three audited rocksalt rows are translation invariant to
  round-off (S and T: 4.6e-15 and 2.4e-15 on LiH/def2-svp, 3.9e-15 and 1.4e-14 on MgO/def2-svp, 6.0e-16 and 6.2e-15 on MgO/sto-3g, where the default enumeration moves by 7.2e-01, 2.7e-02, 9.4e-02, 1.6e-02, 2.4e-06 and 6.4e-06; MgO's list grows 135 -> 369 cells) for `S` and `T`; the default stays off and
  bit-identical; the padded list extends the plain ball as a prefix and
  the builders enumerate it; the switched-on overlap gradient matches
  central differences of `sum_g Tr[W(g) S(g)]`. The strict xfail on the
  default enumeration stays and names the switch, so the default cannot
  flip without its consumer families being re-measured.
* Citation `sharma_beylkin_two_center_2021` added to the database; it is
  routed on the periodic Gaussian routes when the switch becomes their
  default and is cited at the code sites until then.
  `docs/user_guide/periodic_methods.md` documents the switch.

Next (Family 2): the consumers that pair the one-electron list
index-for-index with the two-electron ball, then the default flip per
family. Handed onward: the BIPOLE `J^LR` cache consumed against two cell
lists (a gauge decision, BIPOLE handover ask) and the GDF / GPW / GAPW
Python consumers (GDF refactor once the contract exists).

### Added: the COSMO FINE Cavity of Klamt & Diedenhofen 2018 (issue #558, 2026-09-06)

`vibeqc.solvation.fine_cavity` implements the CFC construction of
J. Comput. Chem. 39, 1648 (2018), `10.1002/jcc.25342`.

vibe-qc's existing cavity paves each atomic sphere with a Lebedev grid and
switches segments off where spheres overlap. That describes the *convex* solute
surface well and leaves the concave crevices between atoms unpaved, which is the
known deficiency of Klamt's original COC construction. It matters more for
COSMO-RS than for a solvation energy: screening charge *density* is the model's
central descriptor, so polarization charge piling up at the edges of paved
regions distorts a sigma profile directly.

The CFC replaces the geometric patchwork with a single smooth iso-surface. A
scalar pseudo-density (eq. 8) is built from the atom positions and the cavity is
its `PD = 1` level set, triangulated by marching tetrahedra. Concave regions pave
automatically because the surface has no seams, and because `PD` is an analytic
function of the atom positions the segment positions and areas are
differentiable. Implemented with the paper's own parameters
(`a1 = -15`, `a2 = -9`, `c = 5`, `m = 4`, `delta = 0.3` Å, NSPH = 92,
NSPA = 162) and its full workflow, including geodesic segment grids on the COC
"magic numbers" `10 n^2 + 2`.

Validated where exact answers exist rather than against COSMOtherm, for which no
reference segment set is published: an isolated atom's `PD = 1` surface is the van
der Waals sphere to five decimal places, which pins the radius-scaled relative
distance in eq. 8; a sphere's triangulated area and volume both converge at
O(h^2) to 0.01 %; the mesh is closed at every grid spacing; segment coarsening
conserves the triangulated area exactly; and the pair term demonstrably inflates
the surface past the union of spheres, which is the whole purpose of the
construction.

**Correction to an earlier measurement.** The COSMO-RS notes recorded that our
cavity was about twice the area Klamt's parameters were fitted on, based on the
24.7 Å² water entry in Klamt 1995 Table 1. That comparison was against the wrong
construction: Table 1 is a COC area, which paves only convex regions, and the
2018 paper states that the standard cavity's ring and triple-point closure
"increases the area of the cavity by about 60 %". Measured directly, the CFC and
the union-of-spheres areas agree closely at the same radii: water 43.05 against
42.08 Å², methane 56.6 against 56.1, trimethylamine 99.6 against 101.1 (within
1.5 % in each case, in both directions). So the protocol mismatch is much smaller
than previously reported, and the CFC's value is homogeneous paving and
differentiability rather than a different total area.


### Performance: generate density-screened erfc lattice pairs before quartet expansion (#21)

The BIPOLE direct erfc builder now joins Schwarz-sorted displacement supports
and uses Cartesian range queries with local density bounds. Shell-prefix
screening rejects groups before quartet expansion; bounded primitive-pair
caches reuse integral setup. The existing accepted contributions and their
summation order are retained. Exhaustive enumeration remains available through
`sr_sparse_traversal=False` and as a bounded-memory fallback.
When periodic density support fills the candidate list, a bitmap represents
domains of up to 4,096 cells within the same 2 MiB scratch budget.

The padded LiH/pob-TZVP home-block kernel fixture (13 basis functions, 2,315
internal cells, overlap density) examines 242,527 rather than 5,359,225 cell
pairs and ran in 6.3 rather than 25.9 seconds locally. Complete 321-block J/K
comparisons and targeted signed-density, angular-momentum, derivative, domain,
and overflow tests agree with the exhaustive build. These are kernel results;
full-node SCF timing remains a separate validation gate. Cutoffs, Ewald split
parameters and SCF tolerances are unchanged.

### Fixed: announce BIPOLE exact confirmation before the cold build (#115)

`bipole_final_density_phase` (landed for #115 as b9d1860b6) announced the
expensive non-incremental rebuild and emitted the loop's energy to the
structured log before it, but #514 then moved that rebuild of a converged
run INSIDE the loop (the exact confirmation, now the #116 terminal check),
ahead of the phase: the verifier found the only cold build of a converged
He/STO-3G (2,1,1) run at call 4 with the phase not yet announced, and the
`scf_final_density_begin` record written after the work it protects, so a
wall-kill during the rebuild still lost the provisional energy. The context
manager also emitted "done" and `scf_final_density_end` from a bare
`finally`, so a rebuild that raised was reported as a successful end.

* `pbc_bipole_common.bipole_confirmation_phase` wraps the in-loop exact
  confirmation in all four drivers: `scf_exact_confirmation_begin` carries
  the loop's provisional energy, iteration and convergence flag BEFORE the
  cold build, the text names the build and its first-iteration cost class,
  and `scf_exact_confirmation_end` carries the wall time. The post-loop
  `bipole_final_density_phase` takes `reused=True` when it reuses that
  build and says so (`status="reused"`, no extra Fock build), so the bound
  on the post-SCF cost is one cold build per exact confirmation the loop
  needed (usually one) and none after the loop. A max-iteration exit builds
  once after the loop unless confirmation already evaluated that density.
  Failed confirmation at the iteration cap retains its exact build for
  finalization while preserving the non-converged verdict.
* Both phases end with `status="raised"` and the exception text when the
  build throws, and re-raise; "done" is emitted only on success.
* `tests/test_bipole_final_density_phase.py` is now ordering-aware: a spy
  on the shared builder records, at every non-incremental build of a real
  converged run, whether the announcement was already in the progress
  stream; the confirmation's begin record precedes its end and the final
  phase's begin, carries the provisional energy, and the final phase reports
  reuse; a raising build ends `raised` with no "done"; a max-iteration exit
  pays exactly one cold build, in the final phase.

### Performance: avoid repeated config parsing in queue policy checks (#547)

Queue policy checks reuse TOML parsing for identical file contents while still
reading and validating the current policy on every check. This reduces retained
queue scan overhead; terminal retention and live-job indexing remain pending.

### Fixed: broker provenance, lease expiry and verifier workflow (#347, #443, #453, #572, #696)

Bugctl now separates expiring work leases from immutable fix manifests,
supports multiple repository commits and hashed carriers, and projects verifier
workflow states. Verdicts require evidence. Deployment and independent
verification remain pending.

### Added: periodic GDF source foundation (#142)

Added native SR/LR periodic GDF integral sources with one zero-mode
convention and memory-admitted workers; production SCF integration remains
in progress.

### Experimental: native selected short-range erfc integrals and multi-k fold

The BIPOLE correlation source now has bounded C++ physical erfc quartet
panels and a complex multi-k phase fold over explicitly ordered integer
image triples. Exact modular phase addressing, immutable input/output
receipts and composed raw/fold memory-work admission are retained without
an implicit k-point weight, density screening or symmetry averaging.
Tiny tests cover independent s/p/d Gaussian moments, shifted meshes,
quartet reanchoring, complete time-reversal-compatible Hermitian-density
basis J/K recontractions, immutable receipts and exact resource boundaries.

This is a selected-contribution interface, not a complete periodic
Hamiltonian or production DLPNO-CCSD(T) route. Finite-domain permutation
closure, the matched long-/short-range and zero-mode source, native HF
capture, and representative-only CCSD/triples execution remain unfinished.

### Fixed: displaced Gaussian-product support in Ewald nuclear attraction (#704, partial)

The shared analytic V_ne Ewald source now pads its short-range nuclear-image
sum for AO-product displacement and Gaussian smearing, not only the bare
point-charge erfc radius. Its analytic derivative uses the same support rule.
The electronic output cells, alpha and exchange-q=0 convention are unchanged.
This repairs the dominant chi multi-k half-translation symmetry defect and
qualifies the three-character He2 regression at the existing sewing budget.
The two-character residual remains gated; full symmetry-reduced multi-k
DLPNO-CCSD(T) and analytic total chi gradients are not enabled.

### Experimental: chi RHF snapshot bridge to native orbital sewing (#703)

D130 connects full-mesh all-electron 3D four-center chi RHF output to the
shared immutable native numerical state. Recorded Fock, overlap, orbitals,
energies and occupations are preserved; recorded k coordinates and weights
are audited under the native uniform-weight contract;
exact frozen bands remain separate from correlated occupied and virtual
spaces. Explicit-array admission precedes snapshot copies. The bridge keeps
the chi finite-torus convention and declared provenance, without treating
them as authenticated integral-source evidence. Native orbital sewing can
now be tested on this chi-owned state; no symmetry-reduced energy or analytic
gradient gate is enabled.

### Fixed: fail closed on 3-D GFN2-SECCM Ewald gamma without a thermodynamic limit (#444)

Non-molecular 3-D `ewald_gamma=True` now rejects at the native route
boundary before the WS-folded Klopman-Ohno-minus-Coulomb kernel is used.
Its pair-dependent `R^-3` remainder can accumulate logarithmically with
cluster size; finite WS ownership and SCC convergence do not cure it.
Public and raw native rejection tests include non-molecular group-order-one
topologies, while exact molecular delegation and 1-D/2-D paths are preserved.
No GFN2-to-Elstner mapping, finite-distance energetics, solver threshold or
replacement scientific default changes. Separate #211/#425 contracts stay
unchanged.

Fixed-charge tests distinguish the historical synthetic cubic Mg4O4 probe
from true B1 rocksalt and isolate both measured size steps to the WS
remainder. Named #130 Cu gates retain their historical energy/size evidence
and now pin explicit production rejection; restart/mixer diagnostics use a
permitted AES-active 2-D fixture. Documentation withdraws the erroneous 3-D
convergence claim and corrects Janetzko 2002 pagination and Bredow 2001's
finite-shell versus exact-Ewald attribution. No broad GFN2 citation route
or IO selector is added.

### Experimental: streamed native reciprocal-Ewald selected integrals

The BIPOLE correlation work now has a C++ explicit-cell AO Fourier panel
and a one-q selected long-range integral kernel. They preserve the declared
cell support and full complex Bloch phases, bound both AO and reciprocal
panels, and expose optional cell-inversion and reciprocal-conjugacy checks
without averaging. Scale-safe weighted products avoid premature underflow
and overflow, including cancellation before a restoring Coulomb weight.

Tiny tests compare independent Gaussian integrals, complete Hermitian-density
basis J/K recontractions and their adjoints, shifted meshes, exact resource
caps, and single selected MgO/diamond pob-TZVP-rev2 integrals on 8x8x8
addressing. This is only the nonzero reciprocal erf arm. It does not yet
provide a complete matched BIPOLE Hamiltonian, HF source, symmetry-reduced
CCSD/triples execution or target-system correlated energies.

### Added: pinned driver update for legacy direct vq hosts (#677)

Added a pinned current-driver update for legacy direct hosts, with archive
integrity checks, configuration-drift refusal, and retained recovery code after
interrupted execution. An explicit bootstrap command lets older remote scheduler
drivers enter the same authenticated runtime through first-class self-update,
preserving global rollout ownership and service checks. Independent fleet
verification remains pending.

### Added: the DLPNO PNO occupation-number convention is selectable and disclosed (#701, 2026-09-07)

`tcut_pno` is a threshold on the eigenvalues of a pair density, so the
published LoosePNO/NormalPNO/TightPNO values only mean what Liakos et al.
calibrated them to mean under the density they were calibrated against.
That density is Riplinger and Neese, *J. Chem. Phys.* **138**, 034106 (2013),
Eq. 23, which ORCA selects as `%mdci PNONorm MP2Norm`:

```
D = Tt T^T + Tt^T T ,   Tt = (4 T - 2 T^T) / (1 + delta_ij)
```

`Tt` is the spin-adapted contravariant amplitude that already carries the
closed-shell pair energy (Eq. 14 of Neese, Wennmohs and Hansen,
*J. Chem. Phys.* **130**, 114108 (2009), which vibe-qc evaluates as
`w * sum(T * (2 K - K^T))` with `w = 2 / (1 + delta_ij)`). vibe-qc's three
closed-shell PNO builders instead diagonalise the density of the **bare**
amplitudes, `D = (T T^T + T^T T) / (1 + delta_ij)`, which is neither the MP2
norm nor the older LPNO IEPA norm.

The consequence is exact and was verified numerically. Splitting
`T = S + A` into symmetric and antisymmetric parts,

```
D_mp2    = [4 S^2 + 12 A^T A] / (1 + delta_ij)
D_legacy = [2 S^2 +  2 A^T A] / (1 + delta_ij)
```

so every published occupation number is between **2x** (a purely
singlet-like symmetric direction, and exactly 2x for any diagonal pair,
whose `T` is symmetric) and **6x** the one vibe-qc compares against. Because
the factor varies within a single pair, no rescaling of `tcut_pno` reproduces
the other convention's PNO set. At the same nominal threshold the historical
density therefore retains fewer PNOs, i.e. it is effectively looser than the
preset name implies. Measured from identical amplitudes in identical domains,
the deficit is 4.6 % to 18.5 % at NormalPNO and grows with basis size
(13.5 % on H2O/cc-pVTZ, 18.5 % on the S22-02 water dimer at cc-pVDZ).

* New `vibeqc.dlpno.pno_density` holds the three conventions with their
  equations and citations inline: `"legacy"` (the historical density),
  `"mp2"` (Riplinger and Neese Eq. 23) and `"iepa"` (the pre-2013 LPNO
  convention, Neese, Wennmohs and Hansen Eqs. 18-19, a per-pair scalar
  `(1 + delta_ij) / N_ij` on top of `"mp2"`). ORCA's `MP2Norm` and `IEPANorm`
  spellings resolve too. Exported as `pair_density` / `resolve_pno_norm` /
  `PNO_NORMS`.
* `LocalCCSDOptions`, `DLPNOMP2Options` and `DLPNOCCSDPilotOptions` take
  `pno_norm`, **defaulting to `"legacy"`, so no shipped number moves.** Which
  convention should ship is #701, a maintainer decision: changing the default
  moves every DLPNO energy and every retained reference, and it should be
  taken on measured recovery, not on this option existing.
* The selected convention is disclosed like the residual domain is: a
  `PNO density norm` row in the `.out` correlated block, `dlpno_pno_norm` in
  the `.system` manifest, and `pno_norm` on the `dlpno_ccsd_done` event.
* H2O/def2-SVP, average PNOs per pair and `e_corr`, same reference and same
  thresholds:

  | preset | legacy | mp2 | iepa | E(mp2) - E(legacy) |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | LoosePNO | 14.60 | 15.50 | 15.70 | -1.17e-4 Ha |
  | NormalPNO | 15.70 | 17.40 | 17.80 | -1.10e-4 Ha |
  | TightPNO | 17.40 | 18.20 | 18.60 | -1.02e-5 Ha |

  The published density recovers more correlation energy at every preset, and
  its NormalPNO result sits essentially on the legacy TightPNO value. The two
  published norms agree to well under a PNO per pair, reproducing Fig. 2 of
  the 2013 paper and the ORCA manual's "near identical".
* Open-shell routes are deliberately untouched and expose no `pno_norm`: the
  `4 T - 2 T^T` adaptation is a closed-shell spin-summation identity, and
  ORCA builds the open-shell PNOs from `T T^dagger` and `T^dagger T` with no
  such factor.
* Tests: `tests/test_dlpno.py::TestPNODensityConventions` pins the algebra
  (both published equations, the 2x-to-6x eigenvalue bound, the exact factor
  of 2 on a diagonal pair, positive semidefiniteness, alias resolution, and
  that `"legacy"` is byte-identical to the historical expression);
  `tests/test_dlpno_ccsd_solver.py::TestPNONormOnRealAmplitudes` pins the
  default being bit-identical to requesting it, the PNO-count direction on a
  real molecule, the two published norms nearly coinciding, and that all
  three agree at `tcut_pno=0` where nothing is truncated.

### Experimental: χ spatial-group and occupied cocycle checks (#697)

D129 checks all products of a supplied closed set of spatial cosets, retaining
the whole-cell translation in nonsymmorphic composition. Integer image laws,
identity, inverses, associativity and the twisted lattice cocycle are checked
before exposing immutable tables. The occupied witness additionally tests
the actual localized C/S representation, finite translations and all spatial
products without discarding complex orbital mixing. Independent real-torus
and native multi-k transport tests pin the translation phase. Memory and
relation-count admission precede the expensive factories. These diagnostics
do not yet enable symmetry-reduced DLPNO energies or analytic gradients.

### Fixed: the periodic PM6 fcc-Ar public-route test carries the post-#419 pins and cross-checks the driver (#641, 2026-09-05)

`tests/test_periodic_runner_semiempirical.py::test_run_periodic_job_pm6_fcc_argon_uses_bounded_native_branch`
was red on `main` since #419 (`44c7ec38a`, 2026-09-02): that change gave the
production Gamma-periodic PM6 lattice sums the exact heavy-heavy sp-sp
multipoles, which for the four-atom fcc-Ar cell makes the first Fock matrix
density-dependent (4 SCF iterations instead of 2) and lowers the cell energy
by 7.0e-5 Ha (-38.833302668977 to -38.833372664189 Ha). #419 re-pinned the
lower-level driver test but not this public-route pin. The values are #419's
intended result, not a regression: `run_periodic_job(method="pm6")` and the
low-level `run_pm6_gamma` agree to 1e-12 Ha and in iteration count on the
fixture, and the lower-level test's dissociation checks hold.

* The test now pins 4 iterations, -38.833372664189 Ha (2e-9) and the
  `.out` iteration line, with the #419 rationale inline, and additionally
  asserts the public route equals the low-level driver's energy (1e-12 Ha)
  and iteration count, so a future driver change cannot re-pin one test and
  leave the other red.
* No runtime code changed.

### Added: `bugctl reopen` reverses a recorded closure with a mandatory reason (issue #693, 2026-09-05)

`bugctl close` had no inverse. The compound `REOPENED` transition (reopen the
issue, remove `resolution::verified`, clear every stale `workflow::*` label,
set `workflow::triaged`) was in the workflow-plan contract and `REOPENED` was
a policy ledger event, but no verb produced either: #444, one of the 128
issues #520 found closed `resolution::verified` without a passing verifier
grant, was reopened by hand through the GitLab API and left no ledger event
behind. `bugctl reopen <iid> --reason <why>` (client verb plus
`POST /v1/reopen`) now applies that transition in one GitLab update and
records a durable, mirrored `REOPENED` event carrying the actor, run,
request, reason, and the labels it removed. The reason is refused as empty
before the broker is called; an issue that is not closed is refused; a
GitLab failure records nothing; a retry with the same derived request ID
replays instead of posting a second event; broker grants are left intact.
Who may reverse a verified closure is raised on #693, not decided here, the
128 issues are not touched, and deploying the broker half is a separate
step.

### Fixed: SECCM symmetry diagnostics retain slab layers and expose scan changes (#421)

The translation-orbit charge-spread diagnostic now compares full Cartesian
lattice displacements and species. Previously it discarded nonperiodic
coordinates and could report a false symmetry violation by combining different
slab layers, parallel chains, or elements. Nonfinite charges now report an
unavailable diagnostic (NaN), rather than zero spread.

`compare_gfn2_seccm_states(previous, current)` reports signed changes in charge
RMS, frontier gap, per-cell SCC/free energies, orbit spread, and electronic
temperature. It records whether parameter and Hamiltonian-option provenance
match and refuses comparisons of failed/nonfinite states. This diagnostic
adds no acceptance threshold or SCC change. It does not establish a unique
physical branch or repair the separate AES and 3-D gamma defects (#348/#444).

### Fixed: a passed-but-untouched KS options object no longer disables the `grid_level` default (#663, 2026-09-05)

`run_job(..., rks_options=RKSOptions())`, an empty default-constructed
options object passed to set `max_iter` or to satisfy a signature, silently
opted the run out of the documented `orca-defgrid3` default and ran on the
C++ construction grid, which is the `legacy` preset (product Gauss-Legendre
17x36, unpruned, Becke partition; 0.1 to 2.8 mHa from ORCA's DefGrid3). The
#251 fix had made "an options object was passed" the proxy for "the caller
chose a grid" (`_rks_options_were_explicit = rks_options is not None`, and the
same for UKS and ROKS), and `GridOptions` carries neither an "unset" sentinel
nor `__eq__`, so nothing downstream could tell an untouched grid from a
deliberately legacy one. Affected: any run since v0.15.142 (#251) that passed
a default-constructed KS options object to `run_job`, the ASE calculator or
`MolecularSCFProvider` ran on the legacy grid; re-run it if the documented
grid was intended.

* `runner.grid_is_untouched(grid)` compares every public `GridOptions` field
  against a fresh instance and `runner.ks_options_need_grid_default(options)`
  is true for no object, a `ROKSOptions` whose `grid` is `None`, or an
  untouched grid. The entry points that take a `grid_level` apply it on
  that rule instead of on object presence: `run_job`'s three branches,
  `_run_single_point` (RKS, UKS and ROKS), the ASE `VibeQC` calculator and
  `MolecularSCFProvider`. `run_job` now forwards its `grid_level` into the
  provider and the ASE optimizer backend it drives, so an explicit
  `grid_level="legacy"` RKS or UKS optimisation stays on the legacy grid
  instead of being re-defaulted downstream. (ROKS optimisations are not
  covered: the wavefunction/finite-difference optimizer path never received
  `roks_options` or `grid_level` and still walks a fresh `ROKSOptions` on
  orca-defgrid3 while the final single point uses the caller's options;
  pre-existing, recorded on #678.) The preset is written into the caller's
  own options object in place, so the object records the grid that ran;
  reuse that object in a later call and its grid counts as chosen (a
  different `grid_level` there is ignored, as documented in `run_job`,
  except after `"legacy"`, whose preset equals an untouched grid). `.system`'s
  `skala_grid_policy` reads `explicit-options` when the grid was customised
  or carries a preset from an earlier call. A grid set by hand to the exact
  construction defaults is indistinguishable from an untouched one; the
  supported way to request that grid is `grid_level="legacy"`.
* Left as they were: the low-level `run_rks` / `run_uks` wrappers use a
  supplied options object as given (dozens of test files build bare options
  for them and pin energies), and NEB and dimer, which have no `grid_level`
  parameter, take a supplied object's grid as given so the legacy grid stays
  reachable there. The wrappers' docstrings state the layering. The remaining
  bare-options sites (for example `run_wb97x_d`, the double-hybrid core,
  `optimize_molecule`, the free-atom references in `atomization.py`, and
  the wrappers themselves) are collected in #678 for a maintainer decision.
* `_copy_grid_options` (the TRAH retry path) now copies every public field;
  it dropped `atomic_grid_profile` and `vv10_grid_factor`, so a SKALA run
  that entered the retry lost its atomic-grid profile.
* Tests (`tests/test_grid_level.py`): the helper is checked field by field
  against the bound `GridOptions` attributes and recognises the legacy
  preset as the construction default; `run_job` with an empty `RKSOptions` /
  `UKSOptions` / `ROKSOptions` receives `grid_level="fine"` on the caller's
  own object (dry-run capture, all three methods; pre-fix the captured grid
  was the legacy default); the issue's repro pins the no-options and
  empty-options H2O/STO-3G PBE energies equal to 1e-12 Ha and different from
  the legacy grid; `_run_single_point` is pinned directly; the ASE
  calculator and the geometry provider apply the preset to an empty options
  object and the provider's gradient grid follows; `run_job(grid_level=
  "legacy")` through the geomopt provider and the ASE backend keeps the
  legacy grid; the reuse semantics (including the legacy-first case), the
  field-complete `_copy_grid_options`, and the low-level `run_rks` /
  `run_uks` contract are pinned.
* Docs: the `run_job`, `run_rks`, `run_uks`, `VibeQC` and
  `MolecularSCFProvider` docstrings, `docs/user_guide/ase_integration.md`,
  `geometry_optimization.md`, `keyword_index.md` and `skala.md` state the
  untouched-grid rule.
### Added: the def2 family beyond Kr, and periodic ECPs on the k-point GDF route (basis/ECP unification M3 + M4, 2026-09-05)

* **def2 through Rn.** libint's def2 files stop at Kr, so def2-SVP ..
  def2-QZVPPD on Ag, Sn, Pt or Bi either failed at the SAD guess or ran the
  atom with zero functions. The eleven files now carry the Basis Set
  Exchange Rb-Rn valence blocks appended to libint's H-Kr bytes (unchanged)
  and ship the def2-ECP as `.ecp` sidecars; AgH in def2-TZVP reproduces
  PySCF's def2-TZVP + def2-ECP to 1e-6 Ha. The diffuse `-d` sets have no
  lanthanide block and refuse one by name.
* **Periodic ECPs run on the default route.** `run_krhf_periodic_gdf`
  (and its RKS/UHF/UKS entries) build V_ne from a Z_eff nuclear frame,
  Bloch-sum the lattice V_ECP into every Hcore(k), use the Z_eff Ewald
  repulsion and fill the valence count, so `run_periodic_job` on a
  pob-TZVP-rev2 cell with Rb-Po or La-Lu atoms applies the ECP on
  jk_method='gdf' (#88). `PeriodicRHFOptions` now carries the four ECP
  fields, so a periodic RHF/UHF request on an ECP basis no longer dies on
  the runner's assignment with an internal AttributeError, and the UHF/UKS
  driver splits alpha/beta from the valence count (AgCl: 18/18, not 32/32).
  An ECP-bearing cell at the default Gamma mesh is routed to the k-point
  drivers at a one-point mesh instead of the `run_pbc_gdf_*` fast paths or
  the legacy Gamma driver, which read no ECP field (the reproduction's Mg
  RKS/PBE was identical with and without the ECP); called directly with
  ECP options those drivers now refuse. RIJCOSX, the Ewald open-shell
  drivers, ROHF/ROKS on GDF, slabs, BIPOLE and AICCM still refuse an
  ECP-bearing cell before any SCF work; BIPOLE/AICCM support belongs to
  those topic clones. The QVF DOS/PDOS/COOP/COHP payload is skipped for an
  ECP cell: it rebuilds a real-space property Hamiltonian from bare Z with
  no V_ECP, and on AgCl / pob-TZVP-rev2 that 4-index build ran for over 40
  minutes after a one-minute SCF. The periodic ECP resolver reads a basis'
  `.ecp` sidecar per element when the basis is not pob-TZVP-rev2, so
  LANL2DZ or def2 beyond Kr on a cell run with their ECP instead of hitting
  the ECP-paired-basis refusal (NaCl / LANL2DZ: Z_eff 1 and 7, 8 valence
  electrons).
* **`BasisSet` coverage guard and coincident centres.** The per-atom guard
  attributes a shell to the first atom at its origin, so two atoms of one
  element on the same point (the DF metric-guard fixture) read as a
  missing element. A coincident centre now borrows its twin's coverage; a
  genuinely absent element still raises.

### Changed: post-HF, ROHF/ROKS and the determinant solvers consume ECP references (basis/ECP unification M2, 2026-09-05)

Every route beyond mean-field refused an ECP reference because its kernel
partitioned occupied orbitals from `Molecule.n_electrons()`. The kernels now
use the reference's valence count, `n_electrons - ecp_total_ncore`.

* **Native MP2, UMP2, CCSD and UCCSD** partition from
  `effective_electron_count`; the element-table frozen-core default (`-1`)
  is refused natively on an ECP reference because it cannot subtract the
  removed cores, and the Python wrappers resolve the ECP-aware count and
  pass it explicitly (`run_ccsd_from_mos` / `run_uccsd_from_mos` require
  an explicit count for a nonzero `ecp_total_ncore`).
* **The published frozen-core convention subtracts the ECP core per atom:**
  `max(0, fc_A - n_core,A) / 2` orbitals.
  `published_frozen_core_orbital_count(molecule, reference)` and
  `resolve_frozen_core_count(..., reference=)` take the SCF result; the CC,
  DLPNO and MP2 wrappers and every `run_job` correlated execution site pass
  it. `refuse_ecp_correlated_reference` is gone.
* **ROHF and ROKS** apply the ECP operator on both routes:
  `ROHFOptions` carries the ECP fields, the sidecar is attached like on the
  native drivers, Hcore is `T + V_ne(Z_eff) + V_ECP` with the `Z_eff`
  repulsion and the valence count
  (`vibeqc.ecp_metadata.one_electron_hamiltonian`), and the results record
  the same provenance fields. Orphan metadata (a core count without an
  operator) is refused.
* **The determinant family** (CISD, CC3, CCSDT, selected CI, DMRG, v2RDM,
  transcorrelated CI, FCI) builds `build_hamiltonian_ao/mo(...,
  reference=)` from the reference operator and count; the HF orbital
  provider goes through the package-level SCF wrappers so the basis
  sidecar is attached. The double hybrids' gate is lifted. CASCI, MRCI,
  CASSCF, NEVPT2, CASPT2 and OVGF still refuse an ECP reference; every ECP
  derivative refusal beyond RHF/UHF/RKS/UKS gradients stays.
* **`BasisSet` refuses an element its file omits.** libint2 returned the
  atom with zero shells; Ag⁺ over benzene in def2-TZVP (bundled through Kr
  at the time) built and ran 88 electrons in ligand functions under the
  HCORE guess.
  The constructor now raises naming the elements; `require_all_atoms=False`
  is available to the coverage diagnostics that inspect gaps on purpose.
  The dead `PeriodicSCFOptions.ecp_centers` / `ecp_library` fields (never
  consumed or bound) are removed.
* Parity pins in `tests/test_ecp_correlated.py`: H2S/LANL2DZ RHF, MP2, CCSD
  and CISD and SH/LANL2DZ UHF, UMP2 and ROHF against PySCF to 1e-6 Ha; the
  QVF importer additionally no longer ends an element block on a blank
  line (def2-TZVP-C lost Ga-Br).

### Changed: one basis registry, ECPs attached inline and decided per element (basis/ECP unification M1, 2026-09-05)

A review of the basis-set and ECP stack, run with executed probes against
`dee0b3da8`, found that ECPs did not work end to end. This milestone lands
the data and metadata half of the fix; the effective-electron-count
plumbing through post-HF (M2), the periodic runner routes (M3) and the
def2 blocks beyond Kr (M4) are tracked in
`handovers/HANDOVER_BASIS_ECP_UNIFICATION.md`.

* **The sidecar is the ECP, attached inline on every route.**
  `attach_inline_ecp_options_from_basis_sidecar` no longer pairs a
  libecpint XML library by core count. That pairing sent Ag/vDZP to the
  Stuttgart `ecp28mdf` potential (13 primitives) instead of vDZP's own
  9-primitive potential (AgH: -146.53201 vs -146.61746 Ha, 85 mHa), died
  on standard-core elements the XML lacks (SiH4/vDZP: `stoi: no
  conversion`), and refused any molecule spanning two core sizes
  (CsI/dhf-TZVP "mixed-row") although the sidecar carried both. All three
  now run on the sidecar's own primitives; an explicit `ecp_centers` +
  `ecp_library` request still uses the XML libraries. CPCM consumes the
  inline route too (`run_cpcm_scf` used to refuse it).
* **Whether an atom needs an ECP is decided per element, never by name.**
  New `vibeqc.basis_registry` (`ecp_requirements`, `basis_replaces_core`)
  reads the sidecar first and then the family rules in
  `python/vibeqc/basis_library/registry.toml`. Consequences, each pinned:
  water in LANL2DZ or dhf-TZVP runs as the all-electron calculation it is
  (both were refused); `x2c-TZVPall`, an all-electron basis, runs on every
  element (it was refused as "ECP-paired"); AgH in `pob-tzvp-rev2`,
  `def2-msvp` or `def2-mtzvp` attaches the ECP (all three ran 48 electrons
  into a 19-valence-electron silver block with no error); iodine in
  `def2-tzvp` or `cc-pvtz-pp` is refused with the elements named, because
  the bundled files are valence-only or absent there and no ECP ships.
  `is_ecp_paired_basis` remains as a legacy label used by no guard.
* **One default-auxiliary table.** `density_fitting.default_aux_basis_for`
  (molecular) and `aux_basis.default_aux_for` (periodic) both read the
  registry. The old periodic table disagreed with the molecular one on
  `def2-qzvp` (`def2-qzvpp-jk`, now `def2-qzvp-jk`) and `def2-sv(p)`
  (`def2-sv(p)-jkfit`, now `def2-svp-jk`); the periodic stand-ins for pob
  and Pople bases are kept behind `allow_standin=True`, molecular fits
  still refuse them.
* **ECP data shipped.** `def2-msvp.ecp` moved out of
  `ecp_library/custom/`, a directory nothing read, into
  `basis_library/custom/` where the setup script copies it (the same move
  keeps `vdzp.ecp` from being deleted on the next library regeneration);
  `def2-mtzvp.ecp` / `def2-mtzvpp.ecp` carry the def2-ECP the 3c bases
  pair with beyond Kr; `pob-tzvp-rev2.ecp` is emitted from the CRYSTAL
  records by the new `basis_crystal.emit_ecp_sidecar` and round-trips to
  the arrays the periodic bridge feeds libecpint (46 elements checked);
  the 46 heavy pob-TZVP-rev2 CRYSTAL records now ship under
  `basis_library/sources/`, so periodic ECP resolution no longer fetches
  from the Bredow site at runtime.
* **`run_periodic_job` refuses an ECP-bearing cell on every route.**
  Measured on Ag fcc / pob-TZVP-rev2 / RKS / 2x2x2: the runner resolved
  the four ECP blocks, set them on the options, and dispatched to
  `run_krks_periodic_gdf`, which reads no ECP field and partitions
  `system.n_electrons()` (188) with bare Z = 47 nuclei. The native direct
  drivers apply periodic ECPs but are not dispatched by the runner. The
  v0.14.0 note "sets them on the C++ options struct, no user wiring
  needed" and the user-guide example were describing the dropped case.
* **QVF sidecars carry every ECP.** The importer knew only `-g potential`
  labels, so every lmax=5 block was dropped (dhf-TZVP: 18 of 35 ECPs, no
  element linked), and the converter never read the `.ecp` sidecar at all.
  Both fixed; 17 QVF records regenerated; `tests/test_basis_qvf_parity.py`
  pins parity for the whole library.
* Docs: `docs/user_guide/ecp.md` (auto-attach, the corrected "when you need
  it" list, XML libraries as explicit-only, honest periodic status),
  `basis_sets.md`, `features.md`, `license.md`, library READMEs.


### Fixed: `write_density=True` no longer discards a completed periodic calculation (#679, 2026-09-05)

`run_periodic_job(..., write_density=True)` raised `IncompleteOutputError`
*after* the SCF had converged and every other sibling file had been written:
the density writer dropped the grid as an OPTIONAL artefact with a warning
while the output plan had declared `{stem}.xsf` GUARANTEED. Measured on the
default GDF route and on the `real-gamma`, `neutral-bloch` and `four-center`
AICCM variants. Four distinct mechanisms sat behind the one symptom; all four
are runner-side, and none changes a converged energy.

* **Spin-channel presence is tested by content, not by attribute.**
  `_exact_periodic_density_grid_artifact` decided "open shell" from
  `hasattr(result, "density_alpha")`. `CCMRealGammaResult` and
  `CCMFourCentreResult` are closed-shell dataclasses that *declare* both spin
  fields as `None`, so both took the open-shell branch, built
  `densities = [None, None]`, and discarded the `LatticeMatrixSet` in
  `result.density`. Now a channel counts as present only when it is not
  `None`.
* **A Gamma-only Bloch mesh carries its density in a one-entry per-k
  container.** At `kpoints=(1, 1, 1)` the multi-k GDF driver returns a list
  holding one block at exactly k = 0, where the Bloch matrix *is* the
  real-space unit-cell matrix; the Gamma path demanded a rank-2 array. The
  same cell therefore wrote its density with `kpoints=None` and was discarded
  with `kpoints=(1, 1, 1)`. `_single_gamma_block_for_periodic_artifact` admits
  that one block, and only when the container holds exactly one k-point at
  exactly k = 0, so a true multi-k stack keeps its refusal.
* **A real-space supercell-Gamma result has no Bloch mesh.** The BvK triple
  (`kpoints_cart`, `kpoint_weights`, `bvk_mesh`) is metadata about a k-mesh;
  the repetition count the runner resolves from `aiccm_lattice_extension`
  describes a supercell. Counting that lone value made the triple look
  half-supplied and refused the artefact. It is now treated as absent when the
  result carries no k-point metadata at all.
* **The per-k routes refuse up front at true multi-k.** `gdf`, `rijcosx` and
  `gpw` return per-k Bloch blocks on a true multi-k mesh and the artifact path
  refuses -- by design -- to invent a real-space lattice density from them.
  Each previously ran its SCF to convergence and *then* raised. They now fail
  in the first second through `_resolve_sidecar_request`, the discipline
  `write_molden_file` already follows; `write_density` accepts `None` (auto)
  alongside `True` / `False`, and its default stays `False`. The routes that
  do return a lattice density -- `bipole` and every `method="aiccm"` variant
  -- are not gated at any mesh.

Measured after the fix on H2/STO-3G in a 6-bohr cube: `gdf` at
`kpoints=(1,1,1)`, `gdf` with `kpoints=None`, `real-gamma`, `neutral-bloch`,
`chi` and `bipole` all write their `.xsf`; `gdf`, `rijcosx` and `gpw` at
`kpoints=(2,2,2)` refuse in 0.0 s. Pre-fix baselines for the three gated
routes were `IncompleteOutputError` after a completed SCF, so no working
capability is withdrawn.

One class remains, and it is not decidable before the SCF: the density
artefact is certified against the electron count, and whether a *given*
converged density will certify is unknown at job start. On the four-centre arm
`sum_g D(g):S(g)` is 2.2292 at a 6-bohr box, 2.0186 at 8, 2.0010 at 10, and
certified at 12 and 16, against 2 electrons -- the route is density-capable,
that run was not. An uncertifiable density is still correctly refused, but the
run is still discarded at finalization because the plan guarantees the file.
The guarantee level is IO-chat territory (CLAUDE.md § 16) and is filed as an
ask in `handovers/HANDOVER_OUTPUT_LOGGER.md`; `plan.py` is untouched.

Regression: `tests/test_periodic_density_artifact_capability.py` (8 nodes,
registered in `scripts/test_gate/update_suite_manifest.py` and regenerated).

### Experimental: bounded native orbital-subspace symmetry checks

A one-Seitz C++ validator now consumes the immutable full-k mean-field
state and retains separate full sewing matrices for the exact frozen-core,
correlated-occupied and virtual masks. Metric, reconstruction, cross-mask,
Fock-stationarity and energy-intertwining checks do not repair the map or
replace genuine degenerate mixing by phase matching. Rank-reduced states
cannot request full-AO scope. The retained state, subspace matrices,
transport panels and workspace are explicitly inventoried before allocation.
Tiny tests include nonsymmorphic/time-reversal composition, degenerate
core leakage with unchanged occupied density, independent orbital gauges,
rank-reduced scope, and actual two-/three-k finite-Gaussian HF states.
This is a numerical state diagnostic, not authentication of a native
BIPOLE Hamiltonian or authorization for symmetry-reduced CCSD/triples.
All existing correlation admission gates remain unchanged.

### Experimental: native Seitz AO Bloch coefficient transport

A bounded C++ kernel now transports one k-point coefficient panel under a
full Seitz operation, retaining fractional translations, integer atom-image
phases and optional scalar time reversal. Exact whole-mesh admission covers
Gamma-centered and compatible shifted grids. Pure and Cartesian shell
rotations through l=6 use their native ordering and normalization; no dense
AO rotation or all-k coefficient store is allocated. Tests cover all 48
primitive-diamond operations, independent Gaussian-value and real-torus
Fourier oracles, exact resource caps, and MgO/diamond pob-TZVP-rev2 panels
on an 8x8x8 mesh without SCF. Physical frozen/active/virtual orbital sewing,
an authenticated native BIPOLE correlation source, and symmetry-reduced
CCSD/triples execution remain incomplete. Existing correlation admission
gates are unchanged; this is not a target-system energy qualification.

### Experimental: direct-Gram periodic pair MP2 and mixed-pair interactions

A bounded native driver now connects actual finite-Gaussian HF, localization
and original pair domains to Gram-generated PNOs and coupled MP2 without a
common factor-row provider or detached integral-array bridge. Native mixed
factor panels and all-q Coulomb/exchange/overlap blocks consume these pair
frames with their original PAO rotations and authenticated geometries.
Whole-owner resource admission, callback source checks, frozen core, positive
and empty PNO ranks, and the MP2-to-interaction connection have tiny multi-k
regression coverage. The integrated CCSD(T) reference still requires common
factor rows; production local contractions, symmetry reduction and the
MgO/diamond/corundum target calculations remain incomplete.
### Fixed: the BIPOLE terminal check judges the operator the SCF converged on, instead of revoking a converged loop (#116, 2026-09-05)

All four BIPOLE drivers (`run_pbc_bipole_{rhf,uhf,rks,uks}`) converge their
