SCF on the incremental `J_SR`/`K_SR` chain (`IncrementalJK`, increments from
`dD` under density-envelope screening) and then re-evaluate the committed
density with one non-incremental build. The accumulated screening error of
the chain makes the two energies differ by a small, structural amount --
2.1e-8 Ha on LiH/STO-3G (2,2,2) at a 25-bohr cutoff (rp218pr01vq-site_i-a02,
`conv_tol_energy = 1e-8`) -- and the post-loop refresh compared that
rebuild's energy against the loop's last row and flipped `converged` to
False after all the work was done: 22 h of correct computation on that LiH
row, 750 core-hours on an Al2O3 corundum (2,2,2) PBE cell (the gradient
leg there) and 2 of 33 rows of the rp218 wave returned no energy at all.
The #514 in-loop confirmation already judged the exact operator's commutator
norm before exiting, but not its energy, so the energy revocation stood.

Reproduced on the laptop: asymmetric BeH2/STO-3G in a 9-bohr box at (2,1,1)
and cutoff 13 with every incremental `dD` scaled by `1 + 1e-6` converges at
iteration 7 and the exact rebuild sits +2.62e-8 Ha above it -> `converged =
False`; at `1 + 1e-5` the gap is 2.6e-7 Ha with the exact commutator norm
still inside `conv_tol_grad` (the LiH signature).

* `pbc_bipole_common.bipole_terminal_check` is the ONE criterion both call
  sites apply: the in-loop confirmation now evaluates the exact rebuild's
  energy (free energy on the smearing drivers, assembled exactly as the
  post-loop finalisation assembles the returned value: `T`, `V_ne`,
  `1/2 D.F2e + e_2e_k_correction`, `e_xc`, `E_nn`, `+U`, legacy
  spheropole, `-T S`) and commutator norm at the committed density against
  `conv_tol_energy` / `conv_tol_grad`, and the post-loop refresh re-applies
  the same test to the same rebuild, so a loop can no longer exit on a
  state the terminal check refuses. No tolerance is widened.
* When the confirmation fails, the incremental chain is re-synced to that
  exact build (`IncrementalJK.seed`, reached through the builders'
  `reseed_incremental=True`, the same closure the accumulator's own full
  build calls) and the loop continues on the operator it is judged by:
  the next iteration is a `dD = 0` build that exposes the drift as the
  loop's own `dE`, and the one after confirms. On the BeH2 probe both
  drifted runs now converge in 9 iterations at the undrifted energy to
  1e-12 Ha (terminal delta 1e-12); undrifted runs are bit-identical (7
  iterations, no extra build).
* Both values are logged and emitted as `scf_terminal_check` structured
  events (`phase`, `energy_loop`, `energy_exact`, `delta_e`,
  `grad_norm_loop`, `grad_norm_exact`, tolerances, `passed`) whether the
  check passes or not, and `run_periodic_job`'s non-convergence
  `RuntimeError` names the terminal `|dE|` and `||[F,DS]||` against the
  tolerances; until now the number that failed was printed nowhere.
* Tests (`tests/test_bipole_fock_ewald_exchange.py`): `IncrementalJK.seed`
  re-syncs the chain (next build sees `dD = 0`, copies); the injected-drift
  BeH2 run converges on the exact operator with the refused-then-confirmed
  event sequence and the undrifted energy; an undrifted run emits exactly
  one passed in-loop check and one passed post-loop check.
  `tests/test_periodic_runner_bipole_callsites.py`: the refusal message
  carries the terminal numbers. `docs/user_guide/bipole.md` states the
  contract.

### Added: COSMOSPACE, the exact surface-pair activity coefficient equation (issue #558, 2026-09-02)

`vibeqc.solvation.cosmors.cosmospace` implements Klamt, Krooshof & Taylor,
*AIChE J.* 48, 2332 (2002), `10.1002/aic.690481023`.

COSMO-RS treats surface patches as thermodynamically *independent*. COSMOSPACE
drops that approximation and solves the pairwise-interacting-segment ensemble
exactly, so its segment activity coefficients satisfy Gibbs-Duhem by
construction. Implemented: the COSMOSPACE equation (eq. 16), the exchange
factor (eq. 17), the residual activity coefficient (eq. 13), the closed-form
binary solution (eq. 19) and the Staverman-Guggenheim combinatorial term.

Both models are exposed side by side rather than one replacing the other: the
shipped parameterization was fitted with the independent-patch sigma potential,
so they are not interchangeable at fixed parameters.

Two things worth recording. First, the self-energy subtraction in eq. 17 is the
whole physical content: for the pure misfit energy it collapses to
`-(a_eff·alpha'/2)(sigma_mu - sigma_nu)^2`, which depends on how *unlike* two
segments are rather than on their sum, and is never positive. That identity is
pinned in the tests, because getting the subtraction wrong turns the difference
back into a sum and still converges.

Second, eq. 19 as printed is numerically unusable at low segment fraction: it
subtracts a square root from 1 and divides by `2·omega·Theta_A^2`, and the
subtraction cancels catastrophically long before the ratio does, returning NaN
at `Theta_A = 1e-9`. Since infinite dilution is the regime activity coefficients
matter most in, it is rearranged into the algebraically identical
`gamma_A^2 = 2(1 + 2·Theta_B·omega/(1+root))/(1+root)`, which cancels `Theta_A`
analytically instead of numerically, needs no division by `omega`, and
reproduces both published limits exactly. The iterative solver and the closed
form now agree to about 14 digits from `Theta_A = 1e-15` to 1.


Nothing released yet. Entries land here as they are merged and are
promoted into a dated version section at the next tag.

### Fixed: the BIPOLE corrected exchange split bounds its default alpha by the exchange cutoff and resolves its reciprocal envelope for it (#674, 2026-09-05)

The four BIPOLE drivers (`run_pbc_bipole_{rhf,uhf,rks,uks}`) defaulted the
Ewald splitting `alpha` to CRYSTAL's `2.8 / V^(1/3)` for every gauge, while
the erfc-screened `K_SR` arm of the corrected exchange split (the default
gauge of every 3D BIPOLE run with exact exchange) is summed over the Fock
output cells, `|g| <= lattice_opts.cutoff_bohr`, an AO-overlap length that
does not grow with the cell. Past `V^(1/3) = 2.8 R_cut / sqrt(-ln tol)`
(7.8 bohr at a 12-bohr cutoff) `erfc(alpha R)/R` has not decayed at the
cutoff and the image exchange beyond it, `-(N_e/2) sum_{|g|>R_cut}
erfc(alpha g)/g` for one doubly occupied orbital, was silently dropped.
The reciprocal envelope of `J_LR` / `K_LR` was CRYSTAL's volume-only
`K_max`, calibrated to CRYSTAL's alpha, so a larger explicit `ewald_omega`
truncated `exp(-K^2 / 4 alpha^2)` instead: on the fixture below
`ewald_omega=0.358` read -1.1032469816 Ha. The gradient code carried the
same volume-only `K_max` at fifteen sites. The J arm is not exposed (its
ket-image ball is padded from alpha) and the one-electron Ewald terms size
their own ball (#478).

Measured on H2/STO-3G in a 30-bohr box at (1,1,1) with the 12-bohr lattice
cutoff of `tests/test_periodic_rohf_multi_k_ewald.py` (laptop, core rebuilt
at b564fa19e), corrected RHF: CRYSTAL's `alpha = 0.0933` gave -1.1170669756
Ha, 1.9e-5 Ha short of the EWALD_3D split-invariant -1.1170858285 Ha; the
one-electron H atom (corrected UHF) -0.4667239569 against -0.4667330007,
9.0e-6 Ha short. With the fix the default (bounded to 0.3577), an explicit
0.2 and an explicit 0.5 give -1.1170858289, -1.1170858286 and -1.1170858294
Ha, the default at cutoff 30 (bounded to 0.1431) -1.1170858286, and the H
atom -0.4667330009: split-invariant to 1e-9 Ha and within 1e-9 Ha of the
EWALD_3D totals. An explicit `ewald_omega = 0.0933` still reproduces the
pre-fix -1.1170669756.

* `pbc_bipole_common.resolve_bipole_ewald_alpha` is the one default-alpha
  rule of the four drivers: an explicit `ewald_omega` wins; otherwise
  CRYSTAL's value, bounded below by `sqrt(-ln tol) / cutoff_bohr` through
  the #651 `default_ewald_alpha` with `tol = ewald_precision` (1e-8, the
  tolerance BIPOLE already uses for its erfc image balls) whenever the run
  carries an erfc exchange arm (corrected split with a nonzero full-range
  exact-exchange coefficient). The legacy CRYSTAL-gauge scaffold
  (`use_exchange_ewald_split=False`) and pure functionals keep CRYSTAL's
  alpha: they have no erfc exchange arm, and the scaffold exists for
  term-by-term CRYSTAL parity. The driver logs the bound when it applies.
* `bipole_ext_el_pole.bipole_ewald_reciprocal_cutoff(V, alpha)` scales
  CRYSTAL's volume-only envelope by `max(1, alpha / alpha_CRYSTAL)`, so
  `K_max / alpha` keeps CRYSTAL's 8.51 (the reciprocal Gaussian resolved to
  1.4e-8) for every alpha at or above CRYSTAL's and a run whose alpha is
  CRYSTAL's keeps its reciprocal sum bit for bit. The drivers and all
  fifteen `bipole_gradient.py` sites (`_matching_ewald_options`,
  `_v_ne_ewald_gradient`, the Gamma and multi-k `J_LR` / `K_LR` gradients,
  the `B0` builders, the KS and open-shell orbital-relaxation terms, the
  Gamma Fock reconstruction and both Bloch-CPHF right-hand sides) derive
  `K_max` from it, so the analytic gradient differentiates the reciprocal
  sum the energy evaluated. `bipole_fock_ewald.build_ewald_j_split_fock_gamma`
  bounds its default omega by its own unpadded cutoff the same way.
* Literature: Ewald's potential is invariant to the screening parameter
  only when both lattice series are summed to convergence, and CRYSTAL's
  `2.8 / V^(1/3)` is a cost optimum for fully summed series, not an accuracy
  requirement (Saunders, Freyria-Fava, Dovesi and Roetti, Mol. Phys. 77,
  629 (1992), Property 11 and Eq. (55), routed as `saunders_bipole_1992`;
  Ewald, Ann. Phys. 369, 253 (1921), now also routed on `bipole` as
  `ewald_lattice_sum_1921`).
* Tests: `tests/test_pbc_bipole_ewald_split_integration.py` pins the
  envelope helper (CRYSTAL's value at and below CRYSTAL's alpha, constant
  `K_max / alpha` above it), the alpha rule (bounded only on the erfc
  exchange arm, explicit omega wins, cells up to 7.8 bohr keep CRYSTAL's
  value), the split invariance of the 30-bohr H2 total across the default,
  0.2 and 0.5 (2e-8 Ha of the EWALD_3D value), the H-atom total, that the
  explicit CRYSTAL alpha stays > 1e-5 Ha short, and that the legacy gauge
  keeps CRYSTAL's alpha on the same box. The two ROHF-vs-BIPOLE cross-route
  windows in `tests/test_periodic_rohf_multi_k_ewald.py` tighten from 5e-5
  / 1e-5 to 1e-7. `tests/test_bipole_gradient.py`: the 9-bohr BeH2 (2,1,1)
  corrected-gauge FD parity now asserts the bounded alpha (0.330 over
  CRYSTAL's 0.311), and a new Gamma test differences the driver energy of
  H2 in a 12-bohr box at a 6-bohr cutoff (alpha 0.715 over CRYSTAL's 0.233)
  against the analytic gradient.
* Moved snapshots (all toward their cross-code references, none on a
  compact cell): the H2/STO-3G/12-bohr Gamma corrected-gauge pin at cutoff
  4 and `ewald_precision=1e-6` (alpha 0.233 -> 0.929) goes
  -1.122386713788 -> -1.122526209887 Ha in
  `test_pbc_bipole_ewald_split_integration.py`,
  `test_bipole_fock_ewald_exchange.py` and `test_pbc_gdf_compcell.py`,
  +0.1973 -> +0.0578 mHa from PySCF GDF; the H2O/PBE0/6-31G 18-bohr box at
  cutoff 15 (alpha 0.156 -> 0.286) goes -76.30237318987 -> -76.30241760934
  Ha, +6.09e-5 -> +1.65e-5 Ha from PySCF and split-invariant against
  `ewald_omega=0.5`; the 6-bohr H2 (2,1,1) drift guard of
  `test_bipole_per_k_band_accessor.py` (alpha 0.467 -> 0.505, SR ball pinned
  at 12 bohr by the fixture) moves -2.4e-6 Ha and its frontier pins by up to
  6e-6 Ha. Legacy-gauge siblings do not move.
* `tests/test_periodic_rohf_bipole_dispatch.py` still carried the
  pre-#651 LiH+ (3,1,1) anchor (-7.5192630685); its copy now follows the
  #651 value -7.5192632201. The six ROHF/GDF reds in the same file (the
  public route refusing its default SAD guess since bbe7b9001) predate this
  change and are filed as #681.
* `docs/user_guide/ewald.md` states the BIPOLE contract next to the
  EWALD_3D one.

Follow-up (2026-09-06): one pin outside the lanes run for this fix had moved
with it and was red on `main`:
`tests/test_bz_integration_gilat_scf.py::test_bipole_open_shell_gilat_matches_gapped_aufbau_fixed_point[UHF]`
(H atom, 30-bohr box, 12-bohr cutoff, the exact system of the H-atom split

### Experimental: χ occupied-space symmetry from localized orbitals (#683)

D128 projects a compact torus AO operation into supplied localized occupied
coefficients using their actual overlap. It validates metric covariance,
orthonormality, occupied closure and unitarity, preserving phases and general
orbital mixing. Immutable results bind the input coefficient/overlap payload
and AO action; a conservative explicit-array memory check precedes copies.
Tests include a physical χ-HF/localization chain, Gaussian p rotations and
adversarial input/gauge controls. This one-operation diagnostic does not yet
certify a complete group, reduce energy work, or enable analytic gradients.
### Fixed: periodic GFN2 gradients and stress differentiate their energy (issue #338, 2026-09-05)

The native Gamma-point GFN2-xTB gradient omitted periodic coordination,
distance-polynomial, AES moment-integral, and reduced-state response chains,
and counted nonzero-image repulsion with the wrong atomic factor. Its stress
also used the wrong virial sign/index order and omitted per-image H0, overlap,
AES, coordination, and response strain terms. Charge-only SCC convergence
could also return before the AES moments had ever been formed. The SCF now
converges its complete charge/moment state, and the derivative path consumes
the result's lattice cutoff, periodic coordination convention, occupations,
and exact pair-selected image blocks. Gapped finite-difference regressions
cover every atomic component and all nine stress components. The route remains
experimental pending broader periodic and external `xtb` parity.

### Fixed: the DLPNO-CCSD extended residual domain is contracted once per domain, in the compiled kernel (#689, 2026-09-05)

The `residual_domain="extended"` default that #98 made the production
recipe was filed as 300-400x slower than the legacy pair recipe: 167-451 s
per preset on the S22-01 ammonia dimer (8 atoms, cc-pVDZ / cc-pVDZ-RI)
against 0.5-1.1 s, within a small factor of the 658 s untruncated
reference, as measured by the #98 verifier. This chat's own NormalPNO
profile on a loaded 18-core box gave 406.5 s for the extended default and
2.5 s for the pair recipe under identical conditions, and put 404 of the
406 s in `cs_ccsd_residual`: the NumPy transcription of the whole
closed-shell CCSD residual over the pair's occupied coupling set and
extended basis was evaluated once per pair per iteration (336 calls of
1.2 s), and only the target pair's block was kept from each. Domain
construction, PNO construction and DF transformation were below 2 s
together. The domain itself is the paper's: the extended domain is the
union of the coupled orbitals' atom domains (Riplinger and Neese, *J. Chem.
Phys.* **138**, 034106 (2013), section II B 1). On the 4-atom monomer every
orbital domain at `tcut_mkn=1e-3` is the whole molecule, so `24.0` is the
paper's domain, not an over-inclusive one. On the dimer the orbital domains
are 3-5 of the 8 atoms, and the code's union over the whole 12-bohr
coupling set spans all 8 atoms (48 virtuals) where the paper's pair-list
condition would give about 44 of 58 AOs; that superset is deliberate (it is
what makes the contraction exact, below) and is a factor of about 3 in the
ladder, not the factor 74 measured. The cost was the per-pair redundancy
and the NumPy kernel, not the domain size.

* The extended basis, its DF factors and Fock blocks depend only on the
  pair's occupied coupling set and extended atom set, so pairs sharing both
  now share one group: the residual is contracted once per group per
  iteration and every member pair reads its own block, projected into its
  own PNO space. The basis, its `(ab|cd)` factor and virtual Fock block
  depend on the atom set alone and are shared by every group with that
  domain. A compact molecule has one group. The contraction runs in
  the compiled `vibeqc::dlpno_pair_residual` kernel (its DF B-tensors are
  basis-agnostic, and it tiles the `(ae|bf)` ladder above the 2 GiB
  in-core budget), with `dlpno_target_pair_residual` for single-member
  groups and the NumPy transcription retained behind `use_cpp_kernel=False`.
  `LocalCCSDResult.n_residual_domains` reports the group count, and the
  `dlpno_ccsd_done` event carries it with `avg_residual_domain`.
* Measured at NormalPNO, OMP 4, same reference and same energy to the last
  printed digit: S22-01 dimer 406.5 s to 5.5 s (14 contractions instead of
  336), monomer 5.2 s to 0.4 s; the size ladder in the #689 record covers
  the water, methane and ammonia dimers and ethane before and after, and the
  larger formic-acid, formamide, ethene and n-alkane cases after only: the
  pre-fix code was not run on those, since by scaling from the dimer profile
  its dense per-pair blocks would need tens of GB and its per-pair residuals
  hours per preset on the formic-acid dimer alone.
* Why this is exact rather than a further approximation, now stated in the
  solver: every coupled pair's PNO space is spanned by the PAOs of its own
  atom domain, that domain lies inside the extended domain by construction
  (the union is taken over the whole coupling set, which is why vibe-qc's
  extended domain is larger than the paper's pair-list condition), and every
  internal virtual index of the CCSD residual is carried by an amplitude, so
  contracting in the extended basis reproduces the full-space result for the
  same coupling set to `lindep` precision (each domain's PAO metric is
  orthonormalised independently). Pinned on two waters 10 A apart, where
  the extended domain is one water's 19 of 38 virtuals and two groups form
  (extended and full agree to 1e-8 Ha), and on three waters 6 A apart, where
  pair domains are proper subsets of their extended domains and those of
  the whole molecule.
* Regressions (`tests/test_dlpno_ccsd_solver.py::TestExtendedDomainGrouping`):
  one contraction per iteration on H2O/def2-SVP, compiled/NumPy parity to
  1e-10 Ha in extended mode, the subset-domain exactness above, and the
  S22-01 monomer Loose/Normal/Tight ladder pinned to #98's verified errors
  (7.3716e-4, 6.0115e-4, 2.5580e-5 Ha, monotone); the dimer
  interaction-energy ladder (0.342, 0.311, 0.143 mHa) is a slow test.
* `vibeqc.memory` prices the closed-shell extended route as one streamed
  group workspace at `n_ext = n_vir` plus its DF factors instead of
  multiplying a pair-PNO workspace by the strong-pair count, and says so in
  the category detail; the open-shell local solver is untouched and keeps
  its per-pair inventory.
  `docs/user_guide/dlpno_mp2.md` and `docs/tutorial/dlpno_local_correlation.md`
  no longer say the extended contraction runs in NumPy.

### Fixed: the SECCM equidistant-image window is 1e-5 bohr in every topology length unit (#669, 2026-09-04)

`build_seccm_topology(..., length_unit="angstrom")` accepted angstrom
coordinates but `_distance_tolerance` applied MSINDO's `neighbors.f` window,
`1.0e-5` bohr, as a raw number in the caller's unit, so an angstrom-tagged
topology judged "equidistant" in a window 1.89x wider (1e-5 Å = 1.89e-5 bohr)
than the bohr routes. Identical physical coordinates then classified
differently: two atoms in a 6-bohr cube whose second atom's two nearest
images differ in distance by 1.1e-5 or 1.8e-5 bohr (the atom 0.55e-5 or
0.9e-5 bohr past the face centre) tie in angstrom and split in bohr, and the
#592 MgO 2x2x2 cell under a 1e-6 coordinate-only dilation (coordinates moved
by up to 1.194e-5 bohr = 6.32e-6 Å) gave 408 records in bohr against 512 in
angstrom (the issue measured 408 / 510), 376 against 480 at 1.2e-6. Every
built-in route builds in bohr (`msindo_ccm.py` converts first) and the SECCM
adapters consume bohr-tagged topologies, so no built-in route's energy moves;
a user-built angstrom-tagged topology handed to `run_neb`'s DFTB0-SECCM route
now rebuilds its displacements at the physical window, and the public
unit-tagged API and its documentation are corrected.

* `topology.py`: `_bohr_per_length_unit(length_unit)` (1.0 for `None` /
  `"bohr"`, `ANGSTROM_TO_BOHR` for `"angstrom"`, the constant the SECCM
  adapters already use) is threaded from `build_seccm_topology` and from
  `rebuild_displacements` into `_enumerate_candidate_classifications` and
  `_distance_tolerance`, which now returns
  `max(1.0e-5 / unit_scale, 256 eps scale)`. The roundoff guard stays in
  caller units (it bounds the representation error of the compared numbers,
  ~5.7e-14 of their scale, and cannot reach the window in either unit). The
  native builder's bohr-only constant is untouched.
* Tests (`tests/test_seccm_topology.py`): the two-atom gap cell at 0.9e-5,
  1.1e-5, 1.8e-5 and 2.0e-5 bohr classifies identically in both units with the
  tie present only below the window; the untagged build keeps the bohr
  convention; the frozen-topology rebuild admits no new image when a 2.0e-5
  bohr reference gap closes to 1.5e-5 bohr in either unit (pre-fix the
  angstrom topology failed closed) and still fails closed in both units when
  it closes to 0.9e-5 bohr; the dilated MgO cell agrees in both units at
  dilations 5e-7, 1e-6 and 1.2e-6; the undilated cell keeps the #592
  record set (512 records, weights 1/6, 1/4, 1/2, 1). With the pre-fix
  window simulated (`_bohr_per_length_unit` forced to 1.0) the 1.1e-5 and
  1.8e-5 gap rows, the 1.5e-5 rebuild row and the 1e-6 / 1.2e-6 dilation
  rows fail and the six controls pass.
* `docs/user_guide/cyclic_cluster_model.md` states that the window is a
  physical length and what an angstrom-tagged topology converts it to.

### Experimental: native multi-k periodic correlation reference

Added an internal C++ finite-Gaussian RHF-to-selected-domain CCSD and
occupied-coupled triples reference, with explicit frozen-core masks,
resource admission and progress callbacks. Direct Gram-based pair-PNO
components are independently tested without a pre-existing common factor
store; the integrated CCSD(T) reference still requires that store.

Validated on tiny finite Hamiltonians: 4,364 tests passed with two expected
skips across the correlation and affected safety checks. This is not public
production DLPNO-CCSD(T): scalable local contractions, space-group reduction,
and the MgO/diamond/corundum targets remain incomplete.

### Documentation: correct the SKALA release chronology (#673)

Restored the SKALA entry under v0.15.158 to the text shipped in that tag.
The later GPW/GAPW and CCM expansion is now recorded under v0.15.160,
and the SKALA guide distinguishes that release from the subsequent
four-center grid/domain and dry-run hardening in #670. This correction
changes no calculation or runtime capability.

### Fixed: BIPOLE geomopt admitted the low-dimensional diagnostic energy (issue #542, 2026-09-04)

`PeriodicSCFProvider` now mirrors the public periodic-job gate and refuses
`dim=1`/`dim=2` before recording provider state or dispatching an SCF. The
low-level BIPOLE drivers retain their `DIRECT_TRUNCATED` diagnostic path, but
its compact-cell energy is cutoff-dependent and is not a low-dimensional
Coulomb optimisation objective. Raising the cutoff is therefore not offered
as a remedy.

The periodic geomopt regression carrier is now a physical 3-D H₂ cell. The
IID 536 trial-refusal recovery contract remains covered by a deterministic 3-D
harmonic surface: a refused full BFGS step backtracks to a genuine lower-energy
half-step, while an initial-geometry refusal still propagates.

### Fixed: the EWALD_3D default splitting alpha is bounded below by the real-space image cutoff (#651, 2026-09-04)

The EWALD_3D Gamma and multi-k SCF drivers (RHF/RKS/UHF/UKS/ROHF/ROKS)
defaulted the Ewald splitting `omega` to CRYSTAL's `2.8 / V^(1/3)` while
the erfc-screened real-space arm of their corrected exchange split (the
`K_SR` of `exchange_exxdiv='ewald'`, the default on every mesh other than a
lone Gamma point and opt-in there) stays cut at the fixed
`LatticeSumOptions.cutoff_bohr = 15`. The two are one truncation contract:
past an 8-bohr cube `erfc(omega r)/r` has not decayed by the cutoff and the
truncated exchange sum is silently short, and the error grows with the cell.
The Hartree `J` (analytic-FT, alpha-invariant) and `V_ne` / `E_nn` (own
alpha from `nuclear_cutoff_bohr`) are not exposed.

Measured on H2/STO-3G in a 16-bohr cube at a (2,1,1) mesh: `omega = 0.175`
(the CRYSTAL value there) at 15 bohr gives -1.1180942761 Ha against
-1.1181372061 Ha at 30 bohr, 4.29e-5 Ha short; `omega = 0.35` at the same
15 bohr gives -1.1181371957 Ha, within 1.05e-8 Ha. A lone Gamma point on
its default molecular-limit exchange gauge is alpha-invariant and does not
move; with `exchange_exxdiv='ewald'` it does: the (2,2,2) H2 supercell of
`tests/test_ccm_periodic_3d.py` at Gamma was 6.1e-5 Ha/cell short at 0.175
(measured by the triage lane: -1.1190742250 vs -1.1191353264 Ha/cell at 0.35;
the bounded default reproduces the latter). The 8-bohr unit cell of that
test already defaulted to 0.350 and does not move.

* `pbc_bipole_common.ewald_alpha_lower_bound(R_cut, tol) = sqrt(-ln tol)/R_cut`
  is the exact inverse of the existing `ewald_real_cutoff_for_alpha`
  (BIPOLE widens its nuclear image ball from alpha; these routes bound alpha
  from the cutoff instead, because widening `cutoff_bohr` would also widen
  every two-electron image sum). `default_ewald_alpha(V, real_cutoff_bohr,
  tolerance)` returns CRYSTAL's value wherever it already satisfies the bound
  and the bound otherwise; the eleven EWALD_3D default-omega sites go through
  it with `tolerance = opts.ewald_tolerance` (1e-12). Explicit `omega` /
  `opts.ewald_omega` are untouched. Raising alpha moves work into the
  reciprocal sums, so every consumer must size its reciprocal envelope from
  the alpha in use (`auto_recip_cutoff`, `corrected_ewald_reciprocal_cutoff`,
  the analytic-FT J grid).
* The ROHF and ROKS multi-k drivers did not: their long-range exchange arm
  was cut at CRYSTAL's volume-only `crystal_ewald_reciprocal_cutoff(V)`,
  calibrated to CRYSTAL's alpha, so the bounded alpha truncated
  `exp(-K^2 / 4 omega^2)` there. H2/STO-3G in a 30-bohr box at (1,1,1) with
  the 12-bohr lattice cutoff of `tests/test_periodic_rohf_multi_k_ewald.py`
  read -1.0789613510 Ha at `omega = 0.438`. Both drivers now call
  `corrected_ewald_reciprocal_cutoff(V, omega)` like the other nine and the
  corrected BIPOLE path, and the total is split-invariant: `omega` 0.2 and
  0.438 at cutoff 12 and 0.438 at cutoff 30 all give -1.1170858285 Ha, while
  CRYSTAL's 0.0933 at cutoff 12 (the pre-fix default) gives -1.1170669756,
  1.9e-5 Ha short; the one-electron H atom in the same box moves 9.0e-6 Ha
  the same way. New tests pin the invariance (2e-8 Ha) and that the explicit
  CRYSTAL alpha stays > 1e-5 Ha short. The LiH+ (3,1,1) DIIS pin on a 12-bohr
  box moves from -7.5192630685 to -7.5192632201 Ha, toward the -7.51926711 Ha
  both alphas give at cutoff 30 (the 3.9e-6 residual is the one-electron
  lattice truncation of a cutoff equal to the box edge, alpha-invariant).
* Not changed here: the BIPOLE corrected exchange split
  (`use_exchange_ewald_split=True`) carries both exposures itself (unbounded
  CRYSTAL alpha, volume-only `K_max`, fifteen more volume-only `K_max` sites
  in `bipole_gradient.py`) and matches the pre-fix EWALD_3D numbers digit for
  digit on the 30-bohr fixtures; the two ROHF-vs-BIPOLE cross-route tests
  pass inside their 5e-5 / 1e-5 windows only because of that shared
  shortfall. Filed as #674 with the measured table; the fix there has to
  move energy and gradient envelopes together.
* Literature: Ewald, Ann. Phys. 369, 253 (1921), p. 273 (the split
  trades the two series against each other through this parameter; already
  routed as `ewald_lattice_sum_1921`); the pointwise `erfc(x) <= exp(-x^2)`
  bound is the Allen-Tildesley / DL_POLY / LAMMPS convention the code named
  already. The closed-form RMS truncation-error estimates (Kolafa and
  Perram 1992; Deserno and Holm 1998) are not in the paper library and are
  requested in `library/maintenance/manual-dois.txt`; the helper's docstring
  says the bound should be upgraded to them once filed.
* Regression: `tests/test_periodic_rhf_multi_k_ewald.py` pins the helper
  contract (CRYSTAL value up to the 8-bohr cube, the bound beyond, inverse
  of BIPOLE's rule), the 16-bohr (2,1,1) default within 5e-8 Ha of the
  30-bohr reference, and that the explicit unbounded alpha is still > 1e-5 Ha
  short (so the fixture keeps discriminating).
* The `omega = 0.35` workaround pins in `tests/test_ccm_periodic_3d.py` and
  `examples/regression/parity_ccm_scm_vs_pyscf.py` (the issue named the
  band-folding test file; the pins live here) are retired: both sides of
  the CCM/SCM band-folding comparison now take the bounded default, which
  is 0.3504 on the 8-bohr unit cell and the 16-bohr supercell alike.
* `docs/user_guide/ewald.md` states the contract and corrects the stale
  "omega=0.5 default for 3D Ewald" line.

### Fixed: MSINDO-NDDO Al through Cl include the source SPDD energy and analytic derivative (#660)

Closed-shell molecular MSINDO-NDDO calculations for Al through Cl previously
selected their 3s3p3d parameter records but omitted the source SPDD Fock terms.
The route therefore returned finite but incomplete energies; AlCl at 2.10 A was
high by 2.317 mHa, and the corresponding analytic gradient failed closed.

The Python and native energy paths now include both asymmetric SPDD Fock
branches, and the Python analytic derivative contracts their radial and
directional derivatives against the converged density. The AlCl source oracle
is `-16.4566380534 Ha` with axial gradients `+/-0.0317797727 Ha/bohr`; nonaxial
rotation, translation, atom-permutation, and finite-difference controls pin the
Cartesian result. Direct, unified, and native-facade routes now expose the same
closed-shell H/Li-F/Na-Cl energy scope, while open-shell NDDO and periodic/CCM
NDDO remain gated. NDDO citation output now includes Voigt's coordinate-invariant
multipole decomposition alongside Dewar and Thiel's two-centre model.

### Fixed: a current fleet driver can recover receipts owned by an older remote vq (#653)

`vq admin recover-update HOST --marker-id ID --with-driver-runtime` now gives
direct hosts an explicit compatibility path when their installed vq predates a
landed receipt-parser fix and the receipt itself blocks updating that vq. The
driver stages its exact running `vq` package under the remote user's
`~/vqscratch`, verifies the uploaded archive SHA-256, and makes the old absolute
`remote_vq` executable import that package for one ordinary recovery attempt.
The staged process verifies that it was loaded from the exact archive before it
reads or mutates recovery state. The archive is removed after a known outcome
and retained with exact reconciliation guidance if SSH loses the result. The
path requires an exact marker ID, never retries the mutating command, does not
install or replace the remote vq, and is unavailable for scheduler-driver
hosts and orphan-receipt quarantine.

### Fixed: unified correlation conventions and result-carried ECP citation provenance (issues #98, #140, #417, #448, and #657, 2026-09-04)

Molecular correlated methods no longer change their implicit scientific
convention when a user changes solver.  Every route governed by the native
MP2/UMP2 options, the CCSD-family options, or one of the six molecular DLPNO
option classes now resolves the same frozen-core default: the element table
in ORCA 6.1, Table 2.69, converted from frozen electrons to doubly occupied
spatial orbitals and summed over the molecule.  The public `frozen_core=`
selector accepts the published default, an explicit orbital count, or the
uniform `False` / `"all-electron"` escape.  The implementation is deliberately
the published **count-only** convention: ORCA's additional AO-character
repair for unusually ordered orbitals, and ECP-aware orbital selection, are
not claimed. Molecular ECP SCF results now carry the authoritative number of
replaced core electrons through RHF/UHF/RKS/UKS. Every result-taking MP2,
CC-family, and DLPNO boundary rejects a positive count because those kernels
still partition occupied orbitals from the molecule's physical electron
count; choosing all-electron correlation does not repair that mismatch.
Explicit-MO UCCSD now requires the caller to supply `ecp_total_ncore=0` for
an all-electron reference, since raw coefficient arrays cannot carry that
provenance. Positive and invalid negative counts fail closed before integral
work.

The same ECP provenance now protects molecular derivative consumers. SCF
results retain the operative XML library and exact centers or inline
primitive payload, as well as the operator flag and replaced-core count.
Public RHF/UHF/RKS/UKS gradient wrappers require that exact provenance to
match before native work; a same-count different library, center, or inline
payload therefore fails closed. XML and inline-primitive analytic gradients,
gas-phase native/Brent/geomopt/ASE optimization, dimer/IRC paths, and
gas-phase finite-difference Hessians preserve the ECP Hamiltonian across every
geometry. Analytic Hessians, top-level NEB, ROHF/ROKS and MR/post-HF
derivatives, and excited HF-CIS gradients or optimization remain unsupported.
CPCM energies support XML ECPs, but ECP+CPCM gradients, Hessians, and
optimization do not; each unsupported route fails closed rather than
differentiating a bare-Z Hamiltonian. Requested molecular and periodic QVF
orbital fallbacks, plus
periodic Molden fallback occupations, derive occupations from the effective,
not physical, electron count, including one-electron alpha occupations for
unrestricted results.

ECP citation detection now reads the provenance on the SCF result that
actually ran rather than only the caller's optional options object. The
documented no-options `run_job` form therefore emits the same Dolg-Cao and
libecpint references as an otherwise identical call with explicit options,
and the same result-carried signal reaches TREXIO's ECP refusal boundary,
closing #657 without changing its energy or population analysis.

All six molecular DLPNO option classes now resolve named `LoosePNO`,
`NormalPNO`, and `TightPNO` presets through one public policy.  `NormalPNO`
is the project default, with the published Liakos et al. Table 1 triple
`TCutPairs=1e-4`, `TCutPNO=3.33e-7`, `TCutMKN=1e-3`.  A route receives only
the coordinates its algorithm actually implements.  Missing coordinates are
reported as unsupported, and the UMP2 pair cutoff is reported as inactive
when `localise="none"`; neither case is disguised as a numerical zero.  This
is a deliberate cross-route vibe-qc policy. The same public names already
have a distinct MP2 meaning in Pinski and Neese 2019, Table I
(doi:10.1063/1.5086544): its Loose/Normal/Tight settings use `TCutPNO`
`1e-7/1e-8/1e-9` and `TCutDO` `2e-2/1e-2/5e-3`. Pinski et al.'s 2015
DLPNO-MP2 calibration (doi:10.1063/1.4926879) likewise uses an MP2-specific,
tighter PNO cutoff. The API, docs, and citation output therefore disclose the
name collision instead of attributing the cross-route choice to Pinski.

Closed-shell local CCSD also changes its operative residual contraction from
the historical pair-PNO shortcut to Riplinger and Neese's atom-based extended
PAO domain. Amplitudes remain pair-PNO objects; each target residual is
contracted in the extended domain and projected back. The legacy
`residual_domain="pair"` path remains available only as an explicit historical
control because projecting before contraction over-correlates under PNO
truncation. The selected residual domain is disclosed in `.out`, structured
completion events, and `.system`. Current extended/full contraction uses the
NumPy kernel; the compiled target-pair kernel remains specific to legacy pair
mode. This closes #98's documented ordering defect: its retained
NH3/cc-pVDZ all-electron witness now converges for all three presets and the
correlation energy tightens monotonically from LoosePNO through TightPNO.

Open-shell local UCCSD applies the same three Liakos coordinates to its
spin-orbital pair treatment. It deliberately does not claim Saitow et al.
2017 section III B's additional `TScaleTCutPairs=0.33`: that published rule
is defined for the paper's single ROHF/QRO-like spatial-orbital set, whereas
the current solver retains independent UHF alpha and beta orbital spaces.
Adding the scale requires a paired-orbital/QRO construction and its own
numerical validation; an alpha canonical index is not a physical SOMO label.
Saitow 2017 is an open-shell DLPNO-CCSD paper, not a DLPNO-UMP2 source, so
its citation has been removed from both molecular and periodic UMP2 routes;
the June 2026 entries below remain the historical record of the superseded
citation behavior.

The convention is disclosed at every high-level route in the human `.out`,
the structured-log completion event, and the `.system` `[run]` fields.  The
manifest uses the already-supported `OutputWriter.update_run_fields` hook;
no IO-owned plan, manifest, writer, or document API changed.  Threshold
provenance records the named preset, requested published triple, applied
subset, unsupported/inactive fields, and the complete set of effective
solver-specific weak-pair, singles, and TNO cutoffs. Frozen-core provenance
records the resolved spatial-orbital count and whether it came from the
published default or an explicit request.
The stored closed-shell MP2 weak-pair companions are now reported as inactive
for all three named presets: their classification boundary equals the earlier
screening boundary, so no retained pair can reach that tier. They become
applied only for an explicit custom `tcut_pairs_weak > tcut_pairs` interval.

Scientific cutoff values in the human block use Python's shortest
round-trip float representation, so the published `3.33e-7` coordinate and
arbitrary custom values are not rounded into a different recipe. DLPNO-CCSD
artifacts also identify the triples mode and the algorithm that actually ran
(`(T0)`, `(T1)`, iterative `(T1)`, exact/canonical, or a dense pilot) instead
of labelling every correction as `(T1)`. The same fields are carried in the
structured completion event and `.system` manifest.
The 2018 Guo closed-shell equation source and the dedicated 2020 open-shell
source are emitted only when the spin-orbital iterative local-basis
`triples_mode="t1-iterative"` algorithm actually runs; local `(T0)`, the
rotated-occupied `t1` compatibility route, exact/canonical, and dense-pilot
executions do not claim that algorithm. A requested correction that never
reaches a triples contraction (for example, because every CCSD pair was
screened) is reported as not executed in `.out`, JSONL, and `.system`, and
likewise does not cite either Guo source. The implementation is described as
a spin-orbital generalization of the 2018 equation, rather than attributing
its open-shell form to the closed-shell paper.
Zero-pair dense-pilot boundaries also retain the reference energy as their
total instead of returning the result dataclass's zero initializer.

#### Default and reference movements

These movements are policy changes, not retrospective corrections to archived
numbers.  A reference whose generating recipe was all-electron or used an old
threshold remains pinned under that explicit recipe.  Only assertions whose
subject is the unqualified *current default* move with the default.

| Route / reference family | Previous implicit convention | New implicit convention | Why it moves, or why it is preserved | Primary source / evidence treatment |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Native RMP2/UMP2, RI/direct/semidirect MP2, and SCS/SOS wrappers | All-electron (`n_frozen_core=0`) | ORCA 6.1 Table 2.69 count-only | Fixes the solver-dependent default from #140. External all-electron parity pins keep `n_frozen_core=0`; their numerical references do not move. | ORCA 6.1 Table 2.69 for the new default; each retained parity test names its explicit all-electron protocol. |
| Canonical CCSD/UCCSD/BCCD-family routes | Route-local chemical-core resolution | The same ORCA 6.1 Table 2.69 resolver used by MP2 and DLPNO | B-Ne molecular witnesses generally retain the same one-core-orbital count; heavier-element behaviour now follows one published table rather than a separate helper. Explicit-zero exactness references remain all-electron. | ORCA 6.1 Table 2.69; no archived energy is relabelled. |
| Closed/open-shell DLPNO-MP2 and DLPNO-CCSD/(T), including dense pilots and local solvers | All-electron (`n_frozen=0`) | ORCA 6.1 Table 2.69 count-only | Removes the CCSD-versus-DLPNO convention split reproduced in #140. Old S22 and M16 results keep `n_frozen=0` and their original thresholds, and are labelled pre-#140/#448 evidence. | ORCA 6.1 Table 2.69; `tests/test_release_paper_dlpno_m16.py` and the S22 handoff preserve the old recipe without rebaselining. |

Historical MP2 accuracy pins keep the old or Pinski-specific values explicitly. | Liakos et al. 2015, Table 1 (doi:10.1021/ct501129s); Pinski and Neese 2019, Table I (doi:10.1063/1.5086544), documents the same-name MP2 preset collision. |
| `DLPNOUMP2Options` | `(0, 1e-8, unsupported)` | `(1e-4 inactive by default, 3.33e-7, unsupported)` | NormalPNO values are stored for implemented consumers; canonical occupieds do not execute pair screening, so provenance says inactive rather than claiming it was applied. | Liakos et al. 2015, Table 1; supported-subset project policy. |
| `DLPNOCCSDPilotOptions` | `(unsupported, 1e-8, 1e-3)` | `(unsupported, 3.33e-7, 1e-3)` | Applies the published NormalPNO coordinates this pilot implements; it still has no pair-screening algorithm. | Liakos et al. 2015, Table 1; Riplinger and Neese 2013 (doi:10.1063/1.4773581) for the original NormalPNO-scale CC defaults. |

Full-domain/exactness tests retain explicit zeros; historical numerical references pin `residual_domain="pair"`, so neither is silently reinterpreted. | Liakos et al. 2015, Table 1; Riplinger and Neese 2013, section II B 1. |

The separate Saitow SOMO-pair scale is not claimed without its required single spatial-orbital construction. | Liakos et al. 2015, Table 1; Saitow et al. 2017, sections II A and III B (doi:10.1063/1.4981521), defines the intentionally deferred open-shell refinement. |

Pinning every coordinate prevents #140/#448 from silently moving their energy sequences. `megacell_run_job` still dispatches through molecular `run_job`, but its equality contract now means the same explicit historical recipe on both sides; the separate `megacell_mp2` TDL helper remains all-electron. | Existing periodic numerical ratchets remain old-convention evidence; no value or tolerance is rebaselined. |
| S22/open-shell MP2 generators and ORCA/PySCF cross-code regression runners | Explicit ORCA/PySCF all-electron protocol, but vibe-qc previously inherited that behavior from its default | Preserved all-electron and now explicit on every vibe-qc MP2/UMP2 path | Their checked-in ORCA decks already say `NoFrozenCore` / `FrozenCore FC_NONE`, and archived parity rows must remain apples-to-apples rather than silently adopting #140 on only one side. The standalone three-code ASE comparison now pins vibe-qc, PySCF, and ORCA to zero frozen orbitals as well. Future executions record the resolved zero count; the 123 archived numeric `.result` files remain byte-for-byte old evidence and are not regenerated. | Existing cross-code rows remain old-convention evidence; generators, generated inputs, and regression runners now pin `n_frozen_core=0`, `frozen_core=False`, PySCF `frozen=0`, and both ORCA `NoFrozenCore` plus block-form `%method FrozenCore FC_NONE` as applicable. |
| Calibrated molecular double hybrids and their ORCA/PySCF regression recipes | All-electron internal scaled-MP2 component | Preserved all-electron explicitly while standalone MP2 changes default | The frozen-core choice is part of each composite model definition, not inherited from generic MP2. vibe-qc sets `n_frozen_core=0`; PySCF reconstructions pass `frozen=0`; the ORCA regression runner adds `NoFrozenCore` and `%method FrozenCore FC_NONE` for B2PLYP, DSD-PBEP86, and PWPB95 alongside `AutoAux`. | Existing double-hybrid anchors do not move; exact recipe tests prevent a one-sided future default leak. |

Two boundary contracts were corrected during review. ORCA Table 2.69 assigns
Lu 46 frozen electrons (23 spatial orbitals), unlike La-Yb at 36; endpoint
tests now pin the Lu discontinuity. Native UMP2 now permits
`n_frozen_core == n_beta_total` for a high-spin reference, where the beta
channels vanish but alpha-alpha correlation remains, and its memory estimator
uses the same zero-active-beta contract. A deliberately passed bare native
CCSD options object is now treated as explicit, so its zero or positive
frozen count is not replaced by the public default.

Memory admission now materializes the correlated option policy before both
the scheduler dry-run estimate and the real preflight. Both paths therefore
size the resolved frozen occupied space, DLPNO threshold/domain choice,
auxiliary basis, triples switch, and spin route that execution consumes. A
process cap is applied to private option clones, refined after reserving the
SCF reference and safety headroom, and then re-estimated; a one-byte DLPNO
process cap is rejected before SCF rather than bypassing admission merely
because the DLPNO engine has no native workspace planner. Density-fitted
canonical MP2/UMP2 also resolves its concrete RIfit identity on that private
clone before both passes instead of using a generic `3*N` auxiliary estimate
only in scheduler dry-run. The DLPNO-MP2 estimator now prices the retained
raw/orthogonalized three-index tensors, metric and Cholesky storage,
closed-shell half transform or both open-shell spin transforms, and their
sequential phase peaks. Its `local_df=True` branch is separate: it charges
the cached raw tensor and metric for every potentially distinct fit domain,
using a fail-closed full-auxiliary dimension bound because `fit_buffer` can
extend beyond the PAO-domain fraction.

The same source-lifetime audit corrected correlated-memory underestimates that
would otherwise weaken fail-first admission after the convention change. It
now prices native and Python DF constructor/resident storage, threaded MO
transforms, analytic DF exchange-gradient occupied factors, canonical CC's
AO-to-MO return boundary and block extraction, DLPNO factor/cache lifetimes,
ROHF/FNO transforms, the FNO five-array MP2 expression peaks, and
A-CCSD(T)'s sequential DF or exact dense-integral build, Python/native bridge,
and retained reverse-AD Lambda graph. Regression formulas pin each phase
instead of comparing only a headline total.

The retained 2026-08-26 S22 rows and the release-paper M16 comparison are
therefore evidence for their **old, explicit** convention only.  They must
not be reused as post-unification NormalPNO results.  This preserves the
scientific record while making future unqualified results route-independent.

## [v0.15.160] - 2026-09-04 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Added: experimental SKALA periodic GPW/GAPW and CCM routes

SKALA's full-grid external-XC interface now reaches 3D GPW RKS at Gamma
or on a complete unreduced multi-k mesh, 3D GAPW RKS at Gamma, neutral
real-Gamma RKS/UKS, and Chi-CCM four-centre RKS/UKS. These extend the
selected periodic AO-grid routes introduced in v0.15.158. All remain
experimental, fixed-geometry, zero-temperature routes; the documented
spin, ECP, symmetry, gauge, and sampling restrictions still apply.
Fitted Chi backends and external-provider literal-WSSC or Chi hybrids
remain gated.

The literal four-centre WSSC library accepts pure external RKS/UKS,
and this release also wires the public `method="aiccm", variant="four-center"`
adapter (#659, below). The later #670 correction forwards the complete
grid/domain controls and aligns dry-run preflight with the live route;
it was not part of the v0.15.160 tag.

### Added: `variant="four-center"` runs the union-and-weight Gamma-CCM construction (AICCM front door M3a, #659, 2026-09-04)

The last AICCM formulation that still failed closed from the runner. All four
variants now dispatch: `real-gamma`, `neutral-bloch`, `four-center` and `chi`.
This is the construction the line is named after, and ruling R1 keeps it
distinct from the two neutral producers, so a difference between it and them
is a construction difference, never a convergence or representation artefact.
AICCM stays experimental.

* New adapter `python/vibeqc/periodic/ccm/four_center_runner.py`, the third
  sibling of the real-Gamma and neutral-Bloch ones. It divides the library
  result by the number of cells and folds the density to unit-cell lattice
  blocks, exactly as the real-Gamma adapter does, because the four-centre SCF
  solves one supercell-Gamma eigenproblem. `AICCM2026DEV_A` leaves
  `_UNWIRED_CCM_ROUTES`, which is now empty, and joins `_IMPLEMENTED` in the
  same commit as the arm.
* **Corrected a wrong normalisation claim in the library.** `CCMKSResult` and
  `CCMUHFResult` both documented `energy` as "total CCM energy per reference
  cell". Measured on H2/STO-3G and on a Li cell at a (2,1,1) cluster, each is
  exactly twice its (1,1,1) value: like `CCMSCFResult`, which says so
  correctly, these are TOTAL cyclic-cluster energies. Anyone who trusted the
  comment was off by a factor of the cell count, which looks like a plausible
  binding energy rather than like a bug. The docstrings now state the
  semantics and the measurement.
* The front door never executes `union12`. The library drivers still default
  to that historical weight, whose Coulomb supermatrix carries a negative
  subspace on any basis with more than one function per centre (#242), so the
  arm always passes the symmetric Born-von Karman-torus weighting and there is
  no runner keyword through which a caller could ask for the other one.
  Changing the library default is a separate change.
* Hartree-Fock runs on the scalable lattice-sum builder, which applies the
  weights inside the shell-quartet loop, because the dense builder
  materialises the full effective integral tensor and runs out of memory on
  the first real three-dimensional cell. The dense entry stays reachable as
  the library `run_ccm_rhf` and remains the validation reference. Open-shell
  HF has no scalable entry, so it uses the dense route and the `.system`
  records which builder ran.
* Fail-closed surface: dimensionality below three, DFT+U, `optimize`,
  `hessian`, an unscreened range-separated functional, and every explicit
  `damping`, `fock_mixing`, `fmixing_percent`, `density_mixer` or
  `level_shift`, which the arm forwards nowhere. No population sidecar yet:
  its population is a crystal population over folded blocks and needs a
  registration in the shared output planner, requested in
  `handovers/HANDOVER_OUTPUT_LOGGER.md`; an explicit request is refused with
  that reason rather than producing a molecular proxy.
* Records: the `.system` names the construction that was BUILT, which must
  never be the neutral producers' "representation control" string, plus the
  weighting executed, the contraction mode, the builder, and an explicit
  "not-applicable" exchange-q0 because a bare 1/r minimum image has no seam to
  declare. The citation route key `aiccm2026dev-a` fires from a job for the
  first time. The supercell orbitals stay out of every unit-cell artefact
  through the gate added for #654.
* Tests: new `tests/test_periodic_ccm_four_center_adapter.py` (T3,
  experimental), and the pins that described the route as unwired now
  describe what it does.

### Fixed: a real-Gamma CCM job no longer ships supercell orbitals in a unit-cell QVF archive (#654, AICCM front door M2, #655, 2026-09-04)

On a Born-von Karman torus larger than one cell, the QVF `wavefunction`
section of a `variant="real-gamma"` job carried the SUPERCELL MO coefficient
matrix while the archive's basis and structure described the unit cell, and
`validate_qvf` passed the result. Measured on H2/STO-3G: at a (2,1,1) torus
the metadata said 4 orbitals over a 2-function basis and the coefficient file
held 16 float64, where a reader reshaping `n_mo * n_ao` takes 8; at (2,2,1) it
said 8 orbitals over 2 functions with 64 float64. Nothing raised and nothing
warned.

* The real-Gamma adapter retains supercell-Gamma orbitals on purpose, which is
  documented, and folds its energy and density per unit cell. What was missing
  is that no artefact writer asked whether a result's orbitals span the unit
  cell before pairing them with the unit cell's basis. The runner now measures
  that (`_mo_coeffs_span_unit_cell_basis`) and omits the QVF wavefunction
  section when they do not, recording the omission and both dimensions in the
  `.out`. The Molden and population sidecars were already protected by their
  own capability gates, and an explicit `write_molden_file=True` still fails
  closed with its reason.
* No energy, density, manifest or citation value moves on any route. A
  neutral-Bloch or plain GDF job is unaffected: its Gamma block is
  unit-cell dimensioned, and its complex coefficients keep the documented
  `complex_split_last_axis` encoding.
* The writer-side half is an ask, not a change: `qvf_wf_data` in
  `python/vibeqc/output/formats/qvf.py` never compares its coefficient matrix
  against the basis payload's `n_ao`, although the natural-orbital and
  localized-orbital emitters beside it both do and return `None` so the caller
  omits the section. That file is IO-chat territory (CLAUDE.md section 16), so
  the guard is requested in `handovers/HANDOVER_OUTPUT_LOGGER.md` under Asks
  pending rather than made here.
* Tests: `tests/test_periodic_feature_input_guards.py` gains the route-agnostic
  sweep (every QVF wavefunction section is either absent with a recorded
  reason or self-consistent and unit-cell dimensioned, across both neutral
  producers and two torus sizes), the real-Gamma regression pin, and a unit
  test that the new helper stays conservative when it cannot read a result's
  dimensions.

Test-only. `tests/test_periodic_gapw_open_shell.py::test_runner_dispatch_gpw_rohf_unsupported_envelopes_fail_closed[ROHF-3-kwargs0-...]`

expected `jk_method="gdf"` to fail closed has run the public
`native-multi-k-gdf-rohf` route since then (Li-atom/STO-3G fixture:
converged, -7.32227152 Ha, 5 iterations). Reverting only that one line makes

### Added: compact real-torus AO point actions for χ symmetry (D127, issue #661, 2026-09-04)

`build_aiccm2026dev_b_real_torus_ao_action` now snapshots one
finite-mesh-compatible χ spatial operation as an immutable action on
real-torus AO coefficient rows, provided its recomputed atom-mapping residual
also meets the action factory's independent \(10^{-5}\)-bohr cap. Because the
plan records the residual but not its input `symprec`, a plan built with a
looser tolerance can be valid diagnostically while D127 rejects its operation.
It combines the existing destination-row/source-column primitive AO rotation
with the exact χ cell scatter `R -> W R + q_action_a`, including atom-dependent
lattice shifts from fractional and nonsymmorphic operations. Equivalent atom
representatives outside the wrapped primitive cell are normalized through
fingerprinted integer reference offsets and corrected action shifts. Proper
and improper rotations are both supported; time reversal remains separate
antiunitary metadata.

The action retains one primitive AO matrix and a linear atom/cell image table,
not the full `(N_c * nbf)` squared torus operator. Its 3-D mesh, operation,
atom and AO mappings, orthogonality, and finite-cell permutations are checked
before every numeric field is detached onto bytes-backed immutable storage
and bound by a SHA-256 action-payload fingerprint. Small dense-materialization
tests reuse the trusted primitive AO rotation to check the χ cell scatter and
factorization for complex proper/improper actions, a fractional-translation
diamond operation and its nonzero representative cocycle, unwrapped atom
representatives, odd/even anisotropic and skew meshes,
identity/inverse/composition, a synthetic invariant metric, malformed inputs,
and storage scaling. Application allocates the result and atom-block-sized
temporaries, but never the dense torus action.

The factory validates basis origins and exact ordered radial-shell equality
across mapped atoms, but radial values remain outside the payload fingerprint.
Spherical \(l\geq1\) orbital AOs and \(s\) functions are supported; Cartesian
\(p\)-and-higher shells fail closed. The fingerprint does not bind the full
system or run identity, localized coefficients or overlap, or a stable spglib
operation enumeration. The action transforms AO rows only, not localized-
orbital columns, their own reference offsets, centres, phases, or local
domains.

D127 is a diagnostic representation primitive, not an execution speedup. It
does not alter SCF or post-HF energies, omit pairs, or feed D123/D126. The next
gate must derive and seal the actual localized-occupied representation,
including phases and the primitive-translation cocycle, then distinguish a
signed/phased monomial gauge from a general matrix-valued petal/flower
representation before physical pair reduction is allowed. D127 does not
construct Casassa-style symmetry-adapted localized Wannier functions or
classify their petals, flowers, and bunches.

### Added: compact conditional point-symmetry planning for χ pair work (D126, issue #656, 2026-09-04)

`build_point_pair_plan` now layers an exact point-symmetry workload quotient
on D123 without expanding the placed occupied pairs. Callers supply explicit
source-to-target occupied-index support permutations; the planner rejects any
permutation that does not normalize the finite pure-translation subgroup,
induces its support action on the D123 rows, closes the row orbits, combines
their exact multiplicities, and binds its factory-only immutable result to
parent, support-generator, and plan SHA-256 fingerprints.

Small odd, even, and anisotropic meshes are checked against the full
placed-pair oracle. In the idealized symmetry-adapted MgO
`A1g + T1u` (`s, p_x, p_y, p_z`) support model, the permutations induced by
all 48 `O_h` operations reduce 4,112 translation rows to 260 conditional work
rows while preserving
2,098,176 placed pairs and the exact per-cell census of 4,098.

This is planner-only and deliberately not wired into MP2, CCSD, or triples.
The support plan carries and fingerprints no orbital signs or phases. The real
χ MgO path still needs a symmetry-covariant occupied gauge, including dense
flower transformations when the localized orbitals are `sp3` mixtures, plus
covariant PAO/auxiliary/PNO/TNO domains and amplitude scatter. No pair is
skipped, no energy or finite Hamiltonian changes, and no achieved symmetry
speedup or reduced-scaling DLPNO capability is claimed.

### Fixed: a fractionally occupied SCC-DFTB-SECCM row no longer reports as an ordinary Aufbau row (#302, 2026-09-04)

`run_scc_dftb_seccm` returned `converged = True` on a rocksalt(100) slab
whose frontier occupation is completely ambiguous, with nothing on the result
to distinguish it from a genuinely gapped row. Measured on `main` at 0.15.159:

| Mg/O rocksalt(100) L3, a = 4.000 A, unembedded, DIIS, T_el = 0.005 Ha |  |
|---|---|
| `converged` / `n_iter` | `True` / 92 |
| `homo_lumo_gap` | 2.441871e-08 Ha |
| `gap_guard_waived` | `False` |
| f(HOMO) / f(LUMO) | 1.3370094 / 1.3370072 |
| `charges.max()` | +2.002335 (Mg carries 2 valence electrons) |

The HOMO and LUMO each hold 1.337 electrons: the applied occupation cannot
resolve them at all, which is the same physical state as the O/O L1 row that
`gap_guard_waived` already flags. It escaped that guard for a dimensional
reason -- the guard compares the gap to an **absolute** epsilon
(`finite_torus_gap_tolerance`, 1e-8 Ha), while the scale that resolves an
occupation under smearing is kT. This row's gap is 2.4x the epsilon and
5e-6 of the smearing width. Commit `4e0b569a6` (#422) closed the case where
the gap is a numerical zero; this is the case where it is not.

`SCCDFTBSECCMResult` now records the occupation it actually applied:
`occupations`, `aufbau_occupation_deviation` (`max_i |f_i - f_i^Aufbau|`,
exactly `0.0` on the T = 0 branch by construction), `aufbau_occupation`, and
the `aufbau_occupation_tolerance` actually used, so the verdict is
reproducible from the record alone. A row with `aufbau_occupation = False` is
a stationary point of the fractional-occupation functional, which differs
from the Aufbau one by exactly the `-T*S` term this route subtracts (Weinert
and Davenport, Phys. Rev. B 45, 13709 (1992), Eqs. 8 and 10'), so it must not
be compared against a T = 0 reference. A deviation at or above `1.0` means the
chemical potential has reached the Aufbau LUMO: metallic, not merely
broadened. The slab above records 1.337; an ordinary smeared HLi chain
records 0.311; every T = 0 row records exactly 0.

`gap_guard_waived` is unchanged, and so is every energy: the diff to
`cpp/src/semiempirical/seccm/scc_dftb.cpp` is purely additive and touches no
term of the functional. The MgO(100) L2 slab still converges in 19 iterations
to `homo_lumo_gap = 0.00428369951148803`, the value
`tests/test_ccm_semiempirical.py` pinned before these fields existed.

**The filed charge premise is refuted, not gated.** #302 asked for a
`|q| <= n_val` acceptance gate. On the slab above the WS overlap is positive
definite (minimum eigenvalue 0.8788, so the #207 screened metric is never
engaged), `tr(DS)` is 96.0000000000 against 96 valence electrons, the natural
occupations of `S^(1/2) D S^(1/2)` lie in `[1.7e-10, 2.0]`, and the Loewdin
AO populations lie in `[0.000473, 2.0]`. The Mg excursion is -0.0023 e of
gross Mulliken population, which Mulliken (J. Chem. Phys. 23, 1833 (1955),
Sec. 3 p. 1835) documents as a property of the partitioning: gross
populations "would ideally" never be negative nor exceed 2.00 per closed
sub-shell, but small excursions occur, and the invariant is the total. vibe-qc
therefore does not gate on a raw charge range. The excursion is a *symptom* of
the unresolved frontier -- at `electronic_temperature = 0.02` the same slab
returns `charges.max() = +1.9931`, inside the formal limit, with no code
change.

Regression: `tests/test_seccm_scc_dftb_basin.py` (4 tests). The user guide
gains the screening rule and the Mulliken caveat, and
`routes.methods.scc_dftb_seccm` now carries the Weinert citation the route
had been relying on unattributed.

### Fixed: the EWALD_3D HF route can be held on one exact-exchange gauge across meshes (#560, 2026-09-03)

`run_rhf_periodic_multi_k_ewald3d` served two different exact-exchange
`q -> 0` conventions depending on the mesh it was handed, with no way to
say which one you wanted:

* a **single Gamma point** took the molecular-limit kernel -- every image
  density block zeroed before the exchange contraction, so the sum has one
  term and there is no `q + G = 0` (Madelung) contribution at all;
* **any other mesh** took the corrected Ewald split, i.e. PySCF's
  `exxdiv='ewald'` (fafeef8b3, because the bare image sum diverges with the
  lattice cutoff once `D(g)` is Born-von-Karman-torus periodic).

Neither number is wrong in its own convention, and both converge to the same
infinite-k limit, but they are **not equal at any finite mesh** -- Carrier,
Rohra & Görling, Phys. Rev. B 75, 205126 (2007), Sec. IV: the singularity
correction and the uncorrected exchange energy "vary oppositely with
increasing number of k points". So a k-convergence sequence taken with the
route defaults was not a sequence in one gauge (21.7 mHa of gauge step
between `(1,1,1)` and `(2,2,2)` on H2/STO-3G in an 8-bohr cube), and a
Gamma-supercell energy could not be band-folded onto a multi-k energy at
all, because there was no way to ask for a Gamma-mesh calculation in the
corrected gauge. That is what
`tests/test_ccm_periodic_3d.py::test_ccm_equals_scm_gamma_band_folding`
had been failing on since fafeef8b3, 2.43 mHa against a 5e-5 tolerance.

New keyword `exchange_exxdiv` on that driver: `None` (default) keeps the
historical per-mesh choice bit for bit; `'ewald'` takes the corrected split
at every mesh including a single Gamma point, and raises rather than
degrading when the split is unavailable; `'none'` names the molecular-limit
kernel and is refused on any real mesh, where that sum does not converge.

Anchored out of process against PySCF 2.14.0 (CLAUDE.md paragraph 10 --
never imported), H2/STO-3G, a = 8 bohr, d = 1.4 bohr, per unit cell:

| | vibe-qc | PySCF `exxdiv='ewald'` |
|---|---|---|
| Gamma, unit cell, corrected | -1.1451987342 | -1.1452192802 (+20.5 uHa) |
| Gamma, (2,2,2) supercell /8, corrected | -1.1191353264 | -1.1191323123 (-3.0 uHa) |
| (2,2,2) mesh, unit cell (unchanged) | -1.1191128978 | -1.1191323123 (+19.4 uHa) |

Band folding inside vibe-qc with both sides on the corrected gauge:
-1.1191353264 vs -1.1191128978, i.e. 2.24e-5 Ha, inside the identity test's
own 5e-5. PySCF band-folds the same pair to 8.7e-13 in either gauge.

**The Gamma-only drivers keep their molecular-limit gauge by default** and
no released energy moves; which gauge should be the default for
`run_rhf_periodic_gamma_ewald3d` and its RKS/UHF siblings is a separate
maintainer decision, recorded on #560.

### Added: `variant="neutral-bloch"` runs the second producer of the neutral Gamma-CCM torus (AICCM front door M1b, #645, 2026-09-04)

Milestone M1b of `handovers/HANDOVER_AICCM_STANDARD_METHOD.md`. Ruling R1
(2026-08-21) says Paper-1 Gamma-CCM denotes the neutral finite-BvK-torus
construction, which has two admissible producers. `variant="real-gamma"`
evaluates it in the real-Gamma supercell representation and has run from the
runner since 2026-07-26; the Bloch producer was library-only. Both are now
reachable through the one front door, so the Fourier identity between them
can be exercised without leaving `run_periodic_job`. AICCM stays experimental.

* New adapter `python/vibeqc/periodic/ccm/neutral_bloch_runner.py`. Unlike the
  real-Gamma sibling it performs no fold and no `N_c` division: the producer
  already runs the production multi-k GDF drivers on the unit cell over the
  torus's own Gamma-centred mesh, so the adapter returns that result (with the
  convention record attached) and every artefact stage keeps working. When a
  density grid or QVF is requested, the adapter now also returns the exact
  inverse-Bloch lattice density beside the unchanged per-k matrices; the
  strict artifact path refolds and validates that producer-owned state rather
  than reconstructing an unauthenticated per-k result. This closes the
  independently reproduced `(2,2,2)` failure where Molden, DOS and QVF were
  written but the requested XSF was missing at finalization. The
  pair-star reduction of the Lpq fits is OFF by default on this arm, so the
  executed Hamiltonian is the production one rather than a star
  reconstruction whose finite cell-list residual is quantitative.
* `PeriodicJKMethod.NEUTRAL_BLOCH` joins `_IMPLEMENTED`; the runner gains the
  guard block, the dispatch arm, the manifest block, the QVF vendor section,
  and membership in the multi-k orbital, level-shift, aux-basis and
  unsupported-functional route lists. Measured: `method="aiccm",
  variant="neutral-bloch"` equals `jk_method="gdf"` on the same Gamma-centred
  mesh exactly, and equals `variant="real-gamma"` to about 1e-13 Ha per cell
  at torus sizes (1,1,1), (2,1,1) and (2,2,1) on H2/STO-3G. RHF, RKS, UHF and
  UKS all run; the SCF reference keeps coming from the front door's inference.
* Fail-closed surface: dim below 3, DFT+U, `optimize`, `hessian`, a READ
  restart, an `exchange_exxdiv` other than the producer's ewald convention,
  and any explicit `damping`, `fock_mixing`, `fmixing_percent`,
  `density_mixer` or `level_shift`, which the arm forwards nowhere and would
  otherwise drop silently. The producer additionally refuses a cell declared
  3-D whose transverse directions measure as pure vacuum and a positive
  converged energy on a neutral cell (both IID 291), so the arm is narrower
  than plain GDF by construction, not by accident.
* Records: the `.system` carries the result-derived convention
  (`exchange_q0` and applicability, `ccm_construction` byte-identical to the
  real-Gamma producer's because it is the same construction,
  `evaluation_representation`, `bvk_nrep`, `bvk_n_cells`, the executed mixing
  values) plus the fit accounting `lpq_pair_symmetry`, `gdf_pair_builds`,
  `gdf_pair_total`, `gdf_pair_reduction_factor` and
  `rsgdf_tail_ke_cutoff_executed`, which is what makes the two producers'
  reciprocal support auditable against each other. The QVF archive gains
  `x_vibeqc_neutral_bloch_convention`.
* Citations: the pre-positioned `routes.methods` key `neutral-bloch` now
  fires with both CCM lineage papers plus the GDF stack the arm executes, and
  a plain `jk_method="gdf"` job on the same mesh still cites neither, which is
  pinned as the negative control.
* Tests: new `tests/test_periodic_ccm_neutral_bloch_adapter.py` (T3,
  experimental; 13 tests covering the adapter contract, the two energy
  identities, the manifest, the QVF record, the open-shell references and the

  artifact), the front-door pins in
  `tests/test_periodic_feature_input_guards.py` extended to the variant, and

  `scripts/test_gate/suite_manifest.json` regenerated (the new file classifies
