### Fixed: electrostatic properties on ECP systems use the effective nuclear charge Z - n_core (issue #642, 2026-09-03)

Wrong answer, high severity, every ECP-bearing molecule whose dipole or
atomic charges were evaluated. `vibeqc.properties.dipole_moment`, the FD
Hessian's `_dipole_at` (which feeds `dipole_derivatives` and the IR
intensities), and the Mulliken / Loewdin / Hirshfeld populations built their
nuclear term from the bare `atom.Z`, while the density of an ECP SCF
integrates to the valence count only. Each ECP atom therefore contributed a
spurious `n_core (R_A - O)` to the dipole and `+n_core` to its partial
charge: a neutral molecule's dipole depended on the origin by exactly
`-n_core` au per bohr, and the charges summed to `sum n_core` instead of the
molecular charge.

Measured pre-fix, H2S/LANL2DZ RHF (S core = 10 electrons, XML-library route):
dipole at the centre of mass 0.148 D with the wrong sign, `-10.000` au per
bohr of origin shift, Mulliken S = +9.84, charges summing to +10.00.
Post-fix: 1.99496 D, origin-invariant to 3.5e-15 au, Mulliken S = -0.1588,
charges summing to zero to 5e-15. CH4/vDZP (inline-primitive route, C core =
2): `-2.000` au per bohr pre-fix, origin-invariant post-fix, and the FD
Hessian's dipole derivatives now satisfy the translational sum rule
`sum_A d mu / d R_A = 0` (max 1e-6; pre-fix `2 I` on the carbon rows), so
the IR intensities of every carbon-moving mode change (strongest stretch
89.89 -> 87.49 km/mol on the test fixture).

The charge every electrostatic term of an ECP calculation sees is the core
charge `Q = Z - n_core` of the valence-only model Hamiltonian (Dolg & Cao,
Chem. Rev. 112, 403 (2012), Sec. 5, Eqs. 54-55; now cited with libecpint on
every ECP run). New `vibeqc.ecp_metadata.effective_nuclear_charges(mol,
options)` returns it per atom for both ECP routes (inline primitive blocks
first, then the XML library, bare `Z` without an ECP), and
`dipole_moment` / `mulliken_charges` / `loewdin_charges` /
`hirshfeld_charges` take a `nuclear_charges=` keyword that defaults to bare
`Z`, so all-electron results are byte-identical. The runner threads the
options the single point actually ran with (the ECP is auto-attached inside
the dispatcher, so the route kwarg may be `None`) to the `.out` properties
block, the structured `properties` event, the population sidecar and QVF
block, and to the `hessian=True` frequency path, which previously received
that `None` and would have differentiated an all-electron Hamiltonian on an
ECP molecule; the FD Hessian resolves the charges once per run; the ASE
calculator and the double-hybrid population writer pass their own options.
Hirshfeld on ECP systems still weights with all-electron free-atom densities,
so its per-atom split there is approximate although the charges now sum to
the molecular charge; documented in `docs/user_guide/ecp.md`.

Not changed: the periodic population route (`_bipole_mulliken_charges` and
`periodic_runner`'s `write_scf_trace`) keeps bare `Z`; periodic ECPs are a
separate audit.

Tests: `tests/test_ecp_scf.py` (Z_eff for the XML route; origin independence
and 1.99496 D with the bare-Z counterexample pinned; population sums; a
`run_job` deck checking the `.out` and population sidecar),
`tests/test_ecp_gradient.py` (Z_eff for the inline route; origin
independence; the FD Hessian translational sum rule and the re-measured
intensity), `tests/test_properties.py` (keyword default and shape guard),
`tests/test_citations.py` (Dolg & Cao fires with libecpint only).

### Fixed: SECCM Wigner-Seitz ties survive finite-precision coordinates (issues #592, #593, 2026-09-03)

The shared SECCM Wigner-Seitz builders (`seccm/topology.hpp`,
`seccm/topology.py`) decided whether two periodic images of an atom are
equidistant from the central atom with a pure roundoff guard,
`256 * eps * scale` (about 1e-12 bohr), since 65f6b0048 (v0.15.138) replaced
the MSINDO `RUND(.,4)` rule with the exact closest-image search. Any input whose
atomic coordinates and cyclic translations disagree above that level -- a
`Molecule` built with the CODATA-2014 Angstrom-to-bohr constant and read back
with vibe-qc's CODATA-2018 one differs by 4.4e-10 relative, 2.8e-9 A -- lost
its shared images: on MgO B1 (2,2,2) the 512 records with Evjen weights 1/6,
1/4, 1/2, 1 collapsed to 320 records with weights 1/3, 1/2, 1, while the
`round(sum of weights) == N-1` validity rule still passed. The MSINDO SECCM
energy of that cluster moved from the exact-tie value -137.589374958906 Ha
(the published article EOS value, vq job 60a32b0a8630 at v0.15.138) to
-137.649212029216 Ha and became labeling dependent (-137.661381291093 Ha with
the anion sublattice translated by a primitive vector; 1.2e-2 Ha, issue #592).
The kernel itself was never wrong: called on exact coordinates it reproduces
the article value to 2.5e-12 for both labelings, so the v0.15.138 article
numbers are the correct cyclic-cluster energies and `main` was wrong for
finite-precision input (issue #593).

Both builders now share images whose distance to the central atom lies within
`1.0e-5` (bohr on every route) of the minimum, MSINDO `neighbors.f`'s
tolerance, kept as `max(1.0e-5, 256 * eps * scale)`
(`kEquidistantImageTolerance` / `_EQUIDISTANT_IMAGE_TOLERANCE`). This is the
Evjen weighting of Bredow, Geudtner & Jug, J. Comput. Chem. 22, 89 (2001),
pp. 90-91, which retains every border neighbour "with the same distance"
because keeping one alone "would lead to a non-symmetric region with a dipole
moment". Exact-tie geometries are bit-unchanged; the 4.4e-10 dilation itself
is worth 2e-9 Ha. Images that tie only within the tolerance now count as
reference ties for the fixed-topology rebuild as exact ties already did, so
`SECCMTopology.rebuild_displacements` asks for `max_tie_score_excursion` on
such geometries too. Regressions:
`tests/test_seccm_topology_cpp.py::test_equidistant_image_ties_survive_finite_precision_coordinates`
(512-record parity of both builders on exact and mismatched input; fail-first
282 records for that test's uniform 4.4e-10 dilation, 320 for the article's
round-tripped geometry above) and
`tests/test_msindo_ccm.py::test_seccm_mgo_222_invariant_under_anion_sublattice_lattice_translation`
(article path through `run_seccm`; fail-first -137.649 / -137.661 Ha vs the
article value).

### Fixed: `run_job(tddft_gradient=True)` no longer prints an HF-CIS gradient for a run that computed a different surface (issue #570, 2026-09-03)

The finite-difference excited-state gradient block in `run_job` was built from
`vibeqc.excited_gradient.make_hf_cis_energy_fn` whatever the run's method was:
an RKS + TDA run, an RKS + Casida run, or an RHF + Casida run all received the
closed-shell HF + CIS S₁ gradient under the header `Excited-state gradient (S₁,
FD, step=1e-3 Å)`, which named no surface. Measured on H2/STO-3G (H at
±0.7 Å, one TDA root): `method="rks", functional="lda"` and `method="rhf",
tddft_type="casida"` both printed 0.02279028 Ha/bohr on the z components,
bit-identical to the RHF/TDA run and to the direct HF-CIS driver, while their
own excitation energies were LDA/TDA and TDHF/Casida values.

`run_job` now refuses `tddft_gradient=True` before any calculation unless the
run is a closed-shell RHF reference with `tddft_type="tda"` (CIS), naming the
missing capability (`NotImplementedError`, no `.out` written). The wired case
keeps its numbers (pinned against the direct driver in
`tests/test_excited_gradient.py`) and labels the block `Excited-state gradient
(S₁, RHF/CIS(TDA) surface, FD, step=1e-3 Å)` with a `Surface:` line naming the
reference, the excitation solver, the state tracking and the step. Wiring the
RKS/TDA and Casida energies into the reference-agnostic FD driver with state
tracking is left as the follow-up the refusal names; `docs/features.md` and
the TDDFT tutorial say which surface the gradient is. The release paper's
Section 2.7 qualification (HF-CIS) stays correct.

## [v0.15.159] - 2026-09-03 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Fixed: T=0 k-point Aufbau degeneracy grouping is transitive and bounded, in the C++ kernels and the Python twin (#544, 2026-09-03)

The zero-temperature Aufbau fills decide "same level" with a roundoff test
(256 ulps at the spectrum's scale, Weinert-Davenport T -> 0 ensemble on the
cut group). All three kernels grouped by comparing every candidate to the
group's **first** member, a ball rather than a chain, so a run of states
each within tolerance of its neighbour could be split into two groups that
sit one ulp apart. When the electron count landed on that split the fill
integer-occupied one member of an effectively degenerate manifold and left
its twin empty, decided by last-ulp arithmetic. The #434 guard turned that
into a recorded unresolved cut on the multi-k routes; the Gamma helper had
no guard and returned the chopped manifold.

Synthetic reproduction (three k-points, one band each, at 0, 4e-14 and
8e-14 Ha, tolerance 5.7e-14 Ha, 4/3 electrons): pre-fix the multi-k fill
returned occupations 2, 2, 0 with `frontier_cut_unresolved=True`; post-fix
the whole manifold shares 4/3, 4/3, 4/3 and nothing is flagged. Gamma
helper on 0, 4e-14, 8e-14, 1.2e-13, 1.0 Ha with two occupied orbitals:
pre-fix 4/3, 4/3, 4/3, 0, 0 (the fourth member, 4e-14 above its neighbour,
chopped off); post-fix 1, 1, 1, 1, 0.

* `global_zero_temperature_occupations` (multi-k DFTB0 / SCC-DFTB),
  `gamma_degenerate_frontier_occupations` (Gamma DFTB0 / SCC-DFTB, both
  spin conventions) and the Python twin `smearing.apply._global_aufbau_with_mu`
  (ab-initio multi-k GDF / GAPW / Ewald routes) now chain neighbours within
  the tolerance and cap a group's span at 16 tolerances. A boundary landing on
  the cap is still recorded by the #434 guard, so no configuration can
  integer-fill across a sub-tolerance split silently.
* The two grouping numbers are named on both sides
  (`kZeroTemperatureDegeneracyUlps` / `kDegenerateGroupSpanFactor`,
  `ZERO_TEMPERATURE_DEGENERACY_ULPS` / `DEGENERATE_GROUP_SPAN_FACTOR`) and
  exported from the bindings as
  `_vibeqc_core.semiempirical.zero_temperature_degeneracy_ulps` /
  `degenerate_group_span_factor`; a test pins them equal.
* `compute_closed_shell_kpoint_occupations`, `KPointOccupationResult` and
  `gamma_degenerate_frontier_occupations` are exposed on
  `_vibeqc_core.semiempirical` so the kernels can be tested on synthetic
  spectra and pinned against the Python twin.
* Regression: `tests/test_smearing_frontier_resolution.py` gains the
  chopped-manifold fixture on both kernels, the Gamma helper case, a
  C++-vs-Python parity sweep on random roundoff clusters, the span-cap
  ladder invariant (fractional or flagged, never a silent integer chop) and
  the constant pins. The #339 bulk-Si fractional-population pins and the
  #434 guard tests are unchanged.
* `smearing.unresolved_frontier_cut` takes the true `max_occupation` (the
  fill passes 2.0): it inferred the full occupancy from the largest value
  present, so a shared fractional group with no fully occupied state below
  it -- the lowest states of a nearly empty band -- was reported as an
  unresolved integer cut. Found while pinning the two kernels' guard
  verdicts to each other on the ladder fixture.
* `docs/user_guide/semiempirical.md` states the grouping rule.

### Fixed: the closed-shell selected-CI basis carries the pair-move coupling (issue #639, 2026-09-03)

Wrong answer, medium severity. `SelectedCIOptions(spin_restricted=True)` walks
closed-shell determinants (a `Det` is a tuple of doubly-occupied spatial
orbitals), and the restricted Slater-Condon dispatch scored those
determinants with *spin-orbital* rules: a one-pair move `i^2 -> a^2` was
evaluated with the one-electron single-excitation formula (the Brillouin
term, ~1e-16 Ha for HF orbitals) and a two-pair move with the same-spin
double rule (a four-electron excitation, whose true coupling is zero).
`build_hamiltonian_matrix`, `hamiltonian_matrix_element`, the deprecated
`hamiltonian_dot`, and the restricted candidate selection and EN-PT2 of the
selected-CI solver all shared the defect, so a closed-shell space was a
diagonal matrix plus noise and returned the Hartree-Fock energy.

Measured pre-fix, H2/STO-3G at R = 1.4 bohr with both closed-shell
determinants {sigma_g^2, sigma_u^2} in the space: off-diagonal 1.0e-16 Ha,
E = -1.1167143251 Ha (= E_HF). Post-fix: off-diagonal 0.18125791 Ha =
<00|11> = K_01, E = -1.1372759436170652 Ha, the FCI energy (the singlet is
seniority-zero), bit-identical to the unrestricted builder over the same two
determinants as ((0,),(0,)) and ((1,),(1,)) -- the exact oracle, which the
new regression uses.

The closed-shell `Det` rules are now the seniority-zero (DOCI) Hamiltonian
(Bytautas, Henderson, Jimenez-Hoyos, Ellis & Scuseria, J. Chem. Phys. 135,
044119 (2011), doi:10.1063/1.3613706, cited on that basis via a new
`bytautas_doci_2011` entry): diagonal unchanged, one pair moved
`H_IJ = <ii|aa>` with phase +1 (new `pair_excitation_matrix_element`,
exported from `vibeqc.solvers`), two or more pairs moved zero. The per-sector
primitives `single_excitation_matrix_element` /
`double_excitation_matrix_element` and the whole `*_unrestricted` family are
untouched. On N2/cc-pVDZ CAS(6e,6o) the restricted ladder that froze at ndet=6
and -108.9594672752 Ha now climbs through all C(6,3) = 20 closed-shell
determinants to the DOCI energy -108.9850687702 Ha (oracle-identical to
1.8e-15), still 36.7 mHa above CASCI because every omitted configuration is
open-shell -- the #107 reachability warning and its `converged=False` on an
exhausted pool short of `target_size` are unchanged and now say that the limit
is the DOCI energy. The memory pre-flight's restricted candidate count drops
its two-pair term to match the kernel.

**Callers of `build_hamiltonian_matrix` over `generate_closed_shell_determinants`
get a different number**: it is the DOCI matrix, equal to full CI only for two
electrons. The `examples/wavefunction/` scripts that labelled that quantity
"FCI" for LiH, H4, BH, CH2 and OH computed neither before this fix.

Tests: `tests/test_solvers_determinant.py` pins the pair element, the zero
two-pair element and the closed-shell builder against the unrestricted oracle
on random symmetric integrals; `tests/test_solvers_selected_ci.py` pins the
H2 closure criterion through both the dense builder and the solver route,
re-pins the three #107 restricted-ladder tests to the DOCI numbers, and
`tests/test_citations.py` pins the conditional citation.

### Fixed: molecular drivers that move atoms now move the ECP centres with them (#643, 2026-09-03)

HIGH-severity follow-up to #576. Both ECP routes store the centres as
absolute coordinates on the SCF options (`ecp_centers[i].xyz`,
`ecp_primitive_centers[i]`), and every driver that evaluated the SCF at a
new geometry reused the caller's options unchanged. The C++ SCF attaches a
centre to an atom only within 1e-6 bohr, so a moved atom reverted to bare
`Z` while `V_ECP` kept acting.

Measured pre-fix on the `tests/test_ecp_scf.py` H2S/LANL2DZ fixture and
[ZnH]+/6-31G/ecp10mdf:

* `run_job(optimize=True)` raised at the first force evaluation
  (`libecpint reports 4 atoms but the molecule has 3`): the ASE-backend
  calculator's first call ran with no ECP at all (the SCF wrappers attach
  it lazily, at the input geometry, only inside the first single point),
  BFGS stepped 0.2 A, and the second call saw moved atoms against the
  stale centre.
* `vibeqc.ase.VibeQC` after moving S by 0.05 A: E = -75.69 Ha instead of
  -10.995 Ha, then the same gradient error.
* The shared image evaluator behind `run_dimer` / `run_irc` did not read
  the ECP fields at all: its warm-start seam builds an all-electron Hcore
  (bare-Z nuclear attraction, full electron count), giving -1777.748 Ha for
  [ZnH]+ at the template geometry versus the ECP value -224.1265 Ha; a
  `run_irc` on that system reported the same -1777.7 Ha surface.
* The native optimisers walked a bare-Z gradient with the centre stuck at
  the start geometry: on H2S/LANL2DZ L-BFGS-B ended unconverged at
  -86.21 Ha with S driven to z = 7.87 bohr (the ECP minimum is -11.0313 Ha)
  and Brent raised "RHF result is not converged" in its line search.

Post-fix, a displaced image, a moved ASE geometry and every optimiser step
equal a fresh SCF + gradient built for that geometry to 1e-9 Ha / 1e-8
Ha/bohr, and `run_job(optimize=True, hessian=True)` on H2S/LANL2DZ
converges to -11.03125 Ha on both backends with three real modes.

* `vibeqc.ecp_metadata` gains `options_carry_ecp` and the permanent
  `reposition_ecp_centres(options, molecule, atom_indices)`; the #576
  context manager now builds on it.
* `neb._evaluate_image` (run_dimer / run_irc path forces) moves the
  centres onto each image relative to the template and restores them,
  runs ECP images through the high-level ECP-aware drivers (no density
  warm-start on that branch), mirrors the ECP fields onto the gradient
  when the caller passes none, and refuses a top-level `grid_options`
  override on ECP RKS/UKS images. `dimer._build_force_fn` refuses centres
  that sit on no template atom before the first SCF. `run_neb` keeps
  refusing molecular ECP paths.
* `vibeqc.ase.VibeQC` fixes the centre-to-atom map at the first geometry
  where the centres sit on the atoms (or right after the SCF wrapper
  attaches them) and repositions permanently at every `calculate()`;
  prebuilt centres off the first geometry raise `ValueError`. The `hessian`
  property routes ECP systems to `compute_hessian_fd`, because the analytic
  RHF/UHF/RKS kernels take no ECP options.
* `molecular_optimize`: `optimize_molecule`, `optimize_molecule_brent` and
  `_gradient_via_central_difference` follow the centres per evaluated
  geometry and restore the caller's options; on ECP systems a `None`
  `gradient_options` becomes the mirror of the SCF options.
* `run_job(optimize=True)` attaches the basis sidecar's ECP for the start
  geometry before any optimiser runs, records which atom each centre sits
  on, and moves the centres onto the optimised geometry (also on the
  non-converged path) before the final single point and the Hessian.
* Regression: `tests/test_ecp_gradient.py` (image evaluator on both routes,
  FD gradient helper, refusal), `tests/test_ase.py` (moved atom, refusal,
  FD Hessian route), `tests/test_molecular_optimize.py` (both native
  optimisers vs a fresh ECP single point), `tests/test_irc.py` (ECP IRC
  smoke, refusal), `tests/test_ecp_scf.py` (`run_job(optimize=True,
  hessian=True)` on both backends).
* Still open, not changed here: ROHF/ROKS have no ECP route at all
  (`ROHFOptions` carries no ECP fields); the CPCM branch of the ASE
  calculator consumes only the XML route and calls `cpcm_gradient` without
  gradient options; #642 (bare-Z nuclear dipole on ECP systems).
  `docs/user_guide/ecp.md` § "What wires this for you" and
  `docs/user_guide/ase_integration.md` state the new contract.

### Fixed: the FD Hessian differentiates the ECP-aware gradient and moves the ECP centres with the displaced atom (#576, 2026-09-03)

HIGH-severity. `compute_hessian_fd` finite-differences the analytic
gradient, and two things were wrong on any ECP-bearing molecule:

* It default-constructed `GradientOptions` when the caller passed none --
  the bare-Z, direct four-index all-electron gradient -- and the two
  production callers, the molecular runner's `hessian=True` frequency /
  thermochemistry path and `run_irc`'s transition-state Hessian, always
  passed none. Only `vibeqc.ase.VibeQC` mirrored the SCF's ECP fields.
* Both ECP routes pin the potential to **absolute coordinates** on the SCF
  options (`ecp_centers[i].xyz`, `ecp_primitive_centers[i]`), and the
  displaced-geometry loop moved the nucleus without them. `cpp/src/ecp.cpp`
  attaches a centre to an atom only within 1e-6 bohr (libecpint assigns by
  position within 1e-4 bohr), so at the first 0.005 bohr displacement the
  ECP atom reverted to bare Z while `V_ECP` kept acting.

Measured pre-fix: [ZnH]+/6-31G/ecp10mdf RHF diverged to E = -7.4e10 Ha at
Zn displaced 0.005 bohr with the centre left behind (CH4/vDZP inline:
-1.3e13 Ha), so `compute_hessian_fd` raised "SCF failed to converge" and
the runner's frequency block was lost; displacing only the all-electron H
converged and silently gave the bare-Z column, d2E/dz_H^2 = 0.6473 instead
of 0.1186 Ha/bohr^2 (5.5x). Post-fix the Hessian elements equal the second
central difference of the ECP-aware energy to 1.1e-6 ([ZnH]+, XML route)
and 4.1e-6 (CH4/vDZP, inline route) Ha/bohr^2, i.e. FD truncation; the
runner reports H2S/LANL2DZ at 1029.3 / 3756.6 / 3814.1 cm^-1 and CH4/vDZP
with its Td-degenerate pattern, identical to a direct
`compute_hessian_fd` call.

* New `vibeqc.gradient_options.gradient_options_from_scf` (moved out of
  `vibeqc.ase` so `hessian` and `irc` can use it without importing ASE;
  the private ASE name is kept as an alias) mirrors the JK backend and the
  ECP fields of both routes; `copy_ecp_fields` re-points an existing
  `GradientOptions` at another geometry's SCF options.
* `compute_hessian_fd(gradient_options=None)` now derives the gradient from
  `scf_options`. This also makes a density-fitted / RIJCOSX SCF's FD
  Hessian differentiate the DF / COSX gradient instead of the direct one,
  the same rule the ASE calculator has applied since June. An explicit
  `gradient_options` keeps its JK-backend fields; its ECP fields are
  synchronised to the SCF options at every displaced geometry.
* New `vibeqc.ecp_metadata.ecp_centres_follow_atoms` context manager moves
  the centres of both routes onto the displaced atoms for each SCF +
  gradient evaluation and restores the caller's options afterwards (by
  value: pybind hands the list elements out by reference).
  `ecp_centre_atom_indices` maps centres to atoms and fails closed, so
  `compute_hessian_fd` now refuses ECP options whose centres sit on no atom
  of the molecule with a `ValueError` naming the centre, before any SCF.
* `run_irc` forwards its `gradient_options` to the TS Hessian.
* Regression: `tests/test_ecp_gradient.py` pins the Hessian-vs-energy second
  difference on both routes (1e-4 Ha/bohr^2), the silent bare-Z column, the
  helper's field mirror, the centre repositioning/restore, and the
  fail-closed refusal; `tests/test_ecp_scf.py` pins the runner's frequency
  block on H2S/LANL2DZ; `tests/test_irc.py` pins the forwarding.
* Not fixed here, filed separately: the nuclear dipole in
  `hessian._dipole_at` / `properties.dipole_moment` uses bare Z on ECP
  systems (IR intensities), and the shared image evaluator behind
  `run_dimer` / `run_irc` path forces and `vibeqc.ase.VibeQC` after the
  first optimisation step do not reposition ECP centres either.
  `docs/user_guide/ecp.md` § "What wires this for you" states the new
  contract and these gaps.

### Fixed: `from_orca.md` attributed the ORCA-vs-vibe-qc DFT offset to the grid; it is ORCA's default RI-J / RIJCOSX (#567, 2026-09-03)

The user-guide comparison page said the ~69 µHa H₂/STO-3G B3LYP residual
was "ORCA DefGrid2". Measured on site_f (vq jobs 45f56c95b9ee and
7982752b32b6, issue #567 note 14198): the HF pair agrees to 2e-10 Ha,
both grid ladders are flat (vibe-qc 0.03 µEh across a 20× point-count
range; ORCA 0.05 µEh from DefGrid2 to IntAcc 7.0), 98 % of the offset
sits in the Coulomb term, and `! NORI` on the ORCA side closes H₂/B3LYP
to 3 nHa. ORCA ≥ 5 turns on Split-RI-J (pure functionals) and RIJCOSX
(hybrids) silently, with `def2/J` auto-attached; vibe-qc's `run_job`
computes exact J and K unless `density_fit=True` is requested. The page
now states this, gives the matched-comparison recipe (`! NORI` on the
ORCA side, or `density_fit=True` with `def2-universal-jfit` on the
vibe-qc side), and corrects the attribution. Two grid-preset comments in
`runner.py` are corrected too: Lebedev order 35 is the 434-point rule
(not 590), and `orca-defgrid3` matches ORCA DefGrid3 *energies*, it does
not reproduce ORCA's grid construction. No code behaviour changes. The
119-deck `dft-grid-default-comparison` parity class in the paper
repository is the article's decision (article #6): regenerate the ORCA
decks with `! NORI` or run the vibe-qc legs with matched density fitting.

### Changed: `run_periodic_job(method="aiccm", variant=...)` is the one front door to the AICCM formulations (AICCM front door M1, #569, 2026-09-03)

Second milestone of `handovers/HANDOVER_AICCM_STANDARD_METHOD.md`: a
selector change with no numerical effect. AICCM stays experimental (the
warnings, the `[run].method_status = "experimental"` stamp, the T3 research
lanes and the experimental catalog rows all stay).

* `method="aiccm"` names the family; `variant` is mandatory and names the
  formulation: `"real-gamma"` (the neutral Γ-CCM torus in its real-Γ
  supercell representation; the former `jk_method="real-gamma"`), `"chi"`
  (χ-CCM; the former `jk_method="aiccm2026dev-b"`), `"neutral-bloch"` (the
  same neutral torus in its Bloch representation through the
  `periodic/ccm/ri.py` producer) and `"four-center"` (the 2014
  union-and-weight lineage). The last two fail closed from the runner with a
  pointer at the milestone that wires their arm (M1b, M3) and at the library
  entry that runs them today; `PeriodicJKMethod.NEUTRAL_BLOCH` exists so the
  manifest vocabulary and the citation route key are fixed now. Omitting
  `variant`, an unknown value, or `variant=` / `scf_reference=` with any
  other `method` fail closed.
* The SCF reference is inferred: `functional` decides HF versus KS, the
  system's multiplicity and electron parity decide restricted versus
  unrestricted (the parity rule the CCM library's `run_ccm_scf` applies);
  `scf_reference="rohf" | "roks"` selects the restricted open-shell
  references explicitly and fails closed on every wired variant today. The
  inferred reference is what `[plan].method` records.
* `jk_method` stays `"auto"` with `method="aiccm"` or must equal the
  variant's own route (member, value or legacy spelling); any other value
  raises naming both. A front-door variant counts as an explicit route, so
  the DFT+U AUTO fallback can never re-route an AICCM job onto BIPOLE.
* One torus keyword for every variant: `aiccm_lattice_extension` (and the
  `aiccm_wigner_seitz_shells` shorthand) now reach the real-Γ producer as
  its Γ-centred mesh; `kpoints` stays the legacy alias; both together fail
  closed before any artefact, on every variant.
* The real-Γ loop forwards `max_iter` and `conv_tol_energy` only, so an
  explicit `damping`, `fock_mixing`, `fmixing_percent`, `density_mixer` or
  `level_shift` on that variant now fails closed instead of being dropped
  silently (CLAUDE.md § 7). Documented in `docs/user_guide/aiccm.md`.
* Legacy `jk_method` spellings (`aiccm2026dev-a`, `aiccm2026dev-b`,
  `real-gamma`, `real_gamma`, `chi`, `chi-ccm`, and the three legacy enum
  members passed directly) keep dispatching and emit a `DeprecationWarning`
  naming the `method="aiccm", variant=...` form, attributed to the caller's
  own line so Python's default filters actually show it; the `.out` line
  under "J/K method" carries the same pointer for logs and for callers that
  filter warnings away. The bare `gamma` / `gamma-ccm` / `gamma_ccm`
  spellings are retired to fail-closed with the ruling-R1 message on the
  runner as on the library (D-2; decisions-log row D124 supersedes the
  bare-`gamma` clause of D89), and the four aliases `neutral-bloch`,
  `bloch-control`, `gdf-control`, `aiccm-ri`, which meant plain unit-cell
  GDF on the runner and the neutral Bloch producer in the library, are
  retired to fail-closed with a pointer (D-2b). Plain `jk_method="gdf"` is
  untouched.
* Records: every AICCM job writes `[run].aiccm_variant` and
  `aiccm_selector` (`"front-door"` or `"legacy-jk_method"`) next to
  `method_status`; a front-door job records the variant's route value in
  `jk_method_requested` / `_resolved` / `_executed`. `describe_jk_method`
  and the `.out` "J/K method" line read `aiccm (<variant>) ...;
  experimental` for every AICCM member, and the GDF description no longer
  advertises the retired aliases. The `.out` line below it reads
  `(selected by method='aiccm', variant='...'; SCF reference RHF inferred)`.
* Gate: `tests/test_test_gate_lanes.py` walks `python/vibeqc/periodic/chi`
  and `periodic/ccm` with `ast` and fails on any import of the sibling
  package (the D56/D74 firewall, previously a docstring). Two stale lane
  trigger globs removed from `scripts/test_gate/lane_manifest.json`
  (`python/vibeqc/ccm*.py` matched nothing; `semiempirical-aiccm` on
  `periodic/ccm/**` recorded a coupling that does not exist).
* Docs: new entry page `docs/user_guide/aiccm.md` (experimental banner,
  variants, inferred reference, torus keyword, convergence mapping, legacy
  spellings, what the outputs record); rows in `periodic_methods.md`,
  `keyword_index.md`, the route matrix, `periodic_jk_routes.md`, the two
  catalog rows, the D89 note and route-keyword section of
  `aiccm2026dev_a.md`, `output_files.md`, and the two package docstrings.
* Tests: `tests/test_periodic_feature_input_guards.py` (T2: dispatch of the
  wired variants, the two fail-closed variants, mandatory variant, conflict
  rule, SCF-reference inference table, ROHF/ROKS fail-closed, the
  deprecation contract incl. enum members, front-door silence, retired
  spellings on the runner, torus keyword and not-both rule, unhonoured
  convergence knobs, the DFT+U fallback), `tests/test_ccm_route.py` and
  `tests/test_periodic_ccm_real_gamma_adapter.py` (resolver rows moved to
  the fail-closed families; front door equals the legacy selector on a real
  run), `tests/test_xc_external_provider.py` and
  `tests/test_feature_citation_end_to_end.py` (front-door cases).

### Fixed: four `.out` golden snapshots predated the closed-shell stability rows (#640, 2026-09-03)

`tests/test_out_format_snapshot.py` was red on `main` (4 failed / 15 passed):
`mol_rhf`, `mol_rks`, `mol_hessian` and `mol_tddft` each lacked the
`internal stability: stable (lowest Hessian eigenvalue ...)` verdict line and
the `SCF stability analysis` timing row. Both became closed-shell output at
`2822ee496` (#144, the RHF/RKS restricted-stability verdict surface), which
gave `RHFResult`/`RKSResult` `stability_checked` and stability phase timings
without regenerating the goldens; `89a3f54c7` (#205) had introduced the
timing row and its volatile scrub and regenerated `mol_uhf` deliberately, so
only the closed-shell snapshots were stale. Goldens regenerated with
`VIBEQC_REGEN_GOLDEN=1`: 8 insertions, 0 deletions, no other line moved. No
format decision is made here -- the rows are #144's and #205's, and both stay
wall-independent under the existing canonicalizer.

### Fixed: the vq daemon tests read the CI host's memory pressure, so the release gate depended on the runner's load (issue #563, 2026-09-03)

`test_scoped_admin_update_hold.py::test_local_job_dispatches_during_a_site_i_rebuild`
went red on the v0.15.158 release-candidate pipeline with
`assert SUSPENDED == COMPLETED`: the daemon's host-pressure watchdog saw the
CI runner at 85.4 % (build-test and vibe-view-test ran beside it) and
SIGSTOPped the test's local job. The identical tree was green on retry.
Two changes: `Daemon._host_pressure_pass` now resolves the pressure probe
through `vq.watchdog` at call time (the `check_host_pressure` default
argument bound the function at import, so pinning
`vq.watchdog.read_host_memory_pressure_pct` never reached the daemon), and
`vibe-queue/tests/conftest.py` pins that probe to 10 % for every test
unless it opts out with `@pytest.mark.no_autopatch_host_pressure`. Guards:
a test that opts out, pins 90 % and asserts the local job is SUSPENDED with
`paused_by = watchdog_host_pressure` (fails at the parent, where the pin was
ignored and the job completed), and its twin with the pin in force that
asserts COMPLETED.

### Fixed: the molecular analytic gradient no longer silently falls back to bare-Z on an inline-primitive ECP (#574, 2026-09-03)

HIGH-severity silent wrong answer. `GradientOptions` carried only the
XML-library ECP fields (`ecp_centers` / `ecp_library`), so an SCF that ran
with **inline primitive** ECPs produced a gradient that differentiated a
different Hamiltonian than the energy: bare nuclear charges in the
nuclear-repulsion and `dV_ne/dR` pieces, no `dV_ECP/dR` term, and an
occupied block sized with the full electron count the SCF never filled.
There was no guard or warning.

The inline route is not a corner case: `attach_inline_ecp_options_from_
basis_sidecar` selects it for every ECP-paired basis whose per-element
cores have no bundled libecpint XML library -- vDZP, def2-mSVP, and
CRYSTAL/pob data -- and it leaves `ecp_centers` empty by construction.
Measured on CH4/vDZP (carbon off the Td centre, where the gradient does
not vanish by symmetry): analytic `+0.33306` vs finite-difference
`+0.17223` Ha/bohr, i.e. ~1.9x the true force.

* `GradientOptions` gains `ecp_primitive_blocks`,
  `ecp_primitive_centers`, `ecp_effective_charges` (per **atom**) and
  `ecp_total_ncore`, mirroring the SCF options structs. Inline blocks take
  precedence over `ecp_centers` / `ecp_library`, matching the selection the
  SCF drivers already make.
* New `compute_ecp_gradient_contribution_from_primitives` supplies
  `dV_ECP/dR` for the inline path. libecpint's first-derivative API works
  unchanged there: `init(deriv)` assigns ECP to atom ids purely by centre
  position and `compute_first_derivs` reads only those ids plus the
  primitive data, so `set_ecp_basis` supports derivatives exactly as
  `set_ecp_basis_from_library` does. Both paths now share one packing and
  contraction helper, so they cannot drift.
* `vibeqc.ase.VibeQC` copies the inline fields onto its `GradientOptions`,
  so `atoms.get_forces()` and `optimize=True` are correct on these bases.
* `run_neb`'s all-electron guard now also rejects inline ECP gradient
  options, which only became expressible with this change.
* Regression: `tests/test_ecp_gradient.py` pins analytic-vs-FD on the
  inline path to 1e-5 Ha/bohr, guards that vDZP really still takes the
  inline route, and pins that omitting the fields reproduces the bug.
* `docs/user_guide/ecp.md` documents the two routes, and corrects a stale
  claim that `compute_hessian_fd` copies ECP fields off the SCF options --
  it does not, and needs an explicit `gradient_options` on ECP systems.


### Changed: selected-CI defaults to the spin-unrestricted determinant basis (issue #107, 2026-09-03)

**Who this affects: every `method="selected_ci"` / `method="transcorrelated_ci"`
/ `solve_selected_ci` call that leaves `SelectedCIOptions.spin_restricted`
unset.** Its result moves. Maintainer decision on the issue (2026-08-27): fix
the unreachable-CAS class at the source rather than only diagnosing it.

`spin_restricted=True`, the old default, walks closed-shell determinants over
spatial orbitals excited by whole pairs. That basis is a closed subspace (no
open-shell configuration is representable) and, measured while fixing this,
its pair-move coupling is evaluated with the one-electron Brillouin formula
and vanishes for HF orbitals: on H2/STO-3G with both closed-shell determinants
in the space it returns the HF energy −1.1167143251 Ha where the same two
determinants in the unrestricted basis give the FCI energy −1.1372759436 Ha
(filed as **#639** and fixed in this release, see the entry above: the
restricted basis is now the seniority-zero Hamiltonian and its N2 ladder
reaches -108.9850687702 Ha over 20 determinants). On N2/cc-pVDZ CAS(6e,6o),
the deck behind the held SI selected-CI row, the default ladder was therefore
a flat line 62.3 mHa above the answer and labelled converged:

| `target_size` | old default (restricted) | new default (unrestricted) E_var | E_var + PT2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 6 | −108.9594672752 (ndet 6) | −109.0100354552 (ndet 11) | −109.0216461138 |
| 20 | −108.9594672752 (ndet 16) | −109.0186535276 (ndet 22) | −109.0217530446 |
| 50 | −108.9594672752 (ndet 16) | −109.0217155036 (ndet 57) | −109.0217768893 |
| 100 | −108.9594672752 (ndet 16) | −109.0217750033 (ndet 96) | −109.0217750033 |
| CASCI oracle | | −109.0217750033 | |

(N at 0 and 2.074 bohr, HF orbitals, vibe-qc 0.15.158 at main 65201761f,
`OMP_NUM_THREADS=1`; the unrestricted ladder is bit-identical before and after
this change.) The new regression asserts on the energy, not the determinant
count: monotone in the budget, bounded by the oracle computed in the same
test, and within 1 mHa of it from `target_size` 50 on
(`tests/test_solvers_selected_ci.py`); it fails at the parent with the flat
ladder above.

Two things make the restricted path honest for callers who still select it:

* **The threshold relaxation floor is one ulp of the total energy, not
  zero.** The floor-0 relaxation of 0b7d1aaf9 admitted ten determinants of
  weight 4e-28..4e-33 Ha (against a 2.4e-14 Ha ulp) whose coefficients are
  0.000000, so ndet grew 6 → 16 while the energy stayed bit-identical and the
  run then stopped on the `energy` criterion. A candidate below the energy's
  resolution cannot move the energy; it is not admitted, and the exhausted
  pool is reported as `stop_reason="space_exhausted"`. The unrestricted N2
  ladder admits nothing below 9e-10 Ha and is unchanged.
* **A restricted run whose pool emptied short of `target_size` reports
  `converged=False`** (with the existing warning, which since #639 names the
  DOCI limit). The closed subspace cannot certify that the configurations it omits
  are unimportant, so `converged=True` was the silent-wrong-answer label the
  issue was filed against. An unrestricted run that exhausts its connected
  space is exact in that space and stays `converged=True` (H2/STO-3G: the
  2-determinant exhausted space is the FCI energy, pinned).

The memory pre-flight (`vibeqc.memory`) reads the basis default from the
option class instead of repeating `True`. `docs/user_guide/non_hf_solvers.md`
states the default, the restricted caveat and the `stop_reason` semantics.
Lanes: `tests/test_solvers_selected_ci.py`, `tests/test_selected_casci.py`,
molecular-correlation.

### Fixed: the Ewald multi-k analytic gradient dropped the erfc Hartree interaction with the image cells (#575, 2026-09-03)

`tests/test_periodic_gradient_g1c.py::test_h2_box_each_kmesh_gradient_matches_own_energy_fd`
was red on `main`: H2/STO-3G in a 37.8 bohr box at kmesh [1,1,1], analytic
minus central-FD of the same SCF energy = -1.03e-5 Ha/bohr against 2e-6.
Measured, not inferred: the residual is FD-step independent
(-1.027/-1.031/-1.048e-5 at h = 5e-4/1e-3/2e-3, Richardson -1.026e-5),
scales as 1/L with the box (-1.303e-5 at 30 bohr, ratio 1.27 = 37.8/30)
while the energy itself is box-converged to 6e-8 Ha, and is identical at
kmesh [2,2,2] (the test asserts [1,1,1] first inside its mesh loop, so the
[2,2,2] leg had never run). A frozen-density per-term decomposition puts
the whole residual in the Hartree term (E_nn, T, V_ne, K and the Pulay
term each agree with their frozen-density FD to below 1e-7).

Mechanism: the Ewald multi-k SCF energies (RHF/RKS/UHF/UKS, and the RHF
single-Gamma molecular-limit branch) evaluate J with the exact analytic-FT
Hartree matrix (`v_G = 4 pi / G^2` over every `G != 0`; every image
interaction present, no real-space erfc pass). The shared corrected
multi-k derivative (`_compute_bipole_gradient_corrected_multi_k`)
differentiates that same J as J_SR(erfc, real space) + J_LR(erf,
reciprocal) + jellium, but its erfc image traversal ran over the density
support (`cutoff_bohr`). With the CRYSTAL default `alpha = 2.8 / V^(1/3)`
the nearest image sits at `erfc(2.8) = 7.5e-5` whatever the cell size, so
a box whose density support holds only the home cell dropped the image
erfc Hartree derivative: +1.026e-5 Ha/bohr measured directly (image erfc
Hartree energy +2.8e-5 Ha over 18 image cells inside r_alpha = 57.9 bohr),
which is the residual. Exchange is untouched: its image terms carry an AO
overlap across the cell length.

Fix: the Ewald consumers (`compute_gradient_periodic_rhf_multi_k`, its
single-Gamma branch, `compute_gradient_periodic_rks_multi_k`,
`compute_gradient_periodic_uks_multi_k`) pass the new
`j_sr_alpha_image_ball=True`, which sizes the lambda/sigma image
traversal of the J_SR derivative from alpha (`sqrt(-ln 1e-8)/alpha`, the
same rule #478 applied to the V_ne erfc image ball) with the density
support kept as the output domain. BIPOLE routes keep their own M5 padded
traversal (`sr_image_extent_bohr`) and their default path is unchanged.
After the fix analytic minus FD is -5.7e-8 (h = 1e-3) at both meshes and
both boxes; the 2e-6 tolerance is unchanged. The test docstring now
records that the two meshes' 8.27e-6 Ha/bohr *FD* difference (the
Sundararaman-Arias mesh-dependent exchange supercell) is real and
separate from this defect, which was mesh independent. A new
box-independence test pins the 1/L signature without finite differences.

### Added: TREXIO writer and round-trip reader (#573, 2026-09-03)

`run_job(..., trexio=True)` writes the converged molecular wavefunction as
a TREXIO file (Posenitskiy et al., J. Chem. Phys. 158, 174801 (2023))
through the optional `[trexio]` extra (BSD-3-Clause, imported lazily,
never bundled), with the HDF5 back end (`{output}.trexio.h5`) or the text
back end (`trexio_backend="text"`, a `{output}.trexio` directory), or to
an explicit path. The artefact is declared in the output plan, dispatched
as `("orbitals", "trexio")`, recorded in the `.system` manifest, announced
in the `.out`, and cites the TREXIO paper (new `posenitskiy2023trexio`
entry, `routes.libraries.trexio`) only when it is written. Written groups:
`metadata`, `nucleus`, `electron`, `basis` (Gaussian, spherical), `ao`,
`mo`, `ao_1e_int` (overlap, kinetic, potential_n_e, core_hamiltonian) and
`state`, for RHF/UHF/RKS/UKS and restricted open-shell results; not
written: `ecp` (an ECP run is refused rather than written with an
incomplete Hamiltonian), `rdm`, two-electron integrals, MO-basis
integrals, `cell`/`pbc`, determinants. `vibeqc.write_trexio` /
`vibeqc.read_trexio` expose the writer and a reader that rebuilds
`Molecule`, `BasisSet` and per-spin MO blocks. Conventions (`prim_factor`
as the axial-primitive norm reproducing the specification's own worked
example, `coefficient = c_eff / prim_factor`, `shell_factor = 1`,
`ao.normalization = 1`, TREXIO spherical order `0, +1, -1, ...`) are pinned
by an exact in-process round trip (`tests/test_output_trexio.py`) and by
an out-of-process PySCF energy rebuild from the stored MOs
(`examples/regression/runner_trexio_pyscf.py`). New user-guide page
`docs/user_guide/trexio.md`; `docs/features.md` and `docs/license.md`
rows.

### Fixed: a stability analysis with no verdict is no longer treated as a clean bill of health (issue #566, 2026-08-29)

`internal_instability` is the fail-closed conjunction
`stability_checked && converged && lambda < -tol`. `False` therefore means
*either* certified-stable *or* no verdict at all — a run whose stability
Davidson exhausted its budget carries exactly the value a verified-stable run
carries. Two consumers keyed on it alone:

* **The multi-guess filter** (`python/vibeqc/__init__.py`, both the UHF and UKS
  sites) skipped only genuinely-unstable seeds, so an unexamined alternate won
  the comparison on energy and was returned as the answer.
* **The loud instability warning** (`python/vibeqc/runner.py`) stayed silent
  for a no-verdict run. Only the `.out` carried the UNVERIFIED line, so a
  consumer reading warnings could not tell the two apart.

Both now distinguish three states. The multi-guess filter sets aside a seed
that was examined and returned no verdict, and the runner emits a distinct
`scf_stability_unverified` warning naming the unverified analysis rather than
claiming instability it cannot demonstrate.

`stability_checked` is what makes this safe: it is also `False` when the
analysis was never requested, so keying on
`stability_analysis_converged` alone would have set aside *every* seed and
silently disabled multi-guess selection. That case is pinned by its own test.

### Fixed: the analytic RKS/UKS gradient refuses or falls back when a functional's terms are missing (#571, 2026-09-03)

`cpp/src/gradient.cpp` differentiates exact exchange through the global
fraction `Functional.hf_exchange_fraction()` only (= `cam_alpha` for a
range-separated hybrid); it carries neither the erf-attenuated long-range
exchange term `cam_beta * dK_erf(omega)/dR` that `rks.cpp` / `uks.cpp`
include in the energy, nor the VV10 nonlocal correlation gradient
(Vydrov and Van Voorhis, J. Chem. Phys. 133, 244103 (2010)). Measured on a
bent O/H/H molecule, STO-3G, `OMP_NUM_THREADS=1`, analytic provider gradient
against the optimizer's own full-energy central finite differences (step
0.005 bohr), max |analytic - FD| in Ha/bohr with max |g| about 0.1: pbe
2.1e-6 (the noise floor), hse06 5.6e-3, vv10 7.0e-4, wb97x-v 5.6e-2.
`geomopt/providers.py`, `optimize_molecule`, `optimize_molecule_brent` and
the ASE calculator behind `run_job(optimize=True)` handed that partial
gradient to the optimizer for every functional, so
`run_job(method="rks", functional="wb97x-v", optimize=True)` optimized on
a wrong surface silently while `docs/features.md` already said RSH
analytic gradients were queued.

* New `vibeqc.functional_gradient_terms_missing(functional)` (module
  `vibeqc.gradient_terms`) names the omitted terms from the C++
  `Functional` predicates `is_range_separated` / `needs_vv10`; empty for
  LDA, GGA, meta-GGA and global hybrids.
* `vibeqc.compute_gradient_rks` / `compute_gradient_uks` raise
  `NotImplementedError` naming the terms and the FD route for such a
  `result.functional`; `allow_incomplete=True` opts into the partial
  gradient. `molecular_optimize._compute_molecular_gradient` (the direct
  C++ dispatch NEB uses) refuses the same way, so NEB, the FD Hessian /
  frequencies, the analytic-Hessian skeletons and CPCM gradients fail
  closed instead of returning a wrong number.
* All three molecular optimizers and the `geomopt` provider share one
  decision (`_mean_field_gradient_terms_missing`, resolving the functional
  exactly as `_run_molecular_scf` does) and walk the full-energy
  central-FD surface for these functionals;
  `MolecularSCFProvider.has_analytic_gradient` is now truthful and
  `.missing_gradient_terms` lists the terms. The `VibeQC` ASE calculator
  does the same on its RKS/UKS force branch. One `Note:` line in the `.out`
  names the omitted terms and the FD step (`vibeqc.output.write`).
* After the fix the provider gradient for wb97x-v agrees with an
  independent full-energy FD gradient to the 1e-5 gate, the pbe control is
  unchanged (same route, feature off), and
  `run_job(functional="wb97x-v", optimize=True)` converges to a stationary
  point of the full energy and reports the fallback.
* Regression: `tests/test_gradient_missing_terms.py` (blocking T1,
  molecular-scf-dft lane). Docs: `docs/features.md`,
  `docs/user_guide/functionals.md`, `docs/user_guide/geometry_optimization.md`.
  The analytic RSH-exchange and VV10 gradient terms are a separate feature;
  no citation entry is new (the functionals' entries and routes exist).

`docs/features.md` previously listed only MSINDO, GFN2-xTB and MACE. The

### Changed: the wired AICCM routes record and cite what they execute (AICCM front door M0, #562, 2026-09-02)

First milestone of `handovers/HANDOVER_AICCM_STANDARD_METHOD.md`, a records
and citations change with no numerical effect.

* The real-Gamma selector's recorded value is now `real-gamma`, the
  front-door variant name: `jk_method_requested` / `_resolved` / `_executed`
  in the `.system` manifest, the `.out` job label and progress line, and the
  QVF `job_spec` all read `real-gamma` instead of `aiccm2026dev-a-real-gamma`,
  a string the resolver itself rejected as input because the A prefix names
  the union-and-weight construction (D89/D90). That spelling and
  `aiccm2026dev-a-direct` stay rejected inputs; `real-gamma` and `real_gamma`
  resolve as before. The `.out` "J/K method" line no longer opens with the
  A-prefixed label; it still ends in `experimental`.
* Every job dispatched through an AICCM selector writes
  `[run].method_status = "experimental"` into `.system` from job start (a
  dry-run, a crashed and a completed manifest all carry it). The real-Gamma
  route keeps its older `experimental_route = true` key for one release; the
  new key is the uniform marker. Documented in
  `docs/user_guide/output_files.md`.
* `run_periodic_job(jk_method="real-gamma")` passed the bare SCF method to
  the citation collector, so its references block read as a plain periodic
  RHF/RKS. It now fires the new `routes.methods` key `real-gamma` (the CCM
  lineage, Bredow-Geudtner-Jug 2001 and Peintinger-Bredow 2014), the GDF
  stack its fold cderi executes (`uses_gdf`, Sun-Berkelbach 2017), and the
  Pulay / Hellmann-Feynman force citations for `optimize=True`
  (`uses_gradient`). A `neutral-bloch` row with the same lineage pair is
  pre-positioned for the M1 variant dispatch and does not fire yet, because
  the `neutral-bloch` / `aiccm-ri` aliases still mean plain GDF. The chi
  line's bare key, claimed in the database as firing, is now pinned end to
  end.
* Tests: `tests/test_feature_citation_end_to_end.py` (real-Gamma single
  point, chi), `tests/test_periodic_feature_input_guards.py` (selector value,
  dry-run manifests of both arms plus a plain-GDF negative control, the
  selector set contract), `tests/test_citations.py` (the two rows and their
  R1 identity), and the moved pins in `tests/test_ccm_route.py`,
  `tests/test_periodic_ccm_real_gamma_adapter.py` (which also gains the
  relaxation's gradient citation) and `tests/test_periodic_aiccm2026dev_b.py`.


### Documentation: the method matrix names SKALA-1.1 and the solvation stack (2026-09-03)

`docs/features.md` now carries the `skala-1.1` functional in the XC table and a
Solvation section (CPCM / COSMO, the solvent analytic gradient, COSMO-RS, and
the gated method families). Both shipped without a matrix row (SKALA in
`aa7e1f9fe`, COSMO-RS in #558); the matrix is a release artefact and moves with
the route (CLAUDE.md § 5).

### Added: exact integer addressing for regular k-meshes (2026-09-02)

`cpp/include/vibeqc/kmesh_address.hpp` + `cpp/src/kmesh_address.cpp` add
`RegularKMesh`, the integer layer the periodic correlated methods will do
their crystal-momentum bookkeeping on. A mesh point is represented by its
*doubled* modular address `a_d = 2 m_d + s_d (mod 2 N_d)`, so a shifted grid
is representable exactly and momentum algebra -- negation, the transfer
momentum `q = k_j - k_i`, and the conserved fourth index `k_b` with
`k_i - k_a + k_j = k_b + G` -- is integer arithmetic with no tolerance and no
float-keyed nearest-neighbour matching. Every reduction can return the exact
reciprocal-lattice vector `G` it wrapped by. k-point addresses and
transfer-momentum addresses are separate C++ types: on a shifted mesh their
parities differ, so substituting one for the other names a point off the grid.

Conserved-index lookup is on demand and O(1) in both time and memory. There
is deliberately no `N_k^3` table anywhere in the API: at the project
reference mesh `(8,8,8)` that is 512^3 entries, over a gigabyte, to store a
number three integer divisions produce on the spot.

* `monkhorst_pack` now builds its unreduced grid through this module. **No
  k-point moved.** `(2 m + s) / (2 N)` is the same IEEE double as the
  historical `(m + s/2) / N` -- numerator and denominator are both exactly
  twice the old ones, every operand is exactly representable, and division is
  correctly rounded -- and the test asserts that bitwise rather than within a
  tolerance, because the tree's periodic reference values were measured
  against the old expression.
* Two inputs `bloch.hpp` only ever documented are now refused rather than
  silently building a different grid: an `is_shift` component outside
  `{0, 1}` (which used to give `(m + 1)/N` for a shift of 2), and a division
  product that overflows the point count (which used to wrap an `int`). The
  Python layer already screened the first, so no caller in the tree changes
  behaviour. The symmetry-reduced branch still routes through spglib and is
  untouched.
* Scope: addressing only. No symmetry, no AO sewing, no GDF, no SCF, no
  coupled cluster. The Python surface is a diagnostic binding
  (`_vibeqc_core._RegularKMesh`), not re-exported and not an API.

### Fixed: the Monkhorst-Pack half-step comment named the wrong parity (2026-09-02)

`bloch.hpp` described `is_shift[i] = 1` as "the classical Monkhorst-Pack
offset for odd meshes" and `crystal.hpp` called it the "Monkhorst-Pack
odd-mesh convention". Both had it backwards. Monkhorst & Pack, Phys. Rev. B
13, 5188 (1976), Eq. (3) places the classical points at
`u_r = (2r - q - 1)/(2q)`: for **odd** `q` that set contains 0, so the
classical mesh is already Gamma-centred and equals `is_shift = 0`; only for
**even** `q` does it sit half a step off Gamma and equal `is_shift = 1`.

Comments only, no behaviour change -- and the user-facing documentation
(`docs/user_guide/k_points.md`, `docs/user_guide/multi_k_scf.md`,
`docs/tutorial/lih_pob_tzvp_solid_state.md`) already said it correctly, so
the reversed claim was confined to the two C++ headers a chat reads before
touching the mesh. `tests/test_kmesh_address.py` now pins the fact itself
against Eq. (3) in exact rational arithmetic, for odd and even meshes, so
the comment cannot drift back.

### Fixed: the compact multi-k UKS/ROKS GPW driver streams its Bloch AO tables like the closed-shell one (issue #89, 2026-09-02)

`d17aae954` bounded the closed-shell compact multi-k GPW route (retain the
all-k Bloch AO cache only below 1 GiB, otherwise stream 64 MiB point
batches) and dropped the P16 NiO estimate from 468 GiB to 1.19 GiB, but
left the open-shell driver -- the one the AFM NiO / DFT+U target actually
runs -- holding one `(n_grid, n_ao)` complex table per k-point
unconditionally; the 2026-08-28 re-test still estimated it at 702.7 GiB
(232 AOs, 128^3 grid, 64 k). `run_periodic_uks_gpw_multi_k` (and the ROKS
driver that shares it) now takes the same decision as the RKS driver,
reading `periodic_gapw_j._COMPACT_BLOCH_AO_CACHE_BYTES` at call time so
one setting governs both: below the target the cache is retained, above it
the per-spin density collocation and the per-k local-potential projections
stream bounded point batches (`_collocate_bloch_density_streaming`,
`_project_potential_to_bloch_ao_streaming`), and the meta-GGA spectral
`tau` and `v_tau` projections retain one complete k table at a time. The
ROKS post-SCF rebuild uses the same path. `estimate_periodic_gpw_gapw`
charges the open-shell compact route the bounded batch model (P16 NiO:
1.55 GiB open shell, 1.19 GiB closed shell). Numerics are unchanged: the
streamed and cached UKS energies agree to 1e-10 on the skewed H2 (2,1,1)
control for PBE and for a meta-GGA.

Regression: `tests/test_memory.py`
(`test_periodic_gpw_p16_compact_bloch_storage_is_kmesh_bounded` now
parametrised over both spin branches), `tests/test_periodic_gpw_compact_multik.py`
(`test_compact_multik_uks_batches_bloch_ao_grid`: every C++ AO evaluation of
a forced-streaming UKS run is bounded by the batch target;
`test_compact_multik_uks_streamed_matches_cached`: cached vs streamed UKS
PBE and TPSS energies and per-k orbital energies agree to 1e-10). Re-pinned
in the same file: `test_periodic_gpw_gapw_estimate_charges_route_and_kmesh`
asserted the dense `GPW compact multi-k Bloch AO tables` /
`GPW meta-GGA AO-gradient scratch` pair on the open-shell compact case and
now asserts the bounded `... Bloch AO cache` /
`... compact multi-k meta-GGA AO/FFT scratch` pair, plus the absence of the
two it replaced. Docs: `docs/user_guide/gapw.md`.

## [v0.15.158] - 2026-09-02 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Fixed: `import vibeqc` under the documentation build's mocked core (issue #559, 2026-09-02)

The SKALA-1.1 adapter (`aa7e1f9fe`) registers its immutable functional names
with the native core at import time. The docs build runs Sphinx with
`autodoc_mock_imports=vibeqc._vibeqc_core`, so the registry query answered a
mock stand-in instead of `None` or a record; the strict adoption check read
that as a registration collision, `import vibeqc` raised, and the v0.15.158
release-gate `docs-build` job was red (pipeline 4997). `vibeqc/__init__.py`
now skips the registration when the core carries Sphinx's `__sphinx_mock__`
marker and leaves the callback unset. A real core that cannot satisfy
registration still fails loudly on import, deliberately: a stale or mismatched
native extension must not import quietly. Guarded by
`tests/test_skala_adapter.py::test_import_survives_sphinx_autodoc_mocked_core`,
which imports the package in a subprocess under a Sphinx-shaped mock module.

### Changed: the chi-CCM line and the real-Gamma runner adapter live in the periodic subpackage (layout, 2026-09-02)

The Gamma-CCM line (`aiccm2026dev-a`) was a proper subpackage,
`vibeqc.periodic.ccm`, while its comparator, the chi-CCM line
(`aiccm2026dev-b`), was seven flat modules beside `banner.py` at the package
root, and the `jk_method="real-gamma"` runner adapter was an eighth. The seven
chi modules are now the sibling subpackage `vibeqc.periodic.chi`
(`scf`, `gradient`, `localization`, `pno`, `posthf`, `properties`, `symmetry`;
the package docstring maps each to the `periodic_aiccm2026dev_b*.py` file it
was), and the adapter is `vibeqc.periodic.ccm.real_gamma_runner`, with the
Gamma line it wraps. `vibeqc.periodic.ccm` itself is untouched.

This is a layout change and nothing else. The two constructions stay
separately implemented, `chi` still imports nothing from `ccm` (now a
structural fact, since they are siblings), and no duplication between the
lines was touched: the PNO stack, occupied localization, and the minimum-image
predicate are a separate proposal (`handovers/HANDOVER_AICCM_LAYOUT_MERGE.md`
§ 8). Every public `vibeqc.<symbol>` is unchanged and its list is byte-identical
before and after; what changes is the deep import path, so
`from vibeqc.periodic_aiccm2026dev_b_posthf import ...` becomes
`from vibeqc.periodic.chi.posthf import ...`, and the seven old module names
are no longer attributes of `vibeqc`. The route support matrix, the Gamma
and chi user guides, the experimental catalog, the roadmap, and the
test-gate lane trigger paths name the new locations. Second and last increment
of the layout merge; the harness moved in the first.


### Added: COSMO-RS / COSMOSPACE thermodynamics and the conductor-surface record (issue #558, 2026-09-02)

vibe-qc can now compute sigma profiles, sigma potentials, chemical potentials,
activity coefficients, partition coefficients and solvation free energies.

`vibeqc.solvation.surface.ConductorSurface` is the layer boundary: segments with
areas, normals, ownership and screening charge density, plus the cavity recipe
and full provenance, serialisable and round-tripping deterministically.
`vibeqc.solvation.cosmors` consumes it and **never sees a Hamiltonian, basis or
density**, so any electronic method that can produce a conductor surface gets
COSMO-RS for free.

Implemented from Klamt 1995 (`10.1021/j100007a062`) and Klamt, Jonas, Bürger &
Lohrenz 1998 (`10.1021/jp980017s`): sigma averaging (eq. 11) and the correlation
descriptor (eq. 14), sigma profiles and mixtures (eq. 16), the misfit energy with
its correlation term (eq. 7/26), the hydrogen-bond term (eq. 22), the
self-consistent sigma potential in both the one-dimensional form (eq. 18) and the
segment-sum form that carries the second descriptor (eq. 23-25), chemical
potentials (eq. 19/20), the gas-phase reference (eq. 21) and the combinatorial
term (eq. 30). The `klamt1998` parameterization is the published section 5.1 set.

The exact conductor limit landed with #548 makes this possible: `epsilon = inf`
gives `f = 1` exactly, which is the ideally screened molecule the whole theory
starts from.

**Measured, not asserted.** vibe-qc's cavity is not the one the 1998 constants
were fitted on. On water, the shipped cavity gives 48.69 Å² and Klamt's *own*
fitted radii give 42.80 Å², against the 24.7 Å² of Klamt 1995 Table 1. Our areas
were checked against an independent Monte Carlo integration of the
union-of-spheres surface and agree to about 2 % (36.96/43.57/49.62 Å² for the
three radius sets), so the cavity is correct for its definition and the
difference is one of construction, not a defect. Consequently the 1998 constants
do not transfer quantitatively, `Parameterization.fitted_protocol` records the
protocol they came from (`dmol/bpw91/dnp/cosmo-inf/nspa92`), and
`SurfaceProvenance` records the protocol a surface actually has, so the pair is
always reportable rather than assumed. Quantitative validation against FreeSolv
is separate and still to be done.

### Fixed: the COSMO citation note credited Klamt with the CPCM factor

`klamt_schuurmann_cosmo_1993`'s note read "the f(ε) = (ε−1)/ε scaling vibe-qc's
CPCM uses". That factor is the `x = 0` member due to Cossi 2003; Klamt's is
`(ε−1)/(ε+1/2)`. Corrected, and the note now records what the paper actually
establishes: the family `f(ε) = (ε−1)/(ε+x)` and that `f(ε)` enters the screening
energy and its gradient together.
### Fixed: the MS-CASPT2 SA-gradient invariance test asked the finite difference for precision it cannot deliver (issue #553, 2026-08-29)

`test_ms_gradient_sa_matches_direct` was red on `main`, failing translational
invariance at `1.5840662115351734e-12` against a `1e-12` absolute ceiling —
bit-identical across runs, rebases and rebuilds.

The MS-CASPT2 correlation gradient on this path is finite-difference derived
(`_ms_caspt2_grad.fd_geom`, default 1e-3 bohr, central), so an absolute 1e-12
bound on the sum of two ~6.3e-3 Ha/bohr components was asking for ~2.5e-10
relative precision. The bound is now stated relative to the gradient
magnitude.

**Whether this was noise or a real one-sided term in the MS Lagrangian was
measured, not assumed** — the issue specifically warned against loosening the
number without checking. Sweeping the step:

| `fd_geom` | \|g0z + g1z\| |
|---|---|
| 1e-2 | 7.5e-14 |
| 3e-3 | 4.0e-13 |
| 1e-3 (default) | 1.4e-12 |
| 3e-4 | **exactly 0.0** |
| 1e-4 | 1.2e-11 |

The residual vanishes exactly at one step and returns at its neighbours, and
grows as the step shrinks — the ~ε/h signature of roundoff-dominated finite
differencing. A genuine one-sided term would be step-independent. No code
change was warranted, and none was made.

The replacement bound (`1e-8 × |g|max`) sits ~39× above the residual at the
default step, holds at every step in the sweep, and still catches a real
invariance break down to 1e-7 relative. The x and y bounds keep their absolute
1e-12: those are structurally zero by symmetry, not finite-differenced. The
sibling test above already bounded the same invariant at 1e-10 absolute.

### Changed: the AICCM-2026 harness lives under `studies/aiccm-2026/` (layout, 2026-09-02)

`aiccm-2026/` at the repository root was the one per-topic harness not under
`studies/`, where `aiccm-real-gamma`, `seccm-bulk3d`, `embedded-cluster-cas`
and the others already live. It is now `studies/aiccm-2026/`, content
unchanged: the scripts stay one self-contained directory with bare sibling
imports (`import probe_host`), so how they run is unchanged except for the
path. Four helpers that derived a location from their own position are
re-rooted one level deeper, because each would otherwise have failed silently
rather than loudly: `run.sh`'s own-checkout venv candidate (it would have
fallen through to a host deployment and computed with the wrong tree),
`curate.py`'s qc-input-library sibling lookup, `make_crystal_jobs.py`'s
repo-relative payload paths, and `make_jobs_b.py`, which now emits
`-d studies/aiccm-2026/` when run from a checkout as README_B.md instructs
while a copy outside a checkout keeps self-deriving its directory name. The
chi comparison producer's D77 source-binding paths follow the move, so an
`--expected-source-sha` older than this change no longer binds; payload and
source must agree, as before. Tests, docs, handovers, the test-gate lane
trigger paths, and two library comments name the new path; CHANGELOG history
is left as written. First of the two layout increments in
`handovers/HANDOVER_AICCM_LAYOUT_MERGE.md`; the library modules follow.

### Changed: one reaction-field step, shared by every method (issue #554, 2026-09-02)

The five lines that turn a solute density into screened surface charges, a
Hamiltonian contribution and an energy split existed twice: inside
`driver.run_cpcm_scf`'s macro-iteration for Gaussian HF/DFT, and inside
`msindo_cosmo._cosmo_reaction_field` for MSINDO, against the same
`SolutePotentialProvider` protocol. Two copies of one equation is the same
failure shape as two copies of one constant (#546, #548), one level up: the
`E_pol = ½ qᵀV` convention and the core/electronic split were each written
twice, and nothing detected a change to only one.

New `vibeqc.solvation.engine` holds the single implementation. Both routes call
it, and `ReactionField` carries `q`, the decomposed `V_elec`/`V_core`/`V_total`,
the Fock contribution and the energy split, which is what the handover's result
contract requires and what Direct COSMO-RS will consume.

The `A` solve is **injected**, so callers keep their own factorization: the
Gaussian route pre-factors once per geometry and reuses the LU across
macro-iterations, MSINDO keeps its fused C++ kernel, and the step does not need
to know which. `ReactionField.with_charges` lets an outer accelerator apply an
extrapolated `q` while reusing the potentials, so q-DIIS costs one Fock scatter
and no second ESP pass.

**Deliberately not unified:** the outer convergence strategy. Gaussian
macro-iterates an outer `q` loop around a full inner SCF with q-DIIS and a
shifted-DIIS warm start; MSINDO folds the field into a single SCF, updating `q`
at every Fock build. Those are different, legitimate strategies over the same
step, and collapsing them would change converged iterate paths for no physical
gain.

No number moves: MSINDO is byte-identical across all four measured cases, and
the Gaussian route agrees to 4.3e-14, which is exactly its own measured
run-to-run noise floor. Re-running the *same* build twice moves 25 of 56 tracked
quantities by up to 4.263e-14 (threaded SCF reductions), including the
gas-phase reference energy this change cannot touch, so byte equality was never
achievable there for any change.

### Fixed: the periodic GDF preflight sizes the auxiliary set the driver allocates (issue #92, 2026-09-02)

`aux_basis=None` (the runner's `<auto>`) is resolved by every GDF driver as
`default_aux_for(basis.name)` before the cderi build, but the preflight
fell back to `3 x n_ao` for it. On the P05 space-group demonstration -- NaCl
conventional cell, 8 atoms, def2-SVP (132 AOs), KRHF (4,4,4) -- that is 396
against the 960 def2-svp-jkfit functions actually built, so the dense
4096-pair Lpq cache was reported at 452 GB while the allocation is
1096 GB: a 500 GB node would have accepted a 1.1 TB build, and the filed
"1225 GB guard" figure was the honest number of its day.
`_periodic_gdf_aux_basis_size` now resolves the default aux exactly as the
drivers do (the `3 x n_ao` floor remains only for a basis with no
registered default, where the driver raises too).

The re-derivation also settles the demonstration itself: the deck passes
no symmetry kwargs, so it never engaged the reduction it exists to show.
With `symmetry='attach', symmetry_reduce_k=True` (Fm-3m, n_IBZ = 10 at
(4,4,4)) the run is 171 GB of Lpq + 45.5 GB of AO-pair FT bundle -- a site_j
or site_f job -- and the primitive cell is 0.9 GB reduced / 7 GB full.
The estimate was right in kind and short by 2.4x in the aux dimension; no
route change is needed.

Regression: `tests/test_periodic_gdf_memory_preflight.py`
(`TestAuxDimensionResolution`: the `<auto>` aux dimension equals the
driver's `make_aux_basis_set(default_aux_for(...))` count and exceeds the
old floor; the P05 deck is > 1 TB unreduced, exactly 6.4x smaller in the
wedge, and 250-450 GB reduced).

### Changed: one dielectric screening factor, carried instead of re-derived (issues #548, #549, 2026-09-02)

`f(e)` was written out independently in **four** places: the Python
`dielectric_factor`, the C++ `cpcm_dielectric_factor`, the solvation gradient
(hard-coded `variant="cpcm"`, the #546 wrong answer), and by hand inside the C++
MSINDO reaction field, in a header that did not even include
`solvation_cpcm.hpp`. Nothing pinned any two of them equal, and a drift is
silent because every path still yields a smooth plausible number.

**CPCM and COSMO are not two formulas.** Klamt & Schüürmann 1993 p. 800 gives
the family they are both points of: `f(ε) = (ε−1)/(ε+x)` with `x` in 0 to 2.
CPCM is `x = 0`, COSMO is `x = 1/2` (p. 801). The new
`vibeqc.solvation.screening` writes that once, with a per-variant `x`, so a new
screening variant is a table entry rather than a code branch, and one test pins
the Python and C++ evaluations **bitwise** equal across the whole family, the
way `test_smearing_frontier_resolution.py` pins its Python threshold to the C++
twin. Neither can now be changed alone.

`ScreeningModel` (variant, epsilon, x, f) is built once per solve and carried on
`SolventResult.screening`. Consumers read `f` off it; a consumer that cannot
re-derive cannot re-derive wrongly, which is exactly how #546 happened.
`epsilon = inf` now returns exactly 1 rather than the closed form's NaN, the
conductor limit COSMO is derived from.

**Removed special case:** the C++ MSINDO reaction field baked the COSMO form in,
so MSINDO was structurally the one route that could not take CPCM screening even
though the generic layer supports both. It now calls the shared helper and
accepts a `variant`, defaulting to `"cosmo"`; `msindo_cosmo(..., variant=...)`
exposes it. MSINDO energies are unchanged at the default.

### Fixed: the gas-phase gradient no longer rejects its own uniform return type (issue #549)

`run_cpcm_scf(..., solvent="vacuum")` returns a `SolventResult` through
`_gas_phase_solvent_result`, whose whole purpose is to give downstream code one
shape. Passing it to the public `cpcm_gradient` raised
`ValueError: epsilon must be > 1`. With `q` identically zero the reaction field
contributes exactly nothing, so the answer is the gas-phase analytic gradient,
and that is now what comes back. Gas phase is represented as *absent* screening
(`SolventResult.screening is None`) rather than an out-of-range dielectric.

Not reachable from `run_job(..., optimize=True)`, which short-circuits gas phase
before the ASE calculator sees a `solvent_result`; reachable by composing the two
public names. Pre-existing, not introduced by #546.

### Fixed: COSMO analytic gradients screen with the factor that built the charges (issue #546, 2026-09-02)

`vibeqc.solvation.gradient.cpcm_gradient` computed the cavity term's dielectric
screening factor as `dielectric_factor(epsilon, variant="cpcm")`, a hard-coded
literal, while `run_cpcm_scf` builds the apparent surface charges with
`variant=SolventModel.variant`. A `variant="cosmo"` run therefore
**differentiated a different energy than it reported.**

vibe-qc stores the scaled charge `q = f q0` with `q0 = -A⁻¹V`, so the
stationary derivative of `E_pol = ½ qᵀV` is

    dE_pol = qᵀ dV + (1/(2f)) qᵀ (dA) q

and the `f` in the cavity term is fixed by the solve; it is not a free choice.
Klamt & Schüürmann 1993 (doi:10.1039/P29930000799) p. 801 introduces
`f(ε) = (ε−1)/(ε+½)` "into the expressions for the screening energy *and its
gradient*", one factor in both; their eq. (13) with `q = f q*` reproduces the
scaled form term for term.

The two factors diverge as ε falls, so nonpolar solvents were worst. On
displaced water/STO-3G in benzene (ε = 2.27) the analytic-vs-central-FD
residual **plateaued** at 4.99e-05 Ha/bohr across h = 4e-3/2e-3/1e-3, the
signature of a systematic error rather than FD truncation, and now converges O(h²)
to 4.70e-07, matching the unaffected CPCM control. The cavity contribution
alone was 18.1 % wrong at benzene and 0.6 % wrong at water. Reachable from
`run_job(solvent={"epsilon": …, "variant": "cosmo"}, optimize=True)`, whose
forces route through the ASE calculator, so COSMO geometry optimization walked
an inconsistent gradient.

**CPCM is byte-unchanged**: the hard-coded literal happened to be correct for
the default variant, which is why the pre-existing water FD test passed and
never exercised the defect.

The screening factor is now read off the result via the new
`_screening_factor(solvent_result)`, which carries the derivation and the
citation at the one site that owns it.

### Changed: solvation gets its own test lane

`tests/test_solvation*.py` was matched only by the `full-fast` and
`slow-nightly` aggregates, both of which have empty `trigger_paths` and are
reserved by `CLAUDE.md` § 14. No lane carried a `python/vibeqc/solvation/**`
trigger, so a solvation change selected only `release-core-cheap`, which runs
`tests/test_release_sentinels.py` and no solvation test at all. That is why
#546 shipped and stayed shipped. A `solvation` lane now owns the cavity,
apparent-surface-charge solve, screening variants, reaction-field
macro-iteration, gradients, and the provider seam, triggered by
`python/vibeqc/solvation/**` and the MSINDO COSMO/GEPOL modules.


### Added: the T = 0 global-Aufbau fill reports frontiers it cannot resolve (issue #543, 2026-09-02)

`vibeqc.smearing.apply._global_aufbau_with_mu` is the Python twin of the C++
`compute_closed_shell_kpoint_occupations` fixed under #434 — same pooled sort,
same `256·eps·energy_scale` roundoff grouping, same fill/cut/fractional branch
structure. It backs the ab-initio multi-k routes (`periodic_rhf_gdf`,
`periodic_k_gdf`, `periodic_gapw_augment`), and it carried the same defect.

When the occupied/empty boundary falls between two states closer than the fill
can resolve, the fill **cuts** them. Which one is "lower" is then decided by
last-ulp arithmetic, so an entire electron moves between k-points with a
rounding difference that varies between hosts — while the SCF still reports
convergence. At the exact 3.2e-07 Ha splitting issue #424 measured, flipping
the *sign* of the splitting moves the electron from one k-point to the other
and both fills report success.

New `vibeqc.smearing.unresolved_frontier_cut(eps_per_k, occupations_per_k)`
returns the measured gap when a T = 0 fill cut an unresolvable frontier, and
`None` otherwise — covering a real gap, an equalized fractional Fermi group,
and a completely empty or filled space. `SmearingResult` records
`frontier_cut_unresolved` and `frontier_gap`.

**It reports; it does not refuse.** These fills run inside SCF loops, so
raising would abort a run whose *intermediate* iterate transits a
near-degenerate frontier but whose *converged* frontier is well gapped — the
same reason the C++ twin records instead of throwing. The predicate is
deliberately stateless over the realised occupations, so each caller decides
*when* to ask; ask on the accepted spectrum.

`MIN_RESOLVABLE_FRONTIER_GAP` (1e-6 Ha) is the Python half of a value
duplicated in C++ as `KPointOccupationOptions::min_resolvable_frontier_gap`.
The two fills are independent implementations of one convention, so
`tests/test_smearing_frontier_resolution.py` pins them **equal mechanically** —
neither can be changed without the other failing.

Behaviour is otherwise unchanged: no occupation, energy or fermi level moves.

### Fixed: BIPOLE Gamma wide cells fail before becoming origin-only clusters (issue #429, stage 1; 2026-09-02)

The high-level Gaussian BIPOLE Gamma entry point now refuses RHF, RKS, UHF,
and UKS jobs when either executed direct-space image set contains only the
home cell. `run_periodic_job` performs the check after primitive-cell
resolution but before creating an output directory, manifest, writer, or SCF:
the interaction list uses the effective BIPOLE operator cutoff, while the
nuclear list uses the real-space radius actually executed after the neutral
Ewald clamp and the alpha/tolerance growth. The latter distinction matters:
an origin-only raw nuclear keyword can still be supported when the Ewald
preflight grows its private one-electron radius to include images. Non-finite
BIPOLE cutoff keywords now fail at the same boundary instead of passing the
old `<= 0` check.

This is deliberately a bounded containment milestone, not the pair-complete
rewrite in issue #429. True multi-k jobs are unchanged, no energy reference is
repinned, and route-specific GDF, RIJCOSX, GPW/GAPW, restricted-open-shell
BIPOLE, AICCM/CCM, low-dimensional, and standalone-driver contracts remain for
their own image-resolution audits. Their molecular-limit, Ewald, or finite-
torus semantics cannot be inferred from a flat 15/25-bohr runner check.

### Added: compact χ translation-pair plan for the MgO 8 x 8 x 8 scaling target (D123, 2026-09-02)

`build_translation_pair_plan(n_bands, mesh)` now represents every unordered
occupied pair on a finite translation group by one exact representative under
simultaneous translation. It records the orbit multiplicity and therefore
handles the half-weight same-band antipodal pairs that occur on even meshes,
without storing placed orbit members or a dense translation-permutation
table. Its canonical immutable arrays are detached from caller buffers and
bound to a deterministic SHA-256 fingerprint.

For the planned primitive-cell MgO `(8, 8, 8)` workload with four active
occupied bands per cell, 2,098,176 placed pairs reduce to 4,112 compact rows:
four home diagonals, 28 nonzero two-torsion rows with weight one half, and
4,080 ordinary rows. The complete payload is 197,376 bytes and its weighted
per-cell census is exactly 4,098. Small odd, even, and anisotropic meshes are
pinned against the existing full-orbit oracle.

This is a workload-plan milestone, not reduced-scaling correlation. It changes
no SCF or post-HF energy, enables no screening, and is not yet consumed by the
local solver. The 8-cubed DLPNO-CCSD(T) target still requires covariant
occupied localization, minimum-image PAO and auxiliary domains, streamed
charge-constrained local RI, representative MP2/CCSD/triples execution, and
distributed CPU/GPU resource qualification.

### Fixed: a T = 0 k-point fill cut frontiers it could not resolve, and reported success (issue #434, 2026-09-02)

At T = 0 with hard Aufbau on a k-point mesh, a frontier pair split by more
than the roundoff-equality tolerance but far less than a real gap was **cut**
by the global fill: the lower state filled, the upper left empty. Which of the
two counted as lower was decided by last-ulp arithmetic, so an entire electron
moved between k-points with a rounding difference — and the run reported
convergence either way. Issue #424 documented exactly this as cross-host
`converged=True at n_iter=1` versus `converged=False at n_iter=500` branch
flips on one shared binary.

`KPointOccupationResult` now records `frontier_cut_unresolved` and the measured
`frontier_gap`, and the two drivers that can reach the multi-k T = 0 path —
`run_scc_dftb_kpoints` and `run_dftb0_kpoints` — **fail closed** rather than
return a raced occupation. The refusal names the measured gap in Ha and eV, the
tolerance it failed, the remedy (`smearing_temperature`), and the explicit
opt-out. `KPointOccupationOptions.min_resolvable_frontier_gap` (default 1e-6
Ha) controls it; `0` disables it.

**The kernel records rather than throws, on purpose.** It runs inside the SCC
