iteration loop, so throwing there would abort a run whose *intermediate*
iterate transits a near-degenerate frontier but whose *converged* frontier is
well gapped. The refusal happens only on the accepted spectrum.

Per the maintainer ruling on #434 (2026-08-28): *"Force finite-T for metallic
frontiers. Do not accept the T=0 near-degenerate race."* A race that can
converge to a wrong occupation and report success is what CLAUDE.md § 7 forbids
treating as a convergence nuisance.

The 1e-6 Ha default was measured, not argued. The six #424 wave-flip fixtures
cut their frontier at 1.66e-5 … 1.09e-3 Ha, so 1e-6 clears the closest by 16×,
while 1e-5 would clear it by only 1.7× and would be unsafe. A scan over Z = 5
and Z = 31 chains at a = 3–9 bohr and meshes 2/4/6 found no natural system
below 1.44e-5 Ha, so the guard does not fire on the existing population — the
regression fixture is constructed by widening the chain until the gap crosses
the threshold.

**Known boundaries, deliberately not widened here**, each filed rather than
quietly left:

* the single-k (Γ/molecular/SECCM) T = 0 branch is **not** covered;
* the Python twin `vibeqc.smearing.apply._global_aufbau_with_mu`, which backs
  the ab-initio multi-k routes, carries the same defect — issue **#543**, with
  a 12-line synthetic reproduction, so the two kernels get one threshold rather
  than two from two lanes;
* degeneracy grouping is a ball around each group's *first* member rather than
  transitive, so a roundoff-degenerate manifold can be chopped and filled
  across the chop — issue **#544**. The guard's predicate is a deliberately
  bare `<=` with no lower bound so that chop fails closed, but failing closed
  is a mitigation, not the answer: the right behaviour there is to *share* the
  occupation, which needs the transitive-grouping change and its own evidence
  against the #317/#339 fractional pins;
* on the full-k **optimize** route, `periodic_runner.py:5055` gates finite-T,
  so the refusal's prescribed remedy is unreachable there — issue **#545**.
  Not a capability regression (those systems already failed, silently or by
  non-convergence), but the user gets two errors instead of one actionable one.

### Added: per-cycle SCF trace on the CCM loops (issue #493, 2026-08-29)

`CCMSCFResult` now carries `scf_trace`, a tuple of `CCMSCFIteration` records
(iteration, energy, `delta_e`, `grad_max`, `homo_lumo`, `diis_dim`) describing
how a CCM SCF actually converged. `grad_max` is the max-abs orthonormalised
commutator `max |Xᵀ (F D S − S D F) X|` — the *same* quantity the exit
predicate tests — so a run can be read against its own convergence gate.

The motivation is diagnostic discipline (CLAUDE.md § 7). A CCM loop previously
reported only `converged` and `n_iter`, so a run that stopped at the iteration
cap was indistinguishable from any other: an oscillation, a monotone crawl and
a hard stall all present as `converged: false, n_iter: 128`. Issue #493 is
exactly such a non-convergence, and no aid should be chosen for it without
knowing which of those it is.

The trace has already earned itself by ruling out two plausible hypotheses on
#493 rather than confirming one — the frontier gap is flat at 0.161 Ha across
the stalled cycles (so it is not near-degeneracy, and a level shift would have
been the wrong aid), and varying the DIIS ring-buffer depth from 8 to 32
changes neither the iteration count nor the cycle at which the residual
plateau breaks (so it is not subspace eviction either).

Diagnostic only: no control flow reads `scf_trace`, so recording it cannot
change an energy, and that is pinned by a test. It is recorded by the shared
closed-shell loop in `periodic/ccm/ri.py`, which is what `run_ccm_rhf_direct`
— the real-Γ evaluation of the neutral fitted-torus control Hamiltonian, and
the route #493 fails on — and `run_ccm_rhf_ri_neutral` both drive. Loops that
do not record one return an empty tuple, which is never `None`, so a consumer
can iterate unconditionally.

**Experimental**, as all AICCM surfaces are.

### Fixed: a killed molecular SCF's `.out` keeps the iterations it completed (issue #482, 2026-08-29)

The iteration table was rendered from `result.scf_trace` only *after* the
native SCF returned, so a process killed inside the SCF never reached the
write: 372 of 373 walltime-killed production cases left a `.out` that stopped
at the memory-estimate banner. The structured sidecar kept its rows (#25), but
it is not written unless `structured_log` is enabled, and the `.out` is the
artifact an operator opens first and the one archived per case.

Rows are now streamed into the `.out` as the native SCF produces them, and
`write_scf_trace` closes that table instead of emitting a second one.
A SIGTERM'd uracil-dimer/cc-pVDZ RHF now retains **17 iteration rows**,
matching its 17 `scf_iter` sidecar rows exactly.

**#482's stated mechanism was wrong, and that mattered.** It hypothesised the
`.out` was "assembled at job end", concluded an incremental-flush hook was
needed, and filed itself as evidence for an ask to the IO chat under CLAUDE.md
§ 16. Measurement says otherwise: `write()` + `flush()` from the native
progress handler reaches disk mid-run and survives SIGTERM — verified by
killing a job at 14 s and recovering the rows. The `.out` lifecycle needed no
change; the runner simply never wrote there. So this is a call-site fix, not an
IO-module one.

A completed run's `.out` is unchanged — the rows land where the table was, and
the only differences against the pre-change output are wall-clock timings.
Both halves are pinned in `tests/test_out_live_scf_rows.py`; the
completed-run half is the one that needs a test, since a duplicated table
renders correct energies twice and is invisible except by counting headers.

Only the primary SCF phase streams: helper SCFs (optimizer steps, atomization
fragments, Hessian displacements) would interleave dozens of tables into the
document.

### Fixed: `PeriodicSCFProvider` silently ran an 8-bohr lattice sum where the drivers it wraps use 15/25 (issue #540, 2026-09-02)

The geometry-optimisation provider defaulted `cutoff_bohr` to **8.0 bohr** and
applied it to *both* the AO and the nuclear lattice sums, while every BIPOLE
driver it wraps inherits `LatticeSumOptions()` at **15.0 bohr AO / 25.0 bohr
nuclear**. The default predates the fold guard by six weeks and nothing
documented it. It is the same shape as issue #307: a wrapper running a tighter
operator than the route it wraps, with no field saying so.

The two defaults do not return the same number. On the tree's own
end-to-end fixture (the 1-D H2 chain of #536, STO-3G, Γ) the 8-bohr default
gave **−0.1993841114 Ha** against **−0.1835461066 Ha** at the driver defaults,
for 2.2× less wall time (5.5 s → 12.4 s). Which of the two is *right* is a
separate question this change does not answer: on that cell the total energy
keeps moving as the cutoff grows further (it turns positive by 30 bohr), even
though the S(Γ) fold drift converges (7.9e-4 at 8 bohr → 2.8e-12 at 15). That
is the driver's documented *diagnostic* direct-truncated path for `dim < 3`,
which `run_periodic_job` refuses but the provider admits silently -- filed as
#542; this change only stops the provider from silently differing from the
drivers.

A second latent defect fell out of the same two lines: the unconditional
overwrite also clobbered any cutoffs a caller passed through
`scf_options.lattice_opts`, so that knob could never tighten or loosen the sums.

* `cutoff_bohr` now defaults to `None`, meaning **inherit** -- the driver
  defaults, or the caller's `scf_options.lattice_opts` when given. An explicit
  value keeps the historical set-both semantics and overrides `scf_options`,
  as documented. The provider records the cutoff that will actually run.
* Blast radius: two constructions in the tree, both tests, neither pinning an
  energy. No pinned value moved.

Three tests pin it: the default equals a fresh `LatticeSumOptions()` (so the
provider follows the drivers if they ever move, rather than a literal), an
explicit value still sets both sums, and caller-supplied `lattice_opts` are
respected. With the fix reverted exactly two of the three go red.
### Documentation: one AICCM route support matrix instead of four docstrings (2026-09-02)

No behaviour change. "Which AICCM route can run DFT, MP2, DLPNO, or analytic
gradients?" previously had to be reassembled from four module docstrings and
the `run_periodic_job` guard block, and the two lines answer it differently
enough that the reassembly was easy to get wrong.

`docs/experimental/aiccm2026dev_route_matrix.md` is now the single index:
per-route energy-method coverage across the three Gamma-CCM routes
(`four-center`, `neutral-bloch`, `real-gamma`) and the three chi-CCM backends,
the cluster-size regime each path actually reaches, and the two questions that
are least obvious from the API surface.

It also tabulates the property and analysis surface of both lines, whose names
do not overlap: the Gamma-CCM functions take `(scf_result, ccm)` and are
route-agnostic, while chi-CCM carries its own `aiccm2026dev_b_*` surface and
refuses COOP/COHP rather than rebuilding a fixed-cutoff Ewald surrogate.

* **DLPNO excludes `four-center`.** The pipeline density-fits its `(ia|jb)`
  from the neutral cderi, so the bare 1/r four-center is not an admissible
  correlation reference. `ccm_dlpno_mp2` only documents that requirement and
  does not guard it, so a four-center `scf_result` returns a wrong number
  rather than an error; the page says so and points at the `*_direct` one-call
  wrappers that make the mismatch impossible.
* **Analytic gradients are three different situations,** not one boolean:
  derived term by term on `four-center` (requires `method="aiccm2026dev-a"`;
  dense `n_pad_ao**4`, so small, 1-D, 2-D only), composed through the verified
  representation identity on `real-gamma` (dim 3, `exxdiv="ewald"`, screened
  and double hybrids fail closed), and fail-closed by design on chi-CCM per
  D56.

Also records what computes through `run_periodic_job` versus what is
library-only, since post-HF is library-only on every line and the
`aiccm2026dev-a` selector still fails closed in the runner. Cross-linked from
the Gamma-CCM reference, the chi-CCM user guide, and the experimental index.


### Fixed: orphaned terminal vq update receipts have an evidence-preserving recovery path (issue #528, 2026-09-02)

`vq admin recover-update` can now quarantine one exact, terminal managed-update
receipt whose runtime assets are already gone, instead of leaving that receipt
as a permanent dispatch fence or requiring an unsafe manual deletion.  The
explicit quarantine mode binds the marker bytes and inode, expected current
source SHA, clean installed tree, serving daemon identity, admin status, absent
assets, and an empty pause-token scope before moving the original marker into
an owner-only retained evidence directory.  Dry-run performs the same proofs
without moving the marker.  Live writers, accounting ambiguity, surviving
assets, paused jobs, replaced state roots, and malformed or changed evidence
continue to fail closed.

### Fixed: `run_periodic_geomopt` died on a fold-guard refusal at a *trial* step (issue #536, 2026-08-29)

`tests/test_geomopt.py::test_run_periodic_geomopt_imports_and_runs` had been a
deterministic red since the BIPOLE fold guard landed (2026-08-05), and the
issue read it as the fixture's default cutoff being too small. Measured, that
is not what happens: every evaluation at the user's geometry passes the guard
(drift 7.9e-4 at the 8-bohr default), and it is the **14th** evaluation --
BFGS's first unit step in *fractional* coordinates, which put the two H atoms
15.2 bohr apart -- that the guard refuses at drift 2.0e-1.

`BipoleFoldUnreliableError` exists precisely so an optimiser can treat a
refusal at a wild trial geometry as a recoverable penalty barrier, and
`bipole_optimize.relax_atoms` already does. `run_periodic_geomopt` never
implemented the contract, so the exception escaped `bfgs` as a fatal error.
Two periodic optimisers, one honouring the documented recovery and one not.

* `PeriodicSCFProvider._run_scf` now returns the penalty with a **zero
  gradient** for a refused or non-converged trial geometry -- and skips the
  6N finite-difference SCFs it would otherwise spend on a geometry already
  refused. A refusal at the *initial* geometry still propagates: there is
  nothing to back off to.
* The barrier value is one shared constant, `BIPOLE_TRIAL_PENALTY_HA` in
  `pbc_bipole_common`, which `bipole_optimize` now reads too, so the two
  routes cannot drift apart on what a refused trial costs.

Deliberately **not** changed here: the provider's own `cutoff_bohr` default
of 8.0 bohr, which is tighter than the 15.0 / 25.0 the wrapped BIPOLE drivers
use and also collapses the nuclear cutoff onto the AO one. It is not what
broke this test, and widening it would move every geometry-optimisation
user's cost. Recorded as a follow-up in the periodic sweep handover.

Three tests in `tests/test_geomopt.py`: a refusal at the initial geometry
propagates; a refusal after one good evaluation returns the shared penalty
with a zero gradient and runs no FD gradient; and the end-to-end fixture
asserts that a refusal *actually occurred* and the optimiser landed on a
genuine energy, so the recovery path is exercised rather than bypassed.

### Fixed: FeCl3 UHF stability analysis reaches a sign-certified verdict (issue #398, 2026-09-02)

The UHF stability solver's residual was tightened to certify the sign of its
lowest Hessian eigenvalue, but its default 60-matvec budget was left below the
measured FeCl3/cc-pVDZ requirement: 64 products still returned no verdict,
while 72 converged without changing the SCF energy, density, spin, or physical
stability threshold. The bounded UHF default is now 80 matvecs. Budget
exhaustion remains fail-closed and is pinned separately from the FeCl3
ground-state regression; UKS retains its existing 60-matvec default.

### Fixed: molecular MSINDO-NDDO analytic gradients differentiate the shipped energy (issue #538, 2026-09-04)

The direct closed-shell NDDO derivative previously used the INDO parameter
context and omitted the HSP core, dipole-monopole, and dipole-dipole terms that
are present in the reported NDDO energy. Errors reached 0.0637 Ha/bohr. The
validated s/p scope now has the complete fixed-density analytic contraction,
matches tight central differences and exact MSINDO source gradients below
1e-6 Ha/bohr, and is exposed lazily through `run_job` and molecular NEB.
NDDO parameter selection is context-local so overlapping INDO/NDDO jobs cannot
corrupt one another. Open-shell and Al-Cl d-shell NDDO gradients fail closed.
The Al-Cl energy route remains callable for compatibility but is scientifically
unsupported until its missing SPDD energy terms are implemented.

### Added: experimental Microsoft SKALA-1.1 neural XC functional (2026-09-02)

Added Microsoft SKALA-1.1 as an optional, hash-pinned neural XC functional
for molecular RKS/UKS/ROKS single points, with experimental periodic AO-grid
support. The checkpoint is fetched on demand from its immutable upstream
revision and verified by size and SHA-256; it is not bundled. Unsupported
gradients, response properties, band/DOS/COHP workflows, periodic dispersion,
GPW/GAPW, and CCM routes fail closed. Tutorials, molecular and periodic
examples, citation routing, licensing guidance, and a property-rich showcase
campaign document the current verification boundary.

### Fixed: incremental direct-Fock screening has no absolute drift floor (issue #468)

Small difference-density updates no longer receive the same absolute Schwarz
omission allowance as a full-density build. The direct molecular builder now
normalizes each nonzero update whose maximum element is below one, applies the
configured density-weighted quartet screen, and scales the linear J/K/G
increment back afterwards. The omitted update error therefore contracts with
the density change, and splitting one density change across many iterations no
longer changes the screened Fock map by an order-one amount. Fused RHF/RKS and
slot-cached RKS/UHF/UKS builds share the policy. Full builds, the eight-update
reset, the drift-stall fallback, and final tight full-Fock certification remain
unchanged.

### Fixed: obsolete plan-bound scheduler holds have a sanctioned exact recovery (issue #431)

`vq admin rollout-latest --supersede-plan-hold ROLLOUT HOST` can now cover one
obsolete recorder-era scheduler hold without editing its journal or releasing
any live drain. The recovery authenticates the historical report and complete
writer-shaped hold, requires a strictly newer accepted report whose complete
scheduler action set is healthy at every exact report pin, and records a
permanent hash-bound receipt only after a supported read-only drain snapshot
proves the named target inactive. Replays are no-ops. Missing, malformed,
live-active, partially healthy, or concurrently changed evidence remains a
hard block, and the command exits before ordinary rollout execution.

## [v0.15.157] - 2026-09-02 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Fixed: periodic Molden regression no longer pollutes the release checkout (issue #537, 2026-09-02)

The multi-k degenerate-orbital regression now gives each BIPOLE/GDF case a
`tmp_path`-scoped output stem.  It previously exercised `run_periodic_job`
with the default bare `output` stem, leaving `output.*` beside the checkout;
the #508 release guard correctly blocked the candidate.  The concurrently
reported auxiliary-basis file was collateral from the shared working
directory and is clean when run independently.

### Fixed: emitted citations point at the versions of record, residual sweep (issue #523, 2026-09-02)

The #523 fix (`7f5d5a272`) moved the MACE-MP and MACE-OFF23 entries to
their journal DOIs but left the MACE-OFF23 entry carrying the preprint's
title and author list: Crossref titles the JACS version of record
"MACE-OFF: Short-Range Transferable ..." (not "MACE-OFF23: ...") and lists
Yixuan Pu between Horton and Kapil. The sweep for the same split found one
more entry: the entanglement-based bond index paper
(`entanglement_bonds_2025`, routed for `properties=["entanglement_bonds"]`)
still emitted the arXiv:2501.15699 DOI although its own notes named the
published version. It now cites Ding, Matito & Schilling, *Nat. Commun.*
**17**, 4732 (2026), DOI `10.1038/s41467-026-73527-w`, Crossref-verified;
`entanglement.py` cites the same. Its `bibtex_key` keeps the historical
`entanglement_bonds_2025` spelling so existing sidecars and routes stay
stable. No other arXiv-only entry has a version of record
(`sun_ciah_2016` is preprint-only; `batatia_mace_2022` is NeurIPS
proceedings and matches the article's `references.bib`). A sweep guard now
fails any entry that routes an arXiv DOI while its notes announce a
published version.

### Fixed: OMx licensing inventory records the per-table source of each set (issue #272, 2026-09-02)

Maintainer ruling 2026-08-28: OMx parameter metadata must not keep an
inherited PM6 MOPAC license string; the values come from paper tables, so
cite the papers. The runtime already satisfied this (OM1/OM2/OM3 report
`license = "published parameter table"` with the Dral 2016 DOI and build
their `ParameterSetMetadata` independently of PM6), but `docs/license.md`
carried one generic "Tables 1-3" row and cited only Dral 2016 although the
`om1` / `om2` / `om3` routes also fire the original method papers. The
inventory now records each set's table and original source (OM1: Dral 2016
Table 1 / Kolb & Thiel 1993; OM2: Table 2 / Weber & Thiel 2000; OM3:
Table 3 / Scholten 2003; corrected 2026-09-06: Weber & Thiel 2000 is the
OM2 method paper, not the table the values came from, see the #272 entry of
that date) with DOIs, states explicitly that the sets are not
MOPAC-derived and carry no Apache-2.0 obligation, and lists the original
papers in the cite block. A new test pins the three legs that must agree
(citation routes, runtime metadata, the inventory) so the split cannot
silently re-open. No license string was invented and no parameter value
changed.

### Fixed: the bug broker projects the workflow label it is the authority for (issue #347, 2026-09-02)

The broker serializes claims, but GitLab's `workflow::` label was written by
hand: a claim did not set `in_progress`, a release or an expired lease did
not clear it, and landing did not move it to `verify`. On 2026-09-02 fifteen
issues had sat at `workflow::in_progress` for four days with zero broker
grants behind them, hidden from every fixer's queue filter. Every fixer-lease
transition now projects exactly one label (`claim`/`resume`/break-glass to
`in_progress`; `release`, `retire-provenance` and lease expiry to `triaged`,
or back to the landed label when a landed generation is still current;
`land` to `workflow::verify`, the provisioned name), lease expiry is swept
at startup and every `BROKER_WORKFLOW_SWEEP_S` seconds with a mirrored
`LEASE_EXPIRED` note, and delivery is an outbox that never rolls back a
committed decision (`/health` reports `pending_workflow_projections`).
Closed issues are never relabelled. Ten focused tests in
`tests/test_bugctl_broker.py`; the suite no longer has any path to a real
GitLab call.

### Fixed: the MPI half-installed guard counts what the session collected (issue #465, 2026-09-02)

The `test_mpi_environment_is_not_half_installed` failure message (landed in
`26bf73d0c`) quoted a literal `23` for the multi-rank tests it was covering
for, which would misreport the moment one was added, parametrized, or
deselected. It now derives the number from the items pytest collected from
the module in that session. Re-verified on a half-installed machine
(`mpirun` on PATH, no `mpi4py`): the whole file gives `1 failed, 23 skipped`
with exit 1 and the `pip install -e '.[mpi]'` remedy in the message; the
guard alone reports `0 collected`. The fail/skip contract is unchanged.

### Fixed: lattice row/column orientation is now declared, not guessed (issue #445, 2026-09-02)

`PeriodicSystem` consumes lattice vectors as the **columns** of its 3x3
matrix. A row-oriented matrix (the ASE / Extended-XYZ convention, and how
every textbook writes a lattice) is still a full-rank lattice, so it was
silently accepted and produced a sheared, physically different crystal that
converged and reported plausible numbers. Four independent instances (#319,
#364, #108, and a live 779 Ha/prim measurement on graphene) all hid on
low-symmetry cells, because cubic and FCC matrices are symmetric and because
the obvious guard, the cell volume, is blind to it: `det(L) == det(L.T)`.

Nothing geometric can refuse the transpose in general (both readings are
valid cells), so the fix makes the orientation *declared*:

* `PeriodicSystem(dim, lattice_vectors=[a1, a2, a3], unit_cell=...)` is a new
  keyword-only constructor that takes the three vectors themselves and stacks
  them into the columns; a 2-D array given there is read one vector per row,
  so the row-major literal lands in the engine's columns. Exactly three
  3-vectors are accepted. `vq.lattice_from_vectors(a1, a2, a3)` is the matrix
  form of the same contract. The `lattice=` matrix form is unchanged and its
  docstring now says so loudly.
* `vq.cell_parameters(lattice_or_system)` returns `|a|, |b|, |c|`, the
  crystallographic angles and the volume as the engine consumes them, and
  `vq.nearest_neighbour_distance(system)` the shortest interatomic distance
  including lattice images. Lengths, angles and that distance move under a
  transpose where the volume does not, which is the reviewer's check the
  issue asked for.
* The periodic `.out` prints a `Cell parameters` block (lengths, angles,
  nearest pair) between the lattice and the atom table, so every job shows
  its consumed cell at the top of the output. The two periodic `.out` goldens
  are regenerated deliberately for that block; no numerical output changed.
* `docs/user_guide/crystal_lattices.md` said "lattice vectors as the rows of
  a 3x3 array" and handed fractional coordinates to `Atom`, which takes
  Cartesian bohr; both examples are corrected to the vector form and to
  Cartesian positions, and `periodic_systems.md` documents the blind spot
  and the two checks.

`tests/test_lattice_convention.py` pins the keyword form against the column
and row readings on monolayer h-BN (a = 2.504 Angstrom, gamma = 60 deg,
B-N 1.446 Angstrom, the literature cell the row-fed #108 fixture missed),
the wrong-count refusal, the 2-D array reading, the volume blind spot
(bit-identical volume, different lengths / angles / nearest pair), and the
`.out` block.

### Fixed: `use_multipole_far_field=True` is refused on every route instead of silently dropped (issue #511, 2026-09-02)

`run_periodic_job` validated the far-field flag only inside its BIPOLE
preflight branch, and the four direct BIPOLE drivers are the only consumers.
So an explicit `use_multipole_far_field=True` on any other `jk_method` reached
neither a consumer nor a guard: the job ran the exact traversal to completion
and said nothing, leaving the caller believing they had measured the far-field
route. The route dispatch now sits in one place ahead of the BIPOLE branch --
and therefore ahead of the dry-run manifest, so queue preflight cannot certify
a request live dispatch would ignore. Non-BIPOLE routes get a refusal naming
the route they actually asked for; BIPOLE keeps its own quartet-domain
refusal; `reject_bipole_quartet_far_field` remains the single owner of the
bool-or-None type contract, now applied on every route. Four tests pin
fail-closed on `direct`/`gdf`, the unchanged default, the route named in the
message, and the type contract off BIPOLE.

### Fixed: the test suite fails a session that writes job artifacts into the working directory (issue #508, 2026-09-02)

`run_job(output=...)` takes a path *stem*, so a test passing a bare relative
name writes the job's `.out` / `.xyz` / `.system` / `.bibtex` / `.references`
/ `.scf.jsonl` siblings into whatever directory pytest was invoked from -- for
this suite, a git checkout. `tests/test_casscf_natural_orbitals.py` did exactly
that, and the six `h2_cas_test.*` files it left in site_a's `vq admin
update`-managed release checkout blocked the next fleet roll (`immutable update
refused: working tree is dirty`) days later, from a guard in a different
system. The same six files sat untracked in a coordinator clone for a whole
session.

The fixture now writes under `tmp_path_factory` and a regression pins its stem
outside the invocation directory (`3d2087da1`). On top of that narrow repair
the suite gains a mechanical guard for the whole class: `tests/conftest.py`
snapshots the invocation directory at `pytest_sessionstart` and, at
`pytest_sessionfinish`, fails an otherwise-green session that left new job
artifacts there, naming the files, the issue, and the `tmp_path` remedy.
Artifacts already present at session start are not blamed on the session (so
an already-dirty tree stays actionable), a failing session keeps its own exit
status, and `pytest-xdist` workers defer to the controller. The hook pair has
its own self-test, `tests/test_cwd_artifact_guard.py` (verified T2), because a
guard that silently stops guarding is the failure mode #508 is about. No
numerics changed.

Independent verification found that the first guard enumerated only the six
files from the original CASSCF incident. It missed planner-declared population
text/JSON, density and orbital cubes, text/JSON performance logs, plus the
runtime crash-dump NumPy sidecars. The inventory is now derived from a maximal
`OutputPlan` rather than duplicated by hand; arbitrary cube labels collapse to
the shared `.cube` tail, and `.dump.*.npy` siblings follow the crash writer's
runtime naming contract. The self-test independently materializes the planner
rows and invokes the crash writer, while ordinary `.txt`, `.json`, and `.npy`
files remain outside the guard.
### Fixed: production periodic PM6 lattice sums carry the exact heavy-heavy multipoles (issue #419, 2026-09-02)

The #244 exact s/p-s/p NDDO tensor was gated on `gamma_only_0 && is_zero_cell`
in `periodic_pm6.cpp`, so every production lattice sum -- including the zero
cell -- still used the collapsed monopole `q_B * gamma_AB`. Measured on CO in
a cubic box at cutoff 15 bohr against the molecular PM6 energy: +69.1, +73.8,
+47.8 mHa at a = 12, 14, 16 bohr, non-monotone. The issue's own remedy
("mirror the sp-H pattern for every cell") was measured before this fix at
-4.9 Ha: it applies the interatomic exchange block to image cells, where the
Gamma-only density has no cell resolution and the undamped 1/R monopole tail
of the tensor diverges with the cutoff (and mirrors each directed image block
a second time).

The directed-image convention is now derived at the code site: the Coulomb
block `J_A += sum_{la,si in B} P(la,si) (mu_0 nu_0|la_g si_g) - Z_B (mu_0 nu_0|s_g s_g)`
lands only on A's on-site block for every ordered pair and cell (the reverse
record supplies B's), so it is ungated everywhere; the exact exchange block
fires in the zero cell only, where P is exact, while non-zero images keep the
S^2-damped monopole exchange model. Two companion corrections were needed to
make the molecular limit reachable: (1) electrostatics are truncated per image
CELL, not per atom pair -- the #316 pair-distance inventory still decides
which cells enter, but an admitted cell contributes every pair, so it enters
as the neutral group it is (per-pair truncation left CO's +-x images at
a = 16 bohr with only their cross pairs inside cutoff 15, over-binding by
12.8 mHa, and drove a -2.52 Ha charge-transfer runaway at a = 10 / cutoff
13); the core-core sum uses the same rule. (2) The SCF seeds with the
spherically averaged neutral-atom valence density (`core_charge / n_ao` on
every AO diagonal, the MOPAC/NDDO minimal-basis atomic guess) instead of
D = 0, whose bare-core-Hamiltonian first iteration fills s twice on expanded
graphene under the exact tensor and converges to a sigma-only solution
0.48 Ha above the pi-occupied one (scale 1.06: -8.133 Ha against the
-8.611 Ha continuing the branch). The seed has to be spherically averaged
rather than shell-ordered: an s-first/p-remainder seed carries the same sigma
bias and does not reach a fixed point at all on scales 1.02 to 1.06, while
the uniform valence seed converges the whole sweep in 2 iterations on the
pi-occupied branch. The graphene sweep now also pins branch SMOOTHNESS
(successive expansion increments grow by 3-9 %, so the ratio stays under
1.5), because the sigma-only outlier is still monotone and the pre-existing
monotonicity assertion does not see it.

After the fix CO approaches its molecular limit monotonically: +179, +96,
+28, +17 microhartree at a = 12, 14, 16, 20 bohr (cutoff 15 / 15 / 15 / 21),
and +6.7 microhartree at a = 24; the a = 10 cell is stable to ~50 microhartree
across cutoffs 13-20. `gamma_only_0` is unchanged (still 1.1e-10 from the
molecular energy). Re-pinned: the four-atom fcc-Ar cell now needs 4 SCF
iterations instead of 2 (exact zero-cell Ar-Ar exchange makes the first Fock
matrix density-dependent) and its cutoff-15-vs-30 residual is the absolutely
convergent 1/R^5 penetration tail of the finite-extent quadrupole charges
(-7.9e-7 Ha/cell, pinned at 2e-6 instead of 1e-9); the
periodic-PM6 graphene fixture handed its lattice vectors as ROWS (issue #445
class) and now uses columns. The v0.15.144 note's "applied in molecular,
periodic, and SECCM PM6 routes" was over-broad on "periodic" until this
change: it meant the molecular-limit diagnostic mode only.

### Clarified: the ideal-cubic T=0 ensemble stress is the derivative of the executed ensemble energy (issue #529, 2026-09-02)

The #310 verification recorded that on ideal cubic Si the Gamma DFTB0 analytic
stress differs from a component-wise central difference of the energy by
10.93 % (2.35 % on conventional diamond C), persisting as the step shrinks.
Measured on `main` before pinning: the analytic tensor is the strain derivative
of the executed objective at fixed Weinert-Davenport ensemble occupations -- a
central difference of `sum_i f_i eps_i + E_rep` with the threefold manifold
traced as a block reproduces all nine components with relative deviations
1.7e-5, 4.3e-6, 1.1e-6, 2.7e-7 at h = 4e-3 ... 5e-4 (O(h^2)), and the
isotropic-strain derivative of the re-filled energy matches the analytic trace
to 1e-6 relative. The offset is the cusp of the T=0 hard-Aufbau energy along a
symmetry-breaking strain: re-filling the split manifold on each side gives one-
sided slopes whose average is `sigma_xx V + (d - s)/3` (singlet slope
s = -1.42e-4, doublet slope d = 3.02e-3 Ha on Si), predicted 3.9713e-5 against
the measured 3.9727e-5 Ha/bohr^3 (analytic 3.5807e-5). SCC-DFTB shares the
behaviour trivially: ideal Si converges to zero charges, so its functional
coincides with DFTB0. No kernel changed; the contract is now stated in the
user guide and pinned by `TestPeriodicStressCubicSymmetry` (ensemble-FD parity
at 1e-9, isotropic-FD parity, the level-splitting cusp, and the SCC control).
A component-wise finite difference of a T=0 energy at a degenerate frontier is
not a stress; routes that need derivatives of re-filled energies need finite
electronic temperature.

### Fixed: GFN2 periodic H0 coordination names a lattice-equivalent atom pair (issue #408, 2026-09-02)

The fcc Cu 2x2x4 refusal `GFN2 H0 coordination pair distance must be finite and
positive` reproduces only with the lattice handed to `PeriodicSystem` as ROWS
(the issue #319 F-TRANSPOSE producer bug): under the transposed lattice the
atoms k and k+2 along the four-fold axis coincide modulo a(1,1,0), while 2x2x2
has no such pair -- exactly the size dependence that made the report look like
an image-enumeration defect. Column-fed, the 16-atom cell assembles at every
cutoff. The periodic coordination builder now names the coincident pair and
its image and points at the column convention instead of failing on the bare
pair-distance guard; `TestGFN2Periodic` pins both the column-fed assembly and
the named refusal. No lattice-sum or coordination arithmetic changed.

### Fixed: the 2-D graphene supercell repulsive ladder is pinned; issue #319 is a transposed producer lattice (issue #319, 2026-09-02)

Re-measured on this issue's own reproduction: with lattice vectors as columns,
`E_rep` per primitive cell is bit-identical at 0.001292104 Ha for graphene
n = 1..5 and the electronic energy per primitive cell moves by under 0.5 mHa;
feeding the same vectors as rows reproduces the filed 783.759 Ha/cell at n = 2
and the non-monotone 5.42 / 1.12 / 20.51 Ha/cell at n = 3..5 to the printed
digits. vibe-qc's 2-D lattice sum is exonerated; the regression the issue
asked for (the n = 1..5 ladder, with the row-fed n = 2 discriminator) now
lives in `tests/test_semiempirical_kpoint_dftb.py`. The orientation hazard
itself stays tracked as issue #445.
### Fixed: ROHF/ROKS EDIIS/ADIIS coupling can no longer desync from the C++ anti-replay guard (issue #487, 2026-09-02)

`run_roothaan_scf` couples the extrapolated EDIIS/ADIIS Fock pair to the
projectors of the density that pair belongs to, `D_tilde = Σ_i c_i D_i` (the
#119 repair). It reconstructed `D_tilde` from a Python-side mirror of the
density history, and that mirror was never told when
`EDIIS::finish_extrapolation` / `ADIIS::finish_extrapolation` erased an
interior history entry (the anti-replay guard): after one guard fire the
coefficient vector no longer indexed the mirror, the reconstruction was
abandoned, and the loop silently fell back to projecting the extrapolated
Fock with the *current* density -- exactly the inconsistent effective Fock
the #119 repair removed. Reachable on a real molecule: CN radical,
ROHF/STO-3G from the SAD guess, where the guard fires once under `ediis`,
`adiis` and `ediis_diis` and the fallback then engaged for 6, 6 and 1
cycles with `|D_tilde - D_current|` up to 0.105 (1.08 under `ediis_diis`);
the converged energy happened to survive on that case (-90.9974703508 Ha,
same as plain DIIS). The C++ accelerators now expose the density they
extrapolated -- `EDIIS.last_extrapolated_density()` /
`ADIIS.last_extrapolated_density()`, combined over the history they hold
with the coefficients of the returned Fock -- plus a
`replay_guard_erasures()` diagnostic counter; the Python mirror and its
`pragma: no cover` fallback are deleted, and a block-count mismatch fails
loudly (`RuntimeError`) instead of coupling with a density the
extrapolation did not use. Pinned in `tests/test_ediis.py` (a scalar
history whose guard erasure leaves mixed survivors, D_tilde = 1.2 vs
current 1.4), and in `tests/test_rohf.py` by an HF-level identity check --
every extrapolated cycle must satisfy `F_extrap == F(D_coupled)` -- on the
synthetic ROHF and on the CN fixture with the guard asserted to have fired.
Adjacent to #486 (`d940ce69d`); no convergence threshold or damping changed.

### Fixed: `CASSCFOptions(compute_wz=True)` no longer adds a spurious gradient component (issue #516, 2026-09-02)

The experimental CP-MCSCF "W^z correction" behind `compute_wz=True` is
retired. Measured on H2 CAS(2,2) at R = 1.4 bohr against a central finite
difference of the converged CASSCF energy (step 1e-3): the default analytic
gradient agrees to 2.2e-7 Ha/bohr (6-31G) and 2.5e-7 (cc-pVDZ), i.e. it is
already the complete derivative -- a converged state-specific CASSCF is
stationary in every orbital rotation and CI coefficient, so by the 2n+1 rule
its first derivative has no response term at all. The "correction" added
0.172 Ha/bohr and flipped the sign of g_z on 6-31G, and put -0.357 Ha/bohr
into g_x on cc-pVDZ (a linear molecule on z, where g_x must vanish): its
implementation solved one z-vector for the first non-zero column of the
perturbed orbital gradient and contracted that same z with every other
column, so any basis with p/d functions -- where the transverse column is
the first non-zero one -- produced a transverse phantom. `compute_wz=True`
is now an accepted no-op alias of the analytic gradient that emits a
`FutureWarning`; `compute_wz="numerical"` (the finite-difference oracle) is
unchanged. The dead W^z assembly (`_compute_wz_correction` and three helpers
nothing else used) is deleted; the orbital-response helpers the CASPT2 /
NEVPT2 relaxed gradients build on are untouched. The geometry optimizers now
keep `compute_wz=True` on the analytic path (it used to force full-energy
FD). `tests/test_casscf_gradient.py` pins the full vector against
full-energy FD on 6-31G and cc-pVDZ, the vanishing transverse components,
and the alias; `examples/regression/casscf_gradient_fd_reproducer.py` now
fails on any path that disagrees with FD, instead of documenting an
"expected ~74 % overshoot". Docs: `docs/tutorial/casscf_multireference.md`,
`docs/user_guide/non_hf_solvers.md`, `docs/user_guide/geometry_optimization.md`
drop the "87 % z-vector-free approximation" description, which was stale
since the 2026-06-19 energy-weighted-density fix.

### Fixed: def2-QZVP transition-metal DF correlation runs are no longer refused (issue #483, 2026-09-02)

`default_aux_basis_for("def2-qzvp", kind="ri")` -- the auxiliary basis every
DF-MP2, DF-CC, FNO-CCSD, DLPNO and ROHF-MP2 run picks up for a def2-QZVP
orbital basis -- now resolves to `def2-qzvpp-rifit` instead of
`def2-qzvp-rifit`. The issue's hypothesis (a truncated BSE fetch) does not
hold: the Basis Set Exchange record `def2-QZVP-RIFIT` version 1 carries
exactly the 42 main-group elements the shipped file has (H..Ca, Ga..Sr,
In..Ba, Tl..Rn); the 3d, 4d and 5d transition metals are absent upstream
(Turbomole 7.3 data), and BSE itself describes the record as the "RIMP2
auxiliary basis for def2-QZVPP". Its 42 blocks are byte-identical to the
same elements of `def2-qzvpp-rifit`, which covers all 72 elements of the def2
RI convention, so the re-route changes nothing for a main-group molecule
(identical shells, bit-identical numbers) and lets a def2-QZVP
transition-metal pairing run instead of failing closed on the #480 coverage
guard. No basis data was added or edited: the shipped `def2-qzvp-rifit.g94`
stays exactly as BSE returns it and remains selectable by name. The
`KNOWN_GAPS` row that pins the file's gap stays (it is real, and upstream);
new tests pin the re-route, its transition-metal coverage, and the
subset identity. Docs: `docs/user_guide/density_fitting.md`.
### Fixed: GFN2-SECCM H0 coordination numbers come from the cyclic Wigner-Seitz records (issue #354, 2026-09-02)

GFN2-SECCM built every H0 image block with Bannwarth-Ehlert-Grimme Eq. 18
coordination numbers recomputed molecularly from the typed home-cell atoms.
The cyclic images that define the finite torus were invisible to the CN, so
the H0 self-energies depended on which coordinate representative the caller
typed for a boundary site and broke the cluster's own translation symmetry.
Measured on a two-replica H2O torus (primitive 6 bohr, replicas (2,1,1)) with
`include_aes=False`: retyping one H by the full torus translation moved the
total energy by -3.83e-3 Ha (e_band0 -3.66e-3 Ha) while the overlap was
invariant to 1e-15, and the two by-construction-equivalent water molecules
carried charges differing by 2.6e-5 e.

The adapter now assembles one atom-local Eq. 18 coordination vector from the
directed WS records - each record contributes `weight * f_CN(Z_A, Z_B, |d|)`
at its physical image displacement, with the Peintinger-Bredow 2014 two-center
ownership weight and no 1/2 - and reuses that vector for every H0 image block
through `build_gfn2_hamiltonian_zero_image_with_cn`. On the same fixture the
representative relabelling now preserves energy, band, SCC, third-order and
repulsion terms to 3.6e-15 Ha, the replica charges agree to 1.8e-15 e, and
atom permutation remains covariant. The 1x1x1 molecular limit is unchanged
(the trivial record set reproduces the molecular CN sum term for term). The
default `include_aes=True` arm keeps a +2.4e-4 Ha representative residual that
is now cleanly attributable to the AES moment integrals (issue #348).

Cyclic-cell pins this legitimately moves, before -> after (fcc Cu,
`ewald_gamma`; the last column is the issue #421 translation-orbit charge
spread, which was measuring this defect):

| recipe | energy (Ha/atom) | spread (e) |
|---|---|---|
| 2x2x2 a=3.615 A, Newton and broyden_eyert, T=0.001 | -3.773689041 -> -3.777337900 | 0.90 -> 9.5e-5 |
| 2x2x4 a=3.7958 A, Newton, T=0.002 | -3.852071156 -> -3.865789830 | -> 3.2e-4 |
| 2x2x2 a=3.7 A, broyden_eyert, T=0.001 | -3.782979671 (spread pin) | 0.903277 -> 8.3e-5 |
| 4x4x4 a=3.7 A, broyden_eyert, T=0.001 | -3.886828 -> -3.904530 | 0.456 -> 5.9e-4 |
| 2x2x2 a=3.615 A, simple mixing, T=0.005 | -3.774155319 -> -3.778602023 | 0.84 (see below) |

Six further GFN2-SECCM energy pins outside the fcc-Cu ladder also moved with
the corrected H0 and are re-measured here. Every structural assertion in each
of those tests is unchanged and still passes: convergence, `physical_basin`,
the Mulliken and shell charge scales, the LiH wire's rigid-translation
invariance, and the MgO Madelung invariants.

| test | before -> after |
|---|---|
| `..._bulk_cu_sane_basin_is_physical` (2x2x2 a=3.615 A, T=0.005) | -3.773069 -> -3.779587241 |
| `..._bulk_cu_compressed_converges_physical` (2x2x2 a=3.434 A) | -3.755123 -> -3.762152203 |
| `..._bulk_cu_embedding_converges_physical` (same, `madelung=True`) | -3.756401160 -> -3.761968564 |
| `..._ewald_gamma_mgo_xtb_scale_charges` (MgO 2x2x2 a=4.212 A) | -4.749699725 -> -4.769076955 |
| `..._ewald_gamma_1d_chain_converges_and_is_invariant` (LiH wire) | -0.805035101 -> -0.804626976 |
| `test_gfn2_indefinite_overlap_..._b1_100_slab` (per atom) | -2.365887702 -> -2.373082177 |

The corrected map exposes the attractor structure issue #421 tracks: at
T=0.005 Newton and broyden_eyert agree on a symmetric metallic state at
-3.779587241 Ha/atom, while plain simple mixing converges into a gapped state
that breaks the finite translation group (spread 0.84 e, q_rms 0.36 e) and
DIIS into a third (spread 0.22 e). All pass the magnitude gates; the spread
diagnostic is reported, not gated (maintainer decision D3, revisit now due).
The 8-atom cell is no longer "spuriously polarized" relative to the 64-atom
cell - both are symmetric and near-neutral - and the size effect is the
0.12 Ha/atom energy gap between them.

Periodic Gamma GFN2 (`gfn2_h0_periodic_coordination_numbers`) already used
physical images and is unchanged; the periodic derivative path still consumes
the molecular CN (issue #338).

### Fixed: basis/integrals gate budget matches its measured slow node (issue #492, 2026-08-31)

The `basis-ecp-integrals` lane imposed a 300-second per-test ceiling even
though `test_lih_filter_unblocks_scf_run` repeatedly required 301-306 seconds
and takes 450.98 seconds on the current isolated clone.  The full file has
also measured 1634.99 seconds against a 900-second file ceiling.  Its budgets
are now 600 seconds per test and 2400 seconds per file.  The test remains in
the verified T2 inventory and continues to run; no basis filter, integral,
SCF, or numerical threshold changed.

### Documented: DLPNO memory preflight is a composition-level bound (issue #497, 2026-08-31)

The DLPNO memory preflight estimates pair and PNO storage from composition,
basis, electron, threshold, and thread counts. It does not construct the
geometry-dependent pair domains, so same-composition isomers can receive the
same conservative estimate even when their local working sets differ. The
formatted estimate and refusal now state that limitation at the point where a
user decides whether an extended or dilute calculation needs independent
peak-RSS evidence and an explicit memory override. Estimator arithmetic,
admission thresholds, and DLPNO numerics are unchanged.

### Fixed: failed GFN2-SECCM attempts report their real physical basin (issue #410, 2026-08-31)

An SCC attempt that exhausted its iteration budget exposed the last atom and
shell charges for diagnosis but stamped `physical_basin=true` unconditionally.
Pathological finite restart states could therefore fail the shared native
charge-state predicate while both the result and attempt provenance described
them as physical. The failed exit now applies the same shell-capacity and local
charge-polarization predicates as a converged exit before stamping its attempt.
Retry and selection semantics are unchanged: an iteration-limit attempt is
still ineligible because it is not converged.

### Fixed: `max_iter=0` is a coherent ORCA `NOITER` evaluation (issue #392, 2026-08-28)

The molecular RHF, UHF, RKS, and UKS native drivers previously returned empty
density and Fock matrices with `energy=0.0` when `max_iter=0`. A later input
guard rejected zero along with negative budgets, which broke the documented
ORCA `NOITER` compatibility path. All six molecular routes (including ROHF and
ROKS) now evaluate the initial guess once and return finite, shape-consistent
density, orbitals, Fock, and energy with `n_iter=0`, `converged=false`, and no
SCF trace entry. Staged COSX and open-shell spin schedules perform that single
evaluation on the reported operator instead of hiding extra iterations.

Negative iteration budgets still fail before SCF work. Boolean and non-integer
budgets now fail at the Python options boundary for the four pybind-backed
routes as well as ROHF/ROKS, so Python's `bool`-to-`int` coercion cannot turn
`True` into a one-iteration calculation. Positive and default budgets are
unchanged.

## [v0.15.156] - 2026-08-31 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Fixed: BIPOLE exact convergence confirmation includes DFT+U (issue #514 successor, 2026-08-31)

v0.15.155 rebuilt the exact Fock for terminal convergence confirmation, but
the DFT+U routes measured the confirmation commutator before applying the
Dudarev correction. The RHF, RKS, UHF, and UKS BIPOLE drivers now apply +U
exactly once to that provisional exact operator before measuring the
commutator, then reuse the matching Hubbard energy during finalization. The
non-+U path, energy equations, incremental-Fock chain, convergence tolerances,
and iteration budget remain unchanged.

### Fixed: scheduler branch runtimes no longer inherit a release tag (issue #535, 2026-08-31)

Scheduler-runtime updates resolved a unique tag at the pinned commit for every
program. Under rule-A release reports, the dev and vibe-view pins can equal the
release commit, so site_i received `--tag` for two branch-tip lanes whose tracked
deploy wrapper correctly refuses it. Automatic tag resolution now remains
limited to `vibeqc-release`, preserving the release-provenance fix from #288;
`vibeqc-dev` and `vibe-view` keep null deployment tags and exact SHA identity
even when a release tag points at the same commit.

## [v0.15.155] - 2026-08-30 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Fixed: verification queue responses expose their real state (issue #519, 2026-08-30)

`bugctl verifier-claim` no longer describes an already-verified generation as
one that never landed, and distinguishes unlanded work from a newer fixer
generation that superseded an earlier landing. Verification-queue rows now
carry their authenticated GitLab lifecycle state, use the documented
`queue_reason` field on both eligible and withheld rows, and identify mirror
freshness as `broker_checkout_status`. The queue remains advisory and
actor-scoped; atomic verifier claims continue to serialize concurrent lanes.

### Fixed: bundled MOPAC parameter caches retain their license notice (issue #522, 2026-08-30)

The full PM6 and PM7 TOML parameter caches carried their Apache-2.0 license
identifier and upstream source URL but omitted MOPAC's copyright notice, even
though the license guide said every redistributed value file retained it. Both
caches now carry the same complete notice as the inline PM6/PM7 parameter
modules. Parameter values, immutable identities, runtime metadata, and method
routing are unchanged.

### Fixed: bugctl cold-resume preserves issue-wide claim serialization (issue #533, 2026-08-30)

`bugctl resume` looked only for a live grant owned by the requesting actor and
run. If another actor already held an unexpired lease, resume could mint a new
generation beside it even though an ordinary claim correctly returned
`already_claimed`. Cold-resume now applies the same issue-wide active-grant
fence before issuing a generation, while preserving same-run replay and
expired-predecessor recovery.

### Fixed: AIC7 records linked-library provenance before running rungs (issue #477, 2026-08-30)

The tracked AIC7 campaign driver imported `banner` from the package root,
where that name deliberately refers to the public banner function rather than
the `vibeqc.banner` submodule. All 21 existing campaign records therefore
carried `library_versions_error` instead of the linked libint, libxc, FFTW,
and spglib identities. The driver now imports the submodule probe directly
and refuses to start a calculation rung when the live stamp is missing or
empty. Historical artifacts remain immutable and retain their explicit error;
this change applies to newly submitted runs only.

### Fixed: emitted MACE model citations use the journal records (issue #523, 2026-08-30)

The per-model citation database still pointed MACE-MP and MACE-OFF23 users to
their arXiv DOI aliases, while the semiempirical article already cited the
published JCP and JACS papers. The emitted BibTeX/JSON citation sidecars now
carry the journal metadata, version-of-record DOI, and DOI URL for both model
families. Model routing and licensing policy are unchanged.

### Fixed: band-overlap T=0 meshes build their density from the global-fill occupations (issue #509, 2026-08-30)

The Ewald-3D RHF/RKS and BIPOLE RKS multi-k drivers built their T=0 density
from a single fixed `C[:, :n_occ]` slice at every k. The #85
global-Fermi-level fill can occupy a different number of bands per k (or a
shared fractional group at mu) on a mesh whose bands straddle the Fermi
level, so those routes had been failing closed with `NotImplementedError`
since #85. All three drivers now select the density builder from the
occupations themselves (`occupations_are_per_k_integer_aufbau`): the fixed
slice stays for the legacy per-k integer pattern (bit-identical numerics),
and the occupation-driven builder (the native multi-k GDF pattern) handles
the band-overlap fill. `use_mom`/`use_oda` and the BIPOLE legacy gauge fail
closed at runtime when a band-overlap fill is discovered. Regressions:
Mg/STO-3G (2,2,2) converges on RHF Ewald-3D and on RKS Ewald-3D with the
anderson density mixer, and the BIPOLE RKS route runs the occupation-driven
density without the refusal (legacy gauge still rejected).

### Fixed: vq tests can no longer escape into live state (issue #527, 2026-08-30)

A raw or inherited `pytest --noconftest` invocation could bypass vq's autouse
fixture, import a stale editable copy, and resolve the operator's real state or
config roots. That path produced a synthetic durable admin-update receipt in
the live queue and could also contact a live daemon over RPC. The earlier #438
marker-specific check did not cover collection-time children, alternate state
consumers, explicit live overrides, or direct socket paths.

Pytest now selects `vibe-queue/src` from project configuration and requires
pytest 8.2's session-wide ancestry marker. Every test-controlled persistent
path -- per-user and multi-user state, archive/config roots, system config,
web credentials, and RPC socket overrides -- must resolve, symlink-aware,
beneath a unique `VQ_TEST_SANDBOX_ROOT`. The vq conftest installs that boundary
before collection, rebinds it per test, verifies checkout provenance, and
fails the run if HOME/XDG sentinel metadata or contents change. The canonical
per-file gate and release CI supply the same isolated roots, preserve a short
AF_UNIX path on macOS, scrub inherited pytest options, and retain Git's exact
checkout trust configuration after HOME changes. Production default-path
semantics remain covered in marker-scrubbed subprocesses with disposable
homes.

### Fixed: the license guide now states the fail-closed MACE model policy (issue #524, 2026-08-30)

`docs/license.md` said an unknown MACE model key was treated as academic-only,
which implied that an ASL acknowledgment could make an unregistered model
runnable. The existing resolver deliberately does the safer thing: it rejects
unknown families, URLs, and local weight paths before backend import or weight
download. The guide now states that contract and a source/docs regression pins
it. No MACE runtime, registry, license gate, or supported model changed.

### Fixed: vq fails closed on broken or stale managed vibe-qc runtimes (issue #521, 2026-08-30)

Legacy `vibeqc-dev` and `vibeqc-release` registrations could omit
`import_check`, so `vq programs` reported `OK` from the interpreter and Git
paths alone even when `import vibeqc` failed against an older compiled core.
The same omission disarmed branch-update import verification and atomic
rollback. vq now recognizes that source layout together with its checkout-local
`.venv`, applies the `vibeqc` import contract automatically, checks that Python
comes from the registered checkout, and fails readiness when the
interpreter-reported core predates native source. Before Git mutation, update
rollback snapshots that live core even when it resides in venv `site-packages`,
along with every loader-visible core candidate, checkout state, and native
compilation-input freshness evidence; it refuses when that state cannot be
preserved. Failed transactions restore core symlinks and remove only newly
created loader candidates. Fresh and reused immutable runtime slots must pass
the same structural runtime gate before activation, with their core contained
inside the slot. Generic pure-Git venv programs retain their no-import behavior.

### Fixed: closed issues cannot re-enter the verification queue (issue #531, 2026-08-30)

A stale LANDED broker generation outlived GitLab issue #501's
`resolution::duplicate` close. `verify-queue` advertised the closed duplicate,
and `verifier-claim` granted a real lease, even though no open verification
question remained. The supported release path prevented a verdict only after
the lane had already been dispatched.

The broker now authenticates GitLab lifecycle state before either advertising
or granting verifier work. Closed duplicates and closed verified issues are
terminal; ordinary open LANDED issues and deliberate second opinions on open
issues remain eligible. Queue reads use bounded `iids[]` batches instead of one
request per issue, and any failed, malformed, incomplete, or duplicate batch
fails the entire queue rather than returning a partially trusted dispatch list.
A tokenless broker can still return a provably empty queue, but it fails closed
on every nonempty candidate set. The existing fixer-provenance checks retain
priority, and queue and claim pass the resulting lifecycle record through the
same eligibility predicate.

### Fixed: the BIPOLE terminal convergence check no longer dead-ends (issue #514, 2026-08-29)

The 2026-08-13 terminal-rebuild gate measures the true (non-incremental)
operator at the density the loop just committed. At a marginal fixed point
that measurement can sit one iteration's step above the gradient gate, and
the driver then revoked a converged loop with no way back: the public
PBE0/H2O default-cutoff row failed with "RKS periodic SCF did not converge
after 8 iterations" on main. All four BIPOLE drivers (RHF/RKS/UHF/UKS) now
confirm the provisional exit on the exact operator before breaking, so the
loop simply runs the extra iteration(s) it needs. The confirmation rebuild
is reused by the post-loop finalisation phase, so healthy rows pay nothing
extra. The row's pin is refreshed to the post-`9cca63c16` (#478) fixed point
with the attribution recorded in the test docstring; the tail itself does
not move the fixed point.

## [v0.15.154] - 2026-08-29 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Fixed: BIPOLE Gilat fixed-point pins tracked a pre-#478 truncation (issue #515, 2026-08-29)

`tests/test_bz_integration_gilat_scf.py` pinned the open-shell Gilat
fixed-point energies to values computed before `9cca63c16` (issue #478)
sized the BIPOLE 1e Ewald real-space sum from the pinned CRYSTAL alpha
instead of the AO overlap cutoff. That deliberate monopole-self-image fix
moved the H-doublet vacuum-box energies by -8.9897e-6 Ha (identical for UHF
and LDA, so shared 1e machinery). The pins are refreshed to the post-fix
values with the reason recorded beside them; the attribution was verified by
re-running the test at `9cca63c16~1` (old pins pass) and at `9cca63c16` (new
values appear) against the same compiled core.

### Added: docs and homepage state all four component versions (2026-08-29)

The repository ships four independently versioned tools -- vibe-qc,
vibe-view, vq and vibe-basis -- on deliberately decoupled version lines.
The docs and the homepage previously showed only the vibe-qc number, so a
reader had no way to tell which viewer, queue, or basis toolkit a checkout
carried, and no reason to suspect the single number they saw did not cover
them. `docs/index.md`, `docs/toolset_lifecycle.md` and the homepage release
band now list all four, each read from that component's own
`[project] version` rather than a copied constant that would drift on the
first release moving one line and not the others. A missing sibling renders
a visible `(unknown)` instead of failing the docs build or printing a
silently wrong version.

### Fixed: the repo-status liveness probe counted its own subprocesses (2026-08-29)

`agentic-loop/gitlab-repo-status.sh` decided whether a checkout was in use
with `lsof -d cwd | grep -c "gitlab/$name$"`, run after the script's own
`git -C <dir>` calls. `git -C` chdirs into the repository, so the probe
counted itself and reported every checkout as occupied -- measured at 2
processes for a bare `git -C <dir> fetch`. A liveness signal that is always
positive cannot distinguish an idle tree from a genuinely occupied one,
which is the single question the check exists to answer before a lane is
dispatched into a clone. It now filters by command name.

### Added: RHF/RKS restricted-stability verdict surface (issue #144, 2026-08-28)

Closed-shell `run_rhf` / `run_rks` now report the lowest orbital-rotation
Hessian eigenvalue at the converged restricted solution, default-on, and warn
loudly when it is negative: `RHFResult` / `RKSResult` gain
`stability_checked`, `stability_analysis_converged`, `stability_eigenvalue`,
`internal_instability`, and stability phase timings; a negative verdict
(`lambda_min < -stability_tol`) fires the existing `scf_internal_instability`
warning in the `.out`. The analysis evaluates the coupled per-spin orbital
Hessian at equal spin blocks -- the union of the Seeger-Pople singlet and
triplet sectors (doi:10.1063/1.434318); the RKS half uses the polarised XC
kernel pinned at (D/2, D/2) per the closed-shell KS stability analysis of
Bauernschmitt & Ahlrichs (doi:10.1063/1.471637).

This is the decision-neutral prerequisite from
`agentic-loop/asks/ask-scf144-restricted-stability-contract-2026-08-27.md`:
**verdict only** -- the restricted route does not rotate, escape, promote to
UHF/UKS, or search other basins. What to do with a negative verdict remains
the two pending maintainer decisions on that ask; the surface just stops the
wrong-root failure from being silent (the four filed #144 cases each report
`converged=True` with no signal today). Fail-closed contract mirrors UKS:
DFT+U and hybrid-COSX RHF, and DFT+U / meta-GGA / range-separated / VV10 /
hybrid-COSX RKS, skip the implicit check and raise on an explicit request;
coupled-solvent (CPCM) RHF/RKS disable the verdict because the reaction-field
density response is not in the Hessian.

### Documented: `union12`'s "validated in 1-D" claim is minimal-basis only (issue #242, 2026-08-29)

The CCM four-centre route table described `method="union12"` as "validated in
1-D, breaks 8-fold ERI symmetry in >=2-D", in the `vibeqc.periodic.ccm` module
docstring and in the `scf.py` route comment. The dimensional half is right and
the validation half is missing its qualifier: the published 1-D validation
holds only in a minimal basis.

The eq-18 weighted four-centre is `M = R^T G-hat C` with `R != C` -- the bra
selector and the weighted image-gathering map applied to the ket are different
operators -- so it is not a congruence of the padded ERI Gram matrix and
carries no positive-semidefinite guarantee. On the published 1-D alternating H
chain it has 77 negative eigenvalues (minimum -0.236) while the CCM overlap is
positive definite, and the SCF descends into that subspace: the traceable DZVP
variants return -7.11 to -8.48 Ha/atom against a published -0.552592, 3-21g
-1.97, 6-31g -4.92. STO-3G
reproduces the published value to 3.2e-06 Ha/atom only because a minimal basis
cannot reach the offending sector, which is why the historical validations did
not see it. Where the form is negative the nominal Coulomb energy has no lower
bound, so the SCF is not failing to find a minimum; there is none.

Documentation only. No guard, no symmetrised weight, no screening and no
`lindep_tol` change: the issue's O21 analysis measured that deleting the entire
eq-18 weighting leaves the minimum eigenvalue unchanged to within 1 % and that
the symmetrised weight reproduces it to five digits, so each of those would
look like a fix while changing nothing. The property belongs to the printed
equation rather than to this port, and a fail-closed refusal on non-minimal
bases remains a maintainer decision.

### Fixed: multi-k pure-DFT never auto-sized its dense-core high-|G| tail, so periodic DFT on tight-core cells was ~1 Ha wrong by default (issue #518, 2026-08-29)

`pbc_gdf._auto_rsgdf_tail_ke_cutoff` is the production resolver that sizes the
rsgdf high-|G| tail to the steepest AO primitive on the dense-core class. The
Gamma routes and both CCM routes have always called it. `periodic_k_gdf.py`
called it **nowhere** -- so multi-k closed-shell pure DFT (`alpha == 0`,
`dim=3`), the one route that also defaults to the EWALD_3D real-space Hartree,
ran with no tail on a J machinery that builds no cderi and cannot carry one.

The result was not a small drift. MgO/STO-3G `(2,2,2)` KRKS-LDA at defaults
returned **-271.5315355 Ha** against CRYSTAL 23 SVWN SHRINK-2
(**-270.49836634642**) and PySCF KRKS/GDF (**-270.4990190962243**) -- two
independent implementations that agree with each other to **0.65 mHa** while
vibe-qc sat **-1033.2 mHa** away. The three P13 rows of the release paper's
periodic table are that number.

Pure DFT now resolves the same auto-tail the Gamma and CCM routes do, which
promotes the run onto the tail-consuming cached-Lpq GDF Hartree. On the MgO
cell the resolver returns 3291.6114 Ha and the default run measures
**-270.502804735242 Ha** (converged, 459 s at 8 OpenMP threads): **+1028.7 mHa
recovered, 99.6 % of the gap**. It is also **~8x faster** -- the untailed
EWALD_3D route it replaces costs ~4848 s -- because the promotion swaps the J
machinery rather than adding cderi cost to an existing one.

The resolution happens *before* the dense-core parity classifier, so the tail
also clears the `+PARITY_HELD` provenance tag rather than leaving a corrected
number still labelled held, which would be a worse artifact than the honest
untailed one.

Scope is deliberately narrow and does **not** reopen the documented decision
that multi-k does not auto-size the tail. That decision's rationale is the
~40x cderi build cost of adding a tail to a machinery that is already the
cached-Lpq GDF J -- KRHF, hybrids, and both open-shell drivers -- and it stands
untouched for them; whether *they* should auto-tail remains the open maintainer
call the code records. Pure DFT is the one branch where the rationale is
inverted by measurement, since more accurate and cheaper is not a trade-off.
Sparse cells are unaffected: the classifier is basis- and cell-driven, resolves
no tail there, and leaves the EWALD_3D default bit-identical.

**A residual remains and is a separate defect.** After the tail, the cell sits
**-3.79 mHa** from PySCF and **-4.44 mHa** from CRYSTAL -- roughly 23x the
documented ~0.16 mHa shared real-space-truncation floor, so it is not that
floor. It survives a parity-sized tail and is filed separately as **#526** --
where the sharpest lead is that the Gamma leg of this same class closes to
+1.3 uHa on the same cell and basis once tailed, so the multi-k leg is ~3000x
worse than its own Gamma twin. #518 is answered on the -1033 mHa mechanism
only. One further consequence now visible: on a dense-core cell a `KUKS(M=1)`
run no longer reproduces its `KRKS` twin, and carries `+PARITY_HELD` where the
KRKS run does not.

`tests/test_periodic_k_gdf.py` pins the routing without an SCF
(`test_multik_pure_ks_auto_tails_dense_core`), the negative control on a sparse
cell where the classifier does not fire
(`test_multik_pure_ks_sparse_cell_keeps_ewald3d`), and the end-to-end default
route as a slow gate
(`test_multik_krks_default_auto_tail_closes_dense_core_offset`). The
pre-existing IID 146 control that asserted the dense-core default keeps
EWALD_3D routing was pinning this defect and is updated, not weakened -- its
"defaults unchanged" role moved to the sparse cell. Fail-first on the unfixed
tree: 2 behavioural failures (both the run reaching an EWALD_3D J entry point),
0 missing-symbol; the negative control passes on both sides.

### Fixed: the DFTB0 placeholder-repulsive warning was silent on the systems that motivated it (issue #306, 2026-08-29)

`DFTB0RepulsivePlaceholderWarning` was added so that no absolute DFTB0 energy
could be promoted as chemistry while the repulsive is an `A/R^12` placeholder.
Its predicate was `has_repulsive_pair()` -- true when the parameter set carries
a table row for the pair -- and that is not the same question. `dftb0_default`
stores every built-in pair as `{A, B = 0}` with an empty spline, so
`eval_repulsive` takes the identical `A/R^12` branch for the tabulated tier as
for the combining-rule fallback; only the value of `A` differs (a hand-rounded
constant instead of `100*U1*U2`). Measured on the shipped set, `E * R^12` is
constant to full double precision for C-C (60), H-H (5), O-O (40), H-O (15) and
N-N (80) exactly as it is for Si-Si (9) and Mg-O (11.1475).

The consequence was that the warning did not fire on the systems the issue was
filed about. The reported downstream symptom -- a carbon-chain EOS still
monotone at 2.5x compression -- is a C-C system, and C-C is tabulated, so that
compute wave ran silent. H2O, CH4, graphene and every other H/C/N/O system were
equally unwarned.

The predicate is now a functional probe of `repulsive_energy` itself: a pair is
a placeholder when `E * R^12` is constant across 2.0, 3.0 and 4.0 bohr. It
cannot drift from what the evaluator does, and it discriminates -- a
spline-fitted pair and a Born-Mayer `A*exp(-B*R)` pair both fail the power-law
test and are not reported. Three probe radii rather than two, so an exponential
cannot impersonate the power law by matching a single ratio.

No equation, solver, default, mixer or parameter value changed; this is
strictly the visibility gate widening to its intended scope. Shipping fitted
splines remains open and needs a validated DFT reference dataset.

`tests/test_semiempirical.py::TestRepulsivePlaceholderWarning` pins both tiers
(H2O and C-C now warn and name their pairs), the identity of the two tiers'
functional form, and the two negative controls. Fail-first on the unfixed tree:
3 behavioural failures, 5 passing.

### Fixed: T = 0 on a k-mesh filled bands per k point, so multi-k jobs reported negative band gaps (issue #85, 2026-08-28)

`vibeqc.smearing.apply_smearing` — the entry point every periodic backend
calls — took a per-k Aufbau on its `temperature == 0` branch: it filled the
lowest `n_occ_each` bands at **each k point independently**. It computed one
global midgap `mu` from the whole mesh and then did not use it.

A finite-k band calculation is one periodic system, so its occupations obey
one particle constraint over the full eigenvalue sum, not one constraint per k
(Weinert & Davenport, *Phys. Rev. B* **45**, 13709 (1992), Eqs. (3) and (8)).
Wherever a band crosses `mu` between k points the per-k fill therefore
occupies a state *above* the Fermi level at one k while leaving a state
*below* it empty at another. `periodic_runner._band_summary` classifies band
edges from exactly these occupations, so it then reported `CBM - VBM < 0` — a
nonphysical **negative indirect gap**, printed with `rc 0`.

On a two-k, three-band reproducer (bands `[-0.20, 0.30, 0.90]` and
`[-0.60, -0.50, 0.80]`, 2 e⁻/cell) the reported edges were VBM = -0.200000 Ha
and CBM = -0.500000 Ha for a gap of **-0.300000 Ha**; they are now
-0.500000 / -0.200000 for **+0.300000 Ha**. The archived production instance is
Si/def2-SVP/PBE at 6×6×6: a **-0.080825-Ha** indirect gap with exactly 14
occupied bands forced at every k point.

Multi-k closed-shell now takes the same one-global-Fermi-level fill the native
multi-k GDF route adopted in `60104fc01` and the C++ k-point routine
(`compute_closed_shell_kpoint_occupations`) already used. This closes a split
between them: the shared dispatcher and `periodic_k_gdf._occupations_per_k`
returned *different* occupations for the same mesh, so which answer a job got
depended on which backend ran it. Affected routes were Ewald-3D multi-k
RHF/RKS, BIPOLE RKS multi-k, and the GAPW multi-k routes.

**Bounded blast radius.** The global fill differs from the per-k fill only
where the per-k fill was wrong:

* **Gapped meshes are bit-identical** — when the electron count lands exactly
  on a group boundary, the occupied set is the same `{0, 2}` arrays and `mu`
  is the same midgap value. No insulator result moves.
* **Γ-only and molecular callers are untouched** — one spectrum has nothing
  for a shared `mu` to reorder, so they keep the historical branch, mirroring
  the `eps_per_k.size() > 1` guard the C++ routine already takes.
* **Open-shell is unchanged.** `apply_smearing_open_shell` documents its T = 0
  branch as deliberately bit-identical to the legacy per-spin per-k Aufbau, so
  it is left alone and raised as an open ask on #85 rather than changed here.

Band-overlap meshes now occupy a different number of bands at different k
points, and a degenerate group cut by the particle constraint takes one shared
fractional occupation so mesh ordering cannot break its symmetry. That is a
sharp `T → 0` ensemble, not positive-temperature smearing.

**New fail-closed on two routes that cannot represent that state.** The
Ewald-3D multi-k (`run_rhf_periodic_multi_k_ewald3d`,
`run_rks_periodic_multi_k_ewald3d`) and BIPOLE RKS multi-k
(`run_pbc_bipole_rks`) drivers build their `T = 0` density from a single fixed
`C[:, :n_occ]` slice at every k, which cannot express a differing per-k
occupied count. Pairing that slice with the global occupations would converge
one density and report the band edges of another, so those sites now raise
`NotImplementedError` naming the per-k occupied counts and pointing at
`smearing_temperature > 0`, `bz_integration="gilat"`, or the multi-k GDF route.
Only band-overlap meshes at `T = 0` reach the guard — exactly the population
that was producing the negative gaps. Giving those routes the
density-from-occupations build the GDF route already has is the remaining half,
tracked as GitLab #509.

The multi-k GAPW routes need no guard: they already build the density from the
occupations `apply_smearing` returns, so they simply become correct.

**A second defect in the same reporting path, reachable only once the fill is
global.** `periodic_runner._band_summary` skipped any k point that lacked
*either* an occupied or a virtual state. Under a per-k fill that never happens
— every k has exactly `n_occ` occupied bands — but under one global Fermi
level a band-overlap mesh can leave a k point with every band above `mu`, and
skipping it hid its virtual states from the CBM search. On the two-k
reproducer the block then reported CBM = +0.80 Ha at the *occupied* k instead
of -0.20 Ha at the empty one: a **1.300000-Ha "direct" gap in place of the
true 0.300000-Ha indirect one**. The VBM and CBM are independent maxima over
the mesh, so each k now contributes whichever half it has; only the per-k
*direct* gap, which is genuinely undefined without both, is still skipped. When
no k point has both, that row now reads `n/a` instead of rendering the
`+1e300` sentinel as a number.

## [v0.15.153] - 2026-08-29 - *Neese's Cheetah*

Fourteen entries. The theme is disclosure: three of them make a quantity the
code already computed *visible* to whoever reads a result, after a week in
which several defects turned out to be things the project knew and could not
see from a run.

**What this release fixes.** BIPOLE's multi-k exchange carried a q=0
finite-size gauge — −2.88 Ha on MgO — folded silently into `e_exchange`. It now
appears as `e_exchange_finite_size` with an explicit *of which q=0 finite-size*
row on all four drivers, and the gauge constant collapses from **eleven
hand-rolled copies across five modules**, including the analytic gradient, into
one definition guarded by an AST scan (#82). The mandatory post-loop
non-incremental Fock build now announces itself before it starts and emits
`scf_final_density_begin/end`, the first carrying the loop's energy *before* the
expensive phase, so a wall-clock kill can no longer destroy a converged result
(#115). `bugctl close` applies the workflow transition rather than only the
state change — 86 of 371 closed issues had been carrying a stale workflow label
and none carried a resolution (#510) — and a landed fix now auto-queues an
independent verifier instead of waiting for a human to notice (#507).

Also: the shipped PM6/PM7 parameters are correctly attributed to MOPAC rather
than Stewart's tables, verified by matching all 118 values exactly at six
decimals (#440); the GFN2 parameter cache honours XDG so it can be seeded on a
cluster (#127); and TDA is matrix-free on a genuinely matrix-free Davidson
(#506).

**What this release does NOT fix.** The STO-6G hydrogen tables in `basis.cpp`
are wrong — ζ=1.24-prescaled data scaled a second time, fitting worse than the
STO-3G row in the same file — and the remedy is a maintainer decision (#44).
The article's sealed reference table still fills the BIPOLE MgO row from a
value retired on 2026-06-16, which holds a paper row at +643.4 mHa where the
correct reference gives +5.19 mHa (#513). `test_run_periodic_job_bipole_rks_h2o_pbe0_default_cutoffs_track_pyscf`
is red on `main` and absent from the known-reds baseline (#514). And #119's
default-accelerator repair is landed but still unverified.

### Fixed: a neutral CCM route's fail-closed message named the wrong entry point (issue #498, 2026-08-28)

`run_ccm_rks_gdf` on a vacuum-padded declared-3-D cell correctly refused, but
the `NotImplementedError` opened with `run_ccm_rhf_gdf:` -- a function the
caller never called, in a different module from the one they were using.

Both routes delegate to the shared `_ccm_gdf` helper, which hardcoded
`who="run_ccm_rhf_gdf"` when invoking the IID 291 guard. The four unshared
entry points each passed their own name and were unaffected, which is exactly
why the one shared path went unnoticed. `_ccm_gdf` now takes `who`, and both
public callers pass their own name explicitly rather than one of them
inheriting the default -- so neither can silently acquire the other's identity.

The guard itself always fired correctly; only the attribution was wrong. No
numerical result changes.

`tests/test_ccm_guard_attribution.py` pins the refusal's attribution for all
nine public neutral routes (four GDF, one RI-neutral, four direct). Verified to
discriminate: with the fix reverted it fails on exactly the two shared-helper
routes and the other seven stay green. Guard-only, so it runs in under a
second.

### Fixed: the GFN2-xTB parameter cache is seedable, not hardwired to `$HOME` (issue #127, partial, 2026-08-28)

`gfn2_params._CACHE_DIR` resolved `Path.home() / ".cache" / "vibeqc"`
unconditionally. It was the only cache in the tree that did: `vibeqc.fetch`,
`basis_filter` and `mlip.mace` all resolve an override, then
`$XDG_CACHE_HOME`, then `~/.cache`. The consequence was operational, not
cosmetic. `docs/user_guide/reference_data.md` documents the offline-cluster
remedy as "rsync `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/vibeqc/` to the cluster", and GFN2 was the
one thing that remedy could not reach, so every host had to fetch its own
copy. When the site_i compute nodes lost outbound network, all 78 GFN2 rows
failed at once with `GFN2ParameterUnavailableError`.

The cache root now follows the house precedence:
`$VIBEQC_GFN2_CACHE_DIR`, else `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/vibeqc/`, else
`~/.cache/vibeqc/`. With neither variable set the path is byte-identical to
before, so no existing deployment's cache moves.

Also documented, because the inventory did not mention GFN2 at all: the
parameters are LGPL-3.0-or-later upstream `xtb` values, fetched on demand and
never bundled, now a `docs/license.md` section of their own with the seeding
recipe.

**This is a partial fix.** Seeding still has to happen: a host with no
network and no seeded cache still cannot run GFN2. Closing #127 as written
means bundling the LGPL-3.0 parameter file into an MPL-2.0 distribution,
which is a maintainer licensing decision under CLAUDE.md § 1 and § 11, not an
implementation agent's, and CLAUDE.md § 1's own guidance for restrictive
