terms is the on-demand fetcher this code already uses. The issue stays open
on that question.

### Fixed: the shipped PM6/PM7 parameters are MOPAC's, not Stewart's published tables (issue #440, 2026-08-28)

`docs/license.md` declared the inline PM6 H/C/N/O/F values as *transcribed
from the published method paper*, and the runtime `ParameterSetMetadata`
reported `license = "published parameter table"` for them. Both were wrong,
and wrong in the direction that under-declares an obligation: the numbers are
copied from MOPAC's **Apache-2.0** `parameters_for_PM6_C.F90`, exactly as
`pm6_params.py`'s own header and its `_PM6_MOPAC_CORE` dict name have said all
along.

Established mechanically against the upstream file rather than asserted: all
**118** shipped PM6 values — 88 element parameters across H/C/N/O/F plus 30
diatomic `alpb`/`xfac` entries — reproduce `parameters_for_PM6_C.F90` at its
six published decimals, with **zero** mismatches. The same check puts the 53
inline PM7 element values on `parameters_for_PM7_C.F90` (corrected
2026-09-06: the inline PM7 *pair* table did not match that file and was
replaced; see the #440 entry of that date). This complements the
negative half already on the issue: none of these values occurs anywhere in
Stewart 2007, whose nearest number to `C uss = -51.089653` is 21 away.

No parameter value changed, so no energy changes and the content hashes are
untouched. What changed is what vibe-qc *says* about them:

* `docs/license.md` now carries the Apache-2.0 terms for the inline PM6 set,
  the inline PM7 set, and — previously absent from the inventory entirely —
  the bundled `pm7_mopac_params.toml` cache, together with the Apache-2.0
  § 4(c)/(d) copyright notice.
* The PM6 inline parameter identity is `published:pm6-mopac-inline-v1`
  (was `published:pm6-stewart-2007-inline-v1`) and reports
  `license = "Apache-2.0"`, matching its full-cache sibling.
* `pm6_params.py` / `pm7_params.py` carry the upstream copyright notice.
* New citation entry `mopac_moussa_stewart_2026` (Moussa & Stewart, *JOSS*
  **11**, 8025, DOI `10.21105/joss.08025`), routed from `pm6` / `upm6` /
  `pm7` / `upm7` / `pm6_seccm` so the attribution actually reaches users'
  `.out` / `.bibtex` / `.references`. The Stewart papers stay: they are the
  *method* references, MOPAC is the source of the *values*.

MOPAC remains an external program vibe-qc does not import or link
(CLAUDE.md § 10); only its published parameter files are redistributed.

### Fixed: `davidson_solve_matvec` is now genuinely matrix-free (issue #506, 2026-08-28)

It was not. It applied the caller's operator to all `n` unit vectors, assembled
the dense matrix, discarded the diagonal it was handed (`(void)diag;`) and
called the explicit kernel — costing the `n × n` allocation the caller asked to
avoid, plus `n` callbacks. Strictly worse than passing the matrix in directly.
Measured on a 2987-dimensional TDA operator for 8 roots: **2987 operator
applications, 104.7 s**, against 11.6 s for simply building the matrix and
calling `eigh`. The eigenvalues were right, so only an application count
catches it.

Both entry points now share one operator-parameterised kernel
(`davidson_kernel_impl`), so the operator reaches the algorithm through a block
product and its diagonal. Keeping a single implementation matters: #503's two
defects live in that loop, and a second transcription would have to carry them.
The explicit path is a thin wrapper and the public signature is unchanged. A
redundant `AV = A·V` in the collapse — whose result was immediately overwritten
— is also gone; invisible for a dense gemm, a whole extra block of operator
applications when matrix-free.

Same problem, after: **118 operator applications, 5.3 s** — a 25× reduction in
applications and 2.7× faster than dense, agreeing to 7.6e-13 Ha.

### Added: TDA excitation energies can be found iteratively (2026-08-28)

`run_tddft_tda` now solves the Casida A eigenproblem matrix-free above
`TDA_DAVIDSON_MIN_DIM` (2000) and densely below it. Forming A costs `dim²`
doubles *on top of* an `eri_mo_ovov` tensor of the same size, and `eigh` is
`O(dim³)`, to obtain the handful of roots a TDDFT run wants — for
adenine-thymine/cc-pVDZ, a 17,204-dimensional matrix (2.2 GB) for ~10 roots.

The threshold is measured, not guessed. cc-pVDZ, 8 roots, dense against
iterative: 0.38× at dim 380, 0.29× at 480, 1.25× at 1920, 1.86× at 2912, 1.34×
at 2987 — so dense genuinely wins below ~1000 and the gate sits on the
conservative side of the crossover. The margin grows with dimension, since
dense is `O(dim³)` with a `dim²` allocation while the iterative path is
`O(dim²)` per application at a root count that does not grow with the system.

Both paths solve the same operator and agree to ~1e-12 Ha, pinned in
`tests/test_tddft_davidson.py` (blocking T1: the two are selected by a
dimension threshold, so a defect would surface only on systems too large for a
dense cross-check).

### Changed: `_build_tda_matrix` is vectorised (2026-08-28)

It was a quadruple Python loop over `(i, a, j, b)` — 91 % of the dense TDA cost
at dim 380, 63 % at 1920, 47 % at 2987. `(ia|jb)` already sits in
composite-index order, so it reshapes for free; `(ij|ab)` needs one transpose.
Dense TDA at dim 2987 drops from 13.65 s to 6.03 s, which benefits every
existing TDDFT run since that is the path they take. Output is **bit-identical**
to the loop (max difference exactly 0.0 across four c_x / kernel
configurations).
### Added: a landing now emits a verification queue a distinct actor can pick up (issue #507, 2026-08-28)

`bugctl land` recorded `LANDED` and then waited for a human. Measured on the
live broker 2026-08-28: **46** issues whose current fixer generation is
`landed`, **35 of them with no verifier lease and no verdict at all** — the
work done and banked nowhere, because every verification was dispatched by
hand, one lane at a time.

`GET /v1/verification-queue?actor_id=<actor>` and `bugctl verify-queue` close
that gap. The queue is **derived per request** from `grants` and
`verifier_grants`: no table, no grant state, no provenance kind, and no event
kind is added, so no whitelist elsewhere has to learn about it, and it cannot
go stale the way a stored request would.

The property that makes it safe to dispatch from is that eligibility is
computed by **the same predicate that authorizes `verifier-claim`** —
`_verification_eligibility`, one function with two callers — so the queue
cannot advertise work the broker would refuse. Measured on the identical
five-issue scenario: the projection a dispatcher could build before this
offered 5 issues of which the broker refused 3 (`self_verify_denied`,
`invalid_provenance`, `already_claimed`); the queue offers 1, refuses 0, and
shows the other 4 with a machine-readable reason.

`actor_id` is required — an actor-less queue is exactly the harmful list, since
23 of the 46 landed generations were landed by one actor — and a recorded
verdict withholds a row from the queue without ever refusing the claim, so a
deliberate second opinion on an open HIGH-severity wrong-answer fix stays
available.
### Added: PM6-SECCM CCM Madelung embedding for 1-D and 2-D, with an acknowledgement gate (issue #217, 2026-08-29)

PM6-SECCM had no long-range electrostatics operator of any kind, while
its header and docstring asserted that neutral cells never need one.
That claim was measurably false: the WS-truncated monopole sum the PM6
Fock actually carries reproduces MgO rocksalt Madelung constants of
1.000000 / 2.412060 / 1.567431 / 1.737375 at 1x1x1 through 4x4x4
against the exact 1.7475645946 - errors of -43% to +38% with the sign
flipping on replica parity - and the truncated kernel is not positive
definite on the neutral subspace at even replica counts.

The opt-in `madelung=True` embedding is the MSINDO CCM operator, read
from the MSINDO sources rather than reconstructed: the classical
point-charge field enters the DIAGONAL of the Fock matrix
(`ccmfockcl.f`: `FA(K,K) = H(K,K) - MADELATOM(I)`), the self-energy
half is accumulated on the core charges (`MADELENRG += CZ(I) * 0.5 *
MADELATOM(I)`), and the potential is the full Ewald lattice sum minus
the WS-internal bare `1/r`, WS-weighted with the self image excluded
(`madelsum.f`, SMADEL branch), because the NDDO two-centre integrals
already carry everything inside the WS cell. The shipped
`indo::_madelung_potential_ewald` was verified to be a faithful port of
exactly that. The deposit is a real diagonal shift, so it preserves the
Hermiticity guard, and it is the derivative of the `1/2 q.V_mad` energy
with respect to the population, so the embedded SCF stays variational.
The Madelung component is recomputed from the converged density rather
than the pre-update iterate, so the reported term matches `1/2 q.V_mad`
at `result.density` exactly instead of only to the convergence
tolerance.

Three cyclic dimensions fail closed (maintainer decision D4): the
WS-folded remainder there has no thermodynamic limit, drifting -0.0233
Ha/cell per ln n out to 2662 atoms with no plateau, so an embedded 3-D
number would not converge with cluster size (issues #211, #425, #444).

A nontrivial cyclic topology now requires either `madelung=True` or an
explicit `allow_truncated_electrostatics=True`. This is a deliberate
behaviour break on existing callers, accepted because a silent 43%
electrostatics error is worse than a loud API change.

Note the embedded route legitimately differs from the isolated molecule
at a trivial one-cell topology whenever the cell is polar, since a
polar cell really does interact with its periodic images; the
bit-for-bit molecular-limit contract is a property of the unembedded
route. The shipped SCC-DFTB-SECCM embedding was measured to behave
identically (1.115e-04 Ha on polar H-F), so this is the established
convention rather than a PM6 quirk.

Citations (rule 8, same merge): new `janetzko_ccm_long_range_2002` and
`ewald_lattice_sum_1921` entries and a kernel-driven
`routes.methods.ccm_madelung_embedding` route that fires for any SECCM
run resolving a `madelung_*` electrostatics kernel, in every dimension
and for every adapter. This closes an existing hole - 3-D SECCM
madelung runs previously fired no lattice-sum citation at all.

### Added: SECCM translation-symmetry charge-spread diagnostic (issue #421, 2026-08-28)

Every GFN2-SECCM result now reports
`translation_symmetry_charge_spread`: the largest Mulliken-charge
spread within any orbit of the bound finite translation group. The
cyclic cluster makes the atoms of an orbit the same crystal site by
construction, so a state respecting the model's own translation
symmetry has spread zero, and any nonzero value is a symmetry
violation.

This closes a structural blind spot. Every existing acceptance screen
is a magnitude bound (shell rms, atomic rms, per-site maxima), and a
charge-disproportionated or state-hopped solution is not necessarily
large - it is wrongly distributed - so no magnitude bound can see it.
The orbit invariant is exact and free for SECCM: it needs only the
primitive vectors and replica counts the topology already attests, with
no symmetry detection, no geometry tolerance and no new dependency.

Per maintainer decision D3 the value is reported and never gated.
Production states currently carry a nonzero spread because GFN2 H0
coordination numbers are computed molecularly and break the cyclic
symmetry upstream of the SCC (issue #354): fcc Cu measures 0.903 e at
2x2x2 and 0.456 e at 4x4x4. A threshold chosen before #354 lands would
be wrong twice, so this exposes the number and leaves the judgement to
the caller. It is NaN on a failed-run result, which carries no charges
to diagnose - a diagnostic must not turn one route error into a
different exception.

Scope: this detects breaking of translation symmetry, which is the
charge-density-wave and state-hopping family. Atoms equivalent only
under a point operation, such as the two basis atoms of diamond, are
separate orbits here and carry no constraint; catching those needs the
crystallographic orbit and remains open.

### Fixed: the multi-k exchange finite-size gauge is now disclosed, and has one definition (issue #82, 2026-08-28)

**The filed defect was in the reference, not in vibe-qc -- and this project
had already established that and retired the reference, two months before the
issue was filed.** `docs/periodic_jk_routes.md` has carried the finding since
2026-06-16 ("the matched-k SHRINK-2-2 comparison is
exchange-convention-confounded. BIPOLE matches CRYSTAL's *k-converged* value,
NOT its coarse-mesh value"), with a maintainer-confirmed methodology correction
retiring the coarse value as a BIPOLE target, and
`tests/test_pbc_bipole_multik_ewald_split.py::test_mgo_shrink22_converged_matches_crystal_kconverged`
pins it. #82 was nonetheless filed on 2026-08-14 against the retired seal and
worked by four lanes. Re-running that exact deck with only `SHRINK` varied
(CRYSTAL23 1.0.1, native; SHRINK 2 reproduces the sealed value exactly)
independently reproduces the documented numbers and decomposes the offset to
0.04 uHa:

| SHRINK | IBZ k | E_HF (Ha) | vs SHRINK 8 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 3 | -271.85639651657 | **-0.63825276675** |
| 3 | 4 | -271.22261953049 | -0.00447578067 |
| 4 | 8 | -271.21780959957 | +0.00033415025 |
| 8 | 29 | -271.21814374982 | 0 |

`E_CRYSTAL(S8) - E_CRYSTAL(S2)` is +0.638252767 Ha (**99.19 %** of the filed
number) and `E_vibeqc(2,2,2) - E_CRYSTAL(S8)` is +0.005185582 Ha; they sum to
+0.643438348 Ha. CRYSTAL applies no Gygi-Baldereschi / probe-charge-Madelung
`q -> 0` correction, so its SHRINK-2 HF total sits 638 mHa from its own
converged value; vibe-qc applies one, so its (2,2,2) total reproduces
out-of-process PySCF KRHF `exxdiv='ewald'` on the same cell to **0.37 mHa**
(and that residual still contains a real 4.212 vs 4.210 Angstrom geometry
mismatch between the two sides of the filed pair). The exact-exchange-off
control -- same cell, same mesh, same code, PBE -- moves only +46.9 mHa from
SHRINK 2 to 8, and in the opposite direction.

**What was wrong on our side is that none of this was visible from a run.**
The convention was documented and tested, and four lanes still could not see
it, because `e_exchange` folded the `K_LR` and `xi_M . S D S` pieces together
and no artifact a lane actually reads named the gauge. The BIPOLE energy-component block now carries an
`of which q=0 finite-size` row, and `PBCBipoleEnergyComponents` an
`e_exchange_finite_size` field, on all four drivers (RHF/RKS/UHF/UKS). It is
the `xi_M` share alone -- exactly what `exchange_exxdiv='none'` removes, and
therefore exactly the amount by which a code that treats the singularity
differently will disagree at the same mesh. On MgO (2,2,2) it is -2.88 Ha.

Not fixed here, because it lives in another repository: the retirement never
reached the article repo's `calculations/ref_crystal_sealed.json`, where
`MgO_sto3g_RHF_shrink2` still carries `"fills": "P03 BIPOLE KRHF (2,2,2)"`
while the k-converged value sits in the same file one entry above
(`MgO_sto3g_RHF_gamma`, -271.21814374982). Re-pointing that one `fills`
assignment turns the paper's held +643.4 mHa gauge row into +5.19 mHa. Recorded
on the issue.

The `q + G = 0` constant `xi_M(BvK) - pi/(alpha^2 V n_k)` was hand-rolled at
**eleven call sites across five modules** -- four in the energy build, four in
the analytic gradient, and one each in the ROHF, ROKS and corrected-exchange
builders. Issue #478 landed that exact failure mode one level up: two copies of
the Ewald real-space cutoff desynced the gradient from the energy the moment
one was edited. It now has one definition,
`vibeqc.bipole_fock_ewald.exchange_q0_gauge_constant`, guarded by an AST scan
over the whole package rather than a module list that could drift.
Numerically inert: every reported energy is bit-identical.

### Fixed: the BIPOLE post-SCF finalisation phase is no longer invisible (issue #115, 2026-08-28)

Every BIPOLE driver ends its SCF loop with one non-incremental Fock build over
the committed density. It restarts the delta-D screening chain cold, so it
costs about a *first* SCF iteration rather than a last one -- ~22,000 s on a
six-basis-function LiH cell whose final iterations cost 819 s -- and it emitted
**nothing**. A 24 h canary converged at wall 67,593 s and then spent >= 5.22 h
in that phase in silence before the wall killed it, losing a converged result
and looking exactly like a hang.

The phase now announces itself before it starts (naming the build and why it is
expensive), reports its own wall time when it ends, and emits
`scf_final_density_begin` / `scf_final_density_end` to the structured log --
the first carrying the loop's energy, iteration count and convergence flag
*before* the expensive work begins, so a wall-kill inside finalisation can no
longer destroy the SCF result. Text through the existing `ProgressLogger`,
events through the existing `structured_log`; no new output surface.

### Fixed: the block Davidson returned wrong roots, and could never converge, for a partial spectrum (issue #503, 2026-08-28)

`davidson_solve` was correct when asked for the **whole** spectrum and broken
when asked for **a few** roots — which is what an iterative eigensolver is for.
Two defects in the subspace-expansion path, which a full-spectrum solve never
reaches because it converges in a single iteration:

**Corrections were not orthogonalised against each other.** Each new correction
vector was orthogonalised against the existing subspace `V` but not against the
other corrections generated in the same iteration. Those are preconditioned
residuals of neighbouring Ritz pairs and are frequently near-parallel, so a
nearly linearly dependent set entered the basis. `H_proj = VᵀAV` then acquired
spurious near-zero eigenvalues and, because `lambda` is sorted ascending, they
sorted *below* the true roots: the solver returned zeros and null eigenvectors
in place of the lowest eigenpairs. Requesting 8 roots of a 500-dimensional
operator returned 5 null columns (vector norms ~1e-8) padded into an `(n, 8)`
result — indistinguishable from converged roots by norm, eigenvalue *or*
residual, since ‖A·0 − 0·0‖ ≈ 0.

**The correction-acceptance threshold was the convergence tolerance.** `dnorm >
tol` rejected corrections once their norm fell to ~`tol` — exactly when they
were still needed — putting a floor under the attainable residual. The stalled
residual tracked the requested tolerance at 3.0×, 4.7×, 3.1× and 3.5× for
`tol` = 1e-3, 1e-5, 1e-6 and 1e-8. It could not converge at *any* tolerance.
Linear dependence is a property of the vector, not of the caller's tolerance,
so the test is now an absolute 1e-12.

The two interacted, which is why they survived: the second prevented
convergence from ever being signalled, so a corrupted basis usually looked
"unconverged" rather than "wrong". Fixing either alone would have looked like a
partial fix.

Measured, 8 roots of a 500-dimensional operator:

| tol | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 1e-4 | never converged, 200 iters, 8 null columns | **converged, 4 iters**, error 7.2e-10 |
| 1e-6 | never converged, 200 iters | **converged, 5 iters**, error 4.8e-14 |
| 1e-8 | never converged, 200 iters | **converged, 6 iters**, error 1.2e-14 |

and the configuration that reported success while wrong — n=200, `n_eig=4`, no
caller guess — goes from `converged=True` at **4.00e+00** error to
`converged=True` at **4.5e-14**.

**No production path changes.** `periodic_{rhf,rks,uhf}_ewald.py` set
`n_eig = Fp.shape[0]`, so they take the full-spectrum path: still converged in
one iteration, unaffected by either defect. That path is also opt-in
(`use_davidson` defaults to `False`), and the unified framework had no
production caller at all — which is why this went unnoticed. Every pre-existing
test in `tests/test_davidson.py` requests the full spectrum.

`tests/test_davidson.py` gains four regressions covering the partial-spectrum
path: true lowest roots with no null columns, convergence signalled without
burning the iteration budget, the specific wrong-roots case, and a guard that
the production full-spectrum path stays at one iteration. Fail-first on the
reverted kernel: the three partial-spectrum tests fail, the full-spectrum guard
passes.

### Added: `per_k_band_energies` / `frontier_bands` — the per-k band accessor carriers kept re-deriving (issue #505, 2026-08-28)

Reading "the bands of this result" looked trivial and was not. The layout
differs by driver:

| result | `mo_energies` | `mo_energies_k` |
|---|---|---|
| `PBCBipoleRHFResult` | per-k `List[np.ndarray]` | **absent** |
| GPW / GAPW multi-k | Γ-only array | tuple of per-k arrays |
| Γ-only drivers | a single 1-D array | absent |

vibe-qc exposed no public way to ask, so every consumer duck-typed the result
object — and the same class of mistake was made **twice in five days**, in two
different campaign carriers, each time *after* a certified SCF and each time
burning a full-node wall:

* **#15** indexed into a degenerate manifold: `float(b[n_occ - 1])` on an
  ndarray.
* **#135** branched on `mo_energies_k`, did not find it on a BIPOLE result, and
  fell back to `eps_k = [mo_energies]` — wrapping the whole per-k list as one
  pseudo-k. Its guard `len(b) > n_occ` then counted *k-points* instead of
  *bands* and passed, so `float(row)` raised.

Measured on a real converged run (H₂/STO-3G, 6-bohr cube, k = (2,1,1),
E = −1.1944690859739715 Ha), the two routes a consumer actually had were both
wrong, and **only one of them was loud**:

```
true       homo -0.5958697315  lumo  0.7875529291  gap 1.3834226606 Ha
wrapping   TypeError: only 0-dimensional arrays can be converted to Python scalars
flattening homo -0.6193305389  lumo -0.5958697315  gap 0.0234608073 Ha
```

The flattening route — the pattern used elsewhere in the tree when
`mo_energies_k` is absent — raises nothing. It mixes the two k-points into one
list, so an **occupied** band at the other k-point is reported as the
conduction band: a 1.3834 Ha insulator rendered as a 0.0235 Ha near-metal, on a
converged SCF, with rc 0.

`vibeqc.per_k_band_energies(result)` returns one 1-D array per k-point for any
periodic result shape, and `vibeqc.frontier_bands(result, n_occ)` returns a
`FrontierBands` with `homo` / `lumo` / `gap` / `homo_k` / `lumo_k`. The VBM is a
maximum over every sampled k and the CBM a minimum, so an indirect gap is found
correctly and a degenerate manifold reduces to a scalar by construction (#15).
`n_occ` is validated against the number of **bands**, a 2-D per-k block is
rejected by name as the #135 signature, and a ragged per-k set is refused
rather than padded.

`tests/test_bipole_per_k_band_accessor.py` runs a real converged multi-k BIPOLE
SCF rather than a constructed object, because the whole defect is that the shape
of a *real* result was not what a reader assumed. At the parent 10 fail / 3
pass; the 10 are all missing-symbol, which is what a missing-API defect looks
like, and the 3 that pass are the behavioural measurements above — they
reproduce the crash and the wrong gap on both sides by design.

### Fixed: the .system manifest declares the coupled-cluster integral route (issue #23, 2026-08-28)

`run_job(method="ccsd(t)")` has silently selected density fitting since the
correlated route shipped, and the only declaration was human-readable prose in
the `.out` (`Algorithm = DF-CCSD(T)`). A machine reader of the `.system`
manifest could not tell a DF leg from a conventional one, so a
DF-vs-conventional parity pair was scoreable rather than refusable -- the exact
hole #23's limb (b) describes (two published parity cells compared a silently
density-fitted vibe-qc leg against a conventional ORCA leg, and the residual
was read as method error). The CC execution block now stamps the executed
route into the manifest's `[run]` section through the existing late-bound
`update_run_fields` extension point (precedent: #344 `runtime_backend`, #426
band edges) *before* the CC step runs: `cc_density_fit` (bool),
`cc_auxiliary_basis` (resolved RI basis, exactly `""` when conventional), and
`cc_algorithm` (e.g. `DF-CCSD(T)` / `CCSD(T)`). A conventional run records
exactly `false` / `""`, never an absent or approximate field.

### Fixed: open-shell Gamma GDF records the resolved RSGDF tail (issue #490, 2026-08-28)

The open-shell Gamma GDF drivers (`run_pbc_gdf_uhf` / `run_pbc_gdf_uks`) resolve
the same auto-sized RSGDF high-`|G|` tail as the closed-shell driver but never
recorded it, so an open-shell cross-route comparison could not assert matched
reciprocal support the way the closed-shell one can after #307. The two
open-shell result classes now carry `rsgdf_tail_ke_cutoff` and
`rsgdf_ke_cutoff` and the drivers populate them with the resolved values, and
the open-shell multi-k result mirrors the closed-shell multi-k surface
(base mesh recorded, tail field present and `None` on a route that applies no
tail). `tests/test_pbc_gdf_compcell.py` pins the explicit-request, the
no-request, the multi-k, and (slow lane) the tight-core auto-size recording.

## [v0.15.152] - 2026-08-28 - *Neese's Cheetah*

Eighteen entries, and the centre of gravity has moved from the bug ledger to
the code it tracks. Two are wrong-answer fixes on shipped periodic routes, four
repair the campaign carriers that produce the project's benchmark data, and the
remaining ledger work closes the identity gap that let two agents in one
checkout act as the same principal.

**What this release fixes.** BIPOLE sized its one-electron Ewald real-space sum
from an AO-overlap length rather than from the pinned alpha, truncating a term
that decays only as 1/L — and getting *worse* with box size. The residual falls
from 2.27e-4 to **1.7e-11 Ha·bohr** and the distance to PySCF GDF on H2/12-bohr
improves from +0.4454 to **+0.1973 mHa** (#478). The molecular semiempirical
constructor accepted an exactly-zero total as ordinary data, which is the
legacy BUG-024 signature of 300 iterations emitting `E = 0.0000000000`; it now
refuses, with a pinned exemption for the one system where zero is correct — a
bare proton has no electrons (#160). GFN2's H0 electronegativity correction
used a Pauling table truncated at Z ≤ 10, so every heteronuclear heavy pair
computed a wrong coupling — Na-Cl got *no* correction at all where it needed
one, and Cu-O got a wrong one rather than none (#433).

On the carriers: artifact stems keep their dots (#254), kill deadlines are
sized from the granted reservation rather than a per-case guess (#120), and a
judged release is reconciled against its artifacts so one bundle cannot report
results from two different binaries (#122). CCM refuses a non-integer nrep mesh
instead of silently truncating it (#390).

**What this release does NOT fix.** #119's default-accelerator repair is on
`main` but still unverified. #142/#154's mesh-independent 3.45 Ha GDF
over-binding stands, and two attempts to re-measure it were OOM-killed at
200 GB and 900 GB — the route exceeds 900 GB for a 2-atom cell at the Γ point,
which may be the more tractable defect. `def2-qzvp-rifit` still omits every 3d
and 4d transition metal (#483). And #43's GFN2 residual is *not* the regression
it was briefly filed as: xtb's total already contains dispersion, so the figure
of record compared a dispersion-free vibe-qc energy against a
dispersion-inclusive xtb total (#502).

### Fixed: a campaign verdict now reads which binary actually ran (issue #122, 2026-08-28)

The loop's ledger carries `release_tag` / `release_sha`, and both are written
from the **dispatch item** (`agentic-loop/supervisor/loop_supervisor.py`).
`record_campaign_verdict` then validated them against the dispatch **contract**
— assumption against assumption. Neither failure issue #122 reports could be
detected from inside the loop at all:

* **A bundle that straddled a fleet roll.** `rp219a07cnvq` ran cases 1–7 on
  v0.15.130 and cases 8–18 on v0.15.133. Its benzene-water interaction energy
  is therefore a difference of two binaries rather than a measurement, and every
  within-bundle comparison from that job is silently invalid. Unpinned
  latest-at-dispatch is deliberate campaign policy *between* jobs; a single
  bundle straddling a roll is not.
* **A ledger release that was simply wrong.** Every site_a arm of that wave ran
  v0.15.134 (`856899989c0a`) while the ledger recorded v0.15.132 — wrong for the
  whole host, and caught only because someone read the per-artifact manifests by
  hand.

vibe-qc has been writing the truth all along: every job's `.system` manifest
carries a `[vibeqc]` table with `version` and `git_sha`. Nothing in the loop
read it. New `agentic-loop/manifest_release_identity.py` does, and
`record_campaign_verdict.record` now gates on it alongside the existing
artifact-status gate:

* members that disagree with **each other** refuse the verdict (a bundle is not
  a measurement unless it is one binary);
* members that agree but contradict the **ledger** refuse the verdict;
* when no manifest exists to read, the verdict still records — an unfetched or
  external arm is not evidence of anything — but the judged job event is
  labelled `release_source = "dispatch-assumption"` rather than
  `"manifest-verified"`, which is issue #122's ask (b): an assumed release must
  never be recorded as though it had been measured.

The judged event gains `release_source`, `manifest_release_version`,
`manifest_release_sha` and `manifest_member_count`; the dispatch-time
`release_tag` / `release_sha` are still recorded, unchanged, beside them. No
ledger TSV schema change.

`tests/test_agentic_loop_release_identity.py`: at the parent 4 fail / 2 pass —
2 behavioural (the recorder accepts a verdict on a bundle built by two
different releases, and on a job whose artifacts contradict its ledger row) and
2 on the new labelling fields, none on a missing symbol.

### Fixed: the AIC7 wave driver sizes its kill deadlines from the reservation vq granted (issue #120, 2026-08-28)

`studies/aiccm-real-gamma/aic7.py` enforced a fixed global budget of 64800 s
(18 h — its own help text admitted the value was "5 h under a 23 h wall") and
fixed per-mode rung caps of 2700 / 3600 / 7200 / 10800 s, none of which
consulted the reservation the job was actually given. vq exports it as
`VQ_WALL_TIME_SECONDS` to every job it dispatches, local and scheduler alike
(`vibe-queue/src/vq/daemon.py`, `_vq_job_env`), and the driver already read it
— but only to *validate* against, never to size from.

Both directions were wrong. Under a **long** grant the driver stopped early and
killed rungs at a cap unrelated to the wall: on a 3-rung ladder inside a 24 h
reservation the first rung was killed at 10800 s with ~21 h of the grant
unspent. Under a **short** grant the 18 h constant failed the run closed — a
4 h reservation was refused outright by
`--budget-s must leave at least 300s of the vq wall for final output`.

This is the shape issue #120 measured on the campaign carriers: 206 members
across 202 cases killed by the harness rather than by the scheduler, one bundle
consuming 2.11 h of a 16 h reservation and still losing two BH9 members at
3540 s and 3660 s.

Now, when a reservation is exported and the flag was not passed:

* `--budget-s` defaults to the whole granted wall less
  `WALL_FINALIZATION_GRACE_S`. No rung can outlive it — the allotment is still
  clipped to `remaining - BUDGET_KILL_GRACE_S`, so every rung completes strictly
  inside the budget line, which is what makes spending the whole wall safe.
* `--rung-cap-s` stops being a ceiling and becomes a **floor**: each rung may
  take `usable / rungs_remaining`, never less than the declared cap. The
  divisor is recomputed from the actual remaining budget at every rung, so a
  rung that finishes early returns its share to the pool.

Passing either flag explicitly still pins it as a hard value (issue #120's ask
2, a declared per-wave parameter). With no reservation exported — a bare local
run — both keep their historical constants exactly.

Each rung record now carries `cap_basis` (`reservation-share` or `fixed-cap`),
`cap_floor_s` and `rungs_remaining_at_start`, and the results document carries
`vq_wall_time_s`, `budget_source`, `rung_cap_source` and `rung_cap_is_floor`,
so a judging pass can tell "we ran out of our own patience" from "we ran out of
wall" without reconstructing the argv. The existing `budget_killed` vs
`rung_timeout` distinction (ask 3) is unchanged.

Seven new cases in `tests/test_aic7_driver.py`; at the parent 7 fail / 29 pass,
3 behavioural (18 h spent of a 24 h grant; a 4 h grant refused; the first rung
allotted 10800 s where its share is 28680 s) and 4 on the newly recorded
provenance fields, none on a missing symbol. The negative control — the same
`main` entry point, same argv, no reservation exported — records 10800 s
exactly on both sides.

### Fixed: an `output=` stem containing a dot no longer truncates or collides (issue #254, 2026-08-28)

`output=` is a documented path **stem** — `docs/user_guide/output_files.md`
states the emitted files are `{output}.out`, `{output}.system`,
`{output}.molden`, i.e. the suffix is *appended*. Every artifact path was in
fact derived with `pathlib.Path.with_suffix`, which **substitutes**: it treats
everything after the final dot of the final path component as a replaceable
extension. For any stem carrying a dot — a lattice constant, a scale factor, a
tolerance, a version — the two differ:

```
Path("output_scale_4.08").with_suffix(".out")        -> output_scale_4.out
Path("output_scale_4.12").with_suffix(".out")        -> output_scale_4.out
Path("lih-gdf-rhf-a4.0082-k222").with_suffix(".out") -> lih-gdf-rhf-a4.out
```

The calculations still converged and still exited 0; only the captured output
was renamed onto a shared path, so each point of a scan overwrote the previous
one. Measured at the parent, a nine-point EOS ladder declared **one** distinct
`.out` path instead of nine, losing 8 logs, 8 manifests, 8 orbital files, 8
geometries, 16 citation files, 8 crash-dump declarations and 8 QVF archives —
64 artifact files from a single ladder. Nothing warned; the loss is visible
only by counting files against members, which is why it recurred three times
before being root-caused.

The truncation was also *partial*, which is what made it hard to see: the two
`{stem}.population.*` artefacts were already built by appending, so a dotted
job emitted a mixture of full-stem and truncated names in one directory.

`vibeqc.output._stem_paths.stem_sibling` now performs the append, and all 87
job-stem derivations across `output/plan.py`, `output/manifest.py`, the
`output/formats/*` and `output/citations/*` writers, `runner.py`,
`periodic_runner.py`, `qvf_job.py` and the double-hybrid dispatcher in
`__init__.py` use it. It returns the path unchanged when the name already ends
in exactly the requested suffix, which preserves the compound-name idiom the
periodic runner relies on (`{stem}.opt.xyz` handed to the `.xyz` writer stays
put) and keeps dot-free stems byte-identical to their historical names. A
suffix without a leading dot is now a loud `ValueError` rather than a silently
misnamed artifact.

Paths that are *not* stems keep substitution semantics deliberately, and are
unchanged: `write_system_manifest(out_path)` derives `.system` from the full
`.out` path, `scan.write_qvf` strips a real `.qvf`, and the `.tmp` sibling
writers append to `path.suffix`.

`tests/test_output_artifact_stem_dot_safety.py` pins the round trip: the
plan-level declaration, injectivity of every artefact role across a real EOS
ladder, two real SCF runs that must not overwrite each other, the dot-free
negative control, the `.opt.xyz` no-op, and a source guard over the three files
that name artefacts. At the parent it is 9 failed / 4 passed, all nine
behavioural or source-level and none a missing symbol.

### Fixed: bugctl identity is scoped to the session, not the checkout (issues #499, #501, 2026-08-28)

#495 moved bugctl's state from the working tree to the *checkout*, so a linked
worktree stops inheriting its clone's identity. That was half the defect. The
other half is that two agents in the **same** checkout were still one principal
to the broker: `agent_id` and `run_id` both lived in a directory keyed only by
the tree, and the broker binds a grant to `(issue, actor, run_id)`. The
consequence is recorded server-side on #205, whose `VERIFIER_CLAIM_GRANTED`
carries a run id belonging to a lane that never claimed it — a complete
verifier claim and a posted verdict under a borrowed identity. Independence
held in substance there (the fixer was a different actor), but the recorded
author was wrong, and `self_verify_denied` is evaluated against exactly that
field.

bugctl now resolves its state directory per **session** (`BUGCTL_SESSION_ID`,
else `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`). The first session to arrive *adopts* the
existing checkout directory rather than rotating it, so the change cannot
orphan grants a live lane already holds; every later session gets its own
subdirectory with its own run id, and finds no `config.json` there — so a
co-tenant falls through to the refused `local-agent` fallback instead of
silently answering as the owning lane. The refusal names the owning session
and #499. `doctor` gained a `state_scope` check reporting the scope, both
directories, this session, and who owns the checkout state and when; it fails
closed for a co-tenant. A shell with no session marker keeps the previous
checkout-scoped behaviour unchanged. Tokens and broker URLs are still
inherited from the checkout — a credential is not an identity.

Two related repairs from #501: `BUGCTL_RUN_ID` now overrides the persisted run
id without touching shared state (the process-local counterpart of
`BUGCTL_AGENT_ID`; the only repair previously available was editing a file
another lane might be using), validated against the character set the broker's
idempotency keys require. And minting a run id beside grant state that names a
different one is no longer silent — the command's result carries a `warnings`
entry naming the orphaned ids, because those grants can then be neither
heartbeated, landed nor released.

### Fixed: bugctl search sweeps for literal identifiers instead of trusting the index (issue #500, 2026-08-28)

`bugctl search` was a thin alias for GitLab's full-text index, which tokenizes
on `_`, `-` and `.`. A verification lane used its `count=0` as proof that no
other issue cited an artifact and wrote that into a posted verdict; the real
citing set was four issues. `search` now also sweeps title+description for a
literal case-insensitive substring and returns the union, each row labelled
`full-text` or `substring`.

The sweep runs on **every** query, not only the zero case. Sweeping only when
the index returns nothing was the first shape of this fix and is not enough:
measured live, `probe_slab_channel_isolation` returns #500 itself — whose body
quotes the identifier as a bare token — so the query never reaches zero while
still missing every issue that cites the file. A partial index hit is a false
negative carrying no zero to warn on, which is the more dangerous of the two.
After the fix that query returns #141, #203, #471 and #500 against 1 from the
index alone, at a cost of ~3 s. An empty result now carries an explicit caveat
that absence is not established and that note bodies were not searched, and
`--full-text` keeps the cheap index-only query for interactive use.
### Added: the GFN2 SCC energy and the published total are pinned apart (issue #502, 2026-08-28)

Issue #502 reported a 13.28 mHa GFN2-xTB regression on adenine "between main
`f3c4accd0` and `941caf57a`". **There is no regression, and no code changed.**
Rebuilt at both SHAs in a dedicated clone against one pinned parameter cache
(`~/.cache/vibeqc/gfn2_xtb_params.toml`, sha256 `6be784c5...`, byte-compared
before and after every measurement), the archived THIEL adenine frame gives
bit-identical numbers at both: SCC `-27.508108468392056` Ha, post-SCF D4
`-0.013278137295` Ha, published total `-27.521386605687525` Ha. The two
recorded "before" and "after" figures are the SCC energy and the total,
measured on the same code; their difference is the D4 term itself.

The filing's prime suspect is eliminated by inspection as well:
`git diff f3c4accd0..941caf57a -- cpp/src/semiempirical/methods/xtb/gfn2_parameters.cpp`
is comment-only (19 added lines of the issue #446 attestation, no code and no
constant), and the molecular GFN2 driver includes none of
`cpp/include/vibeqc/scf_convergence.hpp`, so no SCF/EDIIS/UKS commit in that
range can reach it.

What the confusion costs is real: `xtb`'s total energy already contains
dispersion (its output prints `-> dispersion` as a sub-term of the SCC
energy), so comparing vibe-qc's SCC energy against an `xtb` total reports a
residual that is mostly the missing D4 term. On this adenine frame that turns
the true -21.811 mHa residual into -8.5 mHa — 133x issue #43's 0.1 mHa gate,
and the -8.5 mHa figure of record on that issue.

`tests/test_gfn2_xtb.py::TestGFN2PublicEnergyIsDispersionCorrected` now pins
the two quantities apart: every public entry point returns exactly SCC + D4;
the D4 term clears the 0.1 mHa parity gate on CH4 and H2O, so the two values
are never interchangeable; and on H2 against the live `xtb` 6.7.0 total the
D4-corrected value sits 0.96 uHa away while the SCC-only value sits 50.47 uHa
away, a factor of 52. With the D4 term forced to zero, three of the five nodes
fail behaviourally on numbers. `docs/user_guide/semiempirical.md` states which
energy each entry point returns and that an `xtb` comparison must be
total-vs-total.

Closure criterion 4 of the filing — the parameter-cache digest in run
provenance — was already satisfied before it was asked for: a GFN2 `.system`
manifest carries `gfn2_cache_sha256` alongside `gfn2_parameter_sha256` and
`gfn2_d4_refdata_sha256`.

### Fixed: BIPOLE Ewald real-space cutoff now follows the pinned alpha (issue #478, 2026-08-28)

The BIPOLE drivers pin the Ewald splitting parameter to CRYSTAL's
`alpha = 2.8 / V^(1/3)` but sized the *real-space* half of the sum from
`lat_opts.nuclear_cutoff_bohr` — an AO-overlap length with no relation to
alpha. Because alpha scales with the cell, `erfc(alpha . L)` at the nearest
image is `erfc(2.8) = 7.5e-5` for a cubic cell of **any** side, so that fixed
cutoff truncated a term decaying only as `1/L`. The electron-electron erfc sum
was unaffected (`resolve_bipole_sr_image_extent` pads it to the smeared-kernel
range), leaving the electron-nuclear (`-2 N_e Z`) and nuclear-nuclear (`+Z^2`)
channels short and `-2 N_e Z + Z^2 = -N_e^2` of the neutral cell's monopole
triple uncancelled: a `+0.226 N_e^2 / L` mHa self-image in the Gamma molecular
limit, constant to 0.5 % across a 9x span in electron count and bit-identical
under `ewald_precision` because the cutoff never consulted the tolerance.

`_crystal_ewald_options` now floors `real_cutoff_bohr` at
`sqrt(-ln tolerance) / alpha` whenever an explicit alpha is pinned — the exact
inverse of `auto_alpha` in `cpp/src/ewald.cpp` and the same envelope
`probe_charge_madelung` already used — and the four BIPOLE drivers widen the
matching one-electron `nuclear_cutoff_bohr` so V_ne and E_nn stay paired. The
electronic `lat_opts_2e` cell set is untouched, so the
`clamp_bipole_nuclear_cutoff` invariant (unscreened nuclear tails must not
outrun the compensating electronic charge) still holds.

Measured on a single point charge in a cubic box against the simple-cubic
Madelung constant: the error falls from `-2.251e-4 / L` Ha (constant in
`err . L` for L = 20, 50, 80, 140 — exactly the dropped image tail) to
`-4e-10 / L`. In the SCF, He/Ne/Ar Gamma RKS-LDA now reproduce their molecular
energies to 1e-12 .. 1e-10 Ha across boxes of 35–140 bohr, and the residual
tracks `ewald_precision` (9.4e-8 at 1e-6, 1.7e-11 at 1e-8, -2.2e-13 at 1e-12)
instead of ignoring it. Both molecular-limit pins in
`tests/test_bipole_rks_molecular_limit.py` move by the predicted leak
(He/50 bohr 1.87e-5 Ha, Ar/50 bohr 1.52e-3 Ha) and now equal the molecular
values; two new regressions gate the scaling coefficient rather than an
absolute tolerance, which is what let this sit undetected inside the pinned
5.0e-5 / 2.0e-3 bands.

**A second finding from the same measurement: at the parent this sum had no
working convergence knob.** Sweeping `nuclear_cutoff_bohr` over 6, 12.5, 18.5,
25, 40 and 60 bohr on H2/STO-3G/SVWN in a 12-bohr box returned a bit-identical
energy, because `clamp_bipole_nuclear_cutoff` clamps the value back down to
`cutoff_bohr`. That is why #478 recorded the residual as invariant under
`nuclear_cutoff_bohr` 15 / 60 and read it as structural rather than as a
convergence parameter. It now converges under `ewald_precision`: the same
fixture is stable to 1.5e-13 Ha across 1e-8 .. 1e-14.

**Cross-code corroboration.** The one external comparison the change touches
moves toward the reference, not away from it: on H2/STO-3G in a 12-bohr box at
Gamma, the distance to PySCF 2.13 `RHF(cell).density_fit()` (`exxdiv='ewald'`,
run out of process) falls from **+0.4454 mHa to +0.1973 mHa**, a factor of 2.26.
PySCF computes its own converged Ewald nuclear repulsion, so this is an
independent check on the direction of the correction rather than a restatement
of it.

The two H2 fixed points in `tests/test_bipole_exact_ft_retirement.py` also move,
by an identical -2.484636e-4 Ha on both the padded SR+LR route and the exact-FT
oracle, so their 6.5995e-7 Ha route difference is preserved exactly - the leak
was in the shared one-electron gauge, not in either J route. Note that shift is
3.3x the asymptotic `0.225 N_e^2 / L` estimate: at L = 12 the Ewald `1/alpha` is
4.3 bohr, comparable to the AO-pair extent, so the erfc kernel is sampled inside
its steep region rather than at the image distance. The `1/L` law is the
large-box limit; on compact vacuum cells the leak is worse than it predicts.

Blast radius: the change is a no-op wherever `nuclear_cutoff_bohr` already
exceeds `sqrt(-ln tolerance) / alpha` (= 1.533 `V^(1/3)` at the 1e-8 default),
which holds for the library default of 25 bohr on compact primitive cells:
nuclear image-cell counts are unchanged for the MgO fcc primitive (531), the LiH
fcc primitive (603) and a 5x5x60 bohr slab (81). Vacuum boxes go from 1 to 19
nuclear image cells, and 19 is scale-invariant, so the cost never grows with
cell size. Fixtures that lower `nuclear_cutoff_bohr` below that radius do move.
### Fixed: `use_multipole_far_field` docstring states the enforced fail-closed gate (issue #472, 2026-08-28)

The `run_periodic_job` parameter comment still documented the pre-gate behaviour — "True forces the Saunders 1992 quartet-level bipolar far-field (G6) where the drivers support it" — while since cadcf9630/9fdc5a466 every explicit `True` raises `NotImplementedError` via `reject_bipole_quartet_far_field` (the dormant prototype does not preserve the exact route's three-translation Fock domain). The comment now states the enforced behaviour: `True` is rejected fail-closed in `run_periodic_job` and all four direct drivers, and `False` (the default) selects the exact four-centre traversal, the only supported route. The docstring was the wrong side; the gate and the `pbc_bipole` module docstrings were already correct and are unchanged.

### Fixed: the GFN2 physical-basin gate lives in one shared header (issue #411, 2026-08-28)

The five physical-basin gate constants (`kShellPopulationViolationTolerance`, `kShellRmsPolarizationLimit`, `kAtomicRmsPolarizationLimit`, `kLocalShellPolarizationLimit`, `kLocalAtomicPolarizationLimit`) and their predicates existed in two independently maintained copies: the SECCM adapter (`seccm/gfn2.cpp`) and the periodic Gamma driver (`methods/xtb/periodic_gfn2.cpp`), duplicated by the 1fc1dc73b port. A future recalibration of one copy would silently diverge the two routes' fail-closed behaviour. They now live once in `cpp/include/vibeqc/semiempirical/core/basin_gates.hpp` (constants plus `shell_populations_within_basin` and `charge_state_within_basin`), with both drivers consuming them through thin wrappers that keep their exposed entry points unchanged. The regression anchors are untouched: the Cu CDW basins still fail closed on both routes, the compressed 2x2x2 Cu cell still converges physical, and the localized-outlier predicate still rejects the 11.5 e counterexample.

### Fixed: a direct-vs-GDF parity assertion could not fail, and one producer field was not a measurement (issues #307, #308, 2026-08-28)

### Added: DFTB0-SECCM runs in one, two, and three cyclic dimensions (issue #412, 2026-08-28)

DFTB0-SECCM was gated to one dimension by two hand-written guards and
nothing else. Every stage below them is dimension-generic and is the
same code SCC-DFTB-SECCM already runs in 2-D and 3-D:
`assemble_weighted_dftb_h0` takes its dimension from the topology, the
gradient builds the same lattice matrix set and calls the same overlap
derivative, and the shared validator already accepted one to three
translations. The guards are removed, and the element scope becomes the
explicit repulsive-pair table instead of a hardcoded H/C list, which
widens it to H, C, N, O, F, P, S and Cl and all 36 of their pairs while
refusing an unparameterized pair by name.

Validated against the matched-mesh Bloch reference on an H2 molecular
crystal at replica counts 3, 4 and 5: agreement is 1e-13 to 1e-16
Ha/cell in every dimension, pinned by a new parametrized regression.
The fixture is deliberately weakly coupled so that the Wigner-Seitz
truncation error is negligible and the test isolates what it claims -
that the dimension-generic assembly is correct - rather than the
truncation convergence rate.

Per maintainer decision D2, the even-replica fail-closed gate stays
scoped to SCC-DFTB-SECCM and is deliberately NOT applied here: that
pathology is an SCC charge-map failure, and this charge-free route
shows no divergence at even replica counts even at 95.5% fractional
record ownership. For the same reason the Klopman-Ohno
thermodynamic-limit defect (#444) does not reach DFTB0-SECCM. No
citation route changes: with no parity convention in force, adding the
odd-cell reference here would be a dead citation.

### Fixed: the tight-core tail fix had no gate, and one parity assertion could not fail (issues #307, #308, 2026-08-28)

**Correction to this entry as first published.** It claimed the #307 tail fix
"landed without a single test on the class the defect lived in". That was
wrong: `tests/test_ccm_neutral_tail_parity.py` had already landed alongside
`78cb9aef6` with 16 gates, including end-to-end direct-vs-GDF parity on fcc Be
and diamond, each asserting that the *untailed* control still fails the same
tolerance -- the falsifying half this project cares about. The claim came from
checking `tests/test_ccm_direct.py` alone and generalising. That file is the
canonical tail gate; the tight-core case added here goes through the shared
`_assert_direct_gdf_parity` helper instead, which it does not exercise.

`_assert_direct_gdf_parity` compared the *direct* result's `exchange_q0`
against the module constant `BVK_EWALD` and never read the GDF one, so its
negative branch was unreachable -- `_ccm_gdf` sets `exchange_q0=""` whenever
its `active` read is false and this assertion could not have noticed. It now
reads both sides, requires the two routes to have resolved the same
`rsgdf_tail_ke_cutoff`, and refuses to compare results either side flagged
`parity_held`. A diamond/STO-3G `nrep=(1,1,1)` case exercises that helper on a
tight-core cell, with the LiH negative control pinned explicitly: LiH/STO-3G
resolves no tail, which is why every pre-existing control in that file passed
while MgO/STO-3G sat 0.49 Ha/cell from the GDF route.

`aiccm-2026/run_case_cmp.py` recorded `rsgdf_ke_cutoff_executed` by copying its
own `PINS` request, an `_executed` field that could not disagree with its
`_requested` twin. It is a real read from the driver now, with a pin-violation
check that has a reachable negative branch, plus the executed tail and the hold
flag. `PBCGDFResult` and `PeriodicKRHFGDFResult` gained the executed base
`rsgdf_ke_cutoff` that read requires.

`HANDOVER_AICCM_DIRECT_TORUS`'s D1 table and `HANDOVER_AICCM_A_TESTING`'s
headline are annotated for scope: the D1 rows are correct and never covered
the tight-core class, while all 8 A_TESTING headline systems *are* in it, so
their absolute per-atom numbers carry a hold their -a-vs--b agreement does not
address.

### Fixed: bugctl paginates reads by cursor, never by X-Total (issue #496, 2026-08-28)

`bugctl show` (and every other read) no longer cross-checks the `X-Total` / `X-Total-Pages` headers against the rows received. GitLab computes those counts on a relation that moves between the header and the body — notes are appended continuously on busy issues (measured 46/41 on #280 and 22/18 on #244) — so the reconciliation turned a benign race into a refusal of the whole read. Traversal now follows `X-Next-Page` to exhaustion and trusts the rows; a count disagreement alone never fails a read. Transport and parse failures mid-read, and a cursor that cannot be followed (malformed, repeated, or non-advancing), still fail closed — those are traversal-integrity failures, not count races, and returning a silently partial collection from a broken traversal is how a consumer asserts absence from page 1 of a larger set.
### Fixed: the broker says when it cannot judge `origin/main`, instead of reporting silence as success (issue #489, 2026-08-28)

The broker resolves landed SHAs against `BROKER_REPO_PATH`, a `vq admin
update`-managed checkout it must never fetch (CLAUDE.md § 15). Nothing else
fetched it either, so it trailed `origin/main` by however long since the
updater last ran — measured on example_hub at nearly three hours, with a
fully-formed ancestry that every caller read as usable. Two consequences,
both silent:

* Startup repair printed `abbreviated_shas_reconciled=0`, which reads as
  "nothing needed repair" and meant "could not tell". A single manual fetch
  turned that 0 into 9; the repairs had been blocked for a day, and the cause
  was found only by reading the source. The pre-existing INERT warnings fired
  only on a *missing* ancestry, never a stale one.
* `_main_contains_exact_sha()` gates the legacy-landed-import path, where
  "absent from `origin/main`" and "pushed, but not fetched here yet" are the
  same observation. A genuinely-pushed commit could be recorded as invalid
  provenance.

Since that checkout must stay read-only, the fix is a freshness *argument*
rather than a broker-side fetch. `_checkout_ancestry_status()` reports
`unset` / `unavailable` / `stale` / `fresh` — unknown freshness answers
`stale`, matching `_checkout_could_have_seen()`, so "cannot tell" is never
rendered as "fine". The startup line now prints
`abbreviated_shas_reconciled=ancestry_unavailable` when nothing could be
established, and `N/ancestry_stale` when the count is a lower bound, alongside
a warning naming the checkout's age. The legacy-import gate refuses retryably
with `provenance_unavailable` unless the checkout is current enough to
conclude; a positive membership proof still lands while stale, since fetching
can only add commits, never remove one. Behaviour is unchanged on a fresh
checkout.

Also settles the issue's open worry: all three recorded `UNPUSHED_LAND_DEMOTED`
generations (#124, #139, #145) were re-checked against an up-to-date clone, and
none of those SHAs exists as an object there — so every demotion was correct.
The issue's claim that `_main_contains_exact_sha()` drives that demotion is
inaccurate: it is driven by a recorded `VERIFY_FAILED` verdict, not by the
mirror.
### Fixed: a semiempirical route can no longer report an exactly-zero total energy (issue #160, 2026-08-28)

`SemiempiricalResult` — the single constructor every molecular semiempirical
route in `python/vibeqc/semiempirical/runner.py` funnels its answer through
(PM6/PM7, OMx, MSINDO, DFTB0, SCC-DFTB, GFN2-xTB, and the MSINDO SECCM
adapter) — now refuses a total energy of exactly `0.0` Ha or a non-finite one,
raising the new `SemiempiricalEnergyError` (a `RuntimeError` subclass). A
semiempirical total is an electronic term plus a core-core repulsion or
repulsive term, so for a system carrying electrons neither value is reachable;
both mean the route returned before computing a result. Previously such a row
was returned silently, and a dispatch lane gating on `converged` counted it as
data — the legacy BUG-024 signature, where PM6/norbornadiene on one host ran
300 SCF iterations emitting `E = 0.0000000000` at every iteration with no
exception. The gate is bit-exact rather than a tolerance band, so a
legitimately small total energy still reports, and it is independent of
`converged`: an unconverged run carrying a real energy is still returned.
Regressions drive the production `_run_pm6` route over a native result
carrying each value, with the same route and a real energy as the negative
control. The host-conditioned half of #160 (why that one host produced the
zero) is unchanged by this and stays open.

### Fixed: CCMSystem refuses a non-integer nrep mesh instead of truncating it (issue #390, 2026-08-28)

`CCMSystem` converted every explicit `nrep` component with `int(x)` before
validation, so `(1.9, 1, 1)` became `(1, 1, 1)`, `True` became `1`, and
`array([2.7, 1, 1])` became `(2, 1, 1)` -- the caller silently ran a
different cyclic Hamiltonian and normalization than the one requested.
Explicit meshes are now accepted only as exactly three non-boolean integer
components of value at least one (Python and NumPy integers, via
`operator.index`); floats (including integer-valued ones), strings, booleans,
non-finite values, and wrong lengths raise a bounded `ValueError` before any
supercell, basis, or integral work. Fail-first regression pinned in
`tests/test_ccm_interaction_range.py`.

### Fixed: GFN2 H0 uses the full Pauling electronegativity table (issue #433, 2026-08-28)

The Pauling table behind the GFN2 H0 off-site EN factor (`1 + 0.02*dEN^2`)
stopped at Z = 10 and returned 1.0 for every heavier element, so every
heteronuclear pair involving Na or beyond computed `dEN = 0` and a flat
EN factor where tblite applies the full set. Both the energy and the
derivative paths in `cpp/src/semiempirical/core/hamiltonian_builders.cpp`
now share one table carrying the full Z <= 86 Pauling set exactly as shipped
by mctc-lib (`get_pauling_en`), the values tblite consumes. The source is
cited (`pauling_chemical_bond_1960`) on the molecular `gfn2_xtb` and periodic
`gfn2_seccm` routes. A new regression pins a synthetic Na-Cl H0 element
against the tblite formula; the old table fails it (flat EN factor).

### Fixed: bugctl records checkout provenance on claim and verdict events (issue #495, 2026-08-28)

Every broker mutation payload now carries the calling checkout's provenance:
`checkout_kind` (`clone` or `worktree`, from whether
`git rev-parse --git-dir` differs from `--git-common-dir`) and
`checkout_path` (the working-tree root, with any home prefix rendered as `~`
so the mirrored note never publishes a machine path). The broker validates
the fields and records them on `CLAIM_REQUESTED` / `CLAIM_GRANTED` /
`VERIFIER_CLAIM_REQUESTED` / `VERIFIER_CLAIM_GRANTED` / `VERIFIED` /
`VERIFY_FAILED`, rendering them in the mirrored GitLab notes. A present but
malformed value fails the mutation closed, and a client that cannot resolve
its own checkout metadata refuses before dispatch rather than recording an
unattributable event. This closes the observability half of the worktree
mis-attribution hazard: the worktree-specific state resolution and the
`local-agent` mutation refusal landed earlier (#380, #458); this records the
session's checkout shape so the class is answerable next time instead of
only boundable. Older clients without the fields are still accepted, and
record no checkout provenance.

## [v0.15.151] - 2026-08-28 - *Neese's Cheetah*

A maintenance release dominated by one thread: the bug ledger and the
verification pipeline that the whole loop runs on. Six of the fifteen entries
below are repairs to that machinery, and they matter more than their size —
each was silently discarding completed verification work.

**What this release fixes.** The lifecycle no longer ends at a verdict:
`bugctl close` applies the terminal transition server-side (#451), so verified
issues stop sitting open indistinguishably from untouched ones — 20 issues had
been in that state for 13 days. A phantom landed SHA no longer buys a
verification lane (#485), a stale broker checkout no longer reads as invalid
provenance and aims a destructive remedy at a valid fix (#494), and a resuming
verifier is now told when its question was already answered. On the product
side: vq validates durable dependency IDs before probing the filesystem (#488),
hostless vq commands reject an unreachable inferred default rather than dying
on a raw ssh error (#484), the MPI lane no longer reports green while asserting
nothing (#465), and the channel-isolation probe now builds neutral B1 MgO(100)
planes rather than single-species polar ones (#471).

**What this release does NOT fix.** The default SCF accelerator regression
(#119) is fixed on `main` but its verification is still outstanding, so this
release carries it unverified. `def2-qzvp-rifit` still omits every 3d and 4d
transition metal (#483) — a data gap that #480's guard converts from a silent
wrong answer into a refusal, but does not fill. The GDF route on
Si-diamond/pob-TZVP-rev2 still lands ~3.45 Ha below BIPOLE at both (2,2,2) and
(6,6,6) (#142, #154 — newly linked, and the agreement between meshes suggests
one defect rather than two). And `bugctl` still mis-attributes identity from a
worktree (#495), which is a live hazard to the independence guarantee.

### Added: a resuming verifier is told when its question was already answered (2026-08-28)

Verification is the loop's bottleneck, so re-deriving an answer that already
exists is the most expensive no-op available. A duplicate verifier *claim* was
already refused — a verified generation is no longer `landed`. The costly case
is a lease taken legitimately, then a pause (expiry, host contention, a killed
run), a second verifier finishing in the gap, and the first lane resuming
without re-reading broker state. Measured 2026-08-28: **2 of 4 live verifier
leases were in exactly that state** — half the in-flight capacity.

`verifier-heartbeat` now returns `superseded`, `verified_by` and an advisory
line when another actor has recorded a passing verdict on the same generation.
Advisory rather than a refusal: a deliberate second opinion on a HIGH-severity
wrong-answer fix is legitimate, and the lane is better placed than the broker
to judge that — but it can only judge it if it is told.

### Fixed: a stale broker checkout no longer reads as invalid provenance (issue #494, 2026-08-28)

The #485 guard refuses a `verifier-claim` whose landed SHA names no commit in
the broker's checkout, and points the verifier at `retire-provenance`. Its
inline comment justified using the weaker of the two available checks on the
grounds that "does this name a commit at all" has no false-negative mode,
because "a SHA that resolves to nothing can never become valid."

That is not true, and the reason is structural: **the broker never fetches.**
`_main_contains_exact_sha`'s own docstring says "pre-fetched", and
`BROKER_REPO_PATH` is a `vq admin update`-managed tree that must stay read-only
to the broker (§ 15). A commit that is real, pushed, and an ancestor of
`origin/main` therefore names nothing *in that checkout* until the updater next
runs.

Measured on example_hub 2026-08-28 14:07 UTC: the checkout had last fetched at
13:30 and its `origin/main` was 12 commits behind. Of the 71 distinct landed
SHAs in `bugctl grants`, 9 did not resolve there; re-checked against an
up-to-date clone, 8 are genuinely bad (#443's real instances) and one was a
false positive -- `e4462bfcf`, the #450 fix landed 30 minutes earlier.

The false alarm is not benign, because the message prescribes a destructive
remedy: a verifier who follows it retires the landed generation of a fix that
is really on `main`. So the guard now applies only when the checkout is
demonstrably newer than the landing it is judging (`grants.updated_at` against
the checkout's own freshness, less a margin covering the fetch's duration).
Unknown freshness and unknown landing time both read as "cannot conclude" and
grant: a wrongly-granted claim costs one wasted lane, the cost that already
existed, while a wrongly-refused one invites the destruction of good
provenance. The two are not symmetric.

The #485 property is unchanged and still pinned: a landing the checkout has had
time to see, whose SHA resolves to nothing, is still refused. Making the new
condition unconditionally false reddens #485's own test.

### Fixed: the channel-isolation probe now uses neutral B1 MgO(100) planes (issue #471, 2026-08-28)

`studies/seccm-bulk3d/probe_slab_channel_isolation.py` still constructed the
historical IID 141 stress cell: alternating single-species square planes on an
`a`-spaced in-plane grid. Although the probe had since been labeled synthetic,
that two-coordinate cell was not rocksalt (100) and could not support a
downstream MgO slab interpretation.

The probe now matches the established B1 MgO(100) study contract: each layer
is a neutral 4 Mg + 4 O checkerboard, adjacent layers swap cation and anion
sites, the surface primitives span area `a^2/2`, and the 3-D extension has six
unlike neighbours at `a/2`. The geometry regression compares the coordinate,
species, translation, primitive-vector, and replica contract against the
canonical slab builder, and independently pins plane neutrality, site
swapping, odd-layer stoichiometry, and sixfold bulk coordination.

This correction changes only the diagnostic fixture, not a production solver,
equation, or default. Numerical outcomes from the retired single-species-plane
probe remain observations of that synthetic cell and are not reinterpreted as
MgO(100) surface results. The separate synthetic Jacobian probe and its
historical SCC-map regression remain intentionally unchanged.

Patch-candidate: v0.15.x
### Added: `bugctl close` — the lifecycle no longer ends at a verdict (issue #451, 2026-08-28)

`verify` recorded a verdict and **mirrored nothing**. Closing meant leaving the
documented workflow entirely for a raw `glab api -X PUT`, so agents reasonably
concluded closing was not available to them and said so in writing on 20
issues. Those 20 were fixed on 2026-08-13 and re-triaged COVERED on 2026-08-14,
then stayed open for 13 more days, indistinguishable in `bugctl list` from
untouched defects; 19 more were found in the same state on 2026-08-28.

`bugctl close <iid>` requires a **passing verdict on the current generation**,
so a fix cannot be closed out from under an unfinished verification.
`--administrative --reason "..."` closes without a verdict — stale, duplicate,
superseded, not-a-defect — which is the honest path for closes that are not
verifications instead of dressing them up as ones.

**Closing is deliberately not automatic on a passing verdict.** A verdict is
evidence about a *fix*; an issue can outlive it. Three cases the same day prove
the distinction is real: #224's verdict covered only the parser half while the
regeneration half stayed open, #73 verified structurally but its remaining
claim is a performance *number* needing an uninstalled stack, and #207's
wrong-answer symptom was fixed while the filed indefiniteness remains by design
pending a ruling. Auto-closing on a pass would have silently discarded all
three.

### Fixed: the BUG-024 diagnostic no longer fails on correct PM6 output (issue #469, 2026-08-28)

`scripts/debug/verify_bug024_fix.py` carried `expected = -35.75976498`, a
hot-start value from the original diagnostic that the #244 heavy-heavy NDDO
multipole repair retired. On the current canonical PM6 operator the script
converged norbornadiene in 49 iterations at `-33.0848095873 Ha` and then
**exited 1** on a 2.67 Ha "mismatch" against a reference that no longer
describes the operator -- aborting before it reached its `run_job` and
`.system` manifest checks. A superseded absolute oracle that fails closed on
correct output is worse than no oracle: it hides the checks behind it.

BUG-024 is the SILENT-E-ZERO symptom, so the diagnostic now asserts what it is
actually about -- converged, **finite**, and **non-zero** -- plus a new
operator-independent oracle: `run_semiempirical` and `run_job` must agree on
the same molecule (currently bit-identical, `0.00e+00 Ha`). That catches one
route silently diverging from the other without pinning a value a legitimate
operator repair would retire. Absolute PM6 accuracy stays where it belongs, in
the canonical PM6 regressions that pin MOPAC-oracle parity.

### Fixed: periodic GFN2 canonicalizes lattice-equivalent atom representatives (issue #296, 2026-08-28)

Issue #316 made the finite overlap, H0, repulsion, and AES inventories select
images by physical pair distance, but Gamma GFN2 still built its home-cell
shell-gamma and atom-centred multipole objects from coordinates exactly as
typed. On current `main`, an independent MgO retest found that translating O
by one full lattice vector moved the optimizer closure by 21.201853 mHa and
the raw default-cutoff energy by 18.982194 mHa.

The Gamma driver now maps periodic atom coordinates to one half-open
fractional representative before constructing any home-cell GFN2 object or
the issue #316 pair inventory. The issue #316 physical-distance inventory and
the existing Bannwarth-Ehlert-Grimme Eq. 18 coordination vector are reused
unchanged. Full O and Mg lattice translations now preserve total, free,
electronic, repulsive, shell-SCC, bare-band, AES, and third-order energies;
the accepted one-point Gamma k-mesh copies the same result, and the optimizer
closure agrees with the raw Gamma free energy. Those detailed component
fields are now exposed on both periodic result types. The molecular-limit
guard now tests the image-labelled pair graph for a noncontractible lattice
cycle, so an isolated molecule crossing a cell face still fails closed while
a translated wide supercell remains periodic.

This correction is local to ordinary periodic Gamma GFN2. It does not modify
the issue #130 SECCM physical-basin and charge-covariance gate, the issue #348
SECCM AES torus gauge, or the issue #354 cyclic-H0 coordination assembly. It
does not enable the issue #351 non-Gamma functional or provide the issue #338
matching analytic derivative. The method and citation route are unchanged.

### Added: a periodic lane-health report for the tiers no gate runs (issue #450, 2026-08-28)

There is no per-commit CI (a maintainer decision, § 2) and the once-per-release
pipeline runs the blocking T0+T1 profile only. A commit that reddens a T2 or T3
lane therefore produces **no signal anywhere** -- not at push time, not at
release time -- until someone runs that lane for an unrelated reason. #450
collected six lanes found exactly that way inside two days; one was a
default-path SCF convergence regression that had shipped in three releases.

`scripts/test_gate/lane_health.py` is the missing periodic report. It consumes
the artifacts `run_full_suite.py` already writes and publishes, per red file:
status, tier, owner, whether it is a tracked known-red or a new one, the SHA it
last passed at, and the commit range since -- including the commits in that
range that touched the file. The last-passed anchor is the previous report when
one is supplied (`--previous`) and `suite_manifest.json`'s `last_verified_sha`
otherwise.

It also reports what it did *not* run: an inventory file with no record is
listed as *Not observed* -- unknown, not green. #450's complaint is silence, so
a partial run that read as a clean bill of health would recreate the blind spot.

Report-only by construction, and pinned as such: it accepts every tier (the
mirror image of `gate_verdict.py`, which refuses everything but T0/T1) and
always exits 0 on a successful report, however red the tree is. Nothing about
what the release gate blocks on has changed. Published text is redacted of
local absolute paths so the report can be committed or pasted (§ 12).

Not addressed here: wiring a host and timer to run it -- the same open ask to
the queue chat the nightly cadence already waits on -- and the issue's secondary
suggestion that `bugctl land` require the lane list a fixer ran, which changes
bugctl's contract and belongs with the lifecycle work in #347.


### Fixed: a phantom landed SHA no longer buys a verification lane (issue #485, 2026-08-28)

The broker's `verifier-claim` validated the landed generation's SHA by *shape*
only (`[0-9a-f]{40}`) and never asked whether it named a commit. A well-formed
40-hex that resolves to nothing -- #124's `4028ad845ab8...` is the case --
therefore granted a verifier lease, and the verifier discovered the record was
fiction only after performing the whole parent-vs-fix flip. #443 counts six such
wasted lanes, and verification is the loop's stated bottleneck.

`verifier-claim` now refuses structurally-invalid provenance, pointing at
`retire-provenance` (the verb that exists to clear exactly these records).

Two deliberate limits. The gate asks only *"does this name a commit at all"*,
not *"is it on origin/main"*: the stronger question would also refuse a real
commit that is not yet fetched into the broker's checkout, which is a transient
pushing problem rather than an invalid record, and that false negative would
block good verifications. And it applies only when `BROKER_REPO_PATH` names a
checkout -- `_git_repo_dir()` returns None when it is unset and every git-backed
check then fails closed, so an unconditional gate would turn one missing
environment variable into a fleet-wide verification outage.

Not addressed here: options (a) and (b) on the issue -- non-git provenance kinds
and un-ignoring campaign carriers -- are schema and policy decisions. Option (c),
the `retire-provenance` unblocker, had already landed.

### Fixed: vq validates durable dependency IDs before filesystem probes (issue #488, 2026-08-28)

`JobSpec.depends_on` and `depends_on_any` now apply the same bounded,
path-component-safe validation as the job's own ID during construction,
persisted JSON reads, and assignment. A malformed durable predecessor such as
`../outside` previously reached single-user status rendering as
`<queue>/../outside.json`; it now fails validation before dependency status can
probe the filesystem. Safe generated and legacy IDs retain their original
order and duplicates, so dispatch semantics are unchanged.

Patch-candidate: v0.15.x

### Fixed: D116 MPI validation now applies the filed numerical contract (issue #303, 2026-08-28)

The D116 two-rank PBE receipt originally required bitwise equality even though
issue #303 specified `1e-10` Ha/cell energy and `1e-12` elementwise Fock and
density tolerances. site_i job `8d7cb96cade7` therefore failed closed despite
maximum differences of `2.84e-14` Ha, `5.33e-15` in Fock, and `1.43e-15` in
density under two ranks by ten OpenMP threads.

`d116-rks-mpi-validation/v2` now applies absolute `1e-10` Ha bounds to total,
electronic, nuclear, and XC energies and `1e-12` bounds to every Fock and
density block. It still requires exact array shapes, SCF state, zero Fock
mixing, inactive PBE exchange q=0 applicability, task census and canonical
order, scheduling fingerprint, launcher controls, and source/core process
identity. The artifact preserves `exact_parity` as an observation and records
the normative `contract_parity` result plus the full versioned contract. The
D114 v1 exact validator, D116 v1 artifact meaning, and v1 parallel-execution
schema are unchanged. This changes campaign acceptance only, not SCF
arithmetic or MPI scheduling.

Patch-candidate: v0.15.x

### Fixed: the multi-k sidecar refusal gate matched a message that had moved (2026-08-28)

`test_run_periodic_job_multik_sidecar_request_fails_before_scf`
`[write_population_file]` in `tests/test_slab_2d_routing.py` had been red on
`main`, the only red in the `pbc-core` lane. It matched
`exact (?:single )?Gamma[- ]point` against a refusal whose wording
`2150ec826` (issue #350) rewrote when it admitted `aiccm2026dev-b` alongside
BIPOLE: the population reason now ends "other routes require an exact
single-Gamma result".

The new wording is the intended side, so the assertion was the stale one. It
ships verbatim in `docs/user_guide/output_files.md`, is recorded as decision
D118 in `docs/aiccm2026dev_b_decisions.md`, and is already pinned green by
`test_runner_multik_population_rejection_names_periodic_routes`. Reverting the
message would have broken all three.

The two sidecars now refuse for genuinely different reasons: Molden needs the
Gamma block itself, so its refusal is a statement about the mesh, while
population is a route-capability rule naming the routes that carry a full-k
analysis. Each parametrisation therefore pins its own clause instead of
sharing one pattern widened until it covers both. Runtime behaviour is
unchanged; this is a test-only repair.

### Fixed: EDIIS/ADIIS now find the global simplex minimum on nonconvex hulls (issue #486, 2026-08-28)

The shared EDIIS/ADIIS quadratic-program solver treated its objective as
convex: it solved the KKT stationarity equations on one active set and returned
that point without establishing it was a minimum. Exchange makes real HF hulls
concave or indefinite. On the two-point scalar regression, EDIIS therefore
returned the stationary midpoint at energy 0 instead of either -0.25-Ha
vertex; ADIIS returned an objective of 0.5 instead of the vertex minimum 0.
The physical NH2/STO-3G doublet/sextet hull reproduced the same error: its
interior stationary point is a maximum, 447.6 mHa above the lower vertex.
This supersedes the earlier entry below that correctly repaired EDIIS's density
convention but described reaching a stationary point as sufficient.

Following Kudin, Scuseria, and Cances, *J. Chem. Phys.* **116**, 8255 (2002),
Eqs. 15-16, the solver now visits every non-empty face of the coefficient
simplex, retains feasible stationary candidates, and returns the lowest
objective. Vertices are evaluated directly, so a numerical rank decision can
never discard the best stored iterate. EDIIS and ADIIS now form
newest-relative Fock/density differences before multiplication (and EDIIS
energy differences against the newest iterate), preserving small curvature
that subtraction of extensive absolute traces had already rounded away. The
comparison objective and each face KKT system are additionally put in a
simplex-invariant affine gauge before common scaling. Exact enumeration is
bounded to history depths 2-12 (4095 faces at the cap); a larger shared DIIS
depth fails on first EDIIS/ADIIS use, while plain DIIS-family algorithms retain
deeper histories.

Focused regressions cover concave EDIIS and ADIIS maxima, an indefinite
three-point hull whose minimum lies inside a boundary face, singular history,
old-face anti-replay, extensive energy and density gauges, closed- and
open-shell density conventions, and the depth guard. The tetrazine/cc-pVDZ
HCORE regression additionally requires pure EDIIS to converge to the lower
recorded RHF root rather than reaching its energy while stalling at the
iteration limit. No damping, level shift, switch threshold, or convergence
tolerance changed.

Patch-candidate: v0.15.x

### Fixed: the two neutral CCM controls now evaluate the same Hamiltonian (issue #307, 2026-08-27)
