`run_ccm_rhf_direct` and `run_ccm_rhf_gdf` are documented as two
representations of the *same* block-circulant neutral Hamiltonian. They were
not. At `nrep=(1,1,1)` the GDF sibling delegates to the Γ fast path
(`run_pbc_gdf_rhf`), which auto-sizes an RSGDF high-|G| tail on the tight-core
class, while the direct/fold route had no `tail_ke_cutoff` plumbing at all and
could not request one — so the two routes silently ran different operators and
disagreed by **-4.993362e-01 Ha/cell** on MgO fcc (a = 4.21 Å) / STO-3G, and no
result field reported it. The tailed side is the accurate one: -271.0496 sits
0.3 mHa from the PySCF MDF reference -271.0499, and the untailed side carries
the documented dense-core P01 offset.

* `ccm_neutral_cderi_fold` and `ccm_neutral_cderi` take `tail_ke_cutoff` and
  forward it to `build_lpq_bloch_native_fft`, whose tail kwarg already existed
  and was simply never reached from this route. The whole direct-route family
  (`run_ccm_rhf_direct`, `run_ccm_uhf_direct`, `run_ccm_rks_direct`,
  `run_ccm_uks_direct`, `run_ccm_double_hybrid_direct`,
  `run_ccm_rhf_direct_rijcosx`) exposes it, and refuses it against a prebuilt
  `cderi` — whose tail is already baked in — exactly as `aux_basis` already did.
* New `ccm_neutral_tail_ke_cutoff` resolves the default by **mirroring the
  sibling route's own decision**: the same `_auto_rsgdf_tail_ke_cutoff`
  classifier at `N_c = 1`, and `None` at `N_c > 1`, where the multi-k loop
  deliberately does not auto-tail. Post-fix the MgO pair agrees to
  **+4.09e-11 Ha/cell**; LiH/STO-3G N=1 (which the classifier says needs no
  tail) is unchanged at -2.1e-12, and every `N_c > 1` path is bit-identical
  because the resolved tail there is `None`, i.e. the previous call.
* The resolved tail is now a **result field** on both sides —
  `CCMSCFResult`/`CCMKSResult`/`CCMUHFResult`/`CCMGDFResult` plus
  `PBCGDFResult` and `PeriodicKRHFGDFResult` — read from the driver that ran,
  never re-derived, per the IID 344 discipline. The multi-k loop reports `None`
  even when a tail was *requested*, because it does not consume one (issue
  #146): a requested-but-unapplied tail must not read back as applied.

Auto-tailing fires whenever `10·ζ_max` exceeds `ke_cutoff`, so gates that
deliberately run below the 200 Ha default for speed would silently acquire a
tail. An instrumented audit of every neutral-cderi builder call across 13 CCM
test files found exactly five such cases, all in `tests/test_ccm_symmetry.py`
and all at `N_c = 1`. Each pins a *symmetry relation* — reduced == unreduced,
or `P_aux^T L P == L` — in which the tail is common mode, so it changes
nothing they measure and only multiplies cost (the diamond gate: 2.8 s
untailed, still unfinished after 900 s tailed; the MgO covariance case asks
for a 189× reciprocal ball). All five now pass `tail_ke_cutoff=0.0`
explicitly, restoring the cost and the calibrated residuals they were written
for. No other test file resolves a tail.

A tail the builders would ignore — `0`, or any value at or below `ke_cutoff`,
which they never sweep — normalises to `None`. That keeps an opt-out
byte-for-byte identical to the historical call (`0.0` and `None` are *not*
interchangeable everywhere: `_rsgdf_weighted_3c_tensor_gradient_bloch` rejects
a non-`None` tail alongside external kernel weights) and stops a result from
recording a tail that never ran.

`tests/test_ccm_neutral_tail_parity.py` pins the classifier mirror, the
explicit-override contract and that normalisation, the `N_c > 1` no-op, the
result-surface reads, and end-to-end direct-vs-GDF parity on fcc Be and
diamond. Every end-to-end gate carries its own untailed falsifying control,
because the `theorem1_parity` gate that should have caught this reported a
pass-shaped result over an **empty domain** and had never once returned a
negative.

MgO — the canonical cell — is pinned at the classifier level only. Its
end-to-end gate was written, measured and removed: the tailed MgO fold did not
finish inside 33 minutes, running at ~1 core throughout even though the
pair-FT kernel carries an `omp parallel for`. Diamond's pre-fix gap
(−1.589e−02 Ha/cell) already sits four orders above the tolerance and
exercises the identical mechanism, so the cheap gates carry the coverage and
the MgO numbers stay recorded here and in the test module's docstring.

This also settles the cost half (issue #308): N=1 GDF was never a k-count
pathology, it is the tail's `(tail/ke)^1.5` G-ball on a route that should not
have been silently different. The tail is a correct cost, not one to
special-case away.

### Fixed: CCM overlap diagnostics distinguish indefinite and near-singular spectra (issue #297, 2026-08-28)

The WSSC-weighted cyclic-overlap diagnostic previously described every
eigenvalue below its threshold as "near-singular", including the reproduced
LiH/pob-DZVP-rev2 `(2, 2, 2)` spectrum with
`lambda_min = -0.3535115803113`. Peintinger and Bredow
(*J. Comput. Chem.* **35**, 839-846, 2014, Eq. 5 and the
critical-eigenvalues discussion) identify an indefinite unscreened overlap as
an unphysical finite Gamma-point approximation and prescribe canonical
screening of the small-eigenvalue subspace or a larger cluster. Since issue
#289 the SCF drivers already perform that screening and fail closed when the
retained space cannot hold the occupied orbitals.

`CCMSystem.check_overlap_spectrum` now distinguishes materially negative
indefiniteness (using the shared `-1e-6` structural-noise floor),
noise-scale non-positivity, and positive near-singularity. It also rejects
non-real, non-finite, boolean, or negative diagnostic thresholds before
integral construction. At `lindep_tol=1e-7`, the reproduced LiH matrix retains
76 of 88 directions for 16 occupied orbitals. A synthetic overlap-only,
zero-J/K native-host regression proves that the production host accepts that
screened space, while a 15-direction control still fails closed. The same
probe leaves a well-conditioned LiH/STO-3G control bit-for-bit unchanged with
screening enabled or disabled; it is not a physical four-center energy claim.

This repairs the absolute WSSC-supercell overlap diagnostic used by the
`union12` and `aiccm2026dev-a` four-center line. It does not change χ-CCM's
normalized per-character overlap treatment or establish equality between the
distinct Γ-CCM union-and-weight and χ-CCM finite-character constructions.

Patch-candidate: v0.15.x

### Fixed: hostless vq commands reject an unreachable inferred remote default before acting (issue #484, 2026-08-28)

Hostless non-status per-job commands previously delegated directly to an
unmarked remote `default_host`, so stale or unreachable configuration surfaced
as a raw SSH transport failure. They now perform one bounded, read-only
durable-queue probe against only the inferred default's exact action queue
authority before invoking the requested verb. An unavailable or invalid
snapshot produces a diagnostic naming the inferred default, requests an
explicit host, and performs no requested action. A valid snapshot preserves
direct default routing whether the requested job is found, absent, or
duplicated; this probe is not owner discovery. Explicit hosts, local defaults,
administratively down Baran detours, and `status`'s fleet-wide durable owner
discovery are unchanged.

Hermetic resolver coverage pins the four probe outcomes, with `logs`, `kill`,
and `fetch` regressions proving that an unreachable default invokes no
requested operation.

Patch-candidate: v0.15.x

### Fixed: skipped UHF stability work no longer emits phantom timing (issue #205, 2026-08-28)

The post-SCF stability timer started before UHF decided whether an analysis
would run. Opt-out, nonconverged, and DFT+U jobs therefore returned a few
microseconds of wall and CPU time for work they never performed; the runner
then rendered a false `SCF stability analysis` row and perf phase. The timer
now starts after that skip gate, matching UKS: every no-work route retains
exact-zero fields and emits no phase, while real UHF and UKS analyses remain
measured end to end. The timing regression derives its reconstruction bound
from the output formatter's millisecond resolution and is now registered in
the generated suite manifest. No SCF, stability, Davidson, or energy behavior
changed.

Patch-candidate: v0.15.x

### Fixed: web-console status tests are isolated from live source drift (issue #481, 2026-08-28)

The non-drift verdict and cache tests now pin one stable source-tree digest in
their existing autouse fixture. A concurrent checkout or editable-install
rewrite can therefore no longer turn 14 otherwise unrelated assertions red
mid-run, while the six explicit source-drift tests still override both digest
probes and exercise the production warning paths unchanged. The exact injected
drift reproduction moved from 14 failed / 28 passed to 42 passed.

Patch-candidate: v0.15.x

### Fixed: the MPI test lane no longer reports green while asserting nothing (issue #465, 2026-08-28)

`tests/test_mpi_kpoint_multirank.py` skipped all 23 of its multi-rank tests
when an MPI launcher was present but `mpi4py` was not, and printed
`23 skipped` -- output indistinguishable from a passing lane in every summary
a human or an agent reads. Nothing separated "23 tests verified the MPI paths"
from "23 tests declined to look". Measured on such a machine: 23 skipped in
0.32 s before installing `mpi4py`, 23 passed in 133.56 s after.

A single always-running test now fails loudly on that half-installed case,
naming `pip install -e '.[mpi]'` as the remedy. A genuinely MPI-free machine
(no launcher at all) still skips silently, which is correct -- there is nothing
to run. The reverse asymmetry, `mpi4py` present with no launcher, is
deliberately not an error for the same reason.

This lane is **T2**, and the release gate runs T0+T1 only, so the new failure
is visible to whoever runs the lane but still has no automatic signal behind
it -- the #450 blind spot, narrowed rather than closed. Adding `mpi4py` to the
`[test]` extra (asked for in #465) is *not* done here: `mpi4py` needs an MPI
runtime to install, so it would break `pip install -e '.[test]'` on machines
with no MPI at all. That is a dependency decision under CLAUDE.md §9.

## [v0.15.150] - 2026-08-28 - *Neese's Cheetah*

A small release carrying one correctness fix that matters more than its size
suggests, plus three supporting repairs and a ledger-tooling addition.

**What this release fixes:** density fitting no longer computes a silently
wrong energy when the auxiliary basis has no functions on an element in the
system. On CaH2/cc-pVDZ the density-fitted path returned a *converged*
-868 Ha against a correct -677.87 Ha, with no warning anywhere in the output.
The SCF half of that needed an explicit `density_fit=True`, but the post-SCF RI
half was reachable from a plain default: `run_job(method="dlpno-mp2",
basis="cc-pvdz")`, with no density-fitting option anywhere, resolves an
auxiliary basis that omits calcium. DLPNO and `run_rohf_mp2` are density fitted
by construction, so there was no option a user could set to avoid it.

**What this release does NOT fix.** The default SCF accelerator still returns a
converged, unwarned wrong answer on a non-aufbau case: EDIIS+DIIS gives
-54.73931019 Ha against -54.83449638 from plain DIIS, no DIIS, and level
shifting, which all agree with each other -- a +95.1 mHa gap with zero warnings
(issue #119, under active root-cause investigation, not papered over). Nor does
it fix `def2-qzvp-rifit`, which ships 42 element blocks where its nine sibling
def2 RI-fits ship 72 and so omits every 3d and 4d transition metal (issue
#483). That is a data gap; this release converts it from a silent wrong answer
into a refusal, but the missing blocks remain missing.

### Fixed: the PM6 parameter cache cites its own paper again (issue #271, 2026-08-28)

#271 reported that the generated PM6 cache carried the **PM7** paper's DOI.
That was repaired by *deleting* the wrong reference rather than correcting it,
so `pm6_mopac_params.toml` ended up with **no originating publication at all**
while its PM7 sibling kept one -- a user auditing where the PM6 numbers came
from got silence. CLAUDE.md § 8 requires the per-publication reference in the
file header.

`scripts/parse_mopac_pm6_params.py` now emits
`reference = "J. J. P. Stewart, J. Mol. Model. 13, 1173-1213 (2007),
doi:10.1007/s00894-007-0233-4"` -- the same citation already routed as
`stewart_pm6_2007` -- mirroring the PM7 generator, and the checked-in cache
header carries it so the two agree without a regeneration.

Pinned by a regression over **both** bundled caches asserting each cites its
own paper and not the sibling's, matched on publication year rather than DOI
(the two headers use different citation formats). It guards the whole class,
not just the one direction that was reported.
### Fixed: density fitting refuses an auxiliary basis that skips an element (issue #480, 2026-08-28)

Density fitting silently dropped any centre absent from the auxiliary
basis. libint2 does not raise for an element a fitting file omits — it
returns an auxiliary `BasisSet` with **zero shells on that centre** — so
the fit was built with no auxiliary functions on the uncovered atom and
the SCF converged cleanly, with a tight gradient and nothing in the
`.out` matching `warn|missing|absent|skip|fallback`, to a grossly
over-bound energy:

| system / basis | conventional | DF, auto aux | silent error |
|---|---|---|---|
| LiH / cc-pVQZ | -7.9871767942 | -9.1364654088 | **-1.149 Ha** |
| BeH2 / cc-pVQZ | -15.7729827157 | -16.9774517874 | **-1.205 Ha** |
| NaH / cc-pVDZ | -162.3839486171 | -211.9437602395 | **-49.560 Ha** |
| MgH2 / cc-pVDZ | -200.7293878662 | -246.1552781363 | **-45.426 Ha** |

A **49.6 Ha converged wrong answer** is roughly 31,000 kcal/mol reported
as a successful calculation. The tell was that NaH's auxiliary basis had
the same function count as its orbital basis (23/23): the Na centre
contributed nothing at all.

**Scope — which paths were affected.** The default molecular SCF is
*not* density fitted, and the SCF JK route required an explicit
`density_fit=True` (or `cosx=True`), so a default `run_job` SCF was
never exposed. The **post-SCF RI route was exposed with no flag at
all**: the DLPNO family (`dlpno-mp2`, `dlpno-ccsd`, `dlpno-ccsd(t)`,
`dlpno-uccsd`) and `run_rohf_mp2` are density fitted by construction and
auto-resolve `default_aux_basis_for(basis, kind="ri")`. Verified on this
tree: `run_job(mol, method="dlpno-mp2", basis="cc-pvdz")` on CaH2, with
no density-fitting option set anywhere, resolved to `cc-pvdz-ri`, which
has no Ca. So this is both "a supported option was unsafe" and, for the
DLPNO methods, "a default configuration was unsafe".

**Coverage audit of all 73 shipped auxiliary files.** The gaps are wider
than the originally filed He/Li/Be/Na/Mg:

| Family | Missing |
|---|---|
| `cc-pV{D,T,Q,5}Z-JKFIT`, `augmentation-*` | He, Li, Be, Na, Mg, K, Ca, Sc–Zn |
| `cc-pVnZ-RI`, `cc-pVnZ-RIFIT` | K, Ca (and Sc–Zn at DZ/TZ/QZ) |
| `cc-pV6Z-RI`, `cc-pV6Z-RIFIT`, `augmentation-cc-pVnZ-RI` | Li, Be, Na, Mg |
| `aug-cc-pVnZ-RIFIT` | Li, Na, K, Ca (varies by zeta) |
| `def2-qzvp-rifit` | Sc–Zn, Y–Cd |
| `cc-pwCVnZ-RIFIT`, `aug-cc-pwCVnZ-RIFIT` | H, He, Li, Be, Na, Mg |

The def2 families are otherwise clean, but `def2-qzvp-rifit` is **not** —
it ships 42 element blocks where every sibling def2 RI-fit ships 72, so
it skips every 3d and 4d transition metal. That had been reported as
clean. It is an incomplete BSE fetch rather than an upstream limitation,
so it is filed separately as **#483**: this guard turns it from a silent
wrong answer into a refusal, but cannot manufacture the missing basis
functions. `def2-universal-jkfit`, `def2-universal-jfit` and the
remaining `def2-*-jk` / `def2-*-rifit` sets cover H–Rn. The `*-pp-rifit`
files cover only their pseudopotential element ranges by design.

**The fix.** `vibeqc.density_fitting` gains
`AuxiliaryBasisCoverageError`, `aux_basis_coverage_gaps`,
`check_aux_basis_coverage`, `make_checked_aux_basis` and
`guard_aux_coverage_for_options`. An atom needs auxiliary functions
exactly when it carries orbital functions — it is the orbital pair
density the auxiliary set must span — so a ghost or dummy centre never
trips the guard. Every route that reaches an auxiliary basis is now
checked before any integral work:

* `DensityFitting.__init__` — covers DF-CC, DF-MP2, FNO-CCSD, A-CCSD(T),
  `run_rohf_mp2`, ROHF/ROKS DF-SCF and the `parity` JK builders;
* the four molecular SCF wrappers `run_rhf` / `run_rks` / `run_uhf` /
  `run_uks`, ahead of the C++ driver that builds its own auxiliary;
* the `run_job` SCF dispatch in `runner`. This one needed its own guard:
  `runner` is imported from `vibeqc/__init__.py` *before* those wrappers
  are defined, so it binds the **bare C++ entry points** and the wrapper
  guard never runs on the `run_job` path — the very path the issue was
  filed against. A guard placed only in the wrappers passes a `run_rhf`
  regression while leaving `run_job` silently wrong, so both are pinned;
* the native DF-MP2 and DF-CC option paths, which likewise build their
  auxiliary inside C++, and the four `compute_gradient*` entry points;
* the DLPNO auxiliary construction sites in `run_job`, including the
  `local_df` branch that wraps the auxiliary in a `SimpleNamespace` and
  never builds a `DensityFitting`;
* `run_cpcm_scf`, whose auxiliary goes straight to the C++ JK builders;
* the periodic `make_aux_basis_set`.

The pre-flight guard is deliberately permissive: it may only *add* the
partial-coverage refusal, never change which error a caller already saw.
It gives up silently when the auxiliary cannot be constructed at all, so
a misspelt name still raises its own error and a driver with a more
specific objection — a range-separated hybrid with density fitting, say —
still wins.

**Refuse, not substitute.** vibe-qc does not swap in a covering
auxiliary: by the time a `BasisSet` exists, an auto-resolved name is
indistinguishable from one the caller wrote by hand, so a fallback would
silently re-pair explicitly requested auxiliaries too — changing the
method under the user. This also matches the already-loud
completely-absent case (closed #11), which was the asymmetry that made
partial coverage the only silent one. The refusal names the uncovered
elements and the auxiliary basis, and points at `def2-universal-jkfit`
(JK) / `def2-tzvpp-rifit` (RI), a def2 orbital basis, or
`density_fit=False`.

On the post-SCF route the refusal fires where the auxiliary is
constructed, which is after the (unfitted, correct) SCF rather than
before it. That is a latency cost, not a correctness gap: no fitted
number is produced. Hoisting it would mean duplicating the `aux_basis` /
options precedence chain ahead of the SCF, which is what drifts.

**Covered systems are unaffected.** Only runs whose auxiliary basis
actually omits a present element start refusing; no pinned energy moved.
The `def2-universal-jkfit` control reproduces the conventional SCF energy
on all four systems above to ~1e-5 Ha, which is what shows the
density-fitting machinery itself was always sound — the coverage check
was the missing piece.

Regressions in `tests/test_aux_basis_coverage.py` (55 cases, CURATED
blocking T1): the four measured systems fail-first with converged wrong
energies on the unguarded tree, through both `run_rhf` and `run_job`; the
`def2-universal-jkfit` control and the covered-element cases must keep
running unchanged; an unbuildable auxiliary must keep raising its own
error rather than the coverage refusal; and eleven known shipped-data
gaps stay pinned as detected so a future basis backfill shows up as a
named failure.

Patch-candidate: v0.15.x

### Fixed: AIC7 waves fail closed when planned rungs are not delivered (issue #415, 2026-08-28)

The AIC7 compute-wave driver unconditionally wrote `status: complete` and
returned exit code 0 after its rung loop, regardless of how many planned
measurements succeeded. The recorded LiH hybrid resubmission passed the stable
tag suffix `rhf+pbe0` back through a comma-only parser, planned that text as one
unknown functional, failed both mesh rungs in 0.002 seconds, and still reported
complete with zero delivered rungs. Budget-bound diamond and MgO ladders
likewise reported complete after timeouts and unstarted tail rungs. A global
budget-shortened timeout was indistinguishable from an ordinary per-rung cap,
and its terminal driver correction was not written back to the rung JSON.

The byte-identical deployed payload is now maintained at
`studies/aiccm-real-gamma/aic7.py` with a versioned driver record and an exact
ordered `planned_rungs` manifest. Completion now requires one unique terminal
`ok` record for every planned rung identity; failed, unconverged, timed-out,
budget-killed, missing, duplicate, unexpected, parent-driver-error, and
abnormal-child outcomes produce `status: partial`, explicit counts, and exit
code 1. Budget checks use a monotonic deadline, reserve bounded TERM/KILL
grace, distinguish `budget_killed` from `rung_timeout`, and atomically persist
budget, elapsed, allotment, and attempted metadata to both top-level and rung
records. Non-finite budgets and caps are rejected before output is created.

Comma-separated method lists and their plus-separated tag form now parse to
the same ordered method vector while the established plus tag remains stable.
Ladder and Madelung targets run largest mesh first, and iteration-cap sweeps run
largest cap first; arbitrary cross-system case order and method/construction
tie order remain operator-controlled. A real-Gamma mesh bundle is `ok` only if
every bundled method succeeds.

The two 2026-08-25 parity jobs and four 2026-08-26 fetch-sweep jobs are
backfilled through a tracked SHA-256-bound adjudication overlay. It preserves
their sealed bytes while exposing effective `partial` records and correcting
the affected rungs to ordinary `rung_timeout`, global `budget_killed`, or
scheduler-authenticated `oom_killed` as the evidence requires. The canonical
campaign-verdict recorder now resolves that overlay and refuses to record a
`complete` artifact gate for any of the six jobs; one-off consumers can render
the same effective top-level or per-rung JSON with the tracked reader.
Patch-candidate: v0.15.x

### Fixed: CCM symmetry SCF gates use physical 3-D fixtures (issues #428 and #459, 2026-08-28)

The IID 291 measured-dimensionality guard correctly rejects a 1-D chain that
is declared as 3-D by adding transverse vacuum: the neutral fitted-torus
Hamiltonian would otherwise apply its exchange-q0 seam to transverse images
that do not physically exist. Two consumer files predated that contract. The
`test_ccm_conv_tol_grad.py` doubles lacked the `CCMSystem.unit_system`
boundary, while five production-SCF consumers in `test_ccm_symmetry.py`
described an H2 chain in a 6 x 30 x 30-bohr vacuum-padded cell but invoked
3-D-only direct, RI-neutral, and GDF routes.

The convergence-tolerance doubles were already repaired and independently
verified under duplicate issue #461 (`67d54e333`): they now carry the charge,
lattice, and atom geometry read by the fail-closed guards. The symmetry file
now keeps its padded chain for valid ring/tensor/planner algebra, but uses the
established compact 6-bohr 3-D H2 cell for all five neutral SCF consumers.
Their symmetry-on/off energy identities and 5-of-6 / 8-of-9 build reductions
remain the asserted behavior. No production guard, physical threshold,
energy pin, or convergence setting changed.

Patch-candidate: v0.15.x
### Added: `bugctl retire-provenance` for fixes that can never be a commit (issue #485, 2026-08-28)

The bug-ledger lifecycle assumed every fix is a git commit in the canonical
repository. Some are not. Issue #135's fix landed in a campaign carrier under
`.agents/`, which `.gitignore` excludes wholesale, so no 40-hex SHA exists for
it or ever will. That generation deadlocked completely: it could not be
verified (the provenance gate refuses anything but an exact 40-hex), could not
be demoted (demotion is driven by a recordable `fail`, which requires a
verifier claim), and could not be re-landed with a correct value because there
is no correct value — while the fixer, who alone held the context, was barred
by the self-verification rule from clearing it.

`bugctl retire-provenance <iid> --reason "…"` retires such a generation and
returns the issue to a claimable state. Two invariants keep it from becoming a
way to erase inconvenient history, both pinned by tests: it **refuses
resolvable provenance** (a SHA naming a real commit is retired by recording a
`fail` verdict, not by this verb), and it **refuses the fixer's own actor**
(`self_retire_denied`, the same principle as `self_verify_denied`). It is
idempotent across a retried `request_id`, and it is not a verdict — it closes
nothing and asserts nothing about whether the fix was correct.

This unblocks the deadlocked records but does not fix the underlying category
gap: the ledger still cannot *express* a non-git fix. Content-hash provenance
(`sha256:` plus the paths it hashes) is the follow-up tracked on #485.

### Fixed: the ROHF/ROKS initial guess now carries the target spin electron counts (issue #119, 2026-08-28)

On plain defaults, ROHF/STO-3G on the near-equilibrium NH₂ radical
(r(N–H) = 1.024 Å, ∠(H–N–H) = 103.4°) converged — `converged=True`, zero
warnings — to the excited ²A₁ stationary point at −54.7393101912 Ha, +95.1 mHa
(about 60 kcal/mol) above the ²B₁ ground state at −54.8344963877 Ha, while
`scf_accelerator="diis"`, no-DIIS and level-shift all reached the ground state.

Root cause is the initial guess, not the accelerator. The Roothaan driver takes
`GuessEngine::build_open_shell`'s *density mode* (no `JKBuilder`), which returns
the raw Hund-split atomic densities: their spin traces are the sum of the
free-atom spin populations and are unrelated to the molecule's
`(n_alpha, n_beta)` — measured 7α/2β for NH₂ and CH₃, 6α/3β for OH, 10α/6β for
O₂(³Σ). NH₂ therefore started from a sextet-like `S_z = 5/2` density. The
unrestricted drivers refill by aufbau on their first cycle and never notice; the
Roothaan loop builds its closed/open/virtual projectors *from the density
itself*, and hands the same iterate to the accelerator history, where EDIIS keeps
it as a convex-hull vertex carrying an energy 0.83 Ha *below* the true ground
state (a non-N-representable density is not bounded by the variational minimum).
Pulay DIIS never consumes energies, which is why exactly the energy-model
accelerators — `ediis_diis` (the default), `ediis`, `adiis`, `kdiis` — missed the
basin.

A density-mode ROHF/ROKS guess now keeps its total density and its Hund spin
*pattern* (which BUG 88 put there for FeCl₃ and which a Fock-diagonalise
repackaging would erase) and rescales only that pattern's magnitude so
`Tr(S(Dα − Dβ)) = n_alpha − n_beta`. All seven accelerators plus the two
accelerator-free routes now agree on −54.8344963877 Ha on the filed system, and
the default converges in 8 cycles instead of 11. Verified unchanged on OH(²Π),
O₂(³Σ), CH₃, NO, N(⁴S), Li and FeCl₃ high-spin.

Regression coverage in `tests/test_rohf.py`: the default-route pin, the
cross-route agreement (all seven accelerators, parametrised — the invariant that
was missing), the two accelerator-free routes, and the guess electron-count
invariant over eight open-shell systems.

Patch-candidate: v0.15.x

### Fixed: EDIIS minimised a rescaled proxy instead of the hull energy (2026-08-28)

`EDIIS::solve_qp` implemented Eq. (8) of Kudin, Scuseria & Cancès,
J. Chem. Phys. 116, 8255 (2002) literally, but that equation's factor ½ belongs
to the paper's closed-shell *pair*-density convention (E = 2Tr(hX) + Tr(G(X)X),
so F = ½ ∂E/∂D). Every vibe-qc call site stores the total or per-spin density
with E = ½⟨D|H+F⟩ and F = ∂E/∂D, where the same hull identity carries ¼ — i.e.
the QP's linear term is `2E_i − ⟨F_i|D_i⟩`, not `E_i − ⟨F_i|D_i⟩`. Taken
literally it made the linear term minus the *two-electron* energy where it
should be the *one-electron* energy, so the objective was exact at the pure
vertices and wrong everywhere between them: measured up to 0.33 Ha on NH₂/STO-3G
ROHF iterates and 10.8 Ha on H₂O/STO-3G closed-shell iterates.

With the correction the objective reproduces the exact hull energy to ~4e-14 Ha
along the segment, and the coefficients EDIIS returns land on the stationary
point of the true energy to 2e-14 (`tests/test_ediis.py`). This affects every
driver that offers EDIIS (RHF/UHF/RKS/UKS, the Roothaan loop, and the periodic
Γ and multi-k paths). It is a separate defect from #119 above and does not on
its own change the NH₂ basin; converged energies were unchanged across the
`molecular-scf-dft` and `pbc-core` lanes.

Patch-candidate: v0.15.x

### Fixed: DLPNO preflight follows streamed pair and triples memory (issue #470, 2026-08-28)

The DLPNO-CCSD(T) preflight multiplied a one-target-pair residual workspace by
the full occupied-pair count and a one-occupied-triple workspace by the full
triple count, then added those mutually exclusive transients to the SCF and DF
construction peaks. Its dominant term consequently scaled as N^5.7 over the
blocked S22 cases. S22-05 and S22-13 uracil monomers (132 cc-pVDZ basis
functions, OMP=48) were each predicted at 100.6886 GiB and refused a
90,000-MiB allocation even though GNU-time scheduler receipts measured peak
RSS of only 6747.878906 and 6819.148438 MiB (6.5897 and 6.6593 GiB).

The estimator now mirrors the executed storage lifetimes. It records separate
SCF, DF-construction, local-pair-solve, and perturbative-triples phases; keeps
the static PNO and B_ov/B_oo/B_vv state for the screened strong-pair list;
charges one streamed residual; and charges one occupied-triple work list plus
two dense or tiled virtual buffers per OpenMP worker. Native worker stacks and
thread-local libint/Eigen/BLAS scratch remain resident beside each phase; this
also corrects the old 0.4553-GiB estimate for the OMP=64 S22-02 water dimer,
whose measured peak was 1.1829 GiB. Disabling pair screening still charges the
complete pair list. The profiled uracil case now estimates 9.0049 GiB,
remaining above the larger measured peak while fitting its node.
The formerly worst S22 adenine-thymine dimer (321 basis functions) falls from
17,851.3 GiB to 184.155 GiB at OMP=48 (190.322 GiB at OMP=64), below its
195.3-GiB allocation without a memory override.

Patch-candidate: v0.15.x

## [v0.15.149] - 2026-08-28 - *Neese's Cheetah*

A large maintenance release dominated by two threads: molecular SCF
correctness, and repairs to the bug-tracking ledger that had been silently
blocking verification across the whole project.

**Molecular SCF.** The incremental delta-D Fock drift-stall disengage was
locked out by a gradient gate (#129) — the screening bias floors the *energy*
while the gate tested the *gradient*, so the disengage was blocked precisely
when the gradient was best converged, and affected runs hit the iteration cap
holding the correct energy with `converged=False`. That regression shipped in
v0.15.144 through .148; energies were never wrong, only the convergence flag.
Alongside it: UKS stability following no longer leaves detected saddle points
(#447), UKS convergence certifies the returned determinant (#474), direct SCF
certifies its energy on one Fock map (#418), and native SCF iterations stream
before return (#25).

**Ledger integrity.** Verification had been blocked fleet-wide by provenance
defects nobody could see. Broker git checks ran in a directory that is not a
checkout, so every ancestry test failed closed and silently (#443); abbreviated
landed SHAs made verifier claims impossible on 46 generations; a demoted fixer
generation aborted `reconcile-plan` project-wide (#124); `bugctl land` now
resolves a SHA before recording it, and surfaces the resolved actor rather than
falling back silently to an unconfigured identity (#458). A claimed
self-verification backlog was **retracted** after direct measurement showed 239
cross-actor verifications and zero self-verified — the notes simply never
rendered who verified (#453).

Also: the GFN2 published-parameter identity is re-attested against the
publication rather than an implementation, with the transcription error it
corrects documented (#446), and the parameter converter now keys shell records
by letter instead of line order so an upstream reorder cannot silently
reintroduce that defect (#467).

**Known open, shipping unfixed:**

* **#470** — the DLPNO-CCSD memory pre-flight scales N^5.7 (17.9 TB at 321
  basis functions), which looks like an estimator sizing the full pair space
  rather than truncated PNO domains. It refuses 11 large S22 complexes at any
  allocation. Under investigation.
* **#428 / #459** — two test lanes red on `main` since the IID 291
  dimensionality guard landed without its consumers updated. #428 is the cited
  closure evidence for #295, #360 and #361.
* **#135** — one malformed landed SHA (64 hex, a SHA-256) still aborts
  `reconcile-plan`; every sanctioned verb declines it by a rule that is
  individually correct.
* **#444** (GFN2-SECCM 3-D `ewald_gamma` has no thermodynamic limit),
  **#475**, **#435**, **#436**, **#437**.

### Fixed: UKS stability following leaves detected saddle points (issue #447, 2026-08-28)

The default-on molecular UKS stability analysis could converge its Davidson
solve, report a negative internal-Hessian eigenvalue, and still return the
same higher saddle with zero corrective restarts. Its line search evaluated
only the core, Coulomb, and global exact-exchange energy, omitting the full
exchange-correlation contribution before comparing the trial with the
complete UKS total energy. For ordinary negative XC energies this rejected
every variationally downhill rotation. The follow also searched only one sign
of the unstable eigenvector even though the two internal descents can reach
different minima.

The fail-first neutral stretched-H2 PBE/STO-3G case at 4 bohr converged to the
spin-symmetric `-0.8969689133495264 Ha` saddle with `lambda_min =
-0.10758842736187378 Ha`, identical alpha and beta densities, and zero
stability restarts. An independently atom-spin-seeded calculation reached an
internally stable broken-symmetry determinant at `-0.9356415950363268 Ha`,
38.672681687 mHa lower, with `<S^2> = 0.8923980872` and `lambda_min =
+0.1779604211623518 Ha`.

Corrective following now scores rotated determinants with the complete KS
energy, reconverges both signed Seeger-Pople branches with a fixed-MOM hold
and an Aufbau fallback, selects the lowest converged descent, and repeats
until the returned determinant is stable or retains an honest unresolved
verdict. The UKS caller requests a Davidson residual at least one decimal
tighter than its classification threshold; the shared solver and the UHF
Davidson route owned by issue #398 are unchanged. All trial XC quadrature uses
the existing memory-bounded batch builder, and issue #205 timing covers the
full two-sign line search and reconvergence work.

The H2/PBE default now takes one corrective restart and reproduces the seeded
energy at `-0.9356415950363270 Ha`, `<S^2> = 0.8923980881`, and stable
`lambda_min = +0.17796042097224368 Ha`. The existing H2/B3LYP/STO-3G 3-bohr
default pin likewise moves from the symmetric `-0.9754118004305485 Ha` saddle
to the atom-spin-seeded stable determinant at `-0.9808712966695428 Ha`
(5.459496239 mHa lower, `<S^2> = 0.3314506883`, `lambda_min =
+0.09978308613324736 Ha`). No threshold, damping, level-shift, or initial-guess
policy changed.

The UKS-only orbital-rotation helper also failed outside minimal bases: its
eigendecomposition of the squared skew generator took `sqrt(-mu)` for exact
null modes whose rounded eigenvalues could be slightly positive. The
H2/B3LYP/def2-SVP 3-bohr default therefore returned the spin-symmetric
`-1.0442045368768891 Ha` saddle (`lambda_min = -0.02565820301169941 Ha`)
instead of the atom-spin-seeded stable determinant at
`-1.0453384673384285 Ha` (`<S^2> = 0.1745466754`, `lambda_min =
+0.04426772316830045 Ha`), 1.133930462 mHa lower. UKS now uses the shared,
tested scaling-and-squaring skew exponential used by UHF and the second-order
SCF drivers, so null modes remain finite.

UKS stability checks now also fail closed on every routed surface where the
implemented Hessian is incomplete. The implicit default preserves the
converged first-order result with `stability_checked = False` for meta-GGA,
range-separated, VV10, DFT+U, hybrid COSX, and coupled-solvent jobs; explicitly
requesting the check raises with the missing response term instead of
manufacturing a verdict. NEB keeps stability check-only by setting zero
corrective retries on an internal option copy, preserving electronic-state
continuity across images; a detected unstable image aborts loudly instead of
silently contributing an uncertified energy and gradient. A nonconverged
stability eigensolve aborts for the same reason.

Pure-functional UKS requests with `cosx = true` now take the ordinary RI-J
route because their exact-exchange fraction is zero. This preserves the
documented COSX no-op energy and density while avoiding a needless staged
exchange-grid recompute that previously discarded the converged stage's valid
stability verdict and timing. A bare `cosx = true` without density fitting is
likewise kept on its ordinary direct-JK route because no auxiliary-basis COSX
builder is active; hybrid direct UKS retains its supported stability verdict.

Patch-candidate: v0.15.x

### Fixed: UKS convergence now certifies the returned determinant (issue #474, 2026-08-28)

UKS tested its energy and Pulay-commutator gates on the density used to build
the current Fock matrix, then diagonalized that Fock and returned the resulting
one-map-advanced density without testing it. A loose SH/LDA/STO-3G witness
therefore declared convergence at iteration 6 with a trace commutator of
`7.939030700e-4` against an `8e-4` threshold, while the returned Fock/density
pair had a `9.136884917e-4` commutator, 14.21% above the requested gate.

The converged branch now preserves the idempotent density and occupied
subspace that actually cleared the gates. If damping made the work density
non-idempotent, UKS instead rebuilds and independently tests the freshly
diagonalized determinant; failure of either unchanged tolerance resumes the
ordinary SCF loop. Canonical final orbitals are selected by maximum overlap
with that certified occupied subspace, and deterministic-restart orbital
trackers are synchronized with the rotated determinant. This prevents a
near-degenerate aufbau reordering from reporting orbitals for a different
stationary state and prevents a damped density mixture from being exposed as
an SCF wavefunction.

The old dynamic-damping engagement test also relied on a stationary
non-idempotent OH density mixture. Its replacement HeH/LDA/STO-3G witness
reaches the same physical determinant with and without dynamic damping:
7 versus 21 iterations and energies agreeing within `1.3e-13 Ha`. The damped
result is idempotent, its returned commutator is `1.0333e-9`, and its occupied
projector contains the requested two alpha and one beta electrons.

No checked-in energy expectation moved. The production SH/PBE/def2-QZVPP
case remains at 72 iterations and changes only from `-398.59208072405687` to
`-398.5920807240558 Ha` (`+1.1e-12 Ha`); its returned commutator improves from
`1.04395e-6` to `6.11716e-7`, and the default stability analysis retains its
stable classification. CPCM, CPCM+RIJCOSX, and staged RIJCOSX probes move by
at most `2.36e-8 Ha`, with warm-start iteration counts unchanged.

COSX retains its established split contract: convergence certifies the
uncorrected iterated SCF map, while the returned Fock and orbitals include the
one-center correction. Staged GridX likewise retains its documented final-grid
single-build override. Neither correction is relabeled as an iterated
self-consistency observation.

Patch-candidate: v0.15.x

### Fixed: molecular native SCF iterations stream before return (issue #25, 2026-08-28)

Molecular `run_job` calculations previously announced that their RHF, UHF,
RKS, or UKS loop had started and then went silent until the compiled driver
returned. The native diagnostic callback updated only the `.system` heartbeat;
NDJSON and terminal iteration rows were reconstructed afterward from
`result.scf_trace`. A scheduler kill therefore erased the only detailed trace
of an in-flight calculation, and successful rows received nearly identical
post-return timestamps instead of their actual completion times.

Fail-first on H2/STO-3G paused the process inside native iteration 1. At
`1.751884666 s` the process was alive and `.system` reported iteration 1, but
the NDJSON file contained zero `scf_iter` events and stdout contained zero
iteration rows; terminating the process left zero recoverable rows. The real
S22-19/cc-pVDZ 147-function witness behaved the same way after `6.221 s`.
With this fix, the equivalent paused H2 process had one manifest heartbeat,
one flushed NDJSON event, and one flushed terminal row at `2.071255625 s`;
termination retained that completed row.

The four native drivers now emit each just-completed trace row at full double
precision, including `dE`, through an execution-context-scoped callback.
`run_job` fans it out independently to the structured log, the canonical
manifest heartbeat, and `ProgressLogger`; failure of one optional sink cannot
suppress the other two or fail the SCF. Terminal compatibility replay fills
only genuinely missing rows. Reset iteration sequences receive an `attempt`
label, and `scf_converged` identifies the selected attempt or attempts.
Stability-triggered SCF reconvergence, CPCM aggregation, and staged RIJCOSX
therefore remain exact-once even when rejected or locally renumbered native
segments ran along the way.

Geometry-optimization, atomization, Hessian, and other helper SCFs carry
separate phase labels and finish before the terminal `job_end` record. Their
heartbeats cannot replace the final headline result in `.system`. Callback
state is restored after success, failure, nesting, periodic jobs, and
concurrent molecular jobs. Issue #205's separate stability wall/CPU timing is
preserved: the orbital-Hessian Davidson analysis itself still has no live
iteration callback, while any corrective SCF it launches is visible.

The SCF equations, convergence criteria, densities, and energies are
unchanged; no scientific energy pin moved.

Patch-candidate: v0.15.x

### Fixed: molecular direct SCF certifies energy on one Fock map (issue #418, 2026-08-28)

S22-19 RHF/cc-pVDZ (147 basis functions) was reported as an energy tolerance
below the floating-point floor: its commutator passed while `dE` dithered to
the 200-iteration cap. Reproduction disproved that diagnosis. Archived
nonincremental full-density builds from iterations 44 through 197 span only
`3.979e-12 Ha`, so the requested `1e-10 Ha` is attainable. The default
incremental difference-Fock recurrence instead had median `|dE| = 6.70e-9 Ha`
and excursions to `4.59e-8 Ha`; errors omitted from earlier screened
increments remain in the cached Fock, so those energy differences do not all
belong to one numerical map.

RHF, UHF, RKS, and UKS now treat loose-screened and incremental direct Fock as
a coarse phase. When the orbital gradient first becomes convergence-eligible,
or the existing drift-stall detector fires, the driver forces the configured
tight Schwarz threshold, disables the incremental recurrence, clears every
DIIS, SOSCF, Fock-mixing, damping, TRAH, and oscillation-history epoch, and
reports the transition at standard diagnostic verbosity. The first
full-density row is deliberately non-comparable with its coarse-map
predecessor; only the following same-map row can satisfy the unchanged energy
and gradient criteria. A custom `schwarz_threshold_tighten_at` can no longer
admit a loose-screened result.

This retains the issue #129 follow-up recorded later in this section: a shared
stall is gated on `!converged`, including an energy-only stall after the
gradient has passed, while an actual orbital-rotation restart remains
gradient-gated. The new gradient-eligibility transition normally ends the
coarse Fock phase before that energy-only stall needs to accumulate.

Fail-first on the exact issue deck with 12 OpenMP threads and a 20-iteration
budget ended unconverged at `dE = -5.852484719071e-9 Ha`, gradient
`2.641375647829e-7`; the deterministic commutator-null mock exhausted 8
iterations with `disable_calls = 0`, `dE = -1.999999943436e-8 Ha`, and
gradient `1.087791964408e-15`. After the fix, S22-19 certifies at iteration 15
with `dE = -4.547473508865e-13 Ha`, gradient `2.046303794377e-7`, and returned
energy `-323.607429758890248 Ha`; returned versus terminal-trace energy differs
by `2.615e-12 Ha`. The strengthened mock proves the first full-density row
already passes both numeric tolerances but is rejected until the second
same-map row, in all four molecular drivers.

No convergence tolerance was weakened and no energy pin moved. The final
S22-19 energy differs from the independent nonincremental control by less than
`1e-11 Ha`.

Patch-candidate: v0.15.x

### Fixed: SECCM citations now follow the concrete runtime route plan (issue #463, 2026-08-27)

The molecular and periodic citation emitters independently rebuilt
semiempirical provenance instead of consuming the route plan's complete
citation inputs. In particular, a valid MSINDO-SECCM run emitted the CCM
construction and slab references but omitted both MSINDO engine papers from
`.out`, `.bibtex`, `.references`, and `.system`.

Both high-level runners now merge the plan's route-specific citation inputs
into their job-wide assembly, and molecular results retain the concrete plan
that produced them. The method identity, integral and SCF flags, boundary,
dimensional kernel, electronic temperature, and method-specific extra entries
therefore have one owner while each runner continues to add the rest of the
job's provenance. No citation database route or bibliography record changed;
the already-defined routes now reach the user-facing artifacts.

### Fixed: the incremental ΔD Fock drift-stall disengage was locked out by a gradient gate (issue #129, 2026-08-28)

`incremental_fock` defaults to `True`, so this is the **default** molecular SCF
path. On the adenine–thymine WC monomer B / cc-pVDZ deck at
`conv_tol_energy = 1e-10` the run returned `converged = False` at the iteration
cap while holding the correct energy (3.2e-11 Ha from the full-rebuild fixed
point). It shipped in v0.15.144 through v0.15.148.

The IID 129 disengage (`f7f2ba318`) drops the incremental ΔD cache on a stall so
the fine phase runs the exact screened rebuild. It was nested under a gate
requiring `grad_norm > conv_tol_grad`, inherited from the BUG 64
orbital-rotation restart it shares the block with — where refusing to rotate an
already-converged gradient is exactly right. But the ΔD screening bias floors
the **energy**, not the gradient: the measured stall jitters `dE` at ~3e-8
against a 1e-10 tolerance while `grad_norm` sits at ~3e-7, well *inside*
`conv_tol_grad = 1e-6`. The disengage was therefore locked out precisely when
the gradient was best converged, and the SCF ran to `max_iter` holding the right
answer.

Bisected to `184644342` (scale-aware oscillation detection, IID 152), which is
itself **correct and is not reverted**. Before it, the over-eager detector
engaged a level shift at iteration 15 on a `dE` of 4.4e-9 — a converging DIIS
tail, not a limit cycle, and below that commit's own 1e-8 significance floor —
and the resulting perturbation happened to push `grad_norm` above 1e-6, which is
the only reason the disengage ever fired on this deck. `184644342` removed an
accidental crutch and exposed a latent defect in the `f7f2ba318` gate.

Measured single-threaded on this deck, one native rebuild per tree:

| tree | outcome |
|---|---|
| `f7f2ba318` (the IID 129 fix) | converged, 39 iters; disengage at iter 37, `grad=1.944e-06` |
| `c539eeaed` (`184644342^`) | converged, 39 iters; disengage at iter 37, `grad=1.944e-06` |
| `184644342` | **not converged, 100 iters**; neither level shift nor disengage fires |
| `origin/main` pre-fix | **not converged, 100 iters**; neither fires |

The gate is now `!converged` on the shared block, with `grad_norm >
conv_tol_grad` moved onto the orbital-rotation branch alone. The restart branch
is behaviour-preserving — `grad_norm > conv_tol_grad` already implies
`!converged` — while the disengage now fires on any stall that has not
converged, whichever tolerance is outstanding. Applied to all four molecular
drivers (RHF/RKS/UHF/UKS), matching `f7f2ba318`'s own scope.

Two properties of this defect are worth recording, because both are about how it
stayed invisible rather than about the SCF:

* The lane carrying the regression test is **T2**, and the release gate runs
  **T0+T1** only, so a red default-path SCF lane never blocked a tag and the
  regression shipped four times with no signal (#450).
* The failure is **thread-count sensitive**. `tests/conftest.py` pins
  `OMP_NUM_THREADS=1` on darwin; at the default thread count the larger
  floating-point jitter pushes `grad_norm` across 1e-6 and the old gate happens
  to fire, so the identical build passed standalone and failed under pytest.
  Anyone reproducing this must match the thread count.
### Fixed: broker git checks ran in a directory that is not a checkout (issue #443, 2026-08-28)

The 2026-08-27 deploy of the three startup repairs succeeded and two of them
did nothing. `_main_commit_ancestry` and `_main_contains_exact_sha` both shelled
out to git **without a `cwd`**, inheriting the broker process's working
directory. On example_hub that is the service's own state directory, whose
`.git` is a plain config folder — not a checkout. `git remote get-url origin`
therefore failed, both helpers returned empty, and the abbreviated-SHA
reconciliation refused all 43 candidates. Correct fail-closed behaviour,
entirely silent. The same defect had already disabled the
`legacy-landed-import` provenance check on that host, unnoticed.

Both helpers now resolve inside `BROKER_REPO_PATH`, a read-only canonical
checkout named in `broker.env`, and refuse when it is unset. The remote
comparison also accepts the canonical URL with a trailing `.git` or `/` —
without that, the only canonical checkout on example_hub would still have been
rejected, since its remote carries the `.git` suffix.

Startup now reports what each repair did and warns explicitly when the repo
path is unset or yields no canonical `origin/main`. A repair that silently
does nothing is indistinguishable from one that was never deployed; that is
what cost a full diagnosis cycle here.

Measured against the live broker: pointing at the managed queue checkout
resolves **35 of 41** abbreviated SHAs. The remaining 6 are commits newer than
that checkout's `origin/main`, which advances only at deploy time; the repair
is idempotent and runs every start, so they apply on a later restart. The
broker never fetches or writes there (CLAUDE.md § 15).

### Fixed: a demoted fixer generation aborted `reconcile-plan` project-wide (issue #124, 2026-08-28)

With #124's phantom generation demoted to `released`, its verifier grants kept
referencing it, and `_reconciliation_plan` treated that as invalid remote
state — so the plan still aborted for every issue, with a new message
("references a fixer that was not landed") replacing the old one.

The broker only issues a verifier claim against a landed fixer, so such a
grant records a generation that *was* landed and has since been demoted. It is
history, not corruption, and says nothing about the issue's current state,
which the projection reads from the latest generation. It is now skipped
rather than fatal. A verifier grant naming a generation that never existed is
still rejected.

### Correction: the `verified` backlog is not self-verified (issue #453, 2026-08-28)

Recorded because #453's central factual claim is wrong and work was being
planned on it. #453 states that in all 28 flagged records "the verifying
`actor_id` **equals** the `fixer_actor`". Queried directly against the broker's
`events` table — the only place a verifier's identity is stored, and not part
of the mirrored note body, which is why the notes look like bare three-line
records — the live classification of every `verified` generation is:

| classification | n |
|---|---|
| cross-actor (verifier ≠ fixer) | 239 |
| multiple distinct verifier actors | 8 |
| self-verified (verifier = fixer) | **0** |
| no `VERIFIED` event | 0 |

The startup demotion found and demoted the only two genuine self-verifications
in the database (#31, #222) and correctly spared the rest. It is complete, not
inert. The flagged records are **evidence-free**, which is a real and separate
problem, but they are not self-verifications and demoting them would discard
genuine cross-actor verdicts.

### Hardened: the GFN2 parameter converter keys shell records by letter, not by line order (issue #467, 2026-08-28)

The TOML converter collected the upstream `KCNS`/`KCNP`/`KCND` and
`POLYS`/`POLYP`/`POLYD` records with `.extend()`, in line order, and then
indexed the result by the shell's angular momentum. That was correct only
because every element block in the current upstream revision happens to list
them in s, p, d order (verified: 0 of 86 blocks deviate). Nothing enforced it,
and a future revision that emitted `KCND` before `KCNS` would have silently
re-created the exact rotation that issue #43 fixed and issue #446 re-attested,
with no test failing: a rotated cache is still structurally valid, so the only
symptom would have been the loaded content digest moving off
`GFN2_PUBLISHED_SHA256`, which reads as tampering rather than as a mis-read
source.

Each record is now mapped onto its angular momentum by its own shell letter as
it is read, and a duplicated or unrecognised letter, or a record carrying more
than one value, aborts the refresh instead of being absorbed, so no cache is
written from a source the converter cannot map. Guarded by
`tests/test_gfn2_xtb.py::TestGFN2ShellRecordKeying`, which renders a synthetic
element block with those records deliberately out of order and asserts each
value lands on its own l; the synthetic block is built in the test, since the
upstream parameter file is fetched at runtime and not redistributed.

**Scope.** No parameter value changes. Re-running the converter over the
current upstream `param_gfn2-xtb.txt` reproduces the existing cache
byte-for-byte, so `GFN2_PUBLISHED_SHA256` is unchanged at `0b3c70a5...` and no
pinned energy moves.


### Attestation repair: the GFN2-xTB published-parameter identity is re-attested against the publication (issue #446, 2026-08-27)

`af133afd2` (issue #43) corrected a transcription error in how the published
GFN2-xTB parameters are loaded, which necessarily moved the canonical content
digest of the loaded parameter object. It updated the native pin but not
`GFN2_PUBLISHED_SHA256` in `tests/test_gfn2_parameter_identity.py`, so four
nodes in that lane had been red on `main` ever since (there is no per-commit
CI to catch it). The pin is now re-attested from `71b83ab4...` to
`0b3c70a5...`, **with the transcription error and its published source
recorded** rather than silently bumped.

**What was mis-transcribed.** The upstream `param_gfn2-xtb.txt` lists each
element's shells in occupation order, which is d-first for the 41
transition-metal elements (`ao=3d4s4p`, `4d5s5p`, `5d6s6p`; Z 21-29, 39-47,
57-79), while `KCNS`/`KCNP`/`KCND` and `POLYS`/`POLYP`/`POLYD` are named per
angular momentum. The TOML converter indexed those named records by shell
position, so on exactly those 41 elements the s parameter was applied to the d
shell, the p parameter to the s shell and the d parameter to the p shell. It
manifested as an H0 error growing with distance (Cu2 off `xtb` by
+35.8/+56.8/+139.5 mHa at 2.2/2.5/3.0 Angstrom), non-converging free Cu8/Cu16
clusters, and a spurious charge-density-wave basin in fcc Cu cyclic-cluster
cells. Elements already listed in angular-momentum order are bit-identical.

**Published source.** The re-attested values were checked against Bannwarth,
Ehlert & Grimme, *J. Chem. Theory Comput.* **15**, 1652-1671 (2019),
doi:10.1021/acs.jctc.8b01176, Supporting Information Table S52
("Element-specific shell parameters employed in GFN2-xTB"), which tabulates
the polynomial scaling parameters, the CN-dependent level enhancement, the
level constants and the Slater exponents per shell label; per-l keying is the
paper's own convention (eq 17 and eq 19). For Cu, SI Table S52 gives
polynomial scaling 0.177983 / 0.149778 / -0.265089 and level constants
-6.922958 / -2.267723 / -9.506548 eV for 4s / 4p / 3d, and the loaded set
carries exactly those on l = 0 / 1 / 2. The `tblite` H0 bisection that
originally located the defect is corroboration from an independent
implementation, not from the publication, and is documented as such.

**Scope.** Identity and attestation only; no parameter value and no pinned
energy changes here. The digest difference is attributable solely to the
kcn/poly re-indexing: rotating only those two fields back to shell-positional
order on the 41 d-first elements reproduces `71b83ab4...` exactly. Documented
at the pin, at the converter, at the native digest, and in the user guide
under "Published-parameter identity". Unblocks issue #280, whose tamper-guard
contract was unverifiable while this lane was red.


### Fixed: `bugctl` surfaces the resolved actor and refuses the unconfigured fallback (issue #458, 2026-08-28)

A claude-code session claimed IID 307 and the grant came back as
`actor_id: "codex-loop"`, because that clone's `.git/bugctl/config.json` still
held an earlier session's `agent_id`. `_actor_id()` consults
`BUGCTL_AGENT_ID`, then that file, then falls back to `local-agent`, all
silently, and `bugctl doctor` reported `agent_identity: passed` throughout --
that check only proves the registry of *all* agents parses, and never showed
which actor the invocation would resolve to.

This is not a cosmetic mislabel. The broker's `self_verify_denied` guard is
keyed on `actor_id`, so a fixer running as the wrong actor lets the real actor
later "independently" verify its own fix, defeating the independent-verification
requirement without anyone noticing.

`doctor` gains a named `actor_resolution` check reporting the resolved actor
**and its source** -- `env BUGCTL_AGENT_ID`, the full path of the per-clone
config, or the fallback -- and fails when the actor is the fallback or is
absent from the registry. Naming the file is the point: it is what makes a
stale one findable. Every broker mutation additionally refuses to run as the
`local-agent` fallback, naming the source in the error.

The mutation guard deliberately does **not** re-check registration: the broker
holds the authoritative registry and already answers `Unknown actor`, whereas
checking it client-side would make every mutation depend on the relative
`agent-identity.toml` resolving from the caller's cwd. Read-only commands stay
usable without a configured actor, so `doctor` can still diagnose the problem.

### Fixed: the self-verification demotion missed every record it was written for (issue #453, 2026-08-28)

`_demote_self_verified_generations` read provenance only from `passed`
`verifier_grants` rows. Pilot-era self-verifications predate that table and
have **zero** rows in it, so the migration reached `continue` on every one and
demoted nothing. Measured against the live broker: 56 `verified` generations
carry the pilot-era shape (14 of them on open issues) and the migration as
shipped caught **0 of 56**.

Provenance is now read from the best evidence available. A `passed` verifier
grant remains authoritative when present; otherwise the `VERIFIED` event's
`actor_id` is used, since it is the only surviving trace for pilot-era
records. Those payloads carry `verdict` and `event_id` only — no
`fixer_generation` — so such an event is attributed to a generation only when
the issue has exactly one `verified` generation for it to refer to (true for
all 56 live records). When neither source identifies a verifier, the record is
left alone rather than demoted on an assumption, and a verdict by a distinct
actor is untouched as before.

### Fixed: demotion and `verify` disagreed about who the fixer is (issue #453, 2026-08-28)

`_demote_self_verified_generations` computed the fixer as the grant's
`actor_id`, while `/v1/verify` denies self-verification on `fixer_actor`. The
audited legacy-import path added in `00bab1a5a` records
`actor_id='maintainer'` with the true fixer in `fixer_actor`, so on those
generations the two paths reached opposite verdicts: a genuine
self-verification was compared against `maintainer` and spared, and a genuine
cross-actor verification by the maintainer could be demoted. The migration now
uses `fixer_actor` — `verify`'s notion — and keeps `actor_id` for row identity
only.

### Fixed: abbreviated landed SHAs blocked verification fleet-wide (issue #443, 2026-08-28)

Generations landed before the `080a66a64` resolution guard stored whatever
string the fixer pasted. A raw abbreviation makes `/v1/verifier-claim` refuse
the generation outright ("Current landed provenance is not an exact 40-hex
SHA; run reconciliation before verifier claims"), so completed verification
evidence could not become a verdict — and the reconciliation that error names
had no apply path. Measured live: 41 latest generations carry an abbreviated
SHA, 30 of them on open issues.

A new idempotent startup repair rewrites such a SHA in its exact 40-hex form.
The broker derives the expansion from the stored prefix itself; there is
deliberately no endpoint accepting a caller-supplied target, because a caller
who could name the commit could point a landed generation anywhere. Only 7–39
hex digits matching **exactly one** commit in the pre-fetched canonical
`origin/main` ancestry are corrected — zero matches and ambiguous prefixes are
both refused, and a value already 40 characters is never rewritten. That
ceiling is the safety property: the correction can only lengthen a prefix into
the commit it already designates, never retarget a generation, so it cannot
reach the exact-but-off-main records (#124, #139, #145, #149) and cannot
truncate #135's 64-hex SHA-256 into a fabricated 40-hex value — the padding
failure of #75, in reverse. Verifier grants bound to the same generation move
with it, since `fixer_sha` is the fencing token their leases validate against.

Dry-run against a copy of live broker state: 55 corrections, of which 41 are
the latest generation of their issue (30 open, 11 closed) and 14 are older
generations corrected for ledger hygiene. **The repairs run at broker startup,
so they take effect only when the broker is next restarted.**

Not addressed here, and recorded on the issues: the four exact-but-off-main
records need a verdict from a non-fixer actor (`_demote_unpushed_landed_generations`
already covers #124 on the next restart); #135's SHA-256 needs a human
decision; and #443's fifth mode — a SHA that resolves cleanly but points at a
docs-only commit — is invisible to SHA validation at any point and is a
verification-time concern.

### Added: `bugctl land` SHA-provenance regressions at the command boundary (issue #443, 2026-08-27)

#443 reports six landed generations across four failure modes whose recorded
fixer SHA cannot be resolved against authoritative `origin/main`, each blocking
independent verification. The prevention it asks for already exists: `cmd_land`
resolves through `_resolve_main_commit` against the pre-fetched `origin/main`
ancestry, added by `080a66a64` on 2026-08-26. **All six cited instances predate
that guard**, and the three landings recorded after it all carry valid,
resolvable SHAs.

What was not pinned is the command boundary. `_resolve_main_commit` is
unit-tested, but nothing asserted that `land` itself refuses an unresolvable SHA
*and never reaches the broker* -- so a refactor dropping the resolution call
would leave every existing test green. New
`tests/test_bugctl_land_sha_provenance.py` pins all four filed modes (absent
from main, not a git object, fabricated 40-hex extension of a real
abbreviation, raw abbreviation) plus ambiguity, asserting in each case that no
broker call is attempted; the abbreviation case asserts expansion to the exact
40-hex commit rather than raw storage. Verified by mutation: removing the
resolution from `cmd_land` fails 5 of the 6.

Two residual gaps are **not** closed here and are recorded on the issue: the
broker validates SHA *shape* only, so a client other than `bugctl` can still
record an absent-from-main SHA; and a recorded SHA that is a real main commit
but the wrong or partial one (#280, #359) is not detectable by SHA validation
at any point -- that is a verification-time concern, not a landing-time one.


### Fixed: CCM guide regression ignores line wrapping (issue #455, 2026-08-27)

The CCM Madelung-default documentation gate embedded literal Markdown
newlines in two substring checks, so harmless paragraph reflow left the lane
red while the guide and runtime defaults remained correct. The gate now
normalizes whitespace before checking the same four semantic claims; the
documented high-level and direct-helper defaults are unchanged.

### Added: audited import for legacy LANDED fixes (issue #407, 2026-08-27)

The maintainer-only `bugctl legacy-landed-import` command can migrate one
historical GitLab `LANDED` note into the broker's verifier lifecycle without
replaying a claim as the historical fixer. The broker independently requires
the exact open issue, registered fixer actor, full canonical-main SHA, trusted
non-system GitLab note with one well-formed actor and SHA field, admin token,
and no broker lifecycle history for that IID. The landed generation, import
request, and provenance event are durable and exact replays are idempotent;
mismatched, malformed, off-main, conflicting, incomplete, and
self-verification paths fail closed. This source change neither deploys the
broker nor imports a production issue.
### Fixed: scoped vq rollout planning isolates stale receipts on excluded hosts (issue #356, 2026-08-27)

A structurally valid retained legacy receipt from an older accepted report was
treated as a fleet-global report-identity failure before host selection. In the
v0.15.148 incident, unreachable site_b retained its v0.15.118 full-hold receipt,
so read-only planning for quiescent site_i and site_j failed before either host's
accepted-report lanes were built. Scoped rollout planning now validates every
journal and receipt globally, then carries an exact stale receipt forward only
for a configured host explicitly excluded by `--only` or `--skip`. That host
remains byte-identically retained, deferred, and visible; it receives no
legacy recovery or drain release control, although ordinary read-only fleet
snapshots may still probe it. Unscoped, selected-host, unknown-host, malformed,
partial, and hash-incoherent evidence still fails closed before planning.

### Corrected: the v0.15.148 note on issue #392 over-claimed boolean rejection

v0.15.148 stated that every public molecular SCF route rejects a
"nonpositive, boolean, or non-integer" `max_iter`. **The boolean half is
false for four of the six routes.** Independent verification measured
`run_rhf`, `run_uhf`, `run_rks` and `run_uks` accepting `max_iter=True` and
returning real energies at `n_iter=1` (RHF -1.1167143250625702, UHF
-0.46658184955727544, RKS -1.1212007040063123, UKS -0.4356702329795717).
The cause: `RHFOptions` and its siblings are pybind11 structs whose setter
coerces `True` to `1`, so the shared validator only ever sees `1`. Only
ROHF/ROKS — pure-Python dataclasses — reject booleans, and the fix's own
test parametrises `True` for those two routes only, so the gate cannot
detect the gap.

The nonpositive and non-integer rejections *are* real on all six routes, and
the rejection ordering is correct (before ECP attach, DFT+U and the core
call). Issue #392 is reopened for the boolean half and for a documented
contract this change broke: `docs/user_guide/from_orca.md:103` still maps
ORCA's `! NOITER` to `max_iter = 0`, which now raises.

### Fixed: deterministic HCI PT2 is independent of candidate order (issue #457, 2026-08-27)

The heat-bath and brute-force deterministic Epstein-Nesbet PT2 paths retained
the same `eps2`-screened perturbers and built the same coherent numerators, but
inserted those perturbers into an unordered map in different orders. Reducing
that map directly made the final energy depend on enumeration order and split
the paths by one ULP on the dense-oracle fixture. The outer PT2 sum now follows
a canonical determinant order, preserving the published screening and
coherent-sum equations while making both enumeration paths bit-identical.

### Fixed: vq rejects unsafe durable process identities (issue #462, 2026-08-27)

Durable job records accepted zero, negative, boolean, string, and float values
for local process IDs, process-group IDs, and crash-safe pause-intent groups.
In particular, process-group zero could reach POSIX signal calls and target the
caller's own process group. All three identities now require strict positive
integers or `None` during construction, JSON read, and assignment, so malformed
records fail before pause, resume, kill, watchdog, or recovery process control.


### Fixed: fixer briefs must name a dedicated clone, and build-and-measure cycles abort when HEAD moves (2026-08-28)

`agentic-loop/fixer-brief-contract.md` already required "Isolated worktree
named; shared checkouts explicitly off-limits" (brief checklist item 3), but
dispatched briefs routinely named an existing per-topic clone instead
(`vibeqc-claude-pbc-parity`, `-gpaw`, `-cosx`, `-documentation`,
`-dlpno-general` and others). Those clones belong to their topic chats, so a
dispatched fixer and the chat that owns the tree move HEAD under each other.
On 2026-08-27 that voided an issue #129 bisect leg: the leg was checked out
in a shared clone and a concurrent agent ran `checkout main` + `pull
--rebase` during its ~25-minute native rebuild, so the probe executed main's
Python sources against the leg's compiled core and died with `ImportError:
cannot import name 'MOLECULAR_XC_GRID_MAX_WORKERS'`.

Checklist item 3 now requires a **dedicated clone**, not a worktree, and
states why: CLAUDE.md paragraph 3's editable-install pin means a build inside
a worktree exercises a different tree's Python sources, so a green run there
proves nothing about the fixer's own edits. The checkpoint contract's two
"worktree" references follow.

The loud `ImportError` was the benign outcome.
`tests/conftest.py::pytest_sessionstart` documents the dangerous one — a
mismatched core "can silently produce WRONG NUMBERS, so the symptom looks
like a physics regression rather than a build problem" — and that hook fires
only under pytest, so bisect legs, convergence probes and benchmark drivers
running bare `python` got no warning at all. New
`scripts/head_stable_run.sh` wraps a build-and-measure cycle, stamps HEAD on
either side, and exits 98 — discarding the command's own exit status — if
HEAD moved, so a mismatched pair cannot be recorded as a measurement. Dev
tooling and coordinator process only; no user-facing behaviour changes.

## [v0.15.148] - 2026-08-27 - *Neese's Cheetah*

Seven fixes, drawn from three parallel bug-sweeps working molecular
correlation, molecular SCF and the semiempirical queue.

Two are provenance repairs on user-facing citation surfaces. The three named
DLPNO threshold presets now carry their **published** values (#416) — the
preset called TightPNO previously matched published TightPNO on zero of its
three thresholds, with TCutPairs five times looser, which is the knob
noncovalent interaction energies are most sensitive to. And a DLPNO run's
`.out` now records the thresholds it actually ran at (#417), so a preset
claim in a paper is provable from the artifacts rather than from a payload
script.

On correctness: spin-restricted selected-CI no longer reports an unreachable
CAS target as converged (#107); molecular SCF routes reject nonpositive,
boolean and non-integer `max_iter` budgets at both the C++ entry points and
all six public routes (#392) instead of manufacturing zero-cycle results;
Molden READ preserves ORCA-exported SCF roots (#12); and `upm7` requests
reach the canonical PM7 gate message instead of a generic basis error
(#413). The frozen-core convention of every correlated route is now pinned
by tests (#140).

Known open and shipping unfixed, stated plainly:

* **#129** — the default-path molecular SCF convergence regression
  (`incremental_fock` defaults True) is still open and still present. Its
  test lives in a T2 lane that the release gate does not run (#450).
* **#446 / #280** — the GFN2 published-identity pin remains stale after a
  parameter-table repair, so that attestation still fails.
* **#444** — the GFN2-SECCM 3-D `ewald_gamma` kernel has no thermodynamic
  limit (successor to the #425 analysis, now closed).
* **#435** (producer-side gap convention), **#436**, **#437**.

Ledger note, since it affects how this project's own records should be read:
**#443** catalogues five ways a recorded fix SHA can point at the wrong
commit, and **#453** documents 28 issues whose `verified` state is a
self-verification with no evidence. A re-verification pass found the
underlying fixes sound — the defect is in the recording, not the
engineering — but the records themselves should not be trusted as
independent verification until they are redone.

### Fixed: spin-restricted selected-CI no longer reports an unreachable CAS target as converged (issue #107, 2026-08-27)

`spin_restricted=True` — the default — walks the *seniority-zero* basis:
closed-shell determinants over spatial orbitals, excited by whole pairs. That
subspace holds `C(norb, nelec/2)` determinants and **cannot represent an
open-shell configuration**, so on an active space whose solution has
open-shell character the energy converges to a limit that is not the CAS
energy — and converges honestly, reporting `converged=True` and
`stop_reason="energy"` with no complaint.

On N2/cc-pVDZ CAS(6e,6o) that is a silent **62.3 mHa**:

| `spin_restricted` | ndet | E(variational) | E(PT2) |
|---|---|---|---|
| True (default) | 16 | −108.9594460730 | −0.0000000000 |
| False | 96 | −109.0217859876 | −0.0000000000 |

This is also the explanation for the two observations that looked like
separate defects. The ladder's energy is bit-identical at every `target_size`
from 6 to 400 because the coupled seniority-zero subspace was already spanned
at ndet=6 — the space of CAS(6e,6o) is C(6,3) = **20** determinants, so 16 is
near-saturation of a small subspace, not 4 % of a large one. And `E(PT2)` is
exactly zero because the restricted PT2 enumerates only seniority-zero
perturbers, every one of which is already in-space or uncoupled. It was
correct. This is why the earlier threshold relaxation moved `ndet` from 6 to
16 and left the energy unchanged.

Nothing numerical changes here — there was no wrong arithmetic. A restricted
run that converges **short of its requested `target_size`** has hit the
ceiling, and now says so, naming the size of the subspace it was actually
confined to and pointing at `spin_restricted=False`. It stays quiet when the
restricted space genuinely satisfies the request, and on unrestricted runs;
both are pinned in `tests/test_solvers_selected_ci.py`.

**Whether the default should flip to `spin_restricted=False` is left open**
as a maintainer decision on the issue, since it changes the result of every
existing call that did not set the flag.

### Added: the frozen-core convention of every correlated route is now pinned (issue #140, 2026-08-27)

vibe-qc's correlated routes do not agree with each other about frozen core.
Measured on def2-SVP, in both spin cases:

| route | frozen-core orbitals |
|---|---|
| `mp2` | 0 (all-electron) |
| `dlpno-mp2` | 0 |
| `ccsd` | **1** (chemical-core default) |
| `dlpno-ccsd` | **0** |

On the cases in #140 that difference is the *entire* residual against ORCA —
1.9–2.3e-3 Ha, exactly the core-correlation energy — while the same cases' SCF
sides agree to ~2e-9 Ha, which is what proves the offset is the convention and
nothing else.

`tests/test_frozen_core_convention.py` pins this table, divergence included,
and asserts that each route states its treatment in its own `.out`. It also
refines the issue's own diagnosis: #140 named DLPNO-UMP2 as diverging, but
canonical MP2 is all-electron too — the disagreement is specifically **CCSD vs
DLPNO-CCSD**.

**No convention is chosen here, deliberately.** Unifying them repins every
affected correlation energy by ~2 mHa — about twenty times the threshold at
which a repin needs maintainer sign-off — so the choice is raised as an ask on
the issue rather than taken in passing. What the pin buys meanwhile: the
divergence cannot widen silently, a cross-code comparison that trips over it
finds a named issue instead of a mystery offset, and when the convention is
settled exactly one named test fails and says what changed.

### Fixed: a DLPNO run's `.out` now records the truncation thresholds it ran at (issue #417, 2026-08-27)

`tcut_pno`, `tcut_pairs` and `tcut_mkn` reached **no** artifact — not the
`.out`, not the `.system`. Only the payload script and an opaque
`options_digest` carried them (`a3beca8618c3`, uniform across all 18 jobs of
the 2026-08-26 S22 wave, so it distinguished nothing to a reader). A run's
truncation level could not be checked against the run that produced it, which
makes a named-preset claim in a paper unprovable.

All four DLPNO `.out` blocks — MP2, UMP2, CCSD/(T), UCCSD/(T) — now carry a
`truncation thresholds` row listing the cutoffs the route actually resolved.
The blocks already reported the *consequences* of those thresholds (pairs kept
and screened, average PNOs per pair, frozen-core count); they simply never
reported the thresholds themselves. Only the knobs a route's own option class
carries are printed, since the six classes expose different subsets (#448), and
`0.0` is printed rather than omitted because it is a meaningful setting — no
truncation, full domains — not an absent one.

A side effect worth naming: the row makes #448 visible from any run's own
output. A DLPNO-MP2 job reports `tcut_pairs 1.0e-06  tcut_pno 1.0e-08
tcut_mkn 1.0e-03` while a DLPNO-CCSD job on the same molecule reports
`tcut_pairs 1.0e-04  tcut_pno 1.0e-07  tcut_mkn 0.0e+00`. Both routes are
pinned, in `tests/test_runner_dlpno_mp2.py` and `tests/test_runner_dlpno_ccsd.py`,
precisely because they resolve from different option classes — a single-route
pin would not prove the row reports that route's own values.

**The `.system` half is not done.** Recording resolved settings in the manifest
needs a shape change in `vibeqc/output/plan.py` / `manifest.py`, which is
IO-chat-owned under CLAUDE.md § 16, so it is filed as an ask in
`handovers/HANDOVER_OUTPUT_LOGGER.md` rather than landed here. The ask is
deliberately general: the same gap swallows an explicitly supplied `aux_basis`
(reaches the `.out` of three correlated routes, appears in none of their
`.system` manifests) and the frozen-core convention of #140.

### Fixed: Molden READ preserves ORCA-exported SCF roots (issue #12, 2026-08-27)

`InitialGuess.READ` accepted `.molden` but rejected ORCA's default
`.molden.input` filename. Renaming the file was worse than a workaround:
