ORCA's `[GTO]` block carries primitive-normalized contractions, while the
reader treated every Molden contraction as a raw Gaussian basis-file value
and normalized it again. The imported density therefore did not represent
the exported SCF root. In the fail-first regression a synthetic H2O/6-31G*
export fell from 10 electrons to `Tr(D S) = 7.630665411582`; the matched
tetrazine/cc-pVDZ ORCA export fell from 42 to `32.787124447682`.

The reader now accepts both suffixes, constructs the two documented
contraction interpretations, and selects between them using occupied-MO
orthonormality in the corresponding AO metric. It fails closed if neither
interpretation satisfies that invariant, if an MO omits its occupation or has
a non-finite coefficient, or if an occupied orbital omits or duplicates an AO
coefficient. Existing vibe-qc Molden round trips keep the raw-coefficient path;
both independently exported tetrazine ORCA roots retain 42 electrons and
restart to their source energies in 5-6 SCF iterations.

The original 49.2 mHa report is now classified rather than hidden by changing
an SCF control. Matched ORCA 6.1 runs reproduce both restricted stationary
points: HUECKEL and vibe-qc's default PATOM reach `-294.0434733 Ha`, while
HCORE reaches `-293.9942834 Ha`, 49.189899 mHa higher. The lower occupied
spaces agree with minimum principal cosine `0.99999999995`. Both RHF roots
have external spin-breaking instabilities and follow to different locally
stable UHF endpoints, so neither restricted energy is claimed as the global
ground state. No default guess, damping, level shift, DIIS control, threshold,
or existing energy pin changed.

Patch-candidate: v0.15.x

### Fixed: the broker demotes pilot-era self-verifications and phantom landed SHAs at startup (issues #453, #124, 2026-08-27)

Two historical ledger states could not be repaired through the ordinary
endpoints, and both blocked the close-the-bugs pipeline:

* **#453** — 28 open issues carry `verified` generations whose verifier actor
  equals the fixer actor (pilot-era records from before the
  `self_verify_denied` rule; the notes carry no evidence). On every startup
  the broker now demotes such generations back to `landed` (their verifier
  grants to `released`) and records a `SELF_VERIFICATION_DEMOTED` event, so a
  genuinely distinct actor can claim verification of the ORIGINAL landed
  generation. An ordinary fixer re-claim is deliberately not the path — that
  would forge the provenance the ledger exists to protect. Generations
  verified by a distinct actor are untouched.
* **#124** — a fixer generation `landed` on a SHA that was never pushed made
  `bugctl reconcile-plan` abort project-wide. A recorded `VERIFY_FAILED`
  verdict whose evidence explicitly declares the SHA absent from
  authoritative main now demotes that generation to `released`
  (`UNPUSHED_LAND_DEMOTED` event), returning the defect to the fix queue.

Both migrations are idempotent, broker-internal, and mirrored to the issue
notes when a token is configured. **Activating them requires a broker restart
on the broker host** (BUGCTL_SPEC § 7 deploy recipe; issue #347's maintainer
approval still gates the actual restart — this commit is source only).
Pinned by four new tests in `tests/test_bugctl_broker.py` (109/109 broker +
reconciliation tests green).


### Fixed: molecular SCF routes reject nonpositive max_iter budgets (issue #392, 2026-08-27)

RHF/UHF/RKS/UKS/ROHF/ROKS accepted `max_iter=0` or a negative budget and
manufactured internally inconsistent zero-cycle results: the native drivers
returned `n_iter=0`, `converged=false`, `energy=0.0` and empty density
matrices (UHF pairing a 0x0 density with nonempty orbital energies), while
ROHF/ROKS returned a plausible initial-guess energy labelled as a
zero-iteration nonconverged run.

Every public molecular SCF route now rejects a nonpositive, boolean, or
non-integer budget with `ValueError` before any driver work. The four native
drivers check at their low-level entry points (`run_rhf_scf_with_jk` /
`run_uhf_scf_once` / `run_rks_scf_with_jk` / `run_uks_scf_once` in
`cpp/src/`), and the public wrappers (`run_rhf` / `run_uhf` / `run_rks` /
`run_uks`) plus `run_rohf` / `run_roks` share one
`require_positive_max_iter` helper (`python/vibeqc/rohf.py`). Booleans are
rejected explicitly because `bool` is an `int` subclass in Python.
`max_iter=1` and the defaults keep their existing behaviour; no converged
energy moved. Pinned by `tests/test_scf_max_iter_boundary.py`.

### Fixed: the three named DLPNO threshold presets now carry their published values (issue #416, 2026-08-27)

`vibeqc.dlpno` exports `DLPNO_LOOSE`, `DLPNO_DEFAULTS` and `DLPNO_TIGHT`
under names that promise the DLPNO literature's LoosePNO / NormalPNO /
TightPNO sets. They did not carry those values. `DLPNO_TIGHT` was
`tcut_pairs` 5e-5 / `tcut_pno` 1e-8 / `tcut_mkn` 1e-3 against published
TightPNO's 1e-5 / 1e-7 / 1e-4 — **zero of three matching**, with pair
prescreening five times looser than the published set on the very knob the
source paper singles out as dominating noncovalent interaction energies.

The three constants now equal Table 1 of Liakos, Sparta, Kesharwani,
Martin & Neese, *J. Chem. Theory Comput.* **11**, 1525 (2015),
doi:10.1021/ct501129s, read from the paper rather than from a secondary
description; NormalPNO additionally matches the original DLPNO-CCSD
defaults stated in Riplinger & Neese, *J. Chem. Phys.* **138**, 034106
(2013), doi:10.1063/1.4773581 (Fig. 9 caption). Liakos 2015 is now in the
citation database and routed onto every DLPNO method.

No computed energy moves: these three constants are reference records that
no solver reads. Every DLPNO route takes its thresholds from its own option
class (`DLPNOMP2Options`, `LocalCCSDOptions`, …), and those defaults are
unchanged here. That split — six option classes, six different threshold
defaults, none of them a published set — is a separate defect, filed as
issue #448 with the measured table and a blast-radius note (unifying them
repins DLPNO energies, so it needs a maintainer decision).

`tests/test_dlpno.py` now pins each preset to its published triple with the
publication values in the test comment, pins preset-to-preset monotonicity,
and pins the two weak-pair companions that Table 1 does not fix as
vibe-qc's own convention so they cannot drift silently.

### Fixed: upm7 requests now reach the canonical PM7 gate message (issue #413, 2026-08-27)

Two fail-closed paths reported the wrong thing. `run_job(mol, method='upm7')`
without a basis raised the generic `run_job: basis is required` ValueError
before reaching the PM7 gate, and `run_semiempirical('upm7', mol)` raised
`Unhandled semiempirical method: 'upm7'` from the generic dispatch fallback.
Both now raise the canonical PM7 gate message ("PM7 is gated until the
published feathered electrostatics and all coupled NDDO terms are implemented
and validated.").

`upm7` joins `pm7` in `SEMIEMPIRICAL_METHODS` (the same reason `pm7` was
already a recognized spelling), and the gate message is single-sourced as
`PM7_GATE_MESSAGE` in `python/vibeqc/semiempirical/methods/pm7.py`, raised by
`routes._validate_boundary` too, so every PM7/UPM7 rejection path (route
planner, model wrappers, `run_job`, `run_semiempirical`) surfaces the same
text. Message quality only -- no working method changed behaviour and no
pinned energy moved. Pinned by three regressions in
`tests/test_pm7.py::TestPM7Gate`.


## [v0.15.147] - 2026-08-27 - *Neese's Cheetah*

Five fixes, four of them found by re-testing issues that had been filed and
never re-measured — a sweep pattern that turned out to be the highest-yield
work available.

The MSINDO 2-D Madelung constant was basis-choice dependent (#187): the
Parry/Heyes kernel enumerated its lattice sums over a fixed +/-12 integer
coefficient box instead of the physical Ewald cutoffs, so a unimodular shear
— which relabels the same surface lattice without changing the physics —
moved the constant by up to 8.0e-3. It is now invariant to 2.2e-16. The
native C++ twin carried the identical defect and moved with it. Note the
energy is the wrong probe here: on a neutral cell it shifts by 8.9e-16 while
the gradient shifts 3.5e-05 Ha/bohr.

The PM7 parameter parser dropped every fitted core radius (#224) — a
one-line key-normalisation that had been applied to the PM6 twin and missed
on PM7, leaving `pcore` silently zero for every PM7 element. 1-D CCM jobs no
longer cite the 2-D Parry slab-Ewald paper (#442). vq admin tests can no
longer write a marker into live per-user state (#438). Periodic GFN2-xTB
analytic stress is gated off with its gradient's true error pinned (#338).

Also corrected here: #187's changelog entry was appended into the already
released v0.15.146 section; it has been moved to where it belongs.

**Known open, and shipping unfixed in this release** — stated plainly
because these are not cosmetic:

* **#129** — a default-path molecular SCF convergence regression. The
  incremental-Fock path (`incremental_fock` defaults to True) returns
  `converged=False` at the 100-iteration cap on a Liakos aromatic case where
  the non-incremental control converges. It is present in v0.15.144, .145 and
  .146 as well. Its test lives in a T2 lane and the release gate runs T0+T1

* **#446 / #280** — the GFN2 published-parameter identity pin is stale after

### Fixed: MSINDO 2-D Madelung constant was basis-choice dependent (issue #187, 2026-08-27)

The 2-D (surface) MSINDO CCM Parry/Heyes Madelung kernel `_madkonst_2d`
enumerated its direct and reciprocal lattice sums over a **fixed +/-12 integer
coefficient box** rather than over the physical Ewald cutoffs. A unimodular
shear `a2 <- a2 + n*a1` relabels the same surface lattice, but it hides short
physical vectors behind coefficients outside that box, so the Madelung constant
changed with the choice of basis. Measured on an H2O 10x10 bohr surface mesh:
the converged `madkonst[0,0]` is **-0.390026492000**, while the shear-13 basis
`(10,0),(130,10)` returned **-0.397660474499** and shear-25 returned
**-0.398030563180** -- errors of 7.634 and 8.004 mHa. The required radius grows
with the shear (shear 13 needed ~40, shear 25 ~60), so no fixed radius is
correct. This affected live production code, not only a test oracle: 2-D
MSINDO-CCM energies and analytic gradients, in both the Python and the compiled
kernel. The analytic gradient on a polar Li-H surface cell moved by
**3.5e-05 Ha/bohr** under the same shear -- the sharpest contracted probe, since
a neutral cell's Madelung *energy* is largely insensitive to the near-uniform
part of the truncation error.

Both sums now range over the cutoff-complete sets `{K != 0 : |K| <= K_cut}` and
`{L : |v + L| <= r_cut}` -- sets of physical vectors, identical for every
unimodular basis -- with bounds from the direct/reciprocal dual metric, mirroring
the 3-D `_ewald_lattice_3d` that already worked this way. **No change to the
functional form**: the summand remains eq. (7) of Parry, *Surf. Sci.* **49**,
433 (1975) with the `K = 0` term of de Leeuw & Perram, *Mol. Phys.* **37**, 1313
(1979) eqs. (8)/(12). Post-fix the constant is basis-invariant to **2.2e-16** and
the gradient to **1.5e-12**. Reduced-basis results are unchanged to round-off
(<=1.8e-15 across square, rectangular and hexagonal meshes), so no pinned value
moves.

Two supporting changes: the reciprocal factors are now evaluated in the
`erfc(x) = e^{-x^2}*erfcx(x)` form already used by the shared slab kernel
(`vibeqc::ewald_2d_point_charge_potential`), which removes an `inf * 0 = nan`
overflow that a naive `e^{|K|z}*erfc(...)` hits at large `|K|z`; and a
pathological surface basis whose candidate box would exceed the safe allocation
budget now fails closed, as the 3-D path does. The previous mitigation -- the
public MSINDO route rejecting any non-Gauss-reduced surface basis outright -- is
removed, because the kernel now computes those bases correctly.

The 3-D path was checked and does **not** share the defect (invariant to
5.6e-17 across shears 13/25/40). The GFN2-SECCM half of #187 was already fixed
and is untouched.

### Fixed: 1-D CCM jobs no longer cite the 2-D Parry slab-Ewald paper (issue #442, 2026-08-27)

A 1-D (polymer/wire) MSINDO CCM run with `madelung=True` listed
`parry_2d_ewald_1975` in its references and `.system` manifest for a kernel
that performs no Ewald summation at all.

`routes.methods.wire_ewald_1d` credits Parry 1975 for the converged
background-corrected wire Ewald (`detail::wire_madkonst_1d`,
`cpp/src/semiempirical/seccm/ewald_1d.h`) and gates on the runtime kernel name
ending in `wire_1d`. But that name was built from `(dimension, family)` alone,
so **two different kernels shared it**: the SECCM adapters' Parry wire Ewald,
and MSINDO's `indo::_madelung_potential_1d` -- the truncated +/-1, +/-2 shell
bare point-charge lattice sum of `ccm1dmadelsum.f`, which the wire header
itself names as the kernel it replaced and which stays frozen for MSINDO. The
route therefore credited Parry with the sum his method superseded.

The dimensional-kernel table is now per engine: MSINDO's 1-D kernel resolves
to `madelung_truncated_1d`, so the Parry route cannot reach it, while
`scc_dftb`/`gfn2` SECCM keep `madelung_wire_1d` and their (correct) citation.
MSINDO's 2-D and 3-D paths are unchanged -- they run the genuine
`indo::_madkonst_2d` / `_madkonst_3d` machinery, and 2-D still cites both slab
papers.

`docs/user_guide/cyclic_cluster_model.md` carried the same overclaim in prose
("a classical Ewald (Madelung) embedding, summed in 1, 2, or 3 dimensions")
and now states which branches are Ewald summations and which is the truncated
direct sum.

Attribution-only; no energy, gradient or SCF path changed. Pinned by
`tests/test_citations.py::test_msindo_seccm_1d_does_not_cite_the_parry_wire_ewald`
and MSINDO rows in
`tests/test_semiempirical_route_plan.py::test_seccm_runtime_plan_records_concrete_citation_context`;
it also unblocks
`tests/test_msindo_ccm.py::test_ccm_run_job_lands_citations_on_every_surface`,
which had been failing on `main` since the wire route landed in `27536f799`.

### Fixed: Dewar-Thiel 1977 lands in the citation database; MOPAC version recorded at the PM6 tensor oracles (issue #420, 2026-08-27)

The #244 fix (commit `febe89375`) restored the PM6 heavy-heavy NDDO
multipoles with a correct inline citation but never added the paper to
`python/vibeqc/output/citations/database.toml` in the same merge
(CLAUDE.md Sec.8). The entry now exists (`dewar_thiel_1977`, Theor.
Chim. Acta 46, 89 (1977), DOI 10.1007/BF00548085, `print = true`) and
fires from the `pm6`, `upm6`, and `pm6_seccm` routes, so every
executable PM6 job carries it in `.out`, `.bibtex`, `.references`, and
the `.system` manifest. The `stewart_pm6_2007` note is refreshed to
match the post-#244 state: the complete AO-resolved MNDOD tensor
covers s/p-heavy pairs, with the spherical sigma/pi + Klopman-Ohno
fallback remaining only for pairs without published multipole data.

The new MOPAC oracle tensor pins in
`tests/test_semiempirical.py::TestMolecularPM6::test_oxygen_carbon_tensor_matches_mopac_mndod_oracle`
now record their provenance at the arrays (official Apache MOPAC
v23.2.5, revision 1d9d92b), matching the house style used by the
other #244 pins.


### Fixed: the PM7 parameter parser no longer drops every fitted core radius (issue #224, 2026-08-27)

`scripts/parse_mopac_pm7_params.py` registers MOPAC's `poc_7` array under the
key `poc_`, and `name.rstrip("7")` cannot normalize that -- the string ends in
an underscore, not a `7`. The writer only ever emits `poc`, so all seven
fitted PM7 core radii were silently dropped on every regeneration: the shipped
`pm7_mopac_params.toml` contains **zero** `poc` entries, against **six** in the
PM6 file whose parser already special-cases the same array. The fix mirrors
the PM6 parser exactly.

Pinned by a parser round-trip regression that asserts both the normalized key
and that the value survives `write_toml`, using a synthetic snippet in MOPAC's
Fortran D-format (the parameter source is not redistributed here).

**Not regenerated here.** Refreshing `pm7_mopac_params.toml` requires fetching
MOPAC's `parameters_for_PM7_C.F90`, and that bundled TOML is currently absent
from the `docs/license.md` inventory even though its own header declares
Apache-2.0 MOPAC provenance -- so regeneration should be paired with closing
that inventory gap. There is no runtime impact today: the PM7 and UPM7 routes
are gated closed pending their feathered electrostatics.
### Fixed: vq admin tests can no longer write a marker into live per-user state (issue #438, 2026-08-27)

`vibe-queue/tests/` creates a **real** `admin-update-in-progress` marker at 45
call sites across 10 files (`_arm_receipt` calls the production
`acquire_admin_update_marker`). Their only protection was the autouse
`_isolate_vq_state_env` fixture in `vibe-queue/tests/conftest.py`, which points
`VQ_STATE_DIR` at a tmp dir. That fixture is bypassed by any conftest-less
invocation -- and `--noconftest` is the documented way to run this repo's
root-level bugctl lanes, because the root `tests/conftest.py` imports `vibeqc`.
Such a run wrote `~/.local/share/vq/admin-update-in-progress` on the developer's
machine **and still reported the test as passed**. The resulting marker wedges
the host's admin lane and can be retired by neither `clear-update-marker` (which
redirects to `recover-update`) nor `recover-update` (whose receipt points at a
deleted pytest temp directory).

Both real marker writers -- `acquire_admin_update_marker` and
`write_admin_update_marker` -- now call a guard that, **under pytest only**,
refuses to create the marker when the resolved state root is the per-user XDG
root, before any write happens. Outside pytest the guard is inert, so a real
`vq admin update` is unaffected; an explicit `VQ_STATE_DIR` (a tmp dir, or a
multi-user root such as `/var/lib/vq`) is untouched. A test that would corrupt
live state now fails loudly instead of passing silently.

Not addressed here: retiring a marker whose receipt checkout no longer exists
remains unrecoverable through sanctioned verbs. That is the shared
"recorded state outlives its writer" problem tracked by #309 and #431 and needs
a policy decision rather than a new verb landed in passing.


### Fixed: periodic GFN2-xTB analytic stress is gated off; its gradient's true error is now pinned (issue #338, 2026-08-27)

`compute_periodic_gfn2_stress` is not the strain derivative of the periodic
GFN2 energy, so it now **fails closed** rather than returning a number that
looks like a stress. Measured on a gapped H2 molecular crystal (lattice
diag(8.0, 8.5, 9.0) bohr, converged Gamma SCF, gap 0.8186 Ha) against a
central finite difference in the strain, applied affinely to lattice **and**
positions:

```
V * sigma (analytic)   diag = (-0.3312, -0.0154, -0.0083)
dE/d(eps)  (strain FD) diag = (-0.0622, +0.0047, +0.0024)
```

5.3x too large on `xx` and **sign-inverted** on `yy` and `zz`. Two causes,
both on the issue: the atomic virial contracts as `-R_i grad_j` where the
strain derivative is `+grad_i R_j` (a negative transpose, not a sign slip),
and the electronic gradient it contracts is itself incomplete -- it omits the
AES moment-integral Pulay and density/moment response terms. Correcting the
virial alone would not make it a derivative, so it is deliberately not
half-fixed. `vibeqc.semiempirical.periodic.finite_difference_stress`
(`strain_positions=True` for the full strain derivative) differentiates the
shipped energy by construction and is what `optimize_cell` already uses; the
GFN2 periodic example now uses it. No Python-side caller consumed the analytic
kernel.

The periodic GFN2 **gradient** is deliberately *not* gated -- a ~4% gradient
still optimizes to a nearby geometry, where a sign-inverted stress pushes the
cell the wrong way -- but its true error is now pinned instead of hidden. The
gate this replaces allowed a gradient RMSD below 3 Ha/bohr and checked the
stress only for shape, symmetry, finiteness and `abs(stress[0,0]) < 1.0`,
which is why the defect survived. The new xfail regression measures the real
residual, 2.4e-3 Ha/bohr against a central difference, roughly 12x the 2e-4
target the issue sets.

## [v0.15.146] - 2026-08-27 - *Neese's Cheetah*

A verification-driven release: every fix here was root-caused rather than
patched, and several were found by re-testing issues that had been filed but
never re-measured.

Two false-green defects close. vq no longer records scheduler-killed jobs as
completed/exit-0 (#414) — that had two independent layers: the daemon never
consulted the truthful sacct verdict it had already parsed, and the batch
wrapper's GNU-time capture wrote exit 0 for signal-killed payloads, so the
exit marker itself was lying. And the SECCM positive-gap guard is no longer
skipped wholesale under smearing (#422), which had recorded a healthy 0.49 eV
gap as gapless in one direction and admitted a 1.3e-15 Ha gap as converged in
the other.

The k-route result classes now carry measured band edges and gaps (#426)
using the pooled-aufbau convention — the previous occupancy-partition formula
reported a spurious positive gap on 1,022 of 1,668 measured rows (up to
0.539 eV) and made the negative-gap screen structurally unable to fail
(#435, open for the producer-side half). CCM results carry structured backend
identity and parity-hold state (#344). Unrestricted Gamma DFTB0/SCC-DFTB
degenerate-frontier derivatives are fixed per spin channel (#439);
restricted and unrestricted now agree bit-identically on closed-shell systems.

#424 is closed by diagnosis: the reported cross-process nondeterminism was
never nondeterminism. Per-host outcomes are deterministic; the flip axis was
runtime-dispatched FP kernels destabilizing an exact-but-unstable symmetric
fixed point, and the trigger was already removed by #316 in v0.15.145. The
regression that was missing now pins the restored margin.

Known open and deliberately not fixed here: **#425** — the periodic SCC-DFTB
gamma lattice sum is divergent, not merely truncated (LiH energies oscillate
over ~10 Ha across the cutoff ladder while reporting converged=True). This
release documents it and pins the contract with an xfail; the fix requires
the Elstner Eq. 17 gamma with Ewald and is a pending method decision. Also
open: #435 (producer-side gap convention), #436, #437.

### Validated: fcc Cu bulk lattice constant from GFN2-SECCM, +2.4% (issue #130, 2026-08-27)

With the #43 parameter projection fixed, the 64-atom fcc Cu 4x4x4
cyclic cluster (`ewald_gamma` + `broyden_eyert`, T = 0.001 Ha)
converges in 15 to 20 iterations at every lattice constant from 3.615
to 4.4 A and has a parabolic minimum at **a = 3.7033 A, +2.4% versus
the experimental 3.615 A** - the same accuracy band as the bundled
diamond (-1.2%) and MgO (+1.8%) references, so bulk metals now sit
inside the validated SECCM ladder. The 8-atom 2x2x2 cell has no
minimum on the same grid and carries spurious charges an order of
magnitude larger (q_rms 0.24 to 0.41 against 0.008 to 0.12), which
confirms the previously reported small-cell `e_band0` offset as a
genuine finite-size artifact that converges away with cell size
rather than a kernel or parameter defect. For scale, the same 64-atom
cell before the parameter fix ran a 6 hour Newton solve without
reaching any fixed point.

The compressed-cell behaviour is also resolved, and it is not a
defect: numerical continuation of the fixed point downward in lattice
constant shows the physical branch annihilating in a saddle-node fold
at a_c of about 3.61 A, with the distance from singularity
min abs(eig(J - I)) collapsing from 0.719 at a = 3.9 through 0.441 at
3.7 to 0.0173 at 3.615, and the root gone by 3.58. Below the fold no
solver can find a physical fixed point because none exists, so the
adapter converging down to exactly 3.615 A and failing closed below it
is correct behaviour rather than an iteration-budget problem. The
driving channel is the on-site third-order GAM3 term, whose Jacobian
contribution grows with the compression-induced charge fluctuation:
the same continuation with GAM3 off keeps a healthy root down to at
least 3.4 A. The validated minimum at 3.7033 A sits well above the
fold. Evidence:
`studies/seccm-bulk3d/probe_cu_branch_continuation.py`.

### Documented: periodic SCC-DFTB gamma lattice sum is divergent on ionic systems (issue #425, 2026-08-27)

Diagnosis only -- **no behaviour change**; the fix is a method change pending
a maintainer decision (`agentic-loop/asks/ask-scc-dftb-periodic-gamma-ewald-2026-08-27.md`).

`build_periodic_dftb_gamma_matrix` sums the Klopman-Ohno form
`1/sqrt(R^2 + eta^2)` by bare real-space truncation. That is a sum of `1/R`,
divergent in 3-D; charge neutrality should cancel the divergence, but a
*pair-distance* cutoff gives different pairs different image counts, so each
pair retains a different divergent constant and the cancellation is
incomplete. Measured on LiH (a = 3.8 bohr): the SCC energy oscillates over
~10 Ha as the cutoff moves 12 -> 200 bohr (cutoff 160 gives -10.341, cutoff
200 gives -0.403), with `converged=True` on every rung. Isolated from the SCC
by evaluating the gamma matrix alone: `g_HH` diverges quadratically in the
cutoff (14.16 at 12 bohr -> 730.57 at 80 bohr) and the neutrality-projected
combination that `E_scc` actually sees oscillates at O(1) Ha.

Elstner et al., *Phys. Rev. B* **58**, 7260 (1998) p. 7263 -- the paper this
code cites -- states that the Ohno/Klopman forms "can therefore not be used"
for periodic systems, and gives Eq. 17 `gamma = 1/R - S(R)` with `S`
exponentially decaying so the long-range part can go through Ewald. Adopting
that form repins the whole DFTB surface, so it is not landed here.

Landed instead: an xfail regression pinning the cutoff-convergence contract
(`tests/test_semiempirical_periodic_native_fd.py::test_periodic_scc_dftb_gamma_sum_converges_with_cutoff`)
so the defect cannot be silently re-forgotten, and a user-guide warning naming
the affected system class. DFTB0 is unaffected -- it has no `gamma` term.


### Fixed: unrestricted Gamma DFTB0/SCC-DFTB degenerate-frontier derivatives (issue #439, 2026-08-27)

`e2b72553d` gave the *closed-shell* Gamma drivers the Weinert-Davenport
T -> 0 ensemble (issue #339), but that issue scoped its envelope to
closed-shell, so `run_udftb0_gamma` and `run_uscc_dftb_gamma` kept building
their densities from raw `C.leftCols(n_alpha)` / `C.leftCols(n_beta)`. The
defect #339 describes therefore survived intact in the unrestricted route:
the analytic gradient differentiated whichever eigenvectors the solver
happened to return inside a degenerate manifold. On the very fixture #339
used -- ideal diamond Si, where multiplicity 1 makes both spin channels cut
the same threefold manifold:

```
restricted   DFTB0  max|grad|  2.824347e-16 Ha/bohr   (fixed by #339)
unrestricted UDFTB0 max|grad|  2.800431e-03 Ha/bohr   (before this fix)
unrestricted UDFTB0 max|grad|  2.825431e-16 Ha/bohr   (after)
```

Both unrestricted Gamma drivers now apply the same convention per spin
channel (full occupancy 1.0 per channel, resolved independently because the
two channels cut the shared spectrum at different counts), carry those
occupations into the density and the energy-weighted density behind every
analytic gradient, and expose them as `occupations_alpha` /
`occupations_beta` -- the unrestricted results previously carried no
occupations at all, so a consumer could not even tell a fractional state
from a hard-Aufbau one. A channel whose frontier has an open gap keeps the
exact `C_occ * C_occ^T` assembly, so gapped systems are bit-identical.

**No energies move.** In a degenerate manifold the eigenvalues are equal, so
the occupation-weighted band sum equals the hard-Aufbau sum exactly
(measured: 0.000e+00 Ha/cell on the Si fixture). The defect was in the
density, and therefore in the derivatives, not in the energy. A new
invariant now holds that did not before: on a closed-shell system the
restricted and unrestricted Gamma drivers return bit-identical energies
(-2.2044027744065664 Ha/cell).

Also lands the citation route `e2b72553d` omitted (CLAUDE.md § 8):
`routes.methods.dftb0` and `.scc_dftb` now fire
`weinert_fractional_occupations_1992`, the paper whose ensemble both
drivers implement and name in-code.


### Fixed: vq no longer records scheduler-killed jobs as completed/exit-0 (issue #414, 2026-08-27)

Two site_j jobs OOM-killed by SLURM (sacct `State=OUT_OF_MEMORY`, `ExitCode
0:125`) were recorded `completed` with exit 0: the workspace exit-marker
read 0 and the reap path recorded the marker rc without reconciling the
terminal label against scheduler accounting, so downstream consumers
admitted OOM partials as clean successes. Two fixes in vq (bundled queue,
now reconciling on all three reap paths — marker visible, marker recovered
after final fetch, and accounting-only):

* The daemon now consults the terminal accounting verdict before recording
  a scheduler job's terminal state. A scheduler-attributed abnormal end
  maps to a failed-class state with the scheduler reason recorded —
  `OUT_OF_MEMORY` → `oom_killed`, `TIMEOUT`/`DEADLINE` → `time_exceeded`,
  `CANCELLED`/`NODE_FAIL`/`PREEMPTED`/… → `aborted_by_queue` — with the
  sacct state, accounting exit code, and marker rc preserved as evidence,
  and `scheduler_state` recording the scheduler verdict instead of staying
  frozen at `running`. The exit-marker remains the rc source of truth
  (`COMPLETED`/`FAILED` rows still classify by rc alone, and marker rc
  still wins over accounting rc for those), but a marker can no longer
  certify a clean completion the scheduler disowned. Torque carries no
  abnormality signal in its qstat states and is explicitly unaffected.
* The generated batch wrapper no longer writes marker rc=0 for a payload
  killed by a signal. GNU time 1.7 (still `/usr/bin/time` on older cluster
  nodes) exits with `WEXITSTATUS == 0` for a signal-killed command, so an
  OOM-SIGKILLed payload reached the marker as rc 0; the wrapper now
  recovers the `Command terminated by signal N` verdict from the raw
  collector output and records 128+N, in both the shared-workspace and
  node-scratch execution branches.

Regressions cover the dialect classification, the dispatcher passthrough
from a parsed sacct row of the exact incident shape, all three daemon reap
paths (a fake sacct OUT_OF_MEMORY row can never yield `completed`, with or
without a marker), and the rendered wrapper under a GNU time 1.7-style
collector.

### Fixed: cross-process SCC branch nondeterminism root-caused; regression pins the restored margin (issue #424, 2026-08-27)

Diagnosis of the rp246 flips (identical homonuclear B/Ga chain inputs
landing converged=True at n_iter=1 on one fleet host and converged=False
at n_iter=500 on another, one shared binary): the glide-symmetric dq=0
seed is an exact but dynamically UNSTABLE fixed point of the T=0 SCC
k-point map. The pre-#316 asymmetric lattice-image selection split the
glide-stuck zone-edge frontier pair by ~3.2e-7 Ha -- above the roundoff
scale at which the zero-temperature ensemble equalizes occupations, so
hard aufbau cut the pair; near-degeneracy then amplified per-host
last-ulp kernel differences (runtime-dispatched libm/SIMD paths across
site_h/site_k/site_l/amd node families) into iteration-1 Mulliken
residuals of 1e-13 to above 1e-10, racing conv_tol_charge=1e-10. Hosts
landing below the threshold accepted the seed at n_iter=1; hosts landing
above stepped off into a permanent occupancy-swap limit cycle -- the
binary n=1 / n=500 signature. Reproduced deterministically per host
(20/20; invariant to OMP_NUM_THREADS, PYTHONHASHSEED, and in-process
case history) and flipped locally at the wave SHA by tightening the
tolerance one notch. The #316 pair-distance image selection (660f72862)
already removed the trigger: symmetric image sets restore the exact
degeneracy and the T->0 ensemble occupations, dropping every wave-flip
residual to the 1e-15 rounding floor; #342 makes any surviving
non-convergence loud, and the even-replica 3-D SECCM gate fail-closes
the sibling both-converged attractor splits (p3dwalk/mixers R=4). New
`tests/test_semiempirical_kpoint_scc_branch_determinism.py` pins the
margin at 100x tighter tolerance on all six wave-flip inputs (fails 5/6
at the wave SHA) plus fresh-process byte-identity; suite-manifest row
registered via the CURATED table (also registering the #316 chat's
existing hand-written pair-image-selection rationale so regeneration
preserves it). Residual class risk -- a genuinely metallic T=0 frontier
whose splitting falls in the ~1e-13..1e-6 Ha band between the roundoff
ensemble and a real gap -- is a documented policy question on #424, not
silently patched.
### Fixed: SECCM positive-gap guard is no longer skipped under smearing (issue #422, 2026-08-27)

The finite-torus positive-gap guard was bypassed wholesale by finite
electronic temperature on both smearing-capable SECCM routes, in two
different ways, and both produced rows that passed every screen:

* **SCC-DFTB-SECCM** measured the gap but skipped the verdict
  (`!smeared &&`). The in-tree charged N=3 H-Li chain converges at a
  frontier gap of **1.3e-15 Ha** -- seven orders below the 1e-8 Ha guard
  epsilon -- with `converged=True` and nothing on the record saying the
  positive-gap requirement had been waived. Any screen of the form
  `converged and gap > 0` admitted it, because 1.3e-15 > 0.
* **GFN2-SECCM** skipped the *measurement* too, at both the supercell and
  the molecular-delegated site, so `homo_lumo_gap` kept its struct default
  of `0.0`. A finite-temperature-stabilized LiH-scale cell (LiF at 12 bohr)
  with a perfectly healthy **0.0180 Ha (0.49 eV)** gap was recorded as
  gapless -- wrong in both directions: it fails a `gap > 0` screen and it
  passes a `gap == 0` metallicity screen. This is the wave-scale
  "113/15722 ok rows at `gap == 0.0`, 87 of them from `temp`/`temp_diis`"
  signature.

Both routes now always measure and record the frontier gap, at every
electronic temperature; only the *verdict* is temperature-dependent. A
non-finite frontier is rejected unconditionally. At T = 0 a sub-epsilon
frontier is still rejected (the Aufbau occupation is ambiguous). At T > 0
the Fermi-Dirac occupation resolves that ambiguity, so the state stays
admissible -- but the waiver is now recorded as `gap_guard_waived` on the
result, and SCC-DFTB additionally records the applied epsilon as
`finite_torus_gap_tolerance` (GFN2 already exposed it on `run_controls`),
so a consumer can reproduce the accept/reject decision from the record
alone. No energy changes: this is a record-surface and verdict fix.


### Added: GFN2-SECCM 1-D wire ewald_gamma kernel (2026-08-27)

Nontrivial 1-D cells no longer fail closed under `ewald_gamma=True`:
the new `ewald_shell_gamma_1d` routes the background-corrected
Parry-type wire Ewald (the validated `ewald_1d.h` machinery behind the
1-D Madelung embedding) through the same dimension-free Wigner-Seitz
Klopman-Ohno correction and on-site assembly as the 2-D/3-D kernels,
with sibling e^-30 truncation targets that scale with the Ewald width
(production uses the wire convention alpha = 4/L). Regression anchors:
the kernel is alpha-independent to 1e-12 across alpha in {3/L, 4/L,
6/L} (the Ewald-identity oracle), its pure-Coulomb part matches a
brute-force background-corrected direct lattice sum with Richardson
extrapolation to 1e-9, and a two-cell LiH wire converges into the
physical basin with ionic charges and rigid-translation invariance at
1e-10. The kernel-aware citation routing now fires the wire-Ewald
reference for every SECCM 1-D run whose electrostatics kernel resolves
to the wire (madelung and ewald_gamma families alike; previously the
1-D kernel had no citation route). This closes the last dimensional
gap in the GFN2-SECCM electrostatics matrix: `ewald_gamma` now covers
1-D, 2-D, and 3-D cyclic topologies.
### Fixed: bugctl complete-collection reads no longer fail on redacted rows (issue #430, 2026-08-27)

`bugctl --json show <iid>` died with `api_error: incomplete collection:
X-Total is N but received M rows` on healthy issues (#237 24/22, #206
13/11, #400 8/6, #316), forcing raw `glab` fallbacks. The completeness
check compared the accumulated row count against GitLab's `X-Total` for
equality. That is not a contract GitLab offers: `X-Total` is computed on
the unfiltered relation and the payload is then redacted per caller.
Measured on issue #237, the read-scoped bugctl token is served 22 notes
under `X-Total: 24`; the two withheld rows are `mentioned in commit
<sha>` cross-reference notes, which the token cannot resolve to the
repository (the maintainer token is served all 24). The filed diagnosis
of system-note filtering was close but not the mechanism -- system notes
that are not cross-references are served normally.

`X-Total` is now treated as an upper bound. Completeness continues to be
enforced by the `X-Total-Pages` / `X-Next-Page` traversal, which is
unchanged and is the guarantee that actually detects a short read: a
missing, repeated, non-advancing, or malformed next-page header still
fails closed, as does a page count inconsistent with `X-Total-Pages`.
Receiving *more* rows than `X-Total` cannot come from redaction and means
pages overlapped or repeated, so that still fails closed.


### Fixed: semiempirical k-route results carry the measured band edges + gaps (issue #426, 2026-08-27)

The full-k semiempirical routes computed the indirect gap internally but
stored only `fermi_level` on the result record, so harvest judges were
forced onto torus-gap certificates (159 dual1d pairs demoted for want of a
measured gap). `KPointDFTB0Result`, `KPointSCCDFTBResult`, and
`KPointGFN2Result` now expose the measured edges natively:
`indirect_gap`, `direct_gap`, `valence_band_max`, `conduction_band_min`,
their defining k-indices (`*_k`), the per-k band edges
(`valence_max_per_k` / `conduction_min_per_k`), the structural
`is_metallic` flag, and `gap_above_fermi_manifold`; `KPointGFN2Result`
additionally exposes `occupations_per_k` like its DFTB siblings. The
classification derives from the occupations actually used, with the same
masks as the ab-initio multi-k band-extrema renderer (valence
`n > 1e-8`, conduction `n < 2 - 1e-8`): a fractionally occupied state --
a roundoff-degenerate zero-temperature Fermi group or a finite-T smeared
frontier -- belongs to both classes, so a converged metal / zero-gap row
always measures an explicit unclamped `<= 0` gap, never an absent one
(diamond-Si 3x3x3 measures its Fermi-group `-0`; per-point band overlap
measures its true negative value). NaN appears only where an edge does
not exist in the model space (zero electrons, or a completely filled
valence-minimal basis such as fcc Ar) or on an unconverged #342
diagnostics record, which measured nothing -- never as a stand-in for
0.0. `run_periodic_job` carries the four scalar edge fields into the
`.system` manifest `[run]` section through the existing
`update_run_fields` extension point (non-finite recorded as the explicit
string `"not-measured"`), mirroring the #344 backend/parity_held
surfacing; the `.out` rendering is unchanged.

**The gap at a fractionally occupied degenerate edge.** This is where the
pre-#426 wave records were wrong, quantified by the 2026-08-27 sec8-r4
judge (finding F1, 1,668 k-route rows;
`.agents/agentic-loop-state/runs/2026-08-27-judge-sec8-r4/`). Those
payloads derived "gap" as an *occupancy partition*,
`min(eps | n <= t) - max(eps | n > t)`: a fractionally occupied orbital
counts as occupied for the upper edge and is excluded as a lower-edge
candidate, so the value steps over the entire partially filled manifold.
1,022 of 1,668 rows had a fractional edge; 1,022/1,022 reported a
strictly positive gap and 0/1,022 had a true gap `> 1e-9`, with median
error 8.06e-5 Ha and maximum 1.98e-2 Ha (0.539 eV). Physically the gap
there is exactly 0 -- a fractional occupation means E_F is pinned inside
a partially filled manifold -- and this is not a borderline call: those
manifolds are degenerate to machine precision (spread `<= 8.7e-15` Ha;
1.9e-16 Ha on the diamond-Si 3x3x3 gate).

The shipped `indirect_gap` reports that correct value. It equals the
Gamma route's own pooled-aufbau convention
(`eps[n_fill] - eps[n_fill-1]`) to machine precision -- verified equal to
1.9e-16 Ha on the degenerate Si edge -- so k-route and Gamma-route
duality rungs now compare like with like; on integer-filled rows all
conventions agree exactly, so the correct convention has no regression
surface (the judge measured 646/646 such rows in agreement). Two
consequences are deliberate:

* `is_metallic` makes the gapless case **structurally** visible instead
  of leaving a screen to infer it from a small float. Under a
  zero-temperature global aufbau fill the pooled gap can never be
  negative, so a "negative gap" screen alone is vacuous on mesh rows --
  the judge's 0 negative gaps in 1,625 rows was a tautology, not
  evidence. A regression now pins that this route *can* produce a
  genuinely negative measured gap, so that screen is able to fail.
* the occupancy-partition quantity is still available, but only under
  its own name, `gap_above_fermi_manifold` ("distance to the next
  entirely empty state"), and never as `gap`.

### Fixed: CCM results carry structured backend identity + parity-hold state (issue #344, 2026-08-27)

Completes the #344 record-surface fix (the string-only carry landed as
9861933d7): the parity-hold state is now a structured field on the CCM
result surface, not a substring convention. `CCMGDFResult`, `CCMSCFResult`,
`CCMKSResult`, and `CCMUHFResult` all expose `parity_held` (derived from
the `+PARITY_HELD` marker on `backend`, the hold mechanism's canonical
carrier, so flag and string cannot drift), and every public CCM SCF
producer now stamps a truthful `backend` identity (e.g.
`ccm-fourcenter-direct-union12-rhf`, `ccm-neutral-ri-rhf`,
`ccm-neutral-direct-rks`) -- previously the non-GDF cluster routes carried
no identity at all, which is why the aic7 demotion had to be total. The
aiccm2026dev-b result exposes the same `parity_held` boolean beside its
verbatim `runtime_backend`. `run_periodic_job` now records the executed
backend and hold state in the `.system` manifest `[run]` section (via the
existing late-bound `update_run_fields` extension point) and a held run
states the hold in the `.out` next to the energy it qualifies (ordinary
runs emit nothing, so golden outputs are unchanged). The aiccm-2026 study
records (`run_case.py`) stamp `backend` + `parity_held` on every route,
correlated rungs inheriting the identity and hold of their SCF reference.

## [v0.15.145] - 2026-08-27 - *Neese's Cheetah*

This release carries three wrong-answer-class periodic semiempirical fixes
landed and (in part) independently verified within one day: pair-distance-
correct image selection for every periodic semiempirical lattice sum (#316 -
a Gamma-supercell wider than its cutoff previously became a silent
free-boundary cluster, +1678 uHa/cell on the fail-first case; the DFTB0/SCC
band-folding identity is now exact to ~1e-15 Ha/cell), GFN2 d-first
transition-metal parameter projection by angular momentum (#43), and the
fail-loud non-convergence contract for the periodic k-routes (#342 -
previously 17% of a production wave was silently unconverged under
status=ok). It also records the corrected dense-k SECCM convergence
reference with an R^-2-order gate (#312) and makes the molecular UHF/UKS
post-convergence stability phase a measured, reported quantity (#205).

Verification status, honestly: #316, #342, and #205 were landed by the
claude-code loop and their mandatory independent verifications by a distinct
actor were still pending at cut time (#312's and #206's evidence is recorded
on their issues awaiting broker re-lands). The Gaussian/ab-initio periodic
stack retains translation-length image selection - adopting pair-distance
selection there is staged as issue #429. Known-open wrong-answer defects not
fixed here: #421 (SECCM wrong-attractor family), #424 (cross-process
nondeterministic SCC branch selection), #425 (dim>=2 k-route cutoff tails).

### Fixed: GFN2 d-first transition-metal parameters were rotated across shells (issue #43; also #71, #101, #130 re-baselined; 2026-08-27)

Root cause of the GFN2 transition-metal parity family: the xtb
parameter file lists shells in occupation order, which is d-FIRST for
the transition-metal blocks (`ao=3d4s4p`: Z 21-29, 39-47, 57-79),
while every consumer of the derived per-angular-momentum arrays
indexes them by l. Positional indexing therefore rotated the STO
exponents and on-site levels (C++ core-array projection,
`regenerate_core_element`) and the `kcn`/`poly` fields (TOML
converter) across the shells of all 41 d-first elements - Cu's 4s ran
with the 3d exponent. A third deviation gave every d shell 4 STO-NG
primitives where xtb uses 3. All three sites are fixed: the core
arrays and the converter now project by angular momentum (caches
without the new `projection = "per-l"` marker are treated as stale and
refresh on first load), and the primitive rule follows xtb's
per-shell table.

Measured consequences (Cu2 vs xtb 6.7.0, T = 300 K): the total-energy
deviation drops from +35.8/+56.8/+139.5 mHa at d = 2.2/2.5/3.0 A to
+19.1/+31.5/+47.8 mHa - the remainder is the known missing
anisotropic-ES/D4 channels, flat rather than distance-growing, and
`e_repulsive` matches xtb exactly. The free Cu8/Cu16 clusters that
previously never converged (600+/3600 iterations) now converge in
46/49 iterations, a uniform ~+15 mHa/atom from xtb.

This supersedes three v0.15.144 claims that were measured on the
rotated parameters: (1) the fcc Cu charge-density-wave basin that the
physical-basin gate failed closed was an artifact of the rotation -
Cu 2x2x2 `ewald_gamma` now converges into the physical basin under
every mixer including plain simple mixing (E/atom -3.774155 at
T = 0.005); (2) the ">30-atom charge-solver wall has no physical
fixed point" verdict was a true property of the rotated-parameter map
only - the formerly hopeless Cu 2x2x4 converges in 4 Newton
iterations (E/atom -3.852071) and Cu 4x4x4 in 20 Eyert iterations
(E/atom -3.886142), all physical; (3) the metal-recipe pins moved
(2x2x2 newton/eyert now agree at -3.773689041 per atom at
T = 0.001). The Cu regression tests are re-pinned to the corrected
physics, a former-wall 2x2x4 convergence pin is added, and new
parameter-projection tests pin the per-l Cu values and the Cu2 parity
bounds so a regression to positional indexing fails loudly. Systems
whose elements carry no d shell are bit-identical; main-group species
with d-polarization shells shift by microhartrees from the
primitive-count fix (the TAE pins are re-updated), and the SECCM
MgO/diamond/corundum ladder pins hold unchanged within their
tolerances. Only the 41 d-first transition-metal blocks change
materially.

### Fixed: semiempirical lattice sums select images by pair distance, not translation length (issue #316, 2026-08-27)

`direct_lattice_cells` keeps a translation g only when |g| <= cutoff, but an
interaction cutoff bounds the PAIR distance |R_A - R_B - g|: as soon as a
Gamma supercell is wider than the cutoff, every image is discarded and the
calculation silently degrades to a free-boundary cluster (issue #316: MgO
conventional n>=2 at the 15-bohr default collapses from 27 cells to 1, with
Gamma-ladder errors up to +686 uHa/cell healing as a ~1/n surface term; the
gen-1 fix made this fail closed). Even below the collapse threshold, corner
pairs within the cutoff whose translation is outside it were silently
dropped (19.3-153.1 uHa on n=1 MgO Gamma cells), and the summed matrices
were not invariant under relabeling an atom by a lattice vector.

Every periodic semiempirical route - DFTB0/SCC-DFTB Gamma and k-point,
unrestricted variants, GFN2-xTB Gamma, PM6 Gamma, the NDDO FD batch, and all
analytic gradient/stress partners - now sums the pair-distance interaction
set {(A, B, g): |R_A - R_B - g| <= cutoff}, built by the new
`semiempirical/core/pair_lattice.hpp` (pad the enumeration radius by the
largest intra-cell pair offset, filter each term on the true pair
separation, prune cells with no in-range pair). This is the atom-centred
interaction-region construction of the cyclic cluster model (Bredow,
Geudtner & Jug, J. Comput. Chem. 22, 89 (2001); Peintinger & Bredow,
J. Comput. Chem. 35, 839 (2014)) and the per-atom analogue of the Gaussian
stack's `lattice_pair_cells.hpp` (Sharma & Beylkin, JCTC 17, 3916 (2021)).
Wide Gamma supercells now WORK instead of failing closed: the band-folding
identity Gamma-supercell(n) == matched n-point Monkhorst-Pack mesh is exact
at widths beyond the cutoff (fail-first on the H-Li chain n=4 at cutoff 15:
k-mesh -0.129153019533 Ha/cell vs the silent cluster -0.127475272210
Ha/cell = +1678 uHa/cell; now equal to < 1e-9), the summed matrices are
translation invariant (fail-first: relabeling one chain atom by +a moved
the energy by +4.47e-2 Ha at cutoff 8; now < 1e-10), and genuinely isolated
molecular-limit boxes keep the gen-1 fail-closed guard and the explicit
`gamma_only_0` mode unchanged. `semiempirical.atom_pair_interaction_cells`
is exposed to Python for direct inspection of the image list. The
Gaussian/ab-initio stack's image selection is deliberately unchanged (see
the issue-#316 caller audit for the follow-up). Regressions:
`tests/test_semiempirical_pair_image_selection.py`.

Repins and re-fixtures forced by the corrected semantics: the graphene
GFN2 finite-temperature pin pair moves by -0.028 uHa (added
attractive boundary image pairs; sweep step unchanged); the gen-1
wide-supercell fail-closed pin now asserts the folding identity; the
origin-only guard fixtures widen from 16 to 20 bohr (at 16 the H2 image
pair sits at 14.6 bohr, INSIDE the declared cutoff, so retaining it is
correct); the GFN2 cutoff-consumption probe moves onto an asymmetric
dimerized chain (an equidistant chain is inversion symmetric, so its
exact forces vanish at every cutoff - the old probe's signal was the
pre-fix selection's spurious symmetry breaking); and the SCC-DFTB
polar-box FD gates and the 2-D sheet Gamma anchor are re-pinned in
converged basins (12 and 60 bohr). The last two record a follow-up on
issue #316: the truncated 1/sqrt(R^2+eta^2) SCC gamma is basin-fragile
on polar cells under any ball truncation (the pre-fix anchors sat on
labeling-dependent values), and wide polar GFN2 supercells newly
reachable by this fix can need more SCC iterations than the damped
third-order mixing budget - the durable fix is an Ewald/compensated
long-range gamma, not a different ball.

### Fixed: periodic semiempirical k-routes raise on SCF non-convergence (issue #342, 2026-08-26)

The native k-point SCC-DFTB and GFN2-xTB routes (`run_scc_dftb_kpoints`,
`run_gfn2_xtb_kpoints`) returned a result whose `converged` flag was False
when the SCC loop exhausted its iteration budget, so any caller that
screened on "did not raise" accepted unconverged numbers as results — the
rp246 harvest admitted 6,877 of 40,486 such rows under `status=ok`. Both
routes now raise `SCFNonConvergenceError` (a `RuntimeError` subclass,
re-exported as `vibeqc.semiempirical.SCFNonConvergenceError`) naming the
exhausted iteration budget by default. Diagnostics consumers opt in
explicitly with `allow_unconverged=True` and still receive the honest
`converged=False` record; the `run_periodic_job` engine uses that opt-in,
so its established fatal-log + crashed-manifest failure evidence
(`ff56c4bd7`, retained in `d70f4335b`) is byte-identical. The DFTB0
k-route is non-self-consistent and continues to carry no convergence flag;
a regression pins that no silent non-convergence channel exists there.

### Fixed: dense-k SECCM convergence reference and the gate that guards it (issue #312, 2026-08-26)

The 1-D H-Li chain's "dense-k limit" was pinned at a 12-bohr lattice cutoff
that is not cutoff-converged, leaving the reference about 0.94 mHa away from
the value SECCM actually converges to. The old 1.2e-3 Ha tolerance was wide
enough to absorb that error, so the gate passed because of a mistake in its
own reference, and would have kept passing as SECCM drifted further off.

The reference is now the cutoff-free leading-1/R^2 Richardson limit
-0.107889099350429 Ha, extrapolated from 24-point values at 1280- and
2560-bohr cutoffs, and all four fixed-chain k-mesh fixtures are repinned at a
fixed 60-bohr cutoff. That repair landed in `f814c41e8` and shipped in
v0.15.140 through v0.15.144 with no changelog entry; this entry records it.

Independent verification then failed the gate as still too weak, and this
change completes it. The SECCM test now asserts the O(R^-2) convergence order
directly, with successive error ratios required to fall between 3.5 and 4.5
(measured 4.007, 3.985, 3.996). That order, not any absolute bound, is what
discriminates a correct reference from a displaced one: the pre-repair value
yields 2.49, 1.59, 1.17. The absolute backstop moves from 6.0e-5 to 8.0e-5 Ha,
restoring about 1.4x headroom over the measured 5.82e-5 Ha at 32 replicas
rather than 1.03x, while still rejecting the pre-repair reference by more than
12x. The k-mesh backstop moves from 2.0e-9 to 2.5e-9 Ha for the same reason,
the 60-bohr cutoff having raised the two zero-temperature residuals to about
1.7e-9 Ha.

The 60-bohr fixtures are no longer described as explicitly converged. The two
DFTB0 rows are cutoff-saturated, but SCC-DFTB still carries 35.4 and 9.4
microhartree of cutoff error there, which is harmless for a fixed-cutoff
k-mesh test and wrong to call a thermodynamic limit.

## [v0.15.144] - 2026-08-26 - *Neese's Cheetah*

This maintenance release advances the bundled vq from 0.25.5 to 0.25.6 and
unfences the fleet: the site_j scheduler-runtime deployment probe no longer
inherits Slurm step variables (#400), so the rollout verification that
fenced v0.15.143 on site_j now passes. It carries two wrong-answer fixes —
the periodic BIPOLE Gamma XC overlap corruption (#102, Madelung-scale
overbinding) and restored PM6 heavy-heavy NDDO multipoles (#244) — plus
canonical semiempirical parameter-snapshot identities (#283), the tblite
Eyert Broyden mixer for GFN2-SECCM, serialized independent verifier leases
in bugctl (#347), and a broad vq input-hardening sweep (quota caps, drains,
throttles, timeouts, pause clocks, capacity snapshots, retention windows).

Verification status, honestly: the #102 and #244 fixes are landed with
fixer-side evidence (MOPAC tensor oracle, He/Ar molecular-limit pins) but
their mandatory independent verifications were still in flight at cut time.
This release does not fix the known-open wrong-answer defects #316
(Gamma-supercell cluster collapse), #319 (2-D semiempirical lattice-sum
divergence), or #342 (k-route non-convergence reported as ok).

### Fixed: periodic BIPOLE Gamma XC no longer corrupts the overlap (issue #102, 2026-08-26)

At Gamma, the BIPOLE XC adapter overwrote the shared lattice overlap matrix
set in place with density blocks during XC evaluation. Iteration 1 was
correct; from iteration 2 the corrupted overlap produced Madelung-scale
overbinding (Ar/box50 RKS-LDA over-bound by -2.0604 Ha, He by -16.01 mHa)
in runs that still reported clean convergence. The adapter now returns a
fresh lattice matrix set, an immutability regression pins the overlap
across XC builds, and He/Ar molecular-limit values are pinned.

### Fixed: PM6 heavy-heavy NDDO multipole interactions restored (issue #244, 2026-08-26)

PM6 two-center electron repulsion between two heavy (sp-shell) atoms
previously collapsed to the monopole-only term, dropping the
dipole/quadrupole NDDO multipole contributions for heavy-heavy pairs. The
full sp-shell multipole parameter set (dipole and quadrupole separations
plus the Klopman-Ohno additive terms) is now computed per element and
applied in molecular, periodic, and SECCM PM6 routes. Validated against
the official MOPAC C-O on-axis/oblique tensor oracle; the HCOOH gradient
lands within 7.6e-6 Ha/bohr of the reference.

### Fixed: semiempirical parameter snapshots carry a canonical identity (issue #283, 2026-08-26)

Semiempirical parameter provenance previously could not distinguish
modified parameter sets. Canonical SHA-256 snapshot identities now cover
DFTB/SCC-DFTB, PM6/OMx, and GFN2 parameters across molecular, periodic,
k-point, SECCM, derivative, facade, and output provenance boundaries, so
runs record exactly which parameter set produced them.

### Fixed: vq wait rejects non-finite pause and wall payload numbers (issue #384, 2026-08-26)

Wait-loop payloads accepted NaN and infinite pause/wall-clock numbers and
could propagate them into scheduling arithmetic. Non-finite or overflowing
values are now rejected at payload parsing while finite numbers are
unchanged.

### Fixed: site_j runtime deployment verification probes serially (issue #400, 2026-08-26)

The scheduler-runtime deployment's post-build verification launches its
probe through a one-task `srun` step for compute-node access. The nested
serial wrapper probe inherited `SLURM_PROCID`/`SLURM_STEP_ID`/
`SLURM_STEP_NUM_TASKS` from that step, so vibe-qc's MPI launcher-rank
detection demanded `mpi4py`, the probe failed, and the receipt fenced the
rollout (`healthy=false`) even though the build was good. The serial child
environment now strips the Slurm step variables (preserving
`SLURM_JOB_ID`); vibe-qc's MPI detection itself is unchanged.

### Fixed: vq rejects unsupported pre-v1 job specs (issue #405, 2026-08-26)

Durable `JobSpec` records accepted zero and negative schema versions even
though v1 is the oldest supported format. Unsupported pre-v1 records now fail
validation just like future-version records; existing v1 migration and current
v2 behavior are unchanged.

### Fixed: IRC rejects malformed explicit transition modes (issue #406, 2026-08-26)

The public IRC driver accepted zero-norm and non-finite explicit transition
modes, normalized them into NaNs, and could return a non-finite trajectory.
Wrong-shaped modes also reached the energy/gradient provider before failing
with a low-level broadcasting error. Explicit modes now require the exact
transition-state coordinate shape, finite values, and a nonzero finite norm
before force-provider setup; valid explicit and automatic Hessian modes are
unchanged.

### Fixed: performance evidence rejects non-finite metrics (issue #403, 2026-08-26)

The matched performance evaluator accepted NaN measurements as positive and
could certify them as a reason-free, citable pass. Non-finite ratio ceilings
and comparison floors could also suppress known discrepancies. Supplied wall,
memory, active-CPU, allocation, and policy values now require finite documented
domains before any strict-performance verdict is constructed.

### Fixed: vq rejects malformed daemon capacity snapshots (issue #401, 2026-08-26)

Daemon capacity advertisements accepted zero, negative, boolean, string, and
floating-point CPU, job, and memory limits. A persisted negative CPU cap could
therefore mark every ordinary request impossible instead of degrading to
unknown capacity. All five advertised limits now require strict positive
integers at construction, assignment, write, file-read, and RPC boundaries.
Malformed files resolve to unknown capacity; malformed RPC mappings fall back
to the valid same-mode file or unknown, while positive integers, optional
``None`` gates, bounded reads, and mixed-version field filtering are unchanged.

### Fixed: invalid vq drain expiries preserve maintenance holds (issue #399, 2026-08-26)

Persisted drain state accepted zero, negative, boolean, string, and float
auto-release durations. A negative duration made the next state read delete a
global maintenance hold immediately. New durations now require strict positive
integers; an invalid legacy-file or RPC expiry is ignored as unbounded while
the otherwise-valid hold remains enforced. Valid positive expiries and
explicitly unbounded holds are unchanged.

### Fixed: molecular dynamics rejects invalid recording strides (issue #404, 2026-08-26)

The public molecular-dynamics driver accepted nonpositive and non-integer
`record_stride` values. Zero crashed with division by zero only after force
evaluation had begun, while negative values silently behaved like positive
cadences. Recording strides now require a positive, non-boolean Python or
NumPy integer before force-provider work; all valid cadences are unchanged.

### Fixed: scoped vq payloads verify kernel placement before execution (issue #136, 2026-08-26)

The direct resource collector previously treated a missing or mismatched
named job cgroup as unavailable process-count telemetry and still forked the
submitted command. A root-daemon payload could therefore inherit
`system.slice/vq-daemon-multi-user.service` and its 256 MiB limit instead of
running in the promised `vq-job-<id>.scope`. Scoped local dispatch now verifies
the collector's own cgroup-v2 membership before the payload starts; a mismatch
records `command_status=not_run`, writes exit code 125, and never executes the
command. The kernel cgroup remains authoritative: `VQ_MEM_MB` does not bypass
the inherited limit.

### Added: bugctl serializes independent verifier leases (issue #347, 2026-08-25)

The bug broker v0.3 source now gives verification its own durable claim,
request-deduplication, lease-generation, heartbeat, release, and verdict state,
bound to one exact landed fixer generation. Competing reviewers serialize;
self-verification is denied unconditionally; superseded, expired, or mismatched
leases fail closed; and repeated completed verdicts replay idempotently without
changing the result. New landing events require an exact 40-hex SHA.

The read-only `bugctl reconcile-plan` command projects one atomic,
digest-bound snapshot of the latest fixer generation and its matching verifier
generation onto the v1 lifecycle contract. It uniquely expands legacy
abbreviated landed SHAs inside a pre-fetched authoritative `origin/main`
ancestry and aborts the entire plan on partial API reads, missing or duplicate
state, unknown workflow labels, or missing, ambiguous, malformed, or off-main
commits. The command is dry-run only and reports `apply_supported=false`. This
milestone does not provision labels, mutate or close GitLab issues, deploy or
restart the broker, or perform bulk reconciliation; production apply remains a
separate maintainer gate.

### Fixed: BCCD rejects non-finite orbital-optimization controls (issue #397, 2026-08-26)

The public BCCD route accepted NaN and positive infinity for its Brueckner
singles-norm tolerance and orbital-rotation damping controls. An infinite
tolerance could certify a nonzero singles norm immediately, while non-finite
damping could poison the orbital update. Both controls now require finite,
strictly positive values before integral work; defaults and all positive finite
values remain unchanged.

### Diagnosed: genuine B1 MgO(100) control separates the SCC wall from post-SCC repulsion (issue #301, 2026-08-28)

The fixed-geometry discriminator now proves its neutral Tasker-I
crystallography rather than trusting a fixture label: every plane is an Mg/O
checkerboard and the two-plane 3-D extension is six-coordinate B1 rocksalt, not
issue #471's single-species polar-plane stressor. The L2 unembedded route
converges with a finite frontier gap, while the identical 2-D embedded route
fails closed even with DIIS and finite-temperature occupations. Both paths
preserve issue #306's missing-repulsive warning.

Mg-O and Mg-Mg repulsion is evaluated only after SCC, so it cannot cause this
fixed-geometry charge-map failure. It still invalidates absolute energies,
relaxed structures, surface energies, and EOS work, and the in-house electronic
set does not validate MgO gaps or charges. A source-and-equation audit against
Elstner and Janetzko found no sign, factor, or double-counting defect in the
finite 2-D construction; this does not
resolve the separate 3-D gamma thermodynamic-limit defect in issues #211, #425,
and #444. No equation, solver tuning, fallback route, acceptance gate, default,
or invented repulsive parameter changed.

### Fixed: periodic MACE preserves explicit optimization budgets (issue #396, 2026-08-26)

The periodic MACE position optimizer silently coerced booleans, strings, and
floating-point `max_steps` values with `int()`, so fractional requests could
execute a different optimization budget. Explicit step limits now require a
non-boolean, nonnegative integer before model or optimizer work; zero and
Python or NumPy integer budgets retain their existing behavior.

### Fixed: persisted throttles reject invalid CPU weights (issue #395, 2026-08-26)

Persisted throttle state accepted CPU weights outside systemd's inclusive
1..10000 range. The daemon would try and fail to apply that invalid cgroup
property, leave the new job at default priority, and still report the durable
throttle as active. Direct, stored-file, and daemon RPC state now share the
same range validation before any cgroup work.

### Fixed: invalid throttle durations no longer restore full CPU weight (issue #402, 2026-08-26)

Persisted throttles accepted zero, negative, boolean, string, and floating-point
durations. Invalid values could expire immediately and delete the throttle,
silently returning new jobs to the default CPU weight. New and RPC-written
durations now require strict positive integers. Legacy file and RPC records
with an otherwise-valid throttle preserve it as unbounded instead of dropping
the configured weight; valid timed expiry and explicit unbounded throttles are
unchanged.
### Fixed: the post-convergence stability phase is measured, not averaged away (issue #205, 2026-08-26)

Since the internal stability analysis became default-on, every converged UHF
and UKS job pays for a post-convergence Davidson solve that measured **0.8-3.0x
the wall of the whole SCF loop it certifies** (BH9 03_8TS UKS/PBE/def2-QZVPP,
1000 basis functions: 4025 s of SCF iterations followed by 11373 s of stability
analysis). Nothing recorded that phase: `perf.json` had no entry for it, the
`.out` had no row for it, and the runner divided the *entire* driver wall by
`n_iter`, so `SCF avg. per iteration` silently absorbed it. Any walltime sized
from that average under-estimated by 2-4x.

`UHFResult` and `UKSResult` now carry `stability_wall_s` and `stability_cpu_s`,
charged by the driver across every path after stability work starts (including
rotate-and-reconverge paths). Explicit opt-out and unsupported-response skips
remain exactly zero. The runner reports the phase as its own
`SCF stability analysis` row in the `.out` timing block and as its own
`scf.<method>.stability_analysis` phase in the perf log, and computes
`SCF avg. per iteration` from the SCF-loop wall alone. CPU is accumulated with
`std::clock()`, which sums OpenMP threads, so the perf log's parallelism column
is meaningful for the phase rather than a fabricated zero.

Routes that run no stability analysis (RHF, RKS, ROHF, ROKS, solvers, MLIP)
report `0.0`, emit no extra row or phase, and keep their previous output. A
latent `import math` inside `run_job` that shadowed the module-level import for
the whole function was removed in the same change.

Scope: this is the visibility half of issue #205. Making the phase cheaper
(closure criterion 3, "stability wall <= 1.0x SCF-loop wall") is separate
performance work, and the `[progress]` phase block (criterion 2) needs a
`vibeqc.progress` change that belongs to the IO chat per CLAUDE.md 16.

### Fixed: recovery audit rejects invalid TCP ports (issue #389, 2026-08-26)

Recovery SSH and Cockpit ports accepted values outside the TCP range and
coerced booleans, strings, and integer-valued floats into integers. Invalid
configuration could therefore reach SSH or socket probes and be misreported
as a host recovery outage. Both ports now require strict integers from 1
through 65535 during configuration validation, before any network work.

### Fixed: vq rejects invalid multi-user quota caps (issue #394, 2026-08-26)

Multi-user pending-job and CPU quota caps now require strict nonnegative
integers. Negative values can no longer freeze all dispatch for a default or
per-user scope, and booleans, strings, and floats are rejected instead of being
silently coerced. `None` remains unlimited or fallback, zero remains an
explicit block-all cap, and positive integer quotas are unchanged.

### Fixed: `vq top` tolerates malformed resource samples (issue #388, 2026-08-26)

`vq top` now validates each timestamp, CPU, and RSS field read from the latest
watchdog sample independently. Wrong-type, boolean, negative, and non-finite
values are shown as unavailable instead of crashing text rendering or leaking
non-standard `NaN`/`Infinity` tokens through `--json`; valid sibling fields and
elapsed-time information remain visible.

### Fixed: bugctl resolves clone state in linked worktrees (issue #380, 2026-08-25)

`bugctl` previously treated `.git` as a directory, so every linked worktree
failed local run-identity initialization with `NotADirectoryError`. Actor
configuration, run identity, and grant state now derive from Git's validated
per-worktree directory: ordinary clones keep their existing location while each
linked worktree uses its distinct administrative Git directory.
Unavailable or invalid Git metadata fails closed before command dispatch. The
concurrent first-use serialization from issue #377 remains unchanged.

Development after v0.15.143 belongs here.

### Fixed: vq auto-cleanup rejects destructive invalid retention windows (issue #387, 2026-08-26)

Auto-cleanup policies accepted zero, negative, boolean, fractional, and
string-coercible archive, delete, workdir, per-state, and sweep durations. A
negative delete window produced a future cutoff, making every terminal job
immediately eligible for destructive cleanup, while an invalid interval could
run the sweep on every daemon iteration. Every cleanup duration now requires a
strict positive integer at construction, assignment, and persisted-policy
load. Invalid on-disk policies fail closed as no policy before any cleanup
primitive runs; one-second windows, ordinary positive values, and optional
``None`` fields remain supported.

### Fixed: vq resume rejects invalid pause clocks before control (issue #391, 2026-08-26)

Durable pause and pause-intent records accepted negative, NaN, and infinite
monotonic-clock anchors. Invalid anchors could underbill a pause, send
``SIGCONT`` before failing pause accounting, or release a scheduler hold and
require rollback because NaN is not equal to itself. Both anchors now require
finite nonnegative values at construction, JSON read, and assignment, so a
malformed record fails before local or scheduler process control.

### Fixed: molecular SCF rejects NaN mixing controls (issue #393, 2026-08-26)

Molecular RHF, RKS, UHF, and UKS accepted NaN damping and Fock-mixing
fractions because the shared half-open-range check used only ordered
comparisons. A small one-electron calculation could even converge while
silently ignoring the invalid request; other paths failed later after NaN had
entered a Fock or density. The shared validator and the public low-level
molecular SCF entry points now require finite fractions in `[0, 1)`. Existing
zero and finite fractional controls are unchanged.

### Fixed: vq pause accounting cannot disable wall limits (issue #383, 2026-08-26)

Durable job records accepted negative, NaN, and infinite accumulated pause
durations. Non-finite values were also persisted as non-standard JSON and NaN
or positive infinity made the watchdog's active-wall calculation non-finite,
silently disabling an otherwise exceeded wall-time limit. Pause accounting now
requires a finite nonnegative duration at construction, JSON read, and later
assignment; valid zero and finite accumulated pauses are unchanged.

### Fixed: local vq admin timeout overrides reject infinity (issue #386, 2026-08-26)

The local update-script wall cap, no-output stall cap, build heartbeat cadence,
and daemon readiness window accepted positive-infinite environment overrides.
That could disable safety deadlines, suppress progress heartbeats, or leave
readiness polling unbounded. All four overrides now require a finite value;
invalid values fall back to their documented finite defaults, while zero still
disables only the stall and heartbeat timers.

### Fixed: vq preserves the runtime SHA that actually executes (issue #343, 2026-08-26)

Scheduler directory payloads that named a managed `--program` but launched
through `bash` could fall back to the driver checkout's observational pin. A
wave therefore recorded v0.15.136 with `enforce_git_sha = false` while its
target wrapper ran v0.15.138. Managed scheduler programs now resolve the
target's verified immutable runtime for every entrypoint shape and fail submit
if that identity is unavailable. At dispatch, vq also persists the full
resolved SHA, exports it as `VQ_PROGRAM_GIT_SHA`, and refuses a managed local
runtime whose SHA cannot be read, giving result writers a loud, exact
provenance source instead of an optional package-introspection probe.

### Added: tblite Eyert Broyden mixer for GFN2-SECCM (2026-08-26)

`scc_mixer="broyden_eyert"` is a faithful port of tblite's
`broyden.f90` (the mixer the xtb binary uses): inverse-norm history
weighting and the charge-difference u-vector term that the existing
normalised-history Broyden lacks. On fcc Cu 2x2x2 with `ewald_gamma` it
reaches the sane metallic fixed point at xtb's default temperature
scale (T = 0.001 Ha, 49 iterations with the full-budget history below)
where simple mixing lands in the charge-density-wave basin, and on
benign MgO it reproduces the simple-mixing fixed point bit-comparably.
It is SECCM-only; the molecular driver rejects it (like Newton). It
does not cure the elongated 2x2x4 Cu cell: xtb converges the same
16-atom geometry in 16 iterations while every one of our maps
(molecular and SECCM) fails - a map difference, not a mixer gap (see
the solver-wall and evidence-correction entries below; the xtb run is
a free-cluster reference, not periodic).

### Fixed: Eyert Broyden history depth and per-mixer mixing default (issue #130, 2026-08-26)

The independent mixer audit confirmed the `broyden_eyert` core
arithmetic is an element-for-element port of tblite `broyden.f90`
(compiled-harness trajectory parity 3.6e-16 across buffer rollovers)
but found two wiring deviations, both now fixed. The history was
hardcoded to a 10-vector sliding window while tblite sizes its Broyden
memory to the full iteration budget; the SECCM route now passes
`max_iter`, so the trajectory follows the xtb scheme beyond iteration
10 (fcc Cu 2x2x2 `ewald_gamma` T=0.001: 30 -> 49 iterations to the
same fixed point, E/atom -3.790409). And an unset `charge_mixing`
reached the mixer as the generic option default 0.1 because the
intended xtb-bromix fallback of 0.4 was dead code; `run_gfn2_seccm`
now resolves an unset value per mixer (0.4 for `broyden_eyert`, 0.1
for every other mixer), records it in the attempt provenance, and an
explicit value always wins. One structural difference remains and is
tracked as issue #409: tblite mixes shell charges plus atomic dipole
and quadrupole moments in one Broyden vector, while the SECCM route
mixes shell charges only with lagged AES moments.

### Study: the >30-atom GFN2-SECCM charge-solver wall is a property of the map, not the solver (issues #130/#101, 2026-08-26)

A Python reconstruction of the bare WS-folded SCC charge map (exact to
the native `f(0)` at machine precision) shows the elongated fcc Cu
2x2x4 cell and the 4x4x4 cell have no physical fixed point to converge
to: the neutral-point Jacobian carries a doubly degenerate
charge-density-wave instability (eigenvalue about -14 on 2x2x4; 63
eigenvalues below -1 with minimum -22 on 4x4x4) whose eigenvector is
the longest-wavelength mode the torus supports, and exhaustive hunts
(exact-FD-Jacobian line-searched Newton, hybr, Newton-Krylov
multi-start, and a grid scan of the symmetry-reduced uniform manifold)
find no root with |dq| < 1 while every root found sits in the
large-amplitude CDW basin (|dq_shell| 6.6-8.6 e) that the
physical-basin gate correctly rejects. Electronic temperature does not
tame it (J(0) deepens from -14 at T=0.005 to -23 at T=0.05),
cyclic-symmetrizing H0 does not remove it, and neither does widening
the canonical-orthogonalization screening, so no mixer or damping
schedule can cure these cells - consistent with every native mixer x
kernel x T combination failing while xtb converges the same 16-atom
geometry as a free cluster in 16 iterations (see the evidence
correction below). Probes: `studies/seccm-bulk3d/probe_wall_*.py`;
verdict and consequences in `handovers/HANDOVER_SECCM_BULK3D.md`.

### Corrected: the workstream's xtb references are free clusters, and molecular GFN2 carries an H0-channel parity defect (issues #43/#71/#101/#130, 2026-08-26)

Verified directly against xtb 6.7.0: the `$lattice:` comment line the
`studies/seccm-bulk3d/xtb_*_reference.py` runners write into their xyz
inputs is ignored by xtb (bit-identical total energy with and without
it), and a genuine Turbomole periodic input aborts with "scf:
Multipoles not available with PBC" - xtb 6.7.0 cannot run periodic
GFN2 at all. Every pinned "xtb reference" in the SECCM bulk-3D
workstream (the Cu 2x2x2 lattice curve, the 2x2x4 16-iteration
convergence, the corundum and MgO charge scales) is therefore a FREE
MOLECULAR CLUSTER reference, and earlier claims that xtb converges
these cells "through its periodic H0/S map" were wrong; the affected
entries above are corrected in place. The comparison is still
damning, now differently: xtb converges the free Cu8 cluster in 11
iterations and Cu16 in 16, while our molecular GFN2 fails both (600+
iterations, no fixed point found), and a minimal Cu2 dimer fixture
puts our total +35.8/+56.8/+139.5 mHa above xtb at d = 2.2/2.5/3.0 A
with e_repulsive matching xtb EXACTLY (+0.000024207 Ha both codes at
3.0 A) and SCC/AES/third-order all sub-mHa - the entire deviation
lives in the H0/band channel, the same family as the known #43
adenine residual and the #71 xfailed H0-radius water-dimer gates.
This is the foundation defect for the SECCM completion campaign
(SECCM inherits the molecular H0 channels); tracked under #43
(claimed, Cu2 fixture) with #71 and #101 as siblings.

### Fixed: χ four-center routes reject inert auxiliary bases (issue #385, D122, 2026-08-26)

The χ RHF, RKS, UHF, and UKS selectors accepted `aux_basis` for the complete
`four_center` BIPOLE backend and silently dropped it before dispatch. They now
raise before backend or SCF work whenever that fitted-only control is explicit.
An omitted auxiliary basis leaves every direct route unchanged, while RI and
RIJCOSX continue to forward the requested value exactly. The unified periodic
runner inherits the same fail-closed contract. Historical χ four-center
records that carry an explicit auxiliary-basis request did not execute it and
are provenance-invalid; no energy or Hamiltonian is retroactively changed.

### Fixed: χ-CCM-B Gamma-only RI smearing selector contract pinned (issue #206, 2026-08-26)

The Gamma-only RI RHF route with a nonzero ``smearing_temperature`` request
was investigated for a silent fall-through to the legacy cutoff-selected
Gamma GDF driver. The reproduction was retracted (D109 checkpoint):
``_validate_closed_shell_problem`` already rejects every nonzero B smearing
request before fitted SCF, and ``run_periodic_job`` rejects it earlier, so no
