positive request can reach the legacy backend while the result still carried
finite-torus metadata. This change pins the selector contract in tests:
positive, negative, and nonfinite temperatures all fail closed before fitted
dispatch for Gamma-only RI RHF, while the zero-temperature Gamma-only RI
selector still reaches the fitted backend unchanged.

## [v0.15.143] - 2026-08-26 - *Neese's Cheetah*

This maintenance release advances the bundled vq from 0.25.4 to 0.25.5. It
adds crash-safe, host-independent legacy rollout recovery; contains scheduler
and timing failures locally; and preserves complete log-follow snapshots. It
also restores moving-grid XC terms in multi-k KUKS gradients, makes periodic
DLPNO wrap-pair screening tests causal, and hardens CCM, DFTB, molecular
artefact, and vibe-view lifecycle boundaries. Existing accepted calculation
provenance remains immutable.

### Fixed: toroidal DLPNO screening regression tracks the wrap pair (issue #382, 2026-08-25)

The toroidal DLPNO-MP2 screening regression still correctly retained one
material wrap-around pair that open-cluster Euclidean geometry discarded, but
its historical aggregate-error threshold predated the mandatory periodic
Ewald-J/real-space-K HF route. The changed orbitals, Fock denominators, and
pair-energy decomposition introduced cancellation that moved the Euclidean
control just below that stale threshold. The regression now gates the direct
cause: Euclidean screening must remove exactly one additional pair whose full
correlation contribution remains material. The torus-aware calculation keeps
its original 5e-5 Ha unscreened-reference accuracy bound and must remain more
accurate than the Euclidean control.
### Fixed: vibe-view auto-reload follows the active archive (issue #371, 2026-08-25)

Auto-reload created its change tracker only when the control was enabled.
Switching files or opening an upload, builder result, path, or queue job then
replaced the active QVF reader without transferring watcher ownership. The old
task kept polling the previous archive while new-file changes were never seen;
an in-memory reader could also leave the control falsely enabled. Watcher
ownership is now synchronized with every reader replacement: a new local path
cancels and retargets exactly once, same-path hot reloads reuse the live task,
and pathless readers disable the control. Completed or failed polling tasks
release ownership, flush an honest stopped state to the browser, and can be
started again; scheduler refusal also closes the unscheduled coroutine instead
of claiming that auto-reload is active.

### Fixed: vibe-view isolates live-optimization runs and probes (issues #359, #373, 2026-08-25)

The first reader-switch guard for live optimization stored only the mutable
current reader. Starting a new run on an equal-sized incoming structure could
therefore re-authorize callbacks captured for the cancelled outgoing run;
late step events replaced the incoming geometry, while late completion,
error, and note events overwrote its status. Ineligible edits and history or
mode transitions also left prior callbacks authorized on the same reader.
Every scheduled run now owns immutable callbacks bound to its reader and run
generation, and every geometry/session boundary invalidates the preceding
generation before applying eligibility guards. Undo, redo, symmetrization,
supercell building, Edit-mode exit, explicit disable, and current worker
unavailability all cancel coherently. Availability probes are also
last-writer-wins: a stale reader or toggle generation cannot disable a newer
intent or overwrite its capability and status, while a current unavailable
result cancels the current run before turning auto-optimize off.

### Fixed: scheduler updates reject invalid drain waits (issue #379, 2026-08-25)

The programmatic scheduler-update boundary now rejects NaN, infinite, and
negative drain-wait deadlines before lifecycle locks, markers, drain lanes, or
remote work. The internal drain-lane helper enforces the same invariant. Zero
remains the documented one-shot mode, and positive finite waits are unchanged.

### Fixed: vq deployment timeouts reject non-finite configuration (issue #378, 2026-08-25)

Scheduler runtime deployment and host-update configuration accepted NaN and
positive-infinite command, preparation, verification, and provisioning
timeouts. Bad values could therefore reach delegated deadline arithmetic or
remote-process observation after administrative work had begun. Every
configured deployment timeout must now be finite and positive; the documented
optional ``None`` values remain supported.

### Fixed: failed vq operation no longer hides an inactive obsolete hold (issue #356, 2026-08-25)

Explicit legacy rollout recovery now carries an obsolete exact full hold into
host-local reconciliation even when a terminal failed operation on that host
keeps the global durable pass from releasing it. After an authoritative
inactive snapshot, vq first persists a report-bound, no-launch current-plan
acknowledgement and forward intent. It then settles each exact old hold with
closed action backlinks before the existing verified consumer marks only the
harvested failure fences handled with retry still unauthorized. Crash restart
reuses that durable intent, active or unavailable holds remain retained, and
an unreachable sibling cannot prevent the independent settlement. Final
writes bind a freshly fetched accepted report, a post-status non-fetching
local report epoch, and the complete journal version vector.
 ### Fixed: concurrent bugctl startup preserves one run identity (issue #377, 2026-08-25)

Concurrent first-use commands previously wrote through the same temporary
path and then renamed it, so contenders could crash with `FileNotFoundError`
or return a UUID different from the one persisted for the clone. Each command
now writes a unique, fully flushed candidate and atomically publishes exactly
one without replacement; every contender returns the canonical stored UUID.
Filesystems without hard-link support use the same complete-file guarantee
through a serialized atomic-rename fallback.

### Fixed: daemon run rejects non-finite poll intervals (issue #375, 2026-08-25)

``vq daemon run --poll-interval`` and the defensive ``Daemon`` constructor
accepted NaN and infinite values. The CLI could therefore begin privileged
startup work with an unusable interval, while direct construction could claim
the queue lock before the bad value failed or parked the loop. Both boundaries
now require a finite positive interval before config or filesystem work.

### Fixed: `vq wait` rejects non-finite timing options (issue #374, 2026-08-25)

``vq wait`` accepted positive infinity for ``--poll-interval`` and
``--timeout``. An infinite polling interval could park the client inside one
sleep and suppress terminal-state or timeout checks, while an infinite timeout
defeated the command's bounded-wait contract. Both options now reject
non-finite values before config, host, job, or wait-loop work; the existing
finite minimums, positive values, and omitted timeout remain unchanged.

### Fixed: vibe-view hot reload closes superseded QVF readers (issue #372, 2026-08-25)

Each panel-only watcher refresh replaced the active QVF reader but retained its
predecessor until a later full reload, leaking one open ZIP handle per update.
Superseded readers now close immediately after the fresh reader owns the
controllers, migrated overlays, active panel, and live status. The current
reader, materialized scene, export state, and edit history remain available.

### Fixed: daemon ping rejects unusable timeout values (issue #369, 2026-08-25)

``vq daemon ping --timeout`` accepted zero, negative, NaN, and infinite
deadlines. Those values could trigger lower-level socket errors, a busy retry,
or an unbounded liveness probe instead of the command's documented bounded
check. The CLI now rejects every non-finite or non-positive timeout before
config loading, local RPC work, remote delegation, or fleet fan-out.

### Fixed: scheduler runner failures stay host-local in vq (issue #365, 2026-08-25)

The per-host background scheduler observer could still leak a raw `OSError` or
`subprocess.SubprocessError` from its runner. Consuming that completed flight
then aborted the daemon iteration before healthy sibling observations or local
dispatch were processed. Live and detail runner failures now use the existing
bounded host-local error evidence: ambiguous jobs remain nonterminal and
capacity-reserving, while unrelated scheduler hosts continue in the same pass.

### Fixed: compact molecular artefacts settle before Molden export (issue #28, 2026-08-25)

The molecular runner previously wrote the potentially hundreds-of-megabytes
Molden wavefunction before population, citation, geometry, performance, and
QVF outputs. A carrier timeout during that bulk text export could therefore
discard every smaller result from an already-converged calculation. The runner
now closes and records those compact artefacts first, writes the atomic QVF
archive, and dispatches Molden last. Successful runs retain the same guaranteed
output plan and complete manifest; an interruption during Molden leaves the
converged compact results on disk and recorded for harvest. Numerical results
are unchanged.

### Fixed: BIPOLE CYC0 components retain their density identity (issue #358, 2026-08-25)

The RHF BIPOLE driver correctly evaluated legacy-gauge CYC0 components on its
local SAD density, but its mandatory terminal consistency rebuild then
replaced the sole one-iteration component row with the newly diagonalized
density. That made the end-to-end CYC0 oracle appear 1.21 Ha wrong even though
the standalone spheropole kernel and the driver's first evaluation agreed.
`PBCBipoleRHFResult.initial_density_energy_components` now preserves that
first physical evaluation, while `energy_components[-1]`, `scf_trace[-1]`,
the returned density, and the top-level energy remain aligned exactly as
before. No Hamiltonian, SCF state, convergence threshold, or terminal energy
changed.

### Fixed: multi-k KUKS gradients include moving XC quadrature (issue #158, 2026-08-25)

The multi-k KRKS/KUKS gradient assembly differentiated the XC integrand on
the SCF quadrature but omitted the derivative of the atom-centred quadrature
points and Becke partition weights. On a genuine open-shell LiH triplet/PBE
witness, the KUKS H-z force was wrong by 2.680e-3 Ha/bohr and the cell carried
a 7.143e-3 Ha/bohr net-force residual. The drivers now carry their exact SCF
grid provenance into the gradient and add the existing fixed-density XC
grid-motion correction to the fixed-grid AO response. The deterministic
open-shell regression matches full-SCF central finite differences to about
7e-9 Ha/bohr and restores translational invariance; the restricted sibling
uses the same correction so KUKS(M=1) still collapses onto KRKS. The
displaced-grid basis now round-trips the actual shell metadata instead of
reloading by name, preserving custom, imported, and optimized bases. The
real-Gamma CCM direct-torus route consequently enables open-shell pure and
global-hybrid KS gradients instead of failing closed.

### Fixed: vq log following honors unbounded initial tails (issue #366, 2026-08-25)

`vq logs --follow --tail 0` documented zero as full output but replaced it
with the default 20-line follow snapshot, silently omitting older log lines.
The follow path now carries the unbounded-tail sentinel through local and
scheduler-driver reads. Finite tails remain bounded, and scheduler polling
uses the displayed full snapshot as its incremental cursor so bytes appended
after that snapshot are emitted once.

### Fixed: `vq top --watch` rejects unsafe refresh intervals (issue #367, 2026-08-25)

The live resource view previously accepted zero, NaN, infinite, and
platform-overflowing refresh intervals. Zero could spin the terminal loop
without sleeping, while the other unsafe values reached the platform sleep
call and raised an uncaught exception. `vq top --watch` now rejects invalid
intervals before rendering and caps explicit refresh periods at one day; bare
`--watch` retains its two-second default and ordinary positive finite
intervals are unchanged.

### Fixed: megacell replicas follow lattice columns (issue #364, 2026-08-25)

The finite-supercell correlation helper translated replicas with rows of the
periodic lattice matrix even though `PeriodicSystem` defines lattice vectors
as columns. Axis-aligned diagonal cells were unaffected, but nonsymmetric cells
were assembled at the wrong Cartesian positions before molecular MP2 or DLPNO
correlation ran.
Megacell construction now follows the column convention on all three axes,
with an exact skew-cell regression covering the previously invisible case.

### Fixed: DFTB placeholder repulsives are loud and honestly documented (issue #306, 2026-08-25)

The built-in DFTB parameter sets carry tuned R^-12 repulsive entries only for
the {H, C, N, O, F, P, S, Cl} pairs; every other element pair silently fell
back to a combining-rule ``A/R^12`` estimate that is numerically irrelevant at
equilibrium separations, so absolute energies, EOS fits, and a0/B0/V0 for such
systems were silently non-chemistry. The molecular models and one-shot runners
(``DFTB0Model``, ``SCCDFTBModel`` and their unrestricted siblings,
``run_dftb0``, ``run_scc_dftb``), the periodic Gamma/k route, and
``run_scc_dftb_seccm`` now emit ``DFTB0RepulsivePlaceholderWarning`` naming
the uncovered pair(s) and the surviving fixed-geometry claim scope before any
number is produced; covered systems stay silent and duck-typed parameter
stand-ins are skipped. The three places that claimed spline-fitted production
repulsives (``load_production_parameters`` docstring, the ``dftb0_production``
binding docstring) now state that production currently returns the default set
pending a validated DFT reference dataset, and the garbled ``R⁻¹²`` rendering
is fixed to R^-12. The native fallback behavior is unchanged, so fixed-geometry
SECCM differences keep their exact-repulsive-cancellation contract.

### Fixed: CCM direct optimization validates its iteration budget (issue #368, 2026-08-25)

``run_ccm_direct_optimize`` now requires ``max_steps`` to be an integer of at
least one before it imports optimizer machinery or begins the initial
direct-vs-GDF parity calculation. Zero and negative budgets, booleans,
floating-point values, strings, NaN, and infinities fail deterministically
instead of starting expensive numerical work, silently truncating, or raising
an unrelated downstream exception. The default and positive integer behavior
is unchanged.

### Fixed: χ post-HF rejects invalid numerical-support cutoffs before SCF (issue #370, 2026-08-25)

Canonical and DLPNO χ MP2/CC entry points now require the lattice, RSGDF, and
fitted-metric cutoffs to be positive finite real numbers before starting their
RI-RHF or RI-UHF reference. Restricted guards previously let NaN and positive
infinity pass, and unrestricted gateways had no equivalent check. Booleans,
non-real values, nonfinite values, zero, and negatives now fail with the
offending field named; valid inputs and post-HF equations are unchanged.

### Fixed: CCM shell-guard regression names admissible producers after ruling R1 (issue #357, 2026-08-25)

The shell-aware route test still called ``run_ccm_scf(route="gamma")``, which
has failed closed since ruling R1 (issue #222) made the paper-facing Γ-CCM
spelling reject at resolve time. The regression now names the admissible
producers explicitly: ``route="four-center"`` keeps the historical 2014
union-and-weight triplet value (−0.7749672190 Ha), and ``route="real-gamma"``
(the neutral construction's direct producer) is pinned at −0.7827607825 Ha
with a dispatch assertion that the open-shell cluster reaches
``run_ccm_uhf_direct`` (identical energy to machine precision,
``CCMUHFResult`` result type) rather than the closed-shell driver. The
open-shell driver checks are retained.

### Fixed: CCM lindep_tol screens instead of refusing (issue #289, 2026-08-25)

``lindep_tol`` on the CCM SCF routes was a hard refusal gate: any threshold
above the overlap's smallest eigenvalue raised ``ValueError`` before the
orthogonaliser could act, and the scalable and DFT drivers had the option
commented out entirely, so sweeping the threshold produced a two-valued step
instead of a screening curve. Every CCM driver now forwards ``lindep_tol`` to
the canonical orthogonaliser (``linear_dep_threshold`` on the C++-driver
routes), which projects below-threshold overlap directions out of the Fock
subspace, and fails closed only when screening retains fewer directions than
occupied orbitals. The explicit ``CCMSystem.check_overlap_spectrum``
diagnostic is unchanged.

### Fixed: CCM neutral routes measure physical dimensionality; positive energies fail closed (issue #291, 2026-08-25)

The neutral fitted-torus routes (`run_ccm_rhf_direct` and its RKS/UHF/UKS
siblings, `run_ccm_rhf_ri_neutral`, and the multi-k GDF CCM wrappers) refused
only *declared* sub-3-D cells, so a 1-D chain padded with transverse vacuum
and declared 3-D passed the gate and produced a diverging neutral energy
ladder (positive at N1=1). `ccm_vacuum_directions` now measures the physical
periodicity from the atom positions: an axis whose largest empty inter-atom
slab exceeds 25 bohr and 4x the cell's shortest lattice vector is a vacuum
direction, and the neutral routes fail closed naming those directions -- the
externally validated 20-bohr-transverse H2 anchor cell stays measured 3-D.
Independently of the gate, any closed-shell neutral CCM SCF that converges to
a positive total energy now raises instead of reporting success (covers the
four-center, KS, direct, ri-neutral, and GDF entry points).

## [v0.15.142] - 2026-08-25 - *Neese's Cheetah*

This maintenance release hardens scientific and operational fail-closed
behavior across the current mainline. It isolates scheduler polling by host,
repairs host-independent legacy rollout recovery, preserves trustworthy queue
ETA evidence, validates fetched artifacts and update provenance, and carries
the latest periodic, semiempirical, CCM, molecular, QVF, and campaign-verdict
corrections. The accepted release report and live driver-first fleet rollout
remain separate post-tag gates.

The bundled vq advances from 0.25.3 to 0.25.4 for its user-visible fixes.
vibe-view advances from 2.15.1 to 2.15.2 for the periodic-supercell correction;
vibe-basis remains 0.10.0 because it has no changes in this release range.

### Fixed: wide Gamma supercells no longer silently lose periodicity (issue #316, 2026-08-25)

Public periodic DFTB0 and SCC-DFTB Gamma/k-point drivers, plus the GFN2-xTB and
PM6 Gamma drivers, previously accepted a real-space cutoff shorter than every
nonzero supercell translation. Their lattice list then contained only the home
cell, so the reported periodic energy was actually a free-boundary cluster
result. These routes now fail closed with an actionable cutoff diagnostic
whenever no nonzero image is present. The explicitly selected `gamma_only_0`
molecular-limit modes remain available and unchanged.

### Fixed: fractional ROKS canonicalisation preserves degenerate shells (issue #16, 2026-08-25)

ROKS already converged symmetry-degenerate frontier terms with uniform
fractional occupations, but the result layer then applied integer
Guest-Saunders closed/open/virtual boundaries. For OH(2Pi), that placed the
two 1.5-occupied pi partners in different blocks, split their reported
orbital energies by about 0.032 Ha, and left the energy vector out of order.
Detected fractional frontier shells now retain their converged Roothaan
eigenpairs, which preserve the molecular degeneracy and keep energies,
coefficients, and occupations positionally aligned in ascending energy order.
The result and completed ``.system`` manifest record
``rohf_canonicalization = "roothaan-fractional-shell"``; ordinary integer
ROHF/ROKS remains Guest-Saunders. The citation database also corrects the
Guest-Saunders article DOI.

### Fixed: CCM SCF exposes and validates its DIIS-commutator convergence bound (issues #295, #360, 2026-08-25)

The restricted CCM SCF loops (`scf.run_ccm_rhf`, `ri._rhf_loop` / `_rks_loop`)
and their RHF/RKS/UKS wrappers gated the DIIS-commutator residual on a
hard-coded `1e-6` that no argument could tighten, so `conv_tol` controlled only
the energy half of the exit condition. Issue #295 exposed `conv_tol_grad`
(default `1e-6`, the historical gate) on those routes and forwarded it to the
shared exit predicate; `conv_tol` is documented as gating the energy criterion
only. Defaults are unchanged.

Issue #360 extends the positive-finite input contract to the pre-existing
open-shell `run_ccm_uhf`, `run_ccm_uhf_direct`, and `run_ccm_uks_direct`
routes. The four CCM GDF wrappers also validate a supplied periodic options
object before basis or k-mesh setup; an invalid explicitly named pass-through
keyword fails at the wrapper boundary, while a valid direct keyword remains
unsupported by the downstream GDF API as before. Non-positive or non-finite
values now fail closed with a route-specific `ValueError` instead of silently
disabling convergence or merely exhausting `max_iter`. Focused tests pin every
public CCM SCF boundary, both shared loops, unchanged default/positive
numerics, the tightened stopping gate, and the source scan that refuses a
reintroduced literal.

### Fixed: CCM direct optimization validates its geometry-gradient tolerance (issue #361, 2026-08-25)

`run_ccm_direct_optimize` now rejects non-positive or non-finite
`conv_tol_grad` values before its initial parity calculation or any gradient
work. The historical `4.5e-4` default and valid positive values retain their
existing optimizer semantics; focused regressions pin all four invalid
floating-point classes and unchanged downstream boundary behavior.

### Fixed: campaign validation follows the current input-library layout (issue #346, 2026-08-25)

Static campaign validation previously required the retired
`vibeqc/molecular` directory and therefore rejected the authoritative flattened
input library before any live gate could run. It now discovers
`vibeqc/<compound>/<variant>/input.py` and fails closed when the `vibeqc` root
or every variant input is absent; the retired shape is no longer required or
accepted.

### Added: bugctl publishes the verification-workflow plan (issue #347, 2026-08-25)

The read-only `bugctl workflow-plan` command now reports the canonical intake,
triaged, in-progress, blocked, needs-verification, under-verification, and
verified label contract plus the deterministic provisioning actions required
by the live GitLab project. This milestone does not apply labels or mutate
issues; broker-mediated lifecycle projection remains a later guarded step.

### Fixed: χ QVF no longer emits surrogate DOS and bonding properties (issue #362, 2026-08-25)

The generic periodic QVF property block admitted `aiccm2026dev-b` while
rebuilding a fixed-cutoff Ewald/HF-like lattice operator from the converged
density. That operator neither reused the executed finite-character J/K
assembly nor included XC for KS jobs, so its DOS, projected DOS, COOP, COHP,
and Mayer payloads could describe a different Hamiltonian under a χ label.
χ now skips that generic rebuild, and an explicit COOP/COHP request fails
before SCF until a route-owned implementation exists. Native χ population,
Mayer, band/property, torus-grid, convention, and Wannier paths remain
unchanged; the scientific operator and converged result are untouched.

### Fixed: vibe-view supercells scale the periodic lattice (issue #359, 2026-08-25)

The Build supercell action duplicated periodic atoms while retaining the
archive's original unit cell. A 2x1x1 NaCl build therefore placed atoms out to
fractional x = 1.5 inside an unscaled cell. The immediate rebuilt scene also
lost its unit-cell wireframe, while subsequent structure reads, CIF export, and
generated vibe-qc input retained the archive cell. Edited structures now carry
atoms and lattice as one overlay and one undo/redo transaction. Each real
periodic lattice row scales by its integer replication factor; synthesized
non-periodic rows in lower-dimensional structures remain unscaled. The current
structure read, unit-cell wireframe, CIF export, generated periodic input,
subsequent atom-only edits, and undo/redo now use the same expanded cell.
Committing a physical supercell resets display-only replication to one cell so
later scene rebuilds cannot tile the expanded structure a second time.
Molecular replication remains non-periodic. Follow-up verification found that
the viewer's global undo/redo stacks could outlive the active reader: after a
NaCl supercell build, switching to H2 and pressing Undo produced foreign Na/Cl
atoms and lattice inside the molecular file. Different-file switches and full
archive replacements now clear and dirty both stacks plus atom-indexed
selection and interaction targets. Panel-only hot reloads instead migrate the
unchanged viewer-side atoms and lattice to the fresh reader, preserving one
coherent scene, export, and undo history. Reader replacement also cancels live
optimization and rejects late callbacks, so an outgoing calculation cannot
rewrite a same-sized incoming structure.

### Fixed: site_i scheduler fallback launches the verified runtime (issue #75, 2026-08-25)

site_i's runtime verifier validated the immutable release Python but recorded the
enclosing release directory as `active_path`. When the scheduler-driver
registry was unavailable, vq used that deployment receipt as the runtime pin
and placed the directory at `argv[0]`, causing scheduler jobs to fail with exit
126. The verifier now records the exact validated immutable Python executable,
so receipt fallback produces an executable submit command without changing the
normal program-registry path.

### Fixed: vq rejects unloadable serial CRYSTAL programs (issue #237, 2026-08-25)

`vq programs` previously reported every executable-bit CRYSTAL wrapper as
healthy even when its target died in the dynamic loader before `main()`. The
serial `crystal`, `crystal23`, and `crystal23demo` frontends now receive a
bounded no-input startup probe with closed stdin in an isolated temporary
directory. Missing shared libraries, wrapper exit 126/127, launch failure,
timeout, nonzero/signal exit, and output without CRYSTAL v1.0.1's exact
zero-exit no-input diagnostic report the program unavailable. Relative registry
paths are resolved before the directory switch. The recognized diagnostic
proves startup without running chemistry; parallel launchers remain unexecuted
outside their scheduler/MPI context.
### Fixed: one failed scheduler poll no longer stalls other vq hosts (issue #284, 2026-08-25)

The daemon previously ran every scheduler host's live and detail polls serially
on its dispatch thread. A slow or unpollable handle could therefore delay local
dispatch and unrelated scheduler hosts for the full remote timeout. Production
polling now keeps at most one bounded, read-only observation in flight per host
and applies completed observations on the daemon thread, preserving single-owner
queue mutation without coupling host cadence. A Slurm batch that explicitly
reports an invalid job ID isolates the missing candidates with exact follow-up
probes: live siblings continue normally, while only an affirmatively rejected
handle enters the existing exit-marker and final-fetch terminal fence. Ambiguous
transport and protocol failures remain nonterminal and capacity-reserving, and
the one-time warning names both the vq job and scheduler handle.

### Fixed: scheduler-runtime deploys record their exact release tag (issue #288, 2026-08-25)

Scheduler-runtime deployment previously recorded `tag = null` when the caller
provided an immutable expected SHA without repeating its tag, even when that SHA
was the unique target of the accepted release tag. vq now resolves the unique
tag at the pinned scheduler-runtime source repository and propagates it through
deployment and verification, so runtime manifests and `vq admin status` report
the exact tag/SHA provenance. Ambiguous or absent tags remain null with an
explicit warning; no version-derived tag is fabricated.

### Fixed: paper performance verdicts enforce dispatch intent (issue #256, 2026-08-25)

Campaign timing and memory metrics could previously produce a `pass` or
`performance-bug` even when their jobs were dispatched only for smoke or
accuracy/artifact work. The performance evaluator now requires both immutable
schema-v2 member dispatch contracts, validates the dependency, inventory, and
release identities, derives the actual same-host/resource envelope, and allows
citable ratios only for strict-performance pairs. The verdict recorder anchors
those contracts to the durable queue and payload hashes, checks the resources
actually submitted, and records both contract hashes plus a pair digest.
Legacy rows remain non-citable after an additive header migration, and the
dashboard withholds ratios that lack verified provenance.

### Fixed: vq legacy-hold recovery commits each safe host independently (issue #356, 2026-08-25)

Explicit fleet legacy reconciliation previously sent old pairless full holds
through the fleet-global durable pass unless they already had a retention
receipt or a superseded action. An offline earlier host could therefore abort
the pass before an authenticated inactive host persisted its journal-only
settlement, leaving later host-scoped rollout planning fenced. Obsolete
closed-shape full holds are now inventoried without host controls, authenticated
against their exact historical accepted reports, and reconciled through
per-host atomic journal writes. An unavailable host remains visibly retained;
an already-inactive host settles without a drain release, survives a later
host failure, and is not reprocessed after restart. Current-report identity is
rechecked after each live observation and before its write. Runner launch and
timeout failures are isolated to their host, and a sibling action proof cannot
authorize release of an independently active full hold.

### Fixed: incomplete multi-k GFN2 fails closed (issue #351, 2026-08-25)

The experimental GFN2 k-point driver discarded imaginary Bloch phases,
contracted its bare-band energy with the Gamma Hamiltonian instead of the
matching per-k state, and omitted AES while returning converged numeric
results. General k-point meshes and GFN2 band paths now raise an explicit
unsupported-model error. A one-point Gamma mesh remains compatible by
delegating directly to the supported Gamma driver and copying the fields
shared by the k-point result without recomputation. Examples and guidance no
longer present the disabled wrong-answer route as supported.

### Fixed: vq queue ETA confidence counts distinct retained history (issue #293, 2026-08-25)

`vq status` presented one or two generic command-shape samples as a confident
point ETA, and summing several jobs ahead could count the same retained rows
again for every job until they appeared to meet the confidence threshold.
Generic `command+cpus`, `command`, `cpus`, and all-history estimates now require
three distinct retained job records: weak-only waits render as unknown, while a
mixed strong/weak sum carries an explicit low-confidence qualifier. Stable
retained-job identities preserve that evidence cardinality across aggregation,
so reuse cannot manufacture confidence while three independent rows still
restore the normal numeric ETA. Wait seconds, jobs-ahead ordering, placement,
and the public JSON status shape are unchanged.

### Fixed: periodic SCC-DFTB non-convergence retains failure evidence (issue #342, 2026-08-25)

The public k-point SCC-DFTB route (`run_periodic_job(method="scc_dftb",
kpoints=...)`) had already failed closed since `ff56c4bd7`: it wrote a fatal
diagnostic, recorded the log, marked the `.system` manifest `crashed`, and
then raised. The initial issue #342 change added a redundant earlier raise
that skipped the diagnostic log. The route again uses its established
downstream check so the iteration count and fatal reason survive alongside
the exception and crashed manifest. The internal native driver intentionally
keeps returning its result object with `converged=False`; the DFTB0,
converging SCC, derivative, optimizer, and scientific-operator contracts are
unchanged. The `rp246` rows recorded as `status=ok` therefore require a
separate audit of the caller/status assembler and prior ledgers rather than a
second public-runner guard.

### Fixed: 3-D CCM Madelung sums are lattice-basis invariant (issue #345, 2026-08-25)

The shared MSINDO CCM3D Madelung kernel enumerated direct and reciprocal
lattice vectors through a fixed coefficient cube. An equivalent
determinant-one shear could therefore hide short physical vectors behind
near-cancelling coefficients outside the cube, changing a converged LiH
energy by 1.2301 mHa and propagating the same defect into analytic gradients
and GFN2-SECCM's opt-in Madelung embedding.

Native and Python energy and derivative paths now share physical `exp(-30)`
Ewald cutoffs with dual-basis coefficient bounds and pair-displacement-aware
direct ranges. The cubic LiH result is preserved to roundoff, while a
coefficient-13 shear now reproduces its energy and analytic gradient. Public
MSINDO, forced-reference Python, fixed-WS finite-difference, and GFN2-SECCM
regressions pin the corrected invariant. Pathological unreduced bases that
would require an unsafe candidate allocation fail closed with a reduced-basis
diagnostic. One- and two-dimensional kernels are unchanged.

### Fixed: vq overview distinguishes unconfirmed scheduler reservations (issue #353, 2026-08-25)

Scheduler-backed overview cards treated every driver-owned `RUNNING` record
outside the queued, held, and unpolled phases as confirmed execution. Poll
failures, result-fetch fences, reattachment failures, finishing jobs, and
unknown future phases therefore inflated `queue_counts.running` and
`running_cpus`. Only an exact last scheduler phase of `running` now counts as
confirmed compute. Every other phase remains capacity-reserved in the
compatible pending load, while new `unconfirmed_scheduler_jobs` and
`unconfirmed_scheduler_cpus` fields identify the uncertain subset in text and
JSON. Such a reservation also suppresses an idle claim until scheduler
telemetry becomes conclusive.

### Fixed: vq fetch refuses success without required freshness metadata (issue #294, 2026-08-25)

Whole-tree fetch writers already stamped `_vq/fetch-manifest.json`, but CLI
consumers treated a missing manifest as `fetched_at=null, stale=false` and could
still report success. A schema-only, non-UTF-8, mismatched, or stale manifest
could also produce a clean-looking result. `vq fetch`, `vq fetch-all`, and
`vq submit --fetch-on-done` now validate the sidecar before reporting a fetched
workspace or workdir: it must prove the requested job and tree kind, carry
aware fetch timestamps and provenance, and be explicitly fresh. Single-artifact
`--name` fetches remain the documented sidecar-free exception. Regression
coverage also pins the manifest written after a live daemonless-scheduler
workspace refresh.

### Fixed: unrestricted χ-CCM QVF archives preserve BvK spin multiplicity (issue #355, 2026-08-25)

The visual BvK system used for χ QVF output repeated atoms, lattice, and
charge but hard-coded singlet multiplicity. Unrestricted archives could
therefore report UHF, an odd electron count, and alpha/beta Wannier centres
beside contradictory singlet provenance. The archive now repeats the primitive
spin difference exactly, giving multiplicity `N_c * (M - 1) + 1`, and its
`job.spec` explicitly records the primitive requested charge and multiplicity.
Restricted singlets remain singlets. This is a metadata correction only and
changes no SCF result, density, Hamiltonian, Coulomb kernel, or exchange-q=0
convention.

### Fixed: UHF stability escape no longer misses or abandons the Cr2 descent (issue #138, 2026-08-25)

Molecular UHF could still return an internally unstable Cr2 singlet under
default options. At 2.5 bohr the stability Davidson solve started from one
lowest-diagonal coordinate and remained inside its exact symmetry sector: it
reported a near-zero higher root while the true global Hessian eigenvalue was
-0.3438949. At 3.0 bohr it found the correct -0.2963451 mode and a determinant
0.114 Ha downhill, but the chained SCF restart required every finite history
to lower the energy. Near the new stationary point the residual continued to
shrink while the energy approached its limit by a few nHa from below, so that
monotonic gate abandoned the basin and returned the original saddle.

The matrix-free stability solver now starts from four deterministic,
symmetry-dressed low-diagonal directions, retains several low Ritz vectors on
thick restart, and recovers the previously skipped global Cr2 mode without
materialising the Hessian. The UHF driver enforces a residual one decimal
tighter than the requested instability threshold. The escape searches and
reconverges both signs of the unstable mode as required by Seeger-Pople, falls
back to an unanchored drive when the fixed 15-cycle MOM occupation hold
over-constrains a collective mode, and chains fresh SCF histories while they
remain below the original saddle rather than demanding monotonic
finite-history energies. The existing 60-matvec and three-escape defaults are
unchanged.

With true `UHFOptions()` defaults, Cr2/STO-3G now reaches an internally stable
solution at -2064.1176230283 Ha at 2.5 bohr (one escape, lambda_min =
+0.0326333) and -2064.4247089164 Ha at 3.0 bohr (three escapes, lambda_min
approximately zero from above), instead of the 24.8 mHa-too-high false-stable
basin and the -2063.9308527525 Ha symmetric saddle. Regressions pin the global
2.5-bohr Hessian root in `tests/test_uhf_stability.py` separately from both
end-to-end stable outcomes in `tests/test_guess.py`; the UHF stability, guess,
and core UHF inventories cover the unaffected stable/open-shell controls.

### Fixed: molecular KS entry points share the selected integration grid (issue #251, 2026-08-25)

ASE `VibeQC` and `MolecularSCFProvider` previously built bare RKS/UKS options,
which selected the legacy Product Gauss-Legendre/Becke grid while `run_job` and
the direct KS wrappers selected DefGrid3. For the pinned water PBE-D3(BJ)
regression, that changed the SCF energy by 1.03e-6 Ha even though the D3 term
and convergence behavior agreed. Internally-created KS options now inherit
`grid_level` (DefGrid3 by default), and ASE response properties plus native
optimizer gradients inherit the same grid as their SCF energy. Caller-provided
options and explicit gradient-grid overrides remain authoritative. High-level
`run_job` features that materialize options, such as density fitting or an
explicit initial guess, also retain the selected grid.

### Fixed: `$VQ_WORKDIR` guidance matches scheduler scratch configuration (issue #290, 2026-08-25)

The agent guidance incorrectly promised that `$VQ_WORKDIR` was always a
scratch directory distinct from the submitted payload. Local daemon jobs do
have that managed workdir, but scheduler jobs use the shared staged workspace:
without `node_scratch_dir` it is also the payload cwd, while configured node
scratch gives the command a distinct temporary cwd and copies results back on
normal exit. `CLAUDE.md` and the operator guide now state that discriminator,
the matching fetch and cleanup lifecycles, and the host-independent safety
rule: create a dedicated output subdirectory, prove it is writable, and never
overwrite a submitted file. Runtime behavior is unchanged.

### Fixed: vq self-update refuses Git index locks before daemon stop (issue #236, 2026-08-25)

A managed vq driver update previously stopped the serving daemon before its
first checkout mutation. If the staging checkout already carried an
`index.lock`, that checkout failed and rollback hit the same lock, leaving no
serving daemon. Self-update admission now resolves the active Git index for
ordinary clones and linked worktrees, rejects inherited Git repository
selectors, and refuses any present lock before writing the recovery receipt or
stopping the service. It names and preserves the lock rather than guessing
whether a Git writer is still live. Vq's observational status probes and
managed update script also disable Git's optional index refresh locks;
required checkout locks remain in force.
### Fixed: fully 3-D CCM GDF pair-star reconstruction fails closed (IID 337, 2026-08-25)

The default CCM GDF symmetry path previously reconstructed 53 of 64 LiH/STO-3G
`(2,2,2)` k-pair fits from 11 star representatives and moved the energy by
`1.88e-5 Ha/cell` relative to the exact unreduced route. The group identity is
valid for the infinite lattice sum, but the production 15-bohr Bloch cell list
is not closed under every atom-shifting cubic operation; its worst independently
built versus reconstructed tensor differs at the percent level and converges
away only as the cell list is widened.

Fully 3-D replica meshes now emit an all-build pair plan, and the production
RSGDF driver bypasses the custom star adapter so it retains the generic shared-q
batching rather than issuing one build per pair. The default and explicit
unreduced LiH `(2,2,2)` routes now both report 64/64 builds and agree within the
`1e-10 Ha/cell` regression gate. Proven lower-dimensional reductions remain
enabled, including the `(3,1,1)` 8/9 production-cache and `(2,2,1)` fold gates.

### Fixed: vq reports only applicable admin-update blockers (issue #292, 2026-08-25)

`vq status` previously attached every live admin-update marker to every pending
job, even when the marker protected a different scheduler host. A site_j runtime
rebuild could therefore appear in a site_i job's `pending_blockers` despite the
daemon dispatching that job normally. Status reporting now filters markers with
the same fail-closed scope parser used by daemon admission: matching scheduler
and local-runtime holds remain visible, while recognised foreign-host markers
are omitted. Unreadable or unrecognised marker shapes still report a global
hold, stale ordinary markers remain ignored pending auto-reap, and stale durable
recovery receipts retain their scoped blocker. Scheduler overviews now carry all
marker leases from the driver and project only a matching or fail-closed global
lease, so a foreign first lease cannot hide or mislabel another host's hold.

### Fixed: boundary GFN2 H0 uses boundary coordination records (partial issue #296, 2026-08-25)

Periodic Gamma and multi-k GFN2 previously rebuilt Bannwarth-Ehlert-Grimme
Eq. 18 coordination numbers from the atoms typed in the home cell for every
H0 image block. The result omitted periodic neighbors and changed the H0
self-energy when the same site was expressed through a different lattice
representative.

The Gamma and k-point builders now assemble one pair-complete, physical
15-bohr coordination array and reuse it for every H0 block. Molecular GFN2
keeps its established home-cell path. Regression tests pin periodic
coordination under lattice-site relabelling and atom permutation. Failed Gamma
and k-point result objects now retain NaN energy fields instead of a plausible
zero.

This is a bounded source fix, not closure of #296. Origin-only one-electron
image support is now rejected under #316; the cyclic analogue remains #354;
default GFN2-SECCM AES moment integrals remain representative-dependent under
#348; periodic GFN2 derivatives remain #338; and the incomplete multi-k complex
Bloch/AES functional now fails closed under #351. Periodic GFN2 therefore
remains excluded from quantitative method claims.

### Fixed: vq queue distinguishes scheduler reservations from confirmed execution (issue #304, 2026-08-25)

Scheduler-backed jobs deliberately retain the durable vq `running` lifecycle
from scheduler handoff until terminal proof, but queue state, explicit filters,
JSON, and collapsed-array summaries also treated `poll_failed`, `finishing`,
and other unconfirmed phases as compute-running. `vq status --json` had the
same projection gap. A failed poll after the requested walltime could therefore
remain silently counted as confirmed execution even though handoff time cannot
prove either node start or completion.

Queue and status now share a bounded monitor-facing scheduler phase. Text rows
and collapsed arrays expose that phase, mixed arrays no longer borrow their
first element's cluster label, and the queue footer reports last-confirmed
running jobs against all scheduler-owned lifecycle-running jobs. Raw
`-s running` remains conservative and keeps every reservation so automation
cannot infer idle capacity during telemetry loss; exact phase filters such as
`-s poll_failed` and raw-nonterminal `--active` work consistently for local,
delegated scheduler, and `--all` paths. Queue and fleet-web JSON add
`effective_state`, status adopts the same bounded projection, and all three add
tri-state `scheduler_running_confirmed`. Unknown or unsafe phase strings
project to `scheduler_unknown` in text and filtering while remaining available
in raw JSON for diagnosis.

Poll loss never terminalizes a scheduler job from elapsed handoff walltime.
Operators can use the existing single-job `vq fetch HOST JOBID` path for a
best-effort live workspace snapshot; it neither proves completion nor stamps a
terminal fetch time.

### Fixed: degenerate Gamma frontier gets equal fractional occupations (issue #339, 2026-08-25)

The Gamma-point DFTB0 and SCC-DFTB drivers built their density from
`C.leftCols(n_occ)` (hard Aufbau), so when the integer electron count cuts a
roundoff-degenerate frontier manifold the diagonalizer's arbitrary eigenvector
choice made the analytic gradient and stress non-unique: ideal cubic Si's
HOMO-LUMO gap is ~5e-15 Ha, its forces came out ~2e-3 Ha/bohr, and its stress
violated cubic and lattice-translation invariance. The two drivers now apply a
degenerate-frontier occupation convention: an open-gap spectrum keeps the exact
hard-Aufbau vector bit-for-bit, while a cut degenerate manifold receives equal
fractional occupations across the whole manifold (the Weinert-Davenport T→0
ensemble), preserving the electron count. The occupations ride on the result
and flow through density, electronic energy, energy-weighted density, gradient,
and stress; legacy results without the field fail back to hard Aufbau in the
derivative routes. The three strict cubic-symmetry and translation-invariance
xfails are now active gates, and a direct threefold-manifold fractional-
occupation regression pins the convention.

## [v0.15.141] - 2026-08-25 - *Neese's Cheetah*

**Verification status, stated honestly.** This release adds four bounded
post-v0.15.140 corrections: periodic semiempirical analytic derivatives now
consume the exact SCF lattice cutoff, CCM GDF parity holds reach result records
while an inert `aux_basis` beside a prebuilt `cderi` fails closed, χ-CCM
population sidecars reach the finite-torus writer, and vibe-view panel
separators are keyboard-operable. It also records the validated Newton mixer
recipe for the current GFN2-SECCM metallic test envelope.

**What this release does not establish.** A recorded `+PARITY_HELD` backend is
a machine-readable exclusion, not scientific acceptance. The χ-CCM sidecar
change affects output routing, not energies or Hamiltonians. The unresolved
wrong-answer and containment limits listed for v0.15.140 remain in force,
including issues #306, #313, #316, #318, #319, and #342. Periodic GFN2 remains
characterisation-only, and no held campaign value becomes promotable merely
because this release exposes its status correctly.

### Fixed: χ-CCM multi-cell population sidecars reach the finite-torus writer (issue #350, 2026-08-25)

The periodic sidecar preflight treated every non-BIPOLE multi-k population as
a molecular Gamma-only analysis and rejected χ-CCM before SCF, even though the
χ route already has a dedicated full-character density and overlap
implementation. Explicit requests and the capability-aware default now plan
the χ-specific text and JSON population sidecars on supported multi-cell
character meshes. This is an output-routing correction; χ energies,
Hamiltonians, and exchange-q=0 conventions are unchanged.

### Fixed: vibe-view panel separators are keyboard-operable (issue #341, 2026-08-25)

The two side-panel resize edges and the result-details splitter now expose
exactly three focusable ARIA separators with stable names, orientations,
controlled-panel references, and rendered pixel ranges. Arrow keys resize in
the matching spatial direction, Shift applies a larger step, Home and End move
to the bounds, and Enter collapses or restores the previous size. Mouse drag
behavior remains available, side widths still commit to Trame state, and
conditional panel remounts do not duplicate handles. A `ResizeObserver` keeps
announced values synchronized after native bottom-panel resizing or layout
clamping. Source-contract and trusted-Chromium regressions cover semantics,
keyboard and pointer operation, state persistence, remounting, and browser
errors.

### Fixed: periodic semiempirical analytic derivatives consume the SCF lattice cutoff (issue #340, 2026-08-25)

The analytic periodic DFTB0, UDFTB0, SCC-DFTB, USCC-DFTB, and GFN2 gradient
and stress routes reconstructed their lattice cells with a hardcoded 15.0 bohr
cutoff while the energy drivers accept arbitrary cutoffs, so a nondefault-cutoff
run silently differentiated a different truncated lattice sum. Every periodic
result now persists the effective cutoff (and DFTB0's `gamma_only_0` mode), all
eight derivative routes consume that provenance, and legacy or
default-initialized results without it fail closed with an actionable error.
Nondefault-cutoff gapped finite-difference parity gates now pin DFTB0,
UDFTB0, SCC-DFTB, and USCC-DFTB gradients and the DFTB0 stress at the same
tolerances as the default-cutoff gates, plus the fail-closed provenance
contract.

### Fixed: GFN2-SECCM metallic supercells reach the sane basin via the Newton mixer (2026-08-25)

The tblite-faithful `ewald_gamma` kernel was re-verified against the fetched
tblite source (`tblite/coulomb/charge/effective.f90`, `get_amat_3d`): the
same-atom block carries the d=0 Ewald lattice self potential, so the shipped
kernel is faithful and the fcc Cu charge-density-wave basin is a property of
the map, not a kernel defect. On fcc Cu 2x2x2 the neutral simple-mixing start
lands in that basin at every tested electronic temperature; `scc_mixer="newton"`
with `electronic_temperature <= 0.002` Ha reaches the sane metallic fixed point
in a few iterations, and that fixed point persists as the temperature is
lowered. A regression pins the sane-basin energy and charge bounds next to the
paired fail-closed test. The Cu lattice scan now converges at every scanned
lattice constant with a minimum near 4.0 A; the residual offset vs xtb is
carried by the WS-folded band0 channel (small-cell artifact, 4x4x4 ladder in
flight on site_i). See `handovers/HANDOVER_SECCM_BULK3D.md` for the open
maintainer decisions.
## [v0.15.140] - 2026-08-25 - *Neese's Cheetah*

**Verification status, stated honestly.** This release is dominated by defect
closure rather than new capability: a global zero-T k-point occupation fix
(metals previously got a fixed per-k filling), an analytic GAPW one-centre XC
gradient replacing a radial finite difference that zeroed both angular
components, a repaired dense-k convergence reference, and a run of SECCM and
vibe-view boundary fixes.

**Several of these are containments, not root-cause fixes, and are labelled as
such above.** The SECCM 3-D even-replica branch now fails closed; whether that
divergence is downstream of the `direct_lattice_cells` image collapse (#316) is
unresolved. The dense k-mesh capacity bound was rescaled against a mechanism that
a later 29-mesh sweep falsified, and is pending re-validation (#318).

**What this release does not establish.** The blocking gate is tiers T0+T1, which
is 4 of 739 test files, and the lane manifest marks `scientific_acceptance` false
for every lane. Known-open wrong-answer defects that this release does NOT fix:
#316 (a Gamma supercell wider than its cutoff silently becomes a free-boundary
cluster), #319 (the 2-D repulsive and electronic lattice sums), #342 (the
periodic k-route never raises on non-convergence), #306 (the DFTB0 repulsive is
an A/R^12 placeholder, so absolute a0/B0/cohesive energies are not claimable).
PM6/PM7 (#255), OM1/OM2/OM3 (#163) and periodic GFN2 (#296) remain excluded from
method claims.

### Fixed: GFN2-SECCM and periodic-GAPW boundary and provenance defects (2026-08-25)

Five landed changes that had no `[Unreleased]` entry, reconciled here against the
tree rather than against their commit messages (four carried none).

**GAPW one-centre XC gradient was a radial finite difference.** The atomic-grid
gradient feeding `sigma = |grad rho|^2` in the GAPW XC augmentation came from
`_atomic_density_gradient`, which returns `drho/dr * rhat` with **both angular
components identically zero** — its own docstring assumes a spherically symmetric
density. One-centre densities are not spherically symmetric in general, and an
aspherical core is precisely the case GAPW augmentation exists to represent, so
every GGA and meta-GGA augmentation term inherited an angularly-truncated gradient.
Now analytic. This is a CP2K-parity item and it moves GGA/meta-GGA periodic GAPW
numbers.

**SECCM 3-D even-replica branch fails closed.** The even-R branch diverges with
increasing R (R=2 −0.23376, R=4 −0.33144, R=6 −0.38258) while the odd branch
converges toward the dense-k value (R=3 −0.11460, R=5 −0.11929, dense-k −0.11893).
Only R=2 was gated, and R=2 sits on the diverging branch, so a single-point check
plus a symmetry property were both satisfied by a divergent sequence. Even-R 3-D
SCC requests are now rejected rather than returning a plausible number. Tracked as
issue #313; whether the divergence is itself downstream of the
`direct_lattice_cells` image collapse (#316) is **not yet settled**, so this is a
containment, not a root-cause fix.

**GFN2-SECCM restart boundary is validated** rather than accepted silently, and the
**GFN2 Hamiltonian provenance is now recorded** on the result, so a restarted SCC
can be told from a cold one at read time.

**GFN2 stale-cache diagnostics are preserved** instead of being discarded, so a
parameter cache that is present-but-stale is distinguishable from one that is
absent — the two had the same signature at the call site.

### Fixed: vibe-view local server isolates filesystem and QVF text (issue #334, 2026-08-25)

Directory listings, QVF detail pages, and the cold-start page now encode
filesystem names, paths, and manifest metadata for their exact HTML, URL, or
inline-script context. A crafted local name or valid QVF can no longer add
markup or script to the server origin. Download filenames use an RFC 5987
header value, and error responses keep filesystem and operating-system text
out of the HTTP status line, closing adjacent response-header injection paths.
Adversarial regressions cover both listing modes, detail metadata, loading-page
script termination, special-character URL round trips, and CR/LF-capable
header inputs.

### Fixed: CCM parity holds reach result records; inert aux_basis fails closed (issue #344, 2026-08-25)

`CCMGDFResult` now carries the inner multi-k driver's backend string verbatim
(``.backend``), so the ``+PARITY_HELD`` suffix that marks the dense-core
parity-hold class is visible on the result instead of only in the `.err`
sidecar. The aiccm-2026 campaign records stamp ``backend`` per row (routes
whose result type carries no backend record ``""``), so held numbers can be
separated from converged ones without re-running anything. The direct-route
drivers (``run_ccm_rhf_direct`` et al. and ``run_ccm_rhf_ri_neutral``) now
fail closed with a ``ValueError`` when ``aux_basis`` is passed together with
a prebuilt ``cderi`` -- the cderi already fixes the fitting basis, so the
argument was previously accepted and silently ignored.
### Fixed: dual-engine optimizer records the computed BIPOLE convergence verdict (issue #257, 2026-08-25)

`scripts/dual_engine_optimize.py` computed the BIPOLE SCF verdict inside
`run_bipole` and then discarded it: `SystemResult.bipole_converged` was never
assigned, so every serialized record read `false`, including for runs that
actually converged. `run_bipole` now returns a `BipoleOutcome` carrying the
energy, the SCF verdict, and the iteration count, all three are serialized,
and `delta_mha` is withheld with a note when BIPOLE did not converge, so a
non-converged cycle energy can no longer be mistaken for an engine
comparison. Tests pin the converged, non-converged, and failed-run record
shapes.

### Fixed: local DLPNO-(T0) native TNO truncation initializes its pair inventory (issue #298, 2026-08-25)

The explicit local-(T0) triples path with a positive `tcut_tno` read its
ordered occupied-pair inventory before assignment when the native TNO-density
binding was available. This raised `UnboundLocalError` before a truncated
triples correction could be evaluated, including through the 3-D χ-CCM
DLPNO-CCSD(T) route when `triples_mode="local"` was requested. The pair
inventory is now constructed once and shared by native TNO-density formation
and amplitude projection. A deterministic three-occupied regression proves
that all seven distinct triple domains reach the native density kernel and
that its energy and retained-domain statistics match the NumPy oracle. The
default `(T1)` route and the no-truncation `tcut_tno=0` path are unchanged.

### Fixed: Gamma periodic DFTB analytic derivatives match their energy (issue #310, 2026-08-25)

Gamma-point DFTB0 and SCC-DFTB analytic stress used the negative transpose of
the atomic strain derivative and omitted Wolfsberg-Helmholtz overlap terms for
same-atom periodic images. SCC stress also counted repulsion twice, omitted the
overlap cell-vector derivative, and differentiated a molecular gamma term
instead of the image-summed SCC energy. The restricted and unrestricted
gradients now use every periodic overlap block; SCC derivatives use the same
periodic gamma model as the SCF; and the stress routines assemble atomic,
image-overlap, repulsive, and gamma strain terms exactly once. Periodic SCC
derivatives also reject nonconverged results whose charge response is not
stationary.

Gapped distorted-Si, polar H-F, and open-shell H2+ regressions compare every
Cartesian gradient component and all nine restricted stress components with
central finite differences. The ideal diamond-Si cubic checks remain strict
xfails because hard Gamma Aufbau occupation cuts a threefold-degenerate
frontier; that separate occupation defect is tracked as #339. Periodic GFN2
derivative incompleteness and nondefault lattice-cutoff provenance are tracked
separately as #338 and #340.

### Fixed: CCM guide distinguishes high-level and direct Madelung defaults (issue #336, 2026-08-25)

The cyclic-cluster guide grouped `CCMOptions` and direct `run_ccm` keyword
defaults together and stated that `madelung=True` applied to both. Only the
high-level `run_job` route through `CCMOptions` defaults the embedding on;
`run_ccm`, both direct gradient helpers, and `ccm_optimize` retain their
compatibility default of `False`. The guide and defaults table now distinguish
those API families explicitly so a direct ionic calculation cannot be assumed
to include long-range electrostatics unless the caller opted in.

### Fixed: OM2/OM3-SECCM fail closed without long-range electrostatics (issue #235, 2026-08-25)

The multi-replica OMx-SECCM adapter assembled a Wigner-Seitz weighted OM2/OM3
Fock and reported `electrostatics_kernel="none"`, but still returned energies
for ionic finite groups. A cubic H/F oracle moved by 0.521079 Ha per cell from
the 2x2x2 to the 3x3x3 cluster despite convergence. Janetzko, Bredow, and Jug
(2002) require the ionic Madelung correction in both the self-consistent Fock
and total energy, while Peintinger and Bredow (2014) state that long-range
interactions are mandatory for ionic-crystal CCM.

Every valid OM2/OM3-SECCM topology that is not exactly molecular now rejects
by default at both the public Python adapter and the native C++ boundary. This
includes any group with more than one replica and any order-one topology with
a wrapped or fractionally owned image record. Because partial ionicity is an
SCF output, the guard does not attempt an input-species heuristic. The exact
one-replica, zero-image, full-weight molecular limit remains unchanged.
`allow_truncated_electrostatics=True` is retained only as an explicit
algorithm-mechanics acknowledgement for image-weighting and finite-group
development; it does not make the result a quantitative solid-state
prediction. The resolved acknowledgement is immutable on the native result,
the public result, and its route plan, while the actual electrostatics kernel
continues to report `none`.

### Fixed: zero-temperature multi-k semiempirical occupations use one Fermi level (issue #317, 2026-08-25)

Closed-shell DFTB0 and SCC-DFTB previously occupied the same fixed number of
bands independently at every k-point when electronic temperature was zero.
That is only valid for a globally gapped band manifold. A 3x3x3 diamond-Si
mesh with a small indirect band overlap therefore returned an electronic
energy 8.422 microhartree per cell above its exactly folded 3x3x3 Gamma
supercell. Zero-temperature full-k calculations now fill the globally lowest
states under one weighted electron-count constraint and share fractional
occupation across a roundoff-degenerate Fermi group. DFTB0 band energies and
SCC densities both consume those occupations, and the native multi-k GFN2
exact-zero route inherits the corrected shared kernel. Single-spectrum Gamma,
molecular, and SECCM filling remains unchanged. The DFTB0 band-path helper
continues to occupy each plotted spectrum independently because arbitrary path
points are not Brillouin-zone quadrature weights.

This also corrects a material experimental k-GFN2 zero-temperature result:
the 4x4x1 graphene regression moves from the wrong per-k branch at
-3.368572578632 Ha to the globally filled -3.723221838143 Ha. The default
0.001 Ha finite-temperature GFN2 branch is unchanged. Explicit custom k-point
weights must now sum to one within a mesh-size-scaled roundoff tolerance, so a
small normalization error cannot create spurious fractional hard occupations.

### Fixed: vibe-view dialogs return focus to their launcher (issue #332, 2026-08-25)

All thirteen state-driven dialogs now capture a focus origin when focus enters
the modal and restore that exact connected control after its leave transition.
Origins are keyed per dialog, so a command palette stacked over Settings or
presentation mode returns focus within that still-active surface; transient
menu items resolve to their stable activator. Removed, hidden, disabled, inert,
accessibility-hidden, and closing-overlay origins fail safely without falling
back to an unrelated control. Source and generated-template inventories pin the
complete dialog surface, while trusted Chromium exercises toolbar, menu,
keyboard, nested-modal, presentation-overlay, and invalid-origin paths with a
clean browser console.

### Fixed: vq managed recovery survives systemd runtime drift (issue #309, 2026-08-25)

Managed vq updates persisted the complete `systemctl show` `ExecStart` record
and compared it literally after stop, before restart, and during recovery. The
record mixes the service definition with volatile timestamps, PID, and exit
state, so an ordinary stop or restart could make a valid version-1 receipt look
foreign. vq now binds the path, systemd's joined-argv representation, and
`ignore_errors` field at all three gates while ignoring only those runtime
fields. Malformed, multiline, multiple-command, and non-daemon records fail
closed before mutation; path, joined-argv, and `ignore_errors` changes that are
visible in those fields still reject, launchd remains exact, and existing
well-formed version-1 receipts remain recoverable.

`vq overview` now distinguishes ordinary stale markers that auto-reap from
durable managed or pause-scope receipts that continue to hold dispatch. It
renders the host-qualified recovery action, keeps unreadable or malformed
remote marker data visible with conservative advice, and projects a driver's
marker onto a scheduler card only when that marker can gate the scheduler lane.

### Fixed: dense semiempirical k-mesh capacity accounting (issue #318, 2026-08-25)

The shared closed-shell semiempirical occupation kernel compared an electron
count with a capacity accumulated over every k-point using a fixed absolute
tolerance. A fully occupied argon cell therefore passed at a 22x22x22 mesh but
failed spuriously at 24x24x24. Weight validation and capacity now use compensated
accumulation, and the final bound is derived from IEEE unit roundoff and the exact
accumulation length. Dense filled meshes execute at zero and finite electronic
temperature while a genuinely overfilled minimal basis still fails closed.

### Fixed: GFN2 band paths are diagonalized from a converged reference state (issue #333, 2026-08-25)

The native multi-k GFN2 band-path helper previously assigned uniform weights to
the requested path points and delegated to the self-consistent mesh runner, so
the SCC density, aggregate energy, and even the returned band energies depended
on how the visualization path was sampled. `run_gfn2_xtb_bandpath` now converges
the SCC on an explicit physical reference k-mesh and then diagonalizes the
Hamiltonian at the path points from that converged state. The energy, charge,
and finite-temperature fields are the reference state's own; only the band
spectrum is the path's. The helper fails closed when no reference mesh is
supplied or when the reference SCC does not converge. A path-resampling
regression pins the invariant band spectrum on graphene.

### Fixed: vibe-view clip sliders update the rendered scene (issue #331, 2026-08-25)

Clip-plane sliders now send their axis and event value together, so the
authoritative Python state cannot lag behind the browser's `v-model` before a
scene rebuild. Removed clip and volume actors remain alive until their
replacement graph has been allocated, preventing VTK native-address reuse from
making Trame apply an actor update to a cached property object and abort the
render delta. Two-dimensional slice positions remain visible beside the
controls without turning every keyboard tick into a global live-region
announcement. Controller, actual-PyVista, generated-template, actor-lifetime,
and trusted-Chromium regressions cover the state, scene, and browser console.

### Fixed: vibe-view element-colour input has an accessible name (issue #328, 2026-08-25)

The visible native colour picker in the structure display controls now exposes
the stable name `Element colour override` while retaining its compact layout,
current value, and keyboard focus behavior. The name and matching hover title
are explicitly preserved through Trame's generated template. Source inventory
distinguishes this focusable control from the intentionally hidden file input,
and trusted Chromium coverage verifies the final visible `input[type=color]`
without filtering unnamed controls out of the probe.

### Fixed: vibe-view playback controls have accessible names (issue #326, 2026-08-25)

The trajectory and molecular-orbital previous, play/pause, and next buttons now
forward six distinct workflow-specific accessible names without changing their
icon-only layout. Each play button reacts to live animation state, announcing
Start before playback, Pause while running, and Start again after stopping.
Source and generated-template inventories pin the complete six-control mapping,
and trusted Chromium coverage mounts both conditional panels and exercises the
two state transitions with physical clicks.

### Fixed: vibe-view periodic inputs preserve charge and multiplicity (issue #327, 2026-08-25)

Periodic Python exports and pending QVF containers now pass the parameter
panel's exact charge and multiplicity into `PeriodicSystem`. Controller and
command-line exports, the non-container `vq` fallback, and container
`job.spec` therefore agree instead of silently substituting neutral-singlet
defaults. For the 2D C2 conformance slab, a requested charge of -1 and
multiplicity 2 remains the intended 13-electron per-cell doublet rather than
becoming a 12-electron singlet. Restricted-parser and Python-to-QVF round trips
retain the same state, while neutral periodic defaults and molecular input
generation remain unchanged.

### Fixed: vibe-view periodic inputs preserve the cell and dimensionality (issue #325, 2026-08-25)

The viewer's Python export, command-line export, and non-container `vq`
submission fallback now derive molecular versus periodic construction from the
active QVF structure. Representable 1D, 2D, and 3D structures carry their
validated 3x3 lattice and actual dimensionality into `PeriodicSystem`; a 2D
slab no longer becomes a molecule under the default panel template or an empty
`PeriodicSystem(3, ...)`. Pending containers and generated scripts now share
the same structure translation, and reopening a generated 2D script preserves
its per-axis PBC. Periodic generation without a lattice and QVF PBC masks that
would require axis reordering fail closed. Molecular generation and the legacy
3D default for direct lattice-only generator callers remain compatible.

### Fixed: vibe-view sessions restore periodic replication (issue #324, 2026-08-25)

Loading a version-1 session now validates its saved `Nx`/`Ny`/`Nz` replication
and restores it through the same periodic-axis clamping and scene-rebuild path
as the interactive controls. UI state, render state, and supercell geometry stay
synchronized, the saved camera is applied after the rebuild, and legacy or
malformed replication fields remain non-fatal.

### Fixed: vibe-view sliders have stable accessible names (issue #323, 2026-08-25)

All eleven Vuetify slider controls now forward a unique workflow-specific
`aria-label` to their focusable slider thumb. Screen readers can distinguish
volume isovalue and opacity, clip-plane X/Y/Z positions, cross-fade blend,
trajectory frame, molecular-orbital opacity, ELF isovalue, vibration amplitude,
and spectrum broadening instead of announcing anonymous slider controls.

### Fixed: vibe-view saved volume views restore the rendered scene (issue #322, 2026-08-25)

Applying a user bookmark or loading a version-1 session now restores volume
isovalue, colormap, and opacity in the per-section render hints before the
section is activated. The rebuilt mesh, cache key, live actor, and visible
controls therefore agree instead of showing saved values beside a stale
isosurface. Saved cameras are applied after section activation so scene
rebuilds cannot replace the requested pose. Invalid colormap names and
non-finite or out-of-range saved numeric values are ignored instead of
poisoning the live renderer. Bookmark, session, and presentation replay share
the same ordering helper to keep these paths in parity.

### Fixed: vibe-view presentation mode is visible and controllable (issue #321, 2026-08-25)

Presentation mode now mounts its fullscreen overlay, hides ordinary app
chrome, and keeps the live content underneath it interactive. Three-dimensional
slides use the full VTK viewport; bands, spectra, SCF histories, citations, and
other panel-rendered sections use a full-height presentation panel instead of
disappearing. Every overlay control has a descriptive accessible name.

Slides now preserve each bookmark's section, camera, isovalue, colormap, and
opacity. Stored-volume settings update the renderer hints before activation, so
the mesh agrees with the visible controls. Previous/next buttons and trusted
Left/Right keys navigate cyclically, Escape exits presentation without entering
edit mode, hidden edit shortcuts cannot mutate geometry, and the play control
performs cancellable timed advancement. The shortcut help now matches the
implemented Ctrl/Cmd undo, redo, and command
palette bindings and no longer advertises the nonexistent `f` action.

### Fixed: vibe-view modal dialogs have accessible names (issue #314, 2026-08-25)

Every served modal now forwards a stable descriptive `aria-label` to its
Vuetify `role="dialog"` root. This covers the command palette, molecule and
supercell builders, file picker, vq submission, screenshot/video/raytrace
exports, keyboard help, about, settings, recent exports, and element picker.
Screen readers therefore announce the active modal context instead of an
unnamed generic dialog. A module-wide source contract fails if any current or
future `VDialog` omits either its name or the explicit Trame ARIA mapping. A
trusted Chromium regression also mounts the served viewer and verifies all
thirteen names on the final Vuetify dialog roots.

### Fixed: SECCM adapters preserve zero-record molecular limits (issue #329, 2026-08-25)

A valid one-atom, one-replica SECCM topology has no directed pair records.
The shared public adapter flattened its empty image labels and displacements
to rank-one arrays, while the native boundary requires three-column matrices;
DFTB0's older duplicated flattener had the same defect. Both paths now preserve
exact `(0, 3)` matrices, so one-center calculations reach their intended
molecular delegation or method-specific acceptance gate. Nonempty record order,
weights, and values are unchanged.

### Fixed: molecular GFN2 rejects unimplemented Newton mixing (issue #330, 2026-08-25)

The shared SCC mixer enum exposes Newton for the nontrivial GFN2-SECCM engine.
Passing that value through raw molecular `XTBSccOptions` previously executed
the guarded hybrid or Simple path while attempt metadata still named Newton.
The molecular entry point now rejects the request before basis construction
or SCC work. `GFN2Model` and the supported Simple, DIIS, and Broyden paths are
unchanged.

### Fixed: GFN2-SECCM restart validation and SCC attempt provenance (issues #230-#234, 2026-08-25)

GFN2-SECCM now rejects a nonempty restart that is not one-dimensional or
finite before topology processing. Once parameter availability establishes
the shell count, the native boundary also requires exactly one value per
shell before topology linear algebra or the numerical solve. Exact molecular-
delegation routes reject restarts because the molecular GFN2 driver has no
shell-restart field, rather than silently ignoring them. On nontrivial routes
the supplied restart applies only to the primary SCC attempt; bounded recovery
attempts start from neutral shell charges with the Simple mixer.

Results now retain immutable requested run controls and an ordered per-attempt
ledger. Attempt residual traces concatenate to `scc_max_change_trace`, attempt
iteration counts sum to cumulative `n_iter`, and `selected_attempt_index`
identifies the accepted attempt. Delegated molecular attempts and exhausted
bounded ladders follow the same accounting; `GFN2SECCMConvergenceError`
retains the frozen failed result for inspection. These changes tighten the
execution and provenance contracts of the experimental adapter; they do not
change the GFN2 Hamiltonian.

### Added (EXPERIMENTAL): `optimize=True` wired for `jk_method='real-gamma'` (2026-08-23)

Runner-level geometry relaxation on the real-Γ direct-torus surface, the
last piece of the adsorption-goal chain (energies → forces → relaxation →
runner). `run_periodic_job(..., jk_method="real-gamma", optimize=True)`
relaxes through `run_ccm_direct_optimize`, so the direct-vs-control
energy-parity premise is verified at the initial AND final geometries and
both residuals are written into the `.out` — the route's
"same-Hamiltonian optimizer" claim is checked per run rather than
asserted. Measured on compact H₂ (2,1,1): 1.6000 → 1.4736 bohr,
E = −1.195551311, endpoint parities 1.3e-13, identical to the API driver.
The SCF geometry stays in `{stem}.xyz` and the relaxed one is the separate
`{stem}.opt.xyz` artefact, per the runner's existing convention.

Fixed-lattice only: `optimize_cell=True` fails closed (the route has no
analytic stress), as do `hessian`, DFT+U, dim<3 and non-SCF methods.
IID 199's pin on the *text* of the old optimize refusal is retired with
the refusal it pinned. Gates: `tests/test_periodic_ccm_real_gamma_adapter.py`.


### Fixed: periodic GFN2-xTB fail-closes on the over-polarized shell-transfer basin (IID 300, 2026-08-24)

`run_gfn2_xtb_gamma` used the home-cell (molecular) shell gamma, which carries
no periodic image screening, and had no physical-basin gate. On skew
transition-metal cells (fcc Cu 2x2x2) the SCC map therefore ran into the
spurious over-polarized intra-atomic shell-transfer fixed point and returned
it as a converged -2.39e6 Ha energy (shell-fluctuation rms ~ 170 e, a
third-order term of -2.55e6 Ha); the cubic 1x1x1 Cu cell returned the same
basin at -5.14 Ha/atom against the gated SECCM physical state of -3.90
Ha/atom. The driver now applies the same calibrated physical-basin gate as
the SECCM adapter (shell populations inside [0, 2*n_funcs], bounded
shell/atomic fluctuation rms and maxima): a converged-but-unphysical state
falls through to the bounded stabilization restart and fails closed when the
physical branch cannot be reached. The molecular H2 parity test and the
full GFN2/periodic lanes are unchanged.

### Fixed: site_i dev runtimes include and verify native MPI support (2026-08-24)

The managed site_i `vibeqc-dev` profile now installs the existing `dispersion`
and `mpi` extras together, and the offline preparer carries `mpi4py` in the
wheelhouse. Login-host preparation, pre-activation health, the independent
verifier, and `vq programs` load `mpi4py.MPI` with auto-initialization disabled
and query the linked MPI vendor/library; site_i's site Intel MPI initialization
path SIGILLs on its 2007 login CPU, although the same native extension and
library load. The program inventory applies that preactivation before importing
`vibeqc`, fails if the probe nevertheless initializes MPI, and preserves its
existing version, symbol, clean-tree, and exact-SHA checks.
For a 40-character `--require-sha`, that gate now requires equality with the
full recorded SHA; a matching 12-character display prefix is no longer enough.
The modern build/compute-host health and refresh gates run through an attested
site_i Intel MPI launcher with `-np 1 -ppn 1`, then assert initialization and a
rank-zero, size-one world before activation. A missing package, incompatible
native link, wrong launcher, or compute-host initialization failure therefore
blocks the immutable candidate without treating the login CPU's site-MPI
limitation as a wheel failure. The root install lifecycle also accepts explicit
`--extras mpi` and `--extras dispersion,mpi` profiles. Its generic verification
uses the same no-initialization native-link proof, leaving real initialization
to a cluster's launcher-backed deployment gate instead of assuming singleton
MPI startup is supported.

### Fixed: plain serial imports no longer initialize optional MPI (2026-08-24)

Installing the `[mpi]` extra no longer makes a plain `import vibeqc` load
`mpi4py.MPI` and call `MPI_Init_thread`. Unlaunched processes now retain the
exact serial rank-zero, size-one identity world without touching the native
MPI runtime. Complete Open MPI, PMI/Intel/MPICH, MVAPICH, actual Slurm
