task-step, PMIx, or an explicit vibe-qc required-size launch contract
activates communicator binding. Allocation-only variables do not activate
MPI, while malformed or contradictory rank evidence, missing MPI support under
a detected launcher,
inadequate thread support, and launcher/communicator rank or size mismatch
fail closed instead of duplicating serial work on every rank. The χ-CCM D114
wrapper now declares its exact two-rank requirement before `mpiexec`.

### Performance: χ-CCM-B distributes exact density-diagnostic residue transforms (issue #315, D117, 2026-08-25)

χ-CCM-B SCF diagnostics now partition the inverse finite-character density
transform over actual finite-translation-group residues when MPI is active.
Tied minimum-image representatives from the zero-offset cell set used by the
density diagnostic are grouped before task ownership, their equal alias
weights must sum to one, and those weights are not applied again to the
transformed residue. This does not attest offset-dependent AO-pair, quartet,
or local-domain representatives. Each task retains the complete inner
character sum. Empty oversubscribed ranks skip the native subset call and
contribute an explicit empty parcel, then every rank receives the exact
canonical residue order through the existing exact-once gather.

Restricted and unrestricted results expose a dedicated execution record with
the complete character mesh and labels, unique residue keys, representative
scope, multiplicities and unit weight sums, local and per-rank task ownership,
separate ordered-key and construction fingerprints, and explicit
complete-character/no-extra-Wigner-weight semantics. The scheduler validates
the uniform dual net, complete residue coverage, and representative
congruences, and active ranks reject construction-fingerprint drift. Odd,
even, skew, serial, two-rank, three-rank, unrestricted-spin, and empty-rank
tests reproduce the complete serial finite-character transform exactly.
Unlike the construction-neutral D114/D116 radial AO output tasks, this work
unit is genuinely one χ residue.
It accelerates density diagnostics only: SCF J/K, XC, diagonalization,
localization, QVF/property transforms, post-HF, and gradients remain
unchanged. It is not Γ-CCM WSC farming, changes no Coulomb or exchange-q=0
convention, introduces no distance cutoff, and makes no DLPNO scaling claim.

### Performance: χ-CCM-B restricted four-center RHF/RKS farms complete direct-ERI output blocks (issue #303, D114/D116, 2026-08-24)

The experimental 3D `aiccm2026dev-b` RHF and non-screened RKS `four_center`
routes now distribute complete short-range direct-ERI output-cell blocks
across MPI ranks using a cyclic schedule. Without symmetry-representative
reduction, pure RKS farms J only; a masked pure route may use the shared fused
builder and discard K. Every owned block keeps the full
padded internal translation sum and density support; complete J blocks, and K
blocks when present, are gathered before incremental Fock state is updated.
XC grid work, reciprocal Hartree, long-range exchange, and the BvK q=0 seam
remain unchanged and replicated. Empty ranks skip the native domains call,
whose legacy empty-subset convention otherwise means all cells.

The new scheduling contract verifies exact task ownership and canonical
cell-order fingerprints and emits rank/task execution evidence on both the
BIPOLE result and χ diagnostics. Serial execution remains bit-identical, and
real 2/3-rank tests pin fixed-density, oversubscribed-empty-rank, and
end-to-end χ RHF parity. Serial PBE/PBE0 and real two-rank PBE tests add exact
RKS energy, XC, Fock, and density parity. Automatically selected pair-resolved
and symmetry-representative domains use the same complete-block gather. HSE
screened RKS remains serial because its base J and separate screened-K phases
need a multi-phase execution schema, and the generic driver rejects an
explicit farming request; UHF/UKS, fitted, and post-HF routes also
remain outside this milestone. A unit test now pins that serial contract
at the dedicated screened-K traversal itself, alongside the ctx-field
forwarding the multi-phase schema will need. Its task is a direct radial AO output block,
not a Γ-CCM union-and-weight WSC or an individual χ finite-group residue.
D114/D116 assign no physical Wigner weight; future residue-level work must
aggregate tied Wigner--Seitz representatives. This introduces no electrostatic
distance cutoff or reduced-scaling DLPNO claim.

The B campaign record now serializes this executed scheduling evidence.
Dedicated `run.sh --d114-mpi` and `--d116-rks-mpi` validation profiles
preflight the deployed source and core before MPI launch, require `mpi4py` and
exactly two active ranks, compare the farmed selector with the replicated
BIPOLE reference exactly on every rank, and permit only rank zero to atomically
write the result. D116 fixes the one-cycle c-diamond/STO-3G PBE inputs and also
requires exact XC-energy, executed-zero-mixing, and D83 inactive exchange-q=0
applicability under a distinct schema. These artifacts are explicitly
implementation-parity evidence, not
independently validated absolute-energy or whole-SCF scaling results. The
launcher owns both ranks, divides the total PBS CPU allocation evenly, rejects
scheduler-task declarations that Torque would not reflect in `ppn`, binds
hybrid Intel MPI or Open MPI ranks to disjoint OpenMP core domains, and records
the declared and native thread counts plus the binding policy and fixed
SCF/seam controls.

site_i acceptance at exact clean runtime
`77c5c67563915d63ff636fbc0312567f24328615` completed normally. Serial job
`ba1a57b5f1ad` converged c-diamond/STO-3G `(2,2,2)` RHF in seven iterations
with requested and executed Fock mixing both zero and overlap-fold drift
`1.351e-7`. Two-rank job `c8cbef024690` assigned 177 complete output tasks as
89/88 and reproduced its unfarmed energy, Fock, and density exactly. The
serial total remains subject to the independent D93/D103/D104 reportability
contracts; the MPI artifact is implementation-parity evidence only.

## [v0.15.139] - 2026-08-24 - *Neese's Cheetah*

**Verification status, stated honestly.** Two things dominate this release: a
five-commit molecular SCF parallelization series (IID 204) touching shared
numerical C++ — `df.cpp`, `jk_builder.cpp`, `rks.cpp`, `uks.cpp`,
`xc_kernel.cpp` — and a set of wrong-answer fixes and capability removals in
the semiempirical and CCM stacks. Each parallelization commit pins its result
against the serial path at every requested thread count, preserving the legacy
accumulation order, and retains serial fallbacks for small, generic-Eigen and
unmeasured-BLAS builds.

**Several routes now fail closed that previously returned a number.**
PM7/UPM7, Bloch-periodic OM1/OM2/OM3, OM1-SECCM, χ-CCM-B quadratic-SCF
requests, Γ-CCM open-shell clusters reaching the closed-shell entry points,
and Γ-CCM double hybrids through `run_ccm_rks`. Every one of those was
returning a plausible value rather than raising — a triplet solved as a closed
shell, a double-hybrid request answered with its hybrid-KS SCF half. Upgrading
will therefore surface errors where an earlier run silently produced a wrong
answer. That is the intent, not a regression.

**What this release does not establish.** The blocking gate is tiers T0+T1,
which is 4 of 739 test files, and the lane manifest marks
`scientific_acceptance` false for every lane: pytest and CI are change-safety
evidence, never method acceptance. PM6/PM7 (#255), OM1/OM2/OM3 (#163) and
periodic GFN2 (#296) remain excluded from method claims — the periodic GFN2
energy is not invariant under a lattice translation of an input atom (85 mHa
on MgO, against DFTB0 invariant to 1e-9 on the identical pair). Ionic
SCC-DFTB absolute a₀/B₀ are not chemistry: the 36 explicit repulsive pairs are
exactly the combinations of {H,C,N,O,F,P,S,Cl}, so Mg-O, Na-Cl, Li-F, Ca-O and
Mg-S have none. Paired Madelung/no-Madelung differences remain clean.

### Fixed (EXPERIMENTAL): two wrong-answer defects in the Γ-CCM drivers (2026-08-23)

Both found by a full-surface capability audit and reproduced live before
the fix; both returned a plausible number instead of failing.

* **Silent triplet-as-closed-shell.** `run_ccm_rhf`,
  `run_ccm_rhf_scalable` and `run_ccm_rks` checked electron **parity**
  only, so an even-electron cluster declaring `multiplicity > 1` was
  solved as a closed shell. On H₂/sto-3g (2 e⁻, mult 3, 8-bohr box) that
  returned −1.0491709020 and −1.1023577337 respectively, where the
  shell-aware `run_ccm_scf` dispatches to UHF and gives −0.7749672190.
  The route dispatcher grew this guard in 2026-07-15/16; the per-method
  entry points had not. They now refuse with a pointer to the
  open-shell sibling and to `run_ccm_scf`.
* **Double hybrids failing open.** `run_ccm_rks(ccm, "b2plyp")` returned
  −1.1446213910 — exactly the hybrid-KS SCF half of the true b2plyp
  −1.1490167438 — with no raise and no warning, i.e. a number that is
  not the requested functional. `run_ccm_rks`/`run_ccm_uks` now reject
  double hybrids and point at
  `run_ccm_double_hybrid_direct` for the composed energy (the real-Γ
  route has always failed closed here).

Both guards live in `vibeqc.periodic.ccm.experimental` so the reasoning
and the measured pre-fix numbers sit next to the check. Open-shell
drivers, the route dispatcher and ordinary closed-shell singlet runs are
unaffected. Gates: `tests/test_ccm_shell_and_dh_guards.py` (9);
regression: 109 driver/property/route tests green.


### Fixed: CCM method keys reach their citation routes; canonical UCCSD(T) was mis-attributed (2026-08-22)

**Attribution fix.** `routes.methods` carried twelve compound
`aiccm2026dev-b` keys and none for the Γ-CCM (`-a`) line, so a χ-CCM run cited
Peintinger & Bredow 2014 + Bredow-Geudtner-Jug 2001 while the Γ-CCM route
cited neither. The three `method=` selectors the `-a` drivers actually accept
(`periodic.ccm.scf._CCM_ERI_METHODS`: `aiccm2026dev-a`, the historical
`union12` eq-18 product weight, and the deprecated `aiccmdev` alias) are now
routed to both CCM entries, which already carry `print = true`.

Auditing that surfaced a defect underneath it. Two labels the `-b` drivers
stamp had no route at all: `run_aiccm2026dev_b_uccsd` / `_uccsd_t` pin
`localise="none"` + `tcut_pno=0` and therefore emit `aiccm2026dev-b-uccsd` /
`-uccsd(t)`. A `routes.methods` miss is *silent* (step 5b of
`CitationDatabase.assemble`), so both resolved to the generic periodic set and
dropped the two CCM papers plus Purvis-Bartlett and Raghavachari with no
warning — canonical UCCSD(T) was mis-attributed, not merely un-attributed.
Both rows are now routed and the family is marked.

**Neither route fires yet, and that is why they land now.** The `-a` line is
unwired (`AICCM2026DEV_A` sits in `periodic_jk_method._UNWIRED_CCM_ROUTES` and
`validate_jk_method` raises before any output stage, open FR-1), and the `-b`
post-HF drivers are library-only: unreachable from `run_periodic_job`, whose
`assemble(...)` arm passes the bare `aiccm2026dev-b`, with direct callers
emitting a bare `json.dumps(record)` and importing nothing from
`vibeqc.output`. So a χ-CCM DLPNO-CCSD(T) number produces no citation surface
at all today. Landing the routes first means the wiring merge cannot silently
ship the mis-attribution. Verified as far as FR-1 allows, by forcing
`assemble(method="aiccm2026dev-a")` on a real `run_periodic_job` bundle: both
CCM entries reach the `.out` references block, `.references`, `.bibtex`, and
the `.system` `[citations]` section.

### Fixed: NDDO Hamiltonian boundaries audited — OMx one-centre exchange corrected; PM7 and Bloch-periodic OMx gated (2026-08-21)

**Wrong-answer fix plus capability removals.** Molecular OM1/OM2/OM3 and
heavy-element PM6 energies change, and several previously callable routes now
fail closed.

The molecular OMx one-centre Fock built its diagonal exchange from an
off-diagonal density element — `F(mu,mu) -= 1/2 D(mu,nu) (mu nu|mu nu)` where
the NDDO one-centre expression takes the diagonal population `D(nu,nu)`. The
unrestricted driver carried the same defect, additionally swapped the own-spin
and opposite-spin prefactors of its one-centre off-diagonal coupling
(`(P_sigmabar + 2 P_sigma)` where the NDDO expression is
`(P_sigma + 2 P_sigmabar)`), and clamped its alpha/beta partition to the basis
size instead of rejecting an
electron count the NDDO basis cannot hold. All three are corrected, so every
OM1/OM2/OM3 molecular energy moves. The pre-fix absolute energies pinned for
the Thiel furan, thymine, adenine, imidazole and pyrrole fixtures are retired
rather than restated: those tests now pin iteration-cap invariance, and the
replacement value pins are closed-form one-centre oracles assembled from the
published `uss/upp/gss/gsp/gpp/gp2/hsp` parameters (F- closed shell, nitrogen
quartet) matched to 1e-12 Ha. `e_electronic` now reports `E_total - E_core`
instead of the sum of doubly occupied orbital energies.

Molecular PM6 electron-core attraction now uses the PM6 core Klopman-Ohno
radius (MOPAC `po(9) = EV/(2 GSS)`, with the sparse `poc` parameter as the
explicit override — six of those overrides are added to the bundled cache)
instead of a `Z - 2` valence guess for elements outside H/C/N/O/F, and the
exact NDDO multipole pair block is contracted for heavy-atom/hydrogen pairs
where the previous spherical population approximation dropped the nonzero
dipole and quadrupole components. PM6 numbers therefore change outside the
H/C/N/O/F subset. The new external pin is PM6 UHF OH against official
MOPAC 23.2.5 (`E_electronic + E_core = -302.634001607503 eV`, PM6 UHF DOUBLET
1SCF PRECISE) to 3e-7 Ha. Elements whose bundled record requires d orbitals
now fail closed rather than running with p-channel stand-ins, and MOPAC's
`Z = 100-106` pseudo-atom records are excluded from the executable registry,
so the bundled cache is described as 75 chemical-element records, not 82.

PM7/UPM7 fail closed. The retired prototype loaded PM7 parameters into the
PM6-family kernel without Stewart's feathered electrostatics and its coupled
electron-electron, electron-core and core-core terms, so it could not evaluate
the published method. `run_job(method="pm7")` now raises at route planning,
before sidecar and output planning, so a rejected request leaves no manifest
or job artefact behind; `PM7Model` / `UPM7Model` are fail-closed compatibility
wrappers. The 75-record parameter registry is retained for completing the
implementation.

Bloch-periodic OM1/OM2/OM3 fail closed for the same reason: the retired Gamma
driver omitted the published image-resolved ORT, ECP and penetration terms and
could return finite numbers under an OMx label. `PeriodicOMxModel`,
`optimize_omx_cell`, `run_omx_gamma` and the periodic OMx finite-difference
derivative entry points remain importable as fail-closed compatibility
surfaces. OM1-SECCM also fails closed, its analytic core-valence ECP being
absent; topology-bound OM2/OM3-SECCM is unaffected and stays experimental.

Periodic PM6 keeps the Gamma NDDO route. Its native batched
finite-difference gradient/stress workspace now raises when a displaced SCF
fails to converge instead of differentiating an unconverged energy, and the
periodic PM6 loader and derivative kernel reject a parameter set whose
`method_name()` is not `pm6`. `run_ccm` likewise stops masking a native
MSINDO CCM non-convergence with a silent fall-through to the Python reference:
once the native path is selected (H-Kr) its non-convergence propagates, while
Rb-Xe and binding-missing cases still use the deterministic Python reference.

Status wording moves with the code. PM6/UPM6 goes from "Production
(molecular)" to molecular development — H-only and H-heavy s/p interactions
source-correct, full heavy-heavy two-centre tensor parity open; OM2/OM3 go
from "Production (molecular)" to validated molecular prescreening, explicitly
not an external-parity claim; and `docs/experimental/catalog.md` no longer
states that anything absent from it is production-grade. Stewart 2013
(`stewart_pm7_2013`) and Janetzko 2008 (`janetzko_ccm_2008`) enter the
citation database in the same merge and are routed — PM7 so that even a gated
request names its defining paper, Janetzko for the opt-in OMx-SECCM
`janetzko_eq10` comparison weighting, which the SECCM route plan now records
and cites.

### Fixed: SECCM screens indefinite cyclic overlap by canonical orthogonalization (IID 215, 2026-08-21)

The WS-weighted cyclic overlap matrix of the non-orthogonal SECCM adapters
(DFTB0, SCC-DFTB, GFN2-xTB) can acquire non-positive eigenvalues when atoms
sit on Wigner-Seitz boundaries, the documented C-point failure mode of
Peintinger and Bredow (J. Comput. Chem. 35, 2014, eq. 5 and the critical-
eigenvalues discussion). The ill-posed generalized eigenproblem was the
root cause of the corrected B1(100) slab runaway (IID 215): it anti-screened
the SCC map into a transient 1e6-electron explosion. The adapters now apply
the paper's remedy: when the cyclic overlap fails the positive-definiteness
gate the non-positive subspace is screened and the solve proceeds in the
canonically orthonormalized basis with coefficients back-rotated. Cells that
pass the gate keep the legacy generalized solve bit-for-bit, and a cell whose
screened subspace cannot hold the occupied manifold still fails closed with
the unchanged `overlap matrix is not positive definite` error. The corrected
four-plane B1(100) 2x2 slab now converges to a physical state under every
kernel flavor (ewald_gamma E/atom = -2.3815 Ha, q_rms 0.52, matching the
out-of-process xtb Gamma-only slab reference's charge state) and the
molecular-limit and bulk parity pins are unchanged.

The same screening also converges the neutral surface O vacancy of that slab
(IID 155): the F0 cell lands on the pristine charge scale (q_rms 0.516 against
pristine 0.519) at a raw cyclic vacancy cost of 4.175 Ha, against the
out-of-process xtb Gamma-only reference of 4.058 Ha (q_rms 0.523). Pristine
and vacancy cells are now pinned from one shared test fixture builder, and the
`studies/seccm-bulk3d` xtb reference generator takes a plane count and a
`--vacancy` switch so pristine, vacancy and future adsorbate cells share one
builder on both sides of the comparison.

### Added (EXPERIMENTAL): WSC-axis parallelism + one-call DLPNO on the real-Γ direct route (2026-08-21)

Two capability items for AICCM, both route-local (shared kernels stay with
their owning lanes — see the handover's coordination notes):

* **Parallelization over WSCs / q-channels.** `ccm_neutral_cderi_fold`
  gains `fold_threads`: the per-`(k_a, k_b)` fits of each q-channel are
  independent and every C++ primitive they call releases the GIL, so a
  thread pool over that axis is the CCM analogue of k-point parallelism
  (CLAUDE.md § 15). Star MEMBERS still reconstruct only after their
  channel's builds complete, preserving the serial sweep's
  representative-before-member ordering. Measured on H₂ (3,3,1) with BLAS
  pinned: **67.6 s → 17.1 s (3.95x)** plain and **25.0 s → 6.1 s (4.11x)**
  with the symmetry star reduction, **bit-identical** to serial in both.
  Opt-in (`VIBEQC_CCM_FOLD_THREADS`, `0` = all cores) because an outer
  pool on top of a multi-threaded BLAS oversubscribes; pin BLAS first.
  The same commit vectorizes the fold's torus cell-pair scatter (an
  `N_c²`-iteration Python double loop — 9.4M iterations at (4,4,4) — into
  one einsum over the same disjoint blocks).
* **DLPNO on the BvK-ewald direct reference.** `run_ccm_dlpno_mp2_direct`,
  `run_ccm_dlpno_ump2_direct` (open shell) and `run_ccm_dlpno_ccsd_direct`
  (CCSD(T))
  builds one cderi, the matching SCF, and the DLPNO correlation in one
  call — the SCF/cderi consistency guarantee `run_ccm_ri_mp2` provides for
  canonical MP2, which the DLPNO entry points lacked (a mismatched
  `scf_result` is silently wrong). `reference="direct"` (default) rides
  this route's seam-corrected reference instead of the strict-zero neutral
  one, whose correlation distortion grows with cluster size
  (`HANDOVER_D2_EXXDIV.md`). Gates: no-truncation identity with canonical
  RI-MP2 / UMP2 / CCSD on their own reference at zero truncation
  (3e-17 / 4e-17 / 2e-19 / 9e-17) and pins that the two references
  genuinely differ — measured swings of 25 % (MP2), 36 % (UMP2, where the
  per-spin seam enters both channels' denominators) and 30 % (CCSD). The
  closed- and open-shell entry points refuse each other's clusters rather
  than mis-treating the spin state.

### Fixed: CCM route selector follows ruling R1 nomenclature (issue #222, 2026-08-25)

The paper-facing route spellings `gamma`, `gamma-ccm`, and `gamma_ccm` no
longer silently select the union-and-weight four-centre route. Per ruling R1
(2026-08-21), Paper-1 Γ-CCM denotes the NEUTRAL finite-BvK-torus
construction, whose two admissible producers are `route="real-gamma"`
(`run_ccm_rhf_direct`) and `route="neutral-bloch"` (`run_ccm_rhf_gdf`); the
union-and-weight four-centre is the 2014 lineage that Paper 1 diagnoses as
non-variational. Because a single keyword cannot choose between the two
producers, `resolve_ccm_route` rejects the paper-facing spellings with a
message naming both, and the module docstring, `docs/aiccm2026dev_a.md`, and
the `PeriodicJKMethod.AICCM2026DEV_A` pointer now state that nomenclature.
Regression coverage in `tests/test_ccm_route.py` pins the fail-closed
behaviour. The four-centre route remains selectable under its own name
(`route="four-center"`, the default) for lineage and diagnosis work.

### Added: χ-CCM-B fixed-input unrestricted energy-weighted-density audit (issue #245, 2026-08-21)

The experimental 3D χ-CCM-B gradient surface now provides
`compute_aiccm2026dev_b_fixed_input_unrestricted_energy_weighted_density_lattice`.
For explicit overlap blocks and separate alpha/beta occupied-coefficient and
candidate variational-Fock blocks on the complete character net, it evaluates
`Lambda_s = C_occ,s^H F_s C_occ,s` and
`W_s = C_occ,s Lambda_s C_occ,s^H = D_s F_s D_s`, then sums the two spin
blocks and inverse-transforms the result onto the exact requested overlap cell
support. There is no closed-shell factor of two in either individual spin
block and no alpha-beta cross term. Either spin rank may be zero, while both
cannot be zero; the explicit Fock for a zero-rank channel still passes the
same finite, Hermitian, and per-spin sewing checks.

Independent spin ranks may differ but remain constant across the character
net. The boundary checks overlap orthonormality and occupied-projector and
energy-weighted-density sewing and inverse-character reality independently in
each spin, so violations cannot cancel in the spin sum. In the closed-shell
limit
`C_alpha=C_beta=C` and `F_alpha=F_beta=F`, the unrestricted result reduces
exactly to the restricted `2 C Lambda C^H = D F D / 2` construction.

This remains a fixed-input algebra and D80 composition audit. It does not
infer occupations, rebuild or attest either final physical SCF Fock, prove
stationarity or backend variational closure, bind the inputs to an executed
SCF state, or enable analytic total gradients. The D85 binding, explicit
exchange-kernel derivatives, RI, XC, and response derivatives remain open.

### Added: χ-CCM-B fixed-input restricted energy-weighted-density audit (issue #241, 2026-08-21)

The experimental 3D χ-CCM-B gradient surface now provides
`compute_aiccm2026dev_b_fixed_input_restricted_energy_weighted_density_lattice`.
For explicit overlap, occupied-coefficient, and candidate variational-Fock
blocks on the complete character net, it evaluates
`Lambda = C_occ^H F C_occ`, constructs `W = 2 C_occ Lambda C_occ^H`, and
inverse-transforms `W` onto the exact requested overlap cell support. The
boundary checks Hermiticity, occupied overlap orthonormality, time reversal,
support identity, bounded exact-integer character coordinates, finite derived
algebra, and the real inverse-transform residue.

This is a fixed-input algebra and composition audit for the existing D80
overlap derivative. It does not rebuild or attest the final physical SCF Fock,
infer occupations, establish variational closure, bind numerical provenance,
or enable analytic total gradients. Unrestricted energy-weighted density and
the remaining exchange, RI, XC, and response derivatives are unchanged and
remain open.

### Fixed: SCC-DFTB retry ladder reaches the systems it was failing closed on (issue #78, 2026-08-21)

The Mermin free-energy retry ladder that `run_job` enters after a
zero-temperature SCC-DFTB failure now carries a fourth rung at
`electronic_temperature = 0.002` Ha (~632 K) and gives every rung a
1500-iteration budget instead of 500.

Both changes came from measuring the archived rows that were still failing
closed. The S22 formic-acid dimer converges on the existing
`T = 0.0012` Ha rung but needs 573 iterations, so the 500-iteration budget was
turning a converging rung into a failure. Adenine does not converge on any rung
up to `T = 0.0015` Ha even at 1500 iterations — it stalls at -18.7886,
-18.9226 and -19.1639 Ha — and needs the warmer rung, where it converges in
232 iterations to -19.63356440 Ha.

A rung is only entered after the previous one has failed, so neither change can
alter a system that already converges. Regression coverage in
`tests/test_scc_dftb_retry_ladder.py`, which also asserts the converged energy
is negative: the two remaining #78 rows (thymine and the archived
"S22 benzene-water") are input defects, not convergence defects — thymine
carries a C-C contact at 0.629 A and a hydrogen 0.430 A from a ring carbon, and
the archived benzene-water places the water in the benzene plane with an H-H
contact at 0.600 A. Their archived energies (thymine +476.77 Ha) are not valid
references and should be retired rather than reproduced.


### Performance: χ-CCM-B local correlation retains one exact auxiliary translation (issue #221, 2026-08-21)

The experimental 3D χ-CCM-B local-correlation setup now retains only the
home-auxiliary representative of its translation-covariant real-torus RI
factor. For `N_c` cyclic cells, primitive auxiliary rank `A`, and primitive AO
rank `M`, retained real AO-factor memory falls exactly from
`8 A N_c^3 M^2` to `8 A N_c^2 M^2` bytes. A native circulant AO-to-MO
transform reconstructs the unchanged full logical auxiliary output, and the
unused full-rank identity metric is no longer allocated.

The `N_c^2` momentum-pair cache, logical MO-factor storage, all-pair and
all-triple solver contractions, finite Hamiltonian, and local approximations
are unchanged. This is an exact setup-memory reduction, not a reduced-scaling
correlation claim.

### Fixed: χ-CCM-B restricted four-center level-shift warm-up executes (D110, 2026-08-21)

With an empty explicit `level_shift_schedule`, the experimental χ-CCM-B
restricted four-center wrapper passed only `options.level_shift` to BIPOLE and
copied `options.level_shift_warmup_cycles` straight into diagnostics. BIPOLE
therefore held the shift active for the whole SCF while the record described a
finite release point. The RHF and RKS entry points now resolve the warm-up
before backend dispatch and lower it onto BIPOLE's own `LevelShiftSchedule`:
`-1` (the default) resolves to at most five shifted startup cycles, a positive
request is capped at `max_iter - 1` so at least one scheduled tail cycle is
unshifted, and the wrapper supplies `[b] * n_w + [0.0]`. An active auto or
positive warm-up requires `max_iter >= 2` and fails before SCF otherwise,
because a one-cycle budget cannot truthfully represent both a shifted startup
and an unshifted tail. Explicit `0` keeps the historic persistent static-shift
mode, including at `max_iter = 1`, and the modifier stays dormant and
uninterpreted when the static shift is zero.

The caller's options object is never rewritten: it remains the request, while
`result.aiccm2026dev_b.level_shift_warmup_cycles` now reports the *executed*
effective length. With an empty schedule a diagnostic zero means persistent
for a nonzero static shift and inactive for a zero shift; on a fitted route
with a nonempty explicit schedule it means the warm-up modifier was
superseded, and inactive unrestricted routes record zero instead of the raw
default `-1`. D108 still rejects every nonempty options-level four-center
schedule before this resolver, D72 remains the first lower-dimensional
failure, and D109 still runs after. Pre-D110 declared-3D restricted
four-center RHF/RKS `ok` or `not_converged` records with a nonzero static
shift, an empty explicit schedule, and an auto or positive warm-up are
request-fingerprint-invalid and revision-bound, because the old route executed
a persistent shift while recording a release request; only a trajectory
extending beyond the resolved warm-up proves the intended release point was
crossed, so the quarantine does not by itself prove an energy change.
Error/unsupported records, zero-shift dormant modifiers, and explicit
persistent warm-up zero remain valid. Regression coverage in
`tests/test_periodic_aiccm2026dev_b.py` pins the auto/explicit/capped
schedules reaching the backend, the tail-less refusal before dispatch, the
reported executed length, the zero-shift dormancy, D72 precedence, and a real
three-iteration RHF run whose per-iteration shifts are `0.3, 0.3, 0.0`. This
changes no finite Hamiltonian, Coulomb convention, Γ-CCM/χ-CCM construction
distinction, numerical-support qualification, or analytic-gradient status.

### Fixed: SECCM adapters enforce their audited numerical invariants (IIDs 197, 198, 200-203, 207, 211, 216, 217, 2026-08-21)

**Behaviour change plus one capability removal on the experimental SECCM
adapters.**

The SCC-DFTB-SECCM Madelung embedding is now deposited through the same
overlap-weighted variational operator as the ordinary SCC potential —
`H^SCC = H0 - 1/2 S (V_A + V_B)` with `V = gamma . dq + V_mad` (Elstner et
al., Phys. Rev. B 58, 7260 (1998), Eqs. 20-22) — replacing the
MSINDO-inherited diagonal shift `F(k,k) -= V_mad`. Embedded energies change.
Because the total Mulliken-charge interaction is now variational, the fixed
point is stationary in the charges and the coupled-perturbed SCC response is
gone: embedded gradients report `gradient_method="analytic"` (no longer
`"analytic_cpscc"`) and carry only the explicit `1/2 dq . dM/dR . dq`
derivative. The Python `_embedded_gradient_fd` helper and the
`gradient_fd_step` keyword of `run_scc_dftb_seccm` are removed, and passing
that keyword now raises `TypeError`. Coverage: the N=3 smeared and N=2
zero-temperature chains still match re-converged central differences of the
energy, and a new regression reconstructs the embedded Hamiltonian element by
element and asserts a nonzero off-diagonal Madelung deposit — precisely what
the retired diagonal form could not produce.

Three-dimensional SCC-DFTB-SECCM Madelung embedding fails closed
(`NotImplementedError`): the current Ohno gamma correction has no
thermodynamic limit. The previously passing charged 3-D cube regression now
asserts that refusal. Unembedded 3-D finite-torus runs are unaffected, but
charged cells still require the embedding, so charged 3-D SCC-DFTB-SECCM is no
longer available.

PM6-SECCM rejects any element whose bundled PM6 record requires d orbitals:
the SECCM PM6 Hamiltonian implements s/p channels only, and treating those
five d functions as p stand-ins would evaluate a different model. GFN2-SECCM
now rejects its dependent validation flags at both the Python and native
boundaries (`madelung_s_weighted` and `madelung_no_self` require `madelung`;
`ewald_gamma_molecular_onsite` requires `ewald_gamma`) instead of silently
ignoring them, and both GFN2- and SCC-DFTB-SECCM gate the assembled supercell
overlap for positive definiteness before the SCC. The native Broyden charge
mixer no longer indexes past its history allocation: `reset()` allocates and
zeroes the full `dim x memory` buffers instead of resizing them to zero
columns, and the populated-column counter is clamped to `memory` so a run
longer than the history depth stays inside the allocation. The mixer is
exposed as an internal `_BroydenMixer` binding and its reset, rollover, and
damped-fallback paths are exercised in a subprocess, so a memory fault fails
the test rather than the session. Finally, the shared record flattener
validates the optional translation-orbit reduction only while it is usable, so
a symmetry-breaking geometry is no longer rejected merely because a previously
bound orbit reduction has lapsed.

### Added: GFN2-SECCM SCC restart from supplied shell charges (2026-08-21)

`run_gfn2_seccm(..., initial_shell_charges=...)` starts the experimental
GFN2-SECCM charge iteration from a supplied shell-fluctuation vector
(`dq = population - n0`) instead of the neutral zero vector — a general
warm-start facility for continuation runs and defect ladders, where a
converged neighbouring cell is a better start than neutrality. The default
(`None`) keeps the shipped neutral start bit-for-bit, iteration count
included. A vector that is not exactly `n_shells` long is rejected before the
SCC rather than padded or ignored. Regression coverage on the converging
rocksalt 2x2x2 bulk pins all three arms: a perturbed start reaches the same
converged energy within 1e-8 Ha, a wrong-sized vector raises, and the default
reproduces the neutral run's energy to 1e-12 Ha at the same iteration count.
This is a restart facility only, not a remedy for the map-level transients of
IID 215, which trigger from any near-physical start.

### Changed (EXPERIMENTAL): occupied-rank factored exchange on the real-Γ direct route (2026-08-21)

The direct-route SCF drivers' exchange contraction now runs through an
occupied-rank density factor (`psd_density_factor` +
`ccm_ri_k_neutral_factored`): with the aufbau `D = c X Xᵀ` the loops
always produce (DIIS extrapolates the Fock, never D), both contraction
passes carry the rank `k = n_occ` instead of `n` — the efficiency
program's named K lever (K was ~80% of per-iteration cost at the
(3,3,3)-pob ladder rung). Measured: machine-precision agreement with the
dense reference (2.7e-14 on LiH pob-TZVP-REV2 (2,2,2), gate pinned incl.
the asymmetric-L-block trap a transpose-dropping variant fails at
5.6e-6), 2.3–3.2x at measured sizes, growing as n/n_occ at production
bases. Wired per spin (UHF/UKS), through the seam and screened-σ₀ terms
(`S D S = (S X)(S X)ᵀ`), and guarded (indefinite densities raise). The
dense `ccm_ri_k_neutral` stays as the validation reference. All 54
direct-route gates re-ran green with the factored path live.

### Fixed: vibe-view rebuilds preserve computed and charge overlays (issue #219, 2026-08-21)

Ordinary same-file scene rebuilds now replay the last successfully rendered
MO, total or spin density, ELF, NCI, or density-Laplacian recipe instead of
leaving the replacement structure bare while its visibility control remains
enabled. Hidden computed surfaces remain hidden; failed replay clears the
visible flag while retaining the recipe for an explicit retry. Active atomic
charge labels and optional charge-tinted spheres are also restored before the
scene material/toon pass, with overlapping atom-index labels removed and the
current representation, periodic replication, residue selection, and material
preserved. Computed renders now commit under one lifecycle guard: section/file
switches cancel in-flight MO animation and discard stale actors before a client
push, while panel-only hot reloads serialize their reader swap with the render
and carry session-created re-localized wavefunctions onto the fresh reader.
Failed charge-overlay preparation or replacement now removes stale/partial
actors and restores the neutral structure and appearance when possible. Section
and file switches still clear these per-section recipes, and stored QVF volume
sections retain their existing independent lifecycle.

### Changed: `run_job(density_fit=...)` reaches the geometry-optimization and Hessian sub-drivers (issue #31, 2026-08-21)

**Behaviour change.** Since 2ce60be49 (the BUG 117 memory-preflight fix)
the `density_fit=` / `cosx=` / `aux_basis=` keywords are wired onto the
SCF option structs before the dry-run short-circuit, so a
`run_job(..., density_fit=True, optimize=True)` or `hessian=True` job now
runs its per-step SCFs on the density-fitted route where the same request
was previously dropped before the sub-driver (the final single point was
already correct). This changes the numbers those sub-drivers produce for
callers who passed the kwargs, and it is now pinned by a regression
(`tests/test_runner.py`). The keyword contract itself is unchanged:
callers who never pass `density_fit=` see no difference.

### Fixed: vibe-view rebuilds preserve material and toon appearance (issue #214, 2026-08-21)

The viewer now realizes its declared `cpk_glossy` material on the initial
scene and centrally replays the selected material and toon state whenever a
scene rebuild or file switch replaces its actors. Label, representation,
replication, residue, and element-colour rebuilds can no longer leave newly
created actors at PyVista defaults while the controls still report the old
appearance. Toon snapshots now belong to their plotter and are discarded
before actor names are reused, so disabling toon after a rebuild restores the
new material instead of stale properties from the removed scene. A partially
failed toon pass now restores changed actors and clears its snapshots before
reporting failure.

### Fixed: molecular XC grid batches use the OpenMP allocation (IID 204, 2026-08-21)

Molecular RKS/UKS semilocal quadrature and the default UKS stability-kernel
matvec now evaluate independent 4096-point grid slices concurrently. Each
worker owns its libxc state and private Fock contribution; contributions are
then added in the original grid order, preserving the serial floating-point
fixed point while keeping the linked BLAS path unchanged. Existing nested AO
teams are suppressed inside a batch wave. The SCF and larger stability
workspaces are capped independently at 64 and 16 workers, and molecular DFT
memory preflight now charges those concurrent workspaces. Regression coverage
pins bitwise-identical one- and four-worker RKS/UKS energies, densities, and
polarised stability-kernel matrices.

The density-fitted Coulomb build now assigns independent auxiliary reductions
and disjoint output columns to the requested OpenMP team while preserving each
matrix element's original auxiliary order. Open-shell PATOM guesses also build
their two independent density-fitted exchange matrices together: inner
`B_P D_alpha` / `B_P D_beta` products share a capped wave, then the alpha and
beta `K += X_P B_P` chains retain the original ascending-`P`, BLAS `beta=1`
association. Small contractions and non-DF builders keep the sequential path.
Regression coverage pins the worker gates, repeated bitwise J/K parity, and
the production open-shell PATOM call site.

The density-fitting constructor's Coulomb-metric half transform now partitions
large, independent right-hand sides at dimension-only boundaries and solves
those blocks concurrently through the single-threaded BLAS backend. Boundaries
are aligned to the supported BLAS column micro-kernels, preserving the legacy
monolithic transform bytes on OpenBLAS and Accelerate as well as one- versus
multi-worker parity. The raw-tensor pack and transformed-tensor unpack now use
disjoint-output OpenMP copies. On OpenBLAS and Accelerate, large single and
paired fitted-K builds retain each full-shape `B_P D` product, then assign
fixed 24-column output blocks to workers while every block preserves the
legacy ascending-P accumulation. Small builds plus transforms and K builds on
generic Eigen or unmeasured BLAS backends remain serial, and the existing
four-tensor construction memory charge still covers the bounded K scratch.
Regression coverage pins raw-bit transform/J/K parity, actual worker use, and
small-system fallbacks.

Failed molecular SCFs now omit the derived Mulliken, Löwdin, Hirshfeld,
Mayer, and dipole block before raising the existing fail-closed error. The
old path computed and printed those analyses from a density it immediately
rejected; on large DFT jobs that also repeated a grid and SAD build after the
timed SCF. The convergence trace, energy decomposition, and fatal diagnostic
remain available, while converged-job output is unchanged. The existing UHF
fail-closed regression now pins both sides of that contract.

### Fixed: χ-CCM-B quadratic-SCF requests fail closed when unexecuted (IID 209, 2026-08-21)

All experimental `aiccm2026dev-b` RHF/RKS/UHF/UKS routes now reject a
positive `quadratic_fallback_iter` before backend SCF. The periodic options
and B campaign producer exposed and recorded the C1c activation, denominator
shift, and trust-region cap, but neither the BIPOLE nor fitted GDF/COSX χ
loops read those fields or performed the quadratic orbital-rotation update.
The old route could therefore report a supported conditional convergence
request that the selected engine neither implemented nor attested.

Zero remains the supported inactive setting, negative activation is invalid,
and existing lower-dimensional, Gamma-RI mixing/shift, restricted four-center
schedule, and unrestricted level-shift failures retain precedence. Closed-
shell post-HF inherits the guard through its χ RHF reference. Pre-fix 3D
`ok`/`not_converged` SCF or derived post-HF records that accepted a positive
activation are conservatively request-fingerprint-invalid and revision-bound
because the selected backend neither supported nor attested that conditional
request. This does not show that a quadratic step was reached or that the
energy changed; only a run with `iterations > quadratic_fallback_iter`
definitively crossed the intended trigger. Unsupported/error records remain
valid failure evidence, and nondefault shift/step values with activation zero
remain valid and dormant. The default finite Hamiltonian, distinct Γ-CCM and
χ-CCM constructions, D93 qualification, and analytic-total-gradient
fail-close are unchanged.

Next minor cycle (v0.16): native Born-von-Karman periodic local correlation;
see `docs/roadmap.md` for the gated scope and acceptance evidence.

### Fixed: vibe-view notebook helpers close archive resources on failures (issue #213, 2026-08-21)

`qvf_to_html()` and `qvf_to_image()` now scope every `QVFReader` with its
context manager. Malformed structure data can no longer leave the HTML
helper's archive open, and a failure while constructing the off-screen
PyVista plotter can no longer leak the image helper's already-open reader.
Failure-injection regressions require the original error to propagate while
each reader and every successfully constructed plotter closes exactly once.

### Security: vibe-view notebook HTML keeps QVF text out of executable script context (issue #212, 2026-08-21)

`qvf_to_html()` no longer inserts archive-derived XYZ text into a JavaScript
template literal. A crafted archive filename could previously supply a live
`${...}` expression, while a crafted atom symbol could terminate the inline
script element. The helper now passes JSON-serialized string data to 3Dmol and
escapes HTML parser sentinels before embedding it. The regression proves that
both payload forms remain inert while the exact XYZ text round-trips.

### Fixed: vibe-view Jupyter line magic loads and dispatches documented options (issue #196, 2026-08-21)

`%load_ext vibeview.jupyter` again registers the documented `%vibeview` line
magic. The default structure, section, and provenance view plus `--table`,
`--mo`, `--scf`, `--bands`, and `--capture` now dispatch through current
viewer APIs. Structureless archives remain inspectable, canonical volume hints
are respected, malformed arguments and rendering failures report explicit
messages, and archive metadata is escaped before notebook display. The test
profile now includes the Jupyter extra; real IPython-shell regressions pin
extension loading and every documented option.

### Fixed: MSINDO H-Ar single points compare strict RHF basins (IID 191, 2026-08-21)

Closed-shell H-Ar `run_msindo` single points no longer return the first
converged Hcore/DIIS stationary point without checking the method's
extended-Hückel/WICHT trajectory. Every converged WICHT candidate is
strict-DIIS-refined before the stationary energies are compared, and the
refined density replaces the primary result only when it is converged and lower
beyond the requested convergence resolution. The energy-only WICHT state is
never returned for those jobs. Every proactive H-Ar probe retains the
established 2000-cycle recovery floor, so root selection is stable when the
strict-DIIS cap crosses the primary convergence count. Converged jobs outside
H-Ar do not pay that probe cost. Failed-primary tetrazine recovery, NDDO, UHF,
CCM, COSMO, the oracle-pinned heavy-element energy trajectory, and its
pre-existing strict analytic-gradient route retain their established routing.
MP2, OVGF, CIS/CISD, and CIS-gradient reference-SCF routes are outside this fix
and remain unchanged. Iteration reporting includes all attempted work.

At the oracle-deck acetamide geometry, both native and Python backends now select
the lower stationary determinant at `-39.7743880637 Ha` instead of the
metastable `-39.7334279692 Ha` root. Cyclopropene, propanamide, and pyridazine
controls retain their lower Hcore/DIIS solutions, and the existing tetrazine
cycle recovery remains at 270 aggregate iterations. Ground-state analytic
gradients for H-Ar INDO jobs now reuse the selected strict density: acetamide's
N-x component agrees with finite differences of the selected energy surface
within `1e-6 Ha/bohr` in both backends. A production-backend replay of all 41
retained molecular MSINDO campaign geometries converges every case within
`5e-11 Ha` of its oracle: only acetamide selects the alternate basin, tetrazine
uses failed-primary recovery, and the other 39 retain their primary stationary
solution.

### Tests: four periodic runner smoke tests converge instead of tripping the SCF gate (IID 190, 2026-08-21)

Three `run_periodic_job` option-forwarding smoke tests in
`tests/test_kpoints_recommend.py` (Gilat occupations on closed-shell GDF,
explicit `bz_integration=None` on multi-k GDF, a recommended metal mesh with
auto smearing through BIPOLE RKS) and the BIPOLE population-sidecar/QVF
cleanliness test in `tests/test_output_population.py` still passed
`max_iter=1` as a speed hack. The fail-closed non-convergence gate
(3fc4b068f) raises `RuntimeError` before any forwarding or sidecar assertion
can run, so all four nodes were deterministically red on `main`, and the
fourth reddened the `output-docs` gate lane on every docs or CHANGELOG
touch. Each now drives its dilute H2 cell to convergence (2 iterations at
`conv_tol_energy=1e-6`, cap 10) and asserts its real contract: per-k Gilat
occupations summing to two electrons, finite converged energies, the
recommender's `smearing_source = auto` / `fermi-dirac` metadata reaching the
`.out` options block, and a converged population sidecar whose charges match
the QVF `atom_properties` section. The population test's QVF density grid
moves from 3.0 to 0.5 bohr, which the BvK density integral check accepts
(3.0 bohr tripped the compatibility fallback once the run actually reached
the writer). Same repair shape as IID 104 / 771cc3458; the SCF gate is
untouched.

### Docs: real-Γ adapter test states the wired runner contract; optimize refusal pinned (IID 199, 2026-08-21)

The module docstring of `tests/test_periodic_ccm_real_gamma_adapter.py` still
said the `jk_method='real-gamma'` runner wiring was "the next increment" and
that `validate_jk_method` fails closed, a month after 6ec349703 (2026-07-26)
landed both and the file's own tests began driving `run_periodic_job` on the
route. It now states the wired contract and the milestone-2c status (API-level
forces and fixed-cell relaxation since 2026-08-19/20; runner-level
`optimize=True` awaits its wiring). The runner's refusal message was measured
current and is unchanged; the test now pins that it names
`run_ccm_direct_optimize`, says 2c LANDED, and names the wiring gate, so a
regression to stale prose fails instead of matching "geometry optimization".

## [v0.15.138] - 2026-08-21 - *Neese's Cheetah*

**Verification status, stated honestly.** This release ships a batch of
wrong-answer and convergence fixes as landed, test-backed code: the CPCM
headline energy (#148), the ROHF/ROKS EDIIS/ADIIS projector coupling
(#119), incremental-Fock drift-stall disengagement (#129), scale-aware
oscillation detection (#152), multi-k KRKS consuming `rsgdf_tail_ke_cutoff`
(#146), toroidal MP2 periodic-HF routing (#166/#183), and the independent
semiempirical-CCM audit closures; the vq root-daemon single-user refusal
(#136) is a security hardening. Every one of them carries its own
regression and passed the local T1 gate plus the release-candidate
pipeline at this exact tree; none has yet received the *independent*
broker verification of CLAUDE.md § 3 (a second, distinct agent identity)
-- each of those GitLab issues is still `opened` / `workflow::intake` at
cut time and stays open until a second agent records a PASS. The SECCM
and real-Γ direct-route entries are experimental, default-off, and outside
the release, advisory-profile, and automatic-impact test sets. The vq
fixes (#109, #125, #136, #137, #151) are fleet tooling and ride this tree so the
managed rollout can recover site_a and localhost. The tag is created only
on a green release-gate pipeline (blocking T0+T1, plus `test-vq`,
`ruff-vq`, `vibe-view-test`, `vibe-basis-test`, `docs-build`,
`ci-path-policy`). Green CI is change-safety evidence, not method
acceptance.

Sibling versions at this tag: vibe-view **2.15.1** (bumped, patch - seven
user-visible fixes: #157, #159, #179-#182, #184, #185, #193, and the terminal
spectrum chart), vq **0.25.3** (bumped, patch - #109, #125, #136, #137,
#151), vibe-basis
**0.10.0** (unchanged; no commits since v0.15.134). The vibe-view desktop
update feed is NOT published by this release (maintainer-run deploy,
vibe-view/electron/PUBLISHING.md).

### Fixed: periodic `coop_cohp=True` without QVF output fails closed (IID 195, 2026-08-21)

`run_periodic_job(..., coop_cohp=True, output_qvf=False)` used to run the SCF
to convergence and drop the request without a word: the COOP/COHP analysis
lives inside the DOS/QVF block and has no `.out` or sidecar rendering, so with
the archive off there was no `.qvf`, no bonding data, and not one COOP/COHP
line anywhere. The runner now raises `ValueError` before SCF, naming both
knobs, the way `qvf_wannier_centers=True` already did for the same
container-less case. The user guide states the refusal; the former
citation negative control is retargeted to it and a runner-level regression
pins that nothing is written under the stem.

### Security: root daemon refuses the single-user execution path (issue #136, 2026-08-21)

`vq daemon run` now refuses before client or daemon logging, pidfile creation,
web-sidecar startup, or `Daemon` construction when its effective uid is root
but the full configuration is invalid or does not explicitly set
`[multi_user] enabled = true`. Non-root single-user daemons and valid root
multi-user daemons retain their existing behavior. This removes the
configuration-driven run-as-root fallback that produced root-owned, mode-0600
site_e job artifacts.

The provisioning checker now reads the target's canonical multi-user setting
without borrowing the driver's policy and probes the root systemd unit even
when that setting is disabled or absent. An active root unit beside readable
single-user policy is an explicit unsafe contradiction; unreadable or
malformed target policy remains unknown and fails closed.

This source guard prevents recurrence. It does not choose site_e's supported
deployment model or repair the three affected legacy workspaces; those remain
an explicitly authorized operational step under issue #136.

### Fixed: vibe-view scene rebuilds preserve disabled ambient occlusion (issue #193, 2026-08-21)

The shared scene-rebuild path no longer reinstalls the SSAO render pass after
the user has switched ambient occlusion off. Representation, replication,
label, residue-selection, and element-colour changes now reattach SSAO only
when `ssao_enabled` is true, keeping renderer state aligned with the visible
switch. Regression coverage pins both the disabled path and the enabled
re-attachment control.

### Fixed: vibe-view notebook images honor their requested structure style (issue #184, 2026-08-21)

`qvf_to_image(..., style=...)` now forwards every documented structure
representation to `StructureRenderer` instead of silently rendering the
default ball-and-stick view. The public helper validates its five supported
styles before opening renderer resources, so an unknown value raises a clear
`ValueError` rather than producing an empty-structure PNG. Plumbing-level
regressions observe the renderer configuration for all supported styles.

### Fixed: vibe-view generated density notebook cells use the current volume API (issue #185, 2026-08-21)

`export_notebook_cell(..., include_density=True)` no longer emits two
concatenated statements, tuple-unpacks the summary dictionary returned by
`get_volume()`, or assumes that every archive names its density section
`vol_dens_0`. The generated cell now discovers the first `volume.density`
section by kind, uses its actual ID, reads the documented summary fields, and
prints a clear message when no density volume is present. Regressions compile
the generated source and execute both density-present and density-absent
archives against the public API.
### Fixed: χ-CCM-B restricted level-shift requests fail closed when unexecuted (IIDs 192, 194, 2026-08-21)

The experimental `aiccm2026dev-b` RHF/RI route now rejects a nonzero static
level shift or any nonzero scheduled shift on a `(1,1,1)` character mesh
before fitted backend SCF. The shared Gamma dispatcher otherwise sends a
nonzero static shift to its legacy driver without the selected RSGDF/MDF
method, cutoff, tail, or matched exchange seam; with only a scheduled shift,
the compensated PBC-GDF route runs but does not execute that schedule. The χ
wrapper could then attach `bvk-ewald` metadata to a different operator or an
unexecuted convergence request.

Restricted four-center RHF/RKS now also reject every nonempty options-level
schedule because their BIPOLE calls do not transport it into the separate
driver schedule object. This includes an all-zero schedule: the public
schedule contract supersedes a simultaneous static shift, while the old path
would execute that static value. Static four-center shifting with an empty
schedule and both static and scheduled shifting on fitted routes with at least
two characters remain available; the previous-Fock-mixing error keeps
precedence. Default D93 jobs use zero shift and are numerically unchanged. A
pre-fix Gamma RI static-shift record used the wrong route, while Gamma RI and
four-center scheduled-shift records are request-fingerprint invalid because
the schedule did not execute; all are revision-bound. Fitted and post-HF
records remain `not-qualified`, and the 3D-only SCF boundary and
analytic-total-gradient fail-close are unchanged.
### Fixed: Linux vq legacy-venv adoption recognizes the lib64 alias (IID 151, 2026-08-21)

The managed-install recovery path no longer mistakes a standard Linux
`lib64 -> lib` virtualenv alias for a second PEP 610 provenance record.
Legacy adoption still requires exactly one symlink-free metadata file from the
selected checkout; every aliased match must resolve to that same file, while
foreign, malformed, independent, and symlink-only metadata fail closed. This
restores the supported reinstall path for site_a's unmarked serving vq venv.

Full-host rollout holds also distinguish a complete scheduler-lease-only
status from an operator partial CPU/job cap. They can overlay and later release
their own full hold without changing the independent scheduler sidecar;
incomplete status, legacy lanes, and real partial policy still fail closed.
This removes the order-dependent localhost refusal from the v0.15.137 rollout.

### Fixed: remote vq fetch records fleet harvest state (IID 137, 2026-08-21)

Successful terminal workspace fetches from SSH-backed daemon hosts now update
the authoritative remote JobSpec's `last_fetched_at`, matching local and
scheduler-driver fetches. The receiver derives an exact terminal identity from
the privately staged diagnosis and non-stale workspace manifest, publishes the
tree atomically, then sends a bounded, ownership-checked acknowledgement that
re-resolves the same job generation under its spec lock. Truncated streams,
failed promotion, live snapshots, reused job IDs, stale or foreign receipts,
workdir fetches, diagnosis-free legacy helpers, and ownership failures cannot
create a fetched timestamp. A helper whose workspace protocol is too old or
malformed leaves the received tree intact but fails the fetch explicitly.

An acknowledgement failure leaves the newly fetched tree and its fresh
manifest intact but makes the command fail explicitly. `fetch-all` can retry
the idempotent acknowledgement from an exact prior terminal receipt instead of
leaving successfully harvested fleet jobs permanently unmeasurable. Focused
regressions cover the post-promotion handshake, failure and ambiguity paths,
multi-user authorization, identity races, mixed receipt states, archived
workspaces, and the local/scheduler-driver controls.

### Fixed: bare vq status resolves durable queue ownership (IID 109, 2026-08-20)

Hostless `vq status JOBID` no longer treats an unmarked remote `default_host`
as proof of ownership or recursively invokes `status` to discover a job. It
reads the configured hosts' durable queue rows, including archived specs,
matches scheduler jobs by their persisted `scheduler_target`, reads each
physical driver queue only once, collapses equivalent daemon/local aliases,
and routes the final refresh through the unique owning daemon or scheduler
driver. Local scheduler drivers need no redundant host enrollment. Explicit
`HOST JOBID` and the local-default fast path remain unchanged; multiple
matching searched owners, malformed listings, and unconfigured matching lanes
fail closed.

The release-paper campaign now keeps the permanently retired site_b host in the
known disabled inventory instead of its enabled/preferred probe set. Dashboard
queue-probe failures retain validated cached counts as visibly stale, use the
durable active-state fallback when available, and otherwise report nullable
`unknown` counts rather than a false zero. Malformed successful payloads fail
before health reporting or caching; a successful empty probe still reports
exact zero. The supervisor continues to read already-ledgered retired-host
history but rejects any new unledgered work for that host. Routing,
scheduler-lane, ambiguity, explicit-host, retired-host history/new-work,
cache/no-cache, and successful-empty controls cover the change.

### Fixed: molecular SCF oscillation detection preserves contracting DIIS tails (IID 152, 2026-08-20)

The default-on automatic level shift counted recent `dE` sign changes above a
fixed `1e-10` noise floor, with no scale or progress test. Healthy DIIS tails
therefore looked oscillatory near convergence: the detector purged a full DIIS
history and applied a persistent 0.30 Ha shift, turning qcil_03101 pyridazine
from a 16-iteration archive trajectory into a 41–42 iteration run and sending
qcil_02626/qcil_04032 to the 120-iteration ceiling. The molecular RHF/UHF/RKS/
UKS detector now ignores energy changes within two orders of the run's energy
tolerance, requires both phases of the period-two commutator envelope to be
non-contracting, and treats a DIIS-history drop as a new detector epoch.
Automatic level shift remains enabled and still engages on a sustained
oscillator; detection is skipped while a Newton/TRAH/SOSCF/quadratic step owns
the update.

Regression: `tests/test_scf_oscillation.py` replays every prefix of the exact
63-row thymine archive plus the pyridazine tail, tolerance-scale noise, and the
norbornadiene restart boundary; four negative controls fail against the old
detector and all pass after the fix. The existing no-DIIS H2O/LDA positive
control still requires automatic level shift and converges. Full current-main
replays restore pyridazine to 16 iterations, converge norbornadiene in 37
(versus >=120 broken; the separate IID 129 incremental-Fock fine-phase rebuild
accounts for the post-v0.15.47 overhead), and return thymine within 75
iterations in the archived basin (2.25 uHa from the v0.15.47 energy).
### Fixed: independent semiempirical CCM audit (issues #163-#165, #167-#178, #186-#187) (2026-08-20)

An equation-level audit against the primary CCM, SCC-DFTB, GFN2-xTB, PM6,
Parry/de Leeuw, and official tblite sources found wrong-answer paths that the
existing self-referential tests did not expose. SECCM now has exact skew-cell
Wigner-Seitz ownership and cutoff-complete pair-aware Ewald enumeration;
Peintinger Eq. 13 image weights in OMx; raw Hermiticity fail-close checks in
PM6 and OMx; exact 2-D Ewald K=0 electrostatics; consistent finite-group,
finite-temperature, and Madelung energy derivatives; and citation routing from
the kernel and temperature actually executed. The GFN2 molecular shortcut now
honors supported options, reports the actual stabilization temperature, and
shares the nontrivial path's local physical-basin heuristic and iteration
budget. Correct B1/B2 study constructors replace mislabeled synthetic MgO
fixtures for physical conclusions. The retained aligned-plane cells are
explicitly synthetic stress tests. Earlier claims that this fixture was
MgO(100), that its solver was full Newton, or that its T=0 map had no exact
fixed point are withdrawn. The default-off GFN2 stabilization and long-range
options remain experimental.

### Fixed: vibe-view served-UI accessibility baseline (issues #179-#182) (2026-08-20)

The Trame/Vuetify viewer now keeps toolbar accessible names when its custom
tooltip replaces native `title` text, names icon-only vq close controls and
the focusable VTK viewport, distinguishes all three navigation landmarks, and
announces checkpoint state transitions and general asynchronous status as
polite atomic live regions. Changing checkpoint detail and rapid per-job
refresh chips deliberately remain non-live.

### Fixed: vibe-view symmetry ignored unsaved geometry edits (issue #159) (2026-08-20)

Point-group detection preferred a separate disk-backed lazy reader even after
the molecule editor installed an in-memory geometry overlay on the active QVF
reader. It therefore classified the pre-edit archive while the viewport showed
the edited molecule. Symmetry detection now uses the active reader whenever an
edit overlay is present and retains lazy archive loading for unedited files.

### Fixed: vibe-view multi-file controllers kept the first archive's lazy reader (issue #157) (2026-08-20)

Switching files in one viewer session rebound the primary QVF reader but not
its independently opened `QVFLazyReader`. Point-group detection and the memory
report therefore kept reading file zero; the same stale wrapper survived a
live checkpoint hot-reload. Active-file reloads now replace the lazy wrapper,
panel-only watcher reloads do the same even though they deliberately skip the
full scene rebuild, and each retired wrapper closes its ZIP handle. Controller
regressions pin both file-switch and watcher paths and verify the retired
resources are closed.

### Added: diagnostic χ-CCM-B high-G RSGDF tail transport (IID 156, 2026-08-20)

The fitted χ-CCM-B RHF/RKS/UHF/UKS selectors and the high-level
`run_periodic_job(..., jk_method="aiccm2026dev-b")` surface now accept an
optional `rsgdf_tail_ke_cutoff` for RI and RIJCOSX with
`gdf_method="rsgdf"`. They require a positive finite base cutoff and a finite
complementary cutoff above it, forward the exact value to the shared
tail-consuming GDF driver, and record it as
`aiccm_resolved_rsgdf_tail_ke_cutoff`; four-center and MDF
requests fail before SCF. A Gamma-only dense-core RHF/RI request also stops
when an unset tail would activate the shared automatic production tail; the
caller must supply that cutoff explicitly or use a nontrivial character mesh.
This keeps a successful null B setting equal to no executed complementary
tail. The transport remains diagnostic only: D93 v1 campaign records still
require a null tail, all fitted routes remain quantitatively unqualified, and
χ total gradients plus all 1D/2D SCF routes remain fail-closed.

### Fixed: vq distinguishes configured-cap-impossible pending jobs (issue #125, 2026-08-20)

Ordinary local jobs whose CPU request or effective memory exceeds the daemon's
configured base caps still use the supported durable `PENDING` recovery path,
but no longer masquerade as normally queued work. `vq list` labels them
`pending (over cap)`; status labels the state, gives an explicit configured-cap
blocker, and suppresses the fictional finite dispatch-turn ETA; overview adds a
host-level `over_capacity_pending_jobs` alarm while retaining the compatible
pending count. Queue/status JSON expose `pending_over_capacity` and structured
`configured_capacity_overages`, preserving unknown/not-applicable as `null`;
the overview alarm count is also nullable when its snapshots are unavailable.
The existing `vq submit --json` acceptance receipt now includes local and
forwarded remote `capacity_warnings`, including keyed replays of still-pending
jobs, while no-flag stdout remains exactly the bare job ID. Classification
uses only base daemon caps, including `default_job_mem_mb` for undeclared
memory; scheduler lanes, current usage, drains, live RAM, and quotas are not
misclassified. Regressions cover submit/list/status/overview, replay and remote
forwarding, multi-user capacity, scheduler-lane exclusion, and web-fleet row
parity.
### Fixed: toroidal MP2 retains periodic HF routing beyond the lattice cutoff (IIDs 166, 183, 2026-08-20)

Toroidal supercells silently changed Hamiltonians when their shortest repeated
period exceeded the default 15-bohr lattice support. The Gamma GDF host then
saw only the home cell and selected its molecular-limit J/K branch: the H2 /
STO-3G `(1,1,3)` HF energy was an impossible `-2.7879828252 Ha/cell`, versus
`-1.1164536590 Ha/cell` when periodic image support was restored. Every
toroidal canonical, pair, DLPNO-MP2, CCSD, and CCSD(T) entry point now requires
the periodic Ewald-J / real-space-K branch independent of that numerical
cutoff. The repaired default gives `-1.1164515356 Ha/cell` at `(1,1,3)` and a
consistent thermodynamic-limit size trend.

The audit also withdrew two duplicate `5e-4 Ha` finite-N PySCF KMP2 assertions
instead of loosening them. They compared the legacy mixed-operator producer
(Ewald-J / real-space-K HF followed by a separately built compensated-cell DF
MP2 tensor) against PySCF's internally consistent GDF/KMP2 Hamiltonian; the
current `(1,1,2)` correlation residual is `5.8286451e-4 Ha`. Exact BvK
equivalence still holds when the Hamiltonian and gauge match: the existing
AICCM-B regression agrees with the same out-of-process KMP2 datum to
`2.34e-10 Ha/cell`. The unused scalar `+xi` helper remains available but is now
documented and tested as a mechanical orbital-energy shift, not as Nejad et
al.'s charge-projection plus surface-dipole correction. Focused regressions pin
the repaired `(1,1,3)` energy, every toroidal routing call, internal C++/Python
MP2 parity, and the corrected TDL trend.
### Fixed: incremental ΔD Fock drift-stall disengagement (IID 129, 2026-08-20)

The BUG 87 default flip (`incremental_fock = true`, v0.15.126) routed
mid-size direct SCFs through the Almlöf ΔD cache, whose accumulated
Schwarz-screen bias has a documented ~1e-7 Ha drift floor
(`benchmarks/orca_vs_vibeqc_speed.md`). Tight-tolerance runs stalled on
that floor: 14 large-aromatic Liakos S22 cases that converged at
v0.15.108 (16 iterations) failed closed with "SCF did not converge after
200 iterations" at v0.15.134. On the first stall signal the molecular
SCF drivers (RHF/UHF/RKS/UKS) now disengage the incremental cache via
`JKBuilder::set_incremental(false)`, so the fine phase runs the exact
screened full rebuild — the pre-BUG-87 map — and only a persistent
post-disengagement stall falls through to the orbital-rotation restart.
The converged energy is unchanged; the incremental path remains active
for the coarse phase and for runs that never stall. Regression:
`tests/test_incremental_fock_disengage.py` (adenine-thymine WC monomer B
/ cc-pVDZ, conv_tol_energy 1e-10; fails on the pre-fix source,
converges in ~40 iterations post-fix at the full-rebuild energy).

### Fixed: multi-k KRKS consumes `rsgdf_tail_ke_cutoff` (IID 146) (2026-08-19)

The multi-k pure-DFT (alpha = 0) dim=3 route kept the EWALD_3D
real-space J, which builds no cderi -- an explicit
`rsgdf_tail_ke_cutoff` was accepted, echoed in the `.out`, and
silently ignored: MgO/STO-3G (2,2,2) KRKS-LDA tailed (3291.6) vs
untailed was byte-identical at -271.531535367637 (15 iterations, both
runs) while the same knob on the same cell moves multi-k KRHF by
+0.505030889141 Ha. An explicit tail now routes the run to the
cached-Lpq GDF Hartree -- the same tail-consuming, method-independent
J machinery HF/hybrids (`alpha > 0` promotion) and dim<3 pure-KS
already ride; `rsgdf_tail_ke_cutoff=None` keeps the EWALD_3D default
bit-identical. A tail with `gdf_method != "rsgdf"` on the closed-shell
multi-k driver now fails closed (the `run_kuhf_periodic_gdf`
precedent) instead of being silently ignored (measured: H2 (2,1,1)
mdf + tail ran without complaint pre-fix). Post-fix measurement
(incident harness, MgO/STO-3G (2,2,2) KRKS-LDA, tail = 3291.6):
E = -270.502658896013 Ha (converged, 15 it, 593 s vs 4848 s pre-fix)
vs external PySCF -270.4990190962 -- the P13 dense-core multi-k KRKS
offset closes from -1.0325 Ha to -3.64 mHa, i.e. it was essentially
all tail (mechanism confirmation for the #142 collapse family; the
-3.64 mHa residual is the remaining quantity for its severity ladder).
Regression: `tests/test_periodic_k_gdf.py` -- route-consumption
sentinels on both J machineries (tailed run must reach the rsgdf
cderi build carrying the caller's tail; untailed run must keep the
EWALD_3D routing), non-rsgdf fail-closed, and a `@slow` dense-core
gate running the cheap tail=800 rung (measured -270.545807077311,
8 it): the tailed (2,2,2) energy must land within 0.1 Ha of the
PySCF reference (2.1x the measured -46.8 mHa residual at that tail,
10x below the pre-fix offset) and at least 0.5 Ha off the untailed
fixed point (pre-fix: exactly 0.0). Docs:
`docs/user_guide/periodic_methods.md` GDF dense-core note + the
driver docstring.

### Fixed: ROHF/ROKS EDIIS coupling projected with the wrong density (2026-08-19)

The Roothaan loop coupled the EDIIS/ADIIS-extrapolated Fock pair, which
is `F(D_tilde)` with `D_tilde = sum_i c_i D_i` over the history hull, to
the Roothaan projector of the *current* density instead of `D_tilde`'s.
The damped first DIIS step made the two densities differ enough that the
mismatched effective Fock jumped the SCF into an excited stationary point
that was reported as converged: NH2 radical ROHF/STO-3G landed 68.8 mHa
above the PySCF 2.14 ground-state reference with `converged=true` (the
fleet row mf003/ml003s measured +95 mHa against ORCA, which v0.15.28
reproduced to 9.8e-09). The loop now reconstructs `D_tilde` from the
accelerator's `last_coeffs()` plus a mirrored density history and builds
the effective Fock with `D_tilde`'s projectors (exact at the HF level,
since J and K are linear in the density). Pinned by
tests/test_rohf.py
(`test_rohf_nh2_sto3g_default_options_land_in_ground_basin`, always-on,
absolute-energy pin) and by NH2 joining the PySCF parity parametrisation;
the FeCl3 def2-SVP/def2-TZVP convergence-control suite stays green
(`tests/test_rohf_convergence_controls.py`, 21/21). Issue #119.

### Fixed: vibe-view terminal spectrum chart labelled eV data "nm" and broadened it with a cm⁻¹-scale width (2026-08-20)

`vibe-view show --plain` (and the TUI chart pane) guessed the spectrum
X-unit from the data magnitude, so every eV-valued `spectra.uvvis`
section was plotted in eV but labelled "Frequency (nm)", and
`spectra.ecd` fell through to the cm⁻¹ default; the Lorentzian envelope
floor was a cm⁻¹-scale constant (4.0), which on a 4–10 eV UV-Vis
spectrum drew a γ=4 eV blob spanning −8..22 eV. The terminal
`spectra_plot` now resolves axis label, unit, and broadening floor from
the same per-kind style registry as the Plotly/matplotlib renderers
(`Energy (eV)` for uvvis/ecd, `Frequency (cm⁻¹)` for ir/vcd,
`Raman shift (cm⁻¹)` for raman; γ floored at 0.1 eV electronic /
5 cm⁻¹ vibrational), and the envelope legend names the width's unit.
Browser/PNG/CSV renderers were already correct and are unchanged.
Pinned by `vibe-view/tests/test_tui.py`
(`test_spectra_plot_axis_label_follows_the_kind`, parametrized over the
five spectra kinds with a lockstep assertion against the renderer
registry, and `test_uvvis_terminal_envelope_is_not_cm1_broad`).
Tracked as project-19 issue #153.

### Added (EXPERIMENTAL): geometry relaxation on the real-Γ direct-torus route (2026-08-20)

`run_ccm_direct_optimize`: unit-cell atomic relaxation (fixed lattice) on
the direct-torus surface — the adsorption-goal capability the 2c forces
unblocked. Steps ride the multi-k GDF control objective (scipy L-BFGS-B
on fractional coordinates, the runner's G-PBC-002 relaxer pattern:
non-convergence penalty barrier + independent gradient gate), with the
direct-vs-control parity premise fully verified at the initial AND final
geometries (`parity_check="endpoints"`, default — production cost, no
fold build per step) or at every step (`"every-step"`, validation runs).
Measured: compact H₂ (2,1,1) relaxes 1.6 → 1.474 bohr in 4 steps, final
max|grad| 2.1e-5 Ha/bohr, endpoint parities 1.3e-13. Scope inherits
`run_ccm_direct_gradient` (3-D, ewald, pure + global hybrids, closed
shell + UHF; screened/double hybrids and open-shell KS fail closed at
the initial parity check). Gates in `tests/test_ccm_direct_gradient.py`.

### Added (EXPERIMENTAL): GFN2-xTB-SECCM channel-isolation knobs for the checkerboard over-polarization (IID 150, 2026-08-19/20)

Default-off validation knobs on the GFN2-xTB-SECCM adapter used to pin
the rocksalt(100) checkerboard over-polarization (GitLab #150):
`ewald_gamma_molecular_onsite` (restore the molecular on-site block in the
periodic shell gamma), `ewald_gamma_no_k0` (skip the per-pair Parry/Heyes
k0 term), `madelung_s_weighted`, and `madelung_no_self` (f27f9d655,
78f46da71). The k0 channel isolated the root cause (the pair-form k0
collapses the transient in-plane Jacobian couplings); the `ewald_gamma_k0_global`
rank-1 dipole form (5d70dfb38) was superseded in the same cycle by the exact
pairwise Parry/de Leeuw K=0 kernel of the independent audit below and is
retained as a compatibility no-op. The shipped default path is unchanged
bit-for-bit; every knob is a modified validation Hamiltonian, not a production
kernel. Pinned in `tests/test_ccm_semiempirical.py`. #150 itself stays open.

### Fixed: solvated runs report the in-solvent total as their headline energy

GitLab #148: for a CPCM job the SCF banner and the 'Total energy' row
printed the inner SCF's E_SCF^{w/V_q} (neither the gas-phase nor the
in-solvent total; 23-42 mHa from the run's own in-solvent value), and
the 'Solvation energy' line did not equal in-solvent minus gas-phase.
The banner value poisoned any downstream harvest of ``energy_ha`` (the
v0.15.28 mb075/mf075/ml075* family compared a non-in-solvent number
against ORCA's in-solvent FINAL SINGLE POINT ENERGY). Now:
``result.energy`` of a solvated run IS the in-solvent total (every
consumer -- banner, verdict line, .xyz comment, progress / structured
log, ASE -- harvests the same headline), the components-table row is
labelled 'In-solvent total', and the solvation block decomposes it
exactly: electrostatic 1/2 q.V_tot plus the total shift
(in-solvent - gas-phase, solute polarisation shown explicitly). Pinned
by `tests/test_solvation_cpcm.py::test_iid148_run_job_energy_is_in_solvent_total`.

## [v0.15.137] - 2026-08-19 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Fixed: vibe-view branding version test patched the superseded gate (2026-08-19)

`test_branding_refreshes_vibe_view_version` monkeypatched
`platform.system` while `brand_macos_app` now gates on `sys.platform`
(the 7e565c3c8 fix), so on the Linux CI image branding early-returned and
the synthetic plist never received the version keys the test reads
(`KeyError: CFBundleShortVersionString`). The test now patches
`sys.platform` like the `mac_installer` fixture; verified by simulating
the Linux condition locally (branding runs and writes the keys).

### Fixed: CMake build-graph guard scans only the tracked tree (2026-08-19)

`tests/test_cmake_sources_exist.py` discovered CMakeLists files with a
filesystem glob, so a shared clone carrying other agents' registered git
worktrees scanned those older snapshots as if they were this tree's
build graph and failed on files that exist only in the current tree.
Discovery is now scoped to `git ls-files` (glob fallback when git is
unavailable); the guard's contract - the tracked build graph - is
unchanged.

### Fixed: binary-kind `--program` jobs get the validated executable path (2026-08-19)

A job submitted with `--program orca` (a `kind = "binary"` program)
received `VQ_PROGRAM=orca` but no path variable, and inherited a PATH
(`/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin`) that cannot find the validated wrapper, so a
20-deck ORCA bundle died rc 127 against a healthy recipe. Local daemon
dispatch now exports `VQ_PROGRAM_EXE` (the validated executable) for
binary programs, so payloads can `exec "$VQ_PROGRAM_EXE"` with no
host-conditional path logic; scheduler jobs still receive no
driver-local paths. Pinned by `vibe-queue/tests/test_daemon.py`
(`test_local_dispatch_exports_binary_program_path`) and
`vibe-queue/tests/test_daemon_scheduler.py`
(`test_start_scheduler_job_omits_driver_local_binary_program_path`);
`vibe-queue/docs/SPEC.md` and `vibe-queue/docs/operations.md` record the
contract. Issue #126.

### Fixed: vibe-view Open With branding gate used `platform.system()` (2026-08-19)

`vibe-view/electron/install-electron.py` `brand_macos_app` guarded on
`platform.system()` while the `mac_installer` test fixture (and every
sibling desktop-app function) gates on `sys.platform`. On the Linux
`vibe-view-test` CI image the branding therefore early-returned, the
plist never received `CFBundleDocumentTypes` /
`UTImportedTypeDeclarations`, and
`test_install_electron.py::test_branded_app_declares_document_types_for_open_with`
failed, blocking the cut. The guard now reads `sys.platform != "darwin"`
like `install_desktop_app` / `pin_to_dock`; production macOS behavior is
unchanged and the document-type declarations are exercised on Linux CI.

### Added (EXPERIMENTAL): analytic forces on the real-Γ direct-torus route (2026-08-19)

`run_ccm_direct_gradient` (milestone 2c of the real-Γ line): forces for
the direct-torus control via the route's Fourier-representation identity
composed with the production multi-k rsgdf analytic gradient
(`compute_gradient=True`, public 2026-07-30) — no duplicate fit-derivative
machinery. The same-Hamiltonian premise is **verified per run** by an
energy-parity gate (`parity_tol`, default 1e-6 Ha/cell): runs in the
documented ~1e-4 supercell-fit residual class fail closed instead of
