returning forces of a slightly different Hamiltonian. Measured vs central
FD of the DIRECT energies: RHF 5.6e-9, UHF (genuine triplet) 6.8e-7,
KS-PBE/PBE0 ~1e-4 (the upstream KS gradient's own documented XC-grid
floor). Scope: 3-D, `exxdiv="ewald"`, pure + global hybrids, closed and
open shell **HF**; screened/double hybrids and strict-zero fail closed.
Gates: `tests/test_ccm_direct_gradient.py` (manual research lanes).

**Flagged upstream (GDF lane, not absorbed): the multi-k KUKS analytic
gradient fails FD against its own energy** by 3.7e-3 Ha/bohr on a genuine
open-shell state (triplet LiH/STO-3G, dominant force 0.045 Ha/bohr; KUHF
passes 6.8e-7 on the same fixture — the defect is in the spin-resolved XC
gradient piece, invisible to the upstream suite's m=1-collapse-only KUKS
validation). Open-shell KS forces fail closed here with a pointer; canary
`test_upstream_kuks_gradient_fd_defect_still_present` flips when the fix
lands. Also fixed in the same merge: the open-shell CCM GDF wrappers
(`run_ccm_uhf_gdf`/`run_ccm_uks_gdf`) never recorded
`exchange_q0`/`exchange_q0_applicability`; they now mirror `_ccm_gdf`.

### Added: GFN2-xTB-SECCM self-consistent periodic shell gamma (ewald_gamma)

The GFN2-xTB-SECCM adapter gains an opt-in `ewald_gamma=True` kernel option
(2-D and 3-D, mutually exclusive with `madelung`) that replaces the
WS-truncated Klopman-Ohno shell gamma with the tblite `get_amat_3d`
construction: the full Ewald Coulomb kernel (3-D Ewald, or the 2-D
Parry/Heyes Ewald of the validated `indo::_madkonst_2d` machinery) plus
the Wigner-Seitz folded Klopman-Ohno-minus-Coulomb correction plus the
molecular on-site hardness.
The raw lattice-summed KO kernel is IR-ill-defined for multi-element cells
(its `eta^2/(2 R^3)` tail diverges logarithmically per image sum, and with
pair-dependent hardness the charge-weighted leading term does not cancel);
the WS weights are the convergent truncation, exactly as in tblite, and
the eta-to-zero off-diagonal limit anchors to the bare-Coulomb Ewald
kernel. Design and validation: `docs/design_seccm_gfn2_long_range_gamma.md`.

On the bulk-3D ladder the kernel converges corundum in ~180 iterations
(previously runaway) with Mulliken charges at the xtb scale (q_rms 0.369
vs xtb 0.41) and keeps MgO 2x2x2 at xtb-scale charges (0.40-0.44 vs
0.39-0.41) with the energy tracking xtb's Gamma-only curve shape at a
constant offset of about -88 mHa/atom (the WS-folded H0/AES/repulsion
channels, not the kernel). In 2-D the 2-layer MgO(100) slab converges
through the Parry/Heyes kernel and matches the `madelung=True` embedding
construction on the same cell; 4+ layer slabs still fail closed. The
4-layer cycle mechanism is pinned: a bit-identical Python reconstruction
of the SCC map shows the fixed point (reached by damped Newton) carries
a Jacobian eigenvalue of -221 from the near-degenerate 4-layer H0
frontier - a repeller the cycle orbits - while the 2-layer fixed point
is stable. Broyden and DIIS are opt-in via `scc_mixer` but do NOT
converge the slab as wired (Broyden's unbounded quasi-Newton step blows
up the eigensolver at iter 58); the line-searched Newton mixer below
converges it. The adapter also gains an
experimental `include_aes=False` validation knob (removes the WS-folded
anisotropic second-order channel for SCC instability isolation; not a
production route) and exposes the per-iteration `scc_max_change_trace`
on the result for convergence diagnostics. fcc Cu 2x2x2 now reaches a charge-density-wave
basin whose signature the shipped shell-rms gate missed; the physical-basin
gate gains an absolute atomic-rms bound (2.0 e) so that basin fails closed
(IID 130). The 3-D and 2-D kernels are pinned element-wise against Python
reimplementations through `cyclic_scc_energy`, plus the eta-to-zero
anchors, the option-surface guards, the slab cross-construction parity,
and the Cu/slab fail-closed regressions in
`tests/test_ccm_semiempirical.py`.

### Added: line-searched Newton SCC mixer for GFN2-xTB-SECCM (scc_mixer="newton")

The GFN2-xTB-SECCM SCC loop gains an opt-in `scc_mixer="newton"`
charge mixer: a line-searched full-Newton step on the charge-map fixed
point. The inlined SCC map is factored into a shared
`gfn2_seccm_charge_map` helper (the loop, the finite-difference
Jacobian, and the line search share the same arithmetic bit-for-bit,
mirroring the SCC-DFTB-SECCM `scc_seccm_charge_map` pattern), and each
iteration solves the plain Newton system (J - I) x = residual with a
forward-difference Jacobian (delta 1e-4, lagged shell moments frozen),
a trust-region cap on the step (0.5 e), and the probe's
residual-reduction line search, falling back to damped simple mixing
when no trial reduces the residual. The zero-sum property of the step
follows from the solve itself (the map conserves charge) with roundoff
cleanup.

Two findings from the 4-layer MgO(100) slab (IID 141): the probe's
~60-step Newton convergence was on the GAM3-free bare map (the C++ core
reproduces it in 12-15 iterations), and the production T=0 map has NO
exact fixed point - the near-degenerate 4-layer frontier makes the
T=0 Aufbau occupation switch branches, a discontinuity every solver
plateaus at (damped Newton, warm starts, Levenberg-Marquardt, a GAM3
homotopy: all stall at a ~0.24 e residual). A small Fermi temperature
smooths the occupation (the same mechanism the molecular driver's
stabilization ladder uses) and `scc_mixer="newton"` +
`electronic_temperature=0.002` converges the 4-layer slab in 6
iterations: energy -9.11722295 Ha/prim cell (pinned by regression),
Mulliken q_rms 0.429, the repeller's alternating-layer charge pattern,
physical basin satisfied. The 2-layer slab converges under Newton at
T=0 in 8 iterations to the same fixed point as shipped simple mixing
(energy diff 3.8e-10, charges to 1e-6, 115 -> 8 iterations). The T=0
default path is unchanged bit-for-bit. Regressions:
`test_gfn2_seccm_ewald_gamma_4layer_slab_newton_converges`,
`test_gfn2_seccm_ewald_gamma_2layer_slab_newton_matches_simple`, and
the `scc_mixer` option-surface update.

### Open-shell initial-guess spin symmetry: BS-set evidence + regression pins

The spin-averaged spin-balanced guess (a2e190e46, issue 19) is confirmed
NOT to regress the broken-symmetry singlet class: default runs reach the
same solutions before and after the fix on H2 past the Coulson-Fischer
point, ozone, twisted ethylene, and p-benzyne, because the default-on
stability escape (Seeger-Pople 1977 / Lehtola 2020) carries the descent
from the symmetric saddle. Regression pins for the class land in
`tests/test_guess.py`; the guess policy is documented in
`docs/user_guide/initial_guess.md` and
`handovers/HANDOVER_GUESS_SPIN_SYMMETRY.md`. The Cr2 escape gap (no
descent from a deeply unstable symmetric saddle) is tracked as GitLab
issue 138.

### Fixed: run_job(aux_basis=) now reaches every correlated route

`run_job(aux_basis=...)` used to wire the kwarg onto the SCF options only,
so the DLPNO-MP2 / DLPNO-CCSD routes silently auto-resolved their own RI
basis and the DF-CCSD / LCCSD family ignored the kwarg outright -- an
explicit user request was dropped (GitLab #113). The kwarg now selects the
correlation auxiliary on all four routes (with the route options object as
a fallback and orbital-basis auto-resolution last), a kwarg that
contradicts the route options raises instead of letting one silently win,
and an unresolvable name fails loudly at basis construction. Pinned by
`tests/test_runner_ccsd.py` (kwarg reaches DF-CCSD + LCCSD, sto-3g +
explicit aux passes the fail-early gate, conflict + unresolvable raise),
`tests/test_runner_dlpno_mp2.py` and `tests/test_runner_dlpno_ccsd.py`
(kwarg echoes in the .out, conflict raises).

### Fixed: selected-CI starved spaces are no longer labelled converged

A fixed ``pt2_threshold`` could empty the candidate pool far below
``target_size`` (N2/cc-pVDZ CAS(6e,6o) under defaults saturated at
ndet=6 for every target from 6 to 400, bit-identical energies,
``converged=True`` at every rung). ``SelectedCISolver.solve`` now
relaxes the selection threshold stepwise when the pool starves below
target, so the space keeps growing toward the requested size, and every
result carries a ``stop_reason`` (``"energy"`` / ``"target_size"`` /
``"space_exhausted"`` / ``"max_iter"``) that is printed in the .out
header, so an exhausted space is distinguishable from an
energy-converged run. GitLab #107; pinned by
`tests/test_solvers_selected_ci.py`.

### Fixed: auto-ECP regression now pins the valence electron count

GitLab #143: the archived H2S RHF/LANL2DZ rows landed -89.637 Ha
(78.6 Ha from the matched ORCA valence-only leg) because the ECP was
never attached on those pre-fix releases. The attach defect itself
landed as 0247a07e3; the regression gap is now closed:
`tests/test_ecp_scf.py` asserts that an auto-ECP run treats exactly the
valence electrons (tr(D . S) = 8 for H2S, not the physical 18) and
pins the valence-only energy scale, so an all-electron misapplication
cannot pass silently.

### vibe-view: install-time Dock pin and PATH command link

`vibe-view/scripts/install.sh` gains `--dock` (pin the source-backed macOS
app to the Dock, requires `--with-electron`), `--link-bin DIR` (a marked
`vibe-view` launcher in an existing writable PATH directory), and
`--adopt-desktop` (take over a source app from another checkout).
`uninstall.sh` removes the command link with the environment and unpins the
Dock tile with the app; `--dry-run` previews both. Documented in
`docs/user_guide/vibe_view_desktop.md`, `docs/toolset_lifecycle.md`, the
viewer-only tutorial, and `vibe-view/README.md`.

### Fixed: vibe-view New structure failed on Dock launches (EROFS)

A double-clicked desktop app has no launcher handshake, so the Electron
shell served `process.cwd()` — `/` on macOS Dock/Finder launches — and the
➕ New structure button tried to write `/new-structure.qvf` into the
read-only filesystem root (HTTP 500, EROFS). The desktop shell now falls
back to the home directory when the launch cwd is the filesystem root, and
the browse page marks the action "read-only" (with a 403 from `/new`) in
any non-writable folder instead of failing after the click. Pinned by
`vibe-view/tests/test_serve.py` and `vibe-view/tests/test_electron_onboarding.py`.

### vibe-view: open vibe-qc .py inputs everywhere (2026-08-18)

A .py input from the qc-input-library (periodic `build_system()` style)
opened with no structure: the parser only understood literal
`Molecule([Atom(...)])` / `PeriodicSystem(...)` constructors, so the
library's fractional-coordinate builder resolved to zero atoms.
`vibe-view/src/vibeview/input_parser.py` now carries a restricted AST
evaluator (literals only — never executes input code) that resolves the
library skeleton: `_LATTICE_A` (Å rows) × BOHR, `.T.copy()`, and the
`vq.Atom(int(z), (np.asarray(f) @ lattice_a).tolist()) for z, f in _ATOMS`
comprehension, plus `run_*` runner kwargs and the `_BASIS` / `_METHOD` /
`_FUNCTIONAL` module constants. The branded macOS app declares every
importable format (`.py`, `.qvf`, xyz/cif/cube/pdb/mol2/sdf/mol/gjf/com/gro)
in `CFBundleDocumentTypes` at Alternate rank, so Finder's right-click →
Open With lists vibe-view for .py inputs and structure files without
stealing the default Python handler; the electron-builder
`fileAssociations` mirror it for packaged builds. The open-file loading
page now says the first open can take up to a minute instead of "a few
seconds". Pinned by `vibe-view/tests/test_integration_v2.py` (library
builder + no-exec guarantee) and `vibe-view/tests/test_install_electron.py`
(document-type branding). Validated against 400 sampled qc-input-library
inputs: all parse with atoms.

### vibe-view: IUPAC name detection for .py inputs and standalone installs

The sidebar name header skipped in-memory readers, so a converted .py
input never showed a chemical name; and the standalone viewer
environment could not import the pure-Python `vibeqc_naming` engine at
all (the vibe-view wheel does not ship it). `_iupac_name_entry` now
names pathless readers from their structure atoms (the slab/lattice
route, with a fallback to the structure route for bulk crystals, e.g.
"octac" for diamond), and the installer writes a
`vibe-view-repo-python.pth` into the viewer environment pointing at the
checkout's `python/` directory, exactly the condition
`_naming_available()` already expects. Pinned by
`vibe-view/tests/test_iupac_name.py` and
`vibe-view/tests/test_setup_scripts.py`; documented in
`docs/user_guide/vibe_view.md`.

### Fixed: bugctl broker stale listing falsed on fresh claims (2026-08-18)

`GET /v1/stale` applied the `BROKER_STALE_HOURS` cutoff only to the
`PROGRESS`-event subquery, never to the grant's own age, so every
progress-less active grant was reported stale the moment it was claimed
(a triage lane nearly released a 10.3-hour-old live lease as a result).
A fresh grant must now itself be older than the cutoff before it is
listed, matching BUG_POLICY § 3's 72-hour contract. Pinned by
`tests/test_bugctl_broker.py` (`test_fresh_grant_is_not_stale`, and
`test_progress_records_and_stale_detection` back-dates its progress-less
grant past the cutoff). Issue #105.

## [v0.15.136] - 2026-08-18 - *Neese's Cheetah*

**Verification status, stated honestly.** This release ships four
GFN2-xTB-SECCM features (Madelung/Ewald embedding, the physical-basin
gate, finite electronic temperature, and the CP-SCC analytic gradient)
as opt-in, test-backed work. SECCM remains experimental:
`scientific_acceptance` is false for every lane, and the area stays out
of the release, advisory-profile, and automatic-impact test sets. The
over-polarized bulk-metal basin that motivated the gate remains open as
GitLab issue 130; the gate fails those runs closed instead of returning
the spurious state. Defaults are unchanged (`madelung=False`,
`electronic_temperature=0`), so every existing invocation keeps its
behaviour, and the tag is created only on a green release-gate pipeline
(blocking T0+T1, plus `test-vq`, `ruff-vq`, `vibe-view-test`,
`vibe-basis-test`, `docs-build`, `ci-path-policy`) at this exact tree.
Green CI is change-safety evidence, not method acceptance.

Sibling versions at this tag: vq **0.25.2** (unchanged; only the
v0.15.135 fleet report landed under `vibe-queue/` since that tag),
vibe-view 2.14.1 (unchanged), vibe-basis 0.10.0 (unchanged).

### Added: opt-in Madelung/Ewald embedding for GFN2-xTB-SECCM (2026-08-18)

`run_gfn2_seccm(..., madelung=True)` restores the Coulombic image-sum
tail beyond the Wigner-Seitz cell for neutral ionic cells: the Madelung
potential of the supercell atomic Mulliken fluctuations joins the H
diagonal (MSINDO CCM convention F_add(k,k) = -V_mad) and its classical
self-energy 1/2 dq . V_mad joins the total energy (`e_madelung` /
`cyclic_madelung_energy`), with the SMADEL
short-range subtraction and the same shared kernels the SCC-DFTB-SECCM
adapter uses (1-D background-corrected wire Ewald, 2-D Parry/Heyes,
3-D Ewald). The unembedded 2x2x2 MgO curve decreases monotonically to
below 3.9 A; embedded it has a minimum near 4.30 A (+2% vs experiment)
and Mulliken charges matching the xtb scale (q_rms 0.39 vs xtb 0.41).
The physical-basin gate now uses the absolute shell-rms bound alone:
the embedded map's charge-separated metal basin (fcc Cu compressed,
shell rms 3.8 e with atomic rms 3.3 e) passes the old atomic-mismatch
ratio, so the ratio condition is dropped.

### Added: physical-basin gate for GFN2-xTB-SECCM bulk metals (2026-08-18)

`run_gfn2_seccm` can no longer return the over-polarized intra-atomic
shell-transfer SCC fixed point that bulk-metal supercells visit at
compressed volumes (fcc Cu 2x2x2 at a = 3.434 A: shell dq rms 4.8 e with
near-zero atomic charges, a full p shell against a depleted d shell; the
per-cell energy error against the sane branch is about 2 Ha). A converged
state whose shell populations leave the Pauli bounds, or whose shell-charge
rms exceeds 2.5 e while the atomic-charge rms stays below a quarter of it,
is classified unphysical: the stabilization ladder searches for the physical
basin, and if none is found the run fails closed with a basin-specific
error. The sane 2x2x2 fcc Cu fixed point at the experimental lattice
constant is pinned as a regression, and the result now exposes
`shell_charges` (per-shell Mulliken dq, supercell shell order) and
`physical_basin`. Tracked under GitLab issue 130.

### Added: opt-in finite electronic temperature for GFN2-xTB-SECCM (2026-08-17)

`run_gfn2_seccm(..., electronic_temperature=...)` (Ha, default 0 = hard
Aufbau) applies Fermi-Dirac occupations through the shared k-point
occupation kernel. Metallic supercells (bulk Cu/Pd/Ag) have a degenerate
frontier whose T = 0 occupation switches branches between neighbouring
geometries; a small temperature (0.002-0.01 Ha) converges branch-free and
the reported energy is the Mermin free energy A = E - T*S (`free_energy`
alias, with `entropy` and `smearing_temperature` recorded). The insulating
positive-gap gate is skipped for smeared runs.

### Added: CP-SCC charge response for the embedded SCC-DFTB-SECCM analytic gradient (2026-08-17)

Embedded cells (`run_scc_dftb_seccm(..., madelung=True, compute_gradient=True)`)
now return the analytic coupled-perturbed SCC gradient
(`gradient_method="analytic_cpscc"`) instead of failing over to central
differences. The diagonal Madelung shift leaves the SCC fixed point
non-stationary in the Mulliken charges (the shift is the orthogonal-basis
diagonal form while the Mulliken response is S-weighted), so the exact force
adds, on top of the fixed-charge terms:

- the Madelung derivative 1/2 dq . dM/dR . dq: the 1-D wire-Ewald kernel
gets an additive derivative helper in `cpp/src/semiempirical/seccm/ewald_1d.h`
(validated against central differences of the kernel itself); 2-D/3-D reuse
the validated `indo::_add_madelung_gradient` deposit;
- the V_mad . (dt/dR) correction to the Elstner fixed-charge machinery
(its derivation assumes the gamma-only ground state; t is the per-atom
orthogonal-basis density trace);
- the charge response: J . (ddq/dR) = d(dq_new)/dR with
J = I - d(dq_new)/ddq built by central differences of the charge map (the
SCF loop and the response now share one factored map helper, so the
arithmetic is bit-for-bit; convergence regressions pin it), solved with the
charge-conserving uniform mode pinned, contracted with V_mad + B^T V_mad
(the gamma-channel terms cancel exactly via J . x = b).

For smeared runs the fixed-charge energy-weighted density now uses the
Fermi-Dirac occupations (recomputed through the same kernel as the SCF
loop); the occupation response itself is absorbed by Mermin stationarity.
The N=3 smeared chain and the N=2 zero-temperature chain (81 DIIS
iterations) match re-converged finite differences to ~1e-7 Ha/bohr, and the
sum of forces vanishes to 1e-6.

**Verification status, stated honestly.** This release ships several

* **Slab `V_ne(k)` wrong at every k != 0** (`0877fd800`, issue #106,

  sum, so 2D routes converged to wrong energies without a symptom.

Each of the above carries its own regressions, and the tag is created
only on a green release-gate pipeline (blocking T0+T1, plus `test-vq`,
`ruff-vq`, `vibe-view-test`, `vibe-basis-test`, `docs-build`,
`ci-path-policy`) at this exact tree. Green CI is change-safety
evidence; it is not the independent verification the bug policy
requires, and this note is not a claim that it substitutes.

For completeness: **P2b** (slab-GDF gap unclamp + one-global-Fermi

Sibling versions at this tag: vq **0.25.2** (bumped — `32c97ac91` is
user-visible vq work), vibe-view 2.14.1 (unchanged, no commits since

### Fixed: `vq` remote reads no longer fail silently (issues #111, #114, #118, 2026-08-17)

Three defects made a *failed or stale remote read look like a successful
one*, and `vq fetch` results-presence is the validation loop's mandated
terminal-detection method (LEARNINGS L37) precisely because scheduler state
is unreliable — so all three degraded the one signal that was supposed to be
trustworthy, in the same direction, without a symptom. Measured cost on the
rp218 canary: a false "hung" verdict on a converged run, ~7.7 h of a watcher
reading a frozen file, and a 28-row poll that reported completion after
reading one row.

- **`vq fetch` now refreshes a populated destination (#114, #111).** A fetch
  into a directory already holding a previous fetch of the same job returned
  that directory untouched and printed `fetched -> ...` (`fetch.py`'s
  same-job idempotency short-circuit, in both the local copy and the remote
  streaming path). It now re-copies / re-streams and replaces the previous
  snapshot through a staging directory, so the destination always holds the
  current bytes and files deleted at the source disappear. `vq fetch-all`
  keeps its skip-if-present sweep semantics (it passes `idempotent=False`)
  and still reports each skip explicitly. An unrelated, unmarked, symlinked,
  or foreign-job destination is still a hard collision.
- **A fetch that cannot refresh now marks the tree (#111).** Transport
  failures already exited non-zero, but the previous snapshot stayed on disk
  with no signal for whatever process reads it next. Every fetched tree now
  carries `_vq/fetch-manifest.json` (`vq.fetch-manifest.v1`) recording
  `fetched_at`, source host, source kind, and transport; a failed refresh
  stamps `stale: true` plus `refresh_error` on the existing tree before the
  error propagates. `vq fetch` reports `fetched_at` on its human line and
  `fetched_at` / `stale` in `--json`, so a consumer can age-check the payload
  without trusting the CLI.
- **No vq subprocess inherits the caller's stdin (#118).** `ssh` reads stdin
  greedily and forwards it, so `while read id; do vq status …; done < list.tsv`
  processed the first row and exited 0. The transport layer now passes
  `stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL` (unless a call explicitly pipes `stdin_data`),
  and the audit was applied across the whole CLI surface: 58 further
  `subprocess` call sites in `src/vq` were made explicit, and the five
  indirect ones route through a helper or `setdefault`.
- **Fourth instance of the same class, found by the audit and fixed.**
  `SchedulerDispatcher.tail_file` returned `""` for *every* non-zero remote
  `tail`, so a failed read was indistinguishable from an empty file —
  `vq progress` rendered it as
  `(no .scf.jsonl — structured log not enabled)` and exited 0. Only a
  genuinely absent file yields `""` now; any other failure raises
  `SchedulerError`, which every caller already surfaces.

Regressions: `tests/test_fetch_freshness.py` (14 tests — refresh, manifest,
stale-marking; 12 fail against the pre-fix tree) and
`tests/test_stdin_isolation.py` (9 tests — a real `while read` loop over an
8-row file against a stdin-draining fake `ssh`, which processed 1 of 8 rows
pre-fix, plus an AST guard over `src/vq`). Three tests in
`tests/test_fetch.py` that pinned the old keep-the-stale-copy contract were
inverted with the rationale in place. Docs:
`vibe-queue/docs/agent_interaction.md` gains the fetch-freshness contract and
a stdin note. `test-vq` lane green locally.
FN2-xTB geometry optimizations converge again (GFN2-GEOMOPT, IID 76, 2026-08-15)

The paper-core `GeometryOptimization` rows (CH3OH, CH4, CO2, H2CO, H2O,
HCOOH, NH3, PH3, SiH4) stalled at v0.15.130: ASE BFGS reported a final
max force of 0.26 eV/A with a 6.8e-11 A last displacement - the
signature of an analytic gradient inconsistent with the energy surface
the optimizer minimizes.  The gradient carried the BUG-022 -1/2 S(v+v')
M-matrix sign, fixed by the GFN2-GRADIENT-FD-RESIDUAL work
(`5f4f8d9fa`); with the restored +1/2 convention the optimizer and the
energy walk the same surface.  All nine rows converge on current main
at the paper's fmax = 0.01 eV/A within the 500-step budget (standard
near-equilibrium starts; H2O in ~10 s).  Regression:
`TestGFN2PESGate::test_h2o_geometry_optimization_converges_within_budget`.
The PES-shape xfails the issue listed were already removed with the
E_rep restore and the (n,l) basis fix; the water O-H scan minimum
(1.70-1.95 bohr) is pinned by `test_water_pes_has_minimum_near_equilibrium`.

### Added: multi-replica GFN2-xTB-SECCM adapter (WS-weighted supercell SCC) (2026-08-15)

`run_gfn2_seccm` is now the full WS-weighted supercell engine, not the
molecular-limit slice. The supercell Hamiltonian is the molecular GFN2-xTB
machinery evaluated over the frozen WS record set (the
Bredow-Geudtner-Jug construction shared with PM6/OMx/SCC-DFTB SECCM):

- S and H0: one-center blocks are the molecular ones; every directed
two-center H0 block is `build_gfn2_hamiltonian_zero_image` at the record
displacement, accumulated with its fractional WS weight. The image blocks
keep the H(g) = H(-g)^T nonsymmetric convention of the Gamma-periodic
driver; the validated reverse-image topology reassembles symmetric matrices
(checked at 1e-10).
- Shell gamma: the same-atom block is the molecular one; every other atom
contributes through its WS records at the record distances.
- AES: the molecular driver's shipped default path (ad-hoc shell-resolved
gamma^n multipole potential) accumulated over the records with their
fractional weights. The pair-additive AES has no three-center terms, so the
Peintinger-Bredow eq-13 union construction reduces to the plain two-center
record weight. The experimental atom-resolved faithful AES is not ported.
- GAM3 third order plus the WS-weighted pair repulsion complete the
functional; per-cell fields are the finite-cluster totals divided by the
group order, with `total_cyclic_energy` and the `cyclic_*` decomposition
exposed like SCC-DFTB-SECCM.
- The SCC loop mirrors `run_gfn2_xtb` (damped simple mixing, the same
stabilization retry ladder, the same energy decomposition); D4 dispersion
stays out.

The molecular limit (1x1x1 cyclic cluster) still delegates to the validated
molecular driver `xtb::run_gfn2_xtb` bit-for-bit. New tests pin 1-D chain
translation invariance and per-cell normalization (2 and 3 H2O cells), 2-D
square-lattice axis-swap invariance, the charged/open-shell fail-closed
gate, and the extended molecular-limit component parity.

### Added: Mermin finite-temperature free-energy smearing (2026-08-15)

`smearing_method="mermin"` (with `"meremin"` accepted as a spelling alias)
is now a first-class smearing flavour, previously a deliberate scope deferral
under G-PBC-006. The Mermin free-energy functional `A = E - T·S` is the
correct variational quantity at finite electronic temperature; its occupation
function is the Fermi-Dirac distribution, but the flavour is now its own
module (`vibeqc.smearing.mermin`, exported as
`vibeqc.mermin_occupations_per_k`) with a dedicated citation route to Mermin
1965, distinct from the pragmatic Fermi-Dirac naming.

Periodic SCF: all backend flavour gates (BIPOLE, GDF, GPW/GAPW dispatch, the
semiempirical k-point routes, and the GDF analytic-gradient envelope) accept
`"mermin"`; occupations, entropy, and the free-energy correction flow through
the same `apply_smearing` dispatcher as the other flavours.

Molecular SCF: `run_job` gains `smearing_temperature` and `smearing_method`.
For gapped molecules the post-SCF free-energy correction is computed from the
converged eigenvalues and the result carries `free_energy`,
`smearing_entropy`, `smearing_temperature`, `smearing_method`, and
`smearing_fermi_level` via a transparent wrapper; the raw `energy` stays the
integer-occupation SCF value.

Also fixed: `resolve_smearing_temperature` now passes the resolved method
into `SmearingResolution` on every code path (presets and numeric values
previously always reported `fermi-dirac` regardless of the requested method).

### Added: Pulay DIIS on the multi-k GAPW SCF (2026-08-15)

Completes the convergence work started in `b4f545b52`, which found that the
multi-k GAPW SCF had no Fock extrapolation or density mixing at all and
unblocked it with linear damping. Damping worked but needed hand-tuning
(the 2.20x-expanded LiH cell wanted `damping=0.95` and ~200 iterations).

`run_periodic_rks_gapw_multi_k` now extrapolates the per-k Fock list with
Pulay DIIS, reusing multi-k GDF's `_MultiKPulayDIIS` rather than
re-deriving the k-weighted inner product; the error vector is the
commutator `F(k)D(k)S(k) - S(k)D(k)F(k)` in the orthonormal basis.
`use_diis=True` / `diis_subspace_size=8` / `diis_start_iter=2` match the
Gamma driver; `use_diis=False` recovers the previous behaviour.

Untuned, LiH rocksalt/STO-3G/LDA/(2,2,2) converges at every lattice scale
-- 7 / 11 / 89 iterations at 1.00 / 1.60 / 2.20x -- reproducing the
damping-established fixed points to better than 1e-6 Ha by a different
path, and agreeing with the PySCF-validated multi-k GDF route at
+16.65 / -26.13 / -0.15 mHa. Equilibrium is unchanged and 2.4x faster.

### Changed: GFN2-xTB molecular SCC default is a guarded simple+DIIS polyalgorithm (2026-08-14)

The molecular GFN2 driver's default charge iteration was plain damped
simple mixing at step 0.1, which converges robustly but slowly (12-95x
xtb's iteration count on the five-system wall matrix, IID 101). The
default is now a two-phase polyalgorithm:

- damped simple mixing tracks the physical fixed point (the third-order
  term admits a spurious over-polarized basin that unguarded Broyden/DIIS
  overshoots from the neutral guess - the June guard was correct, not
  obsolete) and halves its step when the residual stalls for 15
  iterations;
- at iteration 30, a genuinely contracting simple phase hands off to
  pulay-DIIS; a DIIS phase that stops improving for 8 iterations is
  abandoned and the driver finishes from DIIS's best charge state under
  simple mixing.

Every branch converges to the same SCC fixed point.  Five-system wall
matrix (h2o/ch4/nh3/adenine/naphthalene vs xtb 6.7.0, one thread):
iterations 125/107/118/1984/110 -> 47/42/45/514/75, adenine wall
8.82 s -> 2.76 s (the small-system walls stay dominated by the ~1.7 s
fresh-process startup).  Converged energies are pinned unchanged; the two
1e-12-grade stopping-point re-pins in `tests/test_gfn2_xtb.py` are
documented there.  The stabilization ladder primary allowance grew
500 -> 700 steps (slow retry 2000 -> 1800, total 3600 unchanged).
Explicit `scc_mixer="diis"` / `"broyden"` still bypasses the
polyalgorithm.  Perf matrix: `agentic-loop/runs/2026-08-14-gfn2-perf-parity/`.

### Fixed: the selected-CI memory pre-flight sized the full CI space (2026-08-15)

`run_job(method="selected_ci", active_space=(6, 6), selected_ci_options=...)`
on N2/cc-pVDZ was refused before any chemistry with *Estimated peak memory
324364.8 GB exceeds effective allocation 23.4 GB*. The estimate was
bit-identical at `target_size` 6, 20, 50, 100, 200 and 400 — six rungs of one
ladder on one runtime — so it did not depend on the selection at all. The CASCI
sibling of the same job, in the *same* CAS(6e,6o) space, ran fine and returned
-109.02178012171076 Ha, which localised the defect to this estimator route
rather than to the active space or the allocation.

The cause was in two places, and either alone would have been enough:

- `runner._memory_estimator_options` handed `selected_ci` nothing but
  `scf_options`. Neither `active_space` nor `selected_ci_options` reached the
  estimator, so no estimate could have varied with `target_size`.
- `selected_ci` was routed to the generic `_wavefunction_estimate`, which sizes
  the *untruncated* determinant space, `C(2 n_basis, n_elec)` = 5.8e12
  determinants here. Selected CI exists precisely to never build that space.

`selected_ci` now has its own estimator modelling what `SelectedCISolver.solve`
allocates: a variational space bounded by
`int(target_size * selection_growth_factor)` — `solve` trims back to
`target_size` past that bound, and builds `H_mat` at the top of the next
iteration, so this bounds every dense matrix formed — and by the determinant
count of the active space it selects from; the dense `ndet x ndet` Hamiltonian
plus the eigenvectors and LAPACK workspace `scipy_eigh` needs; the candidate
dictionary from the selection step, one Python object per *distinct* singles/
doubles-reachable determinant (measured at 476 B for a 7-orbital determinant),
enumerated exactly as `_select_candidates_restricted` /
`_select_candidates_unrestricted` do; and the whole-MO integral transform,
which `build_hamiltonian_mo` performs before the active-space partition and so
stays basis-sized even for a small CAS.

The same N2/cc-pVDZ CAS(6e,6o) ladder now estimates 0.174 GB at
`target_size=6` rising to 0.180 GB at 400, where it saturates because 400 is
the whole active space. `target_size=6` runs to completion on a laptop.

The exact solvers are deliberately untouched: `fci`, `cisd`, `casci`,
`casscf`, `mrci`, `dmrg`, `v2rdm` and `transcorrelated_ci` keep their existing
estimators, because they really do hold the space they are sized for. (A
selected-CI kernel is also reachable through `transcorrelated_ci` and through
`casci(ci_solver="selected_ci")`; the latter already sizes by the active-space
determinant count, the former keeps the full-space estimate pending a model of
its transcorrelated Hamiltonian.)

### Fixed: 2D slab `V_ne(k)` was wrong at every k != 0 (2026-08-15)

The 2D-slab Ewald nuclear attraction evaluated `V_long(-k)` in place of
`V_long(k)`. Away from Gamma the one-electron bands were displaced by up to
**2.8e-2 Ha** on monolayer h-BN/STO-3G at (4,4,1), and by **0.68 Ha** on the
compressed BN sheet the original reproducer staged — both measured
density-free against out-of-process PySCF `get_hcore` per-band dispersions.

The defective term is the `g != 0` long-range block of
`compute_v_ne_slab_ewald_2d_k_matrix`. It needs

    V_long_muv(k) = S_G v(G) S_g e^{+ik.R_g} conj(rhat_muv(g; G)),

because `V_long(r) = S_G v(G) e^{+iG.r}` carries `e^{+iG.r}` while the AO-pair
FT convention is `e^{-iG.r}`, so the sum needs `rhat(g; -G) = conj(rhat(g; G))`
— the AO-pair FT conjugated, the `+ik` Bloch phase untouched. The shipped code
assembled the Bloch sum first and conjugated the result, which conjugated the
phase along with it and flipped the sign of k. (Slab reciprocal kernel: Parry,
Surf. Sci. **49**, 433 (1975); de Leeuw & Perram, Mol. Phys. **37**, 1313
(1979). Bloch AO-pair FT: Sun, Berkelbach, McClain & Chan, J. Chem. Phys.
**147**, 164119 (2017), doi:10.1063/1.4998644.)

Nothing in the suite could have caught it. Every other witness the route has —
alpha-invariance, the 3D-vacuum-limit anchor, the dispatch Bloch-sum identity —
is a Gamma statement, where the phase is 1. The one k-resolved gate, the
PySCF-referenced H2 slab energy, runs a Gamma-centred (2,2,1) mesh, and all
four of its k-points are time-reversal-invariant momenta, where k and -k
coincide by definition: that gate could not have failed on this defect at any
tolerance. (4,4,1) on h-BN is the smallest mesh that separates them — its four
TRIM points reproduced the reference to 1.4e-4 Ha with the bug in place while
the other twelve missed by up to 0.68 Ha. It is also **not** a truncation
problem: the per-band errors were bit-identical with the lattice sums enlarged
from 15/25 bohr to 30/60 bohr.

The presentation was not reliably fail-closed. Monolayer h-BN did refuse to
converge, but an unaffected-looking run could equally converge to a silently
wrong energy, so any `converged = True` result from the 2D slab GDF route on
a mesh with off-Gamma k-points predates this fix and should be rerun.

`periodic_v_ne_slab_gradient.py` carried the same convention at both its
rung-1 sites (the density-weighted Bloch pair FT and the `gweighted` centre
derivative) and is corrected to match, so the analytic surface gradient
differentiates the function the SCF now evaluates.

New gates: an SCF-free h(k)-dispersion parity pin against out-of-process PySCF
`get_hcore` on h-BN/STO-3G/(4,4,1) at 1 mHa per band, and a test that freezes
the assembly order by rebuilding both conventions from the cache at a
non-TRIM k and asserting they differ. The H2 slab gate is unchanged — it
guards the gauge, and it should keep doing exactly that.

### Fixed: a non-converged periodic SCF no longer reports an occupation class (2026-08-15)

`_band_summary` printed `occupation class = fractionally occupied / smeared`
whenever the attached fill was fractional, including when `converged` was
false. On a non-converged run the eigenvalues are the last iteration's and the
fill computed from them is an artefact of an unconverged Fock, not a property
of the material — but the line reads as a statement about the material. That
is how the h-BN slab `V_ne(k)` defect above came to be recorded as "h-BN
classifies as band-overlapping". Non-converged results now print
`SCF not converged - band edges not classified` instead. Converged behaviour,
including the deliberately unclamped negative gap, is unchanged.


### Fixed: regenerating the suite manifest can no longer silently narrow the release gate (2026-08-15)

`scripts/test_gate/update_suite_manifest.py` rebuilds all 733 classification
rows from scratch, and `tests/conftest.py` refuses an unclassified test file,
so every chat that adds a test is obliged to rerun it. Its `CURATED` table
carries a registered row's hand-classification across that rebuild — but only
a row somebody remembered to register. An *un*registered one was still rebuilt
from the lanes, and the guard test could not tell the two resolutions apart:
`test_suite_manifest_matches_a_fresh_generator_run` goes red when the committed
manifest and a fresh run disagree, and **rerunning the generator turns it green
by discarding the hand-classification**. Its own failure message recommended
exactly that. The release cut selects its blocking set with `--tier T1` off
this manifest, so a demotion out of T0/T1 quietly drops files from the gate —
the mechanism that had already cost `tests/test_periodic_molden_gamma_export.py`
its blocking row.

The generator now compares the rows it is about to write against the committed
manifest and refuses to write a weakened one (`detect_demotions`). Refused
moves are a tier demotion (ranked `T0 > T1 > T2 > T3`, with a move out of the
blocking pair called out explicitly), a maturity downgrade (`production >
verified > under-review > experimental`), and a hand-written rationale
reverting to tier boilerplate. The message names each row and points at the
`CURATED` table; a deliberate demotion passes `--allow-demotion <path>` per
file, so it is visible in the command and explainable in the commit message.
Promotions, new files, and deleted files are unaffected, and a clean
regeneration remains a no-op apart from `generated_at_sha`.

The 14 rows in the original report (11 BIPOLE far-field files plus
`test_polipo_parity.py`, `test_grid_level.py`, and
`test_agentic_loop_record_verdict.py`) were registered in `be72aebea`; this
change closes the hole that let them be lost in the first place.

### Fixed: singlet UHF/UKS spin symmetry under the default guess (GitLab issue 19) (2026-08-14)

The Hund-split open-shell guess (2026-08-08, BUG 88) applied per-atom
spin-polarised atomic densities even when the molecular spin counts
balance, so any singlet UHF/UKS containing an atom with an open-shell
Hund ground state (C, N, O, …) *started* spin-polarised and re-symmetrised
only to the SCF convergence threshold — leaving O(1e-7) spurious α/β
density polarisation at default tolerances, failing the RIJCOSX UKS/RKS
singlet parity guard (`test_rijcosx_singlet_uks_matches_rks`, red on main
since 2026-08-08), and permanently disengaging the spin-degenerate
shared-exchange gate (double exchange builds per iteration on singlet
hybrid UKS). Spin-balanced systems (n_α == n_β) now take spin-averaged
atomic occupations in both the PATOM and SAD open-shell guesses; the Hund
split is unchanged for n_α ≠ n_β (BUG 88 FeCl₃ behaviour preserved), and
deliberate broken-symmetry singlet starts remain available via ATOMSPIN.
Energies were unaffected (< 1e-9 Ha). Regression tests pin α/β density
parity (atol 1e-12) for singlet UHF (PATOM + SAD) and default-options
singlet UKS in `tests/test_guess.py`.

### Fixed: MDF wrong answers traced to the fitting-metric linear-dependence threshold (2026-08-14)

Mixed density fitting (`gdf_method="mdf"`) returned grossly wrong energies on
dense-core cells — MgO/STO-3G Γ landed at +4.7e+05 Ha, and was trial-dependent
between runs. The cause was the linear-dependence threshold applied to the
plane-wave-dressed metric J̃ of Sun 2017 Eq. 20, not the lattice cutoff or a
loss of positive-definiteness (both were measured and refuted).

J̃ is the Coulomb metric with the plane-wave space projected out and is
therefore *deliberately* singular ("Projecting the PWs out of the Gaussian
functions in (20) leads to a highly singular matrix", Sun, Berkelbach, McClain
& Chan, J. Chem. Phys. 147, 164119 (2017), doi:10.1063/1.4998644, Sec. II B).
The shipped threshold retained modes lying below J̃'s own construction error:
on MgO at the production real-space cutoff the J̃ spectrum carries up to
5.4e-06 absolute error, while the smallest retained eigenvalue was 2.9e-08
with a 6.6e-08 error bar. Eq. 19 then divides the Eq.-23 numerator by the
square root of that noise, amplifying it ~6e+03 times.

Two changes:

- **The threshold comparison is harmonised to absolute** across all nine
  fitting-metric decompositions in `aux_basis.py`. The compcell and MDF
  builders previously compared eigenvalues against `linear_dep_thr * max_eig`
  while the rsgdf/FFT builders compared absolutely, so one number meant two
  cuts an order of magnitude apart. Absolute is PySCF's convention — a single
  `linear_dep_threshold` used identically by its GDF, MDF and RSGDF builders,
  compared against the raw eigenvalue of the un-normalised metric — and Sun
  2017 Sec. II B states no normalisation.
- **Scale-awareness is now an explicit, per-metric noise floor** rather than
  something hidden in the comparison. The floor guards against the metric's
  own construction error, which scales with the metric, so it is applied as
  `thr = max(linear_dep_thr, fraction * max_eig)`. The plain compensated
  metric keeps a `1e-9` fraction, which reproduces the cut its builders were
  validated at; the PW-dressed MDF metric gets `1e-4`, which is the fix. The
  rsgdf/FFT builders take no floor, preserving their existing absolute
  behaviour. Verified behaviour-preserving: over 88 metric decompositions in
  the compcell and periodic-RHF-GDF suites the retained rank is unchanged in
  every case.

  The MDF fraction is a vibe-qc calibration, not a value from the paper:
  PySCF supports its much tighter 1e-10 because it builds the 2-centre metric
  at a dedicated tighter precision, whereas vibe-qc builds J̃ at the general
  lattice-sum precision. It is applied only when the PW block is active, so
  the `mdf_ke_cutoff <= 0` compcell-equivalent limit stays bit-identical, and
  callers may still set a looser value. Expressing it as a fraction rather
  than an absolute constant matters: J̃'s scale spans seven orders across
  cells (`max_eig` ≈ 1e+01 on MgO and Ne but 9e-06 on a dilute H2 box, where
  the plane waves nearly span the Gaussian auxiliary space), and a fixed
  absolute floor calibrated on the former annihilates the latter's entire
  auxiliary space.

The validated Ne/STO-3G vacuum-box envelope improves from 0.064 mHa to
**0.0024 mHa** against the out-of-process PySCF MDF oracle, a 26x gain in
parity. The dense-core class is no longer divergent (MgO becomes bounded and
physically scaled) but **remains gated**: the threshold that removes the
divergence also discards ~81% of the auxiliary space on that cell, leaving
~92 mHa of basis-set incompleteness error — the other half of the trade-off
Sun 2017 Sec. III describes. Lifting that gate requires building J̃ accurately
enough to support a tighter threshold, which is recorded as the follow-up in
`pbc_gdf._reject_dense_core_mdf`.

Regression: `tests/test_pbc_gdf_mdf.py` —
`test_metric_keep_mask_is_absolute_not_relative`,
`test_plain_metric_floor_preserves_validated_compcell_cut`,
`test_mdf_dressed_metric_threshold_floor`,
`test_mdf_linear_dep_threshold_ne_box_sweep` (promotes the triage sweep that
previously existed only as prose), `test_mdf_dense_core_no_longer_diverges`.

## [v0.15.134] - 2026-08-14 - *Neese's Cheetah*

**Verification status, stated honestly.** Three HIGH-class fixes in this
release ship as landed, test-backed code whose *independent* broker
verification (CLAUDE.md § 3: a second, distinct agent identity) is still
outstanding at cut time: the revDSD-PBEP86 P86 local-part fix
(`ea47228be`, issue 32) and the two periodic slab-GDF fixes
(`db1a6725d`, `c911964a1`). Each carries its own regressions, and the
tag is created only on a green release-gate pipeline (blocking T0+T1)
at this exact tree; none has a second-agent PASS on record yet. Sibling
versions at this tag: vq 0.25.1 (bumped), vibe-view 2.14.1 (unchanged),
vibe-basis 0.10.0 (unchanged).

### Fixed: periodic band gaps were clamped at zero, masking inverted band orderings (2026-08-14)

`_band_summary` reported `max(0.0, cbm - vbm)` and `max(0.0, lu - ho)`, so a
band ordering that came out **inverted** printed as `gap (indirect) =
0.000000 Ha (0.000 eV)`. On the hBN / sto-3g / kRKS-PBE / GDF / (4,4,1)
reproducer the true extrema were VBM −0.2004980334 Ha at `k_idx` 0 and CBM
−0.3206728391 Ha at `k_idx` 13 — the CBM sat **3.270 eV below** the VBM, and
the clamp hid exactly that. A masked inversion and a genuine zero gap rendered
identically, which also silently defeated any regression test written against
the printed line (CLAUDE.md § 7). Both gaps are now reported unclamped, and a
negative indirect gap carries a `negative: band ordering inverted across the
mesh` annotation. Nothing downstream clamped: the `.system` manifest and the
structured log carry no gap field, and `periodic_convergence_auto`'s own gap
was already signed. Positive-gap output is byte-identical. Regressions:
`tests/test_periodic_runner_semiempirical.py::test_band_summary_reports_inverted_ordering_as_a_negative_gap`,
`::test_band_summary_does_not_clamp_a_negative_direct_gap`, and
`::test_band_summary_keeps_a_positive_gap_unchanged`. Signature
`SLAB-GDF-GAP-CLAMPED-AT-ZERO` [HIGH].

### Fixed: 2D slab GDF filled each k point independently instead of under one Fermi level (2026-08-14)

The closed-shell slab-GDF adapter wrote `2.0` into the first `n_occ` slots at
**every** k independently, and the SCF density build occupied
`coeff[:, :n_occ]` per k. That is a per-k Aufbau: when bands cross between k
points it selects states that are not the globally lowest, mis-classifies the
band edges, and lets the selection flip between adjacent iterations. This is
the contract `60104fc01` established for the 3D native multi-k GDF route
(PERIODIC-K6-NONCONV); the 2D slab route was never covered by it. Occupations,
the Fermi level, and the SCF density now come from one weighted global
zero-temperature Aufbau across the mesh, and KDIIS fails closed when that fill
is no longer a fixed per-k integer pattern — mirroring the 3D guard.

On a gapped cell the two conventions agree exactly, so the change is
numerically inert there: the PySCF-referenced H2 slab gate
(−0.9175852704211138 Ha, out-of-process PySCF 2.13.1 KRHF-GDF,
`low_dim_ft_type='inf_vacuum'`) still converges in 2 iterations with
bit-identical `2, 0` occupations.

On hBN the correction is real but **not sufficient on its own**: the run still
terminates NOT converged at 200 iterations and still fails closed. The
oscillation amplitude fell by roughly an order of magnitude (residual
3.4e-2 → 4.8e-3; adjacent-iteration energy swing ±1.8 mHa → ±0.2 mHa), and the
band-extrema block now honestly reports `occupation class = fractionally
occupied / smeared` instead of a fabricated zero gap. The residual
non-convergence is the expected behaviour of a band-overlapping system under
integer T=0 occupations, and closing it needs finite-temperature smearing on
this route, which is not implemented (see below). Regressions:
`tests/test_slab_2d_routing.py::test_slab_gdf_occupations_use_one_global_fermi_level`,
`::test_slab_gdf_scf_density_is_built_from_the_global_filling`, and
`::test_slab_gdf_fails_closed_on_smearing_rather_than_guessing`.

### Changed: the AUTO convergence profiler no longer calls low-dimensional cells "inconclusive" (2026-08-14)

Every `dim=1` and `dim=2` cell reported `no decisive signal (dim=2, …) --
keeping conservative plain defaults`. That reads as "weighed the evidence and
found nothing", but the covalent / ionic / metallic branches are all gated on
`tight`, which is `dim == 3` by construction — no low-dimensional cell can
reach them at all. The profiler now says so: `no low-dimensional branch … the
covalent/ionic/metallic signals are 3D-only, so this cell is unclassified by
construction, not judged inconclusive; a semimetallic or small-gap sheet needs
an explicit smearing choice`. Genuinely inconclusive 3D cells keep the
original wording.

**The knobs are deliberately unchanged**, and the reasoning is evidence-based
rather than conservative-by-habit: finite-temperature smearing is *rejected
outright* by the slab GDF route that 2D systems take
(`NotImplementedError: private multi-k slab GDF does not yet support
smearing`, and `bz_integration` likewise fails closed). Defaulting 2D to
finite-T smearing would therefore make every 2D GDF run fail at startup, and a
hard guard demanding an explicit choice would be worse still — it would demand
a choice no user can currently satisfy on that route. Implementing smearing on
the slab GDF route is the prerequisite for either option; until it lands, the
honest move is to name the limitation instead of dressing it as a confident
default (CLAUDE.md § 7 applied to the profiler). Regressions:
`tests/test_periodic_convergence_auto.py::test_low_dimensional_cells_are_named_unclassified_not_inconclusive`,
`::test_low_dimensional_classification_does_not_change_any_knob`, and
`::test_three_dimensional_inconclusive_wording_is_unchanged`.

### Fixed: revDSD-PBEP86-D4 used the wrong P86 local-part flavor (2026-08-14)

`revdsd-pbep86` / `revdsdpbep86` composed Perdew-86 correlation on the
**PZ81** local part (libxc `GGA_C_P86`, id 132) instead of the **VWN5**
local part (`GGA_C_P86VWN`, id 252) — the flavor `dsd-pbep86` already
used. The recipe as built matched neither the defining paper's
prescription nor any code that implements revDSD.

The 2019 refit itself ran in Q-Chem, which is why the flavor was
previously left as-is behind a "do not harmonize without a gate-clean
reference" note. That reference turned out to be the paper's own
Electronic Supporting Information: the ORCA sample deck for
revDSD-PBEP86 (ESI p. S22) specifies `Exchange X_PBE` / `Correlation
C_P86`, and ORCA composes that on VWN-5 (`LDA part of GGA corr. LDAOpt
.... VWN-5`). The authors' Gaussian deck scales local and nonlocal
correlation by one uniform coefficient, matching the single `c_c` here.

Decomposed against ORCA 6.1.1 on witness M19 (H2O / cc-pVTZ), per
component (vibe-qc − ORCA):

| component | pre-fix | post-fix |
|---|---|---|
| SCF (KS half) | +2.4582 mHa | +0.6613 mHa |
| MP2 (scaled) | −0.2316 mHa | −0.2217 mHa |
| D4 dispersion | −0.0415 mHa | −0.0415 mHa |
| **total** | **+2.1852 mHa** | **+0.3981 mHa** |

The offset lived entirely in the KS half. Of its +2.4582 mHa, the P86
flavor accounts for −1.7969 mHa; the remainder is a *parameter revision*,
not a defect: vibe-qc ships the 2019 Table 4 D4 set (c_c = 0.4210) that
its citation route claims, while the ORCA reference used the later
`REVDSD-PBEP86-D4/2021` keyword (c_c = 0.4224, worth −0.5095 mHa). The
2021 coefficients are deliberately **not** guessed — that paper is not in
the reference library and has been requested; a 2021 member would need
its own alias, damping set, and citation entry.

`vwn_1980` now rides the `revdsd-pbep86` functional and dispatcher
citation routes, matching the `dsd-pbep86` precedent. Documented in
`docs/user_guide/mp2_and_double_hybrids.md` § revDSD-PBEP86. Regressions:
`tests/test_revdsd_pbep86.py::test_revdsd_pbep86_uses_vwn5_local_p86`
(flavor pinned by energy equivalence against explicitly VWN5- and
PZ81-built recipes) and `::test_revdsd_pbep86_scf_half_matches_orca_m19`
(SCF half within 0.15 mHa of the ORCA reference). GitLab issue 32.

### Added: space-group-reduced multi-k GDF exchange from `run_periodic_job` (2026-08-14)

The irreducible-wedge exchange build (`ibz_native`) already worked at the
driver level but was unreachable from the production entry point, and the
memory preflight could not show the saving it exists to demonstrate.

- **New `run_periodic_job(symmetry_reduce_k=True)`**, plumbed to `ibz_native`
  on the four multi-k GDF drivers (`run_krhf/krks/kuhf/kuks_periodic_gdf`).
  Exchange is the one `n_k^2` term: `K(k_i)` is built only at the irreducible
  wedge bras and symmetry-transported across each star, so the dense `Lpq`
  cderi cache holds `n_IBZ x n_k` blocks instead of `n_k^2`. Diagonalisation
  at every `k`, occupations, the energy expression and the result shape are
  untouched, so the reduction is exact — NaCl primitive / STO-3G / `(2,2,2)`
  reproduces the full-BZ energy to 4.7e-07 Ha (the cell-list transport
  residual at the default 15-bohr cutoff, not a symmetry error).
- **Every precondition fails closed** rather than silently running full-BZ:
  `jk_method="gdf"`, `dim=3`, a true multi-k mesh, RHF/RKS/UHF/UKS, an
  attached symmetry model (`symmetry="attach"`), a resolvable wedge, and no
  geometry optimization. A silently-ignored performance flag would make the
  run look reduced while costing the full `n_k^2`.
- **`estimate_periodic_multik_gdf` accepts `n_ibz_kpoints`** and the GDF
  preflight (`check_periodic_gdf_memory`, `_preflight_gdf_lpq_memory`) is
  charged at the reduced bra count. Previously the guard aborted a reduced
  run at the full-mesh number and the printed `[memory]` estimate contradicted
  the cache actually allocated. NaCl primitive / def2-SVP / `(4,4,4)`,
  `n_IBZ = 8` of 64: the `Lpq` term drops 15.95 GB → 1.99 GB (8x), total
  25.08 GB → 4.14 GB. The over-budget message now names the reduction as a
  remedy.
- **The `.out` states the reduction** in the GDF settings block, directly
  above `[memory]`: `symmetry_reduce_k = exchange bras 64 -> 8 (irreducible
  wedge)` plus the cderi-pair count and the exactness note.

Documented in `docs/user_guide/periodic_methods.md` § 3.2.3. Regressions:
`tests/test_periodic_gdf_memory_preflight.py::TestIBZReduction` (4 cases) and
`tests/test_periodic_k_gdf.py` —
`test_symmetry_reduce_k_resolves_the_nacl_wedge`,
`test_symmetry_reduce_k_requires_attached_symmetry`,
`test_symmetry_reduce_k_refuses_non_gdf_and_gamma`,
`test_symmetry_reduce_k_refuses_optimization`,
`test_symmetry_reduce_k_preflight_charges_the_wedge`,
`test_symmetry_reduce_k_matches_full_bz_energy` (slow).

### Fixed: failed fleet updates no longer masquerade as live release tags (2026-08-14)

`vq admin rollout-latest` now derives a managed release lane's tag from the
fresh checkout description reported by `vq programs`/`admin status`. The tag
requested by the last transaction is used only as a compatibility fallback
after that transaction succeeded. A failed atomic update can therefore roll
back to the older healthy checkout without the planner falsely reporting
"same release version has a different SHA" on the next repair.

### Changed: SCC-DFTB-SECCM 1-D embedding uses a converged background-corrected wire Ewald (2026-08-14)

The opt-in 1-D Madelung embedding for charged SECCM cells no longer uses
the truncated ±2-shell bare Coulomb sum (the MSINDO CCM kernel, which stays
frozen on its own validated paths). The bare 1-D image series diverges
logarithmically, so any finite truncation leaves a kernel whose charge
response was nearly singular for even-replica polar chains (the documented
period-2 limit cycle). The new kernel (`cpp/src/semiempirical/seccm/ewald_1d.h`)
is a Parry-type wire Ewald: real-space erfc images, the axial reciprocal
series, and the finite m=0 channel of the neutralizing-background convention
(sum over images of 1/|d+nT| minus 1/|nT| per image), validated against
direct N→∞ background-subtracted lattice sums and the 2 ln 2 alternating-chain
Madelung constant. The N=4 charged chain now converges at T=0 under DIIS
(regression added). Odd-replica charged chains sit at a degenerate frontier
under the converged kernel (the old truncation had masked it with its
self-field), so `run_scc_dftb_seccm` gains an opt-in
`electronic_temperature` (Ha, default 0 = Aufbau, molecular parity
unchanged): Fermi-Dirac occupations through the shared k-point occupation
kernel converge those cases and the reported energy is the Mermin free
energy A = E - T*S (`free_energy`, `entropy`, `smearing_temperature`).
Regression: `tests/test_ccm_semiempirical.py`.

### Fixed: GFN2-xTB water-dimer parity with xtb restored (GFN2-MOL-PARITY, 2026-08-14)

The faithful-AES water-dimer oracle gate (trans 5.6/6.0/7.0 bohr vs live xtb
6.7.1) now passes at all three separations (vibe-qc +12.20/+7.46/+3.26 mHa vs
xtb +11.71/+7.01/+2.92 mHa, gate ±2 mHa; previously +6.1/+2.6/+0.4).  Four
defects were closed:

- The STO-NG basis selected expansion rows by l alone, so every s shell ran
  the 1s table (e.g. O 2s used the 1s expansion instead of the 2s row, with
  the coefficients mispaired to the reordered exponents).  The tables now
  select on (n, l) with xtb slater.f90's rows, the parameter parser carries
  the principal quantum number from the ao=2s2p records, and the GFN2 auto
  primitive count follows xtb's per-shell rule (H,He->3; n>5->6; else->4,
  with the HSP 6s/6p rows for period-6 shells).
- The faithful-AES moments, potentials, and Fock were rebuilt as direct ports
  of xtb's mmompop / setvsdq / buildIsoAnisotropicH1 (global-origin raw
  quadrupole integrals in xtb's component order), replacing the chain-rule
  construction over atom-centred traceless moments that was the derivative of
  a different functional.
- The first SCC iteration now includes the charge-only AES channels (xtb runs
  setvsdq with zero moments at iteration 1).
- The CN-dependent multipole radii (mrad) now consume the GFN2 double-damped
  coordination number (the same CN the H0 self-energy uses), not the D4
  dispersion CN.

The O 2s overlap with H 1s moved from 0.013 to 0.445 (xtb's value), the H0
gap from 9.0 to 14.5 eV (xtb's value), and the converged water charges to
-0.557 (xtb -0.561).  Energy pins in tests/test_gfn2_xtb.py and the GFN2
lanes of tests/test_semiempirical_benchmarks.py were re-measured; the
graphene k-point smearing-contract pin moved to kmesh (4,4,1) because the
corrected basis shifted the frontier so the exact-Aufbau branch at (2,2,1)
no longer converges.

### Added: multi-replica OMx-SECCM with eq-13/eq-10 three-center weighting (2026-08-14)

`run_omx_seccm` (OM1/OM2/OM3) now builds the full WS-weighted supercell
Fock instead of the molecular-limit slice: molecular one-center blocks
plus directed two-center terms (penetration-corrected core attraction,
eq-17 resonance, two-electron Coulomb/exchange, core-core repulsion, and
the eq-8 F1/F2 one-center VORT corrections) accumulated through the WS
records with their fractional weights, exactly like the PM6-SECCM
adapter. The three-center terms (the eq-9 G1/G2 VORT corrections and the
OM2/OM3 ECP) follow the Peintinger-Bredow 2014 weighting (JCC 35, 839,
eqs 10-14): the production eq-13 scheme over the union WSSC(MN) is the
default (`three_center_weighting="peintinger_eq13"`), and Janetzko's
original eq-10 scheme is the opt-in comparison path
(`three_center_weighting="janetzko_eq10"`). The molecular limit
reproduces `run_omx_v2` to ~1e-14 Ha for OM1/OM2/OM3 on CH4, the 2-cell
H2O chain is translation-invariant along the cyclic direction, and the
2-D square-lattice axis-swap invariance holds to 1e-14. Regressions:
`tests/test_ccm_semiempirical.py` (OMx-SECCM section).

### Fixed: GFN2-xTB analytic-vs-FD gradient residual closed (2026-08-14)

Two defects closed the GFN2-GRADIENT-FD-RESIDUAL gap:

- The BUG-022 M-matrix SCC-channel sign flip (commit e8e11cdbc) rested on
  an incorrect premise: it assumed the GFN2 Hamiltonian is
  H^0 - 1/2 S(v+v'), but both drivers (`run_gfn2_xtb` and
  `run_gfn2_xtb_gamma`) build H_scc = H^0 + 1/2 S(v+v'), so the minus sign
  made the gradient differentiate a different surface than the converged
  energy. The plus sign is restored at all three call sites (molecular
  gradient, periodic gradient, periodic stress), and the stress
  third-order shell shift now carries the same minus sign as the
  molecular Fock channel (`-Gamma3 * dq^2`, matching
  `gfn2_fock_shell_potential`).
- `gfn2_h0_image_derivative_terms` copied the H0 builder's |S| < 1e-15
  pair skip, but F = dH0/dS does not vanish at S = 0. Whenever an overlap
  is exactly zero by symmetry (e.g. an O-H bond aligned with a global
  axis), the derivative dropped a real force term and the analytic
  gradient jumped discretely across the alignment point (~2.7e-2
  Ha/bohr on water) while the symmetric fixture geometries passed. The
  derivative now keeps every pair; the s_val-weighted chains vanish
  continuously on their own.

The analytic gradient agrees with central FD of the total SCC energy to
~1e-9 Ha/bohr for H2O (symmetric and axis-aligned), CH4, and NH3, and the
D4-corrected total-energy gradient gate passes; the strict xfail markers
are removed and the water gradient value pin re-pinned to +0.0233107
Ha/bohr. Regression: `tests/test_gfn2_xtb.py`,
`tests/test_periodic_runner_semiempirical.py`, and the GFN2 lanes of
`tests/test_semiempirical_benchmarks.py`.

### Changed: periodic GFN2-xTB smears the frontier by default; exact Aufbau on request (2026-08-14)

The Gamma and k-point periodic GFN2-xTB drivers now apply a default-on
Fermi-Dirac temperature of 0.001 Ha (about 316 K) when
`XTBSccOptions.electronic_temperature` is left unset, so a frontier
crossing on a lattice sweep cannot flip the hard-Aufbau occupations
between SCC branches (GFN2-GRAPHENE-BRANCH-DISCONTINUITY). Setting
`electronic_temperature = 0.0` explicitly restores the exact
zero-temperature Aufbau occupations; an explicit positive temperature is
honoured as-is. The molecular GFN2 path is unchanged (default stays
Aufbau). The Mermin free energy `A = E - T*S` is exposed as
`free_energy` on both periodic result structs, alongside `entropy`,
`fermi_level`, and `smearing_temperature`; the k-point driver now uses
the shared particle-conserving occupation kernel instead of hard Aufbau.
The native fixed-charge periodic gradient and stress build their
energy-weighted densities from the converged fractional occupations, so
they differentiate the free-energy surface of a smeared run; the Python
finite-difference facades and optimizer energy closures follow the same
convention. The public Gamma `run_periodic_job` route applies the same
policy: unset smearing selects the default width, an explicit `0` (or
`None`) selects Aufbau, and a smeared run writes the finite-temperature
block (temperature, entropy, free energy, Fermi level) to the `.out`.
Regression: `tests/test_semiempirical_benchmarks.py` graphene sweep and
`tests/test_periodic_runner_semiempirical.py` public-route contracts.

## [v0.15.133] - 2026-08-14 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Documentation: `dipole_moment` vs `compute_dipole`, and the polarizability sidecar recipe (2026-08-14)

No behaviour change. `docs/user_guide/properties.md` now states outright
that `vq.compute_dipole(basis, origin)` is the AO dipole-**integral**
builder while `vq.dipole_moment(result, basis, molecule)` is the physical
dipole **moment**, and documents the supported `run_job` +
`dipole_polarizability_rhf` properties-sidecar recipe (`run_job` has no
polarizability option). Prompted by COMPUTE-DIPOLE-SIGNATURE-MISMATCH: an
external properties payload guessed a `compute_dipole(molecule, basis,
density)` overload that has never existed and lost its sidecar on 20 runs;
the public runner path had already written the correct dipole to every
`.out`. `tests/test_properties.py` now pins the binding shape, rejects the
guessed three-argument call, and covers the dipole + polarizability sidecar
end to end.

### Fixed: .out format freeze green again; zero-U BIPOLE jobs no longer print a DFT+U row (2026-08-14)

- The periodic BIPOLE energy-component table printed a `DFT+U (Dudarev)`
  row for every job — including jobs with no `+U` sites — because BIPOLE
  results carry `e_dft_plus_u = 0.0` unconditionally and the row was gated
  on attribute presence alone (regression in the 2026-08-13 BIPOLE audit
  landing). The row is now shown only when the contribution is non-zero,
  matching the molecular/scalar branch's documented behaviour; `+U`-active
  jobs are unchanged.
- `tests/test_out_format_snapshot.py` goldens regenerated after per-hunk
  diagnosis (memory-preflight MB rows from BUG 63, explicit HOMO/LUMO/gap
  footers from BUG 81, UHF spin/stability/fingerprint diagnostics, BIPOLE
  crystal-orbital `occ=` column). The canonicalizer now scrubs the
  singular 1-thread footer and the state-fingerprint hex digest, so
  goldens no longer pin the generating machine's thread count or
  bit-exact numerical state.
- `tests/test_scf_log_orbitals.py` assertions updated to the BUG 81
  footer format (red on `main` since 2026-08-11).
- `tests/test_runner.py::test_run_job_writes_out_and_molden` likewise
  (GitLab issue 33, OUT-MISSING-HOMO-LUMO-GAP: the gap line was renamed
  by BUG 81, not dropped).

### Fixed: periodic SCF non-convergence now fails loudly (exit code + manifest), not silently "complete" (2026-08-13)

`run_periodic_job` gains a fail-closed convergence gate mirroring the
molecular runner: an RHF/UHF/RKS/UKS/ROHF/ROKS periodic SCF that hits its
iteration cap writes a FATAL line to the `.out`, crashes the `.system`
manifest, labels the terminal checkpoint "failed", and raises
`RuntimeError` -- so the CLI exits non-zero and pipelines trusting exit
codes / manifest status can no longer promote an unconverged energy into
a validation database (the CaO PBE GDF 200-iter exit-0 incident).
Everything after the gate (dispersion, sidecars, QVF, optimization) is
skipped on the failure path. Regression:
`tests/test_periodic_scf.py::test_run_periodic_job_raises_and_marks_crashed_on_scf_nonconvergence`.

### Fixed: ROKS crash on the default `run_job(method="roks")` grid path (2026-08-13)

`ROKSOptions.grid` defaults to `None` (the driver materialises a default
`GridOptions`), but `run_job` applied the grid-level preset in-place via
`_apply_grid_level(options.grid, ...)` -- `AttributeError` on every default
ROKS run before the driver was reached (first seen at def2-TZVP). The runner
now materialises the grid first, mirroring `run_roks`' own default
construction. Regression:
`tests/test_roks.py::test_run_job_default_roks_grid_materialises_at_tzvp`.

### Fixed: periodic GDF memory preflight counts the dense AO-pair FT bundle (2026-08-13)

The default dense rsgdf fit holds one ``(n_ao, n_ao, n_G)`` complex128
AO-pair FT bundle in RAM while the Lpq factors are assembled; the
preflight never counted it, so a Gamma-only Al2O3/def2-SVP GDF job was
reported at ~0.40 GB while the process peaked at 41 GiB and died
mid-setup.  ``_periodic_gdf_estimate`` now sizes the bundle from
``rsgdf_dense_g_mesh`` at the resolved ``rsgdf_ke_cutoff`` (28 GiB for
that cell at ke=200 Ha, ~5 GiB even at STO-3G), so the
``check_periodic_gdf_memory`` gate tells the truth and fails early with
route-specific remedies.  Regression:
``tests/test_periodic_gdf_memory_preflight.py::TestDensePairFTBundle``.

### Fixed: Γ GDF legacy fallback no longer drops the dense-core +PARITY_HELD marker (2026-08-13)

A Γ-only RKS/PBE GDF run on an ionic-insulator cell (the AUTO fock-mixing
profile blocks the pure PBC-GDF Γ fast path) fell back to the legacy
molecular-limit driver, and the KRHF/KRKS result adapter overwrote the
backend with the bare literal ``native-gamma-gdf-via-k-gdf`` -- so the
~-0.5 Ha untailed dense-core absolute-energy hold (P01 class) was
computed nowhere and published pipelines saw an un-held energy (the BUG 5
convention-audit family).  The adapter now propagates the inner driver's
marker, and the legacy fallback applies the dense-core classifier, warns
(RuntimeWarning + .out line), and tags the result.  Regression:
``tests/test_periodic_rhf_gdf.py::test_gamma_gdf_result_wrapper_propagates_parity_hold_marker``.

### Fixed: dormant BIPOLE quartet far-field branch made internally consistent (2026-08-13)

The dormant G6 branch of `build_bipole_restricted_fock` now consumes the
same skip-masked near-field `jk_near.K` for both the Fock and the exchange
energy (re-adding the Ewald LR correction), matching the unrestricted
path's "near-field exact, far-K skipped" approximation instead of silently
combining the far-field J with the full exact K. Any future re-wiring of
the (currently fail-closed, see above) quartet far-field starts from a
coherent reference. Independent exact-vs-far-field measurement corroborates
the retirement: with the quartet path exercised directly, LiH/STO-3G shows
6.9e-2 Ha (14 bohr), 6.3e-2 Ha (18 bohr), 5.9e-2 Ha (24 bohr), barely
decaying with separation -- a periodic-translation-domain mismatch, not a
truncation artefact.

## [v0.15.132] - 2026-08-14 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Fixed: Gamma Molden export is BLAS-independent for degenerate orbitals (2026-08-13)

Degenerate Gamma-point orbital blocks are now realified from their full
real/imaginary span in the overlap metric whenever simply taking the real
projection would lose orthonormality. The writer requires that span to have
exactly the block's rank, so genuinely complex non-Gamma subspaces still fail
closed instead of being turned into plausible real orbitals. This removes the
Linux/OpenBLAS-only v0.15.131 release-gate failure while keeping
`C.T @ S @ C = I` at floating-point roundoff.

### Added: vq 0.25.0 exact self-update and durable recovery close updater ownership gaps (2026-08-13)

vq now exposes `vq self-update` as the first-class exact-pin repair for its
managed daemon environment. It accepts a full source SHA or an explicitly
selected accepted fleet report and retains the existing lock, update marker,
scoped pause/resume, rollback, required daemon restart, readiness, and exact
source/tree provenance contracts. Accepted-report lookup is bound to that
managed checkout and occurs under the same local checkout-ownership fence as
ordinary admin updates, before any fetch. Managed update scripts coordinate
restart timing with that outer transaction through an exact lock capability;
the service is stopped and proven quiescent before checkout/venv mutation.
The old venv and checkout remain under a durable crash-recovery receipt until
the exact old or target daemon is proven and every token-scoped job is proven
resumed. Per-job pause intent precedes SIGSTOP, dispatch rechecks the marker at
its final RUNNING claim, and unresolved pause/resume work retains the receipt
instead of reporting success. `vq admin recover-update` is the only managed
recovery path: it reconciles and verifies the receipt's exact durable phase,
restoring the old runtime or re-attesting an already committed target without
promoting an unverified target by inference. It proves the receipt's exact
paused-job scope resumed and only then clears the marker. Ordinary clear and
force operations refuse this durable receipt. Losing the daemon identity after
deferral is a failed update, and branch-mode auto-update rejects the daemon's
own environment before job submission.

The standalone `vq admin auto-update --scheduler-runtimes` compatibility flag
now fails closed before config, routing, ref, status, or mutation work. It
directs operators to `vq admin rollout-latest`, where one accepted release
report binds every scheduler-runtime lane to an exact tag and SHA. Direct
scheduler helper and runtime updates now accept only canonical hosts explicitly
marked `fleet_role = "managed"`; aliases and unresolved or excluded roles are
rejected before driver delegation.

An explicit recovery-only `rollout-latest --reconcile-legacy` mode can recover
authenticated pre-recorder `running` actions without inventing an outcome. It
globally authenticates the exact historical report, deterministic rollout ID,
argv, hold shape, and absence of durable orphans before any legacy observation
or write. Healthy same-lane evidence records only `superseded` with unknown
outcome; unreachable, blocked, marker-overlapped, or otherwise unproven action
groups remain byte-identical behind hash- and report-bound retention receipts.
Legacy claims settle only after authoritative inactive evidence, including a
post-release absence snapshot rather than trusting exit zero. Every retained
host remains an explicit deferred plan fence (or a hard block for the driver),
even without a current topology lane, while unrelated hosts may continue. The
recovery invocation exits before rollout actions; an ordinary report-pinned
dry run and a separate ordinary rollout are required next.

### Fixed: vq 0.25.0 lifecycle and runtime-slot replacement is crash-durable (2026-08-13)

Direct whole-virtualenv replacement is now an inactive-environment transaction.
Before moving the old environment, vq fsyncs a private receipt beside the
target; the next invocation reconciles an interrupted candidate, rollback, or
cleanup under the same checkout and target locks and exits without inventing a
service action. Direct `--restart-daemon` is now a fail-closed compatibility
spelling: a serving daemon must use `vq self-update` or `vq admin update`, which
owns source, virtualenv, pause, rollback, service restart, and provenance as one
managed transaction.

Opt-in per-SHA runtime slots now reserve and seal each generation through a
durable build receipt before either pointer can move. Failed or interrupted
builds cannot become `current`; cleanup waits until both pointers and every
stable-wrapper reference prove a generation unused.

### Security: vq 0.25.0 retires privileged unattended `/opt/vq` refresh (2026-08-13)

The root-owned multi-user refresh now requires the accepted full source SHA,
seals that exact commit into root-owned input, assembles the vq wheel without
executing a checkout-provided build backend as root, and installs only
hash-locked binary dependencies after independent artifact validation. Before
service or virtualenv mutation it fsyncs a root-only recovery receipt; failure
or restart recovery restores and proves one exact old or new runtime. Bootstrap
uses the same durable admission boundary rather than an early queue snapshot.

Authenticated `sudo` is mandatory. Deployment removes the former passwordless
`vq-admins` fragment, disables the unsafe root auto-update timer, and installs
fail-closed tombstones so stale enabled units cannot execute privileged update
code. This explicitly supersedes item 1 of the historical **"Added: vq fleet
rollouts no longer need a human typing exact strings"** entry below. That text
accurately records the v0.15.85-era implementation, including its HEAD-derived
identity and optional passwordless rule, but it is not current operator
procedure.

## [v0.15.131] - 2026-08-12 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Fixed: GFN2-xTB third-order (GAM3) energy/Fock convention (BUG-027, 2026-08-13)

xtb computes the third-order term shell-resolved with the l-dependent
GAM3 scaling (`thirdorder.f90` shellGam branch:
E_3rd = sum_sh G_raw*G_scale(l)*q_sh^3/3, Fock shift G_sh*q_sh^2).
vibe-qc used the atom-resolved raw-Gamma form in the energy
(sum_A G_raw*q_A^3/3) and the l-scaled but atomic-charge form in the Fock
(-G_sh*q_A^2) - internally inconsistent and off xtb parity.  All three
drivers (molecular, k-points, periodic) and the analytic-gradient
response machinery now use the shell-resolved convention.  The SCC
fixed points shift accordingly (adenine residual vs xtb 6.7.1:
+245.7 -> +228.9 mHa; water unchanged at ~15.6 mHa - the remaining gap
is the AES-model parity item in BUG-027).  GFN2-xTB remains gated
experimental.

### Fixed: release-gate native builds are diagnosable again; libint build goes quiet-with-heartbeat (2026-08-13)

The three v0.15.131 release-candidate `build-test` failures were
undiagnosable: libint's codegen chatter overflowed the CI runner's 4 MB
trace cap at job minute ~35 (the 5_4_3-era cold build already truncated at
minute ~22 even on success), so the actual error — which struck ~127 min
later, inside the never-before-compiled 5_4_4 generated-kernel build — was
discarded in all three attempts. `build_libint.sh` now routes its
codegen + compile output to `third_party/libint/build.log` via the new
sourceable helper `scripts/_build_log.sh` (per-minute heartbeat with
elapsed time, last Ninja step, and disk/memory headroom; last 200 log
lines replayed on failure; `VIBEQC_BUILD_VERBOSE=1` restores streaming).
The change is logging-only and sits inside `vibeqc-recipe-hash
lifecycle-only` markers, so libint's recipe hash — and therefore every dev
box and fleet install — is unaffected (pinned by
`tests/test_build_log_contract.py`). CI additionally uploads the build log
as an on-failure artifact, prints a disk/memory snapshot at job start, and
banks the `third_party/*/install/` cache `when: always`, so a job that
completes libint but fails later no longer forces the next attempt to
repeat the full multi-hour cold build. The 5_4_4 default itself is
verified buildable: a full cold build from the RC tree completes green
(22.5 min wall / M5 Max, peak 2.2 GB per compile worker, 7.9 GB build
tree, install headers `eri 5 / eri1 4 / eri2 4`, marker `5_4_4`).

### Fixed: periodic BIPOLE density artifacts use the returned SCF state (2026-08-13)

Periodic QVF density preparation no longer copies a converged BIPOLE
density onto an unrelated fixed 18-bohr overlap template. Full,
uniform Monkhorst-Pack results are transformed from the returned real-space
density on one exact Born-von-Karman torus, then refolded against every
returned lattice block before grid evaluation. Unrestricted alpha and beta
channels are certified independently and combined only after that check, so
k-point phases, weights, occupations, spin populations, and any converged
density mixing remain those of the SCF result. No orbitals or surrogate
Hamiltonian are rebuilt.

The grid contraction now uses the same-cell `sum_g D(g):S(g)` orientation,
retains every mathematically nonzero translated block, and writes voxel rows
from the primitive column-vector lattice. Density output is emitted only
after the returned lattice trace, radius-2 to radius-3 AO-image convergence,
and the numerical primitive-cell electron count agree. Missing or malformed
lattice metadata, nonuniform or incomplete k meshes, non-refoldable density
sets, and true multi-k per-k matrix lists now produce a clear nonfatal output
diagnostic and a valid QVF without `volume.density` instead of an approximate
artifact. Molecular QVF output and legacy empty-occupation handling are
unchanged.

### Fixed: multi-k GAPW had no SCF mixing, so expanded cells never converged (2026-08-13)

The multi-k GAPW SCF updated its density as `D_total = D_new` -- a bare
Roothaan fixed-point iteration with no DIIS, damping or mixing of any kind,
where multi-k GDF carries DIIS plus dynamic damping plus accelerators and
even the Gamma GAPW driver has DIIS. An undamped fixed point converges only
while the iteration map is contractive, so the route worked on gapped cells
and failed once bands overlapped -- the reported
`MULTIK-GAPW-BLOCH-FAILS-ON-EXPANDED-CELLS` symptom.

`run_periodic_rks_gapw_multi_k` gains `damping=` (linear density mixing,
