same convention as the Gamma driver, **default 0.0 so every existing run is
bit-identical**). With it, the LiH rocksalt/STO-3G/LDA/(2,2,2) lattice scan
converges at all three scales and agrees with the PySCF-validated GDF
route: **+16.65 / -26.13 / -0.15 mHa** at 1.00 / 1.60 / 2.20x the
equilibrium lattice constant, against a previously non-converging +198 /
+274 mHa. Scale 2.20 needs `damping=0.95` and about 200 iterations.

This is a convergence-machinery fix, not a functional one, and the evidence
distinguishes them: equilibrium is bit-identical across damping values,
scale 1.60 converges to the same energy (-7.750456, six decimals) at two
different damping factors, and the converged energies agree with GDF --
2.20 to 0.15 mHa, better than equilibrium, because nearly isolated atoms
let the per-atom augmentation residuals cancel between routes. A defective
functional cannot converge to the right answer.

Follow-up: DIIS on this driver, so users need not hand-tune a damping
factor.

### Fixed: BIPOLE route audit closes silent Hamiltonian substitutions (2026-08-13)

The end-to-end route audit found several accepted options and post-SCF tasks
that either changed the Hamiltonian silently or reported a method that had not
run. BIPOLE now fails before SCF for ECP-bearing bases, periodic Hessians,
TDDFT, explicit COOP/COHP, non-Fermi-Dirac smearing flavours, closed-shell
multi-k READ restarts without a complete real-space density, and optimization
with dispersion or symmetry constraints that the optimizer cannot preserve.
Implicit QVF output no longer rebuilds DOS/PDOS/COOP/COHP from a fixed-cutoff
HF-like surrogate operator.

Supported paths now preserve the selected Hamiltonian more faithfully:

- public symmetry controls reach all BIPOLE driver callsites;
- unrestricted AUTO Fock reduction stays off unless electronic-state
  covariance is established; explicit reduction now rejects ATOMSPIN, MOM,
  spin-lock, READ/PATOM, warm-density, and site-selective +U controls instead
  of projecting a broken-spin solution into a different symmetry basin;
- UHF/UKS spin-schedule phases retain `exact_zone_bohr`;
- optimization retains the electronic and nuclear cutoffs, exact zone,
  exchange convention, short-range image policy, range screening, BZ
  integration, MOM controls, and DFT+U state;
- open-shell periodic coefficients reach QVF wavefunction preparation;
- RHF results record the electron count and occupations used by SCF, and band
  and orbital summaries classify frontiers from occupations across both spin
  channels instead of the arbitrary sign of an orbital energy; fractional
  occupations are identified without inferring zero-temperature metallicity;
- AUTO routes dim=1 UHF/UKS to the maintained GDF backend instead of selecting
  the public 3D-only BIPOLE route;
- periodic optimization no longer falls through from an executed GPW, GAPW,
  RIJCOSX, direct, or other backend to a BIPOLE objective; uncaptured routes
  fail closed. BIPOLE variable-cell entry points also fail closed because the
  historical strain map used the wrong general-lattice convention and the
  coupled atom/cell optimizer could certify gradients from different
  geometries;
- AUTO Gamma +U plans the exact BIPOLE backend before dry-run instead of
  silently swapping a GDF choice to a truncated DIRECT Coulomb Hamiltonian;
  low-dimensional AUTO +U fails closed;
- open-shell BIPOLE smearing records and renders separate alpha and beta
  chemical potentials instead of labeling the alpha value as a shared Fermi
  level;
- finite-temperature BIPOLE optimization fails closed until optimizer and
  trajectory/QVF schemas distinguish the Mermin free-energy objective from
  internal energy; fixed-geometry smeared SCF remains available;
- GDF optimization likewise rejects positive final temperatures and periodic
  dispersion before dry-run: its analytic smeared force is $dA/dR$, but the
  optimizer/QVF schema would label $A$ as ordinary energy, while its captured
  SCF rerun does not add or differentiate D3 at candidate geometries. Legacy
  Gamma fallbacks, nonuniform k weights, unsupported bulk pure-RKS fits, and
  dim=1 gradients now fail in the same preflight instead of after an SCF;
  the documented empty, `none`, and `diis` density-mixer aliases remain on the
  same explicit-Gamma fast path as the default rather than changing the SCF
  objective;
- periodic GDF KS rejects VV10/nonlocal-correlation and double-hybrid
  functionals before work instead of labeling an SCF that omitted the VV10
  potential or perturbative MP2 correlation term;
- converged UKS smearing reports the free energy formed from the rebuilt final
  density rather than the stale pre-rebuild energy;
- periodic Gaussian NEB rejects low-dimensional cells, dispersion, ECP,
  READ/FRAGMO restarts, and closed-shell PATOM requests before dry-run or image
  evaluation;
- every direct BIPOLE result now rebuilds Fock, energy, DFT+U, component
  history, and the terminal commutator on the exact returned density, even
  after iteration-budget exhaustion; provisional convergence is rechecked on
  that state and finite-temperature progress reports the Mermin objective;
- the historical BIPOLE ODA hook now fails closed because a line-search mixed
  density has no single orbital representation (and the unrestricted slope
  omitted one spin direction);
- restricted-open-shell corrected exchange uses the same padded short-range
  image domain as the four direct drivers, validates complete full-mesh
  weights, and rejects unsupported reduced, twisted, READ, smearing, Fock
  mixing, and +U requests before execution;
- shifted and multi-k UHF/UKS spin diagnostics use the weighted complex
  Brillouin-zone expression instead of a single Gamma block; unrestricted
  Ewald result producers now retain the occupations used by SCF for band and
  orbital summaries. Gamma and multi-k unrestricted Ewald exits now return
  orbitals, occupations, densities, Focks, energies, and terminal trace data
  from one physically evaluated state, with a density fixed-point look-ahead
  preventing provisional or iteration-capped false convergence;
- direct BIPOLE requests for iterative eigensolvers fail closed instead of
  silently running the dense solver, and RKS/UKS damping is range-validated;
- smeared and Gilat-Raubenheimer densities require the corrected Ewald
  J/exchange-split gauge; the legacy gauge now fails closed instead of
  reconstructing its long-range Hartree density with integer occupations.

The same audit repaired the geometry and reaction-path front doors. Fixed-cell
BIPOLE optimization now rejects low-dimensional, non-stationary k-mesh,
legacy-gauge, ECP, READ, finite-temperature, and variable-cell requests before
work. Periodic Gaussian NEB uses a complete validated 3D MP/IBZ mesh, checks
every displaced SCF, applies the same DFT+U energy and gradient, and rejects
unsupported ECP, dispersion, smearing, iterative-solver, and restart modes
before dry-run. Molecular Gaussian NEB now preserves the requested functional,
DefGrid3 or explicit grid, SAD/PATOM/ATOMSPIN/READ initial state, and Hubbard
gradient; path-backed READ is resolved before dry-run with file paths taking
precedence over cached matrices. Unsupported ECP, DF/COSX, multi-guess,
SPIN_SCHEDULE, VV10-gradient, and double-hybrid paths fail closed. Its periodic
minimum-image geometry is now correct for column-vector skew lattices, and an
exhausted band no longer pairs an unevaluated geometry with stale observables.

Direct hybrid components were corrected as well: unrestricted legacy/direct
Fock builds use the full per-spin exchange coefficient, so closed-shell RKS
and UKS agree in 1D/2D diagnostics, and KS results report disjoint Coulomb-J
and HF-exchange components instead of including exchange in both fields.

The audit also fixed a molecular NEB `UnboundLocalError` caused by normalizing
the requested method after its first use. Route, restart, optimizer, output,
smearing, frontier, NEB, and safe-cutoff regression lanes cover these changes.

### Fixed: BIPOLE quartet far-field requests fail closed (2026-08-13)

The four direct BIPOLE drivers no longer advertise the dormant quartet-level
multipole far-field as their default. An explicit
`use_multipole_far_field=True` now raises before SCF setup; the supported
default remains the exact Ewald-J-split route. The audit found that the exact
Fock contraction spans three lattice translations and contracts the density
at their relative translation, while the experimental dispatch, skip mask,
and add-back span only two. Enabling the branch would therefore remove and
restore different periodic quartet domains. Driver, slow-SCF, and retired-
artifact tests now enforce the fail-closed boundary instead of comparing the
exact route with itself.

The user guide and implementation status no longer claim default-on,
hexadecapole/L6, symmetry, exchange, or gradient production coverage for the
prototype. The BIPOLE citation route now includes the 1988 crystalline-HF
monograph that defines the full periodic bipolar quartet sum, and the Pisani-
Dovesi 1980 DOI typo in `_sph_to_cart.py` is corrected.

### Fixed: post-convergence UKS memory spike from the default-on stability analysis (2026-08-13)

The internal stability analysis that runs after every converged UKS SCF
(default-on since 2026-08-08, commits `7a5ed0175` + `83dba8616`) built
its f_xc kernel from dense whole-grid AO tables: ~15 concurrent
`n_pts x n_bf` extents across setup and each Davidson matvec. On a
261-basis-function UKS/PBE/def2-QZVPP DF witness (Lebedev-29 x
75-radial grid) the job ran its entire 14-iteration SCF at ~0.73 GB
RSS and then spiked to 5.36 GB after convergence — invisible to the
memory preflight (estimate: 0.93 GB) and scaling as `n_pts x n_bf`
toward OOM on mid-size systems.

The stability wrapper now uses a memory-bounded polarised kernel
builder (`make_batched_polarised_xc_kernel_builder`) that stores only
O(n_pts) per-point vectors and re-evaluates AOs in 4,096-point slices
inside every matvec — the same streaming contract the batched SCF-loop
XC quadrature uses. The witness peak drops from 5.36 GB to the
stability-off envelope; the matvec is algebraically identical to the
dense builders (pinned by batched-vs-dense equivalence tests for LDA
and GGA in `tests/test_xc_kernel.py`). The opt-in Newton/TRAH
second-order builders keep their documented dense whole-grid caches
and preflight charges.

### Changed: `run_job(density_fit=...)` now governs the coupled-cluster route (CCSDT-SILENT-DF-DEFAULT, 2026-08-13)

**Behaviour change.** The top-level `density_fit=` keyword was wired
onto the RHF / UHF / RKS / UKS option structs only. The coupled-cluster
step read its route from `CCSDOptions.density_fit`, whose constructor
default is `True`, so `run_job(method="ccsd(t)", density_fit=False)` ran
**DF-CCSD(T)** — the request was dropped with no warning. Payloads have
no `ccsd_options=` surface at all, so a payload-driven job could not
reach the conventional route by any means. Two published parity cells
(`m12_ccsd_h2o_ccpvdz`, `qcil_00797_lih_ccsdt_cc_pvqz`) compared a
silently density-fitted vibe-qc leg against a conventional ORCA leg and
read the fitting error — 1.414e-04 Ha and 2.626e-05 Ha — as method
error.

- `density_fit` now defaults to `None` ("not specified") instead of
  `False`. Unset behaves exactly as before: a direct four-index SCF, and
  each post-SCF method on its own default, which for coupled cluster
  remains density fitting on.
- An explicit `density_fit=True`/`False` is a whole-job request and now
  selects the coupled-cluster integral route too, so
  `run_job(method="ccsd(t)", density_fit=False)` runs conventional
  CCSD(T). **Callers who passed `density_fit=False` on a CC job meaning
  "direct SCF" now get the much more expensive conventional CC route;
  omit the kwarg to restore the previous behaviour.**
- Passing `density_fit=` together with a `ccsd_options=` whose
  `density_fit` disagrees raises `ValueError` naming both, instead of
  silently picking a winner.
- One resolver (`_resolve_cc_density_fit`) now answers the question at
  all three sites that ask it — the fail-early RI-aux gate, the memory
  pre-flight, and the execution block — so the estimate and the run
  cannot disagree about the route (the BUG 117 failure mode). A
  conventional CCSD(T) on a basis with no registered RI auxiliary
  (STO-3G) consequently no longer trips the aux gate.

The `.out` method block was already truthful (`Algorithm = CCSD(T)` vs
`DF-CCSD(T)`, `Density fitting = on/off`, `RI auxiliary basis`) and is
now pinned for the kwarg-driven route as well
(`tests/test_ccsd_canonical_noDF.py`).

### Fixed: `.perf.json` artefacts contained plain text, not JSON (PERF-JSON-PLAIN-TEXT, 2026-08-13)

`perf_log=` wrote the human-readable performance report to whatever path
it was given, including paths the caller had named `*.json`. Campaign
payloads pass `perf_log="<stem>.perf.json"`, so 545 of 545 converged
rp209 cases shipped an artefact that began `==== / vibe-qc performance /
debug log` and on which `json.loads()` raised — defeating every
automated performance harvest, and flagged by four consecutive
judgement runs.

- The perf writer now dispatches on the target's suffix: `*.json` gets a
  JSON object, everything else (including the default `.perf` sibling)
  gets the unchanged text report.
- New `vibeqc.output.formats.perf.format_perf_json`, schema
  `vibeqc.perf/1`: `schema`, `pid`, `threads`, `total_wall_s`,
  `n_phases`, `phases[]` (with `wall_s`, `cpu_s`, `pct_wall`,
  `parallelism`), `memory_snapshots[]`, and the per-iteration
  `scf_iters[]` rows verbatim. Durations are raw seconds and memory raw
  MiB — no unit suffixes to re-parse. `parallelism` is `null`, never a
  fabricated `0.0`, when `wall_s` is zero.
- The `.system` manifest's `role = "perf"` entry now declares
  `format = "json"` for a JSON target instead of always claiming
  `"text"`, so a harvest can tell the renderings apart without sniffing
  bytes.
- Documented in `docs/user_guide/output_files.md` § JSON perf artefact.

### Fixed: GFN2-xTB water O-H PES shape — E_rep restored to the total energy (2026-08-12)

`712a589fd` removed the classical repulsion term E_rep from the GFN2-xTB
total-energy assembly on the assumption that H0 already "folds in" the
repulsion.  The GFN2-xTB primary literature (Bannwarth, Ehlert & Grimme,
JCTC 2019, Eqs. 8-9 / Section 2.1.2) defines E_rep as a separate zeroth-order
classical pairwise term that "does not contribute to the tight-binding
electronic energy": dropping it removes the short-range repulsive wall, and
the water O-H potential energy surface collapses (minimum pushed to the
scan edge, no well in either direction).  E_rep is now restored in all four
drivers (molecular, k-points, periodic, unrestricted) together with its
analytic gradient/stress contributions; vibe-qc's repulsion matches live
xtb 6.7.1 to ~1e-8 Ha, and the water O-H minimum lands at 1.81 bohr
(experimental 1.81; xtb 6.7.1 on the identical geometry gives the same
minimum).  The three previously-xfailed PES-shape tests
(`TestGFN2PESGate` + `test_faithful_water_pes_minimum_near_equilibrium`)
now pass as active gates; the strict water-dimer and H2 xtb-oracle parity
gates are unchanged.  A residual electronic-term gap vs xtb remains (water
~15 mHa, adenine ~245.7 mHa) and is tracked as BUG-027 / the STO-NG table
investigation — the GFN2 experimental gate is unchanged.

### Fixed: SCC-DFTB finite-temperature retry is the default runner path (2026-08-12)

Pi-conjugated N/O systems (furan, pyridine, imidazole, triazine, cytosine,
pyrimidine, H2CO, HCOOH, S22 dimers) have no converged integer-occupation
SCC fixed point at T=0: near-degenerate frontier pi/pi* orbitals make the
Mulliken charge response discontinuous, and no mixer stabilises it.  The
`run_job(method="scc_dftb")` route now retries a zero-T failure on the
bounded Mermin ladder verified against all six Thiel pi-conjugated systems:

| Rung | electronic temperature | DIIS | charge mixing |
|------|------------------------|------|---------------|
| 1 | 0.001 Ha (~316 K) | off | 0.05 |
| 2 | 0.0012 Ha (~379 K) | off | 0.05 |
| 3 | 0.0015 Ha (~474 K) | off | 0.05 |

Zero-T-passing systems are untouched (bit-identical energies; the ladder is
reached only after a zero-T failure).  The result and the `.out` now report
the electronic temperature, the cumulative iteration count, and the Mermin
free-energy convention (`E_free = E_internal - T*S`, both labeled).  The
ladder settings are Python-side only: the SCC-DFTB Hamiltonian, parameters,
and energy expression are unchanged.

### Fixed: DF/RIJCOSX memory preflight underestimates (BUG 117 / issue #13, 2026-08-12)

Three cooperating defects made the pre-flight memory estimate a severe
lower bound for density-fitted SCF jobs (BH9 campaign: 515 of 822
def2-QZVPP DF jobs OOM-killed; measured underestimates 2.1-2.6x on the
options-struct path and >10x on the kwarg path):

- **`run_job(density_fit=True)` was preflighted as a direct-SCF job.**
  The `density_fit`/`cosx`/`aux_basis` keyword arguments were wired onto
  the SCF option structs only immediately before the SCF call — after
  both the dry-run estimate (`vq submit auto` RAM placement) and the
  real-run memory pre-flight. The wiring now happens before the dry-run
  short-circuit, so every estimator call sees the DF configuration.
- **The four-extent DF construction peak was gated to n_basis > 500.**
  The native `DensityFitting` constructor (cpp/src/df.cpp) holds four
  `n_aux * n_orb^2` extents simultaneously (raw `Eri3D T`, packed
  `T_flat_`, solve product `B_flat`, unpacked `B_per_P_`) at every basis
  size. The two-resident-blocks x 2x-construction model now applies
  without a size gate (measured witness: UKS n_bf 261 true peak
  1.088 GB vs 0.516 GB estimated). The RIJCOSX path charges the same
  layout — its JK builder embeds the same `DensityFitting`. The
  DF-UCCSD integral-build term switches to the Python `DensityFitting`
  layout it actually uses (two resident extents, reshape views, no extra
  construction factor).
- **`n_aux` disagreed between estimate and execution when `aux_basis`
  was empty.** The estimator charged the generic `3 * n_basis` bound
  (Eichkorn 1995, Eq. 26) while the driver auto-resolves the def2
  JK-fitting default. The estimator now resolves the same default and
  falls back to the published bound only when no default is registered.

Also removed stray always-on `DEBUG:` stderr prints from the DF
aux-resolution path in `runner.py` (left over from the BUG 64/88 work).

### Fixed: BIPOLE far-field L=3/L=4 pair moments (review B4, 2026-08-12)

Three defects in the BIPOLE far-field moment pipeline, each pinned by a new
machine-exact test:

- **Octupole and hexadecapole pair-center shifts double-counted the
  translation** in both the Python (`bipole_pair_moments.py`) and C++
  (`bipole_pair_moments.cpp`) implementations: the multi-index binomial
  shift formulas were fed already-shifted lower-order moments where
  unshifted origin moments belong. Measured octupole error O(50) absolute
  at a 2.6-bohr shift. Both now use unshifted source moments; the shift is
  machine-exact through L=4 against independent-origin libint references
  and an analytic point-mass model.
- **The L=4 spherical merge consumed libint `sphemultipole` values in the
  wrong normalization.** libint emits Perez-Jorda & Yang scaled solid
  harmonics (JCP 104, 8003 (1996)); the merge reconstructed Cartesian
  hexadecapoles against the far-field `cartesian_to_spherical_matrix`
  convention without converting, leaving degree-4 content wrong by exact
  per-m factors up to 96*sqrt(5) (~215x). `_sph_to_cart` now applies the
  derived diagonal conversion (`_L4_LIBINT_TO_MODULE`), verified
  symbolically and against brute-force quadrature moments.
- **`pair_center_moments` silently basis-mixed raw spherical input**
  (treated 25 spherical components as the leading Cartesian ones,
  zero-padded). It now fails closed pointing at the sound merge route.

The previous round-trip recovery test was circular (it asserted the raw
libint values back) and has been corrected; the strict xfail that pinned
the corruption is replaced by pass-gates on the production merged route
(l <= 3 exactness plus an l = 4 spherical-content pin at a displaced
origin). Citation `perez_jorda_yang_1996` added to the database on the
bipole route.

### Fixed: removed vibe-view labels stay removed after camera moves (2026-08-12)

vibe-view's camera-facing label registry now treats the live actor collection
as the source of ownership. When a scene rebuild, label toggle, section change,
or other cleanup removes an atom-index or atom-charge label actor, the next
camera interaction prunes its stale registry entry instead of recreating the
hidden overlay. Labels that remain in the scene still reorient normally, and a
new non-label actor cannot inherit stale label behavior merely by reusing its
name.

### Added: embedded-cluster CAS package, landed as gated research provenance (2026-08-12)

The `embedded-cluster-cas` branch (14 commits, 2026-06-14 to 06-20, ~4057
lines) is absorbed onto `main` at maintainer request during a branch cleanup,
so nothing is lost when the branch goes. It brings `python/vibeqc/embed/`
(Evjen and Derenzo-Klintenberg-Weber Madelung array builders, an OpenMolcas
AIMP library parser, an AIMP-to-libecpint ECP converter, cluster carve, the
`embed_cluster` driver, an out-of-process OpenMolcas XField runner), an
OpenMolcas parity test module, a convergence example, the CAS-in-CCM design
contract, and three citation entries with a `[routes.embed]` table.

**It is gated, and deliberately not shipped as supported API.** The
`handovers/HANDOVER_PERIODIC_MULTIREF.md` orphan-branch audit of 2026-07-15
reviewed this branch and declined it, finding: MR6 uses formal charges rather
than the periodic-SCF-density route and mis-enumerates translated/skew cells;
MR7 omits the AIMP `PROJOP` projector/orthogonality terms; MR8 omits NEVPT2
and hand-formats a report outside `vibeqc.output` (CLAUDE.md section 16); MR9
is a printing example rather than a regression; MR10 exercises only RHF XField
behind an OpenMolcas skip; and the `[routes.embed]` table is not consumed by
the current citation registry (section 8). Its verdict is unchanged: this is
research provenance, and each production increment should be re-derived
against current `main` using it only as a reference.

Landing it therefore does not close MR6-MR10. Per CLAUDE.md section 14 the
incomplete work is gated rather than left for a later chat to discover:

* **No top-level export.** `vq.embed_cluster` does not exist; the branch's
  `python/vibeqc/__init__.py` re-export was dropped. Reach it explicitly with
  `from vibeqc import embed`.
* The package docstring opens with the full defect list above and states that
  every number it produces is unvalidated.
* The branch's root-level `MEMORY.md` moved to
  `studies/embedded-cluster-cas/GOTCHAS.md`; a repo-root `MEMORY.md` collides
  with the per-chat memory-index convention.

Licensing checked (section 1): no AIMP data is bundled. The parser reads from
the user's own OpenMolcas installation at runtime and writes ECP XML to a temp
dir, which is the on-demand pattern section 1 prescribes; the branch's own note
records that LGPL 2.1 AIMP data and MPL 2.0 are incompatible for bundling.
Section 10 checked too: no external QC program is imported in-process,
OpenMolcas is driven by `subprocess` only.

### Fixed: heap write past the end of `gamma` in `DensityFitting::build_J_screened` (2026-08-12)

`cpp/src/df.cpp` sized `gamma` by the **orbital** basis dimension
(`n_orb_idx`) and then indexed it by the **auxiliary** index `P`, which runs to
`n_aux_`. An auxiliary basis is routinely 3-4x the orbital basis, so every
`P >= n_orb_` wrote past the end of the Eigen vector. Sized `n_aux_` now,
matching the correct sibling `build_J` in the same file.

**Severity is low today because the function is unreachable**: `build_J_screened`
is declared in `cpp/include/vibeqc/df.hpp` and defined in `df.cpp`, but nothing
in `cpp/`, `python/` or `tests/` calls it and it is not bound into Python. It is
exported dead API, so the overflow would land on whoever wires up the first
caller. The written value is also never read back inside the function (`gP` is
used directly on the following line), so the write is pure corruption with no
compensating behaviour, and fixing it cannot change any result.

Found in the `codex-ab-initio-remediation` audit branch (`8c03dd421`,
2026-05-26), which never landed and is being retired in a branch cleanup; the
defect was re-verified against current main before fixing rather than
cherry-picked.

### Fixed: batched vibe-view bonds retain order, colour, and replicated cells (2026-08-12)

vibe-view's large-scene bond path now preserves the same single, double, and
triple multiplicity and bond-order palette as the established per-bond path.
Homogeneous batches keep that colour on the actor, while mixed-order meshes
carry a direct RGB value per cylinder. Selected bonds stay in their white
partition; unselected bonds retain their order colours, and material presets
can still deliberately recolour every bond uniformly.

The outer threshold decision is now authoritative across the complete
replicated scene. A structure whose total replicated bond count exceeds the
threshold keeps one uniquely named batched actor per cell and selection
partition, even when a single cell contains fewer than 50 bonds. This prevents
replicas from repeatedly replacing an actor named for the same atom pair. The
small-system path and its `bond_{i}_{j}` / multiplicity actor names are
unchanged.
### Fixed: vq scheduler submission, replay, and daemonless accounting durability

- Python directory, archive, and single-file submissions now validate the
  actual staged entrypoint before queue, workspace, upload, or scheduler
  mutation. Managed daemonless Python routing no longer falls back to system
  Python or inserts an extra literal `python` for a single-file payload.
- `vq doctor` gives every external probe a finite deadline, bounds captured
  output, and reaps its owned process group on timeout. Rollout planning keeps
  exact scheduler-alias fences and fail-closed parity holds during partial
  updater deployment.
- Scheduler-target dispatch persists a submit-once phase and reconciles a
  versioned remote receipt or exact start marker. Ambiguous evidence remains
  nonterminal, reserves capacity, retains staging, and is never submitted
  again automatically. Daemonless terminal refresh remains bounded and
  fail-closed on unknown scheduler evidence.
- `vq submit --idempotency-key KEY` provides opt-in, owner-scoped single-job
  replay at the queue authority. The authority scope binds the execution state
  store and authenticated owner; the canonical intent binds the scheduler
  target, program and runtime pin, payload, name, argv, resources,
  dependencies, tags, and execution flags. Same intent returns the original
  job ID; conflicting reuse fails. Durable claims survive ordinary job
  deletion, while retry, resubmit, rerun-until, and auto-resume do not inherit
  the key.
- Remote timeout, SSH/signal ambiguity, and incomplete receipts retain their
  typed outcome through text and JSON interfaces without automatic replay.
  Proven acceptance cannot be masked by advisory warnings or cleanup.
- The release-paper supervisor durably fsyncs `jobs.tsv` and its parent,
  records a strict versioned keyed `submitting` receipt before invoking vq,
  and reconciles persisted claims before new work. Missing or invalid receipts
  and negative, timed-out, or otherwise ambiguous process outcomes become
  `submit-outcome-unknown`, preserving existing jobs across restart. Its only
  replay is the exact persisted command under the same queue-authority key
  after strict intent and current-host audit validation; the generic CLI still
  never auto-replays ambiguous transport outcomes.
- Scheduler hosts may publish a strict positive lane wall-time maximum.
  Over-limit jobs are rejected before staging rather than silently clamped.
  Daemonless Slurm terminal fetch projects bounded `sacct` CPU and MaxRSS data
  into the existing sample schema without overwriting process-tree samples or
  delaying terminal lifecycle and capacity release.

All source correctness evidence for this audit is local and source-side; no
live queue submission, daemon operation, scheduler command, deployment, or
fleet rollout was used to establish the source verdicts. See the handover for
the separately disclosed unintended legacy-test SCP side effect. The reported
near-capacity SIGKILL still requires an explicitly authorized live stress test
before its root cause can be declared fixed, and the Torque memory-directive
correction still requires deployment.

An authorized exact-SHA vq self-update mini-cycle subsequently deployed
`85885fd83c4d6f36fe3119b3e83941a1d1e8913e` to the local driver and to the
canonical site_j and site_i scheduler helpers. The driver restarted healthy at
the exact source and installed-tree identities; both helpers activated
atomically without draining active jobs. site_j used one scheduler maintenance
allocation for the helper build. Daemonless Slurm accounting remains
operationally open until an authorized short site_j job proves that fetch
returns `_vq/samples.jsonl`; historical waves remain without resource evidence.

### Fixed: restore `examples/experimental/coulomb-method-zoo/`, which main already links to (2026-08-12)

`docs/release_v0_8_0_prep.md` line 238 publishes a GitLab `/blob/main/` URL to
`examples/experimental/coulomb-method-zoo/bug_compute_2c_eri_pshell.py`. That
path did not exist on main, so the link has been dead on both `main` and
`release`. The directory lived only on `claude/jolly-bohr-97bce6`, which a
branch cleanup was about to delete; git history shows it was never merged and
never deleted, i.e. simply never landed rather than declined. Restored whole
(8 files, additive, nothing else touched), which makes the published link
resolve.

What was nearly lost, none of it recorded elsewhere on main:

* The three-line no-SCF reproducer main links to by URL.
* `POSTMORTEM.md`, a measured four-method comparison of periodic Coulomb J
  builders on H2: the EWALD3D-vs-PLAIN_EWALD grid convergence establishing
  h=0.3 bohr as the right spacing for sto-3g (h=0.60 gives 3.96e-3, h=0.30
  reaches the 8.4e-7 FFT noise floor, h=0.15 buys nothing), the Wolf-summation
  rejection with its alpha sweep, the ADFT auxiliary rank-deficiency result,
  and the Makov-Payne gauge-pairing trap with the explicit
  method-to-`CoulombMethod` pairing rule.
* `results/bench_h2_jonly.json`, the raw sweep data behind those numbers.

A negative result nobody else has: Wolf summation and PLAIN_EWALD have zero
mentions anywhere on main, so a future survey of periodic Coulomb methods would
have re-spent this work and re-derived the same rejection.

The prototype builders themselves (`j_builders.py`, `scf_driver.py`, the bench
drivers) are superseded by main's analytic AO-pair-FT machinery and native GDF.
They are kept as the runnable provenance for the numbers above, under
`examples/experimental/`, not as a recommended path.

**One thing for the maintainer to adjudicate, recorded not resolved.** The
POSTMORTEM states the `compute_2c_eri` l>=1 SIGSEGV was "NOT a libint
build-config issue", citing the vendored `config.h`
(`LIBINT_ERI2_MAX_AM_LIST = 5,4,3`) and placing the fault in `cpp/src/df.cpp`'s
Engine usage. `docs/troubleshooting.md` line 233 treats that SIGSEGV as fixed
and attributes any residual reports from older checkouts to a stale libint
built without ERI2/ERI3 flags. These are not necessarily in conflict, since the

### Added: rescue the HF-on-pob-TZVP-rev2 failure scout onto main (2026-08-12)

`docs/basisset_dev/HF_REV2_FAILURE_SCOUT_2026-05-18.md` existed only on the
abandoned rebase branch `claude/stupefied-burnell-b2cb48`, which is being
deleted in a branch cleanup. Every line of code on that branch had already
reached main under different SHAs and its handovers were deliberately retired
by `d5eef0aa0`, but this one file was absorbed nowhere.

It is measured data, not prose, from two dated passes on site_e and site_b:

* **2026-05-18**, ~19 CRYSTAL23 jobs over the 13 cubic-ionic compounds of
  PT2013 Table 4 on `pob-TZVP-rev2` at CRYSTAL's *default* `TOLINTEG`. LiF, CaO
  and MgO fail HF SCF through linear-dependence-driven DIIS collapse (CaO
  settling in a spurious basin far below the physical energy) while PBE and
  PW1PW converge in 7-9 cycles on the identical systems. Per CLAUDE.md § 7 it
  explicitly rules out damping/level-shift as the fix.
* **2026-05-19**, a 36-job three-basis by four-method grid that **revises that
  conclusion**. With `TOLINTEG 9 9 9 18 54` the same three compounds on the same
  rev2 keyword converge in 6-7 cycles, so the instability is a sensitivity to
  integral-cutoff defaults, not something intrinsic to the rev2 exponents. The
  one residual failure is CaO/HF on a user-supplied segmented basis. The report
  reframes Goal 8 from "rev2 is unstable for HF" to a variational-depth
  question, and records the operational consequence: any HF optimisation loop on
  rev2-class exponents must ship tight TOLINTEG or it will spuriously fail
  evaluations that have nothing to do with the candidate exponents.

That self-revision is why the whole file is worth keeping rather than a summary
of its headline: the first pass alone would mislead. Raw outputs were gitignored
and transient, so this is the permanent record; regenerating it means re-running
CRYSTAL23 on site_e.

Landed as a dated record, content unaltered; only em/en dashes were normalised
to satisfy the repo's no-dash prose hook. It sits alongside
`GOAL8_MPEI_TZVP.md`, which is on main, still "active", and carries the same
`Branch: basissetdev` header convention, so this follows existing practice
rather than merging basissetdev code (CLAUDE.md § 4 is unaffected: no code, no
basis sets).

### Fixed: large-protein cartoon startup no longer infers unused bonds (2026-08-12)

vibe-view now keeps structure geometry loading separate from bond-cache
initialization. Startup periodicity checks, element metadata, formula assembly,
and atom-property overlays read only the geometry they need. Within the initial
scene renderer, the cartoon reuses its cached structure without running
atom-pair bond inference. Space-filling stays geometry-only. Switching later to
ball-and-stick, sticks-only, or wireframe initializes connectivity once and
reuses it, including minimum-image inference for repeated periodic renders.

This removes a hidden startup regression for proteins: the default cartoon was
chosen specifically to avoid superlinear bond inference, but the app inspected
the same renderer through its eager `load()` path before drawing the ribbon.
Measured 13,772-atom inputs previously spent 158.7 seconds in that unused work
before the browser could connect. Renderer-contract and end-to-end app tests now
require protein startup to perform zero bond-inference calls.

### Added: residue selections now span every vibe-view representation (2026-08-12)

The existing `A`, `A/24-38`, and `*/24-38` residue selector is no longer
cartoon-only. For any structure with a CA-bearing residue, ball-and-stick and
space-filling render every atom in a selected residue white; sticks-only and
wireframe render a bond white when both endpoints are selected. Boundary bonds
remain unhighlighted, so selecting one residue does not make its neighbour look
selected. The cartoon's existing white ribbon highlight is unchanged.

The same path covers per-atom actors, large glyph-batched structures, periodic
replicas, and batched bonds. Empty or non-matching selections retain the old
actor grouping and colours. Selection availability and summaries now refresh
when the active file changes, and animation/charge-overlay restoration carries
the current selection instead of silently dropping it. Static-scene teardown
now removes batched bonds, selected-bond partitions, and cartoon ribbons, and
leaving compare mode rebuilds the selected structure instead of leaving an
empty scene. Isolate-selection and viewport click-to-select remain separate
follow-ups.

### Fixed: BUG 63 correlated-method memory strategies and estimator (2026-08-12)

MP2 and UMP2 now accept an explicit requested-memory budget with in-core,
integral-direct, and disk-backed occupied-orbital slab strategies. The
canonical direct path evaluates shell quartets without materializing the AO
four-index tensor or global OVOV tensor; the RI path contracts bounded panels
without global OVOV. Disk scratch is method-preserving, uniquely named,
cleaned on success and error, and reported alongside the realized mode and
modeled workspace.

Closed-shell DF-CCSD(T) triples now implement aggregate-budget fast, blocked,
factor-direct, and disk-backed strategies. The nominally tiled kernel's hidden
cubic temporaries are removed, disk mode spills and streams three-index
factors, and result telemetry records the realized mode, virtual tile, worker
count, full triples-phase peak, and scratch extent. Open-shell triples add a
scalar direct fallback while continuing to report the irreducible dense
spin-orbital four-index integral floor; open-shell disk mode fails closed.
All strategies preserve the separate `E[T]` and `E_ST` contributions,
including the semicanonical `Fov*T2` term.

Preflight now models SCF, density-fitting construction, correlation solve, and
triples as sequential phase peaks, honors frozen cores, and uses the same
occupied-slab/tile formulas as execution. A process-wide budget reserves
safety headroom and the live SCF result before deriving the smaller native
workspace cap. The fixed-thread O2/def2-SVP UCCSD(T) regression now estimates
about 212 MiB against the observed roughly 220 MiB peak, replacing the old
27 GiB (123x) estimate. Scaling regressions cover STO-3G, def2-SVP, cc-pVDZ,
and cc-pVTZ.

This does not close BUG 63's production evidence gate. Generic DF construction,
the dense CC iteration, A-CCSD(T), FNO/Brueckner setup, and the open-shell
four-index integral state retain irreducible dense phases. Crambin/cc-pVTZ,
formic-acid-dimer/cc-pVTZ, and FeCl3 remain outside the paper's production
claim until real constrained-RSS calculations complete at an immutable SHA.

### Added: PM7 semiempirical method — Stewart 2013 (2026-08-12)

The PM7 Hamiltonian (Stewart, J. Mol. Model. 19, 1, 2013) is now available
via `method='PM7'` and `SemiempiricalOptions(method='pm7')`. Includes native
MOPAC-derived parameters bundled as `pm7_mopac_params.toml`, a MOPAC parser
(`scripts/parse_mopac_pm7_params.py`), and initial regression coverage.

### Added: deterministic SCF restart, SOSCF guard, and state fingerprint (BUG 64 + BUG 88, 2026-08-12)

SCF now supports deterministic restart via `cpp/src/scf_restart.cpp` and
`python/vibeqc/state_fingerprint.py`. The SOSCF accelerator includes a
divergence guard. A multi-guess infrastructure (`state_fingerprint.py`)
captures the full SCF state for reproducible checkpointing.

### Fixed: D4 reference data packaged as installed resource (BUG 97, 2026-08-12)

The GFN2-xTB D4 reference dataset (`d4_reference_data.json`) is now bundled
as an installed package resource rather than relying on a repository-relative
path that broke on editable installs outside the checkout.
### Added: SECCM adapters for SCC-DFTB, PM6, OMx, and GFN2-xTB (2026-08-12)

The semiempirical cyclic-cluster boundary (SECCM), previously limited to
MSINDO INDO and a gated H/C DFTB0 energy adapter, now covers every shipped
semiempirical Hamiltonian:

- **SCC-DFTB-SECCM** (new C++ engine under `cpp/src/semiempirical/seccm/`):
  the DFTB0-SECCM supercell assembly (Wigner-Seitz weighted S and H0) plus
  an atomic charge SCF with the same vector-Aitken relaxation as the
  molecular driver and optional Pulay-DIIS or modified-Broyden charge
  accelerators (Broyden reuses `semiempirical/core/charge_mixer.hpp` and
  cuts the embedded two-cell chain from 70 to 14 iterations, same fixed
  point to 1e-9 Ha; both accelerators fail closed with a physicality
  fallback). The molecular limit reproduces `run_scc_dftb`
  (8e-15 Ha on H2O); a 1-D H-Li chain converges towards the independent
  k-point dense limit (1.2 mHa at 32 replicas). 1-D/2-D/3-D, closed-shell
  insulating cells. Charged supercells are supported through an opt-in
  Madelung/Ewald embedding (the validated MSINDO CCM kernels: 1-D finite
  Madelung sum, 2-D Parry/Heyes Ewald, 3-D Ewald), which couples the
  Mulliken fluctuations to the H^SCC diagonal and adds their classical
  self-energy; neutral cells do not need it. Even-replica charged polar
  1-D chains stay a documented fail-closed gap: the truncated 4-shell 1-D
  Madelung kernel makes the charge response nearly singular (period-2
  limit cycle under every mixer; see
  `handovers/HANDOVER_SECCM_ADAPTERS.md`).
- **SCC-DFTB-SECCM analytic gradients** (`compute_gradient=True`): the
  fixed-charge force on the frozen WS record set (M = -W +
  D . 1/2 (kappa hbar - V_A - V_B) overlap contraction, WS-weighted
  repulsive derivative, gamma derivative over live record displacements),
  normalized by the group order. The molecular limit is bit-identical to
  the molecular SCC-DFTB gradient (5.6e-16) and the neutral 1-D chain
  matches fixed-topology finite differences to 2e-9. Embedded cells
  (madelung=True) fall back to central differences of the converged
  energy (gradient_method="finite_difference"), since the diagonal
  Madelung shift leaves the SCC fixed point non-stationary in the
  Mulliken charges; the exact analytic force needs the CP-SCC charge
  response (route `scc-dftb-seccm-gradient-analytic`, still experimental).
- **PM6-SECCM** (new C++ engine): the supercell NDDO Fock with every
  directed two-center term (nuclear attraction, resonance, exchange,
  core-core repulsion) accumulated through the WS record weights, the
  same Bredow-Geudtner-Jug construction used by the MSINDO CCM engine.
  The molecular limit is bit-identical to `run_pm6`; gradients use
  fixed-topology central differences of the converged per-cell energy
  (`gradient_method="finite_difference"`), since the analytic molecular
  PM6 gradient is a documented calibration prototype.
- **GFN2-xTB pair-table and AES fixes (BUG-027)**: the
  Wolfsberg-Helmholtz K_ll' now uses the exact Bannwarth Table 2 pair
  values (ksd = kpd = 2.00 instead of the historical 2.04/2.23 shell
  average, which over-coupled d-polarization functions), and the
  faithful AES path gains `aes_damping` (default 0.5) so the on-site
  DPOL/QPOL polarization converges on polarizable heterocycles (adenine:
  period-2 cycle under simple mixing before, converged after; the
  damping is path-only and leaves the fixed point unchanged). The
  TAE-PTComp d/f-element pins were updated to the corrected energies.
- **OMx-SECCM and GFN2-SECCM** (molecular-limit slice): 1x1x1 cyclic
  clusters evaluate the validated molecular drivers bit-for-bit; any
  topology with a nonzero image shell fails closed with
  NotImplementedError until the multi-replica adapters land.
- Shared SECCM internals extracted from the validated DFTB0-SECCM adapter
  into `cpp/src/semiempirical/seccm/seccm_common.h` (record validation and
  WS-weighted DFTB assembly) and
  `python/vibeqc/semiempirical/seccm/_adapter_common.py`.

All new routes are experimental/native in the semiempirical route planner
(`scc-dftb-seccm-energy`, `scc-dftb-seccm-gradient-analytic`,
`pm6-seccm-energy`, `pm6-seccm-gradient-fd`, `omx-seccm-energy`,
`gfn2-seccm-energy`) and registered in the citation database.

### Added: `--libint-max-am`, and a default that reaches g-function Hessians (2026-08-06)

`scripts/build_libint.sh` generated its 2nd-derivative integral stratum at
`max_am=3`, so the analytic-Hessian path (Phase 17b) covered f functions
only and could not run on a g-function basis at all -- def2-TZVPP heavy
atoms, cc-pVQZ, def2-QZVP. The default is now `5_4_4` (every derivative
order at l_max >= 4), and the setting is a build option rather than a
literal in the recipe.

**The option.** `--libint-max-am N_N_N` on `install.sh`, `update.sh` and
`update_native_deps.sh` (environment variable `VIBEQC_LIBINT_MAX_AM`,
resolver at `scripts/_libint_max_am.sh`) sets the max angular momentum at
derivative orders 0/1/2, each part 1..6:

| Spec | Build | Energies | Gradients | Hessians |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `5_4_3` | ~30 min | h (L=5) | g (L=4) | f (L=3) |
| `5_4_4` (default) | ~1.5-2 h | h | g | g |
| `6_5_4` | longer | i (L=6) | h | g |
| `6_6_6` | longest | i | i | i |

Above a stratum's limit libint throws rather than returning a wrong
number, so the spec decides which basis sets each derivative order
accepts and nothing else -- no computed value changes with it. 6 is the
ceiling, and it is vibe-qc's rather than libint's: the periodic AO-pair FT
transforms through `cart_to_sph_data.hpp` (`kMaxL = 6`) and throws above
it, so a higher libint would emit integrals the periodic stack cannot
consume. The rejection message says that, and says what raising it would
take.

**Switching specs is safe in any direction**, which took two mechanisms,
because a build flag that lives outside the recipe file re-opens the
stale-install footgun documented in `docs/updating.md` -- the flags change
while the file on disk does not. (1) `_vibeqc_recipe_hash` folds the
effective spec into libint's v2 recipe hash, so a switch registers as
drift and `./scripts/update.sh` rebuilds libint -- and only libint. The
salt is applied to that one recipe, so no other dep's fingerprint moves
with the setting, and the v1 legacy hash is left unsalted since it is a
fixed-format artifact for readers predating the option. The stamp row
keeps its existing four fields. `vibeqc_stamp_check` reads the installed
marker and reports `BUILD-SETTING DRIFT (max_am=5_4_4 -> max_am=5_4_3)`
rather than a phantom change to `build_libint.sh`. (2) `build_libint.sh`
records the spec it built into `third_party/libint/install/.vibeqc-max-am`
and refuses to short-circuit on a tree carrying a different one.
`doctor.sh` reports the installed spec. A tree predating the marker is
trusted for the default spec and rebuilt for any other.

**The reviewed legacy-stamp alias for libint is retired.** `0255fec94` /
`cd8b3acf5` had whitelisted the pre-unified-lifecycle libint fingerprint so
those stamps migrated to v2 without recompiling, on the premise that only
lifecycle lines had changed. This change breaks that premise: those trees
were compiled at max_am 5;4;3 and their analytic Hessians cannot take a
g-function basis, so they now correctly report drift and rebuild.
`_vibeqc_reviewed_legacy_recipe_matches` keeps its shape for future
entries but admits none, with a comment warning against re-pinning it to
the current hash. libint is likewise dropped from the v0.15.121
fleet-migration tuple in `tests/test_native_dep_artifact_health.py`; the
other five deps are untouched and still migrate without rebuilding.

Documented in `docs/installation.md` and `docs/updating.md`; 48
shell-contract tests in `tests/test_libint_max_am_option.py`, including a
guard tying the ceiling to `kMaxL` and one pinning that the salt does not
leak past libint. Comments in `hessian_integrals.hpp`, `aopair_ft.hpp`,
`bindings.cpp` and `codegen_cart_to_sph.py` that asserted a fixed
`LIBINT2_MAX_AM = 5` are corrected (the regenerated `cart_to_sph_data.hpp`
diff is comment-only; the tables are unchanged).

**No libint rebuild has been run.** The option's parsing, drift detection,
short-circuit and cmake-argument emission are tested -- the last against a
stub `cmake` -- but nobody has compiled libint at `5_4_4` or run a
g-function analytic Hessian against it in this session. The ~1.5-2 h
figure is extrapolated from the previous ~30 min build via the `max_am^4`
kernel-count scaling, not measured.

### Fixed: erfc-screened BIPOLE far-field tensor truncated inconsistently in Python (2026-08-12)

`tests/test_bipole_contractor_parity.py::test_mgo_sto3g_erfc_screened_energy_match`
failed on `main` with a 0.9 % energy disagreement between the C++ and the
Python far-field contractor (C++ 2.588706815596806e-02, Python
2.612016516595338e-02, as measured before the review-B4 moment fix above
changed this test's inputs). Only the erfc-screened case diverged; the
bare Coulomb cases agreed to 1e-14.

The bipolar Taylor expansion of the two-body kernel is clamped at a total
Cartesian order `|alpha| + |beta|`, and
`sr_multipole_interaction_tensor` assembles the short-range tensor by
linearity as `T_bare - T_erf`. The clamp was written out twice in
`python/vibeqc/bipole_multipole.py` and the two copies had drifted:
`b2014370b` raised it from 3 to 4 in `screened_multipole_interaction_tensor`
but not in `multipole_interaction_tensor`. The order-4 block of the
short-range tensor therefore held `-T_erf` with no matching bare part —
on MgO/STO-3G an entry several times larger than every legitimate entry of
the tensor combined. The C++ contractor was correct throughout: it builds
the erfc tensor in a single pass from `d(1/r) - d(erf/r)`, so it cannot
develop this asymmetry.

Both clamps now read one named constant per language
(`_MAX_BIPOLAR_TOTAL_ORDER`, `kMaxBipolarTotalOrder`), documented as
required to move together. The value is unchanged at 3, so the C++ path and
every bare-Coulomb result are bit-identical to before; only the Python
erfc path moves, onto the C++ values.

The parity test's screened-energy tolerance was `rel=2e-3`, loose enough to
make a 0.9 % divergence read as a borderline tolerance question. It is now
`rel=1e-10` (measured agreement on the post-B4 tree: ~1e-14 relative on the
energy and ~3e-16 on Fock elements, i.e. OpenMP reduction order) and
additionally compares the Fock blocks, not only the contracted energy. `tests/test_bipole_multipole_l4.py` gains a structural check that
the bare and erf tensors share a clamp, a check that the short-range tensor
has no support outside the bare tensor's, and an element-wise C++-vs-Python
tensor parity test; its pre-existing `test_l4_sr_tensor_consistency` could
not have caught this, as it restates the implementation of the function it
tests.

Note that L=4 (hexadecapole) is still *not* delivered by either path: with
the clamp at total order 3, `multipole_interaction_tensor(4, 4, R)` returns
a 25x25 tensor whose `l1 + l2 > 3` blocks are zero. Completing the
`b2014370b` extension is deferred — see
`handovers/HANDOVER_BIPOLE_PRODUCTION.md`.

## [v0.15.130] - 2026-08-12 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Fixed: spin-squared structured-log event for unrestricted wavefunctions (BUG 77, 2026-08-12)

Unrestricted (UHF/UKS) calculations now emit a `spin_squared` structured-log
event carrying the expectation value ⟨S²⟩ and the deviation from the exact
eigenvalue S(S+1). Previously the event was missing for open-shell jobs.

### Fixed: ROKS Guest-Saunders canonicalisation fields propagated into ROKSResult (2026-08-12)

The `rohf_canonicalization`, `mo_energies_roothaan`, and `mo_coeffs_roothaan`
fields introduced in v0.15.126 for ROHF now propagate correctly into
ROKSResult for open-shell KS-DFT jobs.

### Added: regression coverage for the BIPOLE quartet tensor cache fallback (2026-08-12)

`build_quartet_tensor_cache`
(`python/vibeqc/bipole_quartet_tensor_cache.py`) probes
`vibeqc._vibeqc_core` for native interaction-tensor kernels and drops to
the pure-Python implementations in `bipole_multipole` when they are
absent. That fallback branch had no test of any kind, and it shipped
unable to execute.

`7e94c7f18` placed a function-local `from .bipole_quartet_far_field
import quartet_effective_screening_parameter` *inside* the
`if _use_cpp_tensor:` branch. Python binds a name imported anywhere in a
function body as function-local for the **entire** body, so that import
shadowed the working module-level binding, and the `else:` branch raised
`UnboundLocalError` on every `ewald_omega > 0` build. It was reachable:
any `_vibeqc_core` built before `1a26e6954` lacks the native symbols, so
the fallback is the live path there. It was also invisible — the sole
call site (`bipole_far_field_infrastructure`) wraps the builder in
`except Exception: pass` on the grounds that "cache is an optimisation",
so the error was swallowed and affected runs silently lost the cache and
re-assembled every quartet tensor per SCF iteration.

The crash itself was already fixed incidentally by `3f33caee9`, which
hoisted that import above its use while fixing an unrelated `mu_eff`
cache-key collision. Nothing pinned the behaviour, so
`tests/test_bipole_quartet_tensor_cache_fallback.py` (new) does: both
fallback sub-branches against their pure-Python references, agreement
between the key `build_quartet_tensor_cache` stores under and the key
`QuartetTensorCache.get` looks up (including `mu_eff`), native-kernel
dispatch arguments via stubs so the C++ path stays covered on an
extension predating the kernels, C++/Python numerical parity where the
native kernels exist, and an AST guard asserting that no function-local
import in `build_quartet_tensor_cache` shadows a module-level name —
pinning the invariant that was violated rather than the single symbol
that happened to expose it.

Two latent gaps in the same function are closed. The native probe tested
only `multipole_interaction_tensor` while the screened C++ path also
calls `multipole_erfc_interaction_tensor`, so an extension exposing one
without the other would satisfy the probe and then raise `ImportError`
mid-loop; the probe now requires both. Both native symbols are bound
under private `_cpp_*` aliases, and the redundant function-local import
of `quartet_effective_screening_parameter` is removed in favour of the
existing module-level one, so no name in the function shadows a
module-level binding. No behaviour change on either path.
### Fixed: closed-shell SCC-DFTB ran the DIIS accelerator that was meant to be off (2026-08-12)

`SCCDFTBModel(...)` defaulted `use_diis` to `True` while the C++ `SCCOptions`
struct defaulted it to `false`, and `dftb0.py` pushes the Python value onto the
options struct verbatim — so Python won and every closed-shell SCC-DFTB run
used the Pulay charge accelerator regardless of the C++ default.

The split dates to `868a3357f`, which added the accelerator with the default
true on both sides. `5535a0c78` ("restore Aitken as default") reverted only the
C++ struct — its diffstat is four C++ files. The BUG-023 revert series
(`64473ca61`, `8baca59e6`, `6c40ade60`, `19c7aad9a`) then restored "v0.15.116
state" faithfully, but v0.15.116 already carried the split, and `19c7aad9a`
covered only the bare `run_scc_dftb()` function and the periodic paths — not
the model constructor. `USCCDFTBModel` never sets the field, so open-shell was
never affected; this was closed-shell only.

Symptom was charge sloshing rather than a clean failure: on the Thiel set the
accelerator drove Mulliken charge excursions of several electrons per atom
between iterations, so molecules that should converge at zero temperature
instead exhausted the 500-iteration cap and fell through the finite-temperature
retry ladder — or exhausted it. `tests/test_runner_optimize_semiempirical_traj.py`
goes from 17 failed / 9 passed to 4 failed / 22 passed; the recovered nodes
cover acetamide, acetone, furan, pyrimidine, pyridine, triazine, imidazole,
cytosine, CH3OH, CO2, HCOOH and H2CO.

New `TestSCCOptionDefaultParity` in `tests/test_semiempirical_dftb0.py` pins
every `SCCDFTBModel` keyword default against the corresponding C++
`SCCOptions` default, so a one-sided revert of this kind fails a test instead
of silently changing the method for months.

The four still-failing nodes in that file are unrelated to `use_diis` and were
verified to fail identically with and without this change; they remain tracked
in `scripts/test_gate/known_reds_baseline.json`.

### Found and pinned: periodic one-electron lattice sums enumerate images by `|g|`, not by the pair separation (2026-08-06)

`compute_overlap_lattice`, `compute_kinetic_lattice` and
`compute_nuclear_lattice` enumerate lattice translations with
`|g| <= cutoff_bohr` and then compute every shell pair at that translation.
Whether a term matters is set by the PHYSICAL separation of the two centres,
`|O_mu - O_nu - g|`, so the translations that contribute form a ball centred
on the intra-cell offset, not on the origin. Bounding `|g|` both misses
images that bring a distant pair into range and visits ones that do not,
asymmetrically between the `(mu, nu)` and `(nu, mu)` orderings.

That is a wrong answer at production defaults, not a truncation tolerance:
the matrix depends on WHICH equally valid description of the same crystal you
supply. Re-describing a rocksalt or zincblende cell by moving the second atom
one lattice vector, both descriptions in-cell, moves the Gamma matrices at
the shipped `cutoff_bohr = 15` by

| cell (intra-cell offset) | basis | S | T |
|---|---|---|---|
| LiH rocksalt (6.68 bohr) | def2-svp | 7.2e-01 | 2.7e-02 |
| MgO rocksalt (6.89 bohr) | def2-svp | 8.7e-02 | 1.6e-02 |
| SiC 3C (3.57 bohr) | def2-svp | 9.8e-03 | 5.5e-03 |
| diamond C2 (2.92 bohr) | def2-svp | 3.2e-04 | 4.3e-04 |

An overlap element is O(1). The drift grows with the intra-cell offset and
with basis diffuseness, and decays to round-off only once the cutoff exceeds
range + offset. A single-atom cell has zero offset, so every vacuum-box
fixture is structurally blind to it, the same reason the identical defect in
the auxiliary 2c/3c ERI lattice sums (fixed 2026-08-03) hid behind a passing
Ne-in-a-box gate while MgO diverged.

The convergence variable is settled in the literature: Sharma and Beylkin,
*J. Chem. Theory Comput.* (2021), doi:10.1021/acs.jctc.0c01195, write the
periodic two-centre integral as `<a|K|b>^per = sum_P <a|K|b_P>` (Eq. 17)
whose lattice-dependent factor depends on `P` only through
`T(P) = rho * ||A - B - P||^2` (Eq. 18).

**This release records the defect; it does not change any number.** A
prototype fix was built and measured, and it works: post-fix invariance is
7.1e-15 on the worst row, `Si/def2-SVP` at the release-paper meshes becomes
positive definite at the default cutoff (so the multi-k GDF cutoff-growth
remediation stops firing for it), and the IBZ-transport asymmetry that
`test_ibz_transport_converges_with_cutoff_on_a_shift_bearing_cell` pinned at
1.19 for cutoff 8 drops to 4.7e-14. But the correct term set needs images
beyond the `|g|` ball, so the one-electron cell list gets ~2.7x longer, and
a large family of consumers pairs that list index-for-index with the plain
ball the two-electron, ECP, Ewald-split and multipole builds use. Landing it
is a coordinated change across the periodic-SCF, BIPOLE, symmetry and slab
areas, not a one-file fix. `handovers/HANDOVER_OPEN_BUGS_V015.md` carries the
measurements, the per-kernel boundary analysis (which sums must NOT get this
treatment, and why), and the consumer inventory.

What does land here is everything that is safe on its own:

* `cpp/include/vibeqc/lattice_pair_cells.hpp` -- the enumeration contract
  written down once, with the rationale and the measured cost of getting it
  wrong. `cpp/src/aux_eri.cpp`, which fixed its own kernels in August, now
  uses that header instead of its private copy.
* `direct_lattice_cells` **stable**-sorts by `|r|`. A crystal lattice has
  large groups of exactly equal `|r|`, and the previous unstable sort could
  order such a group any way it liked, differently between two cutoffs and
  in principle between standard library versions -- which would make a
  cell-resolved result platform-dependent. Stability also makes a cutoff's
  cell list an exact PREFIX of any larger cutoff's, which is what lets code
  pair cell lists of different lengths safely.
* `build_jk_2e_real_space` rejects an out-of-range `output_indices` entry
  with a message naming the cause instead of reading off the end of its cell
  list (previously a segfault, reached by handing it positions derived from
  a different cell list).
* `tests/test_periodic_1electron.py` pins the defect as a **strict xfail**
  with its measured size, plus the prefix property above, so a future fix
  flips it to XPASS rather than landing silently.

### Fixed: large-basis molecular DF memory preflight (2026-08-11)

Molecular RHF/UHF/RKS/UKS preflight now sizes the in-core density-fitting
three-index construction peak from the parsed `n_aux * n_orb^2` extent. For
more than 500 orbital functions it charges two resident tensor blocks plus a
2x construction-overlap safety factor, matching the four full tensor extents
that coexist in the native constructor. The report prints every formula
dimension. A representative BH9 def2-QZVPP/def2-QZVPP-J case now reports a
28.86 GB DF category and a 44.2 GB headline instead of 7.21 GB and 11.7 GB,
while small-basis category estimates remain unchanged (BUG 117).

Periodic open-shell SCF now promotes the default singlet to the lowest valid
doublet when an odd-electron primitive cell reaches the driver, including Cu,

Scheduler-backed jobs no longer require GNU Time to be installed specifically

## [v0.15.128] - 2026-08-11 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Fixed: batch runner memory budget check with sequential fallback (BUG 123, 2026-08-11)

Batch runners now sum per-child memory estimates via `BatchMemoryPlan`,
compare against the PBS allocation, and automatically fall back to sequential
execution when the total exceeds available memory. Prevents OOM-kill of
parallel child processes when PBS `mem=` is per-node but Torque applies it as
a per-process rlimit (1,172 jobs killed across rp107 and rp209 before this fix).

The Python `cartesian_component_indices` function in the BIPOLE far-field

The C++ far-field penetration dispatch now shifts only s4 (the ket shell at

`c1f568717f438b62d42daba8dcbefe2f568ce10d`; current code supersedes the
literal with the latest accepted immutable `0.15.x` fleet report. Campaign

New `jobs.tsv` rows and the dispatch `ledgered-before-submit`, `submitted`, and

execution-time race barrier. The generated payload wrapper now uses the runtime
guard names actually consumed by vibe-qc: `VIBEQC_EXPECT_VERSION` and
`VIBEQC_EXPECT_GIT_SHA`.

Article commit `8425091ad9eef9ec7173ec3a35335cfc8a1b3fd7` applies the same

### Fixed: `rollout-latest` outer holds cover exact scheduler aliases (2026-08-11)

Source commit `7f65b8e58` closes the bounded mutation-side scheduler-alias
hold gap. The existing outer bracket still applies only when one canonical
host has more than one pending non-driver scheduler action. When it applies,
the execution plan protects the canonical scheduler target plus every
transitively resolved nonlocal alias, using each exact target's own configured
`scheduler_driver` control key. Excluded, unresolved, and local aliases are
not inferred. Direct `vq admin update` commands and a rollout with only one
pending scheduler action keep their previous behavior.

Before the first drain control call, the rollout durably records the complete
target/control manifest. Each member has an exact target, canonical
`action_host`, stable `control_host`, and deterministic per-target lease owner.
No protected update starts until every member is confirmed. Partial acquire or
release failure triggers exact-target cleanup attempts; each outcome is
reported and journaled per target. A live, outcome-unknown, or verified failed
durable child retains the whole group by its canonical action binding.

Resume validates the journal against the current plan before any control
mutation. Missing, malformed, removed, reparented, or control-repointed
bindings fail closed with zero control calls. Plan-bound holds are deferred
from fleet-global release until the matching plan can validate them; an
obsolete report produces an actionable fence instead of guessing under a new
report. Historical canonical exact-owner and pre-owner legacy journals retain
their compatibility paths. `--only <canonical>` preserves its protection
group, while selecting a lane-less alias still fails closed.

The target and control keys, including their SSH routing, must not be
repointed while a rollout hold is pending. Restore the recorded mapping and
reconcile first. The execution-only manifest does not change plan/result/verify
wire schemas, accepted-report digest checks, external/manual/full/partial hold
semantics, or final drain-liveness reporting.

## [v0.15.126] - 2026-08-11 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Fixed: GFN2-xTB double-counted repulsive energy (2026-08-11)

The GFN2 H0 Hamiltonian already folds in repulsive contributions through its
parameterisation. Adding E_rep explicitly in the total-energy assembly double-
counted it, shifting all GFN2 energies by +E_rep. The spurious term has been
removed from the energy functional and its gradient/stress derivatives.

### Fixed: SCF AUTO mode defaults lowered, incremental Fock enabled by default (BUG 87, 2026-08-11)

Molecular SCF for large basis sets (cc-pVQZ, def2-TZVP) was 15--60× slower and
used 23× more RAM than ORCA. The AUTO SCF-mode threshold now defaults to 140 BF
(was 200), and `incremental_fock` now defaults to `True` for the INC_FOCK path,
matching ORCA's RIJCOSX performance profile for mid-size molecules.

### Added: `vq` rollout results report final drain liveness (2026-08-11)

Source commit `8869ca33e` completes the bounded R0 P1 reporting
follow-up. After an executing `vq admin rollout-latest` finalizes its durable
journal, and while the global rollout fence is still held, the existing
`vq.fleet.rollout_result/2` gains an additive `drain_liveness` block. Each
configured host is projected from one point-in-time observation of its daemon
control endpoint as inactive, covered by one or more active holds, or unknown.
Text output says `OBSERVED ACTIVE ... (final sweep as of <time>)`; it does not
claim that an observed hold is still active after that timestamp.

The daemon exposes a versioned `vq.drain.read_only_snapshot/1` RPC used by a
hidden, single-control `drain --status --json --read-only-snapshot` path. It
reads the legacy drain document and owner-scoped scheduler-lease store under
their two existing locks, in a fixed order, without creating, expiring,
rewriting, or releasing state. The stores and command output are bounded and
strictly parsed. Missing old-daemon support, busy or unreadable locks,
malformed or incomplete data, timeouts, and response loss become explicit
unknown coverage; there is no fallback to a direct state-file read. An
unreadable scheduler-lease store continues to hold dispatch safe, and its
writer now refuses a store larger than the same 1 MiB reader limit.

Observation endpoints are queried at most once and then projected onto exact
configured targets, including scheduler aliases and excluded or unresolved
targets. Rollout ownership is assigned only by exact journal identity; display
sanitization cannot turn an external hold into an owned one. The historical
`preserved_external_holds` and journal-derived `retained_rollout_holds` fields
remain unchanged. The final sweep does not run for `--dry-run` or
`--verify-only`, and it cannot change rollout status, verdict, or exit code.
Plan `/2`, result `/2`, and verify `/3` schema identifiers remain unchanged.

This is source-only evidence. No accepted report, live host, root daemon,
scheduler, drain, or fleet operation exercised it. That reporting increment
observes and reports aliases without changing rollout hold acquisition; the
later bounded mutation closure is recorded above at `7f65b8e58`.

Periodic GDF/GPW/GAPW/BIPOLE calculations now write `wavefunction.gto` into QVF
archives (Gamma-point MO coefficients via `qvf_wf_data`).  Open-shell periodic
UHF/UKS now write `atom_properties` (Mulliken charges, spin populations, dipole)
into QVF.  BIPOLE DFT+U callsites now forward `bz_integration`.

### Fixed: Semiempirical QVF empty shells (BUG 66)

Periodic semiempirical runs (DFTB0, SCC-DFTB, GFN2-xTB, PM6, OMx) now build a
population summary from native Mulliken charges when the engine exposes them,
so QVF archives carry `atom_properties` instead of bare manifest+structure shells.

### Fixed: Mulliken spin populations in QVF atom_properties (BUG 40)

Unrestricted (UHF/UKS) molecular calculations now compute and write
`mulliken_spin` populations to the QVF `atom_properties` section.  The
`PopulationSummary` gains a `mulliken_spin_atoms` field.

### Changed: ROHF orbital eigenvalues now use Guest-Saunders canonicalisation (BUG 81, 2026-08-11)

ROHF total energies are convention-independent and matched ORCA to
1.5e-09 Ha.  Orbital eigenvalues (HOMO, LUMO) are convention-dependent
because ROHF has no unique Fock matrix -- every code picks a different
effective Fock to diagonalise.  vibe-qc previously used the Roothaan
effective Fock; it now uses the **Guest-Saunders** convention
(Mol. Phys. 28, 819, 1974), which is ORCA's default and the most
common choice in production codes.

**This changes orbital eigenvalues (but not the total energy) for ROHF
and ROKS jobs.**  The change is largest for the singly-occupied
orbitals (SOMOs): in the Roothaan convention the SOMO eigenvalue is an
average of alpha and beta Fock expectation values; Guest-Saunders
diagonalises the alpha Fock in the open-shell subspace, giving
Koopmans-theorem IPs that are typically 0.1--0.4 Ha lower.

The original Roothaan eigenvalues remain accessible as
``result.mo_energies_roothaan``.  The convention is recorded as
``rohf_canonicalization = "guest-saunders"`` in the ``[run]`` section
of ``{output}.system`` so downstream tools can interpret the numbers.

The HOMO, LUMO, and gap are now displayed explicitly in the orbital
table footer for RHF, ROHF, and UHF (previously only the gap was
shown, and ROHF used the label "(occupied)-LUMO gap").

- ``python/vibeqc/rohf.py`` -- new ``guest_saunders_canonicalize()``
  function; ``ROHFResult`` gains ``rohf_canonicalization``,
  ``mo_energies_roothaan``, ``mo_coeffs_roothaan``
- ``python/vibeqc/output/formats/scf_log.py`` -- RHF/ROHF/UHF orbital
  table footers now include explicit HOMO, LUMO, and gap values
- ``python/vibeqc/output/citations/database.toml`` -- added
  Guest-Saunders 1974 entry; ROHF/ROKS routes now cite it
- ``python/vibeqc/runner.py`` -- conducting-state gap check extended
  to ROHF/ROKS; convention recorded in ``.system`` via
  ``extra_run_fields``
- ``tests/test_rohf.py`` -- 8 new tests for canonicalisation,
  HOMO/LUMO access, and ``.system`` recording

## [v0.15.125] - 2026-08-11 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Fixed: DFT integration grid defaults now match ORCA DefGrid3 (BUG 80) (2026-08-11)

The legacy ProductGaussLegendre 17x36 grid produced systematic energy
differences of 0.1-2.8 mHa vs ORCA across all functionals and basis
sets. The new default switches to Lebedev-302 + NWChem pruning +
Stratmann partition, matching ORCA's DefGrid3 to sub-0.01 mHa. A new
`grid_level` parameter on `run_job()` / `run_rks()` / `run_uks()` offers
four presets: `orca-defgrid3` (default), `fine`, `coarse`, and `legacy`.
Explicit `RKSOptions` with custom grid settings are preserved.

### Added: BIPOLE point-group symmetry Fock reconstruction (2026-08-11)

The experimental BIPOLE far-field Fock kernel added point-group symmetry
reduction via shell-index orbit mapping, yielding up to 192x fewer
kernel entries for cubic crystals. No explicit density rotation is needed
-- the per-cell density blocks in the SCF dict already carry the correct
orientation at each cell.

Audit note (2026-08-13): this was prototype infrastructure, not production
coverage. The quartet far-field route is now gated before SCF.

### Added: BIPOLE unrestricted K (exchange) far-field (2026-08-11)

The quartet-level bipolar far-field exchange kernel is now wired into
the unrestricted (UHF/UKS) Fock builder via skip-mask rebuild, completing
the far-field coverage for open-shell systems.
## [v0.15.124] - 2026-08-10 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Changed: BIPOLE far-field default-on experiment (withdrawn 2026-08-13)

This release temporarily defaulted `use_multipole_far_field` to `True` in all
four BIPOLE drivers. The expansion source is Pisani-Dovesi-Roetti (1988),
Ch. II.4c; Saunders (1992) covers electrostatic penetration context, not the
implemented quartet classifier. The 2026-08-13 audit found that the skip and
add-back domains did not preserve the full three-translation Fock sum, so the
experiment is withdrawn and explicit `True` now fails closed.

The far-field Fock kernel is built on a permutation+point-group
symmetry-reduced dispatch (up to 192\u00d7 fewer entries for cubic
crystals) and reconstructed to the full Fock via shell-index orbit
mapping at each SCF iteration.  No explicit density rotation is needed
(the per-cell density blocks in the SCF dict already carry the correct
orientation at each cell).  Dispatch-index tracking ensures correct
alignment between kernel contributions and reconstruction orbits.

C++ far-field kernel apply now computes the Coulomb far-field energy
(was always 0.0).  Infrastructure builder always uses permutation-only
reconstruction.

### Added: `vq` rollout root-daemon provenance inventory (2026-08-10)

`vq admin rollout-latest` now carries a separate, non-executable provenance
record for the possible system multi-user daemon on every canonical local
managed or vq-only host. The existing doctor sweep preserves daemon version,
source SHA, package-tree digest, socket, and multi-user identity, while verbose
daemon ping reports a strict target `/etc/vq/config.toml` tri-state. Explicitly
single-user hosts are recorded as not applicable; an enabled, contradictory,
invalid, unreadable, or old/missing probe defers convergence instead of making
the root `/opt/vq` install disappear. These records cannot invoke sudo or an
update helper. Plan/result/verify schemas advance to `/2`, `/2`, and `/3` for
the new verdict semantics while historical managed-lane counts remain
separate. Verbose daemon ping now capability-probes the responding process
identity and reads the fixed multi-user systemd unit through an absolute,
shell-free `systemctl show` command. Old daemons remain live but explicitly
unsupported for identity, and a legacy remote CLI is retried without
`--verbose` only for Click's exact unknown-option error. Doctor and rollout
records preserve this evidence without treating an auxiliary probe failure as
a daemon failure. Rollout planning now derives the canonical package-tree
digest once from the accepted vq commit object, never from the live driver
worktree, and binds version/SHA/tree/socket evidence into the same RPC response
as PID, effective uid, Python, and argv. An applicable root lane converges only
when that atomic daemon identity and the fixed systemd unit exactly match the
accepted version, SHA, package bytes, root service identity, and `MainPID`;
every missing, legacy, torn, or mismatched field remains deferred. Git replace
refs, dirty/ahead worktrees, and missing local commit objects cannot change or
silently weaken the expected digest. The base ping JSON stays unchanged, and
the exact root-decision increment does not further advance the rollout schema
IDs. Privileged refresh remains a subsequent reviewed increment; the vq-only
user-install lane is the next entry below.

### Added: `vq` rollout lane for vq-only coordinators (2026-08-10)

`vq admin rollout-latest` now treats each canonical local-scheduler
`fleet_role = "vq-only"` host as a required user-vq target. Immediately after
driver self-update and fresh-interpreter re-entry, the plan contains exactly
one report-pinned `vibeqc-queue` action for each non-driver vq-only host; when
the vq-only host is itself the driver, the existing driver action is the one
lane and is not duplicated. These hosts never acquire invented
`vibeqc-release`, `vibeqc-dev`, or `vibe-view` lanes.

The update primitive is the target host's own
`[programs.vibeqc-queue] kind = "venv"` registration. Two successful discovery
sweeps that both show the registration missing, or an explicitly invalid
registration, block with the configuration remedy. A failed, omitted,
malformed, or internally inconsistent admin/program/doctor snapshot defers
instead of being misclassified as unconfigured. An already-current lane skips
only when the live program, installed checkout, canonical non-acknowledged
`LAST OK`, and freshly probed single-user daemon all prove the accepted
version, source SHA, and package-tree digest. Coverage reports this separately
under `vq_user_lanes`, preserving the historical managed-lane count and the
existing rollout schema IDs.

This is a source contract only: no accepted release report or live fleet
rollout has yet exercised it. It does not refresh a root-owned `/opt/vq`
daemon; privileged apply remains a separate reviewed milestone.

### Fixed: site_i release builds preserve the prepared accepted source (2026-08-10)

site_i's automated source feed now pins the accepted full SHA into both
`refs/heads/release` and `refs/remotes/origin/release` for the
`vibeqc-release` profile, together with the release tags. The preparer requires
both release refs to exist, agree with
each other, and equal the accepted SHA before it accepts the release tag or

identity therefore fails before native dependency setup or a core build.

The tracked site_i deploy wrapper now invokes `scripts/install.sh --current`
from the already detached, exact prepared tree. The installer can no longer
