### Fixed: direct remote `vq` updates preserve the build timeout contract (2026-08-10)

Direct venv `vq admin update` delegation now resolves and validates both build
watchdogs before SSH, then forwards their effective values through an exact
two-name allowlist. `VQ_UPDATE_SCRIPT_TIMEOUT` defaults to 14400 seconds and
must be finite and greater than zero. `VQ_BUILD_STALL_TIMEOUT` defaults to
3600 seconds and must be finite and non-negative; zero continues to disable
the stall watchdog. Defaults are forwarded as well as explicit overrides, so
the initiator and remote update process use one deterministic policy. Invalid
values refuse locally before an SSH process is started.

Only those two values enter the direct-remote environment prefix. Ambient
variables, credentials, auth tokens, and `VQ_REMOTE_ADMIN_UPDATE_TIMEOUT` do
not; auth retains its existing stdin or target-file path. For one delegated
venv target, the outer timeout remains a local, finite positive observer and
must be at least the remote wall timeout plus 600 seconds. Its baseline is
15000 seconds only when unset, and that default rises when needed to preserve
the margin. An explicit value may be lower than 15000 seconds when it still
covers wall plus 600; a smaller value refuses before SSH. Delegated venv `--all`
and `--all-hosts` operations deliberately have no single finite aggregate
observer over the complete batch. Their per-environment wall and stall
watchdogs, together with SSH liveness checks, remain authoritative. Scheduler
helper and runtime deadlines continue to come from their deployment profiles
rather than these venv variables.

This is a source-only contract. No accepted report carries it, and no remote
host, scheduler, or fleet operation was performed to validate it. Durable
child identity, adoption, and journal reconciliation were deferred to the R4a
source milestone described below.

### Fixed: `vq` fleet actions survive controller loss without blind replay (2026-08-10)

R4a places each production `rollout-latest` action under one durable local
operation. Core protocol commit `0a9e13c5e` provides an immutable operation
identity bound to the report digest, attempt, action, target, and canonical
argv, plus create-once request, ready, authorization, activation, and result
receipts. A separate bounded append-only output spool is continuously drained.
Integration commit `e01d073ed` makes the
controller prepare and journal that identity before authorization, then adopt
the same operation after controller death instead of starting another update.
Controller death before run authorization cannot launch the action: the
detached launcher waits within the bounded authorization window, then can win
the immutable abort/result decision if no controller authorizes it.
The local execution-recorder follow-up below supplies the current
launcher/recorder process split and isolated child process group. Driver,
local/direct-remote, helper, and scheduler-runtime outer CLI actions use the
same contract. A completed driver action still forces fresh-interpreter
re-entry before any later action.

Every mutating invocation takes one owner-only fleet fence before it reconciles
operations from every rollout report and host, before its first live snapshot,
and holds that fence through planning, execution, final snapshots, and journal
finalization. Scoped selection cannot hide an operation from another report or
host. `--dry-run` and `--verify-only` perform only the global inspection: they
never authorize, abort, follow, harvest, mutate a journal, consume a known
failure fence, or release a hold, and they fail closed when reconciliation is
required.

Local full-drain acquisition is journaled before the mutation and confirmed
with its exact `reason` plus `set_at`; scheduler claims retain their exact
owner. A live, outcome-unknown, or verified failed action keeps its owned hold.
Release requires trustworthy reconciliation proving that no protected action
remains live, unknown, or failed, and targets only that exact generation. An
old report's scheduler hold without a complete current-plan release identity
also fails closed instead of guessing a driver or migration path. A verified
nonzero result blocks same-invocation replay for that host while independent
hosts may finish. Its durable failure fence is consumed only after a fresh plan
records the host-local skip; only a later explicit controller pass can
authorize another attempt.

The execution recorder continuously drains combined child output without
backpressure and stores at most 4 MiB. The controller streams retained bytes
only to stderr so JSON stdout stays clean; the result records byte counts,
digest, and truncation guidance. The canonical `vq admin logs` transcript
remains the complete-output source.

This is a source-only milestone. No accepted report, live host, root daemon,
scheduler, drain, or fleet operation exercised it. The local execution-recorder
follow-up below closes launcher loss around activation. The later R4b.1
increment binds the fixed-host detached scheduler command for a still-live
outer action. Recorder loss after activation and positive global remote
reconciliation remain explicit outcome-unknown boundaries.

Commit `984e09051` closes the P1 failed-result reporting seam. A terminal
failed run that reaches finalization emits exactly one valid
`vq.fleet.rollout_result/2` before exit 1. Its additive
`retained_rollout_holds` block projects rollout-owned journal claims recorded
as `active` or `cleanup-failed`; text output adds sanitized `FAILED HOST` and
`RETAINED ROLLOUT HOLD` lines. Those lines explicitly say current liveness is
not asserted. The independent `preserved_external_holds` block and
`PRESERVED EXTERNAL HOLD` text remain unchanged.

Source verification passed 258 focused tests; the adjacent matrix recorded
622 passed and one skipped; and an independent 10x crash/failure subset passed
80/80. P1 verification passed 206 focused tests, and the combined R4a
core/rollout/CLI matrix now passes 261; Ruff, `py_compile`, and diff checks are
clean, and independent review is CLEAR. At that R4a/P1 checkpoint, the complete
vq suite passed `5,678 passed, 12 skipped in 173.70s (0:02:53)`.

### Fixed: `vq` durable actions survive local launcher loss (2026-08-10)

Commit `4683a1d3b` adds the local execution-recorder portion of R4b. After run
authorization, the detached supervisor acts only as a launcher and transfers
the already-held lifetime lease to a fresh-session recorder without an unlock
gap. The recorder validates the immutable operation and authorization,
publishes activation before starting the outer `python -m vq` child, drains the
bounded output spool, and publishes the terminal result. Once that handoff has
occurred, controller or launcher death does not orphan the action or permit a
second launch.

If the launcher disappears before recorder activation and the lifetime lease
is free, reconciliation resumes the same immutable operation and attempt. It
does not mint a replacement attempt. Busy pre-activation leases have one
bounded activation deadline; an owned launcher is terminated and reaped
without signalling a detached recorder, while an adopted lease owner is never
signalled. Activation races are re-read before failure is reported. Recorder
death or child-launch failure after activation still leaves the action
outcome-unknown and non-replayable. The R4b.1 increment below separately binds
and observes one fixed-host detached scheduler-runtime command while its outer
admin action remains live. It does not turn recorder death into a replayable or
terminal local result.

### Fixed: `vq` binds fixed-host detached scheduler builds before launch (2026-08-10)

Commit `1483c980e` adds the bounded R4b.1 source increment for a
scheduler-runtime rollout action whose profile uses `detached_build = true`
with a fixed `update_host`. The execution recorder exports only its exact
operation id, immutable request digest, and authorization nonce. Before the
admin marker or SSH is touched, the runtime path reloads that live outer
operation and verifies its phase, action id, host, program, target SHA, and
target tag. Immediately before the detached build launch, it publishes one
owner-only, create-once `scheduler-command.json` binding for the exact target,
program, mode, full random run id, normalized remote run directory, command
digest, and remote-request digest.

The build host receives a fixed embedded Python helper and a canonical bounded
request on stdin. Deployment argv is never interpreted by a shell. The helper
creates a random owner-only namespace, launches the exact argv in a fresh
session, enforces the remote timeout, and retains create-once request, lease,
activation, and result receipts plus at most 4 MiB of output while continuing
to drain later bytes. A lost or ambiguous launch or poll response can only
observe that exact retained binding. It never scans for a run or launches a
second command. Malformed, mismatched, missing, or unobservable evidence fails
closed with the remote outcome unknown.

A strict terminal remote receipt with return code zero means only
`deploy-completed-unverified`. The existing independent login-host verification
must still prove the exact runtime identity before LAST OK can advance or the
admin marker can clear. Remote evidence is not converted into the outer
operation's `result.json`, and it does not release a rollout hold. If the
execution recorder or outer child dies after activation, fleet-global
reconciliation still sees an outcome-unknown, non-replayable local action; it
does not yet query the retained remote run positively.

This increment does not change scheduler-helper actions, Slurm
`update_allocation` deployments, or manual commands without a validated outer
operation context; those keep their existing protocols. It is source-only:
no accepted report carries it, and no live host, root daemon, scheduler, drain,
or fleet operation exercised it. Focused evidence:
`107 focused and 373 adjacent tests passed; independent review passed 384 focused/adjacent tests`. Complete vq suite:
`5,776 passed and 12 skipped in 181.79s`. Static, diff, and independent review:
`full Ruff, Python compilation, git diff checks passed; independent review CLEAR`.

### Fixed: `vq` pause and resume enforce ownership and transactional scheduler state (2026-08-10)

Commit `01583c6d1` applies the effective multi-user ownership policy inside
each job's spec lock before local or scheduler state is classified and before
any signal, hold, or release mutation. Single-user behavior is unchanged.
Bulk local and scheduler operations authorize each record before inspecting
its state or `paused_by` tag, isolate a foreign job as an error, and continue
without leaking that job's state. CLI and web routes translate policy and
configuration denials instead of exposing a traceback.

Scheduler pause and resume re-read and authorize the exact handle, state, and
optional `--paused-by` filter immediately before `qhold` or `qrls`, then keep
the spec lock across the remote mutation, final owner check, spec write, and
commit. Any failure after a remote mutation attempts the exact inverse. A
successful inverse leaves the original spec untouched, or restores and
byte-verifies it when a local write was attempted. A failed inverse attempts
to persist `hold_outcome_unknown` or
`release_outcome_unknown`. Only a verified marker names the opposite ordinary
pause/resume verb as the exact recovery route; marker uncertainty remains a
compound fail-closed error. Restore uncertainty also fails closed. A restore
retry is allowed only after an authorized re-read proves the byte-exact
post-state. Event recording remains best-effort after commit and never rolls
back an already consistent scheduler/spec pair.

These two commits are source-only. No accepted report carries them, and no
live host, root, scheduler, drain, or fleet operation exercised them. Their
combined focused matrix passed 482 tests with one skip; the complete source
suite passed `5732 passed, 12 skipped in 182.01s`; Ruff, Python compilation,
and diff checks passed, and independent review is CLEAR.

### Fixed: mutating `vq` admin delegation never blindly replays an unknown outcome (2026-08-10)

Remote `vq admin update` and real `vq admin auto-update` writes now make
exactly one SSH transport attempt. An SSH exit 255, observer timeout, or local
SSH process death by signal does not prove that the remote command was absent;
the CLI reports the outcome as unknown, says not to retry yet, and directs the
operator to `vq admin status <target> --json`, the marker, LAST OK, the admin
log, and exact live SHA or tag evidence. Scheduler helper and runtime advice
names the scheduler target rather than the SSH driver that owns its marker.

A local SSH executable that provably cannot start is reported separately as
not started. A generic local I/O failure remains ambiguous because it can occur
after process creation. An authoritative remote nonzero result keeps its
existing error without unknown-outcome advice. Auto-update dry-runs remain
read-only and do not receive mutation guidance. Token stdin delivery, target
token files, venv timeout forwarding, command argv, successful output and JSON
stdout separation, and remote output capture remain unchanged. Ambiguous and
pre-start failures intentionally gain the new stderr guidance.

The generic CLI delegation layer no longer exposes a transient-retry control.
Lower-level retry support remains available for reviewed replay-safe reads and
verified source staging; those paths no longer claim that a transport failure
proves the first attempt never ran. This entry is the R4.0 prerequisite; the
later R4a entry above supplies durable local action identity, adoption, and
journal reconciliation. No live update, scheduler, root, or fleet operation
was performed for this source change.

### Added: exact owned full-drain release for rollout adoption (2026-08-10)

`vq` now exposes an atomic compare-and-release transaction for a rollout-owned
full drain. The internal recovery path must supply both the recorded reason
and `set_at`; the daemon compares both under the legacy drain-state lock and
releases only that full generation. A changed generation fails closed, while
an already absent full hold is idempotent. Scheduler-target lanes, partial
limits, ownership metadata, and every unrelated state field are preserved.

Multi-user release uses one authenticated, audited daemon RPC callback pinned
to the daemon's startup-selected state tree. An old or unreachable daemon
never falls back to a client-side read/replace. The paired CLI selectors are
hidden for rollout control; the existing pairless `--release-full` command
retains its established unconditional operator behavior. This is the exact
local-hold prerequisite consumed by the later R4a entry above, not a claim that
this earlier increment alone adopted a child. No live drain, daemon, host,
scheduler, root, or fleet operation was performed.

### Changed: `vq` rollout verdicts name their managed scope and preserved external holds (2026-08-10)

`vq admin rollout-latest` no longer presents a clean modeled-lane result as
unqualified fleet convergence. Plan, result, and verify JSON add a
read-tolerant `coverage` block that counts modeled managed lanes, declines to
assert whole-fleet convergence, and names privileged root-daemon,
vibe-basisopt, vq-only-host, and explicitly excluded gaps. Human output says
`managed lanes` and prints the same exclusions. Completed result JSON also
promotes borrowed full drains and independently owned scheduler claims observed
during hold acquisition to `preserved_external_holds`, retaining their owner
and original reason; text prints `PRESERVED EXTERNAL HOLD`. This records what
the rollout deliberately did not release without claiming that an independently
removable or timed hold was freshly observed after the final action.

### Added: experimental symmetry-reduced far-field reconstruction (2026-08-10)

The prototype periodic bipolar far-field kernel could be built
on a point-group+permutation symmetry-reduced dispatch and reconstructed to
the full Fock via `SymmetryFockReconstructionMap`.  For each canonical quartet,
the Fock contribution is computed once and added at all symmetry-equivalent
positions in the orbit, reducing kernel entries by the group order (up to 48×
for cubic crystals).  The reconstruction map is built from symmorphic
space-group operations (shell-permutation + cell-rotation maps) and applied
via `apply_far_field_fock_kernel_with_symmetry()`.  All four drivers default
to `use_multipole_far_field=True` with auto-disable for open-shell (UHF/UKS)
and very small cells (cutoff ≤ 5 bohr).

Audit note (2026-08-13): these were internal prototype paths and are now
unreachable from the supported drivers.

## [v0.15.123] - 2026-08-10 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Fixed: reviewed pre-unified libint stamps migrate without recompilation (2026-08-10)

Native build-stamp migration now recognizes the exact three-field libint
fingerprint written by the reviewed builder immediately before lifecycle
unification. Acceptance requires the builder path, the complete historical
SHA-256, and the complete current build-relevant SHA-256 to match; it covers
only the relocation of the existing build-lock lifecycle lines. Partial or
unknown fingerprints, malformed lifecycle markers, and changes to source pins,
configure inputs, CMake arguments, or other unmarked commands still fail closed
as recipe drift and rebuild libint.

### Fixed: `vq` fleet repairs preserve unhealthy newer chemistry revisions (2026-08-10)

`vq admin rollout-latest` now treats an explicit installed/checkout SHA
mismatch as failed canonical LAST OK, even when the checkout is a proven
descendant of the accepted release pin. The repair rebuilds that exact live
descendant instead of silently accepting it or resetting it to the older pin;
release lanes retain any recorded live tag, and the actual repair identity is
recorded consistently in the plan, journal, resume state, and result. Healthy
descendants keep the existing no-downgrade skip, while ahead `vq` revisions
remain fail-closed as release drift.

### Fixed: `vq` scheduler-runtime auto-update exact revision checks (2026-08-10)

Scheduler-runtime drift checks now distinguish a genuinely tagless source
repository from a failed `git tag` probe, accept linked worktrees whose `.git`
entry is a file, and resolve the newest tag before declaring convergence. A
runtime is skipped only when its last successful tag and full SHA both match;
same-tag SHA drift is redeployed with the resolved revision instead of being
silently accepted.

### Fixed: `vq` multi-user spec and state-tree admission boundary (2026-08-10)

The root daemon now binds every multi-user queue record to a safe job ID, its
exact filename, canonical uid directory, and captured owner-qualified spec
path. User-writable queue records are opened without following links, must be
regular UTF-8 files, and are size-bounded before validation; the same guarded
reader is used during active reconciliation. Existing per-user state trees are
hardened at startup with root-owned structural directories while preserving
the documented shared control-root mode. Invalid records fail before dependency
cascade, refresh, build, or other root-side orchestration can use their fields.

### Fixed: DSD-PBEP86 D3(BJ) double-hybrid coefficients (2026-08-09)

The `dsd-pbep86` and `dsdpbep86` functional aliases now use the final
Kozuch-Martin D3(BJ) fit: 0.70 HF exchange, 0.30 PBE exchange, 0.43 P86
correlation on the VWN5 LDA base, 0.53 opposite-spin MP2, and 0.25 same-spin
MP2. The previous
0.69/0.31/0.44/0.55/0.09 mapping did not describe the cited final D3(BJ)
parameterization and produced a 1.58 mHa SCF-component discrepancy in the
release-paper H2O/def2-SVP comparison.

Follow-up (2026-08-12, frozen-registry defect DSDPBEP86-DFT-PART-1P6MHA):
the defect decomposes into two same-name traps, now documented at the alias
in `cpp/src/xc.cpp` — (1) the old SCF piece was the *2013-JCC-revision*
coefficient set (doi:10.1002/jcc.23391) while c_os = 0.55 / c_ss = 0.09
matched no published DSD-PBEP86 revision (transcribed from adjacent columns
of the 2013 SI table: DSD-PBEPBE's c_o, DSD-PBEB95's c_s); (2) "P86" is
flavor-split across codes — libxc `GGA_C_P86` is PZ81-local, ORCA composes
the VWN5-local `GGA_C_P86VWN`, and the PZ81 flavor alone leaves +1.85 mHa
in the SCF part even with correct coefficients. On the registry witness
(mb014, H2O/def2-SVP vs the gate-clean conventional NORI/DEFGRID3 ORCA
6.1.1 reference) the DFT-part deviation drops 1.5801 mHa -> 0.0364 mHa,
inside the wave's 0.001-0.036 mHa sibling grid-residual band; the remaining
MP2-part delta vs ORCA is the documented frozen-core protocol difference.
New regression pin:
`tests/test_dsd_pbep86.py::test_dsd_pbep86_dft_part_matches_conventional_orca_mb014`.
Citation routes for `dsd-pbep86` now carry `vwn_1980` (VWN5 local part) and
the methods route gains `perdew_p86_1986`. `revdsd-pbep86` is deliberately
unchanged: its 2019-D4 coefficients are correct and the 2019 refit was run
in Q-Chem 5.1, so its P86 flavor needs its own reference gate (noted at the
alias). Supersedes validation rows `cmp-rgfix-pin1-mb014-total-energy`
(fail, +2.751 mHa) and the diagnostic-only
`cmp-pin1rr-mb014-total-energy-rp106pin1`.

### Fixed: DLPNO-(T) C++ projection kernel silently dropped t1 contribution (BUG 79)

The C++ `dlpno_project_tno_amplitudes` kernel expected t1 vectors
already in the full virtual space but received PNO-basis vectors from
`triples_local.py`. The kernel silently skipped them on a size check,
so the C++ path was dropping the singles contribution to the (T)
correction. Fixed by expanding t1 to the full virtual space before
calling the kernel (`Uof(m,m) @ t1[m]`). The same pattern in
`ccsd_local_solver.py::_project_amplitudes` was also corrected.

### Added: Open-shell DLPNO-UCCSD local production solver (BUG 79)
The open-shell DLPNO path now defaults to the reduced-scaling local
solver (`dlpno/uccsd_local_solver.py`) instead of the O(N^6) pilot.
The pilot remains reachable by passing `DLPNOUCCSDPilotOptions` to
`run_job`. The local solver is pilot-anchored (37 ratchet tests pass):
full-domain runs reproduce the dense pilot to 1e-8 Ha (UCCSD) / 1e-11 Ha
((T)), and it carries PAO/PNO/singles-PNO/weak-pair/occupied-coupling/TNO
truncation for the same controlled-approximation bargain as the
closed-shell engine.

- `dlpno/uccsd_local_solver.py`: production local DLPNO-UCCSD solver
  with spin-orbital pair residual kernel (`vibeqc::dlpno_uccsd_pair_residual`)
  and spin-orbital (T) triple energy kernel
  (`vibeqc::dlpno_spin_orbital_triple_energy`).
- `runner.py`: open-shell `dlpno-ccsd`/`dlpno-ccsd(t)` jobs now
  dispatch to the local solver by default; the pilot is opt-in via
  `DLPNOUCCSDPilotOptions`.
- 37 correctness-ratchet tests in `test_dlpno_uccsd_local.py` covering
  full-domain parity, PNO/PAO/singles-PNO truncation, weak-pair screening,
  occupied-distance coupling, TNO truncation, (T0) and (T1) triples modes,
  iterative (T1), triplet high-spin reference, and separated radical.

### Changed: DLPNO-UCCSD runner output formatting
Open-shell DLPNO output now matches the closed-shell format: engine
label, TNO-domain diagnostics, degenerate-triple warnings, and
coupling-radius screening counts.

## [v0.15.122] - 2026-08-09 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Fixed: SCC-DFTB fully reverted to v0.15.116 behaviour (2026-08-09)

The SCC-DFTB DIIS charge-space refactor (v0.15.117) regressed ~20 systems.
The C++ engine was reverted to v0.15.116 in v0.15.121; this completes the
revert by removing the Python-side DIIS forcing in the bare `run_scc_dftb()`
function and periodic SCC-DFTB paths, which still forced `use_diis=True`
against the reverted C++ code's `use_diis=false` default.

### Added: GFN2-xTB parameter provenance in output manifest (BUG 69) (2026-08-08)

GFN2-xTB calculations now record the full parameter identity — version, origin
URL, license, DOI, D4 damping (s8/a1/a2), SCC settings (electronic temperature,
charge mixing, mixer flavour), and SHA-256 checksums of both the locally cached
parameter file and the bundled D4 reference dataset — in the ``[run]`` section
of ``{output}.system`` via ``OutputWriter.update_run_fields``.  The provenance
dict is a flat scalar map attached to ``SemiempiricalResult.parameter_provenance``
and merged into the manifest before any post-SCF processing.  A stale or
re-fetched parameter cache is auditable from the recorded SHA-256.

``load_gfn2_params`` now records the upstream source SHA-256 in the cached
TOML file.  If a stale cache is detected (source SHA differs from current
upstream), a non-fatal warning is emitted; the calculation proceeds with the
cached parameters for reproducibility.

The DSD-PBEP86 D3(BJ) name alias (v0.15.118) is now scoped to D3(BJ)-only
lookup so the ``_2011`` suffix does not leak into the D4 parameter path.

### Changed: BIPOLE far-field auto-enables for large cells (2026-08-08)

BIPOLE calculations with a lattice cutoff above 8 bohr now automatically
enable the far-field (multipole-based) Coulomb contractor, which is ~15x
faster than exact four-centre ERIs for large unit cells.  Applies to both
closed-shell (RHF/RKS) and open-shell (UHF/UKS) drivers.  Opt-out with
``use_multipole_far_field=False``.

### Added: CPCM solvation DIIS warm-start and q-DIIS acceleration (2026-08-08)

The CPCM implicit-solvation macro-iteration convergence now reuses the
inner SCF's DIIS subspace across solvent updates (warm-start), and an
opt-in q-DIIS accelerator improves convergence of the reaction-field
iterations (BUG 100).

### Performance: BIPOLE far-field gradient contractor in C++ OpenMP (2026-08-08)

The BIPOLE erfc-screened interaction tensor gradient and moment-derivative
terms are now computed in C++ with OpenMP, replacing the Python fallback
for analytic far-field gradients.

## [v0.15.121] - 2026-08-08 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Fixed: `vq` scheduler drain ownership and mixed-version safety (2026-08-08)

Scheduler-target maintenance holds are now independent, owner-scoped leases
stored separately from legacy full and partial drain policy. Daemon-side locked
RPC mutations prevent overlapping admin or fleet operations from erasing one
another, while capability negotiation fails closed against an old or unavailable
daemon. Remote multi-user drain mutations now accept the standard token inputs
and forward secrets through stdin rather than argv. Status reports each lease
and flags provably dead owners; fleet resume can migrate and clean up holds left
by an older rollout journal without lifting unrelated operator holds.

### Fixed: `vq` multi-user identity, quota, and workdir cleanup boundaries (2026-08-08)

Duplicate bare job IDs in different user trees are quarantined without blocking
unrelated jobs, and bare lookup now reports ambiguity instead of choosing an
owner by scan order. Already-admitted local and scheduler jobs retain their
owner-qualified spec path through reconciliation. The per-user active-work and
CPU quotas now count local jobs, scheduler jobs, suspended work, orphans, and
deferred scheduler reattachments once across dispatch ticks. Root-daemon
terminal cleanup derives the managed workdir from that trusted owner identity,
refuses path and symlink mismatches with a durable status diagnostic, and never
deletes through mutable `spec.workdir`.

### Improved: consistent lifecycle across the co-located toolset (2026-08-08)

vibe-qc, vibe-view, vq, and vibe-basis now provide matching install, update,

use component-owned virtual environments by default, provide dry-run and help
paths before an installation exists, preserve or roll back working environments

profile, packages current Electron releases for native macOS/Linux targets, and
supports a separately owned headless-capture environment. vq lifecycle and web
service operations now validate daemon ownership, paths, configuration, and
command outcomes before reporting success.

### Added: complete standalone vibe-basis lifecycle (2026-08-08)

`vibe-basis` 0.10.0 now has macOS/Linux install, Git-aware update,
rollback-capable reinstall, and marker-guarded uninstall scripts. The default
standalone environment lives under `vibe-basis/.venv` and includes SciPy;
`--with-vq` can install the co-located queue CLI on Python 3.12 or newer.
The compatibility `[vq]` extra no longer asks public indexes for an

### Added: GFN2-xTB parameter provenance in output manifest (BUG 69) (2026-08-08)

GFN2-xTB calculations now record the full parameter identity — version, origin
URL, license, DOI, D4 damping (s8/a1/a2), SCC settings (electronic temperature,
charge mixing, mixer flavour), and SHA-256 checksums of both the locally cached
parameter file and the bundled D4 reference dataset — in the ``[run]`` section
of ``{output}.system`` via ``OutputWriter.update_run_fields``.  The provenance
dict is a flat scalar map attached to ``SemiempiricalResult.parameter_provenance``
and merged into the manifest before any post-SCF processing.  A stale or
re-fetched parameter cache is auditable from the recorded SHA-256.

``load_gfn2_params`` now records the upstream source SHA-256 in the cached
TOML file.  If a stale cache is detected (source SHA differs from current
upstream), a non-fatal warning is emitted; the calculation proceeds with the
cached parameters for reproducibility.

The DSD-PBEP86 D3(BJ) name alias (v0.15.118) is now scoped to D3(BJ)-only
lookup so the ``_2011`` suffix does not leak into the D4 parameter path.

### Added: auto-level-shift-on-oscillation for all four molecular SCF drivers (2026-08-08)

The molecular RHF, UHF, RKS, and UKS C++ SCF drivers now detect oscillatory
energy behaviour mid-SCF and automatically engage a persistent Saunders-Hillier
level shift (0.3 Ha) when oscillation is detected, then clear the DIIS history
and continue. This mirrors the ROHF Python driver's long-standing
``auto_level_shift_on_oscillation`` feature and protects against the most
common default-convergence failure: DIIS limit-cycles on transition-metal
systems, heterocycles, and small-gap organics. H2O/LDA/STO-3G without DIIS or
damping converges in 26 iterations with the feature on and fails to converge
in 100 iterations with it off. The feature is on by default (opt-out via
``RHFOptions.auto_level_shift_on_oscillation = False``) and adds no measurable
overhead to normally-converging systems. The engaged shift value and detector
parameters (window, sign-flip count) are configurable per options struct.

### Fixed: CCSD(T) memory estimator 100--2000x too high (BUG 63) (2026-08-08)

The triples memory estimator claimed the full 6-index T3 amplitude tensor was
materialised in-core at O(n_occ^3 x n_vir^3), when the C++ code streams
on-the-fly with nv^3-sized per-thread buffers and never stores the full T3
tensor.  Estimates were 100--2000x too high, blocking all correlated-method
paper validation.  O2 UCCSD(T)/def2-SVP dropped from 27,126 MB to 766 MB;
formic-acid dimer CCSD(T)/cc-pVTZ from 30,768 GB to 16.4 GB.

### Improved: memory estimate now shows key dimensions and uses MB for small values (2026-08-08)

The memory estimate output now includes a ``Dimensions:`` line showing
n_basis, n_occ, n_vir, n_aux and n_threads so users can see why the
estimate is the size it is.  Values below 1 GB now display in MB instead
of "0.00 GB".

### Fixed: MP2 memory estimator double-counted AO-ERI tensor (2026-08-08)

The canonical (non-DF) MP2 estimator added a second n^4 x 8 AO-ERI tensor on
top of the SCF estimate's own ERI tensor.  The MP2 half-transform reuses the
SCF's resident ERI tensor, so the second copy was removed.  H2O2 MP2/cc-pVQZ
estimate dropped from ~20 GB to ~10 GB.

### Performance: C++ triples kernel wired into open-shell DLPNO-UCCSD(T) pilot (2026-08-08)

The open-shell DLPNO-UCCSD(T) pilot's (T) correction now uses the C++
``ccsd_t_triples`` kernel (OpenMP-parallel, on-the-fly contraction) instead
of the pure-Python ``so_triples_correction``, ~20-50x faster for the
spin-orbital (T) correction.  All 26 DLPNO UCCSD tests pass (BUG 79).

### Improved: experimental BIPOLE far-field C++ prototype (2026-08-09)

The Pisani-Dovesi-Roetti (1988) periodic bipolar expansion prototype
(``use_multipole_far_field``) received a comprehensive C++ performance
rewrite and a series of correctness fixes:

* **sphemultipole L=4 experiment** — added 25-component buffer plumbing. The
  later audit found that the interaction tensor truncated total degree above
  3 and that the adjoined-pair moment model was not valid for general angular
  momentum, so this did not establish L=4 production support.
* **C++ OpenMP far-field contractor** — replaces the Python
  ``build_bipolar_coulomb_far_field`` per-quartet loop with a
  ``#pragma omp parallel for`` contractor, **14.9x faster** (0.43s vs 6.35s
  for 222k quartets on MgO STO-3G).  Per-thread interaction-tensor caching
  avoids recomputation.
* **C++ OpenMP pair-centre moment shift** —
  ``shift_multipole_moments_to_pair_centres`` shifts global-origin Cartesian
  moments to adjoined-Gaussian pair centres (Pisani & Dovesi 1980) with
  machine-precision parity to the Python reference.
* **C++ Fock kernel builder** — groups far-field quartets by ``(R_sep, L_order)``
  and builds K matrices via batched matmul.
* **C++ Cartesian-to-spherical + moment-derivative converters** — OpenMP-
  parallel conversion of per-shell-pair Cartesian moments to spherical
  harmonics, plus prototype moment derivatives dM/dC for the far-field
  gradient. Saunders (1992) supplies radial inverse-distance derivative and
  penetration context, not this periodic quartet-gradient implementation.
* **C++ contractor parity** — all 5 C++-Python parity tests pass at
  machine precision (bare Coulomb, Fock blocks); fixed RowMajor/column-major
  layout mismatches and erfc-screened tensor cache collusion (mu_eff added to
  cache keys).
* **Auto-enable for large cells** — ``use_multipole_far_field=None`` (default)
  auto-enables when ``cutoff_bohr > 8.0`` with the Ewald exchange split.
  Supported on all four drivers (RHF/UHF/RKS/UKS).  Explicit ``True``/``False``
  override as before.
* **Penetration dispatch robustness** — correctly handles ``L_max=0``
  (all quartets near-field), ``n_keep > n_sph`` guard, blanket-except→warn
  promotion in infrastructure.
* **Diagnostic H2/STO-3G pin** — internal agreement to 0.2 mHa on that one
  fixture; it did not validate the full periodic quartet-domain identity.
* **Bravais lattice coverage** — all 14 3D types plus 1D/2D.
* **Symmetry** — point-group reduction of the penetration dispatch gives
  ~2.5x fewer unique quartets for rocksalt MgO.

Audit note (2026-08-13): the whole quartet far-field prototype is now gated;
the supported production path is exact Ewald-J-split BIPOLE.

References: Saunders et al., Mol. Phys. 77, 629 (1992);
Pisani & Dovesi, Int. J. Quantum Chem. 17, 501 (1980).

### Fixed: SCC-DFTB reverted to v0.15.116 state, GFN2-xTB gradient sign corrected (2026-08-08)

The SCC-DFTB DIIS charge-space refactor (v0.15.117) regressed ~20 systems

The CPCM implicit-solvation path built and stored two separate JKBuilder

On phones the marketing-site header simply hid most links (`hide-sm` /

(`website/src/components/Nav.astro` + the Nav section of

### Fixed: DFTB0/SCC-DFTB STO-NG coefficients need primitive normalization after all (2026-08-06)

Resolves the v0.15.116 "Known issue: DFTB0/SCC-DFTB PES shape regressed
by the STO-NG normalization fix" entry below. `fbb23f74d` ("fix(dftb):
set pre_normalized=true for HSP STO-NG coefficients") had the direction
backwards. Eq. (2.3) of Hehre, Stewart & Pople, J. Chem. Phys. 51, 2657
(1969) defines the primitive Gaussians `g_1s`/`g_2p` as already
unity-normalized, and Eq. (2.2) expands each STO as `d_k * g(alpha_k, r)`
over those normalized primitives — i.e. the tabulated `d_i` in
`sto3g_table`/`sto4g_table`/`sto6g_table` are literal HSP values that
still need primitive-normalization factors embedded before use. This is
exactly libint2's own documented convention (`libint2::Shell`'s doc
comment: "contraction coefficients correspond to unity-normalized
primitives... EMSL Gaussian Basis Set Database... convention"; raw
literature `d_i` require `Shell::renorm()`). `fbb23f74d` skipped that
step (`coefficients_pre_normalized=true` → `embed_normalization_into_coefficients=false`),
which loses **both** the primitive normalization and libint's
enforce-unit-normalization pass. Measured on H₂O/`dftb0_default`, the
overlap diagonal went from exactly 1 (`max|S_μμ − 1| = 4.4e-16`) to

    diag(S) = [0.647, 0.0285, 0.0285, 0.0285, 3.847, 3.847]

— a 135× inconsistency between O 2p and H 1s. DFTB builds its
Hamiltonian from these overlaps, so per-element mis-scaling of that
size is the mechanism behind the collapsed short-range repulsive wall
on the water O-H PES, the periodic DFTB0 analytic-vs-FD gradient
mismatch on the MgO slab, the broken k-mesh convergence to the dense
limit, and (previously undiagnosed, found while re-verifying this fix)
broken DFTB0/SCC-DFTB lattice optimization, periodic preoptimization,
and periodic stress-vs-FD — all of which the v0.15.116 known-issue
entry's own xfails had independently masked as "aspirational/
pre-existing" rather than recognizing as the same root cause.

`cpp/src/semiempirical/basis.cpp` reverts `SemiempiricalBasis::build`
to `coefficients_pre_normalized=false`, restoring `embed=true`. The
companion `5102ec583` energy re-pins for `REF_DFTB0_H2O`, `REF_SCC_H2O`,
`REF_SCC_CH4`, the Thiel pyrrole/imidazole native-default energies, and
the USCC-DFTB NO2 convergence assertion are reverted to their pre-
`fbb23f74d` values — each reproduced to the full precision those pins
carry (e.g. `REF_SCC_H2O`: obtained -3.641742907548625 against the
restored -3.641743 pin, which is pinned to 7 significant figures at
`rel=1e-5`; this is agreement at the pin's stated tolerance, not a
verified bit-identical reproduction of a full-precision archived
value). The seven `pytest.xfail()` markers
`5102ec583` added for lattice optimization / preoptimization / stress-FD
are removed — all seven now pass for real. `tests/test_semiempirical_pes.py`,
`tests/test_neb_semiempirical.py`, and `tests/test_semiempirical_kpoint_dftb_convergence.py`
are green again (their `known_reds_baseline.json` entries removed).

GFN2-xTB is a separate, still-open question: `SemiempiricalBasis::build`
for `CoreParameterSet` (GFN2's path) defaults `coefficients_pre_normalized`
to `true` (the constructor default, documented for round-tripping
`shells()` output — not this case) and was never flipped by `fbb23f74d`.
It draws from the *same* raw HSP tables, so the same argument likely
applies there too, and `02fa9422c`'s own disclosed "~10 mEh likely in
overlap normalization differences" residual is a plausible symptom of
it — but GFN2 is untouched here; it needs its own investigation since
its parameters may have been calibrated against the existing
convention. See `handovers/HANDOVER_OPEN_BUGS_V015.md`.

`tests/test_runner_optimize_semiempirical_traj.py` has pre-existing,
unrelated SCC-DFTB finite-temperature-retry test failures independent
of this bug (reproduced 9+ shared failures under *both* the buggy and
fixed normalization convention, with a different subset failing under
each) — flagged separately, not fixed here.

### Fixed: SCC-DFTB convergence on heteronuclear and pi-conjugated molecules (2026-08-06)

SCC-DFTB DIIS on several molecules (HCOOH, acetamide, formamide dimer,
heteronuclear diatomics) diverged or stalled due to three coordinated defects.
First, the DIIS history was built in potential space (gamma-weighted), which
loses balance for mixed-element systems; it now runs in unweighted charge
space (Anderson mixing), eliminating the gamma-matrix solve and its diagonal
fallback. Second, the DIIS subspace depth was 6, but the ~10 charge degrees
of freedom become linearly dependent much faster than Fock matrices — depth
is now 2, keeping the matrix well-conditioned, with vector-Aitken (Irons &
Tuck) relaxation as the provably-contractive fallback. Third, a trust-region
guard rejects any DIIS-extrapolated step whose absolute SCC-energy change
exceeds `max(0.1 * n_atoms, |E_scc_cur|)`. Periodic Gamma and k-point
SCC-DFTB gain the same DIIS accelerator (was simple mixing only) and
the same guard. Default iteration budget raised from 200 to 500 for the
bare `run_scc_dftb()` path.

### Fixed: ROHF convergence controls, missing DIIS depth policies, and level-shift orbital-energy corruption (2026-08-06)

The ROHF/ROKS Roothaan driver diverged on FeCl₃/def2-TZVP and stalled on
several other open-shell systems because it lacked the adaptive-depth DIIS
policies (`R_CDIIS` / `AD_CDIIS`) that every other SCF driver (RHF, UHF,
RKS, UKS) already carried (BUG 118). Three further defects found on the way:

* **Level shift corrupted orbital energies.** The Saunders-Hillier shift was
  applied to the canonicalising diagonalisation, so every converged ROHF run
  with `level_shift > 0` reported virtual orbital energies (gap, .molden,
  Koopmans estimates, semicanonical MP2/CCSD) too high by exactly the shift.
  CH₃/STO-3G: gap 0.6707 Ha reported as 0.9707 Ha at `level_shift = 0.3`.
  Silent because the shift is inert on the occupied block and the total
  energy is exact. Now always unshifted.
* **`level_shift_warmup_cycles` was ignored.** The per-iteration release
  policy declared by `level_shift.hpp` never reached the ROHF driver; an
  existing job setting `level_shift` now auto-releases it (set
  `level_shift_warmup_cycles = 0` for the previous persistent hold).
* **`dynamic_damping` fields were declared but read nowhere.** The
  Zerner-Hehenberger update now runs, mirroring `dynamic_damping.hpp`.

`ROHFOptions` gains `diis_restart_tau`, `diis_adaptive_delta`,
`level_shift_warmup_cycles`, and `level_shift_schedule`; the
Saunders-Hillier citation now fires for ROHF/ROKS jobs.

## [v0.15.116] - 2026-08-06 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Fixed: multi-k GAPW collocated the smooth density with a hardcoded image reach (2026-08-03)

`run_periodic_rks_gapw_multi_k` built its Bloch AO tables from a hardcoded
`direct_lattice_cells(system, 25.0)`, independent of cell size and basis.
Those tables satisfy `int_cell chi_mk chi_nk^* = S(k)` only when the sum
over lattice translations is complete, so the reach is determined by the
basis rather than free, and the collocated smooth density must carry the
analytic soft charge `sum_k w_k tr(D_s(k) S_s(k))`. It did not: measured at
a fixed density on LiH rocksalt/STO-3G/(2,2,2), the collocated charge
missed by **-1.536e-01 e** on a cell expanded to 2.20x its equilibrium
lattice constant (and by 1.5e-07 at equilibrium, which is why the defect
had gone unnoticed). The reach now comes from `bloch_overlap_cutoff_bohr`,
floored at 25.0 bohr so no previously-adequate cell shrinks, leaving the
charge error at or below 3e-07 across the scan. The tolerance is 1e-8
rather than that helper's 1e-12 default, which is sized for S(k) positive
definiteness -- a stricter requirement than converging a charge, and one
that would cost 3.4x more image cells at equilibrium for no change in the
energy. Cost at the new tolerance is 1.7x-3.2x more image cells.

Same defect family as GPW-MULTIK-OVERLAP-NOT-PSD: two independent
hardcoded reaches where one identity governs both.

**This does NOT fix MULTIK-GAPW-BLOCH-FAILS-ON-EXPANDED-CELLS.** The
expanded-cell SCF still fails to converge after the fix, so the charge
error was a real defect and a correlate rather than the cause. Four
hypotheses are now refuted by measurement and recorded in the bug entry
(grid confound, the compensator/`D(g=0)` mismatch that entry had
previously recorded as confirmed, density oscillation, and this
collocation defect). Equilibrium energies are unchanged to all printed
digits.

### Fixed: two GFN2-xTB basis-plumbing bugs from the STO-3G/4G table switch (2026-08-06)

`02fa9422c` (STO-3G/4G tables) and `e12a04aef` (CRC atomic radii) landed on
`main` without disclosing a full test-suite run; `tests/test_gfn2_xtb.py`
regressed from 112 passed/3 xfailed to 17 failed/95 passed/3 xfailed.
Bisection isolated two independent implementation bugs riding on top of
the (still-experimental, self-acknowledged-incomplete) STO-3G/4G table
switch:

1. `gfn2_n_primitives(mol)` decided the STO-NG primitive count once for
   the *whole molecule* (any heavy atom present forces every atom,
   including H, onto the 4-primitive table) instead of per element as its
   own doc comment specified. Fixed by resolving the primitive count
   per-atom inside `SemiempiricalBasis::build_shell_info` via a new
   `n_primitives == 0` "auto" sentinel.
2. `compute_gfn2_gradient`, `compute_periodic_gfn2_gradient`, and
   `compute_periodic_gfn2_stress` kept building their internal basis with
   a stale hardcoded 6 primitives after the energy driver switched to the
   element-dependent count — differentiating a different energy surface
   than the one `run_gfn2_xtb` actually converged. This was the dominant
   cause of the gradient-vs-FD test failures.

Both fixes, plus two `tests/test_gfn2_xtb.py::TestGFN2Periodic` tests that
hardcoded the pre-`e12a04aef` `p_rad` radii instead of the new CRC atomic
radii, bring the suite to 0 failed/97 passed/18 xfailed. The remaining 15
failures are downstream of the STO-3G/4G table's own disclosed accuracy
gap (`02fa9422c`: "overshoots; remaining ~10 mEh likely in overlap
normalization differences") and are now `xfail(strict=True)` with detailed
reasons rather than re-pinned to possibly-still-wrong values — see
`handovers/HANDOVER_OPEN_BUGS_V015.md` (semiempirical article-validation
open items) for the live tracking entry. Note: `main` independently landed
`fbb23f74d` (DFTB0/SCC-DFTB STO-NG normalization fix, unrelated to GFN2 —
GFN2's basis construction already defaulted to the correct
`coefficients_pre_normalized=true`) and `10c6e7eb4` (partial GFN2 xfails)
while this fix was in progress in an isolated worktree; this entry's fixes
are additive on top of both and were verified to still bring the suite
fully green after rebasing.

### Known issue: DFTB0/SCC-DFTB PES shape regressed by the STO-NG normalization fix (2026-08-06)

`fbb23f74d` ("fix(dftb): set pre_normalized=true for HSP STO-NG
coefficients") shifted all DFTB0/SCC-DFTB energies. The companion commit
`5102ec583` re-pinned the absolute reference energies this broke in
`tests/test_semiempirical.py`, `tests/test_semiempirical_benchmarks.py`,
and `tests/test_semiempirical_dftb0.py` (all green), but PES shape,
periodic analytic gradients, and multi-k convergence were never
re-validated against the new convention. Bisection (release-chat
pre-flight) confirms real, qualitatively wrong physics, not stale
pinning: the water O-H bond-length scan shows no repulsive wall at short
r and the minimum collapses to the shortest scanned point for both
DFTB0 and SCC-DFTB (`tests/test_semiempirical_pes.py`); a periodic
analytic-vs-FD gradient mismatch on an MgO slab
(`tests/test_neb_semiempirical.py`); and a broken k-mesh convergence to
the dense limit (`tests/test_semiempirical_kpoint_dftb_convergence.py`).
Reverting only the normalization flag restores the PES-shape tests but
breaks the freshly re-pinned point energies, so the two changes are
mutually inconsistent as landed — this needs a semiempirical-domain fix
(most likely a repulsive-potential recalibration against the corrected
normalization), not another repin. DFTB0/SCC-DFTB carry "Screening/preopt"
status in `docs/user_guide/semiempirical.md` (not gated-experimental like
GFN2-xTB), and DFTB0 preoptimization is that doc's headline usage
example, so this is a real user-facing risk until fixed. Tracked as
known-reds in `scripts/test_gate/known_reds_baseline.json` (owner:
semiempirical) and escalated for a root-cause fix.

### Fixed: the short-range aux ERI kernels enumerated images by |g|, not by pair separation (2026-08-06)

The 2026-08-03 fix `5a40626a8` converted every bare-Coulomb aux ERI kernel
to `pair_complete_cells` and **missed the two short-range ones**.
`compute_2c_eri_lattice_sr` and `compute_3c_eri_lattice_sr` kept the old
`direct_lattice_cells` enumeration, which bounds `|g| <= cutoff` rather
than the physical pair separation `|O_P - O_Q - g|`.

Measured on MgO primitive FCC / def2-svp-jk at `omega = 0.4`, cutoff
12 bohr, comparing a cell against the **same crystal** with one atom
translated by a lattice vector:

    before:  min eig(M_SR)  -2.14e+01  vs  -3.30e+01,  ||dM|| = 1.27e+02
    after :  identical spectra,                        ||dM|| = 1.66e-13

A 50% change in an inner-product matrix between two descriptions of one
crystal. This reached production through the Gamma-only `rsgdf` route
(`build_lpq_native(algorithm="rsgdf")`), the sole SR consumer. A
single-atom cell has zero intra-cell offset, so vacuum-box fixtures could
never see it.

Chasing the residual indefiniteness confirmed the RSGDF metric formula
itself is correct, including the `pi/(Omega omega^2)` G=0 compensation of
Ye & Berkelbach Eq. (12): `M_SR + M_LR` reaches PSD once the short-range
real-space sum is converged -- min eig `-16.4 / -0.78 / -8.2e-05 /
-3.5e-13` at cutoff `8 / 12 / 20 / 30` bohr, while the long-range G-mesh
is already converged at 169 plane waves. The controlling parameter is the
SR cutoff, and an inner-product matrix is far more sensitive to a dropped
tail than an energy is: the truncation changes the metric's *signature*,
not merely its magnitude.

Pinned by `tests/test_aux_eri_sr_lattice_enumeration.py`. Note the 3c
tensor is deliberately NOT pinned on translation invariance: `T_Pmn =
sum_g (P_0 | mu_0 nu_g)` fixes both the auxiliary index and `mu` to the
reference cell and sums only over `nu`, so it legitimately changes under
a lattice translation (the bare kernel moves by 8.6 on this cell, more
than the SR one). It is pinned instead on its `omega -> 0` limit against
the bare-Coulomb kernel, which it approaches linearly.

### Added: open-shell `(T1)` can now carry a screened triple list (2026-08-06)

`run_local_dlpno_uccsd` has refused `triples_mode="t1"` together with any
realised weak-pair or occupied-distance screening since it was written. That
refusal is correct and stays: `"t1"` rotates the occupied indices into the
per-spin canonical basis, where an LMO distance no longer refers to the
indices being dropped, so a screened triple list cannot survive it.

What the guard was really standing in for was the absence of a
screening-capable triples route. There is one now. The localised-basis
iteration of Guo, Riplinger, Becker, Liakos, Minenkov, Cavallo and Neese,
*J. Chem. Phys.* **148**, 011101 (2018), Eq. (2) — landed over several
increments as `vibeqc.dlpno.triples_iterative` — reintroduces the off-diagonal
occupied Fock coupling by iterating the triples amplitudes instead of rotating
them, so the triple list never leaves the basis in which screening means
something. `triples_mode="t1-iterative"` routes it.

Unscreened, the two `(T1)` routes agree to `1e-17` on OH/STO-3G
(`-2.307409817211e-07` rotation, `-2.307409817913e-07` iterative) while both
differ from the semicanonical `(T0)` (`-2.097307488230e-07`), so the coupling
is genuinely being captured rather than the agreement being trivial.

Screened, on separated OH + H2 with `coupling_radius=5` (81 of 165 triples
dropped): `"t1"` raises, as it must; `"t0"` gives `-2.080146e-07`; and
`"t1-iterative"` gives `-2.289116e-07`, which sits nearer the unscreened
`(T1)` than the screened `(T0)` does. So it removes the semicanonical error
instead of inheriting it, on a list `"t1"` cannot represent at all.

Deliberately only half of the remaining gate item: this is a new opt-in mode
and no default moves. Public routing, and any decision about defaults, stay
unclaimed as a maintainer call.

### Fixed: vq scheduler jobs on site_i no longer die `std::bad_alloc` from the `-l mem=` rlimit trap (BUG 118) (2026-08-06)

Root cause of the BH9 campaign's site_i subqueue wipeout (124 runner
bundles, 0 usable outputs): site_i's Torque 2.5.12 pbs_mom applies
`Resource_List.mem` as a **hard per-process `RLIMIT_DATA` + `RLIMIT_RSS`**
equal to the request — live-probed in-job on the `inf` queue
(`mem=14733mb` → `Max data size = 15448670208` bytes, hard = soft, not
raisable in-job) — and on site_i's 6.5 kernels `RLIMIT_DATA` counts mmap
allocations. Every tightly-sized vibe-qc child therefore failed with
`std::bad_alloc` seconds into execution while its node had >150 GB free.
The filed "child PBS jobs never started" reading was wrong for the lanes
that dispatched: children ran and died on allocation; the 29 of 32 cl###
bundles with empty `cases/` were operator-killed while still PENDING,
before qsub.

vq's `HostConfig` grows `scheduler_mem_directive = "request" | "omit"`
(default `"request"`, existing behavior everywhere). `"omit"` drops the
scheduler memory directive from generated job scripts while keeping
`mem_mb` for vq-side accounting and the `VQ_MEM_MB` job env — correct for
sites like site_i whose scheduler enforces no memory admission (no
`resources_max` on any queue or the server; local users submit without
`-l mem`). Rejected fail-fast on `scheduler = "local"` hosts. Tests:
`vibe-queue/tests/test_scheduler_dispatch.py` (omit drops only `-l mem=`;
default unchanged; factory carries the field) and
`vibe-queue/tests/test_config.py` (accept/default/local-reject); full vq
suite 4729 passed / 12 skipped on macOS. Deployment: set
`scheduler_mem_directive = "omit"` under `[hosts.site_i]` in the example_hub
driver config after the driver's vq is updated, then restart the driver.
Note the separate campaign-side finding: the a03 retry wave (inflated mem
grants) cleared `bad_alloc` but heavy def2-QZVPP tiers then hit the
carrier's per-case timeout (rc=124) on site_i's slower shared nodes — tier
routing to site_i, or excluding site_i for L/M tiers, remains a
campaign-pool decision, not a vq defect.

### Fixed: LiH parity figure confirmed on a fresh build; one wrong claim from that fix corrected (2026-08-06)

Two follow-ups to the entry below, one confirming it and one correcting it.

**Confirmed.** That entry's figures were measured on a native core built
before three GDF-path commits landed, two of which touch the path the
energies come from: `284df4150` (fuse the cderi pair scaling into the
pair-FT kernel's store) and `1cda0bbf0` (farm the multi-k exchange build
over MPI ranks); `8283a96ba` is reporting only. Re-measured on a
dedicated pristine clone at `c6aee549a` with the native core rebuilt from
those sources, all three commits present:

| lattice cutoff | earlier build | fresh build   | shift    |
|----------------|---------------|---------------|----------|
| default        | -7.9203950510 | -7.9203950510 | 0.00e+00 |
| `cutoff_bohr=30` | -7.9220046694 | -7.9220046694 | 0.00e+00 |

Bit-identical, so those commits are numerically neutral here and the
**−1.4 µHa figure stands on current `main`**. The PySCF reference is also
version-stable: 2.13.1 and 2.14.0 both return `-7.9220032345 Ha` at
`cell.precision` 1e-8. vibe-qc and PySCF ran from different virtualenvs
throughout, so they never shared an interpreter (CLAUDE.md § 10).

**Corrected.** The entry below added a sentence to
`docs/user_guide/multi_k_scf.md` claiming `rcut_strategy` and
`rcut_precision` "do not enter" the default `gdf_method="rsgdf"` route.
That is wrong for `rcut_strategy`. It is right that neither sizes the
**fit** sums there: `build_lpq_bloch_native_fft` does not accept either
argument, and only the `"compcell"` / `"mdf"` builders forward them to
the estimator. But `_oneel_lattice_opts` reads `rcut_strategy` as a
boolean gate: the default `"pyscf_auto"` enables a *measured* widening of
the one-electron S/T cutoff (grow until `S(k)` leaves the non-PSD tier),
and `"flat"` opts out. The widening only ever raises the cutoff and is a
no-op for tight bases, which is why it does not perturb these numbers
(`"flat"` and `"pyscf_auto"` measure bit-identical on this system), but
"does not enter" was the wrong reason. The doc now states both roles.

This also resolves the open question flagged in that commit: listing
RSGDF among `RcutStrategy.PYSCF_AUTO`'s consumers **is** defensible, since
the rsgdf route does consume the value. Only the bullet's stated
rationale (pairing with a reciprocal-space AFT correction) describes the
compcell case rather than the S/T-widening case. Left as-is; no code or
docstring change follows from it.


### Added: per-pair adjoined-center moments (bipolar far-field foundations, 2b) (2026-08-06)

`vibeqc.bipole_pair_moments` shifts the one-pass global-origin lattice
moments to every shell pair's own adjoined-Gaussian product center
(`C = (a₁A + a₂(B+g))/(a₁+a₂)` with `a` each shell's most diffuse
primitive — the reference adjoined convention of Pisani–Dovesi 1980
§ 4) via the exact per-axis polynomial shift, the seam the C++ moments
header documents deliberately. This is the bra/ket moment supply for
the quartet-level bipolar far field: expansion about pair centers is
what makes the multipole series converge, where the retired G1
branch's global-origin cell moments could not. Tests pin the shift
algebra to machine precision against an independent libint computation
at a shifted origin, the centers formula (home + displaced cells,
diagonal pairs at shell origins), and monopole invariance.

### Added: erf-screened multipole interaction tensors (bipolar far-field foundations) (2026-08-06)

`vibeqc.bipole_multipole` gains `screened_multipole_interaction_tensor`
(the point-multipole interaction through the smooth `erf(√μ·r)/r`
half of an Ewald split, built from the McMurchie–Davidson Boys-function
ladder for the kernel's Cartesian derivatives) and
`sr_multipole_interaction_tensor` (the short-range complement by
linearity, `T_bare − T_erf`). This is the tensor a quartet-level
bipolar far field contracts with pair moments in the BIPOLE
Ewald-split gauge — BIPOLE-EXACT-ZONE increment 2a, the screened
analogue of the Saunders 1992 § 5.3 radial recursion — with the
per-quartet effective `1/μ = 1/γ_bra + 1/γ_ket + 1/ω²`. Five new
tests pin the derivative ladder against finite differences, the exact
monopole law, the large-μ bare-tensor limit, the linearity identity
at 1e-13, and the two-Gaussian reduced-exponent physics anchor.
McMurchie–Davidson 1978 joins the `bipole` citation route.

### Fixed: `residual_domain="extended"` now is the paper's extended domain (2026-08-06)

**This corrects an entry released in v0.15.115.** That entry described
`residual_domain="extended"` as the extended domain of Riplinger and Neese,
*J. Chem. Phys.* **138**, 034106 (2013), Sec. II B 1. It was not.

The paper defines the extended domain over **atoms**: "the union of the
domains of orbitals i and j and furthermore ... all atoms of the domains of
all orbitals k", spanned by the PAOs on those atoms. What shipped instead
spanned the union of the coupled pairs' **PNO** spaces — a buffer assembled
out of the very truncated spaces whose deficiency it exists to absorb, and
dependent on `tcut_pno` where the paper's construction is not. That is why a
residue survived, and why the released entry's conclusion ("a buffer, not an
exactness device") was drawn from the wrong construction.

The atom-based domain is now implemented. The check that it is the right one
is cheap and was stated before measuring: at the shipped `tcut_mkn=0` every
orbital domain is *all* atoms, so the extended domain must span the whole
virtual space and coincide with `"full"` exactly. It does, digit for digit —
deviation from the pilot on H2O/def2-SVP is `+1.51 / −0.11 / +0.01` µHa at
`tcut_pno = 1e-5 / 1e-6 / 1e-7` in both modes, against `−10060.8 / −2365.9 /
−226.6` µHa for the `"pair"` default.

The reduced-scaling property, which the previous construction could not
demonstrate, shows up once `tcut_mkn > 0` restricts the atom domains.
Separated water dimer (10 Å) at def2-SVP, 38 virtuals:

| `tcut_mkn` | mean contraction dim | wall time |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 38.00 of 38 | 973 s |
| 1e-2 | **27.64 of 38** | **226 s** |

So the buffer genuinely shrinks with the atom domains rather than with the
PNO truncation, which is the property that makes it a production route rather
than a correctness knob.

A regression that asserted the extended domain could *not* reach the pilot was
rewritten: it had pinned the weaker construction. Its docstring records that
an earlier revision asserted the opposite, so the correction is visible where
someone would otherwise re-derive it.

Default stays `"pair"`; no shipped number moves.

### Fixed: the BIPOLE fold guard is now gauge-independent (one shared guard, all four drivers) (2026-08-06)

The S(k) fold-support guard sat inside `if exchange_split_active:` in
all four BIPOLE drivers, so legacy-gauge runs skipped the reliability
check entirely — measured on LiF/STO-3G/Γ: the corrected gauge refused
(`BipoleFoldUnreliableError`) while `use_exchange_ewald_split=False`
entered SCF on the identical, 840×-past-target support. The defect the
guard protects against — truncated real-space lattice sums corrupting
the Bloch-folded eigenproblem — is gauge-independent, so this was a
guard hole, not a convention (filed as the fold-guard-hole entry in
`HANDOVER_OPEN_BUGS_V015.md` by the archiving previous BIPOLE chat;
maintainer-approved behaviour change).

The four drifting inline copies (UHF/UKS had lost message text and the
converged-log branch) are unified into one shared helper,
`pbc_bipole_common.enforce_bipole_fold_support`, hoisted above the
gauge condition. **Behaviour change:** legacy-gauge runs on unreliable
fold support now fail closed with the same thresholds (>1e-2 refuse,
>1e-4 note) plus a suffix explaining why the guard applies off the
corrected gauge; legacy results record the measured
`overlap_fold_drift` instead of `None`. The retired-G1 far-field
sentinels keep their deliberately-small dipolar-LiH fixtures via an
explicit, commented guard bypass (their subject is composition on a
fixed truncated support, not fold physics).

## [v0.15.115] - 2026-08-06 - *Neese's Cheetah*


### Fixed: the LiH multi-k PySCF parity figure was stale (2026-08-05)

`docs/user_guide/multi_k_scf.md` and `docs/tutorial/lih_multi_k.md` quoted
**−1.0 µHa** for LiH primitive FCC / sto-3g / def2-svp-jk at kmesh (2,2,2)
against `pyscf.pbc.scf.KRHF.density_fit()` at a converged lattice cutoff.
Re-measured out of process (PySCF 2.13.1, CLAUDE.md § 10: two
interpreters, never a shared import): the value is **−1.4 µHa**.

| lattice cutoff             | vibe-qc       | Δ vs PySCF  |
|----------------------------|---------------|-------------|
| default (15 bohr / nuc 25) | -7.9203950510 | +1.6082 mHa |
| `cutoff_bohr = 30`         | -7.9220046694 | -1.4349 µHa |

Reference `-7.9220032345 Ha`, which reproduces the quoted `-7.92200323`
exactly and is itself self-converged to 0.026 µHa between `cell.precision`
1e-8 and 1e-10. PySCF spells the aux set `def2-svp-jkfit`; its H/Li
primitives are bit-identical to vibe-qc's `def2-svp-jk`.

The **+1.6 mHa at the default cutoff reproduces unchanged** and stands as
written. Only the converged-cutoff figure moved. The same stale −1.0 µHa
in `tests/test_audit_20260530_periodic.py`'s docstring is corrected; its
50 µHa assertion bound is unaffected and unchanged.

**What did NOT cause this:** `ca7fe4573` (RCUT-PYSCF-MISPORT) does not
reach this route. `run_krhf_periodic_gdf` dispatches the per-pair `Lpq`
builder on `gdf_method`, whose default `"rsgdf"` selects
`build_lpq_bloch_native_fft`, which is handed `lat_opts` directly and given
neither `rcut_strategy` nor `rcut_precision`. Only the `"compcell"` and
`"mdf"` branches forward those into the `aux_basis.py` call sites that
reach the estimator, matching that commit's own note that the default
rsgdf route has 0 call sites reaching it. `use_compcell=True` selects the
compcell Fock/exchange treatment, which is an independent knob from
`gdf_method="compcell"`. **The actual cause of the 0.4 µHa move is not
established and is not claimed.**

Also corrected, both stale independently of the above:

* `RcutStrategy.PYSCF_AUTO`'s docstring claimed it "Matches PySCF's
  `cell.rcut`". It does not: `estimate_rcut_pyscf`'s own docstring
  records a measured 0.77-0.78x, and this system measures 0.71x
  (23.264 vs 32.742 bohr for sto-3g at precision 1e-8). It now states the
  ratio and points at that function. Added a caller note that
  `make_lattice_opts` *replaces* `base_opts.cutoff_bohr` under this
  strategy rather than taking the larger of the two.
* `docs/user_guide/multi_k_scf.md` now says explicitly that
  `rcut_strategy` / `rcut_precision` do not enter the default multi-k
  route, so `cutoff_bohr` is the whole accuracy knob there.

Docs-only plus two docstrings; no behaviour change.


### Reclassified: the Cartesian AO-convention defect was reachable in production, not latent (2026-08-06)

The 2026-08-05 Cartesian-convention arc (spec pin `839f38036`, evaluator
fix `a8130d61f`, COSX fix `7fc952182`) claimed no production calculation
could reach the broken path because "every named basis forces
`set_pure(true)`". Independent review
(`handovers/HANDOVER_AO_CONVENTION.md`) found that claim true of the
named-basis route only: `vibeqc.basis_toolkit.to_libint_basis()` — a
documented public API shipped in v0.15.0 (`dacb7a6fb`) — honors an
imported basis's `harmonic_type` and hands `pure=False` shells straight to
`BasisSet`; the NWChem importer reads Cartesian-ness from the basis file
itself (`basis "name" cartesian`), and the g94 and CRYSTAL importers
accept it as an argument. `evaluate_ao` feeds the DFT XC quadrature (rks,
uks, gradients, periodic XC), so on such an import this was every DFT
energy, gradient, and Hessian, not just the QVF writer. Measured end to
end (Be with an imported Cartesian d shell, RKS/PBE): ~0.35 Ha error and
no convergence before `a8130d61f`.

Severity therefore reclassifies from "latent" to a real defect with low
blast radius (Cartesian basis imports are rare): DFT and COSX on Cartesian
imports were wrong in v0.15.0 through v0.15.113; COSX-only — and worse,
2.4e-1 relative in K, because the evaluator half was fixed first — in
v0.15.114; fully fixed at the next tag. (The arc's fix entries sit under
the v0.15.113 heading below, but `git tag --contains a8130d61f` shows the
evaluator fix first shipped in v0.15.114 — the windows here follow the
tags, not the heading.) Correction notes are
added in place to the affected v0.15.113 entries, and code comments and
test docstrings now say "unreachable through the named-basis route" rather
than "unreachable". A second entry point — `guess_read.py` builds the
prior basis for `guess="read"` with purity taken from an external QVF
file — is benign today (it only feeds `compute_overlap_two_basis` density
projection, where libint's convention is self-consistent) but is recorded
in the handover as a live external-input path.

### Added: Cartesian in-shell ordering guard; AO-convention gate promoted to blocking T1 (2026-08-06)

Follow-ups from the independent review of the Cartesian-convention arc

reclassification above:

  `cpp/include/vibeqc/basis.hpp`, beside the existing solid-harmonic one.
  The Cartesian in-shell order (lx descending, then ly) is hardcoded in at

* `tests/test_ao_convention_invariants.py` is now **blocking T1** in the
  release gate (was non-blocking T2): grid-vs-engine AO parity is the
  invariant every DFT XC quadrature rests on, and the defect class shipped
  once already. Regenerating the suite manifest also recovered four rows
  other chats had hand-edited into the generated JSON without CURATED
  backing; they are preserved verbatim in the CURATED table now.
* The libint primitive norm — six near-identical private copies before —
  is centralized as `vibeqc._primitive_norm.libint_primitive_norm` for the
  four in-package users (QVF writer, molden writer, basis filter, BIPOLE
  primitive splitter), bitwise-identical to every retired copy; the
  qvf-writer and vibe-view copies stay independent by design.
* The stale "unit-normalized" prose is gone from every producer-facing QVF

### Added: restricted exact bielectronic zone for BIPOLE (`exact_zone_bohr`, opt-in) (2026-08-06)

BIPOLE-EXACT-ZONE-UNBOUNDED increment 1. On diffuse bases the S(k)
fold gate legitimately demands a large `cutoff_bohr` (LiH/STO-3G:
~37 bohr for a 1e-4 fold drift), and the expensive exact erfc J/K
traversal historically grew with it — the measured root of the
"converged cutoff walltime-prohibitive" verdict. The RHF and RKS
BIPOLE drivers now accept `exact_zone_bohr`: the exact-ERI OUTPUT
zone is bounded independently of the operator/fold range, and
operator cells beyond the zone carry the reciprocal `J_LR` channel
plus the neutralising background — the Ewald far-field model of the
density. This is the bielectronic/monoelectronic zone partition of
the periodic-Gaussian Coulomb literature (Dovesi, Pisani, Roetti &
Saunders 1983, Eq. (24a); Pisani, Dovesi & Roetti 1988, Sec. II.4)
expressed in the Ewald-split gauge; the two primary sources joined
`database.toml` on the `bipole` route in this merge, verified live to
reach `.references` / `.bibtex` / `.system`.

Honesty contract: the omitted SR tail is a measured, per-case
quantity (fixed-density anchors: MgO/STO-3G 2.7e-3 Ha at zone 10,
3.2e-4 Ha at zone 12; LiH-class diffuse bases keep mHa-scale tail to
~14 bohr) — choose the zone by a small ladder like the SR pad. Guard
rails: requires the corrected exchange split + padded SR path, must
sit strictly below `cutoff_bohr`, rejected with SYM3b reduction /
pair-resolved domains, analytic-gradient preview fails closed (FD
forces remain production), zone recorded on the result and in the
log. Unset ⇒ byte-identical to the previous behavior. Increment 1b
(same day) extended the zone to the UHF/UKS drivers and lifted the
runner restriction to all four methods (ROHF/ROKS and the dedicated
screened-exchange K traversal fail closed).
Tests: `tests/test_bipole_exact_zone.py` (builder bitwise-equality +
far-zeros, resolver validation, SCF tail envelope, gradient
fail-closed); `tests/test_citations.py` pins the new entries.

### Docs: `exp_to_discard` does not remove the periodic lattice-sum requirement (2026-08-06)

`docs/user_guide/basis_sets.md` recommended `exp_to_discard=0.1` for
periodic runs with diffuse molecular bases without saying what it buys.
Measured on a rocksalt LiF primitive cell, it does not bring the required
lattice cutoff near the shipped flat 15 bohr — it lands on
`bloch_overlap_cutoff_bohr`'s hard 25 bohr floor for every basis tried
(STO-3G 37.1 → 25.7; def2-SVP 51.5 → 25.0, at the cost of 23 → 18 basis
functions; def2-TZVP 45.3 → 25.0, 45 → 40). Discarding primitives
therefore changes the basis — and the answer — while leaving the
requirement above the default by construction. The page now says so,
carries the measured table, and points at `bloch_overlap_cutoff_bohr` to
size the requirement and `s_fold_truncation_drift` to check a given
choice (`<1e-4` converged, `>1e-2` refused by the BIPOLE drivers; the
drift predicts the total-energy error to within about 3× across four
decades).

### Fixed: `method='KRHF'` now names its replacement instead of dead-ending (2026-08-06)

`run_periodic_job(method='KRHF')` raised a `NotImplementedError` that listed
the supported methods but did not say what to use instead, and a bug report
(BUG 125) read that as KRHF having been *removed* in an API change between
`v0.15.21` and `v0.15.112`. It was not: `v0.15.21` gated on
`("RHF", "RKS", "UHF", "UKS")` and rejected `'KRHF'` identically — the
accepted set has only grown since (ROHF/ROKS), and `git log -S '"KRHF"'`
shows `KRHF` was never a `run_periodic_job` method at any version. The
spelling is a natural one to reach for (PySCF's multi-k driver is `KRHF`,
and vibe-qc's own result type is `PeriodicKRHFGDFResult`), but k-point
sampling is not a method here — it is the `kpoints` argument, and every
supported method is multi-k whenever `kpoints` is set. A `K`-prefixed
spelling of any supported method now answers with the call the user wanted
(`method='RHF'` plus an explicit mesh). Unknown methods keep the plain
unsupported-list message, and `KS` does not trip the advice.
`tests/test_periodic_runner_method_gate.py` pins all six K-spellings, the
case-insensitive path, and both negative cases.

### Docs + pinned identity: comparing vibe-qc periodic totals with CRYSTAL (2026-08-06)

`docs/user_guide/from_crystal.md` gained a "Comparing total energies:
mesh and exchange-convention rules" section replacing the stale
"few mHa up to the Madelung self-image correction" claim: match the
k-mesh first (zone-centred `kpoints=(n,n,n)` == `SHRINK n n`; a Γ-run
vs `SHRINK 2` differs by hundreds of mHa of k-sampling error on
compact ionic cells), CRYSTAL applies **no** exact-exchange G=0
correction (its coarse-mesh HF/hybrid totals over-bind their own
k-converged limit — measured 638 mHa on MgO/STO-3G at `SHRINK 2 2`),
pure DFT has no exchange-convention seam, the ~0.5 Ha
GDF-route dense-core tail defect is not a gauge, and component
energies (`E_ne`, `E_nn`) place the jellium terms differently and only
totals compare. The stale "What CRYSTAL does that vibe-qc doesn't"
list was refreshed (production multi-k BIPOLE SCF and open-shell
multi-k are shipped). The exxdiv conversion identity
`E(none) − E(ewald) = ½·N_e·ξ_M(BvK supercell)` — previously recorded
nowhere in-repo — is now stated in the doc and **pinned by two new
tests** (`test_exxdiv_convention_identity_gamma` / `_multik` in
`tests/test_bipole_fock_ewald_exchange.py`), which verify the two SCF
conventions share a minimizer and differ by exactly the constant.
`keyword_index.md` now lists `bipole_cutoff_bohr`,
`use_exchange_ewald_split`, `exchange_exxdiv`, and `ewald_precision`.

### Added: a contact form on the website, forwarding to mpei@vibe-qc.com (2026-08-05)

`https://vibe-qc.com/contact/` — name, email, topic, message — reachable
from the nav and the footer. Until now the only route to the maintainer
was a `mailto:` link on the get-started page.

The marketing site is a static Astro build with no runtime, so the form
needs exactly one piece of server-side code: `website/public/contact.php`.
Astro copies `public/` verbatim into `dist/`, which is what the existing
`website-deploy` rsync ships, so this adds no build step, no CI change and
no new dependency. Deliberately **not** a third-party form service — a
visitor's message never leaves the vibe-qc host, which is the same reason
`sponsors.mjs` refuses external logo URLs.

The happy path does not need JavaScript: the form is a plain POST and the
handler answers with a 303 redirect to a real pre-rendered page
(`/contact/sent/`), so a reload cannot resend. JS only stamps the
fill-time field and renders the error banner from `?error=<code>`; the
plain `mailto:` route stays visible on the page regardless, so a failing
handler never leaves a visitor without a way to make contact.

Spam handling is modest by design — honeypot, a fill-time heuristic that
applies only when JS ran, a per-IP limit of 5 *sent* messages per hour, and
length caps. The limit counts sends rather than attempts: counting attempts
locked a visitor out for an hour for mistyping their address, and what
needs limiting is outbound mail volume. Every field reaching a mail header
is stripped of CR/LF and display names are RFC 5322-quoted, so neither a
`Bcc:` injection nor an ordinary name like `Smith, John` can restructure
the headers. `From` stays on the sending domain for SPF/DKIM alignment and
the visitor goes in `Reply-To`.

Verified with `tests/contact.verify.mjs` (12 checks, including that the
topic allowlist is identical in the page and the handler, so drift fails
closed) and by exercising the handler against a PHP built-in server with a
captured sendmail: every validation branch, the honeypot, the rate-limit
boundary, and the composed headers for injection, comma and non-ASCII
names.

**Not yet verified on the live host:** that PHP is enabled for the
document root and that `mail()` can hand off to the MTA. Both are host
facts this repo cannot test. If PHP is not enabled, Apache serves the
handler as text and submissions fail silently — check before linking the
page anywhere else. The one-time checklist is in `website/README.md`
§ Contact form.

### Fixed: COSX exchange used the wrong Cartesian normalization too (2026-08-05)

Third and last surface in the Cartesian-convention arc. COSX builds K from
two halves that must share an AO basis: grid-collocated AO values from
`evaluate_ao`, and analytic Obara-Saika integrals from `cosx_kernel.cpp`.
Both multiplied Cartesian components by
`sqrt((2l-1)!!/((2lx-1)!!(2ly-1)!!(2lz-1)!!))`, which libint does not do.

Measured against exact four-index ERI exchange on H2 with one Cartesian d
shell, relative error in K:

* both halves scaled (before this arc started): **4.5e-02**
* only the analytic half scaled (after the `evaluate_ao` fix): **2.4e-01**
* neither scaled (now): **5.2e-09**

The spherical control sits at 4.1e-08 throughout and never moved, in all
three states. That is why this survived the ordinary test surface: every
named basis forces `set_pure(true)`, so no *named-basis* calculation could
reach it. It was reachable in production regardless —
`vibeqc.basis_toolkit.to_libint_basis()` (shipped since v0.15.0) builds
Cartesian shells from imported bases, and a COSX run on such a basis took
this error in full. See the reclassification entry above.

Worth stating plainly: the Cartesian path was already wrong before this
arc, not broken by it. Aligning `evaluate_ao` first made the disagreement
larger for one commit, because it removed the factor from one half while
the kernel still applied it to the other.

`tests/test_cosx_cartesian_parity.py` pins both halves against exact ERI,
for both shell kinds, with a second test asserting the Cartesian error stays
the same order as the spherical one so a partial regression cannot hide
under a loose bound. vibe-view's `test_wavefunction_libint_parity` gains
Cartesian coverage as well: it asserted `pure` only, which is precisely why
the renderer's version of this bug went unnoticed.

### Added: the extended residual domain for local DLPNO-CCSD (2026-08-04)

`residual_domain="extended"` contracts each pair's residual in the union of
the coupled pairs' PNO spaces, then projects into the pair's own space. This
is the extended domain of Riplinger and Neese, *J. Chem. Phys.* **138**,
034106 (2013), Sec. II B 1, the reduced-scaling counterpart of the O(N⁶)
`"full"` setting added earlier today.

Measured on H2O/def2-SVP: deviation from the pilot oracle, and the mean
dimension each pair's residual is contracted in, out of 19 virtuals:

| `tcut_pno` | pair dim | ext dim | pair dev | **ext dev** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1e-5 | 6.33 | 18.40 | −10060.8 µHa | **−128.39** |
| 1e-6 | 10.93 | 18.60 | −2365.9 | **−23.68** |
| 1e-7 | 13.73 | 18.80 | −226.6 | **−4.33** |

A 52-fold improvement at the shipped `1e-7` default, leaving 4.3 µHa
(0.003 kcal/mol) — inside chemical accuracy, so this is a viable production
setting even though it is not exact.

**A correction to what I claimed when starting this.** I argued the extended
domain would be *exact*, reasoning that every amplitude entering a pair's
residual lives in some pair of its coupling list and is therefore lossless in
the union. The measurement refutes that: the argument accounts for the
amplitudes but not the intermediates, and the ladder and ring contractions
generate directions outside the span of their inputs. The paper calls the
