extended domain a *buffer* rather than an exactness device, and that wording
should have been read literally. The bug entry carries the same correction.

`LocalCCSDResult.avg_residual_domain` now reports the mean contraction
dimension, so the accuracy/cost trade is visible rather than implicit.

The default stays `"pair"`, so no shipped number moves. Whether `"extended"`
should become the default is a maintainer call: it fixes a real defect but
costs roughly 2.7× the residual work at `1e-7` on this molecule, and the
saving relative to `"full"` only appears once the occupied coupling list is
smaller than the whole occupied set.

### Fixed: molecular UHF could converge onto excited SCF solutions with no diagnostic -- internal stability analysis is now default-on (2026-08-05)

**THIS CHANGES NUMBERS on open-shell UHF rows.** E(UHF) <= E(ROHF) is a
variational identity (the ROHF determinant lies inside the UHF space),
and vibe-qc violated it while reporting clean convergence: O2 charge 0
multiplicity 5 / cc-pVDZ converged to -149.1039798772 Ha, **+59.15 mHa
ABOVE** the ROHF energy -149.1631321384 Ha; ferrocene m=3 / def2-SVP was
+150.92 mHa above (registry UHF-ABOVE-ROHF-VARIATIONAL-INVERSION). The
converged UHF orbitals were aufbau-stable in their own Fock, but the
internal orbital-rotation Hessian had a -0.0869 eigenvalue: a saddle
point -- an excited SCF solution -- that DIIS had locked in from the
spin-symmetric guess.

The molecular UHF driver (`cpp/src/uhf.cpp`) now runs a post-convergence
internal (real UHF -> UHF) stability analysis -- matrix-free Davidson on
the existing coupled orbital-rotation Hessian action, one J + two K
builds per matvec (`uhf_internal_stability_lowest`, cpp/src/newton.cpp;
criterion per Lehtola, Molecules 25, 1218 (2020) Sec. 10 / Seeger &
Pople, J. Chem. Phys. 66, 3045 (1977)) -- and, on detection, escapes by
a line-searched rotation along the unstable mode followed by SCF
reconvergence, with the rotated occupied orbitals held as a
fixed-reference maximum-overlap anchor for the first cycles of the
retry (a fixed small-step rotation, and on larger systems even a
line-searched density-only restart, is measurably recaptured by the
original basin), up to `stability_max_retries` times. New `UHFOptions`:
`stability_check` (default **True**), `stability_tol` (1e-4),
`stability_max_retries` (3), `stability_davidson_max_iter` (60). New
`UHFResult` fields: `stability_checked`, `stability_analysis_converged`,
`stability_eigenvalue`, `n_stability_restarts`, `internal_instability`.
The `.out` prints the verdict next to the convergence line; an
unresolved instability warns loudly (role `scf_internal_instability`)
that the energy is an excited SCF solution. Guard rails: +U jobs skip
the check (the +U term is not in the Hessian action); `atomic_spins` /
`spinlock_mode` state-targeting runs are checked but never rotated away
from the requested state. Citations: Seeger-Pople 1977 + Lehtola 2020
(+ Davidson 1975) fire via `routes.methods.scf_stability` whenever the
check runs.

Affected routes and magnitudes: any molecular UHF single point or
UHF-referenced post-SCF (UMP2 / UCCSD / DLPNO open-shell / TDA) where
the legacy driver landed on a saddle now converges lower. Measured: O2
m=5/cc-pVDZ -149.1039798772 -> **-149.1799299198 Ha** (now 16.80 mHa
below ROHF, S^2 6.0463 -> 6.0222); O2 triplet/STO-3G drops 1.51 mHa to
a symmetry-broken minimum (-147.6340485051 -> -147.6355561091). Rows
whose only defect was the ordering inversion are superseded; stable
solutions (e.g. OH doublet) are byte-identical. Opt out with
`stability_check=False` (legacy single-SCF behaviour, bit-for-bit). The
UHF analytic-Hessian PySCF-parity tests pin the legacy solution
explicitly, since the parity claim is solution-matched and the UCPHF
system is near-singular at the new symmetry-broken minimum -- UCPHF
robustness at such minima, plus UKS/ROHF stability wiring, is
registered follow-up scope. The default-on check also exposed and fixed
a latent crash: the coupled UHF Hessian action segfaulted whenever one
spin channel had no occupied x virtual rotation block (e.g. N atom
m=4/STO-3G with every alpha orbital occupied). Guide:
`docs/user_guide/scf_convergence.md` (Internal stability analysis).
Regression: `tests/test_uhf_stability.py`.

### Fixed: open-shell DLPNO routes rejected every fully spin-polarised system (2026-08-04)

`run_dlpno_ump2`, `run_dlpno_uccsd_pilot` and `run_local_dlpno_uccsd` all
guarded the frozen-core count with `if nf < 0 or nf >= nbeta`. The intent is
"you cannot freeze more orbitals than the minority spin has", but `>=` also
rejects the legitimate `nbeta = 0` boundary, where the **default**
`n_frozen=0` is perfectly valid. A plain hydrogen atom was refused with

    ValueError: n_frozen=0 out of range for n_beta=0

naming a parameter the caller never set. The bound is now `nf > nbeta`:
freezing every beta electron is legal, freezing more than exist is not.

This is not only the one-electron case. *Any* fully spin-polarised system has
`nbeta = 0`, including high-spin systems with genuine same-spin correlation
that the method should compute rather than refuse.

Both regimes are verified against independent oracles and pinned:

* **Zero-pair limit.** H atom and He⁺ now return `e_corr = 0.0` exactly from
  all three routes, the only correct answer when no pairs exist.
* **Genuine high-spin correlation.** Linear H3 quartet (3 electrons, all
  alpha, three αα pairs), def2-SVP at full domains: canonical UCCSD gives
  `-0.0015748818634586925`; the DLPNO-UCCSD pilot and the local engine both
  give `-0.001574881869`, agreeing to `-0.000` µHa.

One near-miss is recorded in the bug entry because it would mislead the next
person: triplet He was the first high-spin probe and returned `0.0`, which
looks like the fix silently zeroing real correlation. It is not — for
He/def2-SVP the occupieds are both `s` and the virtuals are a single `p`
shell, so every antisymmetrised αα integral vanishes by symmetry, and
canonical UCCSD agrees at exactly `0.0`. That system cannot discriminate;
H3 quartet is the one that tests the path.

### Fixed: the local DLPNO-CCSD subspace-oracle deviation is understood, with an exact path (2026-08-04)

Yesterday's bug entry recorded that `run_local_dlpno_ccsd` deviates from its
own subspace oracle whenever `tcut_pno > 0`, and named a suspect. The
mechanism is now confirmed and there is a setting that removes it.

The cause is *where the projection happens*. The default path projects each
coupled pair's amplitude into pair `ij`'s PNO space and contracts there
(`Sm @ Tof(m,n) @ Sm.T`), which discards the parts of those amplitudes lying
outside `ij`'s space that would still have fed back into it through the
integrals. The pilot instead expands to the full virtual space, contracts, and
projects the residual back, which is the exact stationarity condition of the
subspace-constrained ansatz.

Riplinger and Neese, *J. Chem. Phys.* **138**, 034106 (2013), Sec. II B 1 call
this out explicitly: there is a second, *extended* domain per pair, and it is
"necessary in order to create a sufficiently large buffer for the accurate
calculation of the pair-pair interaction terms". vibe-qc had no such buffer.

`LocalCCSDOptions.residual_domain="full"` contracts in the full virtual space
and projects afterwards. On H2O/def2-SVP, deviation from the pilot in µHa:

| `tcut_pno` | `"pair"` (default) | `"full"` |
|---|---|---|
| full | +0.0 | −0.0 |
| 1e-5 | −10060.8 | **+1.5** |
| 1e-6 | −2365.9 | **−0.1** |
| 1e-7 | −226.6 | **+0.0** |

A ~7000-fold reduction, which confirms the mechanism rather than merely
improving a number.

`"pair"` remains the default and is bit-for-bit unchanged: `"full"` is
O(N⁶), so it is the correctness setting, not a production one. The
production fix is the paper's *extended* domain, the union of the coupled
pairs' spaces rather than the whole virtual space, which stays open. The bug
entry keeps its strict-xfail on the default path.

Next up on the 0.15 line: BIPOLE-route validation against CRYSTAL23
references (the priority periodic path) and the Gamma single-k branch
repair.

## [v0.15.114] - 2026-08-05 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Fixed: Hirshfeld charges dominated large-molecule wall time (2026-08-05)

`hirshfeld_charges` contracted the density against the AO values as a full
`(n_points, n_bf) x (n_bf, n_bf)` product on every grid block. That is the
dominant cost of the `.population` sidecar, and on an extended molecule it
dominates the whole job: C20H42 / def2-TZVP (62 atoms, 872 basis functions,
2,845,800 grid points) spent 29m25s of an 83m run inside `write_population` —
35.3% of total wall, on a Hartree-Fock job that uses no integration grid
anywhere else.

A density matrix is symmetric, so `P = sum_k n_k v_k v_k^T` and the grid
density is a single sum over natural orbitals,
`rho(r) = sum_k n_k (chi(r).v_k)^2`, rather than a double sum over AOs.
Diagonalising once before the sweep shrinks the per-block product to
`(n_points, n_bf) x (n_bf, rank)`. A converged SCF density has `rank = n_occ`,
which does not grow with the basis, so the saving widens as the basis does:
490/81 = 6x fewer flops for C20H42 at def2-SVP, 872/81 = 10.8x at def2-TZVP.

Measured on the def2-TZVP case with old and new interleaved in one process
(medians of 3, because cross-process timings on the dev box vary by ~2x): the
grid sweep goes 140.53s -> 55.21s (2.55x), and the whole `hirshfeld_charges`
call 168.60s -> 83.32s (2.02x) — the remainder is `build_grid` at 28.03s,
which this does not touch.

The rewrite is exact rather than an approximation: only eigenvalues at the
diagonalisation round-off floor are dropped, so a full-rank density keeps every
mode and costs what it did before, and no new tolerance knob is introduced.
Charges agree with the previous implementation to 5.3e-15 with the grid norms
unchanged — well inside the 1e-12 block-size-independence guard in
`tests/test_hirshfeld_charges.py`.

### Fixed: ROHF stalled in fixed-depth DIIS and could not reach the Chupin restart policies (BUG 118, 2026-08-05)

BUG 118 reported FeCl₃ / ROHF / def2-TZVP / multiplicity 6 failing to
converge in 300 iterations, and described the final state as oscillating
with `dE ~ 1e-3` and `|g| ~ 1e-2`. The run's own `.out` and crash dump say
otherwise: at iteration 300 it sat at `dE = -1.9e-11` and
`|g| = 4.157e-06`, energy-converged to 1e-11 Ha and a factor of four short
of `conv_tol_grad = 1e-6`, having crawled there from `|g| = 2.6e-05` at
iteration 200. The failure is a stalled tail, not an oscillation, and the
convergence aids the report proposed all make a stalled tail slower.

The tail is fixed-depth DIIS going near-linearly-dependent: with the
subspace full of near-identical iterates off a long plateau, the Pulay
system is ill-conditioned and extrapolation stops paying. Restarting that
same run from its own crash-dump density closed it in 11 iterations, which
localises the stall to the history rather than the state.

`vibeqc::DIIS` has implemented the remedy since the Chupin et al. 2021
adaptive-depth work landed (`DIISDepthPolicy::RESTART` / `ADAPTIVE`,
selected by `SCFAccelerator::R_CDIIS` / `AD_CDIIS`), and every C++ driver
reaches it through `make_diis`. The Roothaan ROHF/ROKS loop did not: it
constructed `DIIS(subspace_size)` at the default FIXED policy and its
`_resolve_scf_accelerator` rejected both spellings outright. `ROHFOptions`
now carries `diis_restart_tau` / `diis_adaptive_delta` with the same names
and defaults as `RHFOptions`, and `_resolve_diis_depth_policy` mirrors
`make_diis`.

Iteration counts on this system are chaotic, so the effect had to be
measured over repeats rather than sampled. Two independent sets of 8
repeats of the identical FeCl₃ / def2-SVP input at a 300-iteration cap,
run on v0.15.113 and v0.15.114 (identical DIIS, level-shift and
direct-JK paths):

| configuration | converged | median iters (set 1 / set 2) | spread |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ediis_diis` (shipped) | 8/16 | 114 / 217 | 63-245 |
| `r_cdiis` | 14/16 | 124 / 89 | 57-225 |
| `level_shift=0.6` held + `ediis_diis` | 16/16 | 55.5 / 55.5 | 50-59 |
| `level_shift=0.6` held + `r_cdiis` | 16/16 | 53 / 55 | 48-59 |

Both medians are quoted because that is the honest resolution: on the
unshifted rows they move by a factor of two between sets, so eight
samples do not pin an iteration count. `r_cdiis` buys **reliability, not
speed**: 14/16 inside the cap against 8/16, with an iteration count not
distinguishable from the default's at this sample size. What collapses both the count and the run-to-run scatter is a
**held level shift**, and once the shift is held the accelerator choice
is noise (53 versus 55.5). The user-guide recommendation is therefore the
held shift, with `r_cdiis` as insurance rather than as the remedy.
`ad_cdiis` is not a substitute: it shrinks the depth near convergence
rather than discarding a degenerate history, and measures like the
fixed-depth default at both bases.

The held shift is only usable *because* of the two level-shift fixes
below. Holding it requires `level_shift_warmup_cycles = 0`, which did not
exist on `ROHFOptions`, and trusting the resulting orbital energies
requires the canonicalisation fix.

**Open, escalated, not fixed here: the def2-TZVP state itself is wrong.**
Cross-checking against ORCA 6.1.1 (`! ROHF def2-TZVP TightSCF NORI
NORIJCOSX`, identical geometry and identical ansatz — 36 closed orbitals
/ 72 electrons plus 5 singly occupied, integer occupations on both sides)
shows the default SAD + DIIS path converging **0.520 Ha (1366 kJ/mol)
above** the correct high-spin d⁵ solution. The reachable tell is symmetry:
the default state gives planar FeCl₃'s three equivalent Cl three different
Mulliken charges (+0.204, −0.239, −0.239) and Mayer bond orders 0.726 /
0.726 / 0.189, one Fe−Cl bond nearly gone; the correct state has three
identical Cl (−0.454) and the spin on Fe (population 4.74).

vibe-qc's own ROHF reproduces ORCA to **7.1e-08 Ha** (−2641.1238568 vs
−2641.1238569) in 48 iterations once steered into the right basin with
`level_shift=0.6` held plus `r_cdiis`, so the implementation is correct
and the **initial guess** is what fails. ORCA reaches it because its
default `PModel` model-potential guess starts there; the Roothaan driver
cannot build that class of guess at all (`SAP` / `PATOM` / `HUECKEL` /
`MINAO` are rejected by `_supported_initial_guesses`), which is why a
held level shift is the only in-tree lever. Adding a model-potential
guess to the Roothaan driver is a maintainer call, not a bug-fix.

The same system at def2-SVP is unaffected: −2640.4655173 against ORCA's
−2640.4655183, agreeing to 1 µHa with three equivalent Cl. A cheap-basis
smoke test therefore does not catch this. Documented under
`scf_convergence.md` § "Convergence is not correctness" with the symmetry
and spin-population checks that do, and guarded by
`test_bug118_tzvp_reaches_the_orca_verified_state_under_a_held_shift`.

Chasing this also surfaced three unrelated defects in the same driver:

* **The Saunders-Hillier shift was applied to the canonicalising
  diagonalisation**, so every
  converged run with `level_shift > 0` reported virtual orbital energies —
  and therefore the HOMO-LUMO gap, `.molden`, Koopmans estimates and the
  semicanonical ROHF-MP2 / ROHF-CCSD orbital energies — too high by exactly
  the shift. CH₃ / STO-3G: gap 0.6707 Ha reported as 0.9707 Ha at
  `level_shift = 0.3`. Silent by construction: the Saunders-Hillier operator
  is inert on the occupied block, so the total energy is exactly right and
  no energy assertion could see it. The canonicalising solve is now always
  unshifted, and an unconverged run is re-solved unshifted too so its
  diagnostic orbital table describes the Fock actually reached.
* **ROHF/ROKS ignored `level_shift_warmup_cycles` and
  `level_shift_schedule`** — the `level_shift_at_iter` policy that
  `cpp/include/vibeqc/level_shift.hpp` declares the single source of truth,
  and that `docs/user_guide/scf_convergence.md` already claimed was on every
  driver. It held `options.level_shift` at every iteration with no release.
  Both fields are now on `ROHFOptions` and resolved through the shared
  helper, defaulting to `-1` (auto) as everywhere else. **Behaviour change**:
  an existing ROHF/ROKS job that sets `level_shift` now releases it after up
  to five startup cycles; set `level_shift_warmup_cycles = 0` for the
  previous persistent shift.
* **`dynamic_damping` / `_min` / `_max` were declared and documented on
  `ROHFOptions` but read nowhere.** Setting them did nothing. The Roothaan
  loop now runs the Zerner-Hehenberger update (Chem. Phys. Lett. 62, 550
  (1979)) mirroring `cpp/include/vibeqc/dynamic_damping.hpp`, including
  keeping the live α in a local so `damping = 0.0` + `dynamic_damping = True`
  still mixes, as the C++ UHF driver does.

Documented in `docs/user_guide/rohf.md` § Convergence and
`docs/user_guide/scf_convergence.md` § "A stalled tail is usually the DIIS
history, not the state", which also records how to tell the two failure
shapes apart in a trace, and three things that look like they help on this
system but do not: a damping-first schedule (`damping = 0.5`,
`diis_start_iter = 11`) converges tidily onto a different solution 0.10 Ha
higher; `initial_guess='GWH'` is unavailable to the Roothaan driver (it
seeds from densities only, and raises naming the supported set rather than
downgrading); and a persistent level shift steers the def2-TZVP SCF into a
different basin than the unshifted run reaches.

The ROHF/ROKS accelerator coverage row and its caveats (no second-order
finalizer; `damping` inert under the default `diis_start_iter = 1`) are
now in the `scf_convergence.md` backend table rather than absent from it.

Guarded by `tests/test_rohf_convergence_controls.py`.

### Changed: BIPOLE SR ket-image pad honest, QQR screening cheap — wall-clock only, no numerical change (2026-08-05)

Registry `BIPOLE-SR-PAD-OVERCONSERVATIVE`. Affected route: the
corrected-gauge BIPOLE erfc SR fused J/K build (all four direct drivers
and `run_periodic_job(jk_method="bipole")`); no other route touched.

Two stacked cost constants, measured by the 2026-08-05 BIPOLE
investigation, are removed:

* **The default `sr_image_precision` pad was ~2x over-radius.**
  `bipole_sr_image_extent` conflated a primitive exponent with a pair
  (product-Gaussian) exponent — a pair exponent is the *sum* of its two
  primitives, so the slowest smeared-kernel decay is
  `1/m_w = 1/gamma_min + 1/omega^2`, not `2/gamma_min + 1/omega^2` —
  and inverted the loose tail bound `erfc(x) <= exp(-x^2)` instead of
  the exact `erfc^-1(eps)` (3.459 vs 3.717 at the production 1e-6).
  Both corrections are theorem-level (derivation inline at the helper);
  the derived radius still covers every measured probe-ladder
  bit-stability radius with margin (LiH 29.6 vs 26 bohr, LiF 29.4 vs
  26, MgO 23.7 vs 20, NaCl 27.2 vs 22-26 absolute at cutoff 6). Padded
  cell counts at production cutoff 15 drop LiH 3589 -> 2093, LiF 3805
  -> 2171, MgO 1601 -> 1157, NaCl 935 -> 675; the traversal scales with
  n_pad^2.
* **The QQR screening bound paid one `std::erfc` (and redundant hash
  probes) per candidate.** The fused build now evaluates the bound in
  two stages — a log-domain sufficient-skip test from once-per-build ln
  tables (`x^2 > ln q - ln thr`, valid because `exp(-x^2) >= erfc(x)`),
  with the original erfc expression evaluated bit-for-bit only when
  stage 1 cannot decide — replaces the per-triple `unordered_map` cell
  lookups with dense bounding-box tables, and drops a loop-invariant
  per-quartet `p_block_idx` recomputation. The screening decision set is
  unchanged by construction, so the emitted J/K matrices are
  bit-identical at a fixed traversal ball.

Acceptance measured so far (evidence in the fixer run directory, per
the claims registry): on the pre-fix build at production cutoff 15
with an off-home S-lattice density, shrinking the ball from the old to
the new default radius moves J/K elements by at most 1.0e-13 and
home-contraction energies by <= 6.8e-14 Ha on all four rocksalt
probes — inside the <= 1e-12 Ha acceptance band. The screening change
is decision-preserving by construction (proof inline). CPU deltas are
in the registry entry. `sr_image_precision=None` and explicit
`sr_image_extent_bohr` behave exactly as before.

### Fixed: regenerating the suite manifest silently retiered other chats' tests (2026-08-05)

`scripts/test_gate/update_suite_manifest.py` rebuilds all 687 rows of
`suite_manifest.json` from `lane_manifest.json`, carrying forward only
measurements. Any classification it could not derive was therefore discarded on
the next run — and every chat that adds a test file must run it, because
`tests/conftest.py` fails collection on an unclassified file.

Four rows were being overwritten. `tests/test_periodic_molden_gamma_export.py`
dropped from blocking T1 to "demote T2"; since the release cut selects its
blocking set with `--tier T1` off this manifest rather than by lane, that
quietly removed a file from the release gate. `tests/test_iao_ibo.py` and
`tests/test_ao_convention_invariants.py` lost their owners
(`analysis/localization`, `basis/integrals`) and
`tests/test_periodic_gpw_rset_consistency.py` its reproducer note, all replaced
by generated boilerplate. Each loss was one hunk in a ~700-row JSON diff.

The updater now carries a `CURATED` table of hand-chosen fields, laid over the
derived classification so unpinned fields still track the lanes, and it rejects
an entry naming a file that no longer exists.
`tests/test_test_gate_lanes.py` pins a fresh generator run against the
checked-in file, so an unrecorded hand-edit now fails a test.

`tests/test_ao_convention_invariants.py` also carried a hand-written
`memory_tier` of `light` against a null `measured_peak_rss_mb`. That field is
*defined* as a function of the measured peak, so an asserted value could not
survive regeneration. It is now backed by an isolated run on a current native
build (150.2 MB, 2.9 s), folded in with `--measurements`, and `light` is
derived rather than claimed.

Also repairs the drift already on `main`: `test_file_count` read 685 against 686
rows, which had been failing
`test_tier_selection_is_exhaustive_and_disjoint` since `3ff03199a`.

### Fixed: embedded surface localiser could not run at all (2026-08-05)

Both branches of `vibeqc.periodic_embedding.embedded_localise` were dead
code. Neither `foster_boys_localise` nor `pipek_mezey_localise` returns a
`(C_loc, U)` pair -- both return the localised coefficients alone -- yet
both call sites unpacked two values. That raises `ValueError: too many
values to unpack` for every region-I size except `n_i == 2`, where a
`(2, n_occ)` array unpacks into its two *rows*, silently yielding a 1-D
`C_loc` and a nonsense `U`.

The `boys` branch was doubly broken: it passed the region-I *overlap*
matrix where `foster_boys_localise` expects the Cartesian dipole integrals
`(n_i, n_i, 3)`, so it could not have run even in the `n_i == 2` case.
`method="boys"` has therefore never produced a result on this path.

Both call sites now capture the single return value, and the mixing matrix
is recovered as `U = C_nat^T S C_loc` -- exact, because `C_nat` is
S-orthonormal by construction -- matching
`vibeqc.periodic_localise.localise_periodic_gamma`. Boys builds its dipole
integrals through the new `_region_dipoles` helper: `compute_dipole` over
the full basis, sliced to the region-I AOs. That is the same g=0 home-cell
block, about the same `(0, 0, 0)` origin, that the Γ-point localiser
obtains from `compute_multipole_moments_lattice` with a 1-bohr cutoff; the
two are pinned together by a test.

`centroids` for `method="boys"` are now the true position expectation
values `<i|r|i>` the field was always documented to hold, rather than a
copy of the Mulliken `centers`. `spreads` remains zero and is now
documented as such: `<r^2>` needs region-I quadrupole integrals, whose only
route (`compute_multipole_moments_lattice`) needs a `PeriodicSystem` this
entry point is not given. The module docstring also records the PBC
validity caveat that already applied to the Γ-point Boys criterion --
the home-cell position operator is faithful only for orbitals that do not
wrap the cell boundary.

The single pre-existing test used a two-AO region and asserted
`C_loc.ndim >= 1`, so it passed on the row-unpacked garbage.
`tests/test_periodic_embedding_localise.py` now covers `n_i = 3` as well,
and pins 2-D shapes, orthogonality of `U`, invariance of the localised span
under `D S`, and that Boys maximises the true Boys objective. 15 of its 18
tests fail against the previous code.

### Fixed: Γ-compcell UKS guard test asserted a tag the bypass cannot produce (2026-08-05)

`test_pbc_gdf_uks_lih_ionic_sanity_guard_raises` ran its bypass branch with
`check_energy_sanity=False` and then required
`backend.endswith("+SANITY_FAILED")`. That tag is applied inside
`_check_energy_sanity`, which every driver wraps in `if check_energy_sanity:` —
the flag gates the tag and the raise together, so the assertion was
unsatisfiable and the test failed on the returned `pbc-gdf-compcell-uks`. Only
the `@pytest.mark.slow` marker kept it out of the fast gate lanes.

Test-only fix: the flag keeps its documented meaning (bypass = the guard does
not run at all), and the bypass branch now pins that meaning positively — no
raise, the non-physical fixed point handed back (|E| > 100 Ha, this cell's
runaway bound), backend left untagged. The machine-dependent `converged`
assertion is dropped, matching the `_assert_guard_rejects_nonphysical` helper
that exists for exactly that reason. The UHF twin has no bypass branch and
needed no change.

## [v0.15.113] — 2026-08-05 — *Neese's Cheetah*

### Fixed: `basis.ao` metadata invented a magnetic quantum number for Cartesian shells (2026-08-05)

`qvf_ao_data` derived every AO's `m` as *in-shell index* − `l`. That is the
spherical ordering QVF spec Appendix A.2 mandates, and it is undefined for a
Cartesian shell (`ShellInfo.pure == False`), which has `(l+1)(l+2)/2`
components rather than `2l+1`: the subtraction ran past `+l`, so a Cartesian
d shell was labelled `m = -2 … +3` across its six components, and no value in
that range denotes a spherical harmonic at all.

A Cartesian component is now named by a new **optional** `ao_metadata` member
`cartesian_powers` (`[lx, ly, lz]`, libint's lexicographic in-shell order),
present if and only if the shell is Cartesian. `angular_momentum` keeps its
shape and its required-ness — element 0 (`l`) is meaningful either way — so
the change is additive and carries **no `qvf_version` bump**, per
`qvf-writer/GOVERNANCE.md` (decision entry dated 2026-08-05) and the new spec
Appendix A.3. A separate key rather than a widened `[l, lx, ly, lz]` array
was chosen so that the Cartesian case is *detectable*: an un-updated consumer
reading element 1 of a 4-element array would still get a plausible-looking
`m`.

Only the metadata label was ever wrong. The volumetric payload comes from
`evaluate_ao_on_grid` and the AO index ranges from `vibeqc.cube._ao_ranges`,
both of which already handled Cartesian shells. Note this differs from the
`wavefunction.gto` path, which *rejects* Cartesian shells — that path writes
MO coefficients whose normalization convention Cartesian shells break, which
does not apply to evaluated grid data.

Reachable only via the explicit-`ShellInfo` `BasisSet` constructor; the
named-basis route forces `set_pure(true)`, so no shipped basis set could
trigger it. *[Correction 2026-08-06:
`vibeqc.basis_toolkit.to_libint_basis()` also reaches that constructor,
with Cartesian shells built from imported bases (shipped since v0.15.0),
so the trigger surface was not empty — see the reclassification entry
under \[Unreleased\].]*

### Fixed: every AO of a `basis.ao` shell shared one section id (2026-08-05)

Found while round-tripping the fix above. `_ao_label` / `_ao_section_id` took
an `m` argument and never used it, so all `2l+1` (or `(l+1)(l+2)/2`)
components of a shell produced the identical section id *and* the identical
path inside the archive. `write_qvf` rejected its own output with "duplicate
section id" for **any** shell with `l > 0`, Cartesian or spherical, whenever
contracted AOs were exported — so `basis.ao` export only ever worked for s
shells.

Ids now carry a component tag: `m{m}` for spherical (`ao_O_p_m-1_s0_…`), the
monomial for Cartesian (`ao_O_d_xy_s0_…`). An `s` shell has one component and
keeps its previous id byte-for-byte, so every id that was already unique is
unchanged.

### Found: local DLPNO-CCSD deviates from its own subspace oracle under truncation (2026-08-03)

Yesterday's complete-PNO-extrapolation work could not be routed because
`run_local_dlpno_ccsd` does not converge monotonically in `TCutPNO`. That was
recorded as an open question. It now has an answer, and the answer is a bug.

`run_dlpno_ccsd_pilot` targets the *same* DLPNO ansatz, per-pair PNO spaces,
but evaluates the exact residual in the full space and projects back, which is
the stationarity condition of subspace-constrained CCSD; its own docstring
says the reduced-scaling engine is what it exists to validate. So it is the
oracle under truncation, not only at full domain. Deviation `local - pilot`
at the same `tcut_pno`, def2-SVP, in µHa:

| `tcut_pno` | N2 | H2O |
|---|---|---|
| full | +0.0 | +0.0 |
| 1e-5 | −15505.5 | −10060.8 |
| 1e-6 | −2975.2 | −2365.9 |
| 1e-7 (default) | −1986.0 | −226.6 |
| 1e-8 | −78.4 | −76.7 |

`1e-7` is the shipped `LocalCCSDOptions.tcut_pno`, so N2 sits ~1.2 kcal/mol
from its own oracle at default settings, and `1e-5` is ~10 kcal/mol. The sign
never changes: the local engine over-correlates.

Three controls place the fault in the local engine rather than the method:
DLPNO-MP2 **in the same PNO spaces** converges monotonically and
single-signed (`+8926, +4492, +1810, +852, +469, +173` µHa for `X = 4..9`), so
the spaces are sound and, being eigenvectors of a threshold-independent
density, are nested; the **pilot in the same ansatz** also converges
monotonically (`+10849, +3173, +1022, +614` µHa), matching the published
behaviour of the reference implementation; only the **local engine**
oscillates in sign (`−4657, +198, −964, +536` µHa).

Why no test caught it: every exactness ratchet for this engine compares
against the pilot **at full domain**, where the deviation is identically zero
by construction. The failure lives entirely in the truncated regime, which is
the regime the method exists for. The new
`TestTruncatedSubspaceOracle` pins both sides: the full-domain agreement that
does hold, and a `xfail(strict=True)` for the truncated agreement that does
not, so it fails loudly the day the engine is fixed.

User-visible consequence: tightening `tcut_pno` does not monotonically improve
the answer (N2 `1e-6 → 1e-7` moves the error from `+198` to `−964` µHa), so
the threshold is not a reliable accuracy knob, and no threshold-based
extrapolation can be applied until this is fixed.

### Fixed: the no-Python-threads output guard takes a reviewed allowlist (2026-08-05)

`f179f55f2` (2026-07-29) farmed the O(n_k²) corrected-exchange k loop over
a `ThreadPoolExecutor`, which left
`tests/test_output_channel.py::test_vibeqc_spawns_no_python_threads` red on
`main` for a week. The guard protects a real invariant — `vibeqc.output`'s
active channel lives in a `ContextVar`, which a worker thread does not
inherit, so a `write()` inside one is dropped silently — but it was a flat
"no threads anywhere" grep with no way to record a thread that provably
cannot emit. Its only outcomes were delete the thread or delete the guard.

The guard now takes a per-site allowlist keyed by (file, needle,
occurrence count), each entry carrying the reason the gap is harmless. A
new thread site, a *second* thread in an already-allowlisted file, and an
entry whose thread has been removed each still fail. The one entry is
justified by reading the chain: `k_space_terms_at_k` →
`bipole_fock_ewald.compute_K_long_range_at_k` → `_aopair_ft` /
`bipole_ext_el_pole` / the C++ core, none of which imports `vibeqc.output`
or `vibeqc.progress`, and the core emits nothing by invariant. No
behaviour change; the pool keeps a comment saying it must stay
output-free, and `channel.py`'s "Thread safety" docstring — which still
claimed vibe-qc spawns no Python threads — is corrected to match.
Whether `channel.write()` should grow the `threading.local` fallback, so
threads can emit at all, is filed for the IO chat in
`handovers/HANDOVER_OUTPUT_LOGGER.md`.

### Changed: the multi-k GDF cderi accumulator no longer scales its pair FT in NumPy (2026-08-05)

`_accumulate_chunk` used to apply the per-AO-pair calibration scale — and,
under a fit screen, a masked zeroing — to the batched pair FT with two
NumPy passes over the largest array in the whole cderi build. Both are now
applied by the pair-FT kernel as it stores its result, which costs
**nothing**: that store already writes every element, from inside the
OpenMP parallel region. `ao_pair_fourier_transform_bloch_multi` grew an
optional `pair_weights` argument; both RSGDF accumulators (the SCF builder
in `aux_basis` and its twin in `periodic_gdf_gradient`) pass it.

A/B on site_e at 16 dedicated cores — both arms in ONE process on ONE
build, flipping only which side does the scaling, LiH FCC / STO-3G /
(3,3,3) / 27 k-points, six reps per arm interleaved:

    arm         cderi build   pair-FT kernel   NumPy scaling
    unfused        39.841 s         35.256 s        0.671 s
    fused          39.248 s         35.254 s             0

The kernel does not get slower (0.002 s, noise), so the fusion really is
free; the build loses 0.593 s, **1.5%**, and the cderi build is 97% of a
multi-k GDF SCF. Every digest matches across every arm.

**The output is bit-identical, and that needed care.** NumPy's
`complex128 *= float64` promotes the real factor to complex and runs the
full complex product, so the obvious componentwise `(re*w, im*w)` is a
*different* function — the two disagree in the sign of zero. The kernel
reproduces NumPy's arithmetic exactly, and a weight of exactly 0.0 means
"masked pair" and stores a true `+0.0`, matching the assignment it
replaces rather than a multiply by zero. Six regressions in
`tests/test_rsgdf_shared_q_batch.py` pin this **bit-for-bit**, not to a
tolerance, including an end-to-end cderi comparison against the old
unfused shape with the fit screen off and on.

**This corrects the 2026-08-05 profile's attribution.** That profile
measured `_accumulate_chunk`'s own time at 4.013 s (1 thread) / 4.428 s
(16 threads) and read it as these NumPy passes. Measured directly, the
passes are **0.537 s / 0.671 s** — they do anti-scale, at 0.81x, exactly
the diagnosed shape, but they are ~15% of that own time, not the whole of
it. The rest is the per-k ZGEMM and its neighbours. This also explains why
the micro-optimisation reverted the same day (`22764ec57`) could never
have shown a win: it was reshuffling a sliver, and in the profiled
configuration (`fit_screen_threshold=0.0`) the masked-assignment half of
it never executed at all.

Two other candidates from that profile were checked and are **not** worth
taking: `.reshape(...).T` before the ZGEMM does not copy (traced peak
allocation across the matmul is the result size, 0.024 MB, against the
1.4 MB a transpose copy would need), and the `T_list[i_k] += (...)`
temporary is that same ~1.6% of the pair tensor.

### Added: intrinsic bond orbitals and IAO partial charges, `run_job(localize="ibo")` (2026-08-05)

Knizia's intrinsic atomic orbitals (IAOs) and intrinsic bond orbitals
(IBOs) — *J. Chem. Theory Comput.* **9**, 4834 (2013) — as an opt-in
post-SCF analysis on closed-shell molecular jobs. The localized occupied
set is written to the QVF as a second `wavefunction.gto` section
(`wf_localized`, `orbital_kind="localized"`), which vibe-view renders as a
Lewis-structure view: one row per bond, core or lone pair, labelled by the
atoms it sits on.

That QVF slot has existed and been unused since the writer gained it; this
is the first producer to fill it. New: `vibeqc.iao` (`analyse_ibo`,
`build_iaos`, `iao_charges`), `localise.ibo_localise`, and
`compute_overlap_two_basis` re-exported from the package root (it was
bound in C++ but reachable only through the private `_vibeqc_core`).

Validated against Knizia Table 1 — CH₄ carbon comes out −0.473 / −0.500 /
−0.501 at def2-SVP / def2-TZVPP / cc-pVTZ against published −0.49 / −0.52
/ −0.52, and HCN within 0.02 e — and against his Figure 5: benzene gives
exactly 6 one-centre cores, 12 two-centre σ bonds, and a multi-centre π
system. Methane gives one core plus four equivalent C–H bonds.

**The reference basis is Huzinaga MINI, not `ano-rcc-mb`.** This is the
one non-obvious choice. `ano-rcc-mb` is what the MINAO *initial guess*
uses and is the natural thing to reach for, but as an IAO reference it
shifts the CH₄ carbon charge to −0.389 — 20 % off, and out of agreement
with the paper. Both bases were already bundled and both already carried
citations. A regression test pins the difference so the two do not get
swapped back.

**The published Jacobi increments were not transcribed.** Knizia's
Appendix D prints the p=4 update as `B_ij += 4Q_ij(Q_ij³ − Q_ij³)`, which
is identically zero, and prints the p=2 A-increment with `(Q_ii − Q_ij²)`
where Pipek-Mezey requires `(Q_ii − Q_jj)²`; the subscripts are mangled
throughout that block. The increments were derived instead and are pinned
against a brute-force scan of the rotation functional: p=2 is the exact
maximiser, and p=4 — approximate by construction, since the paper neglects
high-order terms in φ — never decreases the objective and loses a median
1.7×10⁻⁵ of the achievable gain per rotation.

Refused rather than approximated: ECP jobs (an all-electron minimal
reference cannot partition a valence-only target basis — for Au that is 22
functions against 43), elements past Z=86, and Cartesian shells. Each
warns and omits the section rather than failing the job.

Opt-in for now; making it a default is an open decision, tracked in
[Archived `handovers/HANDOVER_IBO.md`](https://vibe-qc.com/docs/) along with the
periodic and natural-orbital milestones.

### Added: Γ-point Wannier centres in periodic QVF output (2026-08-06)

`run_periodic_job(..., qvf_wannier_centers=True)` previously raised unless
`jk_method="aiccm2026dev-b"`. It now also works on any Γ-sampled route, where
the occupied Bloch functions span the whole occupied space of the cell and
localizing them is a well-defined Wannier construction for it. The existing
`x_ccm.wannier_centers` section and vibe-view's existing overlay renderer
carry it; no new section kind, no viewer change.

A multi-k run still refuses, and now says why: localizing only its Γ orbitals
would sample one k point and label the result a Wannier function. The real
multi-k scheme (Zicovich-Wilson, doi:10.1063/1.1415745) is written up in
[Archived `handovers/HANDOVER_IBO.md`](https://vibe-qc.com/docs/) § Milestone 3 and is
not implemented.

**Descriptors only — deliberately no coefficients.** Periodic QVF does not
carry localized orbital coefficients and should not: home-cell coefficients
with no image sum are the home-cell truncation of the Γ crystalline orbital
and clip wherever an orbital straddles a cell face, and a Wannier function is
*defined* by its image sum. Centres and spreads have no such problem. The
emitted centre is the Mulliken-weighted `centers`, not `centroids`, for the
same reason: `centroids` is only faithful for orbitals that stay inside the
cell.

### Added: re-localize a loaded wavefunction from the viewer (2026-08-05)

`vibe-view/src/vibeview/relocalize.py` lets the viewer ask vibe-qc for a
localization criterion that is not already in the file. A QVF carries the
criteria the *producer* chose; this covers wanting a different one.

**vibe-view does not localize anything itself.** It shells out to vibe-qc
(`python -m vibeview.relocalize`), mirroring `live_opt.py`: subprocess, one
JSON request on stdin, JSON events per line on stdout, a `probe()`
availability gate, and full degradation to the sections already in the file
when vibe-qc is not importable. Reimplementing the localizers viewer-side
would have meant reimplementing the integrals too, and putting two copies of
a published method in one repository.

Two things the design gets out of the way rather than working around:

- The basis is rebuilt **by name** from `provenance.basis` in the manifest,
  never from the serialised QVF shells — so the `coefficients_pre_normalized`
  pitfall (shells are written with contraction coefficients divided by the
  primitive norm) simply never arises.
- The canonical occupied block travels in the request, so the worker
  localizes the orbitals actually on screen instead of re-converging its own
  SCF. That saves an SCF and avoids a subtler problem: on a degenerate system
  two SCF runs can produce different-but-equivalent orbitals, and the
  localized results then differ. Measured on benzene before the change: same
  occupied space to 3.4e-10 and an exact signed-permutation match, but a
  different ordering each run.

That fast path assumes the supplied coefficients share an AO ordering with
`BasisSet(mol, name)`. The worker verifies `C^T S C = I` rather than trusting
it, because the failure mode is otherwise plausible but wrong orbitals.

The UI is a criterion dropdown and a Localize button in the MO card. Where
the result *lives* was the one real design question, since everything in the
viewer is section-backed: it is answered by mirroring the existing geometry
edit overlay. `QVFReader.set_wavefunction_overlay` registers the computed
wavefunction plus a synthetic section, and `read_wavefunction_gto`
short-circuits on it — so the renderer, the MO picker and the isosurface
path all work unchanged, with no renderer surgery. Overlays live on the
reader, so a file switch or reload discards them and the file always wins.

Computed sections are `wf_relocalized_*`, distinct from the producer's
`wf_localized_*`, so one never shadows the other and the sidebar says which
is which.

23 tests: the viewer half against a canned-JSON fake worker (no vibe-qc
needed), the worker half skipped when vibe-qc is not importable. The
controller was additionally driven headlessly against a real QVF — the trame
websocket does not connect through the in-app browser, so click-through
review was not possible.

### Changed: localized orbitals are on by default, in three flavours (2026-08-05)

`run_job` now runs IBO, Foster-Boys and Pipek-Mezey by default on converged
closed-shell molecular jobs and emits one `wavefunction.gto` section per
criterion (`wf_localized_ibo`, `wf_localized_boys`,
`wf_localized_pipek_mezey`) for vibe-view to switch between.
`localize=False` turns it off; `localize="ibo"` or
`localize=["ibo", "boys"]` selects a subset.

**Three, because they disagree.** On benzene/def2-SVP the centre census is
6/12/3 (one-, two-, three-centre) for IBO and Pipek-Mezey but 6/15/0 for
Boys: Boys mixes sigma with pi and turns the aromatic pi system into three
more two-centre "banana" bonds, where the population-based criteria keep
sigma and pi apart. Comparing the two pictures is the feature.

Whichever criterion runs, the descriptors -- atomic populations, centre
counts, charges -- are computed on the same IAO yardstick, so they are
directly comparable. The IAO charges come out identical across all three, as
they must: localization is a unitary rotation inside the occupied space.

**Cost, measured against the SCF that produced them:** +16 % on
H2O/def2-TZVPP, +62 % on benzene/def2-SVP. Almost all of the aromatic case
is Boys, whose p=2 functional needs ~89 Jacobi sweeps there against IBO's
14 -- the degenerate-pi case Knizia cites for preferring p=4.

### Performance: the Boys and Pipek-Mezey sweeps are vectorized (2026-08-05)

Both carried the same per-atom Python loop that IBO shed earlier today.
On benzene/def2-SVP, Boys drops 5.60 s -> 1.81 s (3.1x) and Pipek-Mezey
3.52 s -> 0.276 s (12.7x). Boys is **bit-identical** before and after and
Pipek-Mezey agrees to 2.8e-16, so DLPNO -- which calls both -- is unaffected;
its localization step is simply faster now.

The two are slow for opposite reasons, which is worth knowing before
optimizing further: Pipek-Mezey's sweeps were expensive and are now cheap,
while Boys' sweeps were always cheap and it just needs a great many of them
on aromatics. Vectorizing cannot fix the second.

### Added: Edmiston-Ruedenberg citation entry (2026-08-05)

`localise.py` has attributed its Jacobi rotation-angle solution to Edmiston
& Ruedenberg, *Rev. Mod. Phys.* **35**, 457 (1963) in prose since it was
written, with no entry behind it -- a standing CLAUDE.md section 8 gap that
only became user-visible once the localization routes started firing. The
`foster_boys` and `pipek_mezey` routes now carry it. IBO does not: Knizia's
Appendix D attributes its 2x2 rotations to Pipek-Mezey instead.

### Added: IAO charges join `atom_properties` (2026-08-05)

`iao_charge` is now a member of the QVF `atom_properties` section, so IAO
partial charges sit next to Mulliken / Löwdin / Hirshfeld in vibe-view's
charge picker rather than being buried in the localized wavefunction
section's metadata. On CH₄/def2-SVP, Mulliken puts −0.144 on carbon where
IAO puts −0.473 — the picker now makes that comparison a click.

`atom_properties` has a **closed** member set, so this touched the schema
in every place it lives: the canonical copy, both qvf-writer copies (byte-
identical, each with its own drift guard), and the *derived* v2 schema,
which is generated by `scripts/gen_qvf_v2_schema.py` and is the one easy to
forget — `tests/test_qvf_v2_schema_drift.py` is what catches it.
vibe-view's `schema.json` is a symlink to the canonical and needed nothing.

Known asymmetry: the `.population.{txt,json}` sidecars do not carry an IAO
row, because the analysis runs after they are written. The QVF is the
complete record; this is documented in the user guide and the handover.

### Changed: the IBO Jacobi sweep is vectorized (2026-08-05)

The per-atom accumulation inside the sweep was a Python loop, which put the
IBO analysis at 24.5 % of SCF wall time on benzene and 41.2 % on a
C₁₀H₈-sized system — a fraction that *grew* with system size. It is now a
`np.bincount` segment sum, holding at 6.4 % and 7.1 % respectively, and now
roughly flat in system size. Identical sweep counts, orbitals agreeing to
2×10⁻¹⁴, benzene's orbital census unchanged.

Two alternatives were measured and rejected: a per-atom Q tensor (the
pattern the Boys solver in the same file uses) is `n_atoms × n_occ²`, cubic
in system size where `bincount` stays linear; and folding the segment sum
into one matmul against an indicator matrix is *slower* at these matrix
sizes, since BLAS call overhead dominates.

### Fixed: several vibe-view defects a second wavefunction section exposed (2026-08-05)

Found while landing the above; each of these also affected the NTO
sections, which have shared the `wavefunction.gto` kind for longer:

- The sidebar titled every `wavefunction.gto` section "Wavefunction", so
  a file with canonical + localized + NTO orbitals showed several
  indistinguishable rows. Titles are now section-aware.
- `_frontier_indices` is occupation-only, so on an all-occupied localized
  set it tagged the **last orbital as "HOMO"**. Suppressed for localized
  sets, which have no frontier.
- The energy-level diagram rendered an empty 400 px figure for an
  energyless set; it now explains that localized orbitals have no
  eigenvalue spectrum.
- The emitter writes `energies` as explicit zeros rather than null:
  `np.asarray(None, dtype=np.float64)` yields a 0-d `array(nan)` that
  passes the reader's `is not None` guard and crashes downstream.

### Added: the per-iteration multi-k GDF exchange build farms over MPI ranks (2026-08-05)

`HANDOVER_MPI.md` item 4c. Exchange is the one O(n_k^2) term a multi-k GDF
SCF runs every iteration, and it is now distributed over the **bra**
k-index: each rank computes complete `K(k_i)` matrices for its share and
the results are reassembled in global k order with
`KPointPartition.allgather_ordered`.

Ranks exchange whole matrices rather than partial sums, so the farmed
answer is **exact**, not merely close. Under real `mpirun` at 1, 2 and 3
ranks every rank reproduces the serial reference to below 1e-12 relative,
a full (3,1,1) SCF gives `-1.119306844982527` identically at every rank
count, and an uneven split (6 bra rows over 4 ranks) reassembles
correctly. A single rank is the identity partition with a no-op gather, so
the serial path is byte-unchanged (H2/STO-3G (2,1,1) still
`-1.1201398816771202` exactly).

This was cheap to land only because the 2026-08-02 occupied-index refactor
had already reduced the contraction to a kernel taking an explicit `rows`
argument, which is exactly the partition axis. The IBZ-native path passes
its wedge rows through the same argument and is farmed for free.

**It is also faster on a single node, which was not expected.** The
handover recorded a prediction, before measuring, that this would be a
wash at fixed total cores -- as the earlier cderi-setup farming was. That
prediction was wrong. On H2/6-31g** `(2,2,2)` with 8 total cores
throughout and bit-identical energies: 47.69 s at 1 rank x 8 threads,
31.86 s at 2 x 4 (1.50x), 28.36 s at 4 x 2 (1.68x). The likely reason is
that this loop's GEMMs are individually small, so 8-way BLAS threading on
each is inefficient and more ranks with fewer threads recovers the
efficiency. One cell on one node with one BLAS is not a scaling curve,
and multi-node remains unmeasured.

Also worth knowing: `mpi4py` was absent from this dev environment, so the
whole `tests/test_mpi_kpoint_multirank.py` lane had been **skipping**
rather than passing. It is installed now and all 10 tests execute; check
that before trusting a green MPI lane elsewhere.

### Fixed: a BIPOLE fold refusal at a line-search trial geometry no longer kills the optimization (2026-08-05)

`relax_atoms` documents that a line-search probe failing is recoverable:
the objective returns a penalty barrier and L-BFGS-B backs off. But the
fold-support preflight added on 2026-08-01 (`9633ee6bc`) raised a bare
`RuntimeError`, which the barrier's `except SCFNonConvergence` did not
catch — so when the optimizer's first unit trial step in fractional
coordinates threw the atoms ~one lattice vector out of the cell (H2 in an
18-bohr box lands at d(H–H) = 24 bohr, S(Γ) fold drift 1.2e-2), the gate's
correct refusal of that absurd geometry aborted the whole job instead of
shrinking the step. The refusal is now a `BipoleFoldUnreliableError`
(still a `RuntimeError` for existing callers) and the barrier treats it
exactly like a non-converged trial SCF. A refusal at the *initial*
geometry still aborts: there is nothing to back off to. Regression tests
in `tests/test_bipole_production_guards.py`; the periodic geomopt .out
snapshot (which died mid-job on `main`) runs to completion again.

### Fixed: machine-dependent numerical noise leaked into the .out format (2026-08-05)

Two properties-block renderings depended on floating-point noise, so the
same job produced byte-different `.out` scaffolding on different
machines/BLAS builds — tripping `tests/test_out_format_snapshot.py`
goldens that digit-zeroing cannot protect:

* **Mayer bond-order row order.** `prominent_bonds` sorted by raw
  descending bond order; symmetry-equivalent bonds (the two O–H bonds of
  C2v water) are degenerate up to noise, so their display order was a
  coin flip. The sort now quantizes at 1e-6 (well below the displayed 4
  decimals) and breaks ties by atom indices.
* **Signed zeros widened content-sized columns.** A dipole component that
  is zero at the displayed precision rendered `-0.0000` or `0.0000`
  depending on the last bit's sign, and the properties tables size their
  columns from content, so the stray minus widened the whole column. The
  snapshot canonicalizer already normalized the sign glyph (`66d7cc6c8`)
  but could not hide the width change. Values that round to zero at their
  displayed precision (dipole components, charge sums) now render
  unsigned; genuine negatives keep their sign.

The four affected molecular goldens are regenerated (bond rows now in
index order); `mol_uhf.out` passes unchanged now that its Debye column
width no longer depends on the sign of a ±1e-18 dipole component.

### Changed: periodic .out goldens follow the truthful zero-Gram DIIS trace (2026-08-05)

`4024de657` (2026-08-01) made the shared Pulay solver return the raw Fock
instead of "extrapolating" over a zero/singular Gram history. On the H2/Γ
snapshot fixture the commutator is exactly zero by symmetry, so DIIS now
truthfully reports no subspace and the iteration table renders `-` where
it previously showed a fabricated subspace size. `periodic_rhf.out` and
`periodic_geomopt.out` are regenerated to match (the geomopt golden also
gains the coalesced moderate-drift fold Note emitted by the backed-off
line-search steps above).

### Fixed: degenerate Gamma orbitals are re-expressed on a real basis (2026-08-05)

Follow-up to the periodic Molden entry below, and the reason multi-k GDF
exports at all. Dividing one global phase out of each column makes a Gamma
orbital real only when it is real up to *a phase*. Inside a degenerate block
the eigensolver may return any unitary mixture of the partners, and no
per-column phase undoes a rotation *between* columns.

The residual tracks degeneracy exactly, and does so on both routes.
Ne/STO-3G, k222, converged, max|Im|/max|C| after phase removal:

| orbital | gap to nearest level | BIPOLE | GDF |
|---|---|---|---|
| non-degenerate (1, 2, 5) | 1e+0 to 2e-3 Ha | 1e-19 to 1e-17 | 1e-16 to 1e-14 |
| degenerate 2p pair (3, 4) | 1e-15 Ha | 1.1e-05 | 3.9e-03 |

It is also not convergence error: the residual does not shrink as the SCF
tightens, because it is conditioning.

The span of a degenerate block *is* real, since H(k=0) and S(k=0) are real
symmetric. For a block `C = U W` with `U` real and `W` unitary, `Re C` and
`Im C` both lie in `span(U)`, so the real `n x 2m` matrix `[Re C | Im C]` has
exactly that span as its column space. Diagonalising its Gram matrix in the
Gamma overlap metric and keeping the `m` non-null directions returns a real
basis with `B^T S B = I`: S-orthonormal eigenvectors at the same eigenvalue,
which is what a real-arithmetic code would have produced. Any rotation within
an eigenspace is as valid as any other, so which one comes back is not
meaningful; both routes now measure `max|C^T S C - I| = 5e-16`.

Blocks already real up to phase are left untouched, so runs that worked
before keep byte-identical coefficients and the driver's own sign
convention. A block that cannot be real-ified still falls through to the
per-column refusal.

This retires the interim route allowlist: multi-k Molden was briefly
promised only for BIPOLE, because GDF's degenerate frontier orbital was
refused and -- since `plan.py` declares `.molden` a *guaranteed* artefact --
that refusal aborted finalization rather than dropping a sidecar. The
allowlist was treating a symptom. The optional-row ask in
`handovers/HANDOVER_OUTPUT_LOGGER.md` still stands at reduced severity: a
genuine k != 0 orbital should drop a sidecar, not fail a job whose SCF
already succeeded.

### Fixed: periodic Molden export was unusable on every BIPOLE route (2026-08-05)

`run_periodic_job(..., write_molden_file=True)` failed three different ways
on BIPOLE, and the closed-shell one failed silently:

* **Multi-k requests aborted the job before the SCF started.** The sidecar
  capability gate required the k-mesh to *be* Γ rather than to *contain* Γ,
  so `write_molden_file=True` raised `NotImplementedError` on any
  Monkhorst-Pack mesh. vibe-qc's `monkhorst_pack` is Γ-centred at every
  subdivision, so the Γ block those runs need was there the whole time.
  The gate now asks the question that decides the answer, and
  `_gamma_index_for_multi_k` still refuses a mesh that genuinely has no Γ
  rather than exporting some other k-point as if it were Γ.
* **Unrestricted results wrote nothing.** `PBCBipoleUHFResult` /
  `PBCBipoleUKSResult` carry one `(nbf, nmo)` block per k-point under
  `mo_coeffs_alpha` / `mo_coeffs_beta` and have no `mo_coeffs` at all, so
  the runner's Γ proxy, which keyed on `mo_coeffs`, passed the whole per-k
  list to the writer. That raised `too many values to unpack`, leaving a
  "molden write failed" warning and no file.
* **Restricted results wrote a corrupt file under a "written" log line.**
  Bloch MO coefficients are `complex128` even at Γ, and numpy formats a
  complex scalar as `a+bj`, so every coefficient landed as
  `9.93E-01+2.83E-20j`, text no Molden reader can parse. Two such files
  ship in `docs/_static/examples/mgo-route-gdf-bipole/` (196 affected
  coefficient lines each) and are still stale: that fixture bundle is
  generated by a `vq submit` job against a SHA-gated managed build, so it
  is regenerated by resubmitting once this fix is on `main`, not by
  hand-patching artifacts whose `.system` manifest and `summary-*.json`
  would then disagree.

The writer now divides out each orbital's arbitrary global phase and
writes the real part. That is exact at Γ, where H(k=0) and S(k=0) are real
symmetric. Inside a degenerate block the eigensolver returns an arbitrary
unitary mixture of the partners, so roundoff is degeneracy-amplified:
Ne/STO-3G puts its exactly degenerate 2p pair at 7.5e-06, and that
residual does *not* shrink as the SCF converges, because it is
conditioning and not convergence error. Taking the real part remains exact
there, since `Re(c)` of a vector in a real invariant subspace stays in it.
An orbital that is still complex after phase removal, a genuine Bloch
orbital at k != 0, is refused with a diagnostic naming the spin and the
orbital, rather than written as numbers a viewer would misread.

`write_population_file=True` no longer needs Γ on BIPOLE either.
`compute_bipole_population_summary` already contracted the real-space
lattice density and the full SCF k-mesh, so it is a crystal population and
the Γ gate was never its constraint. Other routes keep the restriction,
because they fall back to a molecular analysis of one Bloch block.

**Molden cannot represent a crystal, and vibe-qc now says so.** The format
has no lattice-vector block, no k-point, and no complex coefficients, so a
periodic `.molden` is the Γ block evaluated over home-cell basis functions
with no image sum: the home-cell truncation of the crystalline orbital,
clipped wherever an orbital straddles a cell face. The `.out` states this
where it announces the file, and the user guide now recommends `.qvf` plus
vibe-view for periodic orbitals, which carry the lattice, the k-point
metadata, the complex Bloch wavefunction, and torus-periodic grids that
wrap correctly across cell faces. See
[Molden and periodic systems](https://vibe-qc.com/docs/tutorial/orbital_visualization.html) and
[the BIPOLE sidecar table](https://vibe-qc.com/docs/user_guide/bipole.html).

One side effect worth knowing: the writer now prefers the result's own
occupations when it carries them, so ROHF Γ exports no longer report their
singly occupied orbital as empty (the aufbau fallback floored an odd
electron count to zero), and smeared multi-k exports keep their fractional
frontier occupations.

### Fixed: GPW multi-k pencil built over one converged lattice R-set — THIS CHANGES NUMBERS on every GPW compact-crystal result (2026-08-05)

Two coupled defects in the multi-k GPW drivers (RKS, UKS and the ROKS
wrapper), fixed together because fixing either alone made results worse:

* **`GPW-MULTIK-OVERLAP-NOT-PSD`** — the Bloch overlap
  `S(k) = sum_R exp(ik.R) S(R)` was truncated at the bare 15-bohr
  `LatticeSumOptions` default, leaving the metric INDEFINITE on compact
  crystals with a molecular basis (measured min eig over the (4,4,4)
  production mesh at def2-SVP: LiF -1.507, MgO -0.198, Si -0.155) and
  silently destroying multi-k spectra (negative MgO/LiF gaps in the
  2026-08-02 wave). The drivers now size the sum from the basis with
  `vibeqc.lattice_screening.bloch_overlap_cutoff_bohr` (the Pisani &
  Dovesi 1980 overlap criterion, landed earlier as an unwired helper),
  and an indefinite S(k) now **fails closed** at the per-k
  orthogonalisation site instead of being absorbed by the
  linear-dependence projection.
* **`GPW-SK-HK-RSET-INCONSISTENT`** — each operator's real-space lattice
  sum was truncated independently: S/T over one options object, V_ne over
  a separate bare one. Completing the overlap sum alone (the first
  attempt at the fix above, backed out 2026-08-02) restored the insulating
  spectrum but collapsed LiF/def2-SVP totals by -18.2 Ha at every
  plane-wave cutoff from 300 to 1200 Ha: the neglected far-field
  one-electron terms are proportional to the overlap tail and cancel only
  when H(k) and S(k) drop the same tail (Pisani & Dovesi 1980, Sec. 4
  p. 510). The Hcore pencil alone reproduces the whole collapse (-17.6 Ha
  in the occupied band sum with no grid, no SCF, no density). S, T and
  V_ne are now built over ONE shared basis-derived R-set
  (`multik_one_electron_lattice_options` / `multik_v_ne_lattice_options`).

Acceptance, measured on the discriminator fixture (LiF/def2-SVP,
zone-centre-centred (2,2,2), PBE, multi-k Bloch branch): E =
-107.2926 / -107.3325 Ha at 300 / 600 Ha with a +9.29 eV insulating gap,
converged in 13 iterations — against -107.746 Ha with a destroyed
+0.155 eV near-metallic spectrum (flat 15-bohr truncation) and
-125.933 Ha with the overlap-only remedy, both at 600 Ha. The
cutoff-converged physical target for this cell is -107.385 Ha
(`test_fixed_density_gpw_functional_converges_to_physical_scale`); the
~9.3 eV gap is the literature PBE scale for LiF — the earlier "5.9 eV"
was itself an artifact of the inconsistent pencil.

**Supersedes every prior multi-k GPW number on a compact crystal** —
LiF-class ionic cells move O(10) Ha in the total and O(10) eV in the gap
(the route was production-halted since 2026-08-02; the paper's main-table
GPW cell was withheld for exactly this reason). Affected routes:
`run_periodic_rks_gpw_multi_k`, `run_periodic_uks_gpw_multi_k`, the ROKS
wrapper, and everything the runner dispatches onto them
(`jk_method="gpw"`, multi-k, compact cells). Molecular-limit /
vacuum-padded GPW cells are numerically unaffected (the added lattice
blocks vanish there; one Γ-parity guard tolerance moved from 1e-9 to
1e-8 Ha for the now-included physical inter-image tail). Reproducer +
guards: `tests/test_periodic_gpw_rset_consistency.py`,
`tests/test_periodic_gpw_compact_multik.py`.

### Added: periodic runs report what linear dependence actually discarded (2026-08-03)

The periodic GDF `.out` gains a `Linear dependence` block: basis functions
per k, the dimension retained after canonical orthogonalisation, how many
directions were discarded, the threshold used, the smallest overlap
eigenvalue and the condition number, plus the auxiliary-fit retained
dimension and its own threshold.

Every one of those numbers was already computed inside the drivers and
thrown away -- `n_kept` was collected into a list per k-point and never
read. So a periodic SCF could work in a smaller variational space than its
basis implies, or fit its density on a metric whose small eigenvalues are
truncation noise, with nothing in the durable record to say so.

The block is printed **even when nothing is discarded**, which is the
point: "0 directions dropped" is the observation that rules an
ill-conditioned basis out as the cause of a surprising energy, and its
absence is what made several periodic post-mortems ambiguous. The
non-physical-energy guard now quotes the same state, so instead of listing
candidate causes (gauge mismatch / Madelung convention / inconsistent
cderi cache) it gives the reader something to discriminate among them.

Motivating evidence is first-hand: attributing the fenced MDF dense-core
divergence to `gdf_linear_dep_threshold` (1e-9 gives -62874 Ha, 1e-3 gives
-271.146 against a -271.0499 reference) took three sessions largely
because none of this state was observable.

No numerics change: the block is additive reporting, and the drivers'
energies are unchanged.

_No unreleased changes yet. Add new entries directly below this line.

### Fixed: Cartesian AO normalization, on all four surfaces at once (2026-08-05)

Follow-up to the AO-convention commit earlier today, which pinned the split
but did not close it. libint normalizes a shell with **one** factor taken
from the total `l`, so mixed Cartesian components are deliberately not
unit-normalized: `<xy|xy> = 1/3` against `<xx|xx> = 1` on a d shell. QVF
spec Appendix A.1 specifies exactly that factor, and the QVF writer already
divided by it.

Both AO *evaluators* did something else. `vibeqc.evaluate_ao` multiplied
Cartesian output by `cart_relative_norm`, and vibe-view's reader applied the
same factor as `_cart_correction`, each reaching true unit norm per
component. So a d_xy coefficient vector normalized where MO coefficients
actually live (`c^T S c = 1`) integrated to **3.0** through either one. Both
now follow A.1: grid-evaluated AOs reproduce `compute_overlap` for Cartesian
shells as they always did for spherical ones.

With the readers correct, the writer's Cartesian rejection
(`QVFCartesianShellError`, added hours earlier) was blocking a path that now
round-trips, so it is **removed** — as its own docstring said it would be
once the split was resolved. `wavefunction.gto` emits both shell kinds
again. Named bases still force `set_pure(true)`, so production archives
remain spherical.

Nothing in a normal calculation changes. Spherical shells were never
affected: the transform is defined against the same unnormalized monomials,
so the old code multiplied the factor in and divided it straight back out.
That is precisely why this survived — every named basis is spherical, so the
entire ordinary test surface was blind to it. *[Correction 2026-08-06:
"nothing in a normal calculation changes" holds for named bases only. A
basis imported as Cartesian via `vibeqc.basis_toolkit.to_libint_basis()`
(v0.15.0+) fed the broken evaluators in every DFT XC quadrature, gradient,
and COSX build — this fix changed those results by ~0.35 Ha on a measured
Be/RKS-PBE case. See the reclassification entry under \[Unreleased\].]*

`tests/test_ao_convention_invariants.py` now asserts the positive invariant
(grid integration reproduces `compute_overlap`, l = 0..3, both shell kinds)
and closes the loop end to end: a Cartesian d_xy normalized in vibe-qc's
integral basis, emitted as a QVF payload, evaluated by vibe-view's own
evaluator, integrates to 1 electron. vibe-view's
`test_wavefunction_normalization.py` had asserted unit norm per Cartesian
component — the assertion that let this stand — and now asserts A.1's.

### Fixed: pin the two AO conventions vibe-qc assumes at the libint boundary (2026-08-05)

Two conventions were assumed in several independent places and checked in
none of them. Both fail silently — nothing raises, the numbers are just
wrong — so each now has a guard at the place that assumes it.

**Solid-harmonic ordering.** `cpp/src/ao_eval.cpp`, the molden writer, and
the QVF writer each hardcode libint's STANDARD in-shell order (m = -l..+l);
`grep -rn SHGSHELL cpp/ python/ tests/` previously returned nothing. Under
GAUSSIAN ordering every pure shell with l ≥ 1 would permute with no error.
Guarded now by a `static_assert` in `cpp/include/vibeqc/basis.hpp` and — the
load-bearing half — a runtime check in `ensure_libint_initialized()`.

The runtime check is the one that matters, and that is worth stating: the
`LIBINT_SHGSHELL_ORDERING` build macro is *not* what the integral engine
reads. Upstream deprecated it (libint's own `config2.h` marks it retired);
`SolidHarmonicsCoefficients` consults the runtime
`libint2::solid_harmonics_ordering()` instead. A rebuild of the vendored
libint would therefore not have changed engine behaviour, and a
macro-only assertion would have guarded the wrong thing.

**Cartesian primitive normalization.** libint applies one normalization per
shell, from the total `l`, so a mixed Cartesian component is not
unit-normalised — measured on a single d shell, `compute_overlap` gives
⟨xy|xy⟩ = 1/3 against ⟨xx|xx⟩ = 1. QVF spec Appendix A.1's `N_i` encodes
exactly that convention, so the writer and the spec formula already agreed.
The AO evaluators do not: both `vibeqc.evaluate_ao` and vibe-view apply an
extra per-component factor to reach true unit norm. A d_xy vector normalised
in the integral basis (cᵀSc = 1), where MO coefficients live, integrates to
3.0 through either evaluator.

The QVF writer now **rejects Cartesian shells** (`QVFCartesianShellError`)
rather than emitting a payload its own readers would misread. This is
unreachable through the named-basis route, which forces `set_pure(true)`,
but reachable through the explicit-`ShellInfo` `BasisSet` constructor. The
runner turns the rejection into a visible structured warning, not a job
failure.

Spec Appendix A.1 described its primitives as "unit-normalized" while its
formula said otherwise — the writer implemented the formula and the readers
implemented the prose. A.1 now states the convention explicitly, warns
consumers not to add a per-component correction, and records the vibe-qc
producer limitation; the same wording is corrected in both reference
writers. No schema change was needed: the per-component factor is derivable
from `(l_x, l_y, l_z)`, which A.2's ordering already pins, so it never had
to be carried in the file. The four schema copies remain byte-identical.

Regression coverage in `tests/test_ao_convention_invariants.py`, including a
deliberately pinned test of the `evaluate_ao` / `compute_overlap` Cartesian
disagreement so that aligning them trips a test that says what else to
revisit.

### Fixed: the desktop publishing runbook contradicted the Windows ship decision (2026-08-05)

`vibe-view/electron/PUBLISHING.md`'s platform table still read "Windows —
not in scope. Follow-up branch", which the maintainer decision of 2026-07-08
had already superseded: Windows is a ship target, shipped untested and
unsigned (`vibe-view/docs/desktop_packaging_design.md`,
`handovers/HANDOVER_VIBEVIEW_DESKTOP_PACKAGING.md`). The runbook is the
operator-facing document, so it was the one place an operator would read the
wrong scope. Corrected to match the decision and to name what is actually
missing: a Windows build host, since electron-builder cannot cross-build the
`nsis` target from macOS.

The three Windows caveats — the runbook table, the user guide, and the
`electron/README.md` build notes — now also carry the support offer they
were missing. Each said Windows is untested and asked for feedback; none
said what a user gets in return. **The developer has no Windows machine and
cannot reproduce Windows problems, but is glad to help anyone who wants to
try.** The app's one-time first-run Windows notice
(`maybeShowWindowsNotice()`) says so too, so the offer reaches the user who
is actually standing in front of the untested build rather than only the one
reading the docs.

### Added: a Python API page for vibe-view's supported scripting surface (2026-08-05)

`docs/user_guide/vibe_view_python_api.md` documents the seventeen names in
`vibeview.__all__` — the surface a script is allowed to depend on — with a
runnable example for each. Every output shown on the page was produced by
running the call against the `qvf-writer/conformance/corpus/` fixtures, not
transcribed from a docstring.

The gap it closes is not "no examples exist" but **which examples are the
contract**. The tutorial's Python snippets import from submodules
(`vibeview.capture`, `vibeview.qvf`, `vibeview.align`), so the curated
top-level API in `__init__.py` was the one surface nothing pointed at. The
page states the rule plainly: a top-level import is supported, a submodule
path is an internal detail.

Two things worth knowing that were not written down anywhere:

* **The base install covers everything except `launch_qvf`.** PyVista,
  matplotlib and plotly are core dependencies, so headless PNG capture,
  reading, slicing and diffing need no extra. Only the interactive browser
  viewer needs `[viewer]`. The `capture` extra is deliberately empty and
  exists to document exactly this.
* **`get_volume` does not return voxels.** It reads the array and returns a
  JSON-serializable *summary* — grid geometry plus value range. Its docstring
  claimed "grid + data arrays", which is what a caller would reasonably code
  against and then find missing; corrected, and pointed at
  `QVFReader.read_volume_data` for the `ndarray`.

The page ends by scoping extension rather than implying it: there is **no
plugin API**, composition is the supported answer today, and the five pieces
a real one would need (entry-point discovery, a representation interface, an
importer hook, a panel contract, a versioning policy) are listed so the
decision is informed rather than rediscovered.

### Fixed: the desktop setup screen failed WCAG AA on contrast and announced nothing (2026-08-05)

An accessibility pass over `vibe-view/electron/setup.html`, the first-run
onboarding page — the one screen a user with a broken environment cannot
avoid. Contrast was measured, not eyeballed.

* **White on `--accent` was 3.52:1**, below the 4.5:1 AA floor for normal
  text, and it carried the primary "recheck" button and the step counters —
  the two things the page most needs a user to read. Added `--accent-strong`
  (#5664d9, **4.98:1**) on the same hue for surfaces bearing white text.
  Its hover shade *darkens* to #4b58bf (**6.09:1**); lightening it, the usual
  reflex, is what put the original under the floor.
* **The recheck loop was silent to a screen reader.** Every outcome —
  checking, found it, still not detected — is written to one `<div>` that had
  no live region, so pressing the page's primary button produced no
  announcement at all. Now `role="status"` + `aria-live="polite"`.
* **The command block is a horizontally scrollable region** that no keyboard
  could reach (WCAG 2.1.1). Now focusable with an accessible name.
* **No focus styling existed**, leaving keyboard users the UA default ring
  against a dark card. Added an explicit `:focus-visible` outline.
* **The spinner animated indefinitely regardless of preference.** Now
  honours `prefers-reduced-motion`, keeping a static ring so the busy state
  is still visible.
* The decorative ◈ glyph is `aria-hidden`; the step list keeps its semantics
  under `list-style: none` via `role="list"`; the Copy button's `aria-label`
  moves with its visible text, so the "Copied" confirmation is not silently
  overridden by a stale accessible name.

Verified in a real browser: computed primary background `rgb(86,100,217)`,
the accessibility tree exposing the status region, list semantics and the
named command region, and the recheck outcome landing in the live region.

### Added: the vq fleet console is installable, configurable, and can no longer drift in silence (2026-08-05)

The fleet console (`vq web run --fleet`) told operators three things that were
not true, and had no mechanism that could have noticed.

**What was wrong.** On the reference fleet the console was served by a
hand-staged copy of vq pinned at 0.16.0, commit `a69ef9428`, **1081 commits
behind** the managed checkout on the same machine, running that way since
2026-07-25. It rendered `0.16.0` as *ten different hosts' versions*: the page
header (which is the serving process's own version, unlabelled), the two cards
for hosts that resolve as local, and -- because the deployed code predated
`b68c54fff` -- the eight daemonless scheduler hosts, which borrowed their
driver's number, and their driver was the console itself. Nothing detected it.
No rollout lane, convergence check, or runbook recorded that the unit existed;
`vq admin rollout-latest --verify-only` could and did report the fleet
`converged` while the dashboard served 8-minor-versions-stale code. Separately,
the coordinator was enrolled twice in its own config, so one machine rendered as
two cards -- and, because `FleetSnapshot.jobs` flattens per-host rows, every job
on it was counted twice in the cross-host table and the JSON API.

**Configuration is now data, not an ExecStart line.** New `[web]` config
section (`WebConsoleConfig`) carrying `bind`, `port`, `fleet`,
`fleet_interval_seconds`, `log_level`, `title` and `public_bind_ack`.
`vq.web.settings` resolves one order for every consumer -- CLI flag >
environment > `[web]` > built-in default -- and validates all four layers
against the same model, so a value the config file rejects can no longer arrive
through the environment (`VQ_WEB_PORT=70000` and `VQ_WEB_LOG_LEVEL=chatty` both
used to get through, the latter crashing uvicorn at startup). `vq web config`
prints the resolved values with the layer each came from, and reports the real
source rather than crediting an environment variable whose value was rejected.

**`vq web install` / `uninstall` / `status`.** Writes and enables the service
unit for systemd (user or system) or launchd, with `--dry-run` printing every
file and command first. Two properties matter: the unit's `ExecStart` points at
the vq that ran the install, derived from `sys.executable` rather than `$PATH`;
and the install is recorded in `<config-dir>/web-console-install.json`, so
`vq web status` can compare the installing version against the installed one and
report drift. The unit carries no configuration, so a re-install cannot drop a
flag.

**The console audits itself.** Every page compares the console's own vq version
against the local daemon's and shows a banner when they disagree, naming both
and saying what to do. It never guesses: an unreachable daemon yields no
comparison and no warning. This check alone would have surfaced the drift on the
day it started.

**Host identity is verified rather than assumed.** `HostOverview` gained
`reported_hostname` (the machine's own answer, gathered where it means something
and carried back through the existing JSON -- no daemon change, no new round
trip) and `self_reported`. `_overview_from_json` previously rebuilt the overview
and discarded the payload's identity; that was the seam where verified identity
was being dropped. A card now shows "calls itself &lt;name&gt;" when the machine
disagrees with the config key, and the page banners a duplicate enrolment rather
than silently deduping it -- vq cannot know which key the operator meant to keep,
and the double-counted jobs are a real defect worth naming.

**Versions say whose they are.** The header chip reads `console v<version>` with
the interpreter path and start time in its tooltip. A host's chip is never
blank: a real version, else `vq helper <sha>` for a daemonless scheduler host
(which the CLI already printed and the web console rendered as nothing), else an
explicit `vq version unknown`. Silence was indistinguishable from agreement.

**The page answers the operator's first three questions.** A fleet roll-up
strip -- hosts, running, pending, CPUs busy, unreachable, degraded, and the
count of distinct vq versions, which is the number a rolling update is watching.
Per-host program versions and `helper_source_sha`, both already crossing the
wire and both dropped by the view, making the HTML dashboard strictly less
informative than `vq overview`. Snapshot age with a staleness threshold that
