follows the configured sweep interval, because the sweep thread swallows its
exceptions and keeps serving its last good snapshot while the page goes on
polling every 10 s -- so it animates identically whether or not it is dead.
Failure detail moved out of `title=` tooltips, which are keyboard-inaccessible,
invisible on touch, and uncopyable, into the card body.

**Two fixes to things that were quietly wrong.** htmx is vendored at
`web/static/htmx.min.js` (0BSD, provenance and SHA-256 recorded beside it,
inventory in `docs/license.md`) instead of fetched from `unpkg.com` at render
time -- which made the console silently non-functional on a fleet without
egress and left an unpinned third-party script in the trust path of a surface
that can kill jobs. And `.badge-warn` fell back to `--pending` (grey), so
`draining`, `throttled` and `update in flight` rendered as the least salient
chips on the card.

**Security.** With fleet accounts configured, the single-host pages on the same
port (`/queue`, `/jobs/<id>` including stdout/stderr tails, `/api/v1/*`,
`/docs`) now require the same login as `/fleet`. They were unauthenticated,
which on a console bound to a private overlay meant every peer on that overlay,
uncredentialed, while `/fleet` next door asked for a password. Implemented as
middleware rather than a per-route dependency, because the surface being
protected is exactly the one where a per-route dependency was forgotten fifteen
times. No accounts configured = documented open tunnel posture, unchanged.
`/static` and `/health` stay open so the login page can render and supervisors
can still poll.

New user documentation at `vibe-queue/docs/fleet_console.md`. Tests:
`test_web_settings.py`, `test_web_console_status.py`, `test_web_fleet_identity.py`.

**Follow-up, same day: the self-audit now catches source drift, not just
version drift.** Deploying the above to the reference coordinator reproduced a
case the version comparison could not see. A checkout move replaced a running
console's source underneath it while both the console and the daemon still
reported `0.24.0`, so nothing compared unequal and no banner fired -- the
process simply went on executing code that no longer existed on disk. The
console now also captures a content digest of the vq package *at import* and
compares it against the digest on disk, which is what notices: a running
process keeps executing what it already imported. It stays silent unless both
digests are derivable and differ, so a console that cannot tell never raises an
alarm, and the check needs no daemon because the drift is self-observable.

**The console now counts toward the fleet convergence verdict.** Nothing in
`vq admin rollout-latest` knew the web console existed, so `--verify-only` could
report the fleet `converged` while the coordinator served pages from code 1081
commits behind the vq installed beside it -- which is exactly what it did for
two weeks. `--verify-only` now probes each in-scope host's `vq web status
--json` and folds the answer into the verdict, with `console_failures` added to
the payload (schema `vq.fleet.rollout_verify/2`).

The hard part is not detecting drift, it is not crying wolf. Three outcomes stay
distinct: **not applicable** (no console installed -- the correct state for every
host that is not the coordinator), **ok**, and **degraded** (installed but stale
or stopped). A fourth, **unknown**, covers a host whose vq predates `vq web
status`, an unreachable host, and unparseable output; it never degrades a host,
because otherwise rolling this check out would mark the whole fleet degraded
until every host had been upgraded. The probe never raises.

**Follow-up: `vq.web` no longer needs the `[web]` extra to be imported, and two
invisible-failure bugs on the page are fixed.**

`vq web status` and `vq web config` died with a bare
`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'fastapi'` on any host without the `[web]`
extra -- which is every fleet host except the coordinator, and precisely the
hosts where "no console installed here" is the correct answer they exist to
give. `vq/web/__init__.py` imported FastAPI at module level; `install.py` and
`settings.py` themselves need only stdlib plus `vq.config`/`vq.paths`, so it was
solely that import block dragging it in. The imports and the two route modules
that need them are now deferred into `create_app()`, and `TEMPLATES`,
`FAILED_CLEAR_STATES` and `app` are served by a module `__getattr__` so
`uvicorn vq.web:app` and the existing test that patches `web.TEMPLATES` keep
working. `vq web run` still fails with its readable "requires the 'web' extra"
message rather than a traceback. This mattered beyond the two verbs: it blocked
a fleet-wide console convergence probe, since the probe would have reported a
hard failure on every host where it was working correctly. Building `app`
eagerly at import was a second, quieter bug -- it froze whatever settings were
in effect at first import, which is why `vq web run` had always ignored it.

**A silently frozen page after session expiry.** The fleet grid and jobs table
poll every 10 s; when the 12 h session expires those fragment requests answer
401, and htmx 2.x does not swap non-2xx, so the last-good fragment stayed on
screen while the page went on polling and animating. It looked completely alive
while being arbitrarily stale -- the same failure class as the stale snapshot
above. `dashboard.js` now listens for `htmx:responseError` and
`htmx:beforeSwap`, and on a 401 shows a pinned banner with a "Log in now" link
before navigating to the login form. 401 only, never 403 (a 403 means the
session is fine and the role is not, so bouncing to login would loop), with a
one-shot flag so a burst of concurrent fragment 401s cannot stack banners.

**Wide tables now scroll in their own box** instead of panning the whole page
sideways and dragging the header off screen. `.table-scroll` had been defined in
the stylesheet and applied to nothing. Seven tables across six templates, with
the wrapper placed *inside* each htmx-swapped element rather than around it:
`hx-swap="outerHTML"` replaces the element itself, so a wrapper around it either
survives as a parent and nests one deeper on every poll, or lives only in the
parent page and leaves the bare fragment unwrapped.

Also: `HostOverview.is_scheduler_host`, so a daemonless scheduler host whose
helper record has not been written yet renders `daemonless · helper not
recorded` rather than a bare `vq version unknown`. Those are different
statements -- the first names the fix (run a scheduler-runtime update from this
driver), the second reads like a failure to answer. Surfaced on the reference
fleet, where the helper record did not migrate when the scheduler driver moved
to the coordinator.

### Added: vq fleet rollouts no longer need a human typing exact strings (2026-08-05)

Five changes to `vibe-queue`, aimed at the two remaining places where a fleet
rollout dropped out of the report-pinned path and onto an operator's keyboard,
plus the verification gap that turned a two-minute diagnosis into a handoff.

**1. `/opt/vq` refreshes are one command, and the ordering trap is gone.**
Multi-user hosts (site_e, site_b) run a second, root-owned vq at `/opt/vq/venv`
that `vq admin update` cannot reach by design -- it is the privilege boundary.
Every release therefore failed their vq lane until a maintainer ran a
three-command sudo sequence by hand, and that sequence had a silent-corruption
ordering trap: run `pip install` before the host's checkout reaches the pin and
it installs the **old** code, after which the operator's
`vq source-sha --write-marker <new-sha>` stamps the **new** commit onto it.
Verification trusts the marker, so `vq admin update` then reports `== OK ==`
and `source SHA ... verified` against a lie -- strictly harder to notice than
the honest failure it replaced. The marker's tree binding does not catch it:
that binding proves the marker still describes the package beside it, and here
it does. The lie is in the SHA the operator supplied, and nothing on the host
can check a claim about a commit it was never shown.

`contrib/vq-multi-user-refresh` closes it structurally rather than
procedurally. It **derives** the commit from the checkout it is about to
install (`git rev-parse HEAD`, refusing a dirty tree) and treats
`--expected-sha` purely as a cross-check that can abort the run but never
supply an identity. It then installs non-editable, digests the installed
package *before* stamping the marker, reads both back, restarts the unit, and
requires the restarted daemon to report the derived provenance over RPC before
exiting 0. `contrib/deploy-multi-user.sh` installs it root-owned at
`/opt/vq/bin/vq-multi-user-refresh`.

The accompanying `contrib/vq-multi-user-refresh.sudoers` -- letting `vq-admins`
run that one absolute path without a password -- is **opt-in**
(`deploy-multi-user.sh --grant-nopasswd`), and the reason is worth stating
because it was not obvious: the helper `pip install`s vq from a git checkout,
pip runs that checkout's build backend, and vibe-qc's backend (hatchling)
executes `[tool.hatch.build.hooks.custom]` from the source tree. So anyone who
can write an accepted checkout can run code as root through the helper, and
making that passwordless turns `vq-admins` membership into root. The exposure
itself is not new -- the manual `sudo /opt/vq/venv/bin/pip install
<checkout>/vibe-queue` this replaces always had it -- but it should be a
deliberate decision rather than a side effect of installing a correctness fix,
so the correctness fix lands unconditionally and the privilege grant does not.
The helper additionally refuses a checkout owned by neither root nor the
invoking user, and refuses a world-writable one, which stops it being pointed
at another user's tree or a planted one. Guards:
`tests/test_multi_user_refresh_helper.py`, which pins that `--write-marker`
receives `$derived_sha` and never `$expected_sha`, that the pin comparison
precedes the install, that the helper install sits outside the opt-in block,
and that the rule carries no wildcard and no home path.

**2. `vq admin rollout-latest --only <host>` / `--skip <host>`.** Since a
failed lane became terminal for its own host only, a sweep normally ends with
one degraded host and the rest converged -- and recovering that host meant
leaving the pinned path for a hand-typed
`vq admin update <env> <host> --expected-sha <40-hex>`, which is where
SHA-transcription errors live. The flags are repeatable and mutually exclusive,
and they narrow *which lanes execute* without rewriting one: every surviving
action still carries the accepted report's exact pins and byte-identical argv.
Three deliberate properties: the driver's own vq lane is never narrowed away
(a report-pinned rollout is driven *by* the pinned vq) and the selection
survives the driver self-update re-exec; excluded lanes are recorded as `defer`
with `out of rollout scope`, never `skip`, so a scoped run cannot mark the
fleet complete; and a selection naming no lane fails closed rather than running
to completion having done nothing and exiting 0. The fleet-wide `status` stays
in the result payload unchanged -- nothing is hidden -- while a scoped verdict
beside it under `selection` sets the exit code, so a successful `--only
site_e` exits 0 even while another host is behind.

**3. `vq admin rollout-latest --verify-only`.** Judging convergence was four
commands and a judgement call: `admin status --all --json`, `programs --all
--json`, `doctor --all`, then a second zero-action dry run to confirm the
planner agreed. All four read the state the planner already reads, and the
planner is the thing that decides whether a lane needs work, so the verdict is
now that planner's own answer: one `converged | degraded(hosts...)` line, or
`vq.fleet.rollout_verify/1` JSON whose `degraded_hosts` maps each host to every
reason -- pending lanes with the ancestry relation applied, failed doctor
checks, and topology errors, folded together. Exit 0 converged, 2 degraded. Two
gaps it closes: `--dry-run` exits 0 with pending `update` actions, and
`--dry-run --json` carries no `doctor_failures` at all. Placed before the
blocked-plan guard on purpose -- a verifier that cannot report on a blocked
fleet is useless.

**4. Daemon provenance is verified by installed-tree digest, not by a captured
SHA string.** The comparison at the heart of post-restart verification was a
category error, not a bug in either half: the expectation was
`git rev-parse HEAD` of the **checkout**, while the daemon reported whatever
its **installed package** declares -- a `SOURCE-SHA` marker, or, for a
non-editable install sitting inside an unrelated work tree, that tree's HEAD.
Those are different objects; their equality was assumed, not proved. On site_e
(2026-08-02) that produced a stale-looking SHA from a genuinely new daemon PID
while checkout, editable install and unit were all provably correct, and cost a
handoff.

`rpc.RPCServer` now also captures `source_tree_sha256` -- content-derived from
the package bytes -- and serves it in `ping` and `get_methods`.
`_verify_restarted_daemon` compares bytes to bytes: a matching digest verifies
the restart and says plainly that the *marker* is stale rather than the code,
naming the `--write-marker` command that fixes it; a mismatching digest reports
stale **code**. Capture stays at construction, which is the whole safety
property -- a live per-ping digest would describe the files on disk now, which
after an editable upgrade are the new ones even though the process is still
running old code, and would report a successful reload for a daemon that never
restarted. The expectation is asked of the just-updated interpreter
(`<prog.python> -m vq source-tree-sha256`), not computed in the admin process,
because on a multi-user host those are two different installs on purpose.
**Fails soft:** a daemon predating the ping key reports nothing and
verification falls back to the SHA comparison. Requiring it would have failed
every host on the release that introduced it -- including, structurally, the
`/opt/vq` daemons item 1 targets. The pair is persisted and surfaced in
`vq admin status --json`.

**5. `vq admin provision <host> [--check]`.** Read-only verification of the
preconditions `vq doctor` does not check -- each one having cost hours of a
fleet sweep while doctor reported the host green: `remote_vq` resolving to a
wrapper that exports `VQ_CONFIG_DIR` and `VQ_STATE_DIR` rather than straight to
the venv vq (without it the CLI reads the per-user store while canonical writes
go to the system one, so updates report `success: True` with no work errors and
`LAST OK` never advances); `admin_token_file` present at 0600; `/var/lib/vq`
`root:vq-admins` 2775; the root-owned install and its refresh helper present
and root-owned; `systemd-run` delegation; the unit active; programs registered.
Emitted under its own `vq.admin.provision_check/1` schema and deliberately
**not** into the doctor payload, because `fleet_rollout._host_hold_reason`
turns any failed doctor check other than `scheduler_remote_vq` into a rollout
defer -- a new failing check landing in doctor's payload would defer every host
on the next rollout. Repairing any of these needs root on the target, so
failures are reported with the exact fixing command rather than executed; the
mutating half is deliberately not built. `--check` suppresses the remediation
prose and is the form for a rehearsal such as confirming a driver-migration
candidate's preconditions.

Docs corrected in the same pass: `docs/fleet_update_runbook.md` said
`contrib/deploy-multi-user.sh` "does `mkdir -p` and never chgrps" the state
root, which has been false since `1d24c1838`, first tagged v0.15.106.

**Defects found by adversarial review of this change, before it landed.** Kept
here because each names a mistake the next person is likely to repeat:

* The helper's ownership gate stat-ed only the top of the checkout. Neither
  path that actually runs as root lives there -- pip builds
  `$checkout/vibe-queue`, and git reads `$checkout/.git/config`, which can name
  a program git executes (`core.fsmonitor` runs during `status`, on untracked
  content, so no commit and no dirty signal is involved). A shared
  `root:vq-admins 2775` tree -- the shape this project applies to
  `/var/lib/vq`, and the one an operator reaches for because "root-owned" reads
  as safe -- passed both the ownership test and a mode test that only caught
  world-writable. All three paths are guarded now, group-writable is refused,
  git runs with `core.fsmonitor` and `core.hooksPath` overridden, and `PATH` is
  pinned rather than inherited. The dirty check is also scoped to
  `vibe-queue/`, since the checkout is the whole monorepo and any untracked
  scratch file elsewhere would otherwise block every refresh.
* `_installed_tree_digest` ran `python -m vq`, which prepends the *current
  directory* to `sys.path`. An admin update runs from wherever the operator
  happened to be, and the checkout's own `src/` holds a `vq/` package, so the
  expectation could be a digest of the wrong tree -- one the daemon could never
  match. Now runs with `cwd="/"`.
* `--skip <host>` could not route around a *blocked* host: the block check ran
  over the whole plan, so the flag failed exactly when it was needed. Blocks
  and topology errors are now judged over the selected hosts.
* A scoped run persisted `complete = true` when interrupted. `execute_plan`
  sets that field on every exit from its loop, while the caller's correction
  was only reached on the success path; the scope is passed in now.
* The scoped exit code dropped the driver's own vq lane, so `--only site_e`
  could exit 0 for a rollout staged by a driver that was itself deferred --
  i.e. by a vq the report does not pin. The driver lane is retained in the
  execution verdict (but not in a pure `--verify-only` verdict, which was asked
  about one host).
* `--skip` on a lane-less host was a silent no-op. That is worse than the
  `--only` typo it mirrors: the operator believes a host was excluded and it
  never was, so the run does the thing they were trying to prevent. A scheduler
  alias sharing its canonical host's SSH endpoint is the realistic case. Both
  directions now fail closed.
* `vq admin provision` decided multi-user-ness from the *driver's* config. On a
  mixed fleet that reports a correctly provisioned single-user host as missing
  `/opt/vq`, `/var/lib/vq` and a root daemon it is not supposed to have -- six
  confident failures for a healthy machine -- and, reversed, skips every
  multi-user check on the hosts that need them. It now probes the target's own
  `/etc/vq/config.toml` and says so when it has to fall back.
* Its probes combined stdout and stderr, so an SSH banner in front of a
  `printf "missing"` sentinel turned "no `/opt/vq` install" into a passing
  check, and a `stat` error message reached `int(mode, 8)` as a `ValueError`.
  The probe layer returns the two streams separately now.
* The wrapper check was a substring search over the file body, so a wrapper
  whose *comment* mentioned `VQ_STATE_DIR` passed while exporting nothing --
  the exact split-store failure the check exists to catch. It now requires an
  assignment on a non-comment line, and resolves `remote_vq`'s program rather
  than the whole command line.
* `programs_registered` inspected the driver's registry, which cannot answer a
  question about the target; it now asks the host. And `--all --json` emitted a
  different top-level shape depending on how many hosts happened to be
  configured, which would have broken any consumer the day a second host was
  added -- the shape follows the form now, under a distinct
  `vq.admin.provision_check_fleet/1` schema. `--all` against an empty config
  reported the fleet provisioned, because `all([])` is `True`.
* Documented behaviour that did not match the code: the tree digest can
  *rescue* a verification the SHA comparison would have failed, but cannot
  *fail* one the SHA passes. That asymmetry is deliberate -- making the digest
  authoritative tightens availability rather than precedence, and on a
  multi-user host the admin CLI and the daemon resolve different installs by
  design -- so the docs now state it and a test pins it.

## [v0.15.112] — 2026-08-03 — *Neese's Cheetah*

### Added: Gamma-point phonons and zero-point energy on the Gaussian (BIPOLE) route (2026-08-03)

`vibeqc.basis_optimization.phonons` gives the cohesive-energy pipeline a
ZPE on the same BIPOLE route its single point and its relaxation already
ride. `VibeQcEngine` now declares the `zero_point` capability, so
`CohesivePipeline(..., zero_point=True)` produces `zero_point_applied=True`
instead of recording a skipped stage.

**The Hessian is built from total energies, not from forces**, and that is
the design decision worth stating. The roadmap assumed finite-difference
phonons on the *analytic* BIPOLE force; that premise does not hold --
`bipole_optimize`'s own docstring says the analytic BIPOLE gradient is a
research-preview surface and that finite differences of the energy are the
production force path. So the production force is itself a finite
difference, and differencing it again would stack two FD layers at ~36N^2
SCFs. Central differences of the energy are one differencing layer resting
only on a quantity correct by construction, at `18 N^2 + 1` SCFs (73 for a
2-atom primitive cell). `estimate_scf_count` reports the budget before a
run starts, because it grows quadratically.
`hessian_mode="analytic_force"` offers the `6N` analytic-gradient route
behind a warning, for research on that gradient only.

Three conventions, all recorded on the result rather than assumed:

* **No acoustic sum rule by default.** The Gamma acoustic modes are zero
  in exact arithmetic, so their residual is the calculation's noise floor;
  imposing the ASR silently would make it unmeasurable. `asr="rowsum"` /
  `"project"` impose it and `GammaPhonons.asr` says which you got.
* **Acoustic modes are found by projection onto the mass-weighted
  translation subspace**, not by taking the three lowest frequencies --
  which is wrong exactly when it matters, since a genuinely imaginary
  optical mode sorts below a noisy acoustic residual.
* **Imaginary modes are counted, not discarded**, matching
  `vibeqc.thermo`'s `n_imaginary_modes_excluded`. ZPE is positive and the
  pipeline subtracts it, because a vibrating solid is less bound.

Gamma-only ZPE is an approximation for a solid (one q-point, no acoustic
dispersion) and is labelled as such in the result detail and the user
guide. Cross-route validation against `periodic_gapw_phonon` is driven by
`examples/basisset_dev/gamma_phonon_gate.py`; see
`handovers/HANDOVER_BASISOPT.md` § M1 for its current status.

### Fixed: `VibeQcEngine.relax` passed a raw `(n,n,n)` tuple as its k-mesh (2026-08-03)

`vibeqc.kpoints.as_bloch_kmesh` converts a `KPoints` builder and passes
anything else through unchanged, so `relax` handed a plain tuple to
`relax_full`, which fails on `tuple.kpoints` deep inside the BIPOLE driver
and surfaced as a generic `relax_error`. The engine now normalises through
the periodic runner's own `_runner_bloch_kmesh`, which is what
`crystal_energy` already used -- so the relaxation, the single point and
the phonons cannot sample different meshes. The existing test asserted
`tuple(kmesh) == (2,2,2)`, i.e. it pinned the bug.

### Fixed: periodic runs cited Pulay DIIS for an accelerator they never used (2026-08-03)

`run_periodic_job(..., density_mixer="anderson", density_mixer_kerker=True)`
attributed the wrong convergence method. On H2/STO-3G at kmesh (2,1,1) the
`.references` sidecar carried **4 Pulay/DIIS entries and 0 Anderson or
Kerker entries** — citing a method the run did not perform, while the two
it did perform went uncited. That is the surface users paste into a
paper's Methods section.

Root cause: `CitationDatabase.assemble(...)` takes an `scf_accelerator`
argument that defaults to `"diis"`, and the periodic runner never passed
it. The routes themselves were correct and already pointed at the right
papers — Anderson 1965 (doi:10.1145/321296.321305), Broyden 1965, Johnson
1988, Eyert 1996 (doi:10.1006/jcph.1996.0059), Kerker 1981
(doi:10.1103/PhysRevB.23.3082) — they were simply never reached.

`assemble` takes ONE accelerator key while a periodic run applies a
density mixer and, optionally, the Kerker preconditioner, so the
combination is expressed as composed route keys (`anderson_kerker`,
`broyden_kerker`) in `database.toml` rather than by widening `assemble`'s
signature: routes are the implementing chat's surface (§ 8), `registry.py`
is the IO chat's (§ 16).

The default path is unchanged — a run with no mixer still cites DIIS and
nothing else. Post-fix the Anderson+Kerker run cites 4 Anderson/Kerker
entries and 0 DIIS.

Same class as GPW-GAPW-GILAT-SILENTLY-IGNORED, in the opposite direction:
there a citation fired for a method that was not used; here the method ran
and a different one got the credit.

### Investigated: the MDF dense-core divergence is the linear-dependence threshold (2026-08-03)

No behaviour change; this records a cause and refutes two earlier guesses,
so the next attempt does not re-walk them.

The fenced MDF dense-core class (MgO primitive FCC, +5e5 Ha) diverges
because `gdf_linear_dep_threshold` keeps a shelf of near-null eigenvectors
of the PW-dressed metric, whose `1/sqrt(lambda)` amplification in the
Eq. 19 orthogonalisation IS the divergence. Sweeping it against the PySCF
MDF oracle `-271.0499046`, at a 28-bohr cutoff and `mdf_ke_cutoff=40`:
1e-9 (the default) gives -62874 non-converged; 1e-7 gives -338.199;
1e-5 gives -275.325; 1e-3 gives **-271.146**; 1e-2 gives -271.129. This is
the failure Sun, Berkelbach, McClain and Chan (2017) Sec. II B warns
about: projecting the plane waves out of the Gaussians leaves a highly
singular matrix whose small eigenvectors must be discarded.

**Two hypotheses are refuted, both previously recorded in the tree.**
(1) "MDF inherits the compcell tight-ionic instability" -- superseded last
pass by the lattice-enumeration defect. (2) "the remaining cause is the
compensated-basis rcut" -- refuted here: at a raw 28-bohr cutoff the
metric is fully positive semi-definite (+6.4e-12, residue 6e-15) and MDF
is still -6.3e+04 Ha, with the energy barely moving across cutoffs
20/24/28. The lattice cutoff is not the blocker.

**The fence stays up**, because the threshold makes this class
non-divergent rather than accurate: the residual at the safe value is
96 mHa. `gdf_linear_dep_threshold` is also shared with compcell and the
bare builders, so moving the default needs an envelope sweep over their
pinned cases. Measured safety on the validated Ne/10-bohr gate (0.14 mHa
PySCF parity): 1e-3 moves it by only 0.067 mHa, but 1e-2 moves it by
0.9 mHa and would break it, so 1e-3 is the sweet spot. Callers who want
the dense-core route today can pass `gdf_linear_dep_threshold=1e-3`
knowingly.

Recorded alongside: `precision=1e-8` does not deliver 1e-8 in the
compensated metric (residues 2.4e-07 MgO, 7.1e-06 LiH rocksalt, 1.9e-08
H2 box at the auto rcut), essentially independent of the compensating
exponent -- consistent with accumulation over the ~R^3 lattice terms.
Since that residue sits above the threshold being divided by, tying the
two together is the likely principled rule.

### Added: complete-PNO-space extrapolation, and the measurement that says not to route it yet (2026-08-03)

The open PNO-truncation-correction item asked for something that could fix
both over- and under-correlation, since the truncation error is not
sign-definite (H2O/def2-SVP under-correlates by `+158` µHa at `TCutPNO=1e-7`
where N2 over-correlates by `-965` µHa), which is why the earlier additive
tail estimate could not work: it carries one sign.

The literature answer sidesteps the sign question by extrapolating from *two*
thresholds rather than correcting one. `vibeqc.dlpno.pno_extrapolation`
implements Altun, Neese and Bistoni, *J. Chem. Theory Comput.* **16**, 6142
(2020), Eqs. (1) to (4): `E = E^X + F (E^Y − E^X)`, with `X = −log10(TCutPNO)`
and the paper's recommended flat `F = 1.5`.

The algebra is pinned against the paper's **own published fit constants**
(`E = −1.78656` E_h, `A = 84.92`, `β = 5.55`, benzene dimer, Figure 1): the
analytic Eq. (3) factor recovers that limit to machine precision, from inputs
that are themselves `+11.2` and `+4.1` mE_h off. A regression there means
drift from the paper, not from a locally invented reference.

**But it is deliberately not routed, because vibe-qc does not satisfy its
precondition.** Eq. (1) assumes smooth monotone convergence in `X`; the
paper's fit has `R² = 1.000`. `run_local_dlpno_ccsd` does not converge that
way. Error against its own full-PNO-space energy, def2-SVP, in µHa:

| X | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 | 9 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| H2O | −3662 | −867 | +158 | +195 | +120 |
| N2 | −4657 | +198 | −964 | +536 | +187 |

The sign flips repeatedly across `X = 5..8`, exactly the window a 5/6 or 6/7
extrapolation uses, so the scheme extrapolates noise rather than a trend. On
real runs it lands *further* from the limit than its own tighter input: for
H2O 6/7 the raw `E^7` error is `+158` µHa and the extrapolate is `+916` µHa.

So the useful result here is a redirection: the blocker on this item is not
the choice of correction scheme, it is that the local solver's PNO
convergence is not smooth. A slow-marked characterisation test carries the
live reproducer and says explicitly that if it ever fails because convergence
became monotone, the right response is to re-evaluate routing rather than
relax the assertion.

`altun2020extrapolation` lands in the citation database in the same merge, and
the module names its own citation key so any future route can surface it.

### Fixed: periodic aux 2c/3c lattice sums enumerated the wrong set of images (2026-08-03)

A two-centre lattice sum runs over translations `g` of the ket centre, and
whether a term matters is set by the physical separation `|R_P - R_Q - g|`.
The contributing translations therefore form a ball centred on the
**intra-cell offset**, not on the origin. `compute_2c_eri_lattice` and
`compute_3c_eri_lattice` bounded `|g| <= R_cut` and then computed every
shell pair at that `g`, so they both missed translations that bring a
distant pair into range and visited ones that do not, asymmetrically
between the two pair orderings. Same class as the point-charge Ewald fix
of 2026-08-01.

Two exact invariants caught it, measured on MgO primitive FCC /
def2-svp-jk (intra-cell offset 6.89 bohr): the compensated Coulomb
metric is a Gram matrix and so must be positive semi-definite, but had a
**-5.4e-05** eigenvalue against a largest of 20.8; and translating one
atom by a lattice vector describes the identical crystal, but moved it by
**7.2e-02**. Both are now at round-off (invariance **1.2e-14**).

The kernels now enumerate exactly `{(pair, g) : |R_P - R_Q - g| <=
R_cut}`. The two `*_gradient_weighted` partners and the cell-resolved
`*_blocks` variants were changed in the same pass, so the analytic
gradient keeps differentiating the sum the energy builds and summing the
blocks still reproduces the Gamma result. Cost is unchanged in the
physically-required engine-call count: the padded cell list is filtered
back down to the true pair set.

**Blast radius is near zero.** Any cell whose atoms sit at zero offset
(single-atom cells, and every vacuum-box fixture) was already correct and
is bit-unchanged; that is also why no existing test caught this. MgO on
the rsgdf route is likewise unchanged to the digit.

This was found while root-causing the fenced MDF dense-core divergence,
whose recorded cause ("MDF inherits the compcell tight-ionic
instability") was a hypothesis. **The MDF fence stays up**: the fix is
necessary but not sufficient, and MgO Γ MDF still lands at +4.7e+05 Ha.
The remaining cause is now localised to a truncation problem rather than
an enumeration one -- the metric is positive semi-definite from a
~24-bohr cutoff but `pyscf_auto` picks 15.5 bohr for a compensated
basis, because it estimates decay per Gaussian primitive and a
compensated function's decay comes from multipole cancellation between
two comparable pieces. That is recorded in the fence docstring and as
the next increment.

### Fixed: the Ewald-split grid backend converged 14.5 mHa away from its own reference (2026-08-03)

`VIBEQC_J_EWALD3D_BACKEND=grid` exists to cross-check the `analytic_ft`
default, and disagreed with it by 1.454e-02 Ha on H2/STO-3G in a 12-bohr
box at omega=0.5 -- not discretisation (the gap was flat in the grid
spacing) and not the recent tied-lattice-sum fix (bit-identical across
it).

Root cause: `solve_poisson_erf_screened` pins the WHOLE reciprocal-space
G=0 component of V to zero. The erf kernel transforms as
`4 pi/G^2 - pi/omega^2 + O(G^2)`, so pinning is right for the divergent
`4 pi/G^2` (cancelled by the neutralising background) but also discards
the FINITE `-pi/omega^2`. That omission is a constant potential, hence a
multiple of the overlap in J, and the composed identity
`J_SR + J_LR = J_full` failed by exactly `pi Q^2 / (2 omega^2 V_cell)` --
reproducing the measured ladder +9.089e-2 / +2.968e-2 / +1.454e-2 /
+5.681e-3 Ha at omega = 0.20 / 0.35 / 0.50 / 0.80 (exactly omega^-2), and
verified against the closed form across two cell volumes and two electron
counts.

Restoring the term closes the identity to machine precision (7.7e-14 Ha on
H2) and takes the backend disagreement from 1.454e-02 to 5.3e-08 Ha. The
restoration is OPT-IN (`restore_g0_finite_part=`) on
`build_j_long_range` / `build_j_long_range_periodic`, and passed by the
three composition sites; the default keeps the documented pinned gauge,
because `J_LR` alone is a legitimate object in it and only there does
`J_LR -> 0` as `omega -> 0`. `ewald_j.py`'s "G=0 gauge" section documented
this offset as an accepted property -- it now carries the closed form.

Also improves, without closing, the forced-grid path below three
dimensions (`ewald_3d_j_blocks` forces `backend="grid"` for `dim != 3`):
on an H2 chain the omega-spread of the composed J -- which must be zero,
since `J_full` is omega-independent -- falls from 1.513e-01 to 8.901e-03.
The residual is expected, since the 3D `pi/omega^2` form is not the right
G=0 constant for a wire with vacuum in two directions; the low-D gauge
remains open.
_No unreleased changes yet. Add new entries directly below this line,
above the version header — do not edit inside a tagged section._

## [v0.15.111] - 2026-08-03 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Fixed: the CCM d=1 wire route never applied the libint Y_lm convention, so every l > 0 AO was wrong (2026-08-03)

`ao_pair_fourier_transform` returns the AO-pair transform in the raw
real-solid-harmonic convention: `rho(G=0)` equals the overlap for `l = 0`
but is scaled by `(2l+1)/(4 pi)` for `l >= 1` -- the Racah normalisation
relating `Y_lm` to the regular solid harmonic
`S_lm = sqrt(4 pi/(2l+1)) r^l Y_lm` (Helgaker, Jorgensen & Olsen,
*Molecular Electronic-Structure Theory*, SS 6.4.2). libint absorbs `Y_00`
into the s contraction coefficient but not `Y_lm` above it. The BIPOLE
stack undoes this via `_libint_ylm_correction_per_ao`; the CCM wire route
consumed the transform raw.

Because the factor is exactly 1.0 for an s-only basis, the omission was
structurally invisible: every H/He identity, both erf image-sum oracles
and the M3b/M5 gates are s-only. Everything with p or d functions -- all
carbon, all polyethylene -- was wrong by Hartrees per atom.

Diagnosed by bisection with *matched* exponents, which also overturns
what G-CCM-004 assumed (it blamed tight cores): He/6-31g has the tighter
core (e_max 38.42, l=0) and is correct at +0.038 Ha/atom against the
isolated cluster, while He/cc-pvdz (e_max 38.36, l=1) was -0.728. After
the fix each `l > 0` case lands in the H/He band and agrees with its
s-only sibling to ~7e-5 -- H2/6-31g** -0.124 -> +0.0167 (vs 6-31g
+0.0167), He/cc-pvdz -0.728 -> +0.0378 (vs 6-31g +0.0377) -- which is
how a basis-set-convergent quantity should behave.

Applied in one wrapper used by all three consumption sites
(`ccm_wire_cderi`, `wire_cderi_chunks`, and the streamed J/K builder);
`E_nn`'s reciprocal term is nuclear-only and needs none. Two new gates:
`rho(G=0) == S` for p- and d-containing bases (1e-12, plus the
`Tr[S^-1 rho(0)] == nbf` trace form), and an s-only bit-identity check
that makes this a pure convention fix -- all 28 pre-existing wire tests
are unchanged across it.

This does not by itself lift the `Z > 2` guard on `run_ccm_rhf_wire`:
the core-bearing absolute-energy criterion still has to be re-measured
end to end against the PySCF `dimension=1` oracle. See
`handovers/HANDOVER_OPEN_BUGS_V015.md`.

### Added: Thomas-Fermi screening estimate for the Kerker preconditioner (2026-08-03)

`vibeqc.kerker` gains `kerker_k0_thomas_fermi(n_electrons, cell_volume)`,
which derives the Kerker filter's screening wave-vector from the cell
instead of a hardcoded guess (the module defaulted to `k0 = 1.0`, the GDF
driver to `1.5`, neither with a physical basis).

Read from the defining paper rather than reconstructed: Kerker,
*Phys. Rev. B* **23**, 3082 (1981), doi:10.1103/PhysRevB.23.3082. Eq. (8)
takes the screening constant near the Thomas-Fermi value of the equivalent
homogeneous electron gas, `lambda ~ (4 k_F / pi)^{1/2}` with
`k_F = (3 pi^2 n)^{1/3}`.

Validated against the paper's own worked example rather than an
internally-chosen number: its Ca(001) seven-layer film is quoted at
`r_s = 3.3 a.u.` with "a screening length of 2 pi / lambda = 7.3 a.u."
(p. 3084). Feeding `n = 3 / (4 pi r_s^3)` through Eq. (8) returns
**7.302 a.u.** That round trip is what `tests/test_kerker.py` pins.

The same tests also pin the filter itself against the published limits:
Eq. (10) (`lambda^2 << |G|^2`, output density passes through) and Eq. (11)
(`lambda^2 >> |G|^2`, only a little mixed), plus `f = 1/2` at `|G| = lambda`
and `f(G=0) = 0` so the cell charge is never mixed.

Deliberately **not** made a default: it is the right starting point for a
free-electron-like metal and too aggressive for a gapped system, whose
physical screening length is far longer. No existing run changes.

### Fixed: the IBZ symmetry gate blamed the state for an under-converged overlap (2026-08-03)

Second diagnostic correction to `ibz_native` in as many days, same shape as
the non-symmorphic one: the refusal asserted a cause it had not
established.

A large wedge transport residual has at least two very different causes. It
can be a genuine variational symmetry break, which is what the message
claimed. But an under-converged Bloch overlap sum also produces one: `S(k)`
goes non-positive-definite, canonical orthogonalisation drops a
**k-dependent** number of vectors, and star-related k-points then live in
different-dimensional subspaces that no symmetry transport can match --
however symmetric the density is.

Measured on MgO rocksalt (3,3,3), same geometry, same mesh, symmorphic,
only the basis changed:

    sto-3g   min eig S(k) in [3.5e-01, 4.1e-01]   retained [14]     uniform
    6-31g    min eig S(k) in [-6.4e-07, 2.3e-05]  retained [20, 22] SPLIT

The 6-31g run failed the gate at 2.95e-01 with a perfectly good density.
The gate now inspects `S(k)` on failure and, when the retained count is
k-dependent, says so explicitly -- naming the overlap lattice sum and
pointing at the cutoff rather than sending the user to hunt for a
broken-symmetry SCF solution. When the overlap is healthy the original
symmetry-break wording is unchanged.

This is the same defect family the Bloch-overlap PSD work already tracks
(`handovers/HANDOVER_GPW_MULTIK_OVERLAP_PSD.md`, `bloch_overlap_cutoff_bohr`),
not an IBZ defect; no fix to the overlap itself is attempted here.

### Fixed: the long-range Hartree J image-summed its two AO factors independently (2026-08-03)

`build_j_long_range_periodic` formed
`J(g)_munu = dV sum_r chi_mu(r - R_g) V_LR(r) chi_nu(r)` with **both** AO
factors separately image-summed. With `V` lattice-periodic the all-space
integral folds to the cell with exactly **one** shared lattice sum:

    J(g)_munu = dV sum_R sum_r V(r) chi_mu(r - R - R_g) chi_nu(r - R)

Substituting `r -> r + R` on the old form shows the pair sitting at
separation `R_g + R' - R`, so everything with `R' != R` was deposited into
the *wrong* lattice block. The error is contamination BETWEEN blocks, not
a scale factor. Same defect class as the sibling density fix
(PERIODIC-DENSITY-GRID-DOUBLE-COUNTS-IMAGES, `2ef4c79fc`), which routed
this follow-up; the fix mirrors that one's tied-sum structure.

A compact cell is required to see it. On H2 in a roomy 12-bohr box the
cross terms are exponentially negligible and old and new agree to ~1e-7.
On a 5-bohr cell, `|J(g)|` per block at `ao_image_radius=2`:

    pre-fix    0.083368   0.056456   0.061218   0.072734   0.056311 ...
    post-fix   0.075565   0.003269   0.003269   0.000932   0.000932 ...

The far blocks were inflated 17-78x and, diagnostically, **did not decay
with distance at all**; post-fix they decay and symmetry-orbit partners
agree exactly.

Blast radius: the grid backend is a documented cross-check reachable via
`VIBEQC_J_EWALD3D_BACKEND=grid` and the public
`vibeqc.build_j_long_range_periodic` export, **plus** every `dim != 3`
caller of `ewald_3d_j_blocks`, which forces `backend="grid"` because the
analytic-FT kernel is 3D-only. No 3D default SCF route reaches it.

**Not closed by this fix:** the routed acceptance criterion asked that the
grid backend reproduce `analytic_ft` at (1,1,1). It does not, and the
tied sum is not why -- the two backends converge 14.5 mHa apart on H2 in a
12-bohr box, unchanged (bit-identical) before and after, and the gap
survives grid refinement from spacing 0.40 to 0.15. Filed separately as
GRID-BACKEND-CONVERGES-WRONG.

### Fixed: periodic density-on-grid double-counted lattice images (2026-08-03)

`evaluate_periodic_density_on_grid` image-summed its two AO factors
independently -- `sum_R chi_mu(r-R_g-R)` times `sum_R' chi_nu(r-R')` --
so the written density grew with `ao_image_radius` instead of converging
to the electron count. The periodic density carries exactly one lattice
sum, shared by both factors; equivalently, the image sum belongs on the
product density, not on each AO. On LiH rocksalt (STO-3G, Gamma GDF,
40^3) the integral read 0.2134 / 3.6161 / 3.9915 at radius 0 / 1 / 2
against a reference `sum_g tr(D(g) S(g))` of 2.7407 (the lattice set's
own trace, computed with the same `LatticeSumOptions` -- that equals the
physical electron count only for a converged set, so a truncated
Gamma-only set legitimately reads below N_elec) -- already 46 % over at
the shipped default and still climbing; the user-facing `.xsf` / `.cube`
artifacts on every periodic route inherited the error. A single-g
lattice set gives no immunity, since the double count comes from the two
independent AO image sums: the multi-k GAPW artifact, single-g and
assumed healthy, read 8.24 against an exact 3.82 and is fixed too. With the sums tied it reads 0.2134 / 2.7320 / 2.7407 and stays
there, and a vacuum-padded H2 box is exact at every radius. Cost is
unchanged: the same number of AO cell-evaluations, organised correctly.
`build_j_long_range_periodic` is deliberately left byte-for-byte
unchanged -- the same question applies to its matrix elements, but that
is a different quantity on a route this change has not validated, and it
is recorded as a follow-up rather than altered silently.

### Fixed: `ibz_native` blamed your density for its own missing glide phase (2026-08-02)

`ibz_native=True` on a **non-symmorphic** cell (silicon/diamond, Fd-3m) ran
several SCF iterations and then failed the symmetry gate with a relative
transport residual of 5.8e-01, reporting a "variational symmetry break" and
pointing the user at a broken-symmetry SCF solution. There was no such
solution: the density was fine and the transport was incomplete.

The wedge transport applies a per-atom lattice-shift Bloch phase, which
represents a point operation followed by a *lattice* translation. A
non-symmorphic operation carries a fractional translation `tau` (a glide or
screw), contributing a further `exp(-i k.tau)` that the representation never
built. Measured: Si diamond (Fd-3m, No. 227) has **24 of 48** operations
with a fractional translation; LiH rocksalt (Fm-3m, No. 225) has **0 of
48**, which is why every existing IBZ-native result -- all on symmorphic
cells -- is unaffected.

Non-symmorphic groups are now refused **up front**, before any SCF work,
naming the space group, the count of offending operations, and the fact
that this is an `ibz_native` limitation rather than a problem with the
user's density or convergence. `ibz_native` is opt-in and off by default, so
no shipped result changes; the full-BZ path has never had this restriction
and stays correct on these cells.

Found by running the flag on a system other than the rocksalt cells it was
developed against. Supporting non-symmorphic transport is left as a
deliberate follow-up rather than guessed at here.

### Fixed: GPW/GAPW accepted `bz_integration="gilat"`, dropped it, then cited it (2026-08-02)

`run_periodic_job(..., bz_integration="gilat")` was accepted by the GPW and
GAPW dispatch even though neither driver threads the flag into its
occupation logic, so the run silently used Fermi-Dirac while claiming
Gilat-Raubenheimer. On H2/STO-3G in a 12-bohr box at `(2,1,1)`, RKS/PBE, the
energy is **bitwise identical** with and without the flag
(`-1.152074940754` either way) -- the request never reached the occupations
-- while the `.out` recorded `smearing_method = fermi-dirac` and
`bz_integration = gilat` at once and the sidecars cited Gilat-Raubenheimer
1966 + Gilat 1972 (4 hits in `.references`, 5 in `.bibtex`) for numerics the
run never performed. That is a citation-integrity break (CLAUDE.md § 8), not
just an ergonomics wart: a paper written off such a run would cite a method
it did not use.

The flag now fails closed on those two routes, *before* the citation route
is registered, so a GR entry cannot fire for a backend that did not perform
GR. Refusal rather than honouring is deliberate -- threading GR occupations
into the GPW/GAPW drivers is a feature needing its own physics validation,
whereas the integrity break was live on a public route; honouring it there
remains open. GDF, RIJCOSX and BIPOLE are unaffected and still honour the
flag, and the no-flag GPW/GAPW path is bitwise unchanged. Reported by the
general-PBC chat as GPW-GAPW-GILAT-SILENTLY-IGNORED; its stale G-PBC-006
"remaining gates" entry is corrected in the same commit.

### Added: F_Cut and T_CutIter for the iterative (T1) (2026-08-01)

Milestone 4 of the Guo et al. (2018) Eq. (2) work: the paper's approximations
2 and 3, which are what make its iterative `(T)` cost 2 to 3 times `(T0)`
rather than 8. `f_cut` neglects the coupling between two triples carried by an
occupied Fock element below the threshold; `t_cut_iter` freezes a triple once
its energy stops moving between sweeps. Both default to `0.0`, so the
unapproximated scheme is what you get unless you ask otherwise, and both zero
thresholds are bit-identical to the previous behaviour.

`f_cut` has an exact structural limit that is pinned as a test: set it above
*every* off-diagonal occupied Fock element and no coupling survives, so
Eq. (2) degenerates into Eq. (3) and the result is bit-identical to the
semicanonical `(T0)`, reached in a single sweep.

**The `f_cut` error is not sign-definite, and that is worth knowing.** Every
other truncation in this stack is: dropping virtuals from a TNO domain can
only lose correlation, so those errors are always positive. `f_cut` drops
*couplings*, whose contributions carry either sign, so the energy can
overshoot the unapproximated reference and a recovery figure above 100% is
expected rather than a bug. Measured on two systems differing only in the
occupied-Fock seed, the signed deviation changes sign between them while
`|deviation|` is monotone in both. A tighter `f_cut` is never worse, but a
recovery percentage is not a bound. This corrected a test that had assumed
signed monotonicity by analogy with the TNO case.

`t_cut_iter` trades sweeps for accuracy monotonically: on the test system,
7 sweeps at `0`, then 4, 3 and 2 sweeps at `1e-4`, `1e-3` and `1e-2`, holding
99.995%, 99.988% and 99.976%.

The paper does not state whether `T_CutIter`'s increment is absolute or
relative. Its thresholds span `1e-1` to `1e-4`, which read as fractions, so
this implementation uses the **relative** increment and says so in the
docstring rather than silently choosing. Note also that this iteration is
Jacobi where the paper's is Gauss-Seidel: the freezing criterion transfers
unchanged, but sweep counts are not comparable to the paper's timings.

Nothing is wired into a route, so no existing behaviour changes.

### Fixed: the GPW multi-k -18 Ha is not the plane-wave grid; target value established (2026-08-02)

`HANDOVER_GPW_MULTIK_OVERLAP_PSD.md` left the Bloch-overlap production
switch unlanded because converging the lattice sum moved LiF/def2-SVP/
(2,2,2)/PBE from -107.25 Ha to -125.43 Ha unexplained, and queued a ~6 h
big-memory cutoff ladder to decide whether all-electron GPW simply fails
to resolve the F core. Evaluating the same GPW energy functional at one
fixed physical density (no SCF, no k-mesh, no metric) settles the grid
half in minutes: -106.883860 / -107.347426 / -107.387798 / -107.385236 at
150 / 300 / 600 / 1200 Ha. The functional converges to about **-107.3852
Ha**, the physical scale, and the whole discretisation error at 150 Ha is
0.50 Ha, not 18. The core-resolution hypothesis is refuted, the queued
cluster ladder is unnecessary, and the correct target for this cell is now
known (the handover was working from "about -107.6", itself from a run
with the broken metric).

The shift localises to `e_nuclear_attraction` (-22.881 Ha) against
`e_kinetic` (+4.307) -- density contracting onto the nuclei -- with the
V_ne *operator* identical in both arms (the driver builds it from its own
`EWALD_3D` options, which the patched lattice options never reach). Also
eliminated by measurement: the linear-dependence threshold (energy flat at
-125.4315 from 1e-4 to 1e-2) and the hardcoded 25-bohr Bloch-AO grid image
reach (moving it to 51.53 alongside the metric changes 0.04 Ha). Why the
SCF collapses is explicitly still open.

No production behaviour changed. Adds the regression pin
`test_fixed_density_gpw_functional_converges_to_physical_scale` and
corrects `GpwMultiKScfResult.density`'s docstring, which claimed the
Hartree-J and V_xc are built from that field: true only in the
molecular-limit regime, while a compact crystal uses the per-k Bloch
tables and the Gamma fold is then not consumable by the Gamma-folded
helpers (it yields 2.2e5 electrons / +8.9e7 Ha for a state the driver
reports at -125.4 Ha).
### Fixed: `kpoints=(N,N,N)` never said which Brillouin-zone mesh it meant (2026-08-02)

KPOINT-CONVENTION-UNPRINTED. The mesh-tuple form builds the
**Gamma-centred** mesh `{0, 1/N, ..., (N-1)/N}` per axis; ASE/GPAW read the
identical-looking argument as the **classical shifted** mesh, offset by
half a step. Neither the convention nor the resolved k-list appeared
anywhere in the `.out`, so a cross-code comparison could silently compare
different samplings — which is what happened, and it cost a full periodic
validation wave.

Found while fixing it: **vibe-qc reaches both conventions through the same
`kpoints=` argument.** `vibeqc.monkhorst_pack` (and the mesh tuple) is
always Gamma-centred; `KPoints.monkhorst_pack` applies the classical
auto-shift, so it is *shifted* at even N — agreeing with ASE/GPAW exactly
where the tuple form does not. The convention is therefore **measured from
the resolved k-list**, never inferred from the mesh: hardcoding one label
would have made the `.out` confidently wrong for the other caller, which
is worse than printing nothing. When it cannot be measured the line says
`unresolved` rather than guessing. `docs/user_guide/k_points.md` had
called the classical convention "vibe-qc's default" — true of `KPoints`,
false of the tuple form; corrected.

Measured while claiming it, and sharper than the original report: the two
conventions **agree exactly for odd N and are disjoint for even N**. For
odd N the half-step offset wraps onto the same lattice; for even N it lands
exactly between vibe-qc's points.

    mesh       n    shared with ASE
    (2,2,2)    8      0
    (3,3,3)   27     27      <- identical
    (4,4,4)   64      0
    (5,5,5)  125    125      <- identical
    (6,6,6)  216      0

That is what makes it a trap rather than a nuisance: a cross-code check
validated at (3,3,3) passes and says nothing about the (4,4,4) production
run beside it.

Every periodic route that reports a mesh now prints the convention and the
resolved k-point count beside it, and the full fractional k-list at
`VIBEQC_OUTPUT_LEVEL=verbose`, so the sampling is reconstructable from the
`.out` alone. The full-k semiempirical route, which reports a k-point count
rather than a mesh, states the same convention. `run_periodic_job` and
`monkhorst_pack` docstrings now name it too.

**No mesh changed.** This is provenance only — `kpoints=(N,N,N)` builds
exactly the set it built before, so no existing periodic number moves.

### Changed: every multi-k GDF driver now builds exchange in the occupied-index form (2026-08-02)

`run_krhf/krks/kuhf/kuks_periodic_gdf` (and the IBZ-native wedge path) join
the ROHF driver on the factored exchange contraction, at the maintainer's
direction. Exchange is the one O(n_k^2) term in a multi-k GDF SCF: it used to
contract the cderi cache against the nbf x nbf density at `2 naux nbf^3` per
k-pair, allocating a full `L.conj()` copy each time. It now contracts against
signed Gram factors of the density, whose rank is the occupied count, at
`2 naux nbf^2 n_occ` with no conjugate copy.

No driver plumbing changed: `_build_k_from_lpq_cache` and `_build_k_ibz_native`
keep their signatures and recover the factors from an eigendecomposition
internally, so every call site is untouched. The split is **signed**
(`D = sum_t s_t W_t W_t^H`, `s_t = +-1`), which makes it exact for any
Hermitian input rather than only for a positive semi-definite one -- a density
difference or a rough restart density is carried exactly, not projected onto
its positive part. A genuinely non-Hermitian input falls back to the
historical dense contraction verbatim, because `eigh` reads one triangle and
would silently symmetrise it.

**Nothing needed re-pinning.** The reassociation moves converged energies by
0 to 2.5e-11 Ha (measured on H2/sto-3g (2,1,1), H2/6-31g** (2,2,1), LiH
rocksalt/sto-3g and /6-31g (2,2,2), and a triplet UHF case), below every
pinned tolerance in the suite, with identical iteration counts.

**On the speedup, stated precisely.** The exchange build itself is 1.18x to
5.78x faster in situ on those fixtures, and 1.5x to 12.6x faster measured in
isolation across a size ladder from nbf=2 to nbf=160. End-to-end wall time on
those fixtures is *unchanged*, because at test-cell scale the exchange build
is ~0.0% of the run: the rsgdf cderi build dominates completely. The win is
therefore an investment in the regime where exchange dominates (production
meshes and realistic bases, per `HANDOVER_PERF_OPT.md`); **no production-scale
end-to-end speedup has been measured on this box, so none is claimed.** The
change is free at small sizes -- the worst measured ratio anywhere is 1.48x in
the builder's favour.

New tensor-level guards in `tests/test_periodic_k_gdf.py` pin the factored
result against the retained dense contraction (`_k_from_densities_dense`) for
the low-rank, indefinite and non-Hermitian cases, and pin that an aufbau
density really does factor to `n_occ` columns -- so a regression that quietly
restored the nbf^3 cost while staying correct would still fail.

### Fixed: the PySCF-style rcut estimator was short by sqrt(2) (2026-08-02)

`estimate_rcut_pyscf_per_shell` decayed with the single-shell exponent
`alpha` where it must decay with the pair reduced exponent `alpha/2`
(RCUT-PYSCF-MISPORT). What the cutoff truncates is a lattice sum over AO
*pairs*, and by the Gaussian product theorem two Gaussians of exponent
`alpha` separated by `R` overlap as `exp(-mu R^2)` with
`mu = alpha*alpha/(alpha+alpha) = alpha/2`; a pair therefore reaches
sqrt(2) further than the single-shell amplitude. Every radius the
estimator returned was short by that factor. This is the same correction
the `OVERLAP_PAIR` work above identified independently, now applied to the
shared estimator rather than worked around beside it.

The user-visible defect was that `precision` did not mean what it said. On
compcell H2 in a 12-bohr box at STO-3G / kmesh (2,1,1) the energy did not
move at all between `precision=1e-6` and `1e-12`, sitting **2.14e-06 Ha**
away from its own cutoff-converged limit; post-fix the 1e-8 default lands
on that limit to 1.8e-11 Ha. Cost on that case: rcut 9.15 -> 12.94 bohr,
wall +12%.

**Blast radius is narrow.** The default `rsgdf` route never calls this
estimator; only `compcell` and MDF reach it, and CCM sizes its own cutoff
via `RcutStrategy.FLAT`. Rows that move: the fused def2-svp-jk + chg
compcell basis goes 7.21 -> 10.20 bohr, and compcell energies gain the
~2e-06 Ha they were missing. Pinned by
`test_pyscf_rcut_uses_pair_reduced_exponent` (the exact sqrt(2) ratio, for
every alpha/L/coef rather than one basis's magic number) and
`test_pyscf_rcut_default_precision_is_cutoff_converged`.

Checked out-of-process against PySCF 2.13.1, whose `_estimate_rcut` does
open with `theta = alpha * .5`. The estimator is nonetheless still *not*
numerically equal to `cell.rcut` — H2 at precision 1e-8 gives a ratio of
0.77–0.78 across sto-3g / 6-31g / def2-svp, up from ~0.55 pre-fix. The
residual is PySCF's squared coefficient, its iterated polynomial factor
and its kinetic-operator penalty, none of which this closed form carries.
The docstrings that previously asserted outright equivalence now state the
measured ratio instead.

### Fixed: the wire azimuthal rule needs the two-object product bandwidth (2026-08-02)

Same-day correction to the offset-adaptive azimuthal quadrature added
yesterday. `required_n_ang` used the bandwidth of a *single* transverse
phase, `g * b_max`. The azimuthal integrand is a **product** of two
reciprocal objects -- two pair transforms in the four-center, a pair
transform against the bare nuclear structure factor in `V_ne`, `|S(G)|^2`
in `E_nn` -- and each carries its own translation phase, so the product's
bandwidth is `g (b_1 + b_2)`, bounded by `2 g b_max`. The rule was short
by up to 1.75x in the band where the pair-FT envelope is 1e-4..1e-7: a
~1e-5 accuracy leak, not the Ha-scale one (the retired flat `n_ang = 32`
was short where the envelope is still ~0.14, which is the +22.69 Ha/atom
figure).

Found by costing the polyethylene-shaped fixture properly rather than by
a test: the existing oracle gate uses a *single* off-axis atom, and both
rules pass it, because the H exponents there kill the envelope before the
shortfall bites. The new regression places two atoms antipodally about
the axis -- the worst case the `b_1 + b_2` bound exists for -- where the
retired rule leaves 7.5e-5 against the exact erf image-sum oracle and the
product rule leaves 1.9e-7.

Also measured while costing it, and recorded in the function: an
envelope-aware cap (skipping nodes where `e^{-g^2/4 p_max}` is already
negligible) is *not* worth it -- it costs slightly more (1.476x vs 1.435x
of the old flat grid), because `V_ne`'s nuclear structure factor has no
Gaussian envelope and sets the large-`g` bandwidth by itself.

### Fixed: `vq` self-update verification pinged the wrong daemon on multi-user hosts (2026-08-02)

`vq admin update`'s post-restart provenance check reported a stale
`source_sha` — and so failed restarts that had actually succeeded — whenever
the invoking process had `VQ_STATE_DIR` pointing at the multi-user root.

The self-update lane restarts the **user** daemon (`systemctl --user` / the
launchd user domain), and the check deliberately pinged the single-user
socket to match. But `rpc.socket_path(multi_user=False)` resolves through
`paths.state_root()`, which honours `$VQ_STATE_DIR` — and admins on a
multi-user host are documented to run admin verbs as
`VQ_STATE_DIR=/var/lib/vq vq admin ...` (`docs/state_file_audit.md`). The
"single-user" socket was therefore `/var/lib/vq/daemon.sock`: the root
system daemon, which the lane never restarted. The earlier site_b fix passed
`multi_user=False`, which expressed the intent but could not enforce it.

On site_e this presented as a frozen user daemon rather than a routing
fault: unlike site_b, site_e's root daemon *does* carry a `source_sha` (a
`/opt/vq` `SOURCE-SHA` marker pinned one release back), so verification
failed with a confident mismatch naming that commit — indistinguishable from
a user daemon stuck a release behind, and reproducible on every retry. The
user daemon was correct throughout.

`rpc.user_socket_path()` now resolves the per-user daemon explicitly: it
still honours an ordinary `$VQ_STATE_DIR` (relocated single-user roots and
the test fixtures depend on it), but when the override lands exactly on the
multi-user socket it falls back to the XDG default, which is provably not a
per-user daemon. `paths.xdg_state_root()` exposes that override-free root,
`rpc.call` gained a `socket_override`, and `rpc.ping_user_daemon()` is the
pinned entry point the verification uses. As a second gate,
`_verify_restarted_daemon` now rejects any envelope reporting `multi_user`
as a routing fault naming the remedy, instead of grading the root daemon's
provenance against the user daemon's expected SHA.

No recovery action is needed on affected hosts: nothing was written wrongly,
and the lane's `LAST OK=false` clears on the next successful update.

### Added: the iterative local (T1) runs in per-triple TNO domains (2026-08-01)

Milestone 2 of the spin-orbital generalization of Guo et al. (2018) Eq. (2).
It reduces each retained triple's virtual dimension, but the open-shell route
still builds dense global spin-orbital source tensors and therefore is not a
reduced-scaling triples phase. Milestones 1 and 3 ran in the full virtual space,
where every triple shares one basis and the inter-triple overlaps of Eq. (2)
are the identity. `iterative_t1_triples_correction` now accepts per-triple
semicanonical TNO domains: `W` is built inside each triple's own domain, and
the coupling between two triples is carried through
`S = V_T(ijk)^T V_T(ijl)`, applied to all three virtual indices of the
coupled amplitude.

Two invariance ratchets pin the `S` path, and the second is the one that
actually exercises it:

* handing every triple the full virtual space makes each overlap the
  identity, and the result is **bit-identical** to the full-space path, so the
  general code collapses exactly onto the special case it generalises;
* handing every triple a *rotated* full span, same space in a different basis,
  leaves the energy invariant to `1e-15`. Here the amplitudes really are
  carried between bases, so a wrong `S` contraction cannot hide.

Genuine truncation behaves as the earlier `(T0)`/`(T1)` TNO work predicted,
now reproduced independently by the iterative scheme. On a 4-occupied /
7-virtual system with TNO occupations spanning 0.011 to 0.070, the error grows
monotonically with the threshold and is signed (truncation only ever loses
correlation), the mean domain shrinks monotonically, and there are two
regimes: while every domain keeps at least three virtuals the degradation is
smooth, and once domains fall below three the correction goes to zero
identically rather than becoming small. `degenerate_tno_triples` reports that
boundary, so a threshold cannot silently truncate the correction out of
existence.

Still out of scope: the paper's `F_Cut` and `T_CutIter` approximations, and
public routing. Nothing is wired into a route, so no existing behaviour
changes.
### Fixed: multi-k GAPW on compact crystals - Hartree term ported to the Bloch fold (2026-08-01)

`run_periodic_rks_gapw_multi_k` (and `run_periodic_job(jk_method="gapw",
kpoints=...)`) routed only its XC by regime while always building the
Hartree term from the Gamma-folded density matrix `D(g=0)`. That is
correct only in the molecular limit, where cross-cell AO products
vanish; on a compact crystal it double-counts inter-cell density.
Measured on LiH rocksalt (primitive fcc, STO-3G, (2,2,2)): the folded
density integrates to **9.82 electrons instead of 4** (a 145% charge
error, worth 340 mHa in E_H at a fixed density), and the SCF fails to
converge 2.6 Ha *above* its own (1,1,1) result. The existing multi-k
pins were structurally blind because they all use `(1,1,1)`, which
collapses to the Gamma regime.

Fixed by splitting the GAPW Hartree by locality (`build_J_bloch`): the
smooth term's density now comes from the Bloch sum and its potential is
projected **per k** onto soft Bloch AOs, while the one-centre terms stay
k-independent on `D(g=0)` -- correct because the atomic regions are
non-overlapping by construction, so only same-cell image pairs reach
inside them. Against the PySCF-validated multi-k GDF route on LiH
rocksalt/LDA the route goes from non-convergent to **+17.7 mHa at
(2,2,2)** and +25.4 mHa at (3,3,3), grid-converged (N=32 vs N=48 agree
to 2e-8 Ha). That is the ordinary GAPW augmentation-accuracy class, not
sub-mHa parity; the residual is tracked under G-PBC-003. Follow-up
validation showed the agreement holds only near the equilibrium lattice
constant - expanded cells leave the SCF unconverged and cohesive
energies do not inherit the molecular error cancellation - filed as
MULTIK-GAPW-BLOCH-FAILS-ON-EXPANDED-CELLS. A fold-charge
guard (>1 % excess electrons, measured at SCF start) still covers the
paths the port does not reach; it is keyed on that measurement rather
than the `_multik_gpw_is_molecular_limit` flag, which calls He/8-bohr
(0.0 % fold error), He/6-bohr (+0.5 %) and LiH (+145 %) all "compact"
and would refuse two working configurations.

### Added: overlap-magnitude lattice-sum screening, and the GPW Bloch-metric defect it diagnoses (2026-08-02)

`vibeqc.lattice_screening` gains `RcutStrategy.OVERLAP_PAIR`,
`estimate_rcut_overlap_pair`, `estimate_rcut_amplitude`,
`atom_pair_span_bohr` and `bloch_overlap_cutoff_bohr`: a real-space cutoff
sized by bounding the largest primitive-pair overlap a truncation drops,
rather than by a flat radius. This is the criterion GPW prescribes for
itself (Lippert, Hutter and Parrinello 1997, Eq. 36) and the one CRYSTAL's
ITOL1 has used since Pisani and Dovesi 1980. Two corrections over the
existing PySCF-style estimator, both measured: a pair decays with the
Gaussian-product reduced exponent, and cells are selected on the lattice
vector while the quantity that must decay is the atom-pair separation.

The immediate reason it exists: **the multi-k GPW Bloch overlap
`S(k) = Σ_R exp(ik·R) S(R)` is not positive definite.** S(k) is the Gram
matrix of the Bloch orbitals, so it is positive semidefinite exactly when
that sum is complete; the drivers cut it at the bare `LatticeSumOptions`
default of 15 bohr, far inside the tail of a diffuse molecular basis on a
compact crystal, and the dropped tail enters with alternating phase away
from k = 0. Measured minimum eigenvalue over a Γ-centred (4,4,4) mesh at
def2-SVP: LiF −1.506940, MgO −0.198158, Si −0.155202. That is what produced
the 2026-08-02 validation wave's negative band gaps (MgO −0.619 eV, LiF
−0.215 eV), its 0.0017 eV silicon gap against a 1.1818 eV GPAW reference,
and its k-dependent retained-orbital counts. Counting the negative
directions at 15 bohr reproduces the wave's own retained-orbital histogram
exactly.

`bloch_overlap_cutoff_bohr` makes S(k) non-negative on all three crystals
and across five basis sets, and an end-to-end LiF run turns a −0.040 eV gap
into +5.88 eV. **It is deliberately not wired into the drivers in this
release**, so no number changes here: switching the production cutoff also
moves the total energy on all-electron compact cells by an amount this
release cannot explain, and breaks Γ-versus-multi-k parity invariants in the
GAPW stack. The symptom is pinned by tests, the fail-closed guard
(`_assert_bloch_overlap_psd`) is written and tested but unwired, and the
remaining work is in
[Archived `handovers/HANDOVER_GPW_MULTIK_OVERLAP_PSD.md`](https://vibe-qc.com/docs/).

Until it lands, multi-k GPW band structures on compact crystals with a
diffuse molecular basis are not trustworthy; use `jk_method="gdf"` or
`"bipole"`, or a basis designed for solids.

## [v0.15.110] - 2026-08-02 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Changed: the release gate runs once per cut (2026-08-02)

Version tags now reuse the successful exact-SHA `release-candidate/*`
evidence instead of launching a second identical 35-minute pipeline. The
native `build-test` job also runs only seven producer-coupled vibe-view files;
the dedicated viewer job retains the complete viewer inventory. The blocking
regression tier is again limited to the owned production sentinel, while all
demoted coverage remains in T2.

### Fixed: vibe-view release tests run as an unprivileged user (2026-08-02)

Both GitLab release-gate invocations of the viewer suite now drop privileges
before pytest while leaving dependency installation and artifact building with
the container's root user. This preserves the standalone uninstaller's strict
root/sudo refusal and makes its lifecycle tests exercise the intended user
contract. The shell guard now reads Bash's readonly `EUID` instead of resolving
`id` through caller-controlled `PATH`.

## [v0.15.109] - 2026-08-02 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Added: safe vibe-view uninstall and reinstall commands (2026-08-02)

`vibe-view/scripts/reinstall.sh` now rebuilds the standalone environment from
the current checkout through the existing failure-atomic replacement. The old
environment remains available until creation, installation, mode verification,
and optional Electron synchronization pass; `--desktop` refreshes the reviewed
runtime and source-backed desktop app without fetching Git.

`vibe-view/scripts/uninstall.sh` adds an idempotent dry-run-first removal path
for macOS and Linux. It requires an installer ownership marker or exact PEP 610
source metadata on a legacy auto-detected viewer path before deleting a
virtualenv, rejects symlinked and unsafe targets, and serializes lifecycle
changes with a Python-backed setup lock available on stock macOS and Linux. It
removes only a recognizable direct-download Electron runtime, and on macOS
rechecks source-app ownership under the shared Applications lock. npm-managed
runtimes, packaged/unknown apps, and apps owned by another checkout are left
untouched. The matching stale desktop-interpreter pointer is removed, but QVF
files, configuration, settings, recents, logs, window state, and the app-managed
data environment remain intact. `--keep-desktop` retains the Electron runtime
and source app.

### Added: vq install / update / reinstall / uninstall scripts (2026-08-02)

`vibe-queue/scripts/` gains the entry points its sibling subprojects already
had, in the same shape: a shared `_venv_helpers.sh`, `--dry-run` on every
command, `--help` extracted from the header block, and failure-atomic venv
replacement that restores the previous environment if creation, installation, or
verification fails.

Three things differ, because vq is not a library:

* **The daemon.** A vq environment usually has a daemon running out of it, and
  replacing it swaps code under a live process. Every mutating path detects
  one, refuses without `--restart-daemon`, and cycles it when asked. Detection
  is scoped to the venv being operated on via the pidfile's process executable
  — a daemon socket is per *state directory*, not per venv, so "a daemon
  answers" would otherwise mean rebuilding a scratch environment stops the
  user's real daemon.
* **Provenance.** Every install path restamps the `SOURCE-SHA` marker, since
  pip does not track it and daemon RPC reports it.
* **State is data.** `uninstall.sh` removes the environment and nothing else.
  The queue, workspaces, history, and host config survive unless you pass
  `--purge-state` / `--purge-config`, and a state purge is refused outright
  while queue entries remain unless you also pass `--force`. Systemd units,
  launchd plists, and `/opt/vq` are named at the end, never removed.

`reinstall.sh` is the one with no sibling precedent: it rebuilds the
environment from the checkout *without* moving the checkout, for when the
environment is the suspect rather than the code. `--keep-venv` reinstalls the
package in place instead.

Root-owned `/opt/vq` targets are refused by all four, pointing at the
multi-user deployment doc.

### Fixed: a `SOURCE-SHA` marker can no longer outlive the code it labels (2026-08-02)

`vq`'s daemon RPC reports the exact source commit a helper is running, and
scheduler-compat gates believe it. Two independent paths could report a commit
that had nothing to do with the bytes in memory, and both presented as a frozen
SHA that survived reinstalls, restarts, and a correct checkout — site_e,
2026-08-02, three identical failures across two hours.

**The marker.** `SOURCE-SHA` is a literal file written into the installed
package directory *after* `pip install`, so it is absent from the wheel's
`RECORD`. pip removes only files it tracks, so an upgrade leaves the previous
marker orphaned inside the *new* package directory and the new code reports the
*previous* commit indefinitely. Nothing bound the two: `source_tree_sha256()`
excludes both provenance markers from its digest (correctly — a digest must not
cover its own output), which left a stale marker indistinguishable from a
correct one.

`write_source_sha_marker` now records that digest *in* the marker, and
`read_source_sha_marker` returns `None` when it no longer matches the package
beside it. A stale marker reads as "no marker installed" — fail-closed, naming
a real remedy — instead of confidently naming an absent commit. `vq source-sha`
distinguishes the two cases in its error, because "missing" and "stale" have
different fixes.

Markers without the digest line are **trusted unchanged**. Every helper
deployed to date carries that shape, and `vq source-sha` gates whole scheduler
lanes; rejecting them would fail the fleet at once. Write side strict, read side
tolerant.

**The checkout.** `current_source_sha` runs `git rev-parse HEAD` anchored at the
installed package directory, and git discovers repositories by walking *up* — so
a non-editable install that merely sits inside some unrelated work tree answered
with that tree's HEAD. Root-owned `/opt/vq/venv` installs are deliberately
non-editable, making them exactly the shape that hits this. Such a value is
stable, wrong, and absent from every file under vq's state, config, and package
directories, so grepping those cannot find it.

`current_source_sha(..., require_tracked=True)` now demands that the anchor is
actually tracked by the repository git found. Daemon RPC prefers, in order: a
checkout that tracks the running file, the installed marker, then an enclosing
checkout as a last resort. That last rung is kept deliberately — dropping it
would report *no* identity on hosts that report fine today, failing gates that
currently pass. This tightens precedence, never availability.

Neither change closes the runbook's ordering trap (`--write-marker` run before
that host's checkout reaches the pin stamps a pin onto an honestly-installed
older build, and is self-consistent); `docs/fleet_update_runbook.md` documents
it and now says plainly that the three-step refresh is not optional in parts.

### Added: open-shell Gilat integration on the public BIPOLE route (2026-08-02)

`run_periodic_job(..., method="UHF"/"UKS", jk_method="bipole",
bz_integration="gilat")` now reaches the existing per-spin
Gilat-Raubenheimer occupation kernel on full and symmetry-reduced
Monkhorst-Pack meshes. The direct `run_pbc_bipole_uhf` and
`run_pbc_bipole_uks` entry points expose the same selector. Alpha and beta
eigenvalue fields are integrated independently at their fixed populations
with single-spin degeneracy, zero entropy, and the fractional-density path
used consistently for density rebuilding and Pulay commutators. Positive
finite-temperature smearing combined with Gilat integration fails closed.

No existing energy, default, Ewald/exchange convention, or XC quadrature
changes. On the gapped H/STO-3G `(2,1,1)` doublet probe the new UHF and
UKS/LDA routes converge in two iterations to `-0.4666424077023147 Ha` and
`-0.4356612432939519 Ha`, respectively, bit-identical to their BIPOLE Aufbau
twins at reported precision (`0.0 Ha` difference). Existing validation rows
are not superseded; this makes a previously gated capability reachable.
Sharp-T=0 Gilat-driven metallic SCF remains outside the supported convergence
surface: use smearing for the metallic SCF and Gilat for post-SCF integration.

### Fixed: unified native MSINDO preserves the requested geometry (2026-08-02)

The common molecular `run_native_energy` facade converted vibe-qc's
bohr-valued `Molecule` coordinates to Angstrom with the current CODATA
constant, then the native MSINDO engine converted them back with MSINDO's
pinned 1986-CODATA convention. That mixed round trip scaled every facade
geometry by `0.999999928007109` before evaluating either the INDO or NDDO
Hamiltonian.

The facade now uses the exact reciprocal of the engine's existing conversion,
so the geometry is preserved. This changes only unified native-facade MSINDO
and MSINDO-NDDO energies; the ordinary `run_job`, direct MSINDO, periodic CCM,
parameters, equations, and SCF behavior are unchanged. For H2 at 1.4 bohr,
the facade INDO total changes by `-4.349915983e-10 Ha` and the NDDO total by
`+1.233010805e-9 Ha`. Validation rows obtained through `run_native_energy`
should be regenerated; other MSINDO rows are not superseded.
### Fixed: periodic ROKS preserves a degenerate one-electron shell (2026-08-02)

The multi-k BIPOLE ROKS driver selected its singly occupied orbital by the
alpha Fock, but then forced one arbitrary member of an exactly degenerate
alpha-energy shell to occupation 1. Subsequent density folds converted every
positive occupation back to 1, and the effective-Fock build had no explicit
open-space projector. Symmetry-equivalent frontier orbitals could therefore
exchange roles while the energy was already flat, leaving the commutator to
settle over tens to hundreds of extra iterations.

For the bounded one-open-electron case, an exactly degenerate alpha-energy
group is now locked as one Roothaan open shell. Its electron is distributed
uniformly (`f = 1/g` for a `g`-fold shell), fractional spin densities survive
the k-to-real-space fold, and the effective Fock uses the explicit closed and
open projectors. Fixed fractional occupations are the zero-temperature
symmetry ensemble, not finite-temperature smearing; metallic global filling
and multiple partially occupied open shells remain out of scope.

Li/PBE/STO-3G in a 6-bohr cubic cell on the `(2,2,1)` mesh now converges in 6
iterations at the unchanged `1e-9 Ha` energy and `1e-6` commutator gates,
instead of 87 iterations, with the affected twofold shell occupied `0.5/0.5`.
Its energy changes from `-7.391462335228043 Ha` to
`-7.390588217162255 Ha`, a `+0.874118 mHa` correction. This numerical change
