affects multi-k BIPOLE ROKS only when its single open electron selects an
exactly degenerate shell; nondegenerate ROKS and every ROHF route retain
integer occupations. Validation rows for that degenerate periodic ROKS case
are superseded.
### Fixed: MSINDO now uses its reference-derived Bohr convention (2026-08-02)

MSINDO recomputes its geometry conversion from separately rounded 1986 CODATA
constituent literals in `const.f`, giving `0.5291772575069162 Angstrom/bohr`
under the executable's REAL*8 convention. vibe-qc instead used
`0.529177249`, the separately tabulated 1986 CODATA Bohr radius. That relative
`1.6e-8` reference-convention mismatch shifted large electronic and core-core
contributions in opposite directions, allowing their cancellation to hide the
defect in exact-executable parity. This pins the parametrized reference
convention; it is not a claim that the executable's recomputed value is a more
accurate physical constant.

Python and C++ molecular MSINDO, CCM energy and gradients, CIS finite
differences, and GEPOL cavity construction now use the same reference-derived
constant. For the exact-release MgO(100) slab reproducer, the electronic and
Madelung-nuclear errors fall from `+1.413e-6` and `-1.380e-6 Ha` to below
`1e-9 Ha`; the total changes from `-66.4395926925366` to
`-66.4395927265675 Ha`. A tight-SCF oracle gives `-66.4395927266 Ha`.

The retained H-F-chain gradient discrepancy was not a force-formula defect.
Its frozen oracle used the reference executable's default `DELEN=1e-8` SCF
stop; tightening only that oracle input to `1e-14` changes its analytic
gradient to within `3.4e-9 Ha/bohr` of vibe-qc's exact fixed-Wigner-Seitz
energy derivative. No gradient equation, convergence threshold,
finite-difference default, damping, or Wigner-Seitz rule changes.

All MSINDO-family numerical rows generated through the old Angstrom conversion
are superseded at their geometry-sensitivity scale. The CCM MgO slab total and
decomposed reference components in particular are superseded by the values
above; method parameters and user inputs are unchanged.

### Fixed: molecular-limit GAPW HF defaults to the fit-free analytic one-centre Hartree path at Gamma (2026-08-02)

The Gamma GAPW one-centre default is now method-aware and regime-safe. With
`one_centre="auto"` (the public default), RHF and UHF select the fit-free
analytic-ERI hard-minus-soft Hartree augmentation when the caller declares
`molecular_limit=True` (or `gapw_molecular_limit=True` on
`run_periodic_job`). Without that declaration HF fails closed rather than
guessing from geometry or returning to the known-wrong block functional. RKS
and UKS retain the established block construction because a variationally
safe multi-atom XC augmentation is not yet available. Explicit `"block"`,
`"analytic"`, and `"projector"` selections remain available with their
existing gates; explicit analytic is the expert opt-in spelling of the same
molecular-limit assertion.

This closes the public H2O wrong-answer path. H2O/STO-3G in a 12-bohr cube
previously converged cleanly with the block construction to
`-83.8226256933 Ha`, `-8.859694 Ha` below the molecular RHF reference. The
same call with `molecular_limit=True` now selects the analytic construction
and lands `+11.499 mHa` from that reference. The literature-backed cause is in the
one-centre density construction: the block path keeps only the atom-owned AO
block, but the GAPW partition requires the total density inside each atomic
augmentation region, including off-centre orbital tails. The fit-free route
contracts exact hard and soft ERIs with charge-conserving compensators and
retains the Hartree identity `1/2 tr(D J) = E_H` to numerical precision, so
the SCF cannot exploit a fitted self-repulsion hole. Earlier default HF GAPW
results for bonded, core-bearing molecules should be regenerated.

The promotion is deliberately limited to declared molecular-limit,
single-Gamma HF. No numerical or geometry heuristic is used because the
existing volume and cross-cell-overlap classifiers cannot distinguish every
vacuum-padded molecule from an arbitrary dense supercell.
It does not validate the analytic augmentation for compact or dense crystals,
multi-k GAPW, or multi-atom DFT; use GDF or BIPOLE for those all-electron
regimes. Direct GAPW analytic gradient and stress entry points fail closed on
an analytic-mode result. High-level GAPW HF optimization, cell optimization,
and Hessian requests also fail closed rather than changing Hamiltonians. The
`VibeqcGAPW` ASE calculator instead uses full-SCF central finite differences
for forces in that mode. GAPW HF phonons require explicit block-mode opt-in;
DFT phonons retain their block default. Result objects and `.system` manifests
record both the resolved one-centre mode and whether the molecular-limit
envelope was declared.

### Added: public periodic ROHF/GDF dispatch (2026-08-02)

`run_periodic_job(method="ROHF", jk_method="gdf")` now reaches the existing
native `run_krohf_periodic_gdf` engine in 3D at default Gamma, explicit Gamma,
and full Monkhorst-Pack meshes. The public route preserves one restricted
spatial-orbital set, integer 2/1/0 occupations, exact spin-pure metadata, the
`exxdiv='ewald'` BvK exchange convention, native-GDF memory preflight, and the
standard output, manifest, Molden, and citation lifecycle. ROKS/GDF, smearing,
DFT+U, gradients and optimization, restarts, response, density/Fock mixing,
and BIPOLE-only controls remain fail closed.

No existing energy changes. For identical H/STO-3G Gamma inputs, the newly
reachable public route reproduces the standalone driver to less than
`1e-12 Ha`; existing standalone and other-backend validation rows are not
superseded. This is a public capability change only.

### Fixed: multi-k Ewald gradients now differentiate their SCF energy (2026-08-02)

The public 3D Ewald RHF/RKS multi-k gradient wrapper, and the corresponding
pure-DFT UKS wrapper, mixed corrected-Ewald orbital energies with
direct-truncated nuclear, attraction, Coulomb, and exchange derivatives. On
H2/STO-3G in a 20-Angstrom box this returned about `+0.02865 Ha/bohr` for
atom 0 instead of the same-mesh energy derivative near `-0.14857 Ha/bohr`,
an error of about `0.17722 Ha/bohr`.

Supported full Monkhorst-Pack meshes now reuse the energy-matched Ewald
derivative assembly, including the background, short-range exchange,
reciprocal exchange, and `G=0` terms. Plain RHF's deliberate molecular-
exchange single-Gamma branch receives its matching molecular exchange
derivative; RKS global hybrids and pure-DFT UKS retain corrected periodic
assembly. Explicit Ewald alphas reuse the corrected-exchange SCF's
alpha-resolved reciprocal cutoff across the derivative's Ewald components,
and result objects retain the effective lattice support selected after
truncation optimization. Symmetry-reduced meshes and explicit meshes that are
not equivalent to full uniform Monkhorst-Pack sampling fail closed until
gradient-side star unfolding is implemented. An explicit single Gamma point
is physically identical to the `(1,1,1)` mesh and remains accepted. Hybrid
and fractional-occupation UKS remain fail closed. Non-Ewald, slab, and
direct-truncated routes are unchanged.

The old regression also incorrectly required two finite k meshes to have
identical forces. Their independently converged energy derivatives differ by
`8.2685e-6 Ha/bohr` in this finite cell and approach one another as `1/L^3`;
each mesh is now tested against its own central finite difference. The H2
chain RHF bond derivative changes from `+/-0.000763624279` to
`-/+0.148518375057 Ha/bohr`, and the PBE/6-31G bond derivative changes from
`-/+0.082355587999` to `-/+0.082140867423 Ha/bohr`. Periodic RHF and hybrid
force validation rows produced by the old wrapper must be regenerated.

### Fixed: molecular XC quadrature no longer retains whole-grid AO tables (2026-08-01)

Molecular RKS and UKS previously evaluated AO values and derivatives for the
entire Becke grid before the first SCF iteration, then retained those
`n_grid x n_basis` tables while building density and Fock intermediates.
Analytic XC gradients repeated the same whole-grid allocation with AO
Hessians. The resulting peak grew as `n_grid * n_basis`: large def2-QZVPP
single points could fail memory preflight before doing any chemistry.

Energy, Fock, and analytic-gradient contractions now traverse the unchanged
grid in contiguous batches of at most 4,096 points. This is an exact regrouping
of Becke's weighted point sum: no point, weight, pruning rule, functional,
threshold, or default changes. VV10 keeps a two-pass path because its
correlation energy is a genuine double-grid integral: the full-grid density is
built first, all cross-batch pairs are evaluated once, and the global
potential is then projected through batched AO tables.

On the qc-input-library 15-atom S22 benzene-water r2SCAN/def2-QZVPP input (639
basis functions, 688,500 default product-grid points), the conservative `DFT
grid + chi` estimate changes from 29.67 GiB to 0.28 GiB. ROKS, TDDFT, and
explicit Newton/TRAH XC kernels remain dense and are still charged that way;
the conditional large-RKS TRAH retry now rechecks its dense peak before it can
start. Ordinary LDA, GGA, meta-GGA, and full-grid VV10 SCF values are preserved
to the numerical reassociation envelope.

### Changed: a scheduler submit now costs three remote round trips, not six (2026-08-01)

`SchedulerDispatcher.submit` opened six SSH/scp connections per job — `mkdir`,
scp the workspace tarball, untar, `rm` the tarball, write the job script,
`qsub` — and four of those were plumbing with no decision between them. At
2–5 s each on a busy login node that is what capped campaign dispatch, with
thousands of jobs pending.

The four setup steps now run as one `sh -c`, with the rendered job script piped
in on stdin, so the same connection that unpacks the workspace also writes
`job.pbs`. The per-job `mkdir` moves inside it; only the *jobs root* has to
pre-exist for the scp, and that is shared by every job on the host, so it is
created once per dispatcher rather than once per job. A submit with no
workspace to stage drops from three connections to two.

Deliberately **not** batching `qsub` across jobs. That is the other way to cut
round trips and it is unsafe here: `qsub` is pinned at zero retries precisely
because an ambiguous transport failure could duplicate a batch job, both
submit-id parsers are strictly single-id, and `_fail_dispatch` is per spec.
Collapsing one job's plumbing keeps every one of those properties — failure
attribution is unchanged, and a staging failure still lands exactly that spec
FAILED.

`RemoteRunner` gains `upload_file`, the primitive this needs: land a tarball
without unpacking it, so a single follow-up call can unpack, clean up and write
the script together.
### Fixed: molecular UKS now measures Pulay errors in the orthonormal basis (2026-08-02)

Molecular UKS formed the correct per-spin AO commutators but fed their raw,
basis-dependent Frobenius norms to both DIIS and `conv_tol_grad`. Pulay's
algorithm instead transforms each error as `X^T (F D S - S D F) X`, where
`X^T S X = I`, before building the residual metric. Ordinary nonorthogonal
bases could therefore inflate an already stationary UKS solution just above
the default gate. The shared Pulay solver also mixed a residual Gram block of
order `1e-12` with unit constraint entries. Its full-pivot rank decision then
changed as the residual shrank. The Gram block is now scale-normalized before
the bordered solve, an exact transformation that changes only the Lagrange
multiplier and leaves the mathematical extrapolation coefficients unchanged.

The archived B3LYP/SH radical/def2-SVP release-paper cell now converges in 10
iterations at the unchanged `1e-6` threshold instead of exhausting 120
iterations at `1.34215e-6`. Its final energy changes from the discarded
flat-tail value `-398.5689396505852 Ha` to `-398.5689396504567 Ha`, a
`+1.285e-10 Ha` change. PBE/OH/def2-SVP and PBE0/OH/def2-TZVP also recover in
22 and 47 iterations; their final energies move by `-5.38e-9 Ha` and
`-9.43e-8 Ha`, respectively, relative to their discarded 120-cycle tails.
This affects molecular UKS convergence traces and can change the final
stopping-cycle energy for every functional. The algebraically invariant
Pulay solve correction is shared by molecular and periodic DIIS consumers,
but energy expressions, grids, and thresholds are unchanged. Previously
failed open-shell validation rows whose only defect was the near-threshold
UKS residual floor are superseded; genuinely divergent rows, including
LDA/SH, are not reclassified by this fix.
### Fixed: direct MACE now preserves true slab periodicity (2026-08-02)

The direct periodic MACE wrapper previously set all three ASE periodic flags
whenever a cell was present. A genuine VibeQC `dim=2` slab was therefore
silently evaluated as a 3D periodic stack along its synthetic bookkeeping
axis. Direct energy/force evaluation now maps `dim=1`, `dim=2`, and `dim=3`
to the exact leading-axis ASE PBC masks.

`optimize_periodic_mace_positions` adds fixed-cell position relaxation with
frozen atom indices for wires, slabs, and bulk systems. It returns the relaxed
`PeriodicSystem`, convergence/force diagnostics, and model/runtime provenance,
and preserves the input dimension, lattice, charge, multiplicity, and atom
order. Slab stress and variable-cell relaxation now fail closed because the
non-periodic bookkeeping vector does not define a physical 3D volume.

Unregistered MACE keys, arbitrary URLs, local weights, and out-of-scope model
families now fail before backend import instead of passing through an
ASL-acknowledged generic loader. Molecular MACE output additionally records
the loader, device, dtype, and cache location. The materials registry now
pins the upstream 89-element table instead of treating it as unrestricted.
New examples and a website tutorial cover an explicitly acknowledged
MACE-OFF23 molecular-geometry handoff to DLPNO-CCSD(T), plus MACE-MPA-0
H2O/h-BN sheet relaxation followed by periodic PBE. The MACE and electronic
absolute energies remain incomparable; MACE selects the geometry only.

### Fixed: multi-k GDF T=0 Aufbau now has one Brillouin-zone Fermi level (2026-08-01)

Closed-shell native multi-k GDF documented global Brillouin-zone Aufbau but
silently filled a fixed band count independently at every k point when
`smearing_temperature=0`. The P15 Si/def2-SVP/PBE 6x6x6 release-paper run
therefore kept 14 occupied bands everywhere despite a reported
-0.080825-Ha indirect overlap, then stalled for 120 iterations with a
3e-3-to-8e-3 commutator.

The T=0 GDF path now selects the weighted globally lowest states under one
particle constraint and shares a boundary occupation across roundoff-equal
Fermi states. Gapped cells are bit-identical. Band-overlap closed-shell GDF
energies can change: on the archived P15 final Fock, 12 occupied states empty,
13 lower states fill, and two symmetry-equal Fermi-boundary states become
half-occupied. Those 27 occupation changes lower the occupied eigenvalue sum
by 0.0068673843 Ha per cell at exactly 28 electrons; the self-consistent
total-energy change awaits the ordinary release-loop rerun on the newly
memory-bounded streamed Ewald-J route. The convergence gate now verifies the
global occupations against the current Fock. KDIIS and analytic gradients
fail closed only for nonuniform or fractional T=0 global occupations because
their fixed-occupied-subspace / sharp-Fermi-surface response is not
implemented; ordinary EDIIS_DIIS/DIIS energies remain supported without
enabling damping, loosening thresholds, or silently turning on smearing.

### Fixed: r2SCAN-3c D4 now uses its refitted charge dependence (2026-08-01)

The r2SCAN-3c recipe already selected its published D4 damping constants and
`s9 = 2`, but it left the charge-scaling parameters at D4's general defaults
instead of the composite fit's `(beta, gamma) = (2, 1)`. On the sealed
water-dimer comparison, the D4 component changes from `-0.000338822689` to
`-0.000399206538 Ha`, a change of `-0.000060383849 Ha` (`-0.060383849 mHa`),
and now agrees with ORCA 6.1.1's printed `-0.000399198 Ha` to 9 nHa.

This changes r2SCAN-3c D4 components, composite total energies, and D4
gradients. Validation rows derived from those values, including the M06
r2SCAN-3c D4 and total rows, must be regenerated. The SCF and gCP components
are unchanged. Other D4 routes, including ordinary r2SCAN-D4 and PBE0-D4,
retain the general charge model and are numerically unchanged.

### Fixed: 2D screened hybrids now unfold symmetry-reduced k meshes (2026-08-01)

Multi-k RKS/UKS `SLAB_EWALD_2D` jobs with screened exact exchange
(`c_sr != 0`, including HSE06) previously skipped the Pisani/Dovesi
full-star density reconstruction on symmetry-reduced Monkhorst-Pack meshes.
The driver instead multiplied each irreducible representative density by its
star weight, which is not the orbit average required by the whole
Brillouin-zone density.

Both spin routes now unfold valid 2D stars before folding the real-space
density and fail closed when declared star coverage cannot be reconstructed.
The slab exchange operator keeps the same raw finite-cutoff convention as the
corresponding full mesh; this change is limited to the erroneous density fold.
On the sealed P4/mmm HeH2/STO-3G `[2,2,1]` HSE06 reproducer, the reduced-mesh
RKS and UKS totals move upward by about `18.906 mHa`, and reported screened
exchange moves upward by about `26.515 mHa`, into full-mesh parity within
`1.2e-9 Ha`. This supersedes reduced-mesh 2D screened-hybrid validation rows.
Full meshes, Gamma-only jobs, pure DFT, full-range exchange, explicit weighted
k-point lists, GDF/COSX routes, defaults, and convergence controls are
unchanged.

### Fixed: oblique k-star matching follows the native reciprocal basis (2026-08-01)

The symmetry-unfolding helper converted Cartesian k points to reciprocal
fractions by solving `B.T q = k`, although `PeriodicSystem` stores reciprocal
vectors as columns and native Monkhorst-Pack meshes construct `k = B q`.
Orthogonal lattices hid the transpose. Valid oblique 2D and 3D reduced meshes
could therefore fail star coverage and be rejected as inconsistent.

The inverse conversion now solves `B q = k`. A `[3,3,1]` oblique slab
regression pins all nine full-mesh members, five irreducible representatives,
time reversal, and direct-overlap transport to `1e-12`. This opens meshes that
previously failed closed; already accepted orthogonal meshes and numerical
results are unchanged.
### Added: vibe-view now has a standalone onboarding and importer workflow (2026-08-01)

`vibe-view demo`, `doctor`, and `formats` provide a producer-independent first
run, installation diagnostics, and an exact inventory of built-in, optional,
and third-party import capabilities. Project-authored examples ship inside the
Python package and can be copied without a vibe-qc checkout.

`vibe-view import` persistently converts individual loose files or recursively
discovered job-directory inputs into validated QVF archives with atomic writes,
collision-safe names, and overwrite protection. External codes can add formats
through the versioned `vibeview.importers` Python entry-point API; built-in
parsers retain precedence and a broken plugin cannot disable other formats.

The bundled demo and persistent imports publish through same-directory
temporary files, preserve restrictive access modes, and leave an existing file
untouched after validation, disk, forced-replacement, or racing-writer failure.
Browser directory scans are bounded, symlink-safe, and prune cache/venv trees;
recursive globs are rejected with guidance to use that safe scanner. The
authored demo archive is byte-reproducible across runs.

The macOS/Linux checkout installer now uses a regular local source install while
PEP 610 metadata keeps the source-only Electron companion discoverable.
`install.sh --force` and `update.sh --recreate-venv` retain a same-parent backup,
build the replacement at its final path, and restore the previous environment
after creation, pip, verification, or Electron failure. Default updates honor
the current branch's configured upstream instead of assuming `origin` and a
same-named branch, including renamed remotes and local tracking branches.

The packaging gate now builds and checks both wheel and source distribution,
smoke-tests the installed wheel from outside the checkout, records checksums,
and refuses to replace immutable same-version hosted-wheel bytes. Historical
versioned wheels remain available for desktop repair URLs. The install and
onboarding documentation now distinguishes the `vibeview` distribution from
the `vibe-view` command and describes browser, desktop, TUI, HPC, and
third-party producer routes without requiring vibe-qc.

### Fixed: Linux memory preflight now honors scheduler allocations (2026-08-01)

`available_memory_bytes()` previously returned psutil's host-wide available
RAM immediately, so a process inside a smaller Linux scheduler cgroup could
pass preflight and die during allocation. In the sealed reproducer, a job with
a 4 GiB PBS request estimated about 22.0 GiB, reported 91.3 GiB available, and
printed `Proceeding` before raising `std::bad_alloc` prior to the first SCF
iteration. A sibling 6 GiB request failed the same way with a 22.9 GiB
estimate and 90.6 GiB reported available.

The probe now bounds host availability by the remaining allowance from finite
cgroup v2 or legacy cgroup v1 memory limits, including tighter limits inherited
from parent cgroups. Those reproducer shapes now report less than their 4 or 6
GiB allocations, respectively, and abort before constructing the SCF driver.
This changes available-memory reports and preflight admission decisions for
cgroup-constrained Linux processes only. Memory estimates, batching, grids,
defaults, energies, and other numerical results are unchanged.

### Fixed: molecular DFT memory estimates now honor Lebedev grid orders (2026-08-01)

Molecular RKS/UKS and COSX preflight always charged the legacy product-grid
dimensions of the selected grid object, even when its angular scheme selected
a different bundled Lebedev tier. The estimate now uses the active Lebedev
point count; pruned grids conservatively charge their densest active tier.

For the sealed 13-atom, 619-function BH9 reproducer at 75 radial x Lebedev
order 29, the `DFT grid + chi` category changes from 22.07 GB to 10.89 GB and
the raw total from 23.53 GB to 12.35 GB. With the current 1.5x default
headroom, the reported total changes from 35.30 GB to 18.53 GB. Conversely,
order 47 now charges 770 angular points instead of 612, a 25.8% increase that
prevents an unsafe underestimate. This changes memory reports and preflight
admission decisions only; SCF grids, defaults, energies, and other numerical
results are unchanged.

### Fixed: an unpinned submit no longer dies when the runtime rolls (2026-08-01)

`vq submit --program NAME` captured a runtime pin at submit time **even when no
`--expected-sha` was given**, and dispatch enforced it. Any job queued across a
runtime roll then failed with `runtime pin mismatch before dispatch` — which is
precisely what an unpinned submit exists to survive. On a fleet rolling hourly
that is fatal, not annoying: all 123 of the campaign's bundle jobs died this
way when `vibeqc-release` rolled from `e56c6ee1de3a` to `574d0020604a` between
their submit and their dispatch tick, and they died again on every resubmit.

Three different things were landing in one field:

* an explicit `--expected-sha` — the operator naming a commit;
* a configured `[programs.NAME] expected_git_sha` — the site pinning its
  program;
* failing both, whatever `current_git_sha()` happened to return at submit.

The first two are **intent** and are still enforced, unchanged. The third is an
**observation**, and enforcing an observation is the bug. `ProgramRuntimePin`
gains `enforce_git_sha`, set `False` only for that auto-captured case: the SHA
is still recorded on the spec for provenance, but dispatch skips the equality
check and the job runs on whatever the runtime currently is — "the calculation
that is next shall always take the latest version".

Defaults `True`, so every explicitly pinned submit and every spec written
before this change behaves exactly as before. Provenance is unaffected either
way: the job's actual runtime is recorded in its `.system` manifest.

### Fixed: auto-cleanup no longer starves live-job reaping (2026-08-01)

Daemon auto-cleanup used to run synchronously at the end of every due
`iterate()` pass, including the same pass that had just dispatched a local
child. On a driver retaining roughly 20,000 queue specs, the cleanup scan could
occupy the main loop long after that child exited. The unreaped zombie kept its
spec falsely `running`, retained build exclusivity/dedup state, and made an
otherwise successful `vq build-env` look wedged.

Automatic retention now defers while any local, reattached, or scheduler job
is active and retries when the daemon is quiescent. Lifecycle reconciliation
therefore always gets the next poll; explicit operator `vq cleanup` remains
available while jobs run.

### Fixed: the BIPOLE `EXT EL-POLE` helper no longer returns a different Ewald component under that name (2026-08-01)

`compute_ext_el_pole_reciprocal_sum` returned `-3.7642513866 Ha` for the
sealed MgO/STO-3G CYC 0 density while documenting CRYSTAL's
`EXT EL-POLE = -528.6042534080 Ha` as its target. The discrepancy was not
the previously recorded AO-pair Fourier normalization defect: on current
main, the corrected zero-mode transform agrees with the libint overlap to
`9.2e-16`, and its density contraction is exactly the 20-electron count.

The implemented scalar is only the non-negative, alpha-dependent `K != 0`
reciprocal electron-electron Ewald contribution. CRYSTAL's named diagnostic
uses the Saunders shell-multipole
model minus point-multipole interactions inside a selected penetration zone;
the legacy implementation constructs no shell model and defines neither its
multipole order nor its `T2` penetration criterion. The old entry point now
fails closed with that requirement instead of returning a wrongly labelled
number. The valid scalar remains available as the explicitly
named `compute_electronic_reciprocal_ewald_energy` diagnostic. No production
SCF route called the retired helper, so the exact Ewald-J total-energy route,
spheropole, Fock matrices, and converged energies are unchanged. Regressions
pin `rho_hat(0) = sum_mn P_mn S_mn = N_e` for mixed s/p MgO, its
operator-energy consistency identity, and the fail-closed public surface; the
stale strict xfail has been removed.

The adjacent dipole helper is also explicit about what it computes:
`dipole_depolarization_surface_energy_spherical` requires neutral moments and
applies `2 pi |mu|^2 / (3 V)` for a spherical macroscopic sample independent
of primitive-cell metric. The historical `*_cubic` and `assume_cubic` API
names remain as compatibility wrappers; they no longer reject tetragonal or
skew cells or accept charged electron-only moments as a physical surface term.

### Fixed: dense-cell 3D Ewald cutoffs include shifted pair images (2026-08-01)

The 3D point-charge Ewald energy, gradient, and short-range potential used to
enumerate only translations with `|g| <= R_cut` before applying the physical
`|R_A - R_B + g| <= R_cut` filter. In a multi-atom cell, a basis displacement
can shift a translation from outside the first sphere into the second. Those
valid screened images were never visited, making finite-cutoff results depend
on the chosen unit-cell representative.

Each source-observer displacement is now reduced to a centered periodic
representative. A pair-complete integer translation box is derived from the
cutoff and the three interplanar spacings, while the physical pair-distance
filter remains unchanged.

For primitive MgO, the 18-bohr nuclear energy now agrees with the 80-bohr
result at the screening floor instead of differing by `2.11e-5 Ha`; the
corresponding gradient error falls from `2.57e-5 Ha/bohr` to the numerical
floor. Moving the oxygen by dozens of exact lattice vectors leaves the energy,
gradient, and point-charge potential invariant without expanding the search.
The 2D slab Ewald implementation is unchanged.

### Fixed: an untrackable scheduler spec no longer reserves capacity forever (2026-08-01)

A `reattach_failed` spec reserves a slot against `max_scheduler_jobs` because it
*may* still be live on the cluster. For a spec that kept its `scheduler_job_id`
that is correct and open-ended -- vq holds a handle, so `_reconcile_scheduler`
will reap it. For a spec with **no** id there is nothing to poll: the only
recovery is `recorded_job_id`, retried each tick, and a live job writes that
record before it runs anything. Surviving the window without one means vq will
never recover it, so reserving forever is not caution -- it is permanent
starvation.

Such a spec now stops reserving after
`SCHEDULER_UNTRACKABLE_RESERVATION_SECONDS` (15 minutes, many retry ticks, so a
slow or briefly unreachable cluster never trips it). The slot is released; the
spec is deliberately **not** reaped, because vq can prove only that it cannot
track the job, not that the job is dead. The row stays visible for an operator
or `vq cleanup` to resolve.

**This is not the whole of site_i's stuck-capacity problem.** Evidence gathered
the same day shows ~254 specs in `running` against 9 real PBS jobs, and the
sampled ones have real job ids, `Exit_status=0`, and PBS-confirmed `COMPLETE`
20+ minutes earlier -- so they are neither `reattach_failed` nor id-less, and
this change does not release them. The completion-detection/reap path for that
shape is a separate, larger defect, recorded as item 0 in
`handovers/HANDOVER_VQ_DEV.md`.

### Added: `--branch` / `--python` now apply to `--dir` and `--compressed` submits (2026-08-01)

Both flags used to raise for a directory or tarball payload — "put the
interpreter in the explicit command". That reads as a minor ergonomic
restriction and was not. On a scheduler host the interpreter is a per-host
pinned wrapper path, so obeying it meant hardcoding a cluster path into every
submit line, which is exactly the leak `[hosts.HOST.branches]` exists to
prevent.

Sites reached instead for `scheduler_program_hooks.NAME.command_wrapper`, the
one remaining mechanism that could inject a launcher. When site_i's wrapper was
removed on 2026-07-21 (it double-wrapped single-file submits), its `--dir`
submits silently lost their launcher and ran as bare `run.py` — the exit-127
class that `0f60d951d`'s pre-submit refusal was later added to catch. Roughly
2,300 campaign jobs were refused on site_i on 2026-08-01 for this reason.

The resolved interpreter is now prepended to the explicit command, so
`vq submit site_i -d ./sweep --program vibeqc-release --branch release -- run.py`
routes through site_i's pinned release wrapper with no cluster path in the submit
line. A payload that carries its own interpreter simply keeps not passing these
flags, exactly as before.

Six tests that pinned the old rejection were rewritten to pin the new
behaviour rather than deleted, so the change is covered from both the CLI and
the local/remote submit paths.
### Fixed: BIPOLE stops before SCF on critically truncated lattice folds (2026-08-01)

The corrected-gauge RHF/RKS/UHF/UKS BIPOLE drivers measured their Bloch
overlap-fold drift before SCF and labelled values above `1e-2` as
`UNRELIABLE`, with spurious metric states possible, but then continued into
the expensive direct two-electron build. The release-paper LiH/STO-3G Gamma
case reproduced `7.0985e-2` drift at the default 15-bohr cutoff: its preflight
and one-electron setup take 2.54 s on the matched local build, while its first
Fock build did not finish inside a 180-s local cap and the archived 30-bohr
attempt consumed more than 2.4 h without completing.

All four direct drivers now record the existing semantic warning and raise
before the first Fock build whenever the already-established critical
`drift > 1e-2` branch fires. The exception names both public cutoff controls
and retains the existing instruction to converge below `1e-4`. Moderate
`1e-4 < drift <= 1e-2` runs retain their truncation note and execute; folds at
or below `1e-4`, explicit legacy-gauge diagnostics, equations, gauges, SCF
thresholds, and defaults are unchanged. No accepted energy changes: cases
that previously entered SCF after declaring their support unreliable now
fail in preflight instead. For the archived LiH cell, 25 bohr is the first
sampled reliable point (`3.4031e-5` drift), versus `6.6250e-8` at its
unnecessarily costly 30-bohr probe.

### Fixed: Gamma-periodic GFN2 exposes its finite-temperature free energy (2026-08-01)

`PeriodicGFN2Result` no longer discards the Fermi-Dirac occupation entropy.
Its existing `.energy` remains the internal energy for compatibility, while
`.free_energy` now exposes the variational Mermin/Helmholtz potential
`A = E - T*S`. The result also carries the dimensionless electronic entropy,
Fermi level, and requested `k_B*T` in Hartree; at zero temperature entropy is
zero and `.free_energy == .energy` exactly. This follows the dual-field
contract already used by periodic k-point DFTB and the finite-temperature term
in Bannwarth et al., JCTC 2019, Eqs. 8 and 10.

This is a native Gamma-result bookkeeping fix. It does not enable smearing on
the public Gamma `run_periodic_job` route, select a temperature automatically,
promote finite-temperature gradients, or change periodic GFN2's experimental
status and broader external-`xtb` accuracy gates.

### Fixed: pure-DFT multi-k GDF no longer retains the all-cell/all-G Ewald-J tensor (2026-08-01)

The 3D true-multi-k RKS GDF path for pure functionals cached one complex
AO-pair Fourier-transform tensor with shape
`(n_cells, n_AO, n_AO, n_G)` before SCF. That allocation was 38.9 GiB for
the release-paper P15 Si/def2-SVP `(2,2,2)` / `(4,4,4)` inputs and 296.8 GiB
for the P10 conventional NaCl/def2-SVP `(4,4,4)` input, so both records failed
before their first iteration.

The driver now retains the fast pre-SCF cache only when its tensor plus one
similarly sized construction temporary fits a 4 GiB cache target. Larger
cases contract the same exact, `G = 0`-omitted Ewald Hartree J directly from
`D(k)` under the existing 512 MiB reciprocal-vector/output-cell batch target,
then Bloch-fold the completed cell blocks; the full tensor is never
materialised. Small and moderate jobs keep their existing cache reuse and
runtime. The Ewald gauge,
`VIBEQC_J_EWALD3D_KE` cutoff, functional and SCF defaults are unchanged;
Gamma, HF/hybrid cached-Lpq, `use_compcell=True`, lower-dimensional, and
diagnostic grid-backend routes are unchanged. When forced through the
streamed branch, the non-TRIM H2 `(3,1,1)` RKS/PBE total is `6.7e-15 Ha`
above the former route (same three-iteration fixed point), and fixed-density
J blocks agree within `7.9e-14 Ha`.

### Fixed: shared periodic nuclear gradients honor the 3D Ewald gauge (2026-08-01)

`nuclear_repulsion_gradient_per_cell` no longer falls through to the
truncated direct `1/r` derivative when `coulomb_method=EWALD_3D`. It now
constructs the same `EwaldOptions` as `nuclear_repulsion_per_cell`, including
the `nuclear_cutoff_bohr` to `real_cutoff_bohr` mapping, and differentiates
that Ewald energy. This repairs the nuclear term used by the generic Gamma and
multi-k periodic gradient assemblers without changing direct-truncated or
lower-dimensional behavior.

On the H2/12-bohr regression, the old helper differed from a finite difference
of its paired nuclear energy by `3.3900956e-3 Ha/bohr`; the matched Ewald
derivative agrees to `1.6e-11 Ha/bohr`. This change does not address the
separate dense-cell cutoff-convergence issue or claim that every electronic
term in the generic Ewald gradient assemblers is complete.

### Fixed: VQ-DRAIN-RPC — a drain status view that denied a live hold (2026-08-01)

`vq drain --status` reported "no drain" while `drain.json` held an active
`full_dispatch` hold, so `--release` / `--release-full` found nothing to
release and silently no-op'd. The operator could neither see nor clear a hold
that was still parking the fleet, and it misled a fleet updater's restore
verification.

`read_drain_state(via_rpc=True)` asked the daemon, then returned `None` on two
paths where it had simply failed to *interpret* the answer: a record it could
not validate, and any unexpected result type. Every caller reads `None` as
"nothing is draining". Meanwhile the daemon's own dispatch loop reads the file
directly (`via_rpc=False`), so it kept enforcing the hold — status and file
disagreed, and the file was the one with teeth.

An answer vq cannot read is a failure, not evidence of absence. Both paths now
fall back to the direct file read, exactly as `try_rpc_or_fallback` already
does for a dead socket, and log a warning naming the likely cause (client and
daemon running different vq versions). A daemon that explicitly answers "no
drain" stays authoritative — pinned by a test, so this cannot make a released
drain look active.

### Added: the iterative local (T1) now carries a screened triple list (2026-08-01)

Milestone 3 of the Guo et al. (2018) Eq. (2) work, and the one that carries
the point of it. `iterative_t1_triples_correction` accepts a
locality-screened `triple_list`, and Eq. (2)'s `l`-sums run over surviving
triples only, which is the paper's "only a subset of triples is considered".

This is the capability the canonical-rotation `(T1)` cannot have. That route
rotates the occupied indices into the canonical basis, where an LMO-based
screening decision no longer refers to the indices being dropped, which is why
the open-shell engine fails closed on any realised screening. The iterative
scheme never leaves the localised basis, so a screened list survives it.

Pinned by four new ratchets, the last of which is the substantive one:

* passing the complete list explicitly is bit-identical to not passing one;
* dropping a triple changes the answer, and by less than the whole;
* with a diagonal `f_oo`, a screened run is exactly `(T0)` over the subset, in
  one sweep;
* in a genuine **non-interacting two-fragment limit** (every integral,
  amplitude and occupied-Fock element mixing the fragments set to zero),
  screening all 18 of the 20 triples that span both fragments changes the
  energy **bit-for-bit not at all**. Those triples carry an identically zero
  `W`, so an exact method must be unchanged. This also pins that restricting
  the `l`-sums does not corrupt the surviving triples: if the coupling
  restriction leaked, the fragment amplitudes would shift and the difference
  would be nonzero.

Milestone 3 was taken before milestone 2 (real TNO overlaps `S`), reordering
the plan recorded earlier today, because the two are independent: screening
restricts the *occupied* triple list while `S` concerns the *virtual* space, so
screening is fully expressible at the full virtual space milestone 1 provides.
Still out of scope: `S` overlaps, the `F_Cut`/`T_CutIter` approximations, and
public routing. Nothing is wired into a route yet, so no existing behaviour
changes.

### Fixed: a helper rebuild no longer waits for running jobs it cannot touch (2026-08-01)

`vq admin update <scheduler-host>` refused to rebuild the vq **helper** while
any job was running on that host. On 2026-08-01 a paper-critical GPW
calculation, four hours into a twelve-hour budget, was **killed** to satisfy
that wait so v0.15.107 could land on site_i. Solid-state jobs can run for weeks,
so at the current release cadence one long job could block every subsequent
helper update indefinitely.

The wait was justified by a comment claiming the helper "replaces the vq that
the scheduler side uses to poll and dispatch" and has "no per-SHA bundle and no
atomic flip contract behind it". Both halves were false, and the second had
been false since `908e5eceb` / `87621aad7`:

* site_i and site_j run **no vq daemon** — `scheduler_dispatch`'s architecture is
  *"off-cluster, SSH-driven, stateless-on-cluster"*;
* `qsub`/`qstat`/`qdel` are raw shell over SSH **from the driver**, not through
  the helper, and all live job state is the driver's;
* the helper is a short-lived per-invocation process used only for `--version`,
  provenance and stage GC, so an invocation in flight during a flip keeps its
  own root's inode;
* the generated job script never invokes vq, so compute jobs do not depend on
  it either;
* both hosts' deploy scripts already publish an immutable per-SHA helper root
  and switch the stable path by rename.

The wait is now gated on evidence rather than on that reasoning. The site
scripts emit an activation receipt (`VQ-DEPLOY-METRIC helper_activation=atomic`
plus the active path and the SHA); `helper_activation_is_proven` consults it and
skips the wait only for a host that has proven atomic activation **with the same
configured deploy command**. Everything else fails closed: no record, no
receipt, a receipt naming a different commit, or a repointed command all keep
the wait — including any host still on `contrib/update-scheduler-vq.sh`, which
rsyncs over the live tree and installs editable, where the wait is genuinely
load-bearing.

Because the wait precedes the deploy, the receipt is read from the previous run
— which is the right question, since "does this host stage and flip?" is a
property of the installed script, and both hosts re-sync their scripts from the
verified archive every update. **Expect a one-cycle bootstrap lag:** the first
update after this lands still runs the old script, emits no receipt, and waits.
### Added: safe source-backed vibe-view desktop updates (2026-08-01)

`vibe-view/scripts/update-desktop.sh` now updates the Git checkout, standalone
Python environment, and source-backed Electron desktop application in one
command. The equivalent `update.sh --desktop` mode refreshes the launcher,
vibe-view version metadata, branding, interpreter record, and macOS
Applications copy; `--adopt-desktop` is required before a different checkout
may take ownership of an existing source app.

Desktop replacement is fail-safe: packaged `app.asar` applications and
unknown bundles are never overwritten, another checkout's source app is left
alone by default, and a same-checkout replacement is staged, signed, verified,
and swapped with rollback. Missing, corrupt, or mismatched Electron runtimes
now synchronize transactionally to the reviewed `33.4.11` lockfile version and
verify the release SHA256 before extraction. An installer lock serializes
concurrent runtime work, and a shared Applications lock rechecks ownership
before the final swap across checkouts. Historical refs without the safe update
protocol are refused, and packaged applications retain their separate
update-feed or replacement-installer workflow.

The same workflow now has explicit macOS and Linux coverage. The downloader
selects arm64 or x64 per host, the macOS runtime is probed without accidentally
launching its branded app, and Intel package builds verify their actual
`dist/mac/` output. On Linux the ZIP fallback preserves Electron's executable
bits, an installed pinned runtime with missing GTK libraries produces
actionable diagnostics without being redownloaded, root desktop launches are
refused, and `--no-sandbox` is an
explicit warned last resort for restricted trusted environments. Packaged
updates remain enabled only for the currently published macOS arm64 feed;
local Intel, Linux, and Windows builds cannot consume an incompatible feed.

### Fixed: a scheduler job the driver never named is no longer lost (2026-08-01)

`_start_scheduler_job` claims `RUNNING` and writes `scheduler_job_id=None` under
the spec lock, submits **outside** the lock, then records the real id in a
second write. A driver death in that window — and a driver self-update restarts
the daemon — leaves the spec permanently `RUNNING` with no id.

Startup already refused to reap such a spec, explicitly because *"a qsub may
have succeeded just before the driver daemon died"*, and deferred to a later
retry. But that retry called `_reattach_scheduler_job`, which returned `False`
immediately when there was no id. **The recovery path was a permanent no-op for
the one case it was written for.** When the qsub had in fact succeeded, vq
silently lost a live cluster job: still consuming the cluster, no longer
tracked, and unnameable by any vq command.

The job now records its own scheduler id (`$PBS_JOBID` / `$SLURM_JOB_ID`) to
`_vq/scheduler-job-id` on the shared workspace, before it runs anything, and
reattach reads it back when the driver has no id of its own. The workspace path
derives from vq's own job id, so recovery needs no scheduler handle — which is
the point, since the missing handle is what it rebuilds.

Deliberately conservative: a missing record means "cannot say", never "no such
job" — a queued job has not run its script yet, and a transport failure is not
evidence either, so the spec stays live and retries rather than being reaped. A
spec that went terminal meanwhile is not resurrected: an operator who gave up on
an unnamed job must not have it silently re-tracked. Array elements do not
record an id, because an element's id carries its index and is not the parent
handle vq holds.

This is the genesis of the `reattach_failed` ghost that `2675b568b` stopped from
blocking drain-waits. That fix kept a ghost from wedging an update; this one
keeps the ghost from being minted, and recovers the live job behind it.

### Added: χ-CCM-B has a fail-closed high-level route-control producer (2026-08-01)

D101 adds `aiccm-2026/run_case_cmp_b.py` and `audit_cmp_b.py` for the pinned
1D/2D/3D campaign. The producer calls the public RHF
`jk_method="aiccm2026dev-b", aiccm_backend="ri"` route, keeps every campaign
cell declared 3D, binds the exact numerical pins and D83/D88/exchange/nuclear
evidence, and requires an exact contract-valid nonquantitative System 3D
receipt before either embedded-object run. `run.sh --comparison-b` selects
this producer, including site_j's stable development-Python wrapper path.

The public `run_periodic_job` B selector gains
`dynamic_damping=None|True|False`; `None` preserves the method option default,
while an explicit value reaches the underlying B options. Other J/K selectors
fail closed on an explicit value until every dispatch preserves it. Fitted B
results expose the GDF method and cutoffs as
`aiccm_resolved_*` selector settings forwarded into the lower driver, not as
backend-owned execution telemetry or numerical-support qualification.

The schema is `vibeqc.aiccm2026dev-b.campaign-1d2d3d/v1`. Successful records
are explicitly `route-plumbing-diagnostic`, `not-qualified`, and
`no-gamma-chi-construction-comparison-defined`; no absolute energy is written
to campaign JSON. D77 clean-checkout binding is mandatory; D91 bundle
attestation remains rejected because its transport/producer/auditor
implementation is absent. D93 continues to disqualify fitted support, and
the reportable Γ/χ approach map stays empty. This adds no Hamiltonian,
backend support, lower-dimensional route, total gradient, or construction
identity.

Incoming `a8b9ac2f8` records an open shifted-pair enumeration defect in the
shared 3D Ewald nuclear helper. D101's separate call to that same helper is
therefore routing/assembly evidence, not a convergence audit. This does not
alter the energy-free D101 contract, but it withdraws the earlier D99
convergence and single-cause wording and makes affected χ absolute-energy
records revision-bound pending the shared repair and rerun.

### Changed: χ-CCM-B localization audits use native low-rank contractions (2026-08-01)

D100 removes two full complex AO-supercell projectors and their dense
translation and projector-Fock temporaries from the occupied-localization
diagnostic path. Density invariance, one-particle-energy invariance, and the
translation-projector residual are now evaluated by a native kernel from
occupied-space Gram matrices and `C^H F C`. Peak diagnostic scratch falls
from `O(n_AO^2)` to `O(n_AO n_occ + n_occ^2)`, and the energy audit avoids a
dense projector-Fock matrix multiplication. The former NumPy projector
formula remains a private parity oracle. Near exact Gram-norm cancellation,
the native kernel streams the AO-pair difference to retain the former small-
residual accuracy without storing the projector.

This is an exact diagnostic rewrite. It does not change localized orbitals,
the localization objective, PNO/domain semantics, the χ-CCM Hamiltonian,
the 3D-only local-correlation boundary, or any analytic-gradient gate.

## [v0.15.108] - 2026-08-01 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Study: the ATOMBSSE ghost-shell re-run settles 6 of 9 open sites (2026-08-01)

`studies/bsse_ghost_shell/RESULTS.md` gains a second sweep, run at current
protocol defaults, over the 9 atom sites the first sweep could not settle plus
3 already-converged controls. Merged: **41 sites converged, 4 insufficient,
none failing outright** (was 36 / 6 / 3).

* The vibe-basis 0.9.0 `ORIGIN`/`TRASREMO` fix holds on the cluster. All three
  space-group-227 systems produce energies where every rung previously died at
  input parsing; `Si|1` and `Ge|1` are converged, and `Ge|1` agrees to
  0.00000 kJ/mol between an x86 host and a local arm64 CRYSTAL23.
* The `NaN` failure class is gone: 35 ok and 13 timeout across 48 runs, with no
  `scf_nan` and no `MULTIP`. Rungs that NaN'd in seconds now converge. The
  sweep changed `TOLINTEG` and `HUGEGRID` together, so which one is responsible
  is not separated.
* **The protocol change does not move the answer.** Three controls re-run at
  the new settings agree with their old energies to at most 0.011 kJ/mol over
  nine comparable rungs -- 45x inside the 0.5 kJ/mol convergence tolerance --
  and every chosen `(nstar, rmax)` is unchanged. The first sweep's converged
  settings stand, and the assumption that ghost-shell extent is only weakly
  grid-dependent is now tested rather than assumed.
* **It does cost 2.5x to 5.5x more wall clock** on identical rungs. Three sites
  (`C-diamond|1`, `BN-beta|1`, `BN-beta|2`) therefore remain unconverged on a
  single ladder point each, their next rung exceeding a four-hour budget, and
  one previously converged site (`MgO|2`) drops to two points. These are
  reported as insufficient rather than dressed up: whether they warrant the
  compute is a maintainer call.

### Fixed: a third of the ATOMBSSE sweep's failures were misdiagnosed (2026-08-01)

`studies/bsse_ghost_shell/RESULTS.md` said the first ghost-shell sweep's 83
failed CRYSTAL runs were "resource failures, not deck errors". Reading every
failing output back off the compute host splits them three ways instead: 32
really did run out of wall clock, 15 were the non-symmorphic `MULTIP` defect
already fixed in vibe-basis 0.9.0, and **36 had the SCF energy go `NaN`**, 30
of those then dying on a `SIGSEGV` inside CRYSTAL. The crash leaves no
`ERROR ****` line, so the runner had nothing to name them by and "no energy"
read as "ran out of something".

They are not size-driven either, which is what makes the resource reading
untenable: one site NaN'd at 436 basis functions after 22 s while a larger
run on the same system completed the densest rung. A longer timeout cannot
fix arithmetic that broke on SCF cycle 1, so the affected rungs need
diagnosis rather than a bigger budget, and per CLAUDE.md section 7 they are
not to be tuned away with damping or a looser tolerance.

`examples/basisset_dev/bsse_sweep/run_sweep.py` now records `scf_nan` as its
own status, ahead of the "did we see any energy at all" test -- such a run has
usually printed a good cycle-0 energy first and would otherwise be filed as
`not_converged` with that number attached.

### Added: the ATOMBSSE sweep can be re-run per site, resumed and merged (2026-08-01)

Settling the sites a previous ghost-shell sweep could not close meant
re-running all 225 CRYSTAL jobs. The sweep tooling under
`examples/basisset_dev/bsse_sweep/` gained:

* `build_payload.py --sites 'Si|1,LiF|1'` (or `--sites @file`), which writes
  the restriction into the payload as `sites.json` so the submitted artefact
  records what the job was for. Omitting the flag selects every emittable
  site, unchanged.
* `SWEEP_TIMEOUT_S`, `SWEEP_LADDER` and `SWEEP_SEED_RESULTS` environment
  knobs. The last resumes across job boundaries: `results.json` lives in
  `$VQ_WORKDIR` and a resubmitted job gets a new one, so without it a job
  killed to fix its worker count recomputes everything it had finished.
* Ladder-major task ordering, so the sweep always holds a uniform-depth
  picture across every site rather than a complete picture of three sites
  and nothing for the rest.
* `merge_results.py`, which combines several sweeps into one table with a
  `from` column naming the sweep behind each row. The sweeps do not share a
  protocol, so a merged table that forgot a number's origin would put two
  protocols under one verdict.
* Deleting CRYSTAL's `fort.*` scratch once a run is done. The first sweep
  left a 109 GB workdir across 225 runs, almost none of it the output the
  runner was careful to clean up.

### Fixed: a ghost job no longer blocks a drain-wait forever (2026-08-01)

`_active_scheduler_job_specs` excluded a spec with no scheduler job id only when
it was `PENDING`. A ghost — `scheduler_state: reattach_failed`, `RUNNING`, no
PBS id, absent from `qstat` — failed that test and counted as active. Since vq
holds no cluster handle for it, **no scheduler job will ever finish on its
behalf**, so a drain-wait behind one is not merely slower: it can never be
satisfied.

site_i, 2026-08-01: a helper rebuild's drain-wait sat behind a real 4-hour GPW job
*and* a ghost (`f53f1cc9bb6c`). The real job was killed to unblock the rebuild,
losing 4+ hours of paper-critical work. The ghost would have blocked it
regardless.

Such a spec is now excluded. Deliberately narrow: only one vq has already given
up on (`reattach_failed`) **and** that has no job id. A `RUNNING` spec with no
id but no reattach marker may simply be mid-dispatch, and skipping that would
declare quiescence while a job is starting — pinned by a test, as is the case
where a reattach failed but the cluster id survived, which is a real job worth
waiting for.

This does not close the underlying gap: the helper lane still waits for genuine
running work, so a long solid-state job still blocks a helper rebuild. That is a
design problem recorded separately.

### Added: one-command standalone vibe-view install and update (2026-08-01)

`vibe-view/scripts/install.sh` now creates a checkout-local
`vibe-view/.venv`, installs the base viewer plus browser/desktop-server and
interactive-TUI dependencies, installs the previously missing Python wheel
builder, verifies every requested command surface, and records the interpreter
for direct Electron launches. Electron remains a lazy first-launch download,
with `--with-electron` for an eager setup. The script does not install or build
vibe-qc.

`vibe-view/scripts/update.sh` fast-forwards the current branch by default (or
selects `main`, `release`, another branch, a tag, or a commit), refreshes the
same regular source install, and repeats the checks. Its default update follows
the current branch's configured upstream even when local and remote names
differ. It refuses dirty tracked trees and unsafe venv deletion targets,
supports dry runs and failure-atomic same-parent venv backup/rollback, and
supports a `--skip-git` reinstall from the current tree.

The build and QVF launch helpers now use the same venv resolver, preferring
`vibe-view/.venv` while retaining the old repo-level locations as read-only
fallbacks. The updater mutates only viewer-owned or explicitly selected
environments, so it cannot mistake a shared vibe-qc venv for its standalone
target. This fixes the loop where `build.sh` said to install vibe-view but no
provided command created an environment it could reliably find.

### Added: a spin-orbital iterative local (T1), milestone 1 (2026-08-01)

vibe-qc's `triples_mode="t1"` is **not** the algorithm of that paper. It
diagonalises the occupied Fock and rotates the occupied indices into the
canonical basis, where `(T)` is exact because the occupied Fock is diagonal
there. That is exact and cheap, but it delocalises: a canonical occupied is a
mixture of every LMO, so a locality-screened triple list cannot survive the
rotation. That is precisely why the open-shell engine fails closed on any
realised screening.

`vibeqc.dlpno.triples_iterative` generalizes the paper's closed-shell Eq. (2)
(doi:10.1063/1.5011798) to spin orbitals: keep triples in the **localised**
occupied basis and reintroduce the off-diagonal occupied Fock coupling by
iterating the triples amplitudes. Because the triple list never leaves the LMO
basis, this is the route on which screening is expressible. The dedicated
open-shell method-family source is Guo et al. 2020
(doi:10.1063/1.5127550); this implementation does not claim to reproduce all
of that publication's implementation-specific approximations.

The reduction is the reason to trust it. For a diagonal occupied Fock the
three `l`-sums in Eq. (2) collapse to `T(f_i+f_j+f_k)`, leaving
`R = W - T*D` and `T = W/D`: exactly the semicanonical `(T0)` amplitude the
existing kernel already forms, which is Eq. (3) of the same paper. Both limits
are pinned as exact ratchets:

* diagonal `f_oo` reproduces `(T0)` to `0.0` in a single sweep (the starting
  guess is already the fixed point);
* non-diagonal `f_oo` converges in 6 sweeps to the exact `(T)` to `8e-17`,
  where the reference is built the other way round, by rotating to the
  canonical basis and evaluating `(T0)` there. A third assertion checks the
  off-diagonal coupling actually moves the answer, so the agreement cannot
  pass trivially.

Milestone 1 is deliberately narrow and **not yet wired into any route**: full
virtual space, so the inter-triple TNO overlaps `S` of Eq. (2) are the identity
and no overlap bookkeeping appears; full triple list. TNO-truncated domains
with real `S`, the paper's `F_Cut` and `T_CutIter` approximations, screening
integration, and public routing are later milestones. Nothing about existing
`(T0)`/`(T1)` behaviour changes.

### Fixed: compact multi-k GPW streams Bloch AO grid tables (2026-08-01)

Compact multi-k RKS GPW no longer retains one complex
`(n_grid_points, n_basis)` Bloch-AO table for every k-point without a bound.
Small jobs retain the iteration-saving all-k cache only while it fits under a
fixed 1 GiB cap; larger density-collocation and local-potential projections
use 64 MiB point batches. Meta-GGA spectral derivatives retain at most one
k-point's whole-grid table. The compact path also stops building an unused
real Gamma AO cache, and the memory preflight mirrors these bounds instead of
multiplying large grid tables by the k-mesh size.

For the P16 NiO/PBE/GPW dimensions (232 AOs, 128 cubed grid, 64 k-points), the
raw preflight estimate falls from 468.228 GiB to 1.186 GiB, so the explicit
DFT+U route fits a 48 GiB node instead of failing before SCF. Energies and
defaults do not change: forced multi-batch density and potential projections
match the former dense primitives to 1e-13 and 1e-12, respectively.

### Added: `vq admin status` reports when installed code and checkout disagree (2026-08-01)

Closes the half left open by the rollback-baseline fix. A rollback resets the
checkout but never re-runs the editable install, so `.dist-info` keeps
describing the previous commit — and nothing distinguished that from a healthy
env.

`last_installed_sha` now records the commit the venv was actually installed
from, distinct from `last_sha` (where the checkout ended up). A **successful**
update sets it; a **failed** one carries the previous value forward, because the
install did not move. `vq admin status --json` gains it plus
`installed_sha_matches_checkout`.

`None` when either side is unknown, deliberately — an env vq has never updated,
or a checkout whose SHA could not be read, is not evidence of agreement.
Reporting absence-of-evidence as health is the exact failure this exists to
stop.

Diagnostic rather than destructive: nothing is uninstalled and no update path
changes behaviour. The mismatch is surfaced so an operator (or a fleet sweep)
can see it, which is what was missing when a live env served months-old code
under a current version string.

### Changed: χ-CCM-B pins the shared fitted nuclear assembly (2026-08-01)

D99 closes an inherited-route provenance gap at the
`jk_method="aiccm2026dev-b"` boundary. Since shared commit `ddbe859d1`, all
supported 3D fitted Gamma-only paths and all multi-k RHF/RKS/UHF/UKS paths use
`ewald_nuclear_repulsion` instead of the truncated
`nuclear_repulsion_per_cell` helper. The routing change is real, but incoming
`a8b9ac2f8` proves that the shared helper's finite real-space cutoff can omit
shifted pair images. The former claim that this established a converged value
and uniquely explained the dense-cell discrepancy is withdrawn. Affected
fitted and four-center absolute energies are revision-bound until the shared
repair lands and fresh fingerprints are run. Gamma-only names the one-character
χ evaluation path here; it does not assign union-and-weight Γ-CCM identity.

The B selector also preserves two shared fitted-support changes explicitly.
Compact dense-core MDF jobs in the MgO/STO-3G class inherit the `6ce142339`
fail-close, while the separately validated vacuum-padded MDF envelope remains
unchanged. Every fitted row is still D93 `not-qualified`. The bounded shared-q
auxiliary Fourier-transform cache from `ad96a2f63` is a bit-identical
memory/performance inheritance. Every fitted B RHF/RKS/UHF/UKS dispatch now
pins `ibz_native=False` and `compute_gradient=False`, so future generic IBZ or
GDF-gradient defaults cannot replace the complete unreduced character mesh or
open a total-gradient route. The 1D/2D SCF and total-gradient fail-closes remain
in force, and D83, D88, and D98 are unchanged.

The comparison producer now identifies `run_ccm_rhf_gdf` as a neutral
fitted-torus Bloch/GDF representation control, not Γ-CCM production. It also
calls the same shared Ewald nuclear helper separately and fails closed unless
that value matches the executed fitted result. This is dispatch/assembly
evidence, not an independent convergence check. Non-finite Madelung or
nuclear-energy evidence is rejected rather than treated as a comparison match.
### Fixed: MP and cold smearing now report variational generalized free energies (2026-08-01)

Methfessel-Paxton orders 1 and 2 had a zero or mismatched generalized
entropy, and the Marzari-Vanderbilt path returned zero entropy while using
a different occupation kernel from the published cold-smearing expression.
Both methods now use their published occupation and entropy pairs, with
`s'(x) = x f'(x)`, so their reported `free_energy = energy - T * entropy`
is stationary at fixed particle number. The GDF analytic-gradient envelope
remains Fermi-Dirac-only until separate non-Fermi-Dirac full-SCF force gates
land; MP occupations can be negative and are incompatible with the current
square-root fractional-block assembly.

### Fixed: a failed build rolls back to what was running, not to a stale branch (2026-08-01)

The atomic-rollback baseline was captured **after**
`_reattach_clean_detached_checkout_for_update`, which runs `git checkout
<branch>` and moves the working tree. A pinned fleet never advances the local
branch ref — every `--expected-sha` update checks out a detached HEAD — so the
baseline was wherever that branch was last left, not what the environment had
been serving.

Localhost, 2026-08-01: a bare `vq admin update vibeqc-dev localhost` hit a
transient build failure and the rollback landed a live v0.15.106 checkout on
`95c141c790ca` — v0.15.48, months old. Worse, the `.dist-info` from the last
successful editable install was untouched, so `vibeqc.__version__` still read
`0.15.106` while the source on disk was months behind: silent wrong-version
execution, with every version-reporting surface agreeing it was fine.

HEAD is now recorded before the reattach. The native-artifact snapshot
deliberately stays after it — `build/` is gitignored, so `git checkout` never
touches it and the `.so` on disk is the serving one either way.

Not fixed here, and worth knowing: rollback still does not invalidate the
installed `.dist-info`, so a rollback across an install boundary can still leave
version metadata describing code that is no longer on disk. This change removes
the months-wide gap; it does not close the metadata question.
### Fixed: D4 `run_job` results expose their method total (2026-08-01)

Non-composite molecular `run_job(..., dispersion="d4")` calls now return the
same transparent correction wrapper as D3(BJ), exposing `e_scf`,
`e_dispersion`, and `energy_total`. The raw `.energy` remains the uncorrected
SCF reference for backward compatibility. When dispersion wraps an MP2 or CC
result, `energy_total` now adds the correction to that method's total rather
than falling back to the SCF reference.

No calculated energy changed. This repairs programmatic result selection: the
MF074 H2O/PBE-D4 campaign row previously received a raw `RKSResult` and stored
the SCF value, while the correct D4 total was present only in output and the
structured `job_end.e_total`. On the regression geometry the newly exposed
total differs from `.energy` by -0.0002013122 Ha. Collectors should prefer
`energy_total` (or `job_end.e_total`) and re-extract affected historical rows.

### Fixed: named molecular ECP bases now attach their sidecar automatically (2026-08-01)

Molecular `run_job` now applies the bundled ECP sidecar for a named ECP basis
when the caller did not provide explicit ECP options. Previously, standard XML
sidecars such as `lanl2dz` were recognised for citation purposes but were not
attached to the SCF options, so their cores stayed in the electron count and
the all-electron Hamiltonian was used with a valence-only basis.

This changes affected molecular RHF, UHF, RKS, and UKS energies materially.
For the MF076 H2S/LANL2DZ RHF reproducer, the calculation now uses 8 valence
electrons instead of 18; the erroneous all-electron result differed from the
matched LANL2DZ reference by 78.63 Ha. Earlier default-option results for
bundled ECP bases are invalid and should be recomputed.

### Fixed: molecular GFN2-xTB reuses cached SCC fixed points for public gradients (2026-08-01)

`GFN2Model.energy()` and `GFN2Model.gradient()` now share the same
geometry-keyed native SCC result inside one model instance. Calling
`energy()` followed by `gradient()` on an unchanged molecule no longer repeats
the full native GFN2 SCC solve; the gradient consumes the already-converged
SCC density and still evaluates the post-SCF D4 gradient separately. The cache
key includes charge, multiplicity, element order and Cartesian coordinates, so
displaced geometries continue to trigger fresh SCC work. This is another
bounded molecular GFN2 performance fix; external `xtb` numerical, wall-time
and peak-RSS parity remain open, and GFN2-xTB remains experimentally gated.

### Fixed: molecular GFN2-xTB public gradients use the native SCC gradient (2026-08-01)

`GFN2Model.gradient()` no longer inherits the generic finite-difference
model gradient that reran the full native SCC plus post-SCF D4 correction at
`6N+1` geometries. It now evaluates the native GFN2 SCC once, uses the
validated native SCC analytic gradient, and finite-differences only the cheap
post-SCF D4 correction so the returned gradient still differentiates the
public D4-corrected total energy. A water-gradient repro drops from 19 native
SCC calls to one. This is a bounded molecular GFN2 performance fix; the
remaining external `xtb` numerical, wall-time, and peak-RSS parity gates stay
open, and GFN2-xTB remains experimentally gated. The semiempirical benchmark
lane also now keeps rare-gas periodic GFN2 as a fail-closed check and uses
non-rare-gas carbon-chain cells for the periodic GFN2 derivative smoke tests,
matching the 2026-07-27 rare-gas physics gate.

## [v0.15.107] - 2026-08-01 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Fixed: an auto-generated build job declares memory that fits (2026-08-01)

Completes the pair started by the CPU clamp. A build job that declared no
`mem_mb` was charged the daemon's `default_job_mem_mb`; on site_b that **exceeds**
`max_mem_mb`, so every undeclared job there — builds included — was
unadmittable forever.

The build now requests a fraction of the host's memory cap (half), so it fits by
construction and leaves room for the work already running: a build is
maintenance, not the point of the machine. Same authority order as the CPU
figure — the daemon's advertised effective budget first, since it is the only
source reflecting a CLI-only `--max-mem-mb`, then the durable `[daemon]` config,
then nothing at all on an uncapped host, which behaves exactly as before.

Declaring rather than clamping was the deliberate choice: clamping CPUs costs a
build wall time, whereas clamping memory gets it OOM-killed halfway through,
which is worse than not starting.

### Fixed: IBZ-native exchange matched wedge matrices to the wrong stars on (4,4,4) meshes (2026-08-01)

The wedge rows were returned sorted, but the star map carries its
representative index positionally into the wedge's own k-point list — so
sorting silently paired each symmetry-transported exchange matrix with
the wrong star. Below (4,4,4) the wedge order happens to be ascending
already, which is why it never showed: (2,2,2) gives [0, 4, 6] and
(3,3,3) gives [0, 9, 12, 21], both unchanged by sorting, while (4,4,4)
gives [0, 16, 32, 20, 36, 52, 40, 57], which is not. The error was
0.44 Ha, and the symmetry gate passed throughout because the density
itself was fine.

Only a production-scale run could surface it, and the fix is an
order-preserving dedupe. The regression additionally asserts that the
(4,4,4) wedge order is still non-monotonic, so it cannot quietly stop
discriminating if spglib's ordering changes.

### Changed: what IBZ-native exchange is actually worth, measured at (4,4,4) (2026-08-01)

On LiH FCC / STO-3G at a 26-bohr cutoff, a (4,4,4) mesh takes 90.9 s
full-BZ and 63.0 s IBZ-native — a **1.44×** speedup with the energies
agreeing to 3.7e-11 Ha.

That is well short of the 7.1× the pair count suggests, and the reason
is worth recording: the two optimisations overlap. Both paths span the
same 64 unique momentum transfers, because the exchange ket sum runs
over the whole zone regardless of where the bra sits. Only the batch
width shrinks, from 64 to 8 — and the shared per-cell
McMurchie-Davidson pass, which dominates, does not depend on the width.
Instrumented, the total ket folds fall 16384 → 760 while the shared work
is unchanged. The earlier shared-q batching had already converted the
`n_k²` build into an `n_k` one, so the remaining gain is the fold and
the exchange contraction alone.

The pair count is therefore a misleading proxy for this feature's
benefit on top of the batching already in place: 1.44× is the number to
quote.

### Added: restricted open-shell HF (ROHF) on the native GDF route (2026-08-01)

`run_krohf_periodic_gdf` closes the ROHF-on-GDF sub-gate of the periodic
restricted-open-shell workstream. One spatial orbital set per k-point with
integer 2/1/0 occupations, so the determinant is a spin eigenfunction and
`<S^2> = S(S+1)` exactly rather than approximately. Gamma is the `(1,1,1)`
mesh of the same code path, so there is no second driver to keep in sync.

Everything below the orbital step is the existing, PySCF-pinned multi-k GDF
machinery: the per-(k_i,k_j) cderi cache, Hartree J from the BZ-summed total
density, the `exxdiv='ewald'` supercell Madelung shift applied once per spin,
and the converged Ewald nuclear repulsion. Only the Fock combination is new
(Roothaan's effective Fock, complex-Hermitian away from Gamma). At
multiplicity 1 it reproduces `run_krhf_periodic_gdf` exactly (0.0 Ha on
H2/(2,1,1)); where ROHF and UHF describe the same determinant it reproduces
`run_kuhf_periodic_gdf` to 1e-16 Ha; Li/STO-3G in a 10-bohr box sits
+2.86e-5 Ha from out-of-process PySCF 2.13.1 KROHF/GDF, collapsing to
+2.2e-7 Ha as the rsgdf mesh is refined - the shared fit-truncation ladder,
not a convention difference.

Exchange, the one O(n_k^2) term, is built by contracting the cderi cache
against the occupied MO blocks instead of the nbf x nbf densities: the same
operator at n_occ/nbf of the flops, with no per-pair `L.conj()` copy, as two
GEMM calls per k-pair so the work stays inside threaded BLAS (measured 5.5x
at nbf=90 / n_occ=12 against the density form, agreeing with it to 4e-15
relative). Damped iterates reuse the previous exchange by linearity rather
than rebuilding, which keeps every build at exactly n_occ columns; the damped
SCF is pinned to the undamped fixed point. The rsgdf cderi setup rides the
existing MPI k-point farming unchanged.

ROKS on GDF is a separate increment and raises rather than silently running
something else, as do smearing and 2D slabs. Analytic gradients, COSX
exchange and `ibz_native` are not on this driver's argument surface at all.
The standalone entry point remains available. Public runner dispatch, with
the ordinary output and citation lifecycle, was added in the 2026-08-02
increment above.

### Added: offset-adaptive azimuthal quadrature for the CCM d=1 wire kernel (G-CCM-004, first increment) (2026-07-31)

The wire four-center's transverse quadrature used a flat azimuthal count
(`n_ang = 64`) at every radial node. The azimuthal bandwidth of an
off-axis pair is `|G_perp| x offset` (Jacobi-Anger; trapezoid-rule
convergence per Trefethen & Weideman, SIAM Rev. 56, 385 (2014)), so a
flat count silently under-resolves whenever the oscillation outruns the
pair-FT envelope `e^{-g^2/4p}` -- exactly the tight-core off-axis regime
of polyethylene, where the recorded +22.69 Ha/atom garbage came from.
On-axis chains (the validated H/He wires) never see it, which is why the
H/He gates stayed green.

`wire_quadrature` (and every builder above it: cderi, streamed J/K,
V_ne, E_nn -- the nuclear structure factor oscillates identically) now
takes `b_max`, switching to a per-radial-node count
`required_n_ang(g, b_max)`; `run_ccm_rhf_wire` derives `b_max` from the
supercell geometry automatically. `b_max = 0` and the `b_max = None`
default preserve the historical flat grid bit-for-bit. Pinned against
the exact erf image-sum oracle on an off-axis fixture chosen so the
bandwidth beats the envelope: flat `n_ang = 16` fails at > 1e-4 while
the adaptive grid with the same floor recovers the oracle to < 1e-6.

Scope honesty: this closes the *integral-accuracy* half of G-CCM-004.
The carbon-chain SCF oscillation is a separate defect -- reproduced as
an exactly degenerate pi HOMO/LUMO flip-flop that is bit-for-bit
insensitive to quadrature refinement (integrals verified to ~1e-6
against the oracle) -- i.e. SCF conditioning, needing
smearing/fractional occupations or a gapped (dimerized) anchor; the
`Z > 2` fail-closed gate on `run_ccm_rhf_wire` therefore stays until
that second half lands. Citations: Rozzi 2006 (the wire kernel) and
Trefethen-Weideman 2014 (the convergence law) added to the database on
the new `ccm_wire_kernel` route; the experimental wire entry point has
no citation assembly yet, recorded for the -a chat.

### Added: triples screened by coupling_radius are now counted and reported (2026-08-01)

`LocalCCSDOptions.coupling_radius` is advertised for linear scaling on
extended systems. It drops whole occupied triple keys, and nothing reported
how many. The 2026-08-01 TNO-domain reporting made the *virtual*-side
truncation visible; the *occupied* side stayed invisible.

It can be far more aggressive than it looks. On an H10 chain at 1.8 bohr
spacing (16.2 bohr long, strongly coupled occupieds) a `coupling_radius` of
5 bohr drops 16 of the 25 distinct triple keys and takes **90% of the triples
energy** with them, `e_t` falling from `-1.614e-03` to `-1.556e-04`. That is a
property of the system rather than a defect (correlation in a delocalized
chain is genuinely long-ranged, so a locality cutoff is the wrong
approximation there), but it should not be silent.

`LocalCCSDResult` gains `n_triple_keys` and `n_triple_keys_screened`, the
`.out` appends `(N screened by coupling_radius)` to the triples line when
screening fired, and the structured event gains `n_triple_keys_screened`.
No threshold policy is invented: the counts are reported and the user judges.

A suspicion is also retired, with measurements rather than argument. The
`(T1)` path screens triple keys on LMO centroid distances but indexes
amplitudes whose occupied indices have been rotated into the canonical basis,
which reads like a correctness bug. It is not one in any regime tested:
measured against its own unscreened reference, screening costs 0.074 µHa under
`(T1)` versus 0.071 µHa under `(T0)` on H2O + H2 at 8 Å, 0.422 versus 0.372 µHa
on two identical waters, and 1459 versus 1142 µHa on the H10 chain. The
separated-fragment cases are weak tests, since negligible inter-fragment
occupied-Fock coupling leaves the Jacobi sweep near-identity and canonical
approximately localized; the chain is the discriminating case and `(T1)` still
tracks `(T0)`.

### Added: sub-mHa molecular HF atomization energies on the analytic GAPW route (2026-08-01)

The first end-to-end artifact of the PW-limit atomization workstream:
molecular HF atomization energies computed entirely on the analytic
GAPW route (Hund-ground-state open-shell atoms via the newly landed
polarised analytic mode, closed-shell molecules) match exact molecular
references to <= 1 mHa - H2 +0.01, H2O +0.85 (12-bohr boxes), LiH
+0.98 mHa (16-bohr) - because the ~+7..+12 mHa per-system absolute
residuals cancel between atoms and molecule. The box-size rule is
measured and pinned: diffuse-valence atoms (Li) need L >= 16 bohr; at
L = 12 the compressed Li 2s degrades LiH's cancellation to -11.4 mHa.
Gate: tests/test_periodic_gapw_projector.py::test_analytic_mode_hf_atomization_sub_mha.

### Fixed: `vq drain --status` no longer promises an auto-release it cannot deliver (2026-08-01)

A scheduler lane outlives its own `--duration`. At expiry `read_drain_state`
clears the global hold, **preserves** `scheduler_hosts`, and nulls
`duration_seconds` — so the lane becomes permanently unbounded exactly when its
countdown runs out. `--status` nonetheless printed a bare
`auto-release in 3599s`, telling an operator to wait for something that would
never happen.

That is not a corner case: `rollout-latest` passes `--duration` on **both**
branches, so every rollout-owned scheduler lane advertised a bound it did not
have. It is also the shape that let the 2026-07-26 site_i lane leak sit unnoticed
— a bounded-looking hold nobody thought to check.

The countdown now says what it actually covers, and names the release as manual.
`--json` gains `duration_releases_everything` so a machine reader is not misled
the way the text was. A plain full drain really is cleared outright on expiry,
so its countdown was never wrong and stays terse.

The preservation behaviour itself is unchanged and deliberate — a lane
protecting an in-flight cluster operation should not vanish on a timer. A test
now pins that expiry really does keep the lane and drop the bound, so if that
ever changes, this warning becomes the new lie and fails loudly.

### Changed: IBZ-native exchange gates on the state's symmetry, not on multiplicity (2026-08-01)
