Investigating a magnetic-symmetry (spin space group) wedge for
spin-polarised systems established that it is the wrong fix, so the
`multiplicity > 1` refusal it would have replaced is gone in favour of a
runtime check that measures the thing that actually matters.

Three measurements make the case. The failing LiH triplet has no
magnetic ordering to describe: its frontier is non-degenerate at every k
and star partners carry identical eigenvalue spectra, so the nuclear
point group is already the correct spatial group. The break is
variational rather than numerical — star-partner densities differ by
6.8e-4 in trace, stable from a convergence threshold of 1e-8 through
1e-12, and the broken solution lies 7e-4 Ha *below* the symmetric one,
which is the classic symmetry dilemma. And the IBZ constraint does not
repair it: under the flag the converged density is still 1.7e-3
asymmetric, so exchange is built symmetric while the density is not, and
that internal inconsistency is what costs the energy.

A different wedge would not stop a UHF solution from breaking the
spatial symmetry it is offered. So `ibz_native` now checks, every SCF
iteration, whether the density actually respects the wedge, comparing
its transport residual against a floor measured on the overlap — a
self-calibrating reference, since a truncated Bloch sum is not exactly
symmetric either and comparing against zero would refuse everything. The
check runs each iteration rather than once because the initial guess is
symmetric even when the converged state is not.

This is strictly better than the multiplicity proxy, which both let a
closed-shell broken-symmetry solution through and refused spin-polarised
systems whose solutions are symmetric.

One limitation is worth knowing: the diagnostic only separates cleanly
once the cell list is converged. Symmetric and broken states differ by
roughly 6000× at a 26-bohr cutoff but only 3× at 20, where a broken
state can pass — the same regime the driver already warns about.

### Fixed: vibe-view lost the unit cell when importing via ASE (2026-07-28)

Opening a VASP POSCAR, or any other structure read through the optional ASE
extra, kept the atoms but discarded the unit cell while still marking the
structure as periodic. The result rendered as a molecule: no cell drawn, no
bonds across the cell boundaries, and no replication. Nothing announced the
problem, because every atom arrived with the right element and position. The
cell is now carried through, so a crystal imported this way behaves like one.
Structures that are genuinely non-periodic are unaffected.

### Added: an abandoned drain lane is now identifiable (2026-08-01)

`vq admin update <scheduler-host> --drain-wait` killed mid-wait leaves its lane
behind — a `finally` cannot run through an external kill. vq's own "never lift
an operator's hold" rule then reads the corpse as intentional, so the host sits
`accept_pending`, taking submissions and dispatching nothing, until someone
releases it by hand. site_i, 2026-07-26.

A vq-taken lane now records the owning PID plus its `/proc` start time, and
`vq drain --status` reports when that owner is gone or its PID was recycled —
in JSON as `orphaned_lane_reason`, and in the text status as a loud line paired
with the exact release command. That command is worth printing: a scheduler
lane lives on the **driver**, which is the invocation people get wrong.

**It reports; it never lifts.** An operator's deliberate hold and a leaked one
are identical on disk precisely because vq must not guess between them, and
guessing wrong drops a hold someone is relying on. What this removes is the
ambiguity, not the human decision.

Conservative throughout, mirroring the admin-update marker's staleness check:
indeterminate liveness reads as alive, a recycled PID needs the fingerprint to
disagree, and a lane with **no** recorded owner is treated as an operator hold —
a deliberate hold has no process to outlive, so it can never be called
abandoned.

The `DrainState` field this needs was blocked until every host was past the
forward-compat release (`b1c2c8069`); verified before adding it.

### Fixed: analytic-mode GAPW DFT smooth-XC Fock was not the energy derivative; DFT envelope re-measured (2026-08-01)

Two coupled changes on the experimental `one_centre="analytic"` GAPW
route. First, a genuine Fock/energy inconsistency: the smooth XC
energy is `E_xc[rho_tilde(D_soft)]` but its potential was projected
onto the FULL AO basis (the block-mode recipe); with the otherwise
exact analytic Fock the SCF then converged away from the energy
minimum - Ne/6-31G LDA walked +373 mHa uphill from the exact molecular
density (+393 vs +15.1 mHa after the fix). The projection now lives in
the soft block, the exact derivative. Second, the DFT envelope was
calibrated across bases and TIGHTENED to single-atom cells: atoms are
HF-quality across bases (Ne LDA +15.1/+18.1/+22.7 mHa at
6-31G/STO-3G/def2-SVP), but the fitted off-centre XC densities'
variational softness grows with basis richness (LiH LDA -10.6 -> -54.1
-> -105.0 mHa; H2O -545 -> +72 -> -21106), so the earlier
neighbour-count gate was unsound and multi-atom DFT now fails closed
with the ladder in the message. HF on the analytic route is unaffected
and separately validated at production bases (H2O +7.4 mHa at 6-31G,
+26.0 at def2-SVP).

### Added: open-shell GAPW analytic one-centre mode (UHF/UKS) (2026-08-01)

`one_centre=` is now wired through `run_periodic_uhf_gapw` and
`run_periodic_uks_gapw`. UHF rides the existing fit-free analytic-ERI
Hartree augmentation unchanged (it only ever sees the spin-summed
density): O triplet +12.4 mHa and the multi-atom OH doublet +12.6 mHa
vs molecular UHF at 48^3/STO-3G, where block mode sits at +15.0 on the
atom. UKS adds a spin-polarised projector-density XC augmentation
(`projector_xc_correction_polarised`, mirroring CP2K's per-spin
one-centre densities in `calculate_vxc_atom`) with exact per-spin Fock
matrices (directional FD parity, LDA+GGA incl. the v_sigma_ab cross
terms) and the soft-block smooth-XC projection on the polarised path:
O triplet LDA +12.4 mHa vs molecular UKS. Envelopes are inherited, not
widened: analytic-mode DFT stays single-atom-only, projector mode
stays HF-only/single-atom, and block mode is untouched. This unblocks
the O/C/N open-shell atomic references for the PW-limit atomization
target (G-PBC-003). New gate:
`tests/test_periodic_gapw_open_shell_analytic.py` (registered T3
experimental in the suite manifest).

## [v0.15.106] - 2026-08-01 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Fixed: a freshly provisioned multi-user host can actually run admin operations (2026-08-01)

`contrib/deploy-multi-user.sh` created `/var/lib/vq` with a bare
`sudo mkdir -p`, leaving it `root:root 0755`. The admin-update marker is written
directly under the state root, so on a brand-new multi-user host **every**
`vq admin` operation failed at marker acquisition — with the host otherwise
fully provisioned and the daemon running, which reads as a vq bug rather than a
missing permission.

The state root is now `chgrp`ed to the admin group and set `2775`. The setgid
bit matters: files created there inherit the group rather than the creator's
primary group, so the next admin's marker is writable by the one after.

This is the state **root** only. The per-user subtrees under `$STATE_DIR/users`
keep their own stricter modes, and this does not pre-empt ISO-1's second half,
which tightens those.

Guarded by tests that grep the script, including that `groupadd` still precedes
the `chgrp` — that ordering is what makes it work on a fresh host. Grepping is
the honest test for shipped shell the suite cannot execute: it guards the line
against a future edit rather than proving modes on a real host.

### Added: IBZ-native exchange reaches the open-shell drivers, and refuses spin-polarised systems (2026-08-01)

`run_kuhf_periodic_gdf` and `run_kuks_periodic_gdf` now take
`ibz_native` as well. Both spin channels transport through the same
per-spin path, and at multiplicity 1 the flag reproduces the full-BZ
energy to 9.6e-12 Ha.

Wiring it up exposed a real physical limit rather than a coding one, so
the flag refuses spin-polarised systems outright. The irreducible wedge
comes from spglib, which derives it from the *nuclear* positions — but
the symmetry the transport actually requires is the *density's*, and a
spin-polarised density need not share it. On LiH FCC (2,2,2) at a
converged 26-bohr cutoff the triplet's alpha density transports with
1.8e-3 relative residual against the singlet's 1.6e-7, and the resulting
energy sits 7e-4 Ha off.

What settles it as a symmetry break rather than an accuracy knob is that
the error is flat in the cutoff: 7.5e-4 at 20 bohr, 7.0e-4 at 26, where
a truncation effect would fall by orders of magnitude. Supporting these
systems needs a magnetic-symmetry (spin space group) wedge, which is not
implemented; until then `multiplicity > 1` raises rather than returning a
quietly wrong number.

`k_exchange='cosx'` is also refused, since COSX builds K in real space
from its own bridge and never touches the fitted cderi cache the flag
reduces.

### Added: dlpno-ccsd(t) reports its triples domain, and warns when it collapsed (2026-08-01)

The 2026-07-29 work put `avg_tno`, `tno_per_triple` and
`n_degenerate_tno_triples` on `LocalCCSDResult`, but only on the Python
object. The public route reaches that solver through `run_job` with a
caller-supplied `LocalCCSDOptions`, so a user can set a positive `tcut_tno`
via `dlpno_ccsd_options` and get no mention of the triples domain anywhere:
not in the `.out`, not in the `dlpno_ccsd_done` event, and no warning even
when a triple had been truncated out of existence.

That last part is the reason this matters. A triple excitation promotes three
electrons into three *distinct* virtuals, so a domain holding fewer than three
contributes exactly zero rather than approximately. On H2O/def2-SVP the first
triple collapses between `tcut_tno=1e-6` and `1e-5`, and the triples error
jumps 400-fold at that point, so the failure is both reachable and invisible.

The `.out` block now carries a domain line beside the pair line:

```text
  pairs / avg PNOs         = 15 / 19.0   (frozen core: 0)
  triples / avg TNOs       = 25 / 15.7   (smallest domain: 1)
```

and a collapsed domain raises a warning naming the count and the fix. The
structured event gains `n_tno_triples`, `avg_tno_per_triple`,
`min_tno_per_triple` and `n_degenerate_tno_triples`.

Default behaviour is unchanged: `tcut_tno` defaults to `0.0`, so a default job
truncates nothing and prints the full domain with no warning. The open-shell
route runs the UCCSD(T) pilot, which builds no TNO domain, so the line is
omitted there rather than printed as zeros.

## [v0.15.105] - 2026-08-01 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Added: opt-in IBZ-native exchange for multi-k GDF (2026-08-01)

`run_krhf_periodic_gdf` and `run_krks_periodic_gdf` take `ibz_native`
(default off). With it, exact exchange is built only at the irreducible
wedge and symmetry-transported to the rest of the mesh, cutting both the
density-fitting build and the per-iteration contraction — the one term
in the multi-k SCF that scales as `n_k^2`.

The implementation transports **K**, not the density. That was a
measurement result rather than a preference: K transports about sixty
times more accurately than D on the same cell list (1.5e-3 against
8.9e-2 at a 15-bohr cutoff), and transporting it lets the driver keep
diagonalising at every k. Occupations, the energy expression and the
per-k result shape are therefore all unchanged, so band, DOS, COOP/COHP
and QVF consumers see exactly what they saw before.

On LiH FCC (2,2,2) it reproduces the full-BZ energy to 1.0e-07 Ha at a
20-bohr cutoff and 9.6e-12 Ha at 26; (3,3,3) agrees to 2.6e-07 Ha.

The saving is real but its wall-clock benefit is size-dependent, and
worth stating plainly: the cderi pair count falls 729 → 135 at (3,3,3),
yet end-to-end wall improves only 1.17× there, because exchange is not
the bottleneck for a six-function cell. A fourteen-function basis gives
1.52×. The exchange build only dominates from about (4,4,4) with a
realistic basis, which is the regime the flag exists for and which has
not been measured here.

Accuracy has a precondition, and the driver says so rather than
degrading quietly: the transport is only as good as the cell list, so
below a 20-bohr cutoff it warns. It refuses outright without attached
symmetry, on a mesh it cannot reduce or match, and on a pure functional,
where there is no exchange term to reduce.

## [v0.15.104] - 2026-08-01 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Added: IBZ-native exchange builder for multi-k GDF (2026-08-01)

First increment of IBZ-native reduction, the open lever on the multi-k
GDF exchange cost. Exchange is the one term that scales as `n_k^2` —
measured at 3.47 s per SCF iteration on a (4,4,4) mesh with a small
basis, and already at 117 GFlop/s, so the cost is algorithmic rather
than an implementation defect.

`_build_k_ibz_native` evaluates the exchange at the irreducible-wedge
bras only, from an `n_IBZ x n_k` cderi sub-block instead of the full
`n_k x n_k`. The symmetry saving is on the **bra** index alone: `K(k_i)`
still sums its ket index over the whole Brillouin zone. Reducing the ket
sum as well is the error that measured +1.389 Ha on MgO — weighting
irreducible representatives is not orbit summation — and a mutation
check confirms the regressions catch exactly that.

Nothing is user-visible yet: no driver calls it. Wiring it into the SCF
comes next, behind an opt-in flag defaulting off, because an IBZ-native
run returns `n_IBZ` per-k quantities where a full-BZ run returns `n_k`,
and bands, DOS, COOP/COHP and QVF all read those.

## [v0.15.103] - 2026-08-01 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Fixed: vibe-view drew bonds between metal ions in salts (2026-07-28)

Automatic bonding sized every atom as a neutral atom, but a metal cation is far
smaller than its neutral form, so in an ionic solid the metal ions were close
enough by that measure to be joined to each other. Magnesium oxide rendered with
a bonded magnesium lattice running through it and caesium chloride with bonded
caesium, neither of which exists. Metal atoms are now bonded to each other only
in a structure that is entirely metal, where those contacts are the bonding, so
copper metal still renders fully bonded while the salts do not. Bonds between a
metal and a non-metal are unaffected, and connectivity supplied by a producer
continues to override this entirely.

### Changed: analytic-mode GAPW DFT runs its XC augmentation on projector one-centre densities (2026-08-01)

The analytic GAPW mode's DFT path now telescopes the XC augmentation
over the projector one-centre densities instead of the block-restricted
ones, with exact LDA and GGA Fock matrices (directional FD parity
~1e-9). Fixed-density H2O/LDA telescoping error drops from +1567.5 mHa
(block) to -70.5 (projector); allowed-class SCF numbers improve (LiH
LDA -8.9 mHa vs molecular, was -11.8). The >=2-neighbour pruned-core
DFT class stays fail-closed with the new measurements in the message:
the fitted XC densities are variationally soft at minimal bases
(H2O/STO-3G LDA SCF converges -545 mHa below molecular, while
H2O/6-31G lands +72 mHa - the drift shrinks ~8x with a double-zeta
basis, consistent with KP2000's sub-mHa at 6-31G*). Calibrating that
class across production bases and then relaxing the guard is the
recorded next step. HF on the analytic route is unaffected.

### Fixed: smeared periodic GDF SCFs with DIIS no longer freeze occupations on zero-commutator fixtures (2026-08-01)

On symmetry-locked fixtures whose FDS-SDF commutator vanishes
identically (H2-in-box class: the sigma_g/sigma_u eigenvectors are
fixed by symmetry, so [F, D] == 0 from iteration 1 for any
occupations), the finite-temperature (Fermi-Dirac) Γ open-shell and
multi-k GDF SCFs with DIIS terminated after ~3 iterations claiming
convergence (dE = 0 exactly) at a state whose occupations were NOT the
Fermi filling of the converged Fock's own eigenvalues — reported
smeared energies/occupations were wrong, not only gradients (measured
2026-07-30 on H2 2.4 bohr / 12-bohr box / sto-3g / kBT = 0.05 Ha:
stored occ_alpha 0.998955 vs recomputed 0.999126, free energy off
~1e-4 Ha, analytic-vs-FD forces off 3.3e-3). Root cause: DIIS received
zero error vectors, its Pulay B matrix was exactly singular, and the
unconstrained extrapolation weights froze the mixed Fock's
eigenvalues. Two-part cause fix: (1) every Γ and multi-k periodic SCF
accelerator now skips extrapolation (and records nothing) when the
commutator error is numerical noise on the Fock scale, so the plain
Fock is diagonalised and the occupation fixed point converges exactly
as with `use_diis=False`; (2) the smeared convergence tests of
`run_pbc_gdf_uhf` / `run_pbc_gdf_uks` / `run_krhf_periodic_gdf` /
`run_kuhf_periodic_gdf` additionally require the stored occupations to
match the Fermi filling of the current Fock's own eigenvalues within
`vibeqc.smearing.smeared_occupation_selfconsistency_tolerance`
(sqrt of `conv_tol_energy`, floored at 1e-9). Post-fix the DIIS-on
runs converge to the plain-iteration fixed point (free-energy match
~1e-12 Ha, stored == recomputed filling to ~1e-15); regression
coverage in `tests/test_periodic_gdf_smearing_diis.py`.

## [v0.15.102] - 2026-07-31 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Added: DFT on the analytic GAPW mode for atoms and single-neighbour cores (2026-07-31)

`run_periodic_rhf_gapw(one_centre="analytic", functional=...)` now runs
RKS where the (still block-based) XC augmentation is validated: single
atoms and pruned cores with at most one near neighbour. Measured vs
molecular RKS at 48^3: Ne LDA +18.1 mHa / PBE +9.8 (block mode: +53 /
+45), LiH LDA -11.8. A pruned atom with two or more neighbours within
4 bohr fails closed with the measurement in the message: the block XC
augmentation mis-telescopes bond density inside the sphere by Ha-scale
there (H2O LDA +1.585 Ha, PBE +1.719 - the XC-side sibling of the fixed
Hartree bug). Porting the XC augmentation to the analytic/projector
one-centre densities is the recorded next step; HF on the analytic mode
is unrestricted within its molecular-limit envelope.

## [v0.15.101] - 2026-07-31 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Added: fit-free analytic-ERI GAPW augmentation - H2O lands at +11.5 mHa (opt-in, experimental) (2026-07-31)

`run_periodic_rhf_gapw(one_centre="analytic")` evaluates the GAPW
Hartree augmentation as the exact hard/soft ERI difference plus
charge-conserving s-compensators: every term is an exact contraction,
an analytic Gaussian integral, or a bounded-kernel grid quadrature, so
the SCF has no fit-error hole to exploit and the Fock is the exact
derivative (`1/2 tr(D J) = E_H` to 1e-12). On the filed H2O
wrong-answer reproducer the analytic mode converges to +11.5 mHa vs the
molecular reference (default block augmentation: -8.86 Ha); the full
validation set lands within +-18 mHa (LiH -7.1, Ne +18.1, O +12.4, He
+0.4, H2 -0.03). Envelope: molecular-limit Gamma cells, HF-only (DFT
functionals fail closed until the XC augmentation is ported); the
default route is unchanged pending the maintainer's call on flipping
it. The intermediate fitted-projector mode's variational hole
(root-caused to non-charge-conserving per-atom Mulliken partitions,
then to fit-error self-repulsion undercounting) is documented in
HANDOVER_GAPW_PRODUCTION.md, with the charge-conservation property now
pinned by a regression test.

## [v0.15.100] - 2026-07-30 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Fixed: RIJCOSX multi-stage COSX grids no longer iterate the SCF on the final grid (BUG87-A) (2026-07-30)

The staged COSX grid progression ran a full SCF segment to the user's
tolerance on the FINAL (largest) grid. Because the inter-grid exchange
difference re-excites the DIIS error vector to the 1e-2-Frobenius class,
that segment re-converged the SCF from scratch at the most expensive
per-iteration price: on the fleet glycine/def2-TZVP RHF RIJCOSX pair, 12
fine-grid K builds dominated the 2277.6 s wall (32.9x ORCA 6.1.1 on the
same node; RHF has no XC grid, so the defect sat in the shared RIJCOSX
machinery — BUG87-A). The published scheme this progression is modeled
on (Helmich-Paris, de Souza, Neese & Izsák, J. Chem. Phys. 155, 104109
(2021), Sec. IV.A) prescribes the opposite: converge the SCF on the
middle grid, then recompute the exchange energy ONCE on the final grid.
`run_cosx_staged_scf` now converges the second-to-last stage to the
caller's tolerance and performs a single non-iterated final-grid Fock
rebuild + energy recompute at the converged density; the returned trace
concatenates all stages (renumbered, seam dE recomputed), `converged`
reflects the converging stage, and the reported energy is the
final-grid recompute. Measured on the fleet glycine reproducer
(1 thread, local): def2-svp 148.5 s → 58.7 s, def2-tzvp 495.6 s →
195.7 s (2.5x), with the final energy CLOSER to the exact-RI-K (RIJK)
SCF on the same deck than before (def2-tzvp error vs RIJK truth
+2.1e-5 Ha, was −1.7e-4; def2-svp −1.6e-4, was −3.0e-4). The shipped
RIJCOSX total consequently moves by ~+1.5e-4 Ha (def2-svp) / +1.9e-4 Ha
(def2-tzvp) — the middle→final-grid quadrature difference at fixed
density, within the published DefGrid accuracy class and now on the
truthful side. Correctness fallback: a degenerate open-shell system can meet a
commutator floor on the converging grid above the caller's tolerance
(measured: OH·/def2-svp UHF stalls at ~3e-5 on the middle GridX grid);
when the converging stage fails to reach tolerance, the final grid runs
as a full converging segment (the pre-fix behaviour) so floor-limited
systems keep their convergence. Structural guards:
`tests/test_cosx_variants.py::test_multistage_final_grid_is_single_recompute`
and `::test_multistage_commutator_floor_falls_back_to_final_grid`.
The remaining gap to ORCA is the scalar per-point ESP kernel
(`cosx_nuclear_pair_into`, 76 % of profile samples); the
batch-vectorized kernel rewrite is characterized with a costed proposal
in the fixer evidence.

### Fixed: .perf SCF iteration walls are measured, never fabricated (2026-07-30)

The `.perf` "SCF iterations" table printed `wall (s)` = 0.000 on every
iteration of a 2258 s SCF: `SCFIteration` carried no wall field and the
renderer defaulted the missing key to 0.0 — rendering an unmeasured
quantity as a plausible measurement. The four molecular SCF loops now
record a measured per-iteration wall (`SCFIteration.wall_s`,
steady-clock, charged with everything since the previous trace row so
Fock build + energy + DIIS + diagonalization are covered), the runner
replays it into the perf tracker, and the renderer prints `--` for
genuinely unmeasured rows instead of a fabricated 0.000.

## [v0.15.99] - 2026-07-30 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Fixed: RIJCOSX analytic nuclear gradient parity (2026-07-29)

The RIJCOSX analytic gradient disagreed with ORCA 6.1.1 EnGrad on
glycine/def2-TZVP at the 25 %-of-norm level (|grad| 0.1090 vs 0.0870 Ha/bohr,
componentwise max 7.15e-2) while the SCF energy agreed to 0.2648 mHa, with a
per-atom error that tracked nuclear charge. A fixed-density finite-difference
decomposition proved the chain-of-spheres K-gradient contribution was the
cause: (i) it contracted the overlap-fitted density Qᵀ D Q on BOTH sides of
the seminumerical bilinear form while the energy is the mixed
(D′χ)ᵀA(Dχ) form (Izsák & Neese, J. Chem. Phys. 135, 144105 (2011)), and
(ii) it froze the overlap-fit matrix Q although the reference gradient
carries the fit derivative (ibid., Sec. II.D). Both terms are now
implemented; the analytic K gradient matches finite differences of its own
frozen-grid surface to ~1e-7 Ha/bohr, and the glycine gradient lands at
|grad| 0.08696 vs ORCA 0.08703, componentwise RMS 3.3e-3 (was 1.60e-2), max
1.1e-2 (was 7.15e-2). Remaining, documented residuals: neglected
grid-point-motion/Becke-weight derivatives (~2e-4 typical, ~3e-3 worst
measured) and the FITTED-variant Fock/energy self-adjointness response —
see `cpp/include/vibeqc/cosx.hpp` and `tests/test_rijcosx_gradient_fd.py`
(new FD-oracle gate) plus
`examples/regression/rijcosx_gradient_fd_decompose.py` (new instrument).
`docs/features.md` no longer claims gradient parity from the energy-only
ORCA comparison.

### Fixed: explicit n_frozen_core=0 no longer labelled "(chemical-core default)" (2026-07-29)

`opts = CCSDOptions(); opts.n_frozen_core = 0` (attribute assignment) was
honoured numerically but printed as "(chemical-core default)" in the `.out`
and structured log — only the constructor-kwarg path marked explicitness.
`CCSDOptions.n_frozen_core` is now a write-through property that records
user intent; run_job's internal chemical-core defaults keep the default
label.

### Added: finite-temperature (Fermi-Dirac) smeared GDF analytic forces via the Mermin free energy (2026-07-30)

G-PBC-002 smearing gradient envelope. `compute_gradient=True` with
`smearing_temperature > 0` no longer fails closed on the Γ open-shell
(`run_pbc_gdf_uhf`/`run_pbc_gdf_uks`, compcell + rsgdf) and multi-k
(`run_krhf/krks/kuhf/kuks_periodic_gdf`, rsgdf) drivers: the analytic
gradient is `dA/dR` of the driver's reported Mermin free energy
`A = E - T.S` at fixed `(T, N)`. Theory (per CLAUDE.md § 8, from the
library PDFs): Mermin, Phys. Rev. 137, A1441 (1965) makes A stationary
at the self-consistent finite-T solution, so with the Fermi-Dirac
entropy — the exact conjugate of the occupation function,
`dA/df_i = eps_i - (eps_i - mu) = mu` with `sum df_i = 0` — every
occupation- and mu-response term in `dA/dR` vanishes and the T = 0
assemblers apply unchanged at the fractional-occupation
`D = sum_i f_i c c^H` and free-energy-weighted
`W = sum_i f_i eps_i c c^H` (Marzari & Vanderbilt, PRL 82, 3296
(1999): the smeared-force statement; occupation-function hierarchy
per Methfessel & Paxton, PRB 40, 3616 (1989)). Implementation is pure
wiring: the Γ drivers hand sqrt(f)-scaled orbital blocks to the
occupation-agnostic assemblers (`W`, the `f_i.f_j`-weighted exchange,
and the exxdiv `D S D` term all come out exactly right; T = 0 slices
bit-identical), the multi-k drivers build `W(k)` from
`result.occupations`. Envelope restriction, audited: Fermi-Dirac ONLY
— the Methfessel-Paxton and Marzari-Vanderbilt entropies as
implemented in `vibeqc.smearing` are NOT the consistent conjugates of
their occupation functions (MP N=1/N=2 return zero / a mismatched
integrand instead of `1/2 A_N H_2N(x) exp(-x^2)`; MV returns zero
instead of its Eq. (2) form), so A is not variational there and those
flavors fail closed by name; `bz_integration="smearing"` is accepted
(literally the same occupation path), `"gilat"` stays guarded. The
GDF optimizer objective is coupled: a smeared
`run_periodic_job(optimize=True)` relaxes on `free_energy` with the
matching forces. Gates (`tests/test_periodic_gdf_gradient.py`),
central FD of the DRIVER's free_energy at h = 2e-4 vs 1e-6, at
genuinely fractional occupations (f ~ 0.08-0.92 per spin, asserted):
Γ UHF 3.8e-10 (compcell) / 1.9e-10 (rsgdf), KRHF (2,1,1) 3.5e-10
Ha/bohr; FD of `.energy` instead disagrees by the `T.dS/dR` term
(~0.1 Ha/bohr — the gate would catch differencing the wrong field);
T -> 0 consistency at kBT = 1e-4 on gapped H2: smeared vs T = 0
gradient <= 1.2e-15 (gate 1e-9). Known issue recorded (not papered
over, CLAUDE.md § 7): on symmetry-locked fixtures whose FDS-SDF
commutator vanishes identically, the smeared SCF + DIIS terminates
with occupations from a stale extrapolated Fock (zero error vectors
make the DIIS weights unconstrained) — the FD gates run with
`use_diis=False` and the reproducer is in
`handovers/HANDOVER_GATED_ITEMS.md`.

### Fixed: `run_periodic_job(optimize=True)` relaxes GDF-routed jobs on the GDF objective (2026-07-30)

G-PBC-002 optimizer wiring. Previously the runner's optimize block
unconditionally called `bipole_optimize.relax_atoms`, so a job whose

point of a surface the job never reported. The GDF dispatch now

and the multi-k KRHF/KRKS/KUHF/KUKS drivers alike), and the optimizer

force objective (`force objective = GDF analytic gradient (rsgdf)`).

rejects (mdf fits, smearing, DFT+U, ...) surface the driver's

use `jk_method="bipole"` / `relax_full` for variable-cell work).
Non-GDF routes keep the BIPOLE relaxation byte-identical.

## [v0.15.91] - 2026-07-30 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Fixed: GDF nuclear energy was a truncated Ewald sum -- and it was the whole "dense-core gradient discrepancy" (2026-07-29)

The 3D GDF drivers computed `e_nuc` via `nuclear_repulsion_per_cell`
under the forced EWALD_3D gauge, whose real-space Ewald sum truncates at
`lat_opts.nuclear_cutoff_bohr`. On dense ionic cells that is unconverged:
MgO primitive FCC at 18 bohr carries a 2.1e-5 Ha error with a spurious
geometry dependence (FD slope +2.574e-5 Ha/bohr where the converged Ewald
slope is +3.074e-7). The Gamma setup (`_pbc_gdf_gamma_setup`, all four
`run_pbc_gdf_*` drivers), `run_rhf_periodic_gamma_gdf` (Ewald-JK branch
only; the molecular-limit branch keeps its matched-cutoff bare-gauge
pair), and both multi-k GDF drivers (`run_krhf_periodic_gdf` 3D path,
`run_kuhf_periodic_gdf`) now use the converged `ewald_nuclear_repulsion`
for `dim == 3`; the slab path is unchanged. Dense-cell GDF total energies
shift by up to ~2e-5 Ha (toward PySCF's converged `energy_nuc`);
vacuum-box anchors are unchanged at the 1e-9 level.

This closes the long-standing dense-core analytic-vs-FD gradient
inconsistency (~2.544e-5 Ha/bohr on MgO/STO-3G, step-size-independent):
the analytic gradient differentiates the converged Ewald nuclear term and
was exact all along -- the FD was differentiating the energy's truncation
artefact. Post-fix, the untailed MgO full-SCF FD gate collapses from
2.544e-5 to 3e-10..5e-9 across h = 1e-4..8e-4, and the tailed (auto-tail)
gate passes at 3.7e-9/5.9e-9. Consequences: the tailed dense-core rsgdf
gradient holds are lifted (the failure was tail-independent, exactly as
the driver-level artefact predicts), and the dense-core RuntimeWarning
advisory ("forces accurate to ~1e-4") is retired.
`PBCGDFResult.gradient_conditioning` remains as an informational
fit-response sensitivity diagnostic.
`tests/test_periodic_gdf_gradient.py`: 48 passed.

## [v0.15.89] - 2026-07-29 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Added: a G-resolved-weight pair-FT gradient kernel makes GDF forces 11x faster (2026-07-29)

The 3c side of the GDF gradient assemblies used to drive the scalar-weight
pair-FT gradient kernel once per auxiliary function, redoing the expensive
Fourier-derivative work each time. The per-aux batch reduces exactly to one
contraction with the G-resolved complex pair weight
`Q[munu, G] = sum_p pw_p[munu] rw_p(G)` (one ZGEMM), so the new OpenMP
kernel `ao_pair_fourier_transform_gamma_gradient_gweighted` does a single
FT-derivative pass for the whole batch. The existing scalar kernel is
byte-identical; a separability parity gate pins batched == summed-looped at
~1e-12 on both the s-s fast path and the general-L branch, and the 3c
isolation FD gates re-verify end-to-end exactness at 1e-7 unchanged.

Measured: the production-default rsgdf RHF gradient (H2/STO-3G, ke=200)
drops 34.7 s to 3.1 s (11.2x) with the gradient value unchanged, and the
full gradient test file drops ~105 s to 36 s. This also removes most of
the cost blocker recorded against tailed dense-core gradients (whose
12,841 s was dominated by exactly this loop); their accuracy diagnosis
remains open before the fail-closed guard lifts.
`tests/test_periodic_gdf_gradient.py`: 47 passed.

## [v0.15.88] - 2026-07-29 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Fixed: screened hybrids (hse06) on symmetry-reduced meshes now use the exact wedge fold and the orbit reduction (2026-07-29)

A `c_sr`-only functional never builds the corrected Ewald split (its erfc
exchange arm is convergent in real space), so the wedge-native IBZ work
never reached it: on a symmetry-reduced mesh its real-space K_erfc
consumed the plain weighted wedge fold of the density. That fold uses
each irreducible representative in place of its orbit average -- a
**first-order** density error in exchange on shift-bearing cells at
multi-cell cutoffs, invisible on pure DFT (where the error is second
order) and untouched by the full-range tests. The RKS and UKS drivers now
build the standalone star unfolding for `c_sr`-only jobs on reduced 3D
meshes, feed J/K/XC the exact orbit-summed fold, and route K_erfc through
the SYM3b orbit reduction -- the same treatment the full-range path got.
H2 hse06 wedge == full mesh is pinned bit-identical for both drivers,
with `used_kpoint_symmetry_unfolding` set on the wedge result. Slab
(2D) screened hybrids on reduced meshes keep the historical fold; that
gap stays recorded in `handovers/HANDOVER_OPEN_BUGS_V015.md`.

### Added: projector-based GAPW one-centre expansion module (energy evaluator, experimental) (2026-07-29)

`vibeqc.periodic_gapw_projector` implements the oracle-validated
multipole-consistent augmentation construction (LHP99 Sec. 4.2 / KP2000
Eqs. 11-25): augmentation spheres only on pruned atoms, exact on-centre
plus confined region-weighted LSQ off-centre one-centre expansions with
shared hard/soft off-centre coefficients, per-lm compensation, no radial
window. On the H2O/STO-3G fixed-density Hartree identity it lands within
tens of mHa of the gauge-consistent target where the production
block-restricted augmentation is -4.2 Ha off (the filed H2O wrong-answer
bug); single atoms Ne/He validate under the same construction.
Energy-evaluator only: the production GAPW SCF is unchanged until the
matching analytic Fock lands (`tests/test_periodic_gapw_projector.py`;
overlapping pruned spheres fail closed).

### Performance: wedge (IBZ) exchange builds are orbit-reduced -- 4.8x per iteration on the real-space arm (2026-07-29)

The wedge-native IBZ support shrank diagonalisation and the k-space
exchange arms by the star multiplicity, but the **real-space** erfc
exchange build (`build_jk_2e_real_space`) still paid full cost -- profiled
at **94 %** of a wedge SCF iteration on LiH rock-salt at a 12-bohr cutoff
(45 s of 45.2 s), which is why a wedge run could come out *slower* than
the full mesh (measured 0.68x).

The wedge path now routes its erfc exchange arms through the SYM3b
orbit-reduced builder (`bipole_symmetry_fock.build_jk_reduced_symmetrized`,
the machinery BIPOLE has used since `754de6fd1`): K is built only at
orbit-representative shell-pair blocks (104 of 880 on LiH at cutoff 12;
the ratio grows with cutoff) and the rest reconstructed by Wigner-D
rotation. Measured on the LiH wedge SCF: **45.2 -> 9.4 s per iteration
(4.8x)**, 1187.9 -> 149.8 s wall (7.9x with the iteration-count change).
The mapping is built once per SCF on the same radial cell list the K
builder uses, so block indexing is untouched, and one mapping serves both
exchange arms and every iteration.

Scope and honesty notes. The reduced build equals the **symmetrized**
full build; on shift-bearing cells that differs from the raw build by the
operator truncation asymmetry at loose cutoffs (the LiH wedge energy
moved 2.7 mHa at cutoff 12 -- *toward* the full-mesh answer, narrowing
the wedge-vs-full gap from 4.41 to 1.67 mHa; both still coincide once the
sums fold-converge). The reduction is therefore enabled **only on the
wedge path**, whose density is already the orbit-symmetrized object --
full-mesh jobs keep the raw builder and stay byte-identical, pinned by
test. The bare `1/r` kernel arm (Gamma molecular-limit path) always uses
the full builder: the SYM3b bit-identity suite pins only erfc kernels.
Bit-identity of the reduced K against `symmetrize_fock_blocks(full K)` is
pinned in situ on the EWALD route (1e-12, shift-bearing LiH cell).

rebuilt at 2.14.0, doc links updated to match.

### Added: the public closed-shell DLPNO-(T1) route now reports its TNO domains (2026-07-29)

`LocalCCSDResult` carried the triples energy and nothing about the domains
behind it. A user who set a positive `tcut_tno` got no feedback at all: no
per-triple sizes, no mean domain, no indication that a triple had been
truncated out of existence. The experimental open-shell engine was better
instrumented than the production closed-shell route it was derived from.

This is not a shipped wrong answer: `LocalCCSDOptions.tcut_tno` defaults to
`0.0`, the full union span, so a default `dlpno-ccsd(t)` job truncates
nothing. The gap was for users who opt in.

`LocalCCSDResult` now reports `avg_tno`, `tno_per_triple` and
`n_degenerate_tno_triples`, the last counting triples whose domain retained
fewer than three virtuals. A spatial triple excitation promotes three
electrons into three *distinct* virtuals, so such a triple contributes exactly
zero rather than approximately.

That diagnostic immediately locates the usable envelope on H2O/def2-SVP (full
domain `e_t = -0.003009059087680666` Ha, 19.0 TNOs per triple):

| `tcut_tno` | error | mean TNOs | smallest | collapsed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `1e-9` | `-0.000` µHa | 18.52 | 7 | 0 |
| `1e-7` | `+0.018` µHa | 18.20 | 4 | 0 |
| `1e-6` | `+0.086` µHa | 17.80 | 4 | 0 |
| `1e-5` | `+33.39` µHa | 15.68 | 1 | 1 |
| `1e-4` | `+582.45` µHa | 10.68 | 1 | 1 |

The error curve breaks exactly where the first triple collapses: 0.086 µHa at
`1e-6` with every domain at least four virtuals, then a 400-fold jump to
33 µHa at `1e-5` as one triple falls to a single virtual. The energy alone
cannot show that; the domain count can. The closed-shell route also tolerates
far coarser thresholds than the open-shell engine, which costs 30 to 64 µHa at
`1e-6` on comparable systems.

Collection is opt-in at the call site (`stats=` on the triples correction
entry points, `None` by default), so the truncation loops pay nothing when the
caller does not ask.
### Added: analytic forces on the production rsgdf Gamma GDF route (2026-07-29)

`run_pbc_gdf_rhf(gdf_method="rsgdf", compute_gradient=True)` computes the
analytic RHF gradient on the PySCF-µHa-parity production Gamma fit
(G-PBC-002 milestone 6, rungs 1-4). The rsgdf metric and 3c tensor are
reciprocal-space sums whose only atom dependence is each shell FT's
`exp(-iG.R)` phase, so their weighted centre derivatives are exact
ZGEMM-shaped kernels (base mesh + high-|G| tail, G-chunked; each pinned in
isolation at 1e-7); a dedicated cache reuses the compcell gradient's
divided-difference Fréchet inverse in the aux frame with the rsgdf
ABSOLUTE eigen threshold, and the J/K weight algebra carries over with
identity compensation. Fixed-density J and fixed-C K FD gates pass at 1e-7
with dropped modes forced; the full-SCF central difference on H2/STO-3G
sits at 3.6e-9 (ke=60) and 3.8e-9 (the ke=200 production default) against
1e-6 gates.

The envelope fails closed with pinned errors everywhere the derivative is
not exact yet: KS on rsgdf, Schwarz-screened fits, tailed dense-core fits
(the SCF's tail sweep is pair-FT-screened; the gradient rebuild is not),
and MDF. `tests/test_periodic_gdf_gradient.py`: 45 passed.

### Fixed: IBZ meshes on the multi-k GDF route crashed DFT and could expand a shifted mesh Γ-centred (2026-07-29)

The v0.15.85 IBZ→full-BZ expansion (375b6363d) expanded only the k-point
arrays inside the mesh normaliser; the driver's `BlochKMesh` handle stayed
the caller's wedge. Pure HF never noticed — its loop folds no real-space
density — but every KRKS/KUKS IBZ job died at the first XC build with
"size mismatch across k inputs" (8 per-k densities against the 6-point
wedge on H₂/STO-3G (2,2,2)). The drivers now adopt the expanded mesh for
*everything* derived from the kmesh — k-point arrays, weights, occupation
metadata, real-space density folds, and the result's k list — so the
mismatch cannot recur by construction.

Two adjacent expansion defects fixed in the same pass:

* **Shifted reductions expanded against the wrong parent.** The expansion
  read the shift flags as `is_shift` (the native `BlochKMesh` name); the
  Python `KPoints` dataclass calls them `shift`, so a classical
  half-step-shifted `KPoints` reduction silently rebuilt the **Γ-centred**
  mesh — a different BZ sampling (~44 mHa apart on MgO (2,2,2)). The
  original LiH verification compared exactly such a shifted reduction
  against the Γ-centred tuple mesh, so the bug masked itself: it "matched"
  because the shift was dropped. Both attribute spellings are honoured
  now, and the regression pins that a shifted reduction reproduces the
  shifted full mesh and *not* the tuple mesh.
* **`use_symmetry=True` meshes that reduce nothing were refused.** A mesh
  whose points all sit in distinct orbits (identity `ir_mapping`, e.g.
  (2,1,1) on a cubic vacuum box) already *is* the full quadrature; the
  expansion's metadata check mistook it for an unexpandable reduction.
  It now simply runs.

Verified IBZ == explicit-full-mesh on H₂/12-bohr: RKS-PBE0 (2,2,2)
bit-identical closed shell, KUKS-PBE bit-identical on the H₂⁺ doublet,
and shifted-KPoints KRHF bit-identical against the shifted full mesh.
Regressions: `test_periodic_k_gdf.py::test_ibz_reduced_kmesh_dft_matches_full_mesh`,
`::test_ibz_expansion_rebuilds_the_shifted_parent_not_gamma`,
`::test_symmetry_requested_but_unreduced_mesh_is_accepted`, and
`test_periodic_kuhf_gdf.py::test_kuks_ibz_reduced_kmesh_matches_full_mesh`.

### Fixed: vibe-view showed crystals with half their bonds (2026-07-28)

Each bond recorded only which two atoms it joins, with no room to say which
periodic copy of the second atom it reaches. In a dense crystal a pair of atoms
is bonded through several copies at once, so those bonds collapsed onto one and
the structure appeared under-bonded: rocksalt showed three neighbours per ion
instead of six, and face-centred copper three instead of twelve. Bonds now carry
that information, and a crystal renders with its full coordination, every bond
drawn at the real interatomic distance. Structures whose neighbours are all
distinct atoms, including diamond and ordinary molecules, were already correct
and are unchanged. Connectivity supplied by a producer is also unchanged.
### Added: ASE-driven periodic relaxations on the GDF gradient ladder (2026-07-29)

`VibeQCPeriodic(backend="gdf")` (and `periodic_forces(backend="gdf")`)
routes Gamma-only jobs through the compcell GDF drivers with the analytic
gradient ladder landed this cycle — RHF, RKS, UHF, and UKS, pure and
global-hybrid functionals, on the production AFT-corrected fit — so ASE
optimizers, NEB, and MD can drive them (G-PBC-002 milestone 5). This also
fills the ASE bridge's historical open-shell-HF hole: the default
`backend="ewald"` defers UHF forces, the GDF backend has them. Multi-k GDF
gradients fail closed with an actionable error (the Item-4 follow-up).

Gates: calculator energy+forces are identical to the direct
`run_pbc_gdf_rhf(compute_gradient=True)` values (1e-10), the open-shell-HF
triplet works end-to-end, multi-k fails closed, and a BFGS relaxation of
stretched H2 on LDA converges in a dozen steps to a sane bond length.
`tests/test_ase_periodic_calculator.py`: 13 passed (4 new).

## [v0.15.85] - 2026-07-29 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Added: symmetry-reduced (IBZ) k-meshes now work for exact exchange on the multi-k EWALD_3D drivers, wedge-native (2026-07-29)

`run_{rhf,rks,uks}_periodic_multi_k_ewald3d` accept
`monkhorst_pack(..., use_symmetry=True)` meshes for Hartree-Fock and global
hybrids. Until now these failed closed whenever full-range exact exchange was
needed, because exchange couples `D(k')` at every full-BZ point to a
`k - k'`-dependent kernel: weighting the irreducible representatives is not
orbit summation (measured **+1.389 Ha** wrong on MgO before the guard
existed).

The SCF stays **wedge-native** -- it diagonalises only at the irreducible
points, which is the whole efficiency of a reduced mesh (6 of 27 points at a
cubic `(3,3,3)`) -- and the density is unfolded to the full Brillouin zone
per iteration by the star transport `D(Vk) = W D(k) W^H` with the
phase-dressed representation matrices `W(V;k)` of Pisani, Dovesi & Roetti,
*Hartree-Fock Ab Initio Treatment of Crystalline Systems* (Springer, 1988),
Eqs. II.7.15/II.7.21, plus time reversal `D(-k) = D(k)*`; the real-space
density is rebuilt from the unfolded list (the orbit sum, Eq. II.7.48),
since the weighted wedge fold uses each representative in place of its
orbit average and is wrong at multi-cell cutoffs. This is distinct from
the GDF route's 2026-07-28 IBZ handling, which expands the mesh up front
and pays full-mesh cost; here the wedge saving is real: the exchange
target loop and every diagonalisation shrink by the star multiplicity.

Verified: H2/12-bohr HF and PBE0 at `(2,2,2)` and `(3,3,3)` (13
time-reversal star members) are **bit-identical** between the wedge and the
full mesh, including the reported J/K split; closed-shell UKS == RKS holds
on the wedge. On shift-bearing cells (rock-salt: 42 of 48 operations move
the anion into a neighbouring cell, so the transport carries atom-dependent
Bloch phases) the wedge and full-mesh results agree only once the lattice
sums are fold-converged -- at loose cutoffs the truncated operators
themselves break the point symmetry (a radial cell list is not closed under
the pair-resolved cell action `R.g + s_b - s_a`), and the two answers
differ by that truncation asymmetry: measured on MgO `(2,2,2)` Hcore
densities, max transport residual 1.19 (cutoff 8) -> 3.6e-2 (12) ->
4.8e-6 (16) -> 8.0e-9 (20). The wedge answer is the symmetrized one. A
regression pins both the loose-cutoff asymmetry and its collapse.

Explicit k-point lists (no Monkhorst-Pack star metadata) still fail closed
-- there is nothing to unfold from.

Citations: Pisani/Dovesi/Roetti 1988 + Dovesi, Int. J. Quantum Chem. 29,
1755 (1986) (the journal version of the SS II.7 machinery) fire via the new
`kpoint_symmetry_unfolding` route whenever a result carries
`used_kpoint_symmetry_unfolding`.

### Added: analytic Gamma UKS gradient completes the GDF compcell ladder (2026-07-29)

`run_pbc_gdf_uks(functional=..., compute_gradient=True)` computes the
analytic Gamma compcell gradient on either AFT setting (G-PBC-002 milestone
4), completing the Gamma ladder: RHF, RKS, UHF, and now UKS all
differentiate the fit they converged. The shared open-shell assembly takes
the functional's exact-exchange fraction — scaling the per-spin exchange
gradient and its per-spin Ewald-shift term, with 1.0 reproducing the UHF
path bit-identically and 0 (pure DFT) skipping both — and the driver adds
the spin-polarised XC Pulay via the existing
`xc_lattice_gradient_contribution_uks` primitive on exactly the SCF's own
grid and density-set conventions.

Gates: UKS(M=1) collapses onto the FD-validated RKS gradient at machine
precision (3e-15, energies bit-identical) for LDA and PBE0, and the H2
triplet passes central-difference FD on the production AFT-on surface at
4e-8 (LDA) and 4e-7 (PBE0), against the 1e-6 gate. rsgdf and smearing
requests fail closed. Full gradient file: 39 passed.

### Added: (T1) TNO calibration extended across radicals and spin multiplicity (2026-07-29)

The `tcut_tno` calibration landed earlier today rested on a single doublet
(OH/def2-SVP), which is not enough to recommend a threshold. Repeating the
sweep on NH2 and on triplet CH2 (error vs full domain; `d` counts triples that
collapsed below three spin virtuals):

| system | multiplicity | `1e-9` | `1e-6` | `1e-4` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| OH  | 2 | `+12.39` µHa | `+63.37` µHa | `+759.06` µHa, `d=13` |
| NH2 | 2 | `+7.62` µHa | `+37.02` µHa | `+1177.91` µHa, `d=9` |
| CH2 | 3 | `+5.73` µHa | `+30.25` µHa | `+706.18` µHa, `d=10` |

Across all three, `1e-9` stays within 12 µHa and `1e-6` within 64 µHa, and the
collapse into degenerate triples sets in between `1e-6` and `1e-4` in every
case. The triplet is not an outlier, so neither the `1e-9` recommendation nor
the `1e-6` calibrated boundary depends on spin multiplicity over this sample.

Scope, stated because it is a small sample: three systems, one basis
(def2-SVP), first-row radicals only. CH3 was in the planned set and was
dropped after its full-domain point failed to finish in 27 minutes; its
49-dimensional spin-virtual space makes it impractical for this Python engine
at full domain. The multi-system numbers are recorded evidence, not pinned by
a regression: each def2-SVP point costs 2 to 4 minutes, and no cheaper system
can stand in, since a minimal basis collapses at every positive threshold. The
existing slow-marked OH ratchet remains the pinned one.

### Added: reclaim runtime slots no live job is using (2026-07-28)

Slots would otherwise accumulate forever. After a successful flip, slots that no
non-terminal job is executing from are deleted.

Liveness is derived from each spec's **command** — the path the process actually
exec'd — rather than a recorded pin, so it stays true even if a pin was written
differently, is missing, or was later rewritten. Terminal jobs hold nothing:
their process is gone.

Conservative in the safe direction throughout. An unrecognised or unparseable
spec contributes no SHA, and `reclaimable` independently refuses to propose
`current` or `previous` regardless. Deleting a slot a running job holds would
turn a silent version mix into a hard `ImportError` — better, but still a broken
run — so a held slot is never a candidate.

Reclamation runs at flip time rather than on a timer, because that is the only
moment the set grows, and it is best-effort: a slot that cannot be removed is a
disk-space problem, never a correctness one, and must not fail an update that
already succeeded.

### Added: first high-spin coverage for the open-shell local DLPNO engine (2026-07-29)

Every test of `run_local_dlpno_uccsd` in `tests/test_dlpno_uccsd_local.py`, and
every case in `tests/test_dlpno_uccsd.py`, used `multiplicity=2`. The alpha and
beta occupied blocks were therefore always within one orbital of each other,
and nothing exercised the code that treats them separately: the `(T1)` rotation
diagonalises the occupied Fock in each spin block on its own, and the pair,
singles and PAO domains are built per spin.

Triplet CH2 (`multiplicity=3`, two more alpha than beta occupieds) now pins
both triples modes against the dense pilot at full domain. The test asserts the
fixture is genuinely high-spin rather than trusting the multiplicity argument,
so it cannot silently degrade into another doublet case.

No bug surfaced: the engine already reproduces the pilot exactly for high spin
(`e_corr` to 1e-8, `e_t` to 1e-11). This closes a coverage gap, not a defect.

### Fixed: vibe-view missed bonds across periodic boundaries (2026-07-28)

Automatic bonding looked only at raw coordinates, so a periodic structure lost
every bond that continues through its own cell walls: two atoms a normal bond
length apart across a boundary were treated as being a whole cell width apart
and left unbonded, while the same pair in mid-cell bonded as expected. Crystals
and slabs therefore rendered with their surfaces artificially unbonded. Bonding
now accounts for the surrounding periodic images. Only directions that are
actually periodic are considered, so a slab does not bond through its vacuum
gap, and non-periodic structures are unaffected.

### Added: slot-enabled venv updates build alongside and flip on success (2026-07-28)

Completes the immutable-runtime work for venv hosts. A program with
`runtime_slot_root` set now builds a **new** per-SHA slot alongside the running
one and flips `current` only after the build and its import check pass. A job
already running keeps the interpreter it started with, because that interpreter
lives in its own slot and nothing in this path writes to it.

That is the whole point: an in-place update rewrites the very files a live
process imports from, so a job paused across one can serve some modules from
`sys.modules` while importing others off the rewritten disk — two versions in one
process, silently. Reproduced 2026-07-26.

A failed build leaves `current` where it was. There is no rollback step because
there is no forward step to undo: the flip is the last thing that happens, so a
half-built slot is simply never published.

The inner build reuses the ordinary update path verbatim against a slot-local
program — fetch, checkout, tag verification, update script, import check —
rather than forking that logic, which would be two code paths to keep honest
instead of one.

Slot updates require `--expected-sha`: a slot is keyed by commit and must be
chosen before the build starts, whereas an untagged `git pull` only learns its
SHA afterwards. Every fleet update already passes it from the accepted release
report, so this costs nothing operationally.

**Opt-in and inert by default.** `runtime_slot_root` is unset on every host
today, so every host keeps the historical in-place behaviour until someone opts
a host in. Pinned by a test.
### Fixed: the GDF gradient's months-old 3.4 mHa/bohr FD residual was a nuclear-gauge mismatch; AFT-corrected fits are now differentiable and the UHF gradient wiring is released (2026-07-29)

Three connected closures on the Gamma GDF compcell gradient (G-PBC-002
milestone 3):

**The residual, identified and fixed.** Every GDF gradient route carried a
documented, flat `3.394e-3 Ha/bohr` FD residual on the H2 control whose
origin had resisted identification. Milestone-2/3 measurements narrowed it
— identical across RHF/LDA/PBE/PBE0/UHF-triplet, at both `V_ne` meshes,
and on both AFT surfaces, so density-independent and purely geometric —
and a two-line isolation probe then found it whole:
`nuclear_repulsion_gradient_per_cell` differentiates the truncated
*direct* 1/r lattice sum regardless of `coulomb_method`, while the GDF
setup's `e_nuc` is the Ewald-gauge value (the BIPOLE route had
independently hit and fixed the same inconsistency). Both GDF assemblies
now use the gauge-consistent `ewald_nuclear_repulsion_gradient` (itself
FD-exact at `2.6e-9`), and the full-SCF FD residual collapsed six orders
of magnitude to `3-6e-9 Ha/bohr` across RHF, PBE0, and the UHF triplet.
The FD gates tightened from the historical `5e-3` to `1e-6`, and a
suspected-sibling flag is filed for the other periodic-gradient owners
whose routes consume the same helper.

**AFT-corrected fits are differentiable.** The weighted 2c and 3c AFT
centre derivatives (landed as milestone 3a, each FD-pinned in isolation at
`1e-7` in both FT conventions) are wired into the J/K gradient assemblies
through new AFT provenance on the fit state and gradient cache, and the
closed-shell result now retains `aft_ft_convention`/`aft_precision`. The
`compute_gradient` requirement of `apply_aft_correction=False` is retired:
RHF and RKS gradients differentiate the production AFT-on fit exactly
(the AFT-on energy differs by ~70 mHa on the control, so a wrong AFT force
term could not hide inside the gate).

**The held UHF public wiring is released.**
`run_pbc_gdf_uhf(compute_gradient=True)` no longer raises: the 2026-07-20
hold existed precisely because forces on the incomplete AFT-off fit were
not worth exposing, and that reason is gone. The UHF(M=1)≡RHF algebra gate
now runs for real (agreement at `5e-7`), and the UHF triplet passes the
new AFT-on FD gate with everything else.

Tests: `tests/test_periodic_gdf_gradient.py` 37 passed, including the new
`test_full_scf_gradient_vs_fd_aft_on` (RHF/PBE0/UHF at `1e-6`, observed
`3-6e-9`) and the reworked hold pins.

### Changed: UHF and UKS BIPOLE share their spin helpers (2026-07-29)

First slice of M4 in the BIPOLE unification workstream. The three spin
helpers — per-k density splitting, single-spin density construction, and
per-spin Fermi-Dirac occupations — were duplicated as nested closures in
both open-shell drivers. They now live once in `pbc_bipole_common` and
are called from both. The copies differed only in type annotations,
docstring wording and line wrapping, plus one dead assignment in the UKS
copy; the richest form was adopted, following the M3a/M3b precedent.

Results are bit-identical: energies, iteration counts and full
per-iteration SCF traces match across UHF, UKS-LDA and smeared UHF for
both singlet and triplet.

M4 was re-measured before being taken, because the ruling that closed M3
asked for exactly that. In the ruling's own metric, UHF↔UKS is 76%
line-identical with 38 runs of at least ten lines covering 847 lines,
against RHF↔RKS's 50% and 24 runs covering 360 — about 22 shared lines
per hook point where M3 offered 4. M3's closure stands; this does not
reopen it.
### Fixed: GAPW radial Poisson diagonal double-count (2026-07-29)

`solve_poisson_radial` counted the `k' = k` radial shell in both its inner
and outer cumulative sums; at `r' = r` the two kernels coincide, so every
self-shell entered the Hartree potential twice. Individual radial Hartree
quantities (Gaussian self-energies, the compensator self-energy) were
systematically overestimated by 5-13% at the default `n_radial = 80`, worse
for sharper densities and only ~halved by doubling the grid. The error
largely cancels in the GAPW hard-minus-soft augmentation difference, which
is why total-energy parity gates never caught it; converged GAPW totals move
by O(10 mHa) on second-row atoms. The duplicated diagonal is now subtracted;
`tests/test_periodic_gapw_augment.py::TestRadialPoisson::test_poisson_gaussian_self_energy_matches_analytic`
pins Gaussian self-energies to <0.5% across exponents 1-414 on the
production Ne grid (pre-fix: 5.5-13.3%).

Recorded alongside (validation-method finding, no code change): the
historical GAPW second-row parity numbers ("Ne +339 mHa, O +215 mHa") were
measured against `run_rhf_periodic_gamma_gdf`, which on steep-primitive
dense-core cells is the G-GDF-001 `+PARITY_HELD` legacy fallback and sits
~0.38 Ha *below* the molecular limit for an isolated Ne atom in a 12-bohr
box (legacy GDF -126.9808 vs exact molecular RHF -126.6045; an isolated
neutral spherical atom's periodic total should approach the molecular value
to mHa). Against the honest oracle, GAPW Ne/STO-3G at 48^3 after this fix
is +53 mHa, not +413/+339 mHa. Future GAPW atom-parity gates should use the
molecular limit or a validated (rsgdf/PySCF-parity) reference, not the
legacy Gamma GDF fallback, on dense-core cells.

### Changed: GPW/GAPW results carry their converged Fock and overlap (2026-07-29)

`GpwScfResult` and `GapwScfResult` now store the (post-DIIS) Fock the SCF
actually diagonalized plus the Gamma lattice overlap, and the C++-hosted
driver forwards its native `RHFResult.fock`. `gpw_result_to_runner_shape`
surfaces these directly instead of reconstructing an HF-shaped
`Hcore + J - K/2` from scratch: the reconstruction cost a fresh AO-on-grid
chi build plus a molecular-limit JK build (~36% of a small GPW
`run_periodic_job` wall time) and was the wrong operator for KS/GAPW
results (un-augmented GPW J, no V_xc). The stored (F, S) eigenpairs
reproduce `mo_energies` to machine precision, pinned by regression tests;
the reconstruction path remains as a fallback for producers that predate
the fields.

### Added: materialize a runtime slot's source at an exact commit (2026-07-28)

`runtime_slots.materialize_source` populates a slot with a checkout at exactly
its own SHA, cloning from the host's existing checkout rather than the network —
the objects are already local, and a scheduler host may have no outbound access
at all.

`--local` hardlinks git's object store, and that is safe here precisely where it
was **not** safe for a venv: git objects are immutable and content-addressed,
never rewritten in place, and the slot's hardlink keeps its own reference alive
even if the source later prunes or repacks. A venv records absolute paths and
cannot be shared at all.

The checkout is verified against the requested SHA afterwards and fails closed
on any mismatch. Publishing a slot that does not contain its own commit is the
one failure this design cannot tolerate, so the post-check is unconditional
rather than trusting `git checkout`'s exit status. Idempotent, so a retried
deployment does not re-clone.

Still unreachable: nothing calls it, and no host behaviour changes. It does not
create the venv or build — that is the update script's job, run against the
derived slot-local program.

### Changed: canonical CC frozen-core default is the chemical core (documents a change shipped in v0.15.40)

Canonical and density-fitted CCSD and CCSD(T), and the FNO convenience
path in `run_job`, freeze one noble-gas chemical core per atom when no
explicit `n_frozen_core` is given (H2O freezes 1 orbital, CO2 freezes 3).
The previous default correlated all electrons. The change landed in
`d2e46663a` (the validated closed-shell DF-CCSD/(T) rewrite) and first
shipped in v0.15.40, but was not announced at the time; this entry
documents it retroactively per the maintainer decision of 2026-07-29.

Explicitly pinned inputs are unaffected. A pinned all-electron rerun of
the archived H2O/cc-pVDZ CCSD(T) case on v0.15.72 reproduces the
v0.15.21 artifact value to 1e-10 Ha, so the change is a default swap,
not a numerical regression. DLPNO-MP2/CCSD/CCSD(T) (`n_frozen = 0`) and
plain MP2/SCS-MP2/SOS-MP2 keep their all-electron defaults; the
double-hybrid internal MP2 pins all-electron explicitly.

Practical consequence: rerunning a stored correlated input written
before v0.15.40 without an explicit convention now computes the
frozen-core quantity. Pin `ccsd_options.n_frozen_core` (0 for
all-electron) to reproduce archived numbers exactly.

### Added: analytic Gamma RKS gradient on the periodic GDF preview route (2026-07-29)

`run_pbc_gdf_rhf(functional=..., compute_gradient=True)` now computes the
closed-shell KS analytic gradient instead of raising (G-PBC-002 milestone 2),
on the same explicit compcell/`apply_aft_correction=False` preview envelope
the RHF wiring already uses. `compute_gdf_gradient_rks_gamma` composes the
existing general-`alpha` compcell J/K/one-electron/overlap-Lagrangian
machinery — pure functionals skip the exchange gradient entirely; global
hybrids scale the exchange and its Ewald exxdiv-shift term by the
functional's exact-exchange fraction, a scale factor the former
`alpha_hf=1.0` guard had made moot (bit-identical at RHF's `alpha=1`) —
with the separately validated lattice-summed XC Pulay primitive
`xc_lattice_gradient_contribution`, rebuilt on exactly the SCF's own XC
quadrature (molecular grid + home-cell density, or periodic-Becke grid +
Gamma-torus density, following the SCF's `use_periodic_becke`). The
energy-weighted density uses the converged KS eigenvalues directly, which
are variational on this route because the GDF Fock includes `V_xc`.
Range-separated functionals never reach the gradient (the SCF fails closed
on them); rsgdf/AFT-on requests keep their fail-closed errors for KS.

Verified: LDA (the `alpha=0` no-exchange branch), PBE (the GGA piece of the
XC Pulay), and PBE0 (`alpha`-scaled exchange + shift) each match a central
difference of the same driver's energy at the landed 5e-3 Ha/bohr gate on
H2/STO-3G/12-bohr, and a sharper differential gate holds the KS-added terms
to 2e-4 of the documented, still-unidentified ~3.4e-3 residual the RHF
preview already carries on that control. The same measurements narrowed that
open residual: it is functional-, alpha-, and V_ne-mesh-independent, so it
lives in the non-XC, non-exchange assembly
(`handovers/HANDOVER_GDF_GRADIENT_DEFERRED.md` §1). Three new regressions in
`tests/test_periodic_gdf_gradient.py` (full file 38 passed).

### Performance: the GPW route stops rebuilding the same V_ne three times (2026-07-29)

A GPW `run_periodic_job` built the *identical* nuclear-attraction matrix
three times over — once inside the SCF, once in `evaluate_gpw_energy`,
and once more in the runner adapter — for the same system, basis and
lattice options. On LiH in a 6-bohr cube (STO-3G, PBE, 80 Ha) that was
1.72 s of a 4.64 s run, about a quarter of the wall spent recomputing a
matrix already in hand.

The three paths share one chokepoint, `_ewald_v_ne_gamma`, which is a
pure function of `(basis, system)`, so it now memoises. Measured
alternating with the cache disabled, best of three: **8.10 s → 5.95 s
(26%)**, builds 3 → 1, energy bit-identical.

The key is the matrix's *content*, not the identity of the objects that
produced it. That distinction is load-bearing rather than fastidious:
`PeriodicSystem` is mutable from Python — `atom.xyz` and `lattice` are
both settable — so an identity-keyed cache would hand a geometry
optimiser the previous step's V_ne and return a wrong answer rather than
a slow one. A regression moves a nucleus in place and requires the cache
to miss. Results are handed back as copies, so a caller scaling its own
V_ne cannot poison the next one, and the cache is bounded to two entries.

### Added: open-shell DLPNO-(T1) TNO thresholds are calibrated, and domain collapse is now visible (2026-07-29)

Positive `tcut_tno` under `triples_mode="t1"` ran but had never been
calibrated: the only coverage pinned a single unphysical `1e-18` threshold,
which says nothing about what a user should set.

Measured on OH/def2-SVP (full domain `e_t = -1.778474224055274e-03` Ha at 29.0
spin virtuals per triple). Truncation only ever loses correlation, so every
error is positive:

| `tcut_tno` | error vs full domain | mean TNOs/triple |
|---|---|---|
| `1e-12` | `+11.27` µHa | 26.07 |
| `1e-9`  | `+12.39` µHa | 24.73 |
| `1e-6`  | `+63.37` µHa | 19.92 |
| `1e-4`  | `+759.06` µHa | 10.55 (collapsing) |

`1e-9` — the `T_CutTNO` default of Guo et al. (2018) — costs 12 µHa
(0.008 kcal/mol) for a 15% smaller triples domain. No positive threshold is
free: `1e-12` already costs 11 µHa, so `tcut_tno=0` remains the only exact
setting. A slow-marked ratchet pins that the error grows monotonically with
the threshold, that it is signed, and that the domain shrinks monotonically.

`1e-6` is the coarsest *calibrated* value: through it every triple keeps at
least three spin virtuals (smallest domain 8), so the error is pure
truncation. By `1e-4` the smallest domain is a single virtual and 13 of the 84
triples are identically zero, so that row mixes truncation with collapse and
is not a truncation error.

The calibration also turned up a trap worth naming. On a **minimal basis the
threshold is all-or-nothing**: OH/STO-3G retains only 3.0 TNOs per triple, and
a triple excitation needs three *distinct* spin virtuals, so any positive
`tcut_tno` drops 75 of its 84 triples below three and `e_t` collapses from
`-2.29e-07` Ha to order `1e-46`. The correction does not degrade — it ceases
to exist. Read as a calibration curve that would look like catastrophic
threshold sensitivity; it is a basis-size artefact.

`LocalUCCSDResult` therefore gains `n_degenerate_tno_triples`, counting
evaluated triples whose TNO domain holds fewer than three spin virtuals. A
nonzero value distinguishes "truncated a little" from "truncated past the
point where the correction exists", which the energy alone cannot show.

### Fixed: a non-PSD periodic `S(k)` was misdiagnosed as a code defect (2026-07-29)

Hitting this while benchmarking: a multi-k job on LiH/6-31G in a 12-bohr cube
aborted with *"An AO Gram matrix must be PSD by construction; this indicates
an upstream bug (lattice cutoff, image-cell summing, or Bloch sampling)."*
That framing is wrong for a periodic overlap, and it sends users hunting for
a defect when the first thing to try is a larger cutoff.

`S(k) = sum_g e^{ik.R_g} S(g)` is a Gram matrix of Bloch functions, so the
**converged** sum is positive-definite. A radial cutoff keeps `g` and `-g`
together, so the truncated sum stays Hermitian --- but Hermitian is not PSD,
and the Gram structure that guarantees it survives only in the limit. A
negative eigenvalue at a loose cutoff is an expected truncation artefact that
shrinks as the cutoff grows. Measured on a (4,4,2) mesh:

* LiF/6-31G, 8-bohr cube: min eig `S(k)` = -1.400 (cutoff 8) -> -0.557 (12)
  -> -0.102 (16) -> -3.6e-3 (20) -> **+7.4e-5** (26) -> +9.6e-5 (40, flat).
* LiH/6-31G, 12-bohr cube: -0.115 (12) -> **+0.021** (20) -> +0.0183 (40).

Both recover. The converged values are genuinely small because 6-31G on cells
that dense is close to over-complete --- a basis and cell choice, not a bug.
This is what CRYSTAL calls *numerical linear dependence*, and its EIGS
documentation makes the same connection: the more severe the computational
conditions, the closer to zero an eigenvalue may sit without numerical risk,
and negative values signal numerical linear dependence (CRYSTAL23 manual,
EIGS).

So the periodic message now leads with the actual cause and the actionable
fix --- raise the cutoff, the eigenvalue should climb toward a small positive
value --- and only then says what to suspect if it *doesn't* converge, which
is the signature that would indicate a real image-summing or Bloch-sampling
defect. The molecular path keeps the original "upstream bug" wording, where
it is correct because no lattice sum is involved; that is pinned by an
existing test.

The remediation hint also now actually reaches the multi-k EWALD_3D drivers.
`run_rhf_periodic_multi_k_ewald3d`, `run_rks_...` and `run_uks_...` called the
overlap preflight without it, so only the GDF route was giving users guidance;
all four now share one hint, moved to `vibeqc.linear_dependence` from the GDF
module that happened to own it.

### Fixed: dense-core MDF fails closed instead of returning garbage, and MDF's validated vacuum-box envelope loses its false parity tag (2026-07-29)

`gdf_method="mdf"` on compact dense-core cells (Z >= 8 in < 250 bohr³/atom,
the MgO/STO-3G class) inherited the Gamma-only tight-ionic instability of its
compcell real-space Hartree lineage, and returned the wreckage behind a
`+PARITY_HELD` warning whose remediation — the rsgdf high-|G| tail knob —
does not exist for MDF. Measured while closing the G-GDF-001 MDF sub-gate:
Gamma MDF on MgO primitive FCC/STO-3G is non-convergent and trial-dependent
at `mdf_ke_cutoff=40/60` (+1703/+2143/+418 Ha) and falsely reports
`converged=True` at `ke=80` at -1651 Ha — ~1380 Ha below the out-of-process
PySCF MDF reference (-271.0499 Ha) and past the energy-sanity guard; the
multi-k `(1,1,2)` route lands -11741 Ha non-converged. All five GDF drivers
(`run_pbc_gdf_{rhf,uhf,uks}`, `run_k{r,u}hf_periodic_gdf`) now raise
`NotImplementedError` on this class, naming the working alternative (the
default rsgdf, which auto-tails to PySCF parity at Gamma and accepts
`rsgdf_tail_ke_cutoff` at multi-k).

The same classifier was also wrong in the other direction: it tagged MDF's
*validated* envelope — the steep-core atom in a vacuum box, where MDF closes
the all-electron floor at a modest mesh (Ne/STO-3G/10-bohr: 0.14 mHa vs
PySCF MDF) — as `+PARITY_HELD`, because its tight-basis branch keys on the
rsgdf reciprocal mesh, which is irrelevant to MDF's real-space core
handling. MDF now holds only on the compact-dense-core class (which raises),
so the Ne-in-box run carries a clean backend tag and no warning; its energy
is unchanged (pinned to 1e-6 Ha). rsgdf classification and behavior are
untouched. Regressions: three new tests in `tests/test_pbc_gdf_mdf.py`
(fail-closed across all five entry points, two-sided classifier pins,
untagged-backend + energy pin).

### Fixed: vibe-view slab cutting used a spacing that was not a distance (2026-07-28)

Cutting a crystal along a Miller plane computed the spacing between planes from
the Miller indices alone, without reference to the lattice, so the number had no
units and was wrong for every cell: the (001) planes of a cubic 5 angstrom cell
were treated as 1 angstrom apart. Slab thickness and the choice of which atoms
form each layer both followed from it, so a slab was neither the thickness it
reported nor the number of layers requested. The spacing is now derived from the
reciprocal lattice.

Orientations this builder cannot represent are now refused rather than returned.
Vacuum is stacked along the third cell vector, which only produces a real slab
when the other two lie in the cut plane; other orientations previously came back
as a box that was not the surface it claimed to be.

### Performance: the corrected multi-k exchange now runs in parallel over k (2026-07-29)

The `q = k - k'` channel loop behind the corrected Ewald exchange split is
**O(n_k^2)**, and v0.15.84 put it on the critical path of every multi-k
Hartree-Fock job and every multi-k global hybrid. Measured on an
18-basis-function cell it cost 16.5 s per SCF iteration at a 32-point mesh
and 23 s at 64 points, single-threaded: the per-k loop was plain Python.

Each k is independent given the shared channel cache and the full density
list, and the contractions spend most of their time inside BLAS with the
GIL released, so the loop now farms over threads.
`VIBEQC_EXCHANGE_K_THREADS` overrides the worker count (`1` forces
serial); the default follows `get_num_threads()`, and meshes below four
k-points stay serial because the pool costs more than it saves.

* **Kernel:** 3.8x in a controlled same-process comparison at 32 k, and
  7.1x on 16 threads (16.5 s -> 2.3 s) measured against a cold-cache
  baseline.
* **End to end:** an SCF gains in proportion to how exchange-dominated it
  is. A small H2/6-31G job at 32 k went 4.55 s -> 3.58 s, with identical
  energy and iteration count; a large hybrid at many k-points, where
  exchange dominates, approaches the kernel figure.
* **Results are bit-identical, not merely close.** Every k performs the
  same operations in the same order; threads only decide who runs which
  k. Pinned by
  `tests/test_periodic_corrected_exchange.py::test_threaded_k_loop_is_bit_identical_to_serial`,
  which asserts `np.array_equal`.

The first pass over k stays **serial on purpose**: the channel tables are
built lazily, so a cold parallel pass would have every worker miss,
recompute the same `B` tensors, and race to store them, orphaning the
losing writers' entries so they are recomputed on every later iteration.
One serial pass fills the cache; every later call is a pure read.

This is also an MPI seam, and a *different* one from the k-point farming
already landed under `handovers/HANDOVER_MPI.md` next-step 4: that
partitions the GDF cderi q-groups once per SCF setup and has nothing per
iteration. This loop runs every iteration and is where the O(n_k^2) cost
lives, so it is the one that rewards multi-node farming. Same per-k split,
results gathered rather than shared.

### Added: vibe-view builds from a SMILES string in the molecule dialog (2026-07-28)

The Build molecule dialog gains a SMILES field beside the molecule-name one, so
structures the curated name database does not cover can be typed directly. The
new structure arrives with auto-optimize switched on, so what the user keeps is
a vibe-qc relaxed geometry rather than the generator's starting guess. The field
appears whether or not the optional extra is installed; without it, building
reports the exact install command. A malformed string reports the problem and
adds no file.

### Fixed: vibe-view kept the previous file's zoom when another was opened (2026-07-28)

Opening or building a structure framed it correctly on the server but left the
browser showing the zoom from the file that was open before, because the viewer
renders in the browser and the browser keeps its own camera until a new one is
sent. Loading a large molecule while a small one was open put most of it outside
the viewport. The camera is now sent along with the new geometry. Live
hot-reload is unaffected and still preserves the viewpoint on purpose.

### Fixed: open-shell local DLPNO-(T1) refused screening thresholds that screened nothing (2026-07-29)

`run_local_dlpno_uccsd(..., triples_mode="t1")` rejected any `tcut_pairs > 0`
or `coupling_radius > 0` up front, before knowing whether those thresholds
removed a single triple. The refusal was decided on the raw threshold values,
so a `coupling_radius` chosen generously enough to screen nothing still
blocked (T1) outright.

(T1) rotates the occupied indices into the per-spin canonical basis, where a
weak-pair label or an occupied distance has no meaning — every canonical
occupied is a mixture of every LMO — so it genuinely cannot carry a screened
triple list. That part of the guard is correct and stays. What changed is
*when* it fires: the decision now uses the realised screened-triple set, so
thresholds that screen nothing run the exact full triple list, and thresholds
that remove even one triple still fail closed, now reporting the offending
count (`screen 84 of 84 occupied triples`) instead of a bare refusal.

The guard and the (T0) triple loop were also collapsed onto one shared
`triple_is_screened` predicate, so the two cannot drift apart.

Scope check, recorded because it bounds the benefit: on OH/STO-3G 16 of the 36
spin-orbital pairs carry an identically zero MP2 energy, so *any* positive
`tcut_pairs` — even 1e-14 — screens them and every one of the 84 triples. Only
`coupling_radius` reaches the new no-op branch on that system; a test pins
this rather than leaving the relaxation looking broader than it is.

Not claimed: the screened local (T1) itself. Recovering it needs the iterative
Gauss-Seidel algorithm of Guo, Riplinger, Becker, Liakos, Minenkov, Cavallo and
Neese, J. Chem. Phys. 148, 011101 (2018), Eq. (2), which couples surviving
triples through the off-diagonal occupied Fock inside the LMO triple list
instead of rotating the list away. Positive `(T1)` TNO thresholds remain
uncalibrated and the route stays experimental and unwired from `run_job`.

### Added: multi-k GDF accepts symmetry-reduced (IBZ) k-meshes (2026-07-28)

Passing a symmetry-reduced mesh to the multi-k GDF drivers used to raise
`NotImplementedError`. It now works: the drivers rebuild the full
Monkhorst-Pack mesh from the reduction's own `mesh`/`is_shift` metadata
before any integral is built — the same up-front expansion the BIPOLE
drivers already performed.

The refusal existed for a good reason, and the reason has not gone away.
A reduced mesh cannot simply be *weighted* for HF exchange: `K(k_i)` needs
the `k_j` sum over the full Brillouin zone, and the omitted orbit members
are not equivalent to their representative unless `L` and `D` are
symmetry-unfolded onto each star member. Weighting instead converged
1.389 Ha away from the full mesh on MgO/STO-3G (2,2,2). Expanding
sidesteps that entirely by summing the full zone, which is what the
exchange actually requires.

**This makes IBZ input correct, not cheaper.** Every full-mesh point is
still built and diagonalised, so there is no wedge saving to claim. On
LiH FCC (2,2,2) a two-point IBZ mesh and the explicit eight-point tuple
mesh now give bit-identical energies.

Expansion is refused — still fail-closed — when the reduction's declared
parent mesh cannot account for it. That is the `to_bloch_kmesh`
metadata-loss shape, where an explicit `KPoints` list reports the C++
default `(1,1,1)`; the same gap once produced a 78 mHa exxdiv error, and
expanding against fabricated metadata would silently run a different
Brillouin zone than the caller asked for.

True IBZ-*native* reduction — diagonalising only at the wedge — remains
open. The exact symmetry transport it needs already exists and is tested
in `vibeqc.periodic_k_symmetry`, so that work is driver wiring and
validation rather than a derivation.

### Added: SMILES structure building and the two missing extras are documented (2026-07-28)

`smiles_to_qvf` landed the same day and was documented nowhere in the viewer
pages, and neither `[ase]` nor `[smiles]` appeared in the command reference's
extras note.

`docs/user_guide/vibe_view.md` gains a section under the programmatic API, and
it says what the feature actually is rather than what the extra's name
