suggests: a Python entry point (`vibeview.converters.smiles_to_qvf`, not
exported at top level), with no subcommand and no SMILES file format the open
dialog accepts. Signature and the missing-RDKit error path were checked
against the installed package.

The geometry caveat is stated prominently, because it is the part a user can
get wrong: the structure is an RDKit ETKDG embedding with no force-field
cleanup, which is a sensible starting geometry and not an optimised one.

The extras tables in the command reference and the getting-started tutorial
now list `[smiles]`, and the reference's note also mentions `[ase]`, which it
had omitted.

### Fixed: counterpoise decks failed on non-symmorphic space groups (2026-07-28)

Every space-group-227 system in the pob set (C-diamond, Si, Ge) failed
at every rung of the ghost-shell sweep with

    ERROR **** MULTIP **** SYMMOPS DO NOT FORM A GROUP

It looked like a group-14 chemistry problem. It is a symmetry one.
`ATOMBSSE` carves a 0D cluster out of the crystal, and an operator
carrying a translation cannot map a finite cluster onto itself, so in a
**non-symmorphic** group the surviving operators do not close. Rocksalt
(225) and zincblende (216) are symmorphic, which is why every other
system in the set was unaffected.

Isolated by running one system three ways: the plain bulk deck works,
and counterpoise fails with *and* without `SYMMREMO`, so `ATOMBSSE` is
the trigger rather than the spin treatment.

The reference set's own diamond decks carry the fix, and the CRYSTAL23
manual explains it: `ORIGIN` moves the origin "to minimize the number of
symmetry operators with finite translation components" and `TRASREMO`
removes what remains. `emit_input_atom_counterpoise` now emits both,
immediately before `ATOMBSSE`.

Emitted unconditionally rather than keyed to a space-group table,
because that was measured rather than assumed. On CRYSTAL23 v1.0.1 at
PBE/pob-TZVP-REV2, nstar=5 rmax=4.0: Si goes from the `MULTIP` error to
-289.21198632 Ha, while LiCl gives -459.94485757623 Ha **with and
without**, bit for bit. On a group with no translational operators
there is nothing to minimise and nothing to remove.

vibe-basis moves to **0.9.0**. Opt out with `trasremo=False`.
### Fixed: the website shipped a two-release-old vibe-view wheel (2026-07-28)

vibe-view had moved to 2.13.0 while `docs/_static/downloads/` still held
2.12.1 and every download link still named it. The guard added with the
download did not catch it: it checked that the linked file *existed*, which
stays true after a bump because `build_site.sh` restages the wheel on every
publish. The file goes forward, the link does not, and the published download
404s while every local check reads green.

The wheel is rebuilt at 2.13.0 and the five links across `docs/index.md` and
`docs/tutorial/vibe_view_getting_started.md` now name it.
`tests/test_docs_download_links.py` gained the check that was missing: the
staged wheel must equal the version `vibe-view/pyproject.toml` declares, and
the docs links must name that same file. Verified by simulating a bump, which
now fails with the file to rebuild and the script to run.

Verified: the staged wheel installs into a clean venv with vibe-qc absent,
reports 2.13.0, and carries no hostnames or home paths.

### Fixed: the GDF aux-FT reuse cache now respects the build's memory knob (2026-07-28)

The shared-q cderi builder reuses Sweep A's per-chunk auxiliary Fourier
transform in Sweep B instead of recomputing it — a clean removal of
duplicate work. But that cache was the one allocation in the build that
does not follow `tail_chunk_g`: it accumulates one `(n_aux, chunk)` block
per chunk, `(n_aux, n_base)` overall, so it did not shrink when a caller
lowered the knob to bound memory. It became a floor the knob could not
reach. Measured on a four-batch skew-LiH fit, dropping `tail_chunk_g`
from 16384 to 64 moved peak memory 15.6 → 7.2 MiB and then stopped dead
against a 6.4 MiB cache floor — a 256-fold reduction in the knob buying
nothing past that point.

The cache is now budgeted (`VIBEQC_GDF_AUX_FT_CACHE_MIB`, default
256 MiB, `0` disables): chunks are retained while they fit and recomputed
afterwards. The common single-chunk case keeps the reuse for free, since
there the cache *is* the transient that already existed, while dense
multi-chunk builds stay bounded — the same fit at `tail_chunk_g=1024`
now spans 7.51 MiB down to 2.09 MiB as the budget tightens. Results are
bit-identical at every setting, which is the point: the cache removes
duplicate work and reassociates nothing.

### Added: derive a slot-local program for the runtime-slot update path (2026-07-28)

`runtime_slots.slot_local_program` returns a copy of a `VenvProgram` whose
`git_dir` and `python` name a specific slot. That is what lets the ordinary
update path run *inside* a slot: repoint the program, and fetch, checkout, tag
verification, update script and import check all work unchanged, on a tree no
running job is importing from.

The derived paths name the slot directly and **never** resolve through the
`current` symlink, which is a correctness requirement rather than a preference.
A venv is bound by absolute path to the tree it was created in — its editable
`.pth` holds a literal path — so a runtime resolved through `current` would
follow a later flip and change a running job's source underneath it, silently
reintroducing the exact mutation slots exist to prevent. `current` is resolved
only by the launcher at exec time. A root that would route a derived path
through the pointer is refused outright.

Still unreachable: nothing calls it, and no host behaviour changes.

## [v0.15.84] - 2026-07-29 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Fixed: multi-k RHF and UKS hybrid exchange no longer diverges with the lattice cutoff (2026-07-28)

Completes what v0.15.82 started for RKS. The full-range (`c_full`)
exact-exchange arm of the multi-k EWALD_3D drivers was summed as a bare `1/r`
kernel over a radial image ball. On a finite k mesh the SCF density is
Born-von-Karman-torus periodic, so `D(g)` does not decay and that sum does not
converge.

**Multi-k RHF was the worst affected**, because pure Hartree-Fock carries the
full-range arm on *every* job -- there is no pure-functional path to fall back
on. H2/STO-3G in a 12-bohr cube on a `(2,1,1)` mesh moved from `-1.4505` to
`-1.6863` Ha going from a 12- to a 20-bohr lattice cutoff. It now moves
**0.0001 mHa** over that sweep and sits **+0.021 mHa** from PySCF 2.14.0
`KRHF.density_fit()` with `exxdiv='ewald'` (`(2,2,1)`: `+0.020 mHa`, zero
spread). Multi-k UKS is fixed in the same way, per spin.

Both drivers now use the shared corrected split in
`vibeqc.periodic_corrected_exchange`: `erfc(alpha r)/r` short range in real
space, a reciprocal channel per momentum transfer `q = k - k'`, and the
probe-charge `q + G = 0` term.

**Two fixes to the shared helper itself, which also correct the released RKS
route.** Its reciprocal cutoff was derived from the cell volume alone, matched
to the volume-tuned Ewald alpha; a caller supplying its own larger alpha
widened the Gaussian envelope `exp(-K^2 / 4 alpha^2)` and that cutoff then
truncated the sum while the summand was still large -- 53 % of peak on a
30-bohr box at `alpha = 0.5`, worth 1.1e-4 Ha even on a 12-bohr box. `K_max`
is now the tighter of the volume-based default and the one that actually
resolves the given alpha, and the precision driving it is exposed. Separately,
the k-space arms now take the driver's own per-k densities instead of
reconstructing them from the real-space density: that reconstruction requires
the lattice cell list to *cover* the Born-von-Karman torus, which standard
fixtures do not (a 30-bohr cell at a 12-bohr cutoff holds exactly one cell).

**Unchanged by design.** Screened hybrids (`hse06`, `c_full = 0`) are entirely
the convergent `erfc` arm and never touch this path. Pure functionals build no
full-range arm. Multi-k RHF at a `(1,1,1)` mesh keeps its molecular-limit
branch, which zeroes every image block first -- its bare sum has exactly one
term and *is* the molecular-limit K -- so `(1,1,1)` RHF stays in bit-parity
with the Gamma driver.

**Behaviour change.** A hybrid or HF multi-k job on a true mesh now uses the
Ewald exxdiv gauge, so it no longer matches the Gamma-only drivers
bit-for-bit; those keep their own truncated gauge. Two test assertions that
pinned that equality encoded the pre-fix bare sum and now assert the intended
difference instead.

**Still uncorrected, and logged rather than silently claimed fixed:** 2D slab
gauges, `dim != 3`, and symmetry-reduced or explicit k lists cannot use this
construction (the reciprocal cache is 3D-only; the torus density needs a
uniform-weight Monkhorst-Pack mesh). Those routes keep the historical kernel
and emit a line saying so. See `handovers/HANDOVER_OPEN_BUGS_V015.md`.

## [v0.15.83] - 2026-07-28 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Fixed: chart panels hung past the bottom of the window (2026-07-28)

Every 2-D panel in the bottom drawer (bands, DOS, phonons, equation of state,
spectra, SCF convergence, COOP/COHP) rendered into a card that could not fit
the space it was given. The panel is `height: 35vh`; the card inside it was
auto-height; the iframe asked for `min-height: 300px` with `height: 100%`,
and `height: 100%` against an auto-height parent resolves to nothing, so the
iframe fell back to its minimum. Title plus 300 px does not fit in 35vh, so
the chart overflowed its own panel and its x-axis was clipped by the drawer's
`overflow: auto`.

Measured before, on a 900 px window: the band-structure iframe ran from 635 to
935, i.e. 35 px past the bottom of the viewport, and the offset tracked the
window height, so no window size fixed it.

The drawer is now a flex column, each chart card fills it, and each chart
iframe takes the height its title leaves rather than demanding a fixed 300 px.
After: every chart panel ends at or before the window edge (bands, DOS and SCF
at 892 of 900; IR at 899), with the Plotly figure still drawn.

This is the layout half of the problem. The other half, charts drawing nothing
at all because two activators never opted into the iframe sandbox, was fixed
separately in `36bce32bc`; both were needed before a chart panel was usable.

The text properties panel is deliberately left on the old pattern: it carries
run logs and citation text, where overflowing into the drawer's scroll is the
wanted behaviour.

### Added: the multi-k GDF cderi build farms k-point work across MPI ranks (2026-07-28)

The first production periodic k-point farming path. The multi-k GDF
density-fitting setup already grouped its work by momentum transfer, and
those groups are independent — each owns one q, builds its own metric and
pair-FT, and shares no mutable state. So farming them across ranks is one
partition plus one ordered gather per SCF *setup*, with nothing per
iteration, which is what keeps it viable on ordinary Ethernet.

Every rank ends up with the complete cderi cache (the replicated-data
model), so the SCF loop itself is untouched: this parallelises build
*time*, not the memory footprint. Under a single rank the partition is
the identity and the gather a no-op, so serial runs are unchanged.

Verified on LiH FCC `(2,2,2)` KRHF: `E = -7.920890544177 Ha` in 9
iterations on 1, 2 and 4 ranks — identical to all twelve digits, with the
group split confirmed at 8/8, 4/8 and 2/8.

One caveat stated plainly: on a *single node at fixed total cores* this
is a wash (1.37 s at 1 rank x 18 threads, 1.32 s at 2 x 9, 1.37 s at
4 x 4). That is the expected result rather than a disappointment — MPI
here redistributes work OpenMP was already exploiting on the same cores,
and the measurement's value is that it shows no communication penalty.
The real win is multi-node and has not been measured, because there is no
cluster in the development environment.

### Added: a k-point partition primitive for MPI, with real multi-rank tests (2026-07-28)

`KPointPartition` (`vibeqc.mpi`) is the foundation for farming periodic
k-point work across MPI ranks — the coarse-grained target the MPI
strategy note names first, because the per-k tasks are independent and
couple through one reduction rather than chatty exchange.

Splitting k-points is the easy half; putting the answers back together
is where it goes wrong. Each rank holds results for its own subset, and
a plain allgather returns them ordered **by rank**, not **by k**. So the
class owns both halves: `local_indices` for the split and
`allgather_ordered` for the reassembly, which returns the full list in
global k order on every rank. It also refuses to paper over trouble —
local values that do not line up with the assignment, and partitions the
ranks disagree about, both raise rather than yielding a quietly short
result that would read as a converged answer.

That the reassembly deserves its own method is not obvious, and a
mutation check is why it has one: replacing it with a rank-order flatten
still passed every *block*-strategy test and failed only the cyclic
ones. With contiguous blocks rank order and k order coincide, so the
naive version looks right until someone picks a different strategy.

Block and cyclic strategies are available; serial is the identity
partition, so non-MPI runs are unchanged. New
`tests/test_mpi_kpoint_multirank.py` runs genuine `mpirun -np {2,3}`
jobs — until now every MPI test was single-process and exercised only
the serial fallbacks — and skips cleanly when the `[mpi]` extra or a
launcher is missing (verified both ways).

Driver wiring is deliberately not part of this: the intended seam is the
per-momentum-transfer group loop in the multi-k GDF cderi build, and it
lands as its own increment.

### Fixed: multi-k RSGDF shared-q cderi build no longer computes the same auxiliary-basis Fourier transform twice (2026-07-28)

`build_lpq_bloch_native_fft_shared_q` (the shared-q batched cderi builder
behind the multi-k GDF drivers) recomputed `rsgdf_aux_fourier_transform` for
every G-chunk twice on a q-metric cache miss: once while building the 2c
metric `M(q)` ("Sweep A"), then again for the identical chunk while building
the ket-batched 3c tensor `T(q; k_ket)` ("Sweep B"). Sweep A now caches its
per-chunk result and Sweep B (both the base-mesh and high-|G| tail loops)
reuses it instead of recomputing — the same deterministic function on the
same input, so results are bit-identical, not merely reassociated.
`tests/test_rsgdf_shared_q_batch.py` (9/9) is unchanged. On MgO primitive
FCC/STO-3G/def2-svp-jk (2,2,2), the untailed default now runs in 33.76 s vs
34.37 s pre-fix (energy identical to 10 dp, `-271.7175948855 Ha`); the
duplicate call was 3-7% of one q-group's wall time depending on system size,
shrinking further as the orbital basis grows because the now-dominant
G-block-parallel pair-FT kernel (`a9b968e83`, landed the same day) scales
with `n_orb^2`, not `n_aux`.

Also recorded: a fresh, same-machine (18-core) profiling pass of the "full-mesh
multi-k GDF wall scales ~n_k^2" open item (`HANDOVER_OPEN_BUGS_V015.md`) shows
the three 2026-07-27/07-28 q-batching and G-block-widening landings already
closed most of the gap the historical "24x/12109s" number described — see the
handover for the updated same-machine numbers and what's still open.

### Added: vibe-view builds a 3D structure from a SMILES string (2026-07-28)

Installing `vibe-view[smiles]` lets the viewer turn a SMILES string into 3D
coordinates. RDKit parses the string and generates the initial geometry; the
structure is then refined by the same vibe-qc semiempirical optimizer the
editor already uses, so the coordinates a user ends up with come from vibe-qc
rather than from a force field inside the dependency. RDKit stays optional,
being a large package that nobody opening a QVF needs, and attempting to build
without it reports the exact install command.

The same generator is deterministic: the same SMILES always produces the same
starting structure, rather than a slightly different one on every attempt.

RDKit was also already used, undeclared, for local IUPAC naming in vibe-qc. It
is now a declared `[naming]` extra so that route can be installed by name, and
both it and ASE are recorded in the licensing inventory.

## [v0.15.82] - 2026-07-28 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Fixed: `vibe-view capture-selftest` was registered twice (2026-07-28)

`cli.py` carried two `@main.command("capture-selftest")` definitions, so the
healthcheck added in v0.15.23 (the one that renders a built-in structure QVF
through `vibeview.capture` and reports the render backend) was dead code: click
kept the older sphere-rendering definition further down the file, and the
module-level function name collided too. 29 decorators, 28 commands, no
warning from either click or Python.

The v0.15.23 implementation is now the only one. It keeps what the shadowing
definition did better: `--size WxH` (default `400x300`), the read-back check
that the rendered PNG is not uniformly blank, the `capture-selftest: OK`
success line the fleet healthchecks report, and removal of the temp PNG when
`-o/--output` is not given, so a queue host running this before every capture
job no longer leaks a temp dir per run. Exit codes are unchanged, so
`healthcheck_command = "xvfb-run -a vibe-view capture-selftest"` behaves as
before; the success output now also lists the pyvista/VTK versions.

Pin: `vibe-view/tests/test_cli.py::TestCommandRegistry` asserts the number of
`@main.command` decorators in the source equals `len(main.list_commands(ctx))`
and that no module-level function is defined twice, which is what makes a
future duplicate registration visible.

### Added: a vibe-view command reference (2026-07-28)

vibe-view ships **28** CLI commands. Auditing them against the docs found five
with no mention anywhere (`batch-compare`, `dashboard`, `examples`, `h-add`,
`vq-features`) and several more with a single passing reference, so a user's
only route to them was `--help` on a command they did not know existed.

`docs/user_guide/vibe_view_cli.md` covers all 28, grouped by task: look at an
archive, render and export, inspect and compare, transform archives, work with
the queue, setup and self-check. Each row also says which install extra the
command needs, since that is the first thing that goes wrong: only `open`,
`compare`, `serve` and `dashboard` need `[viewer]`, only `tui` needs `[tui]`,
and everything else runs on the base install.

The command names, argument signatures and one-line descriptions are extracted
from the CLI's own click objects rather than retyped, and every option named on
the page was checked against `--help`.

Linked from the section index and the getting-started tutorial.

## [v0.15.81] - 2026-07-28 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Security: `vq status` and `vq logs` now check job ownership (ISO-1, first half) (2026-07-28)

`vq kill` has gated on ownership since v0.6.x. The read paths never did, so on a
multi-user host any local user could inspect another user's job and read its
stdout/stderr through vq itself. `show_status`, `show_status_json` and the
shared log resolver now call `check_spec_path_owner`, the same gate `kill` uses.

**This does not close the hole on its own, and should not be reported as
closing it.** The per-user state directories remain world-readable, so a
determined user reads the spec or log file directly and bypasses vq entirely.
Tightening those modes (`users_root` 0711, per-uid subtrees 0700) is the other
half of ISO-1; it changes permissions on live multi-user hosts running
calculations and needs validating on a real host before it lands.

Inert wherever multi-user is off, which is every host today — the gate returns
immediately in single-user mode, so this ships without changing current
behaviour. Pinned by a test, alongside the two that prove a foreign job is
actually refused.

Reverses the 2026-06-05 deferral, per the maintainer decision in `4a7815658`.

## [v0.15.80] - 2026-07-28 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Fixed: vibe-view could not read the CIF it exported (2026-07-28)

Exporting a molecule to CIF and opening the result failed with "no atom sites
found". A structure with no unit cell has no fractional coordinates, so the
export correctly writes Cartesian atom sites, but the reader only understood
the fractional spelling and rejected any Cartesian CIF regardless of who wrote
it. Those coordinates are now read as the angstroms they already are; files
carrying both keep using fractional, as the crystallographic convention
requires. Found during a sweep that exports all twelve formats from both a
molecule and a crystal and validates each output as its own format; the other
eleven were correct in both cases. The export help also listed only nine of the
twelve formats.

### Added: the vibe-view wheel is downloadable from the website (2026-07-28)

The repository is a private project, so "clone it" is not an answer for
anyone outside it, and the hosted package index is not published. The viewer
is pure Python, though, so one wheel is a complete install: no compiler, no
native build, no vibe-qc.

`vibe-view/scripts/make_wheel.sh` builds it and stages it into
`docs/_static/downloads/`, mirroring how `qvf-writer/scripts/make_archive.sh`
already supplies the toolkit archive, and `scripts/build_site.sh` calls it
before the Sphinx build so the published link always ships the current viewer.
A built copy is committed as the fallback the site uses if that step fails.

Linked from the homepage's QVF and vibe-view section and from
`docs/tutorial/vibe_view_getting_started.md`, which no longer tells the reader
to email the maintainer for a build.

`tests/test_docs_download_links.py` guards the coupling this introduces. A
wheel's filename carries its version and pip refuses a renamed one, so the
link text has to change on every version bump; the test fails if any
`_static/downloads/` link points at a file that is not there, and if more
than one artifact per product is staged (a stale second wheel would let a
reader install a version the docs do not describe).

Two notes for the build script: the repo's scikit-build-core `build/`
directories shadow the PyPI `build` tool, so the script checks
`import build.__main__` from a neutral directory and runs the build from one
too. And `python3 -m pip install './name.whl[all]'` must be quoted, because
zsh reads an unquoted `[all]` as a glob and a bare `$VAR[all]` as an array
subscript.

### Changed: QVF and vibe-view are now prominent on the homepage and in the menu (2026-07-28)

The format and the viewer are meant to be adopted outside vibe-qc, but the
homepage mentioned them only in passing: one clause inside the Tooling
paragraph of "Capabilities today", plus an admonition about the macOS desktop
app's update gate. The sidebar buried the section below Getting started,
Tutorial and User guide. A reader arriving to open a `.qvf` a colleague sent
them had no visible entry point.

* The lede now states what a job leaves behind: one archive, four ways to open
  it, and that QVF is an open format with an Apache-2.0 reference writer.
* A new homepage section, **"See your results: QVF and vibe-view"**, sits
  directly after the first calculation, where the reader has just been told a
  `water.qvf` was written and had nowhere to go with it. It carries a viewer
  screenshot, the four-deployment-mode table (browser, terminal, desktop,
  headless) and four routed entry points: new users to the standalone
  getting-started page, tourists to the walkthrough, cluster users to terminal
  mode, and other codes' developers to the toolkit and adoption guide.
* The **QVF and vibe-view** sidebar caption moves from fourth to second,
  directly under Getting started.
* `installation.md` opens with a note that none of its build requirements
  apply if you only want the viewer, which is the most likely reason somebody
  bounces off that page.
* The `vibe-view --version` samples on three pages read `2.1.0.dev0` while the
  shipped viewer is `2.12.1`; they now show a current number and say it will
  differ.

## [v0.15.79] - 2026-07-28 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Added: a getting-started tutorial for vibe-view on its own (2026-07-28)

Corrected after testing on a real machine: the repository is a **private**
project, so the anonymous HTTPS clone the page recommended returns 401 and the
`git+https://...#subdirectory=vibe-view` shortcut fails with 403. Both are now
stated honestly, with a wheel route that needs no repository. The install also
survives PEP 668: bare `pip` on a Homebrew or Debian Python refuses with
`externally-managed-environment`, so the venv step is non-optional, carries a
`sys.prefix` check, and the command is
`python3 -m pip install './vibe-view[all]'` (non-editable, from the clone
root). A troubleshooting block carries the verbatim text of the three most
likely failures.

The docs had a quickstart for vibe-qc but nothing for somebody who was sent a
`.qvf` and just wants to look at it. Every install path on offer started by
building the native core, which the viewer does not need: `vibeview` is a
pure-Python package, so `pip install` is the whole story.

`docs/tutorial/vibe_view_getting_started.md` is that path, on Linux and macOS:
HTTPS clone, venv, `pip install -e 'vibe-view[all]'`, then open one of the
three sample archives that ship in the clone. It covers the three ways to read
an archive (browser, terminal with no graphics at all, headless to a PNG), a
table of what each extra buys, the platform differences that actually exist
(GL runtime on minimal Linux images, SSH port forwarding, the macOS desktop
app), and where to get archives of your own. Git is the documented route
because the hosted package index is not published yet.

Every command, flag, and section id in the page was executed against a clean
virtual environment with vibe-qc absent, which is how the `--auto-compare`
flag got corrected from an invented `--compare`.

Linked as the first entry of the viewer track in `docs/visualization.md`.

### Fixed: `vibe-view open` pointed at an install extra that does not exist (2026-07-28)

Running `vibe-view open` without the `[viewer]` extra raised a bare
`ImportError` traceback whose remedy read `pip install -e '.[gpu]'`. There is
no `gpu` extra: vibe-view ships `viewer`, `capture`, `tui`, `ase`, `povray`,
`blender`, `jupyter`, `test`, `all`, and `dev`. So the one message a new user
was most likely to hit named a command that fails.

It now matches what `vibe-view tui` already did: a one-line
`click.ClickException` naming `vibeview[viewer]`, noting that `show` and
`capture` need no extra, and exiting 1 instead of dumping a stack.
### Fixed: the SCF convergence panel drew nothing (2026-07-28)

vibe-view's bottom panel served two kinds of content through one
`properties_html` channel and one iframe: renderer-built Plotly charts, and
archive text that must never execute (run logs, embedded attachments,
citation text, job specs). The iframe's sandbox was therefore a *decision* —
`sandbox=("properties_allow_scripts ? 'allow-scripts' : ''",)` — defaulting
to deny, reset on every section activation, and opted into by exactly one
activator.

The two chart activators never opted in. `scf_history` and `dos.coop` /
`dos.cohp` pushed a Plotly figure into the deny-by-default frame, so
plotly.js was blocked and the panel rendered as a blank white box. Measured
in the browser on the showcase archive: the SCF panel came up with
`sandbox=""` and zero drawn SVG elements, while its Raman and
equation-of-state neighbours — which have their own hardcoded
`allow-scripts` iframes — drew three each.

The channel is now split by what the content *is* rather than by what an
activator remembered to ask for. `properties_html` carries archive text
only, in an iframe with a hardcoded empty sandbox and no state key that can
turn scripts on. A new `chart_html` carries renderer-built figures (SCF
convergence, COOP/COHP, orbital energies) in its own iframe with a hardcoded
`allow-scripts`, matching the bands / phonon / EOS / spectra panels that
were already arranged this way. A text renderer can no longer acquire
scripts, and a chart renderer can no longer lose them.

Verified in a browser: the SCF panel draws three SVGs with a populated
energy axis, the run-record and bond-order panels stay at `sandbox=""` with
none, and the orbital diagram's click-to-render bridge still round-trips
(clicking a level posts through to `mo_click_request` and renders the MO).

Two neighbouring defects surfaced while verifying the COOP half. The click
dispatch had no branch for `dos.coop`, `dos.cohp` or `bond_orders` at all,
so clicking those sections in the sidebar did nothing at all — silently, and
only the `viewer_defaults` auto-open path ever reached their activators. And
that auto-open path passed a bare `state` for `topology.qtaim` and
`dos.coop` where no such local exists, raising `NameError`, with a duplicate
`dos.coop` branch dead behind it. Both are fixed, and a guard now fails if
any panel kind lacks a click branch — the existing smoke test only asserted
that activation does not *raise*, which a missing branch satisfies
trivially.

### Fixed: release pipelines now run the producer-coupled viewer tests (2026-07-28)

`vibe-view-test` deliberately does not install vibeqc, because that would
pull the libint build into a job whose whole point is being pip-only and
fast. The documented consequence was that "the few vibeqc-dependent tests
skip via importorskip". Measured, it is fourteen -- and they are not
peripheral: they include `test_kind_drift`, the guard that every kind the
writer emits is handled by the viewer, and the QVF job-container
submission tests. They were green-by-absence in every release pipeline.

`build-test` has already built vibeqc into `.venv`, so the release-gate
branch of that job now also installs vibe-view and runs the viewer suite
there (one pip install plus about 90 seconds). Ordinary `main` pushes are
unaffected -- the step is gated on tag / release-candidate exactly like the
T1 block beside it. Verified with the precise CI invocation from the repo
root: 1301 passed, 1 skipped.

Not changed, having checked: the remaining `[ase]` skip is not a gap. That
test asserts the *missing-extra* path, so installing the extra would only
swap which of the two complementary tests skips.

### Fixed: a scheduler host reports its own helper, not the driver's vq version (2026-07-28)

Scheduler hosts are daemonless, so `gather_scheduler_overview` copied the
**driver's** `vq_version` onto site_i and site_j. But each runs its own helper vq
— the one that polls, reconciles and dispatches — and its skew from the driver
was a whole incident earlier this cycle. Showing the driver's number next to a
scheduler host hid precisely the disagreement an operator needed to see.

`vq_version` is now `None` for a scheduler host, and a new `helper_source_sha`
carries the helper's verified SOURCE-SHA from the canonical helper record,
short-form. The header reads `==== site_i (vq helper 136f49090630) ====` instead
of borrowing a version that was never that host's. It survives the JSON round
trip, so it is available for a remote host.

Read from the helper's own record rather than compared against the driver — the
point is to make a disagreement visible, not to assert agreement. An absent
record stays `None` rather than being filled with a guess: a helper deployed
before canonical bookkeeping legitimately has none, and a malformed or
short SHA is rejected rather than displayed.

Note the field is an identity, not a version: the helper record carries a SHA
and no version string. That is deliberate, and better than a confident wrong
number. Non-scheduler hosts are unchanged and still show their own vq version.

## [v0.15.78] - 2026-07-28 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Added: `runtime_slot_root` opts a venv program into per-SHA runtime slots (2026-07-28)

The config surface for the immutable-runtime work. Absent — the default, and
every host today — keeps the historical in-place update, so nothing changes
until a host is deliberately converted. Set to an absolute slot root, it marks
that program as using the `vq.runtime_slots` layout. Inert for now: nothing in
the update path reads it yet.

A relative root is rejected at config load, because the root is handed to a
build that runs elsewhere and would otherwise resolve against whatever working
directory that build inherited — better to fail on load than when a release is
already half-applied.

**Ordering constraint, and it is sharper than a normal config addition.**
`_ProgramBase` sets `extra="forbid"` and `load_config` raises `ConfigError` on a
validation failure, so a vq predating this field does not ignore the key — it
fails to load the config at all, and *every* command on that host breaks.
Shipping the field is safe; writing the key into a config a host reads is not,
until that host runs a vq carrying it. Convert per host, after updating it.

Left strict deliberately, in contrast to `DrainState`, which now tolerates
unknown keys: that is machine-written state where a strict reader silently
un-drained a host, whereas program config is hand-edited, where rejecting a typo
is worth the ordering cost.

### Performance: the single-k pair-FT parallelises over G-blocks too (2026-07-28)

Completes the sweep: all three pair-FT kernels now spread work over more
than the shell-pair axis. `ao_pair_fourier_transform_bloch` — which feeds
Γ GDF, CCM post-HF, COSX and the RSGDF high-|G| tail — had the same
ceiling as its batched sibling, measuring 3.32 s → 1.27 s and then flat
(2.6×, nothing past 4 threads).

It gets the same (shell pair, G-block) task space, and here the result is
**bit-identical**, not merely reassociation-equivalent: every output
element's accumulation over cells, primitive pairs and Hermite terms stays
wholly inside one task in the original order, so only *which* worker owns
a given G changes. A regression pins that by comparing runs under
different `OMP_NUM_THREADS` and requiring exact equality.

Scaling goes 2.6× → **10.7× on 18 threads** (1.267 s → 0.356 s), and a Γ
GDF setup drops 1.59 s → 1.12 s. The one cost is ~10% single-threaded,
which is codegen rather than algorithm — at a single worker the kernel
takes an unchanged single-block path — and is accepted for the 3.6× at the
multi-threaded default.

### Performance: the multi-k GDF cderi pair-FT parallelises over G-blocks (2026-07-28)

With the V_ne fix below in place, the batched cderi pair-FT became 85% of
a multi-k GDF run — and it had the same defect: it spread work over shell
pairs alone. On LiH/STO-3G that is 16 tasks of very uneven cost, and it
measured *completely flat* from 4 threads upward (0.457 s at both 4 and
18 threads) because the critical path is one long task.

Unlike V_ne, the cell axis is not available here — this kernel's cell
loop is a Bloch *sum*, so splitting it would need a reduction. But its
output tensor is indexed by G, which makes a G-block an exclusively-owned
output slice: free, reduction-less parallelism. The task space is now
(shell pair, G-block), sized to roughly four blocks per worker. Per-worker
scratch shrinks from full-mesh to block-sized as a side effect.

Scaling goes from 2.7× (flat past 4 threads) to **11.8× on 18 threads**;
the kernel drops 0.457 s → 0.106 s. End to end, the LiH FCC `(2,2,2)`
KRHF anchor falls from **8.58 s to 2.18 s**, and together with the V_ne
change below from **11.16 s to 2.18 s (5.1×)** — energy bit-identical to
all printed digits at the same iteration count throughout. A new
regression pins that the G-block decomposition is unobservable: the result
must be identical however the blocks fall.

### Performance: the periodic V_ne reciprocal sum parallelises over cells, not just shell pairs (2026-07-28)

The Ewald-split nuclear attraction built its long-range half one image
cell at a time, calling the Bloch pair-FT kernel per cell and
materialising a full `(nbf, nbf, n_G)` tensor only to contract it away
against `v_long(G)`. Profiling a LiH FCC `(2,2,2)` KRHF run put that
block at 33% of the whole SCF.

The per-cell loop was not the problem — batching the calls is worth only
1.1×. The ceiling was parallelism: the Bloch kernels can only spread work
over shell pairs, because their cell loop is a *sum*. With a small basis
and many image cells (LiH/STO-3G: 16 shell pairs, 135 cells) that
saturated at 2.97× on 8 threads. But V_ne wants per-*cell* blocks, not
the Bloch sum, so the cell index is free parallelism.

The new `ao_pair_fourier_transform_weighted_per_cell` kernel folds the
reciprocal weights into its innermost Hermite reduction — `Re()` commutes
out because every remaining factor is real — and returns per-cell blocks.
The dense tensor never exists, and the flattened (shell-pair, cell) task
space parallelises with no reduction. On the same anchor the V_ne block
goes **3.65 s → 1.18 s (3.09×)**, of which 0.69 s is now the unrelated
libint erfc sum, and OpenMP scaling rises from 2.97× to 4.44×. The
`(2,2,2)` KRHF energy is unchanged to all printed digits at the same
iteration count; the kernel matches the dense reference to ≤1.6e-14
through L = 3. Every periodic route that builds V_ne — GDF (Γ and
multi-k), BIPOLE, GAPW — sees it.

Also fixed while there: the G-chunk for this path was still sized against
the eliminated dense tensor, which would have over-chunked a large basis
by orders of magnitude (nbf = 500 asked for 32-point chunks). The
contracted path's `n_G`-proportional storage is the shared `(-iG)^t`
power tables, independent of `nbf`, and is sized as such.
## [v0.15.77] - 2026-07-28 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Added: terminal mode draws a backbone trace, and reports colour fallbacks (2026-07-28)

The biomolecular colour schemes had never seen a residue. There is no
biomolecular archive anywhere in the corpus, so `chain`, `secondary` and
`bfactor` had only ever run against four-atom stubs. Converting a real
protein (a 167k-atom solvated system, 1046 alpha carbons, 337 helix / 246
strand / 463 coil) found a bug immediately.

`bfactor` painted every atom one flat colour. The fallback only fired when
the column was entirely NaN, and this file, like a great many, writes a
constant 0.00 rather than omitting the field. A constant column then scaled
to a single point on the ramp. It now falls back to element colouring
whenever the column carries no variation, which is the same call the cartoon
renderer already makes for missing residue names: something meaningful
rather than one flat hue that says nothing and reads as a rendering fault.

Silent substitution is its own defect, since the status line would go on
asserting a scheme the viewport is not showing, so a scene now carries the
reason and the status line appends it.

The same protein showed why an all-atom render is not a picture of a
protein: 167k atoms resolve to a solid mass. A `backbone` representation
draws one point per alpha carbon, joined along each chain and coloured by
secondary structure, which makes the fold legible at terminal resolution.
Chains are traced separately: a single trace over a flat CA list would draw
a bond from one chain's C-terminus to the next chain's N-terminus, inventing
a covalent link across a gap that can be the width of the box. A structure
with no alpha carbons falls back to all atoms and says so.

Measured while looking: 8000 atoms build in 0.10 s and render in 0.012 s, so
the quadratic bond-inference cliff does not bite here and no performance
work is needed. A full extruded ribbon with secondary-structure cross
sections remains the next increment; this is the trace it will be built on.
### Fixed: multi-k hybrid exchange no longer diverges with the lattice cutoff (2026-07-28)

`run_rks_periodic_multi_k_ewald3d` summed the full-range (`c_full`)
exact-exchange arm as a bare `1/r` kernel over a radial image ball. On a
finite k mesh the SCF density is Born-von-Karman-torus periodic, so `D(g)`
does not decay with image distance -- every image block was measured to
carry the identical norm -- and that sum does not converge. Adding image
shells just kept adding non-decaying contributions: H2/PBE0/STO-3G in a
12-bohr cube fell **177 mHa** going from a 12- to a 20-bohr cutoff, and the
result matched neither PySCF `exxdiv` convention because it was not a
well-defined quantity.

The `c_full` arm now rides the convergent Ewald split that the
ROHF/ROKS/BIPOLE routes already used: `erfc(alpha r)/r` short range in real
space, a reciprocal channel per momentum transfer `q = k - k'`, and the
probe-charge `q + G = 0` term. The same cutoff sweep now moves the energy by
**0.0001 mHa**, and the result sits **+0.038 mHa** from PySCF 2.14.0
`KRKS.density_fit()` with `exxdiv='ewald'` (at both `(1,1,1)` and `(2,1,1)`),
and within 5e-5 Ha of `run_pbc_bipole_rks`.

The split lives in one place, `vibeqc.periodic_corrected_exchange`, so it is
not reimplemented per driver.

**Screened hybrids are unaffected by design.** `hse06` and friends resolve to
`c_full = 0, c_sr = 0.25` -- they are entirely the `erfc` short-range arm,
which is already convergent in real space and stays on the existing path.

**Two behaviour changes worth knowing.** A hybrid multi-k job now uses the
Ewald exxdiv gauge at *every* mesh size, including `(1,1,1)`, which is what
PySCF's `exxdiv='ewald'` and the BIPOLE route do. `run_rks_periodic_gamma_ewald3d`
keeps its own truncated gauge (legitimate at Gamma, where the molecular-limit
density does decay), so multi-k `(1,1,1)` and the Gamma driver no longer agree
bit-for-bit for a hybrid; they differ by a Madelung-scale amount. Pure
functionals build no full-range arm and are untouched. Second, a hybrid on a
mesh the split cannot serve -- a 2D slab gauge, `dim != 3`, or a
symmetry-reduced / explicit k list, none of which give the uniform-weight
Monkhorst-Pack torus the construction needs -- now fails closed with a message
naming the precondition, rather than silently summing a divergent series.

The regression test uses a cell whose image ball holds more than one lattice
cell and asserts cutoff-independence. The previous hybrid test could not have
caught this: it ran in a 30-bohr box at a 12-bohr cutoff, which yields exactly
one cell, so there was no image sum to diverge.

Multi-k RHF and UKS carry the same defect on the same arm and are the next two
increments; they are recorded in `handovers/HANDOVER_OPEN_BUGS_V015.md`.

### Fixed: 12 committed QVF archives carried a real hostname (2026-07-28)

Fallout from the opt-out bug below. Auditing every tracked `.qvf` found 12 of
30 naming the machine that produced them: 11 the maintainer's personal
workstation and one a cluster node, shipped in a public repository as docs
examples (`docs/_static/examples/*`) and one vibe-view test fixture. The
remaining 18 were already masked, by the conformance corpus omitting
provenance and the vibe-view showcase archives using `<host>`.

All 12 are now `<redacted>`. Only `manifest.json` was rewritten and every data
member copied byte-for-byte, so per-member sha256 values stay valid, all 18
non-corpus archives still pass `validate_qvf`, and the numbers the examples
document are untouched.

`scripts/qvf_redact_hostname.py` is the audit and redaction tool, exiting
non-zero when any archive still carries a real host so it can be used as a
pre-publication gate:

```sh
python scripts/qvf_redact_hostname.py $(git ls-files '*.qvf')
```

### Fixed: the hostname opt-out never reached the `.qvf` archive (2026-07-28)

`record_hostname=False` and `VIBEQC_NO_HOSTNAME=1` are both documented for
"runs you plan to share publicly", and the second is recommended by name for
"public examples, paper artifacts, and shared issue reproductions". Both
redacted the `.system` manifest only. `_build_provenance` in the QVF writer
called `socket.gethostname()` unconditionally, so the archive kept the real
machine name.

That put the leak in the worst possible artifact: the `.qvf` is the one the
docs push hardest for sharing (hand to a colleague, attach to a paper's SI),
it travels as a single opaque file, and it is what the release-paper
calculation set is made of. Verified on v0.15.76 before the fix: with either
lever set, the `.system` read `hostname = "<redacted>"` while the sibling
`.qvf` provenance carried the fully-qualified host.

Both levers now cover both artifacts, sharing the canonical
`_hostname_redacted()` predicate with the `.system` writer, and both write the
same `<redacted>` placeholder rather than dropping the field so consumer shape
stays stable. `record_hostname` is threaded into the QVF dispatch context from
`run_job`, `run_periodic_job`, and the periodic semiempirical runner. Three
regression tests pin the kwarg lever, the env lever, and the record-by-default
case.

Docs corrected to match in `docs/user_guide/output_files.md` and
`docs/tutorial/reference_outputs.md`, which previously implied the opt-out was
complete, and `docs/tutorial/qvf_file_format.md` gained a note at the point
where it recommends attaching an archive to a paper's SI.

**Archives written before this fix still carry the host.** Check an existing
one with `json.loads(zipfile.ZipFile(p).read("manifest.json"))["provenance"]`.

### Fixed: the QVF tutorial understated `output_qvf` (2026-07-28)

`docs/tutorial/qvf_file_format.md` said an archive is written "when you pass
`output_qvf=True`". It defaults to `True` on both runners, so the flag reads as
opt-in when it is opt-out. Corrected, matching the entry-point pages fixed in
`319749dac`.

### Added: vibe-view reads the long tail of structure formats via an optional ASE extra (2026-07-28)

Installing `vibe-view[ase]` lets the viewer open anything ASE can read, including
VASP's extensionless POSCAR and CONTCAR files, `.extxyz` and `.traj`. ASE stays
optional because it is a large dependency that most people opening a QVF never
need; opening a file that requires it now produces an error naming the file and
the exact install command rather than a bare mention of the package.

Also fixes a mismatch between the two places that decided what vibe-view can
open. Scanning a directory used one list of extensions and the opener used
another, so files the converter accepted were never offered, and files without
an extension could not pass the filter even when they were. Both now ask the
same question, "would the opener take this", so the browser and the opener can
no longer disagree.

### Added: `vq overview` reports the quota that actually gates dispatch (2026-07-27)

`overview` showed core count and the daemon's `max_cpus` but not the
per-submitter `[quotas] default_max_concurrent_cpus`, which on a multi-user host
is usually the tightest of the three and the one that actually stops a job.
site_e on 2026-07-27: 32 physical cores, `max_cpus = 32`, quota 16, and a
pending 24-CPU job sitting for hours against an idle queue with nothing in
`overview` explaining it. The investigation went to daemon health instead.

`vq overview --json` now carries `quota_max_concurrent_cpus`, and it survives
the remote-forwarding round trip so it is available for a remote host, which is
where a fleet operator reads it. `docs/multi_user_deployment.md` records that
the three limits are independent and can disagree.

Text rendering is unchanged: that renderer shows no CPU figures today, so there
was no "next to core count" to add it to without inventing a section.

## [v0.15.76] - 2026-07-28 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Fixed: `rollout-latest` no longer halts the whole fleet on one host's failure (2026-07-27)

A failed lane aborted the entire invocation. On this fleet that made the tool
unusable: the site_e/site_b multi-user `/opt/vq` gap (runbook §3b) fails **by
design** every release until a maintainer runs its sudo step, so
`rollout-latest` was guaranteed to halt on every release, leaving every host
ordered behind site_e unverified. The operator hit it twice during the v0.15.75
sweep and finished the remaining venv lanes by hand from the manual recipe.

The asymmetry was the tell: the manual `--all-hosts` commands already continue
past a single host's failure, so the automated path — the one that exists to
produce a fleet-wide picture — was the strict regression.

A failure is now terminal for **its own host** and no further. Remaining hosts
are attempted, per-host verdicts are collected, and the degraded set is named in
the result (`failed_hosts`) rather than inferred from where the run stopped.

Deliberately per-host, not blind continue-everything: within one host a failed
lane still stops its siblings, because a host whose release lane just failed is
not a host to keep installing onto. A run that skipped a host is still not
`complete`, so nothing reads a degraded sweep as convergence, and a
rollout-owned drain on the failed host is still released.

## [v0.15.75] - 2026-07-28 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Added: periodic ROKS on the BIPOLE route (2026-07-27)

`run_periodic_job(method="ROKS", functional=..., jk_method="bipole")` now
reaches a multi-k restricted open-shell Kohn-Sham SCF, at Gamma and on full
Monkhorst-Pack meshes. It runs on the same corrected-Ewald-exchange EWALD_3D
engine that the ROHF route was wired onto: each per-spin Fock is
`Hcore + J - c_full*K_sigma + V_xc^sigma`, and the two are combined by the
same Roothaan coupling, so the determinant stays spin-pure
(`<S^2> = S(S+1)` exactly). Previously ROKS was Gamma-GPW only and failed
closed on BIPOLE.

LDA, GGA, meta-GGA and **global** hybrids are supported. Screened hybrids
(`hse06`) need an erfc-attenuated exchange arm this engine does not carry
and fail closed, as do long-range-corrected functionals, double hybrids,
smearing, DFT+U, gradients and restarts.

A pure functional builds no exchange at all — neither the exchange caches
nor the O(n_k^2) long-range K loop — so dense meshes cost what a pure-DFT
mesh should. Every per-iteration Bloch fold rides the fused OpenMP multi-k
kernels, including the `V_xc` fold, which was the last per-k serial fold
left in this driver family.

Verification: the Li/PBE/STO-3G `(1,1,2)` anchor agrees with an
out-of-process PySCF 2.14.0 `KROKS().density_fit()` reference (matched BvK
supercell spin counts) to `+0.111 mHa`; the closed-shell PBE0 limit
reproduces the BIPOLE RKS route to `0.023 mHa` and PySCF `KRKS/PBE0`
(`exxdiv='ewald'`) to `0.038 mHa`; the closed-shell pure limit reproduces
the multi-k RKS driver to machine precision; and the open-shell energy
tracks the landed multi-k UKS driver to `1e-7 Ha` across lattice cutoffs
from 12 to 18 bohr.

## [v0.15.74] - 2026-07-28 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Added: CASSCF publishes its natural orbitals, and its QVF carries them (2026-07-27)

A correlated solver's orbitals never left the solver. `run_job(
method="casscf", output_qvf=True)` wrote structure, citations and
run.record and no wavefunction at all, because the QVF payload is built from
mean-field `mo_coeffs` that a CASSCF result does not have. The orbitals
existed the whole time: `C @ sc.mo_rotation` was already being formed inside
the gradient branch and then discarded.

`SolverResult` gains `natural_orbitals` and `natural_occupations`, populated
for the CAS family. The inactive and virtual blocks pass through unchanged,
being already eigenvectors of the density with eigenvalues 2 and 0; only the
active block is diagonalized, and its eigenvectors are ordered high
occupancy first so that "highest occupied" refers to something. H2 at 2.4 A
in 6-31G with CAS(2,2) gives 1.88542 and 0.11458, summing to its 2
electrons.

`qvf_natural_wf_data` is the payload builder for them. Its sibling
`qvf_wf_data` derives occupations from the electron count, 2.0 for the first
n_elec/2 orbitals and 0.0 after, which is right for a single determinant and
wrong for anything correlated: it would erase precisely the fractional
occupancies the calculation was run to find.

Verified rather than assumed: the orbitals are orthonormal against the AO
overlap to 1.6e-15, and the density built from them and their occupations
gives tr(PS) = 2.00000000. Six tests pin the exposure, the electron-count
sum, the ordering, orthonormality, the density trace, and the QVF section;
all six were confirmed to fail without the change.

Löwdin, Phys. Rev. 97, 1474 (1955), which defines natural orbitals as the
eigenvectors of the one-particle density matrix, is added to the citation
database and routed for method='casci'/'casscf'. A paper reporting these
occupation numbers is reporting that construction. Verified to reach the
.out references block, the .bibtex sidecar and the QVF citations section.

The vibe-view fixture that pins the viewer's HONO path is regenerated from
this real CASSCF path, replacing the broken-symmetry UHF stand-in that was
the closest producible equivalent before.

### Fixed: `vq overview` no longer reports `daemon: FAIL` on a healthy multi-user host (2026-07-27)

`overview` derives its daemon line from `lifecycle.verify_user_systemd_contract`,
which cross-checks four **systemd-user** sources. On a multi-user host the vq
daemon is a **system** service that systemd-user does not supervise, so that
contract measures a different manager entirely and reports FAIL for a daemon
serving normally. site_e and site_b did exactly that on 2026-07-27: `vq overview`
showed `daemon: FAIL` while `vq doctor` was 5/5 on both, `doctor --all` was
14/14 fleet-wide, and RPC answered on both.

The cost was not the wrong line. A health field reading FAIL on a healthy host
invites a repair that is not needed, and it did — a wrong handover, a
retraction, and a cross-chat investigation, while the job that prompted it was
capacity-blocked on an unrelated quota.

Multi-user hosts now take the RPC-liveness path, pinging the multi-user socket.
That path already existed for the same class of false negative on macOS —
"systemd-user supervision is not the daemon's supervision mechanism" — and was
simply never wired for multi-user, because a multi-user Linux box *does* have a
user manager; it is just irrelevant to this daemon.

Not weakened: a multi-user daemon that is not serving still fails, and the
single-user Linux path is untouched, so an unreachable user manager there is
still a genuine fault. Both are pinned by tests.

## [v0.15.73] - 2026-07-28 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Fixed: emitted decks now match the pob reference protocol (2026-07-26)

Two mismatches between vibe-basis's CRYSTAL decks and the protocol that
produced the published pob cohesive energies, both large enough to
matter at the sub-kJ/mol tolerance a cohesive-energy gate works to.

**`TOLINTEG` was never emitted**, so decks ran at CRYSTAL's own
integral-screening defaults. Every one of the 1759 decks in the
reference set uses `9 9 9 18 54`, which is far tighter. That is now the
default here; pass `tolinteg=None` for CRYSTAL's defaults.

**`HUGEGRID` was emitted for SCAN-family functionals, and should not
have been.** It was added on the CRYSTAL23 manual's recommendation
without checking what the reference set actually did: not one of those
1759 decks uses it. When the goal is reproducing a published result,
matching its protocol beats following the manual, so the default is now
off and the manual's advice is available as `hugegrid=True`.

The grid choice was also asymmetric, applied to the atom emitter but
not the bulk one. A cohesive energy subtracts a bulk from its own free
atoms, so a grid difference between the two does not cancel; it surfaces
as a few kJ/mol that reads as chemistry. The plane-wave reference work
hit the same shape of error by holding atoms at a fixed cutoff while
sweeping the solid. All three emitters now agree, and a test pins that
agreement rather than either side alone.

With this, an emitted single-point deck reproduces the reference bulk
energy for LiCl at r2SCAN/pob-TZVP-REV2 to **0.012 kJ/mol**
(-467.83953254 against -467.83953721 Ha), against the milestone's
1 kJ/mol bar.

`emit_input_inline` also gets its first live CRYSTAL test. It shares the
basis and SCF blocks with the atom emitter and was fixed alongside it
when five deck defects were found, but sharing a fix is not the same as
being tested.
## [v0.15.72] - 2026-07-28 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Fixed: `vq doctor --all` no longer reports a healthy host as failed (2026-07-27)

`--all` probes up to eight hosts concurrently, which is enough to push a host on
a slow ssh route past its probe timeout. A timed-out or exit-255 probe becomes
`remote_vq: ok=false`, and the host's overall `ok` is the AND of its checks — so
a lost race is reported identically to a real fault. Example_hub did exactly this
on 2026-07-27: `verdict: failed` from one `--all` run, 5/5 ok on its own moments
later.

It is not only a reporting problem. `fleet_rollout.doctor_failures` turns any
not-ok in-scope host into `status="blocked"`, so a contended probe can block an
entire rollout.

A failure whose message is an ssh transport failure is now re-probed once,
serially, before being reported. vq already distinguished transport failures
from remote-side errors — it just used that only to append a diagnostic, never
to qualify the verdict.

Scoped deliberately: only transport failures retry, only once, and a genuinely
unreachable host still fails. It must, because a host vq cannot probe must never
be silently skipped by a rollout; it now costs one extra serial attempt to say
so. A remote-side fault (vq reached the host and found something wrong) is not
retried at all.

## [v0.15.71] - 2026-07-27 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Performance: BIPOLE production drivers' per-iteration Bloch folds ride the fused multi-k kernels (2026-07-27)

The four direct BIPOLE drivers (`run_pbc_bipole_rhf` / `_rks` / `_uhf` /
`_uks`) and the shared unrestricted Fock builder no longer run serial
per-k Python `_bloch_sum_blocks` folds in their SCF hot loops. The
per-iteration `F^{2e}(k)` Fock assembly folds, the DFT+U per-spin
`P_s(k)` folds, the iteration-1 local-guess `D(k)` folds, and the
accelerator `D(k)` folds (legacy multi-k gauge) now go through a shared
`_bloch_sum_blocks_multi_k` helper in `pbc_bipole_common` that calls the
fused OpenMP `bloch_sum_multi_k` kernel (k-parallel, one pass over the
real-space blocks) when available, with the serial per-k Python fold
retained as the ImportError fallback — the same pattern the multi-k
ROHF/UHF/UKS Ewald drivers adopted in v0.15.69/v0.15.70. Accumulation
order is unchanged (cells in list order; the kernel's cos/sin phase is
within one ulp of `np.exp`). Under the production Ewald exchange split
the density folds continue to use the exact BvK torus representative
(`_split_k_density_list`); only genuine Bloch-fold call sites moved.
New regressions pin the helper against the serial fold (1e-14) and all
four drivers' fused deterministic 2-iteration multi-k SCF against the
Python-fallback SCF (energy to 1e-10 Ha, per-k Fock to 1e-10) in
`tests/test_pbc_bipole_multik_ewald_split.py`. No numerics, options, or
output change.

## [v0.15.70] - 2026-07-27 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Changed: multi-k UHF/UKS Ewald drivers get the v0.15.69 ROHF hot-loop treatment (2026-07-27)

`run_uhf_periodic_multi_k_ewald3d` and `run_uks_periodic_multi_k_ewald3d`
no longer recompute the overlap lattice integrals every SCF iteration just
to obtain a `LatticeMatrixSet` container for `D_total = D_alpha + D_beta`:
the container is built once per SCF from the overlap template and its
blocks are overwritten per Fock build (the shared
`_build_uhf_fock_blocks_ewald3d` / `_build_uks_fock_2e_blocks_ewald3d`
helpers gained an optional `d_total_buffer`, `None` preserving the one-shot
behaviour). Their per-iteration per-k Fock Bloch transforms now ride the
fused OpenMP kernels — `assemble_fock_multi_k` for the UHF
`F^{2e,s}(k) + Hcore(k)` assembly, `bloch_sum_multi_k` for the UKS
`F_HF^s(k)` folds — with the serial per-k Python fold retained as the
ImportError fallback (same per-block accumulation order; the kernel phase
differs from `np.exp` by at most one ulp). The pinned UHF/UKS multi-k
suites pass unchanged, and new regressions pin the fused SCF against the
Python-fallback SCF (energy to 1e-10 Ha, per-k Fock matrices to 1e-10)
and the reused container against the one-shot path (blocks to 1e-13,
including a second reuse). The UHF driver's per-iteration accelerator
density transforms (the `D_s(k)` folds feeding
`MultiKPeriodicUHFAccelerator.extrapolate_uhf`, computed every DIIS-on
iteration) ride `bloch_sum_multi_k` the same way. Kernel-level scaling
numbers are in the v0.15.69 entry below; no numerics, options, or
output change.

### Added: open-shell multi-k GDF accepts the dense-core high-|G| tail (2026-07-27)

`run_kuhf_periodic_gdf` / `run_kuks_periodic_gdf` now accept
`rsgdf_tail_ke_cutoff`, closing the recorded "no tail plumbing on the
open-shell route — held unconditionally on the class" gap: dense-core
cells (P01/MgO class) can now lift the `+PARITY_HELD` absolute-energy
hold with a parity-sized tail exactly like the closed-shell drivers,
instead of being held with no remedy. The tail extends the rsgdf fit's
M / T G-sums over the exact complementary reciprocal shell, so
`E(ke_cutoff=a, tail_ke_cutoff=b)` equals `E(ke_cutoff=b)` by
construction; non-rsgdf `gdf_method` values fail closed on the knob.
The shared-q batched cderi build (below) amortises the tail's dominant
pair-FT pass across the k-points of each momentum transfer, which is
what makes the tail affordable on multi-k meshes. Regressions: exact
same-support energy identity on the triplet-H2 (2,1,1) route, the MgO
warn/lift sentinel pair, and the fail-closed guard
(`tests/test_periodic_kuhf_gdf.py`).

## [v0.15.69] - 2026-07-27 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Performance: multi-k RSGDF cderi builds share one pair-FT pass per momentum transfer (2026-07-27)

The dominant cost of the multi-k GDF setup was the ket-Bloch AO-pair
Fourier transform, run once per `(k_i, k_j)` pair — `n_k^2` full passes
for hybrid exchange. But the per-cell McMurchie-Davidson work in that
kernel is k-independent: the ket momentum enters only through the Bloch
phase `exp(+i k·R)` applied at the per-cell fold. The pairs sharing one
canonical momentum transfer `q = k_j - k_i` now run ONE OpenMP-parallel
pair-FT pass (base mesh and high-|G| tail alike) folded into every ket
momentum with its own phase — the three-centre companion of the
q-metric cache that already shared `M(q)`.

Hybrid-exchange cderi builds drop from `n_k^2` to `n_k` pair-FT passes
on a regular full mesh; diagonal-only builds (pure DFT J, COSX
exchange) drop from `n_k` to one. The per-k 3c contraction now runs as
a threaded BLAS ZGEMM instead of a single-threaded einsum loop.
Measured on LiH primitive FCC / STO-3G / def2-svp-jk at a Γ-centred
(2,2,2) mesh (64 hybrid pairs): 115.3 s → 10.1 s, 11.4×, with max
|ΔLpq| 3.5e-13 across all pairs — exact work-sharing, no screening,
storage, or convention change. Both closed- and open-shell multi-k
RSGDF drivers batch; the CCM `_lpq_cache_builder` hook and the
mdf/compcell branches keep their per-pair paths. The per-q group loop
is the designated seam for future MPI k-point farming. New surface:
`ao_pair_fourier_transform_bloch_multi` (C++ kernel + wrapper) and
`build_lpq_bloch_native_fft_shared_q`. Regressions:
`tests/test_rsgdf_shared_q_batch.py` (kernel and builder parity at
2e-12 including tail/screen/cache, per-unique-q call counting,
diagonal collapse, python-fallback exactness).

### Added: public multi-k periodic ROHF on the BIPOLE route (2026-07-27)

`run_periodic_job(method="ROHF", jk_method="bipole")` now dispatches to the
validated corrected-Ewald-exchange EWALD_3D restricted-open-shell engine
(`run_rohf_periodic_multi_k_ewald3d`) at Gamma and on full Monkhorst-Pack
meshes, closing the BIPOLE half of the G-PBC-007 "GDF/BIPOLE/GAPW
ROHF/ROKS backends" gate. AUTO now resolves `method="ROHF"` to the BIPOLE
route (the open-shell arm of the established heuristic); previously every
jk_method except explicit Gamma-only `"gpw"` failed closed. The public
route produces the ordinary `.out` / `.system` / QVF / citation output
(Roothaan 1960 fires), exposes real 2/1/0 occupations to the band-extrema
and sidecar writers, and reproduces the standalone driver's LiH+/STO-3G
`(3,1,1)` anchor — validated out of process against PySCF 2.13.1
KROHF/GDF to +0.062 mHa — to 2e-11 Ha. BIPOLE knobs the engine does not
honour (MOM, ODA, multipole far-field, `ewald_omega` overrides,
`sr_image_precision`, Fock mixing), ROKS/BIPOLE, smearing, DFT+U,
gradients, optimization, TD-DFT, COOP/COHP, and restarts fail closed.
Maintained preview; method maturity unchanged.

### Changed: multi-k SCF hot loops parallelise over k-points (2026-07-27)

Two per-iteration inefficiencies in the multi-k EWALD_3D machinery are
gone. The shared C++ inverse Bloch fold
(`real_space_density_from_kpoints` / `_fractional`, run every iteration by
every multi-k Ewald driver) no longer re-materialises the real/imaginary
parts of P(k) once per lattice cell and now parallelises the per-k P(k)
builds and the per-cell folds with OpenMP, keeping the historical per-block
accumulation order (bit-identical). The multi-k ROHF driver no longer
recomputes the overlap lattice integrals every SCF iteration as a density
container, and its per-iteration per-k Fock transforms now ride the fused
OpenMP `assemble_fock_multi_k` kernel instead of a serial per-k Python
fold. The pinned ROHF anchors (energies to 1e-8 Ha, iteration counts) are
unchanged, and a new regression pins the fused kernels against a direct
NumPy reference.

## [v0.15.68] - 2026-07-27 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Added: a committed natural-orbital fixture pins the HONO path (2026-07-27)

The viewer's ground-state natural-orbital branch had no real data behind it:
every `orbital_kind: "natural"` section in the wild is a natural
*transition* orbital, and a CASSCF archive cannot be produced at all.
`run_job(method="casscf", output_qvf=True)` writes only structure, citations
and run.record; the sidecar plumbing refuses a molden with "the returned
solver result does not expose format-ready mean-field orbitals and AO
density", and the QVF wavefunction section is absent for the same reason.

CASSCF itself runs fine, and its natural occupations are reachable by
diagonalizing the returned `rdm1` (H2 / 6-31G / CAS(2,2) at 2.4 Å gives
1.88542 and 0.11458), but the orbitals to go with them are not exposed, so
there is nothing to write.

The fixture is therefore the closest producible equivalent: the natural
orbitals of a broken-symmetry UHF solution, which is exactly the case Pulay
and Hamilton analyse, and the same object mathematically, a diagonalized
ground-state 1-RDM. H2 at 3.0 Å in 6-31G gives occupations 1.5594 and
0.4406 summing to the 2 electrons. `examples/vibe_view/
showcase_natural_orbitals.py` regenerates it;
`vibe-view/tests/data/h2_natural_orbitals.qvf` (2.9 kB) is committed so the
test cannot skip, and two tests assert the HONO and LUNO labels, the
occupancy readout instead of an eV gap, the Pulay window count, and that the
fixture's occupations still sum to its declared electron count.

Also fixed a cosmetic defect the real data exposed: a natural occupation of
-6.6e-17, an ordinary diagonalizer zero, formatted as "-0.000" and read as a
defect. Rounded and normalized before formatting.

Worth recording as a gap: writing a genuine CASSCF natural-orbital section
needs the solver to expose its optimized orbitals (`CASSCFResult.mo_rotation`
exists but `run_job` returns a `SolverResult` without it), and
`qvf_wf_data` hard-codes restricted occupations to 2.0 / 0.0 with no route
for fractional ones, which is why the NTO emitter builds its `mo_metadata`
by hand and why this fixture does too.

### Added: per-SHA runtime slot layout for venv hosts (2026-07-27)

The layout primitive behind "build in the background, never halt the queue".
Scheduler hosts already work this way — an immutable per-SHA bundle plus an
atomically flipped pointer — which is why a runtime update there needs no drain.
Venv hosts still `git pull` and `pip install -e` in place, so a live
interpreter's own source is rewritten underneath it, and a job paused across
that update can serve some modules from `sys.modules` and import others off the
rewritten disk. That is why venv hosts still drain.

`vq.runtime_slots` owns only the on-disk shape: `releases/<sha>/` built
out-of-place, with `current` and `previous` symlinks. The flip is a single
`rename(2)` onto `current` via a temporary symlink, never unlink-then-symlink —
the latter leaves a window in which `current` does not resolve, and a job
dispatched into that window would find no interpreter at all. Symlink targets
are stored relative so a slot root stays relocatable.

It refuses what would break the guarantee: a relative root, a SHA that is not
full lowercase hex (it arrives from release reports and remote command output,
and one containing a separator would place a slot anywhere), activating a slot
that was never built, and a real directory at `current` — which means an
un-migrated in-place install, where a flip would discard a live runtime.
Reclamation never proposes a slot named by `current`, by `previous`, or declared
in use by a live job.

**Unreachable until wired.** Nothing calls it yet, and no host behaviour
changes. Building the layout separately keeps the correctness risk — the flip
and the path handling — testable without a fleet. See
`vibe-queue/docs/design_immutable_venv_runtimes.md`.

### Fixed: a natural-orbital frontier is claimed only for actual occupancies (2026-07-27)

Checking the HONO change against real archives rather than stubs turned up a
problem. Across 18863 `wavefunction.gto` sections on this machine, 364 carry
`orbital_kind: "natural"`, and **every one of them is a natural transition
orbital**, not a ground-state natural orbital. There is no CASSCF archive in
the corpus at all, so the branch had only ever been exercised synthetically.

The two share that `orbital_kind` value but not the meaning of their
numbers. The spec defines `occupations` as an electron count per MO, which
holds for natural orbitals of the 1-RDM; an NTO's numbers are transition
weights that sum to about 1 however many electrons the molecule has. On the
H2CO TDDFT archive the ground-state section sums to 16.0000 for 16 electrons
while `wf_nto_S1_hole` sums to 1.0042. Rounding the leading NTO weight to 1
and calling it the HONO would have been exactly the category error the
previous entry set out to avoid.

A frontier is now named only when the occupations account for the system's
electron count, taken from provenance. When they do not, the pane says which
it is (transition weights, or a partial listing) instead of labelling
anything, and Pulay's active-space count is withheld on the same condition,
since that window classifies occupancies too.

Worth noting for the format: `orbital_kind` cannot currently distinguish
ground-state natural orbitals from natural transition orbitals, and the
viewer only tells them apart by summing occupations against an optional
provenance field. A producer that omits `n_electrons` gets no frontier even
for a genuine CASSCF set.

### Fixed: periodic GFN2 rare-gas cells fail closed (2026-07-27)

Periodic GFN2-xTB no longer returns the known nonphysical fcc-Ar
attractive-collapse curve. The exact article cell converges in one SCC
iteration and is cutoff-stable, but falls from `-17.11618 Ha` near
dissociation to `-17.26896 Ha` at scale 0.70. This is an H0
coordination-number physics error, not an SCF-convergence problem.

The Gamma and native k-point drivers now reject cells composed entirely of
noble-gas atoms before building the Hamiltonian. Molecular GFN2 and
non-rare-gas periodic routes are unchanged. Restoring rare-gas support
requires the H0 coordination convention and cached KCN transformation to
land together with the existing molecular external-parity gates; a physical
rare-gas equation of state additionally requires validated dispersion.

## [v0.15.67] - 2026-07-27 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Changed: natural orbitals get a HONO, not a HOMO (2026-07-27)

Refines the previous entry, which withheld a frontier from every
fractionally occupied block. That was too blunt for natural orbitals, where
the literature does speak of a highest occupied one. Pulay and Hamilton,
*J. Chem. Phys.* **88**, 4926 (1988), doi:10.1063/1.454704, § II, classify
natural orbitals by occupancy into doubly occupied, fractionally occupied
(the MC-SCF active space) and virtual, so the frontier is meaningful and
rounding identifies it.

It is not a HOMO though. A natural orbital's eigenvalue is an occupation
number, not an orbital energy, so the Koopmans reading that "HOMO" carries
does not apply. Those blocks are labelled HONO / LUNO, and instead of an eV
gap, which would subtract two numbers that are not energies, the pane
reports the two frontier occupancies. It also reports how many orbitals fall
in Pulay's 0.02 to 1.98 window, with the window named: the paper calls it
"somewhat arbitrary" in as many words, so it is shown to the reader rather
than used to decide anything silently.

Canonical orbitals with fractional occupations are a different case and
still get no frontier: that is smearing or an ensemble, where the frontier
is a Fermi level rather than an orbital. Localized orbitals still get none
either, having no energy ordering.

Four papers were added to the library wishlist
(`maintenance/manual-dois.txt`): Löwdin 1955, which defines natural orbitals
and is Pulay's own reference 12; Takatsuka 1978 and Staroverov 2000 on the
odd-electron and effectively-unpaired-electron measures; and Head-Gordon
2003, whose continuous N_u is the principled alternative to thresholding a
NOON at all.

### Changed: HOMO and LUMO are only labelled where they are defined (2026-07-27)

Follow-up to the frontier-orbital fix below, on the sharper point that an
orbital is occupied or it is not. The QVF spec defines `occupations` as an
electron count per MO, so wherever "highest occupied" means anything the
value is an integer and the test is which integer, not whether a continuous
quantity clears a margin. The occupied test is now nearest-integer, which is
both the honest reading and the one robust to float round-trip through the
archive's JSON: 1.9999999 is occupied, 0.4 is not. The old 1e-6 floor called
both occupied.

That distinction decides more than a boundary case. Where the occupations
are *not* integers, HOMO and LUMO do not exist rather than being hard to
locate: natural orbitals carry fractional occupations by construction, and
so do smeared or finite-temperature canonical orbitals. Picking the last one
above an arbitrary cut invents a frontier the wavefunction does not have,
with the cut deciding where it lands. Those blocks are now left unlabelled
and say why, and the HOMO-LUMO gap is withheld with them, since a gap
between undefined endpoints is meaningless. Localized orbitals are excluded
for a separate reason: they are not energy ordered, so "highest" has no
referent even when the occupations are clean integers.

Full population analysis, which is what would actually characterise a
fractionally occupied wavefunction, is not something the MO listing
attempts; `atom_properties` carries the population data an archive has.

### Fixed: molecular GFN2-xTB honors explicit SCC iteration budgets (2026-07-27)

The molecular native GFN2-xTB auto-stabilizer now treats `max_iter` as the
total SCC budget across the primary solve and any third-order stabilization
retry. The previous path could accept `max_iter=1` on the BUG45 pyridine
outlier, run 2280 internal SCC iterations, and return a converged energy. The
robust default is now an explicit 3600-step total budget, preserving the
existing BUG45 recovery while making deliberately smaller caps fail closed.
External `xtb` numerical, wall-time, and peak-RSS parity remain open, and
GFN2-xTB remains experimentally gated.

### Fixed: periodic GFN2 uses requested finite-temperature occupations (2026-07-27)

The Gamma-periodic GFN2-xTB driver previously ignored
`XTBSccOptions.electronic_temperature` and always built a hard-Aufbau density.
That made its declared stabilization surface inert and left a finite energy
jump when the corrected graphene screening cell crossed a nearly degenerate
frontier-orbital ordering at scale 0.98005--0.98006.

The driver now uses the shared particle-number-conserving Fermi-Dirac
occupation kernel when the caller explicitly supplies a positive electronic
temperature, while temperature zero remains exactly Aufbau. At
`k_B T = 0.001 Ha`, the energy step across that crossing falls from
`5.0197e-4 Ha` to `4.002e-6 Ha`. This is a bounded opt-in correction, not
automatic smearing: Gamma sampling and broader external-`xtb` parity remain
open, and the reported value is the fractional-occupation internal energy
rather than a Helmholtz free energy.

### Fixed: EOS fitting rejects flat semiempirical rare-gas curves (2026-07-26)

`vibeqc.eos.fit_birch_murnaghan(...)` now centralizes the BM3 fit used by
periodic screening tooling and marks fits as `ill_conditioned_fit` when the raw
energy span is below a meaningful threshold or when the fit residual is a large
fraction of the total signal. The regression uses the archived fcc-Ar DFTB0
curve whose `6.75e-8 Ha` span previously produced a fake bracketed minimum with
`4.26e-6 Ha` RMSE. This fixes the bounded DFTB0/SCC-DFTB fitter failure only;
periodic PM6 and GFN2-xTB rare-gas physics/parity remain open.
### Added (EXPERIMENTAL): `jk_method='real-gamma'` wired into `run_periodic_job` (2026-07-26)

Step 2 of the real-Γ runner integration (the FR-1 follow-up): the neutral
fitted-torus real-Γ control now runs through the unified periodic runner —
RHF/UHF/RKS/UKS including screened HSE-class hybrids, with the Γ-centred
k-mesh argument defining the BvK torus (`nrep`), the full artefact set
(`.out`/`.system`/`.qvf`/structure sidecars), and the convention records
landing in both the `.system` manifest and a
`x_vibeqc.real_gamma_convention` QVF vendor section: RESULT-derived
`exchange_q0` + `exchange_q0_applicability` (a screened hybrid records
"inactive" regardless of the requested `exchange_exxdiv`), D86 executed
values (structural 0.0 mixing/damping/level shift),
`lattice_vector_convention="columns"`, BvK `nrep`/`n_cells`,
`cderi_build`, and the SR-direct screened-exchange assembly triple.
Geometry optimization, Hessians, DFT+U, smearing, and dim<3 fail closed;
`jk_method='aiccm2026dev-a'` (the Γ-CCM construction) remains unwired and
fail-closed, and the A-prefixed control spelling stays rejected (D89).
Runner-vs-API parity is exact per method. Gates:
`tests/test_periodic_ccm_real_gamma_adapter.py` (7);
`tests/test_ccm_route.py` pins updated for the supersession.

### Fixed: terminal mode labelled every occupied orbital "HOMO" (2026-07-26)

The MO listing in `vibe-view tui` marked all occupied orbitals HOMO instead
of only the highest. The marker was chosen inside the same loop that was
still advancing the HOMO index, so at row *i* the running index always
equalled *i* and every occupied row matched. The reported HOMO-LUMO gap was
correct throughout, because it is computed after the loop from the final
index, which is what made the display wrong but plausible.

The frontier orbitals are now resolved before any row is rendered. That also
fixes a latent second bug in the same lines: the LUMO was the first
zero-occupancy row rather than the lowest virtual *above* the HOMO, so a
non-aufbau occupation would place the LUMO below the HOMO and invert the
gap. Three tests pin it, including the hole-in-the-occupations case; all
three were confirmed to fail against the previous logic.
