`output_qvf` defaults to **True** on both `run_job` and `run_periodic_job`, so
every calculation has been writing a QVF archive all along. None of the pages a
new user actually reads said so.

Verified by running the homepage's own water example: it writes ten artifacts,
not the three the page listed, and `water.qvf` (19 kB, carrying `structure`,
`trajectory`, `wavefunction.gto`, `atom_properties`, `bond_orders`,
`scf_history`, `run.record` and `citations`) was not among the three.

* `docs/index.md` now lists the `.qvf` as one of the four files you reach for

* `README.md` mentioned neither vibe-view nor QVF anywhere in its 370 lines.
  The Visualization capability bullet and the Documentation section now cover

* `docs/quickstart.md` section 4 sent readers to Avogadro / VMD / PyMOL /

### Fixed: GFN2 parameter TOML is cached across loads (2026-07-26)

`load_gfn2_params()` now reuses a validated in-process parse of the cached
GFN2-xTB TOML when the cache file identity is unchanged. Each call still
constructs a fresh mutable native `GFN2ParameterSet`, so callers cannot mutate a
shared global parameter table, but repeated molecular and periodic GFN2 setup no
longer reparses the same TOML before entering SCC. This is a bounded setup
performance/memory mitigation; GFN2-xTB remains gated experimental and the
external-xtb numerical, wall-time, and peak-RSS discrepancies remain open.

### Fixed: scheduler fetch preserves terminal outputs for sealed payloads (2026-07-27)

Scheduler result archives were extracted directly over the driver's existing
job workspace. Content-hashed campaign payloads seal their inputs read-only, so
the extraction stopped with `PermissionError` on the first repeated input and
never reached `stdout.log`, `stderr.log`, ORCA's full verbose result, or later
scientific artifacts. The job could still become terminal from its durable exit
marker, and a later `vq fetch` then copied only the unchanged input workspace.

Scheduler archives are now security-filtered into a clean staging directory
before their files are atomically overlaid onto the local workspace. This
replaces read-only inputs safely, preserves the newer driver event history,
retains terminal markers and every safe result artifact, and keeps archive or
merge failures retryable.

### Fixed: the SSH section of the vibe-view walkthrough pointed away from vibe-view (2026-07-26)

`docs/tutorial/vibe_view_walkthrough.md` closed its "Remote viewing over SSH"
section with "the cheap alternative for SSH-only access is moltui, which
renders to the terminal directly". That was true when written and is now
exactly wrong: it is the one place a reader goes looking for this, and it
sent them to a different tool for something vibe-view does itself. The
section now leads with `vibe-view show` / `vibe-view tui`, keeps port
forwarding and interface binding for readers who specifically want the
browser UI, and keeps moltui as the answer for loose files from other codes.

Terminal mode is also now shown rather than only described. Seven figures
are generated by a new `vibe-view/docs/capture_tui_screenshots.py`, the
terminal counterpart of `capture_screenshots.py`: TUI frames come from
Textual's own `export_screenshot()` driven through `App.run_test()`, and
`vibe-view show` frames from Rich's `Console.export_svg()` over the ANSI the
command really prints. They are embedded in the walkthrough, the terminal
tutorial and the vibe-view user guide.

SVG rather than PNG, because the content is text: it stays crisp at any
zoom, remains selectable and screen-reader readable, and lands at a mean
152 kB against the existing PNGs' 174 kB.

Three things the generator gets right that a naive capture would not. It
selects sections by kind rather than by counting Tab presses, after an early
draft produced a figure captioned "IR spectrum" that was actually showing
`bond_orders`; it asserts the frame it exports really is that kind. It runs
the ANSI through `Text.from_ansi` instead of printing it as a string, which
otherwise bakes literal `[0m` sequences into the figure. And it strips the
`@font-face` rule that both exporters point at cdnjs.cloudflare.com, since a
committed docs asset must not fetch a font from a third-party CDN when the
page renders, with a guard that fails the run if any `url(http...)` survives
while ignoring the SVG namespace URI.

### Fixed: a newer vq's drain state no longer un-drains older hosts (2026-07-27)

`DrainState` used `extra="forbid"`, and `read_drain_state` deliberately treats
an unparseable drain.json as "no drain" so a corrupt file cannot wedge the
dispatch loop. Those two safe-looking choices combined badly: the fleet is
routinely mid-rolling-upgrade, so a state file written by a newer vq is read by
older ones, and a single added field made the file fail validation, be treated
as corrupt, and read as **no drain** — the daemon resuming dispatch into a host
an operator had explicitly held.

Verified before changing anything: a state file carrying one unknown key parsed
to `None`, taking a held `scheduler_hosts=["site_i"]` lane with it.

Unknown keys are now ignored rather than rejected. A genuinely unparseable file
still reads as "no drain", because that fallback exists to stop a bad file
wedging dispatch and is unchanged.

This does **not** retroactively protect readers at vq <= 0.20.0, which still
forbid extras. No field may be added to `DrainState` until the fleet is past the
release carrying this change, or those hosts will un-drain. The constraint is
recorded on the model itself.

Found while designing owner-liveness for drain lanes — that work needed a new
field, which is precisely what would have tripped this.

## [v0.15.66] - 2026-07-26 - *Neese's Cheetah*
### Fixed: every CRYSTAL deck we emitted was malformed (2026-07-26)

Running vibe-basis's emitted decks through a real CRYSTAL23 for the
first time, while converging the counterpoise ghost shell, found five
defects. Each one made CRYSTAL refuse the input outright, so the
emitters had never produced a deck the program would accept.

* **No `ENDBS`.** The ` 99 0` sentinel ends the basis *data*, but the
  basis *section* still needs a terminator before the SCF keywords.
  Without it CRYSTAL reads `DFT` as a basis keyword and stops with
  `ERROR **** INPBAS **** KEYWORD NOT ALLOWED`.
* **Blank lines.** CRYSTAL reads the SCF section one keyword per line,
  so a blank line is an empty keyword: `ERROR **** READM2 **** KEYWORD
  NOT ALLOWED`. Every emitter interpolates blocks that are empty when
  an option is off, and each left a blank line behind.
* **Space group 1 with one lattice parameter.** The isolated-atom box
  is triclinic P1, which takes all six cell parameters; only the cubic
  groups accept a single number. `FORMAT ERROR IN INPUT DECK`.
* **`SHRINK 0 0`.** A large box is still a 3D periodic system and wants
  a real Monkhorst-Pack grid. One k-point is the right answer at a 10 A
  box, where the bands are flat.
* **No r2SCAN.** The functional list predated the cohesive-energy work,
  so the emitter rejected the functional the reference set is computed
  at. SCAN, r2SCAN and the r2SCAN hybrids at 10 / 25 / 50 percent HF
  exchange are now accepted, and SCAN-family decks request `HUGEGRID`,
  the pruned (300,1454) grid the manual prescribes for them: meta-GGA
  grid noise is a few kJ/mol, the same size as the differences a basis
  campaign resolves.

None of this was reachable by inspection, and the existing tests could
not have caught it: they compare emitted decks against expected strings
that were themselves never run. `test_deck_accepted_by_crystal.py` pins
each defect and, where a CRYSTAL binary is present, feeds a deck to it
and asserts positively that the program built a basis from it.

That last part matters more than the individual fixes. An earlier
version of the live test only asserted that two error strings were
absent, and passed vacuously when the deck failed for a third reason.
Absence-of-error is not evidence that something worked.

vibe-basis moves to **0.7.0**.

### Fixed: commit the vibe-view showcase fixtures so CI actually runs 26 tests (2026-07-26)

Five vibe-view test modules gate on three showcase archives via
`skipif(not _WATER.exists())` and friends, and all three were gitignored. CI
therefore never had them, so **26 tests skipped through every release gate**
while passing locally for anyone who had generated the showcases. Measured
from clean checkouts, which is what CI sees: 87 passed / 27 skipped before,
113 passed / 1 skipped after (the remaining skip is a content condition, not
a missing file). That is a
false green, not a gap in coverage: the container-submission regression fixed
in v0.15.65 was caught by a developer running locally, never by the gate.

All three are now committed, with two changes that had to happen first.
Their provenance recorded the real machine's `hostname`, replaced with
`<host>` per the privacy rule. And the water and formaldehyde showcases were
1.25 MB and 1.11 MB, several times the largest fixture already tracked, of
which 97% was volume grids of poorly-compressing float noise. Those grids are
strided down 2x with their voxel vectors scaled to match, so the field keeps
its real extent; no test asserts on their resolution (only that the sections
exist and render), giving 155 kB and 165 kB while keeping every section kind
and therefore every test's coverage. `vibe-view validate` passes on all three.

The ignore rule needed restructuring as well: git cannot re-include a file
whose parent directory is excluded, so `examples/vibe_view/runs/` became
`runs/*` plus targeted negations. Verified that the negations admit exactly
the three archives and none of the other generated artifacts under `runs/`.

### Added: counterpoise free atoms, matching the published pob protocol (2026-07-26)

Every free-atom deck in the pob cohesive-energy reference set uses
CRYSTAL's `ATOMBSSE`: the atom computed in the ghost basis of its own
crystal rather than bare. The published cohesive energies are therefore
counterpoise corrected, and one assembled from bare atoms was not the
same quantity. `emit_input_atom_counterpoise` now emits that deck,
verified structurally identical to the reference set's own.

Wired through as an engine capability rather than a flag on the
emitter: `EnergyEngine.atom_energy` takes `host=`, `"counterpoise"`
joins the capability set, `CohesivePipeline` takes `counterpoise=`, and
`CohesiveResult.counterpoise_applied` records which convention produced
the number. An engine that cannot do it records a skipped stage instead
of quietly falling back to bare atoms, the same honesty rule the
zero-point stage follows.

The cost is structural and worth knowing before enabling it. A
counterpoise atom is computed in its own host's ghost basis, so the
oxygen in MgO and the oxygen in CaO are genuinely different
calculations. Cache keys include the host, which deliberately disables
the cross-system atom sharing that makes a campaign affordable. Use it
for reference comparison; leave it off for the inner loop of an
optimisation, where a consistent convention cancels.

The ghost-shell extent (`nstar`, `rmax`) is not converged. The
reference set uses per-system values, LiF 30/10.0 and MgO 10/5.0, and
the defaults here are LiF's; converge them per system rather than
inheriting them.

vibe-basis moves to **0.6.0**. Breaking: `atom_energy` implementations
must accept `host`.
### Added: M0 gate 1a, the cohesive pipeline reproduces published pob energies (2026-07-26)

`CohesivePipeline` now has a regression test pinning it against the
`E_pob` column of the cohesive-energy reference set, and it passes
exactly: LiCl 688.2 against a published 688.1 kJ/mol per formula unit,
MgS 780.0 against 780.0. Both are inside the milestone's 1 kJ/mol bar.

The milestone's gate 1 turned out to be two questions that fail for
unrelated reasons, so they are now separated. Gate 1a asks whether our
*assembly* reproduces the published number given the reference
calculation's own total energies; it is exact, costs nothing, and is
what this test closes. Gate 1b asks whether our *emitted decks*
reproduce those total energies, which needs CRYSTAL23 runs and stays
open. A failure in the first is arithmetic; a failure in the second is
chemistry or deck construction.

Closing 1a certifies the sign convention, the Hartree to kJ/mol
constant, the formula-unit division, and the stage bookkeeping against
numbers produced by the code that made pob in the first place.

Three protocol facts were read off the reference set rather than
assumed. The free-atom decks use exactly the `SYMMREMO` + `SPIN` +
`SPINLOCK` combination corrected in vibe-basis 0.5.0, including the same
50-cycle lock, which independently confirms that fix. The published
cohesive energies are static-lattice: the comparison corrects
experiment upward by zero-point and thermal terms rather than
correcting theory downward, so a run reproducing `E_pob` must report
`zero_point_applied == False`. And the sign and unit convention match
ours, `SUM E_atom - E_bulk` converted at 96.485 kJ/mol per eV.

One gap is now explicit. The reference free atoms are computed with
`ATOMBSSE`, in the ghost basis of the crystal, so the published numbers
are counterpoise-corrected; ours are not. Gate 1b will differ by that
BSSE until it is addressed. Its magnitude is deliberately not estimated:
every atom output in the reference tree uses `ATOMBSSE`, so there is no
uncorrected counterpart to subtract from.
### Fixed: fleet updates no longer serialize unrelated lanes (2026-07-26)

An active scheduler-helper update on one cluster used the driver's single
`admin-update-in-progress` file as a global mutex. A site_i helper update waiting
for scheduler quiescence therefore made fleet rollout defer unrelated site_j
and localhost runtime updates even though those lanes shared no mutable
component.

Admin updates now acquire owner-specific, scope-aware marker leases. The same
local component, the same scheduler runtime, and a scheduler helper plus any
runtime on that scheduler host still conflict. Different hosts and different
runtime components may update concurrently. Unknown or unreadable marker shapes
remain global and fail closed. Heartbeats, phase transitions, rollback state,
stale-marker handling, explicit `--force`, scheduler-target drains, and
helper-quiescence checks retain their prior safety semantics. Fleet planning
uses the same overlap model, daemon dispatch holds the union of active leases,
and targeted marker recovery cannot clear an independent host's lease.

### Added: vibe-view atom labels now face the viewer (2026-07-26)

Atom index and atom charge labels are drawn as real 3D text, because the
browser renderer does not draw the 2D label actors VTK would otherwise use.
They were built lying flat in a fixed plane, which reads correctly from one
viewpoint and appears skewed and squashed from every other. Each label is now
turned to face the camera and raised along the camera's own up direction, so it
sits above its atom on screen instead of drifting to one side, and labels are
rebuilt whenever the viewpoint changes. This also closes a deferred
label-orientation finding from an earlier audit. Orientation refreshes when an
interaction finishes rather than continuously, so a label lags during a drag
and settles when it ends.

### Fixed: the CRYSTAL free-atom reference was spin-restricted and spherical (2026-07-26)

`vibe_basis.backends.crystal_atom.emit_input_atom` emitted no
`SYMMREMO`, no `UHF`/`SPIN` and no `SPINLOCK`, so every **open-shell**
free atom was computed spin-restricted and symmetric. Oxygen's triplet
ground state came back as a closed shell.

Nothing failed. Those SCFs converge perfectly well and simply return the
wrong energy, in the free-atom half of a cohesive energy, which is why
this survived unnoticed. It is the error class the plane-wave reference
work already quantified: spin-restricting the bromine reference alone
moved KBr's atomization energy by 37 kJ/mol, against a milestone gate
that has to hold to 1 kJ/mol.

Per the CRYSTAL23 manual, whose single-atom route states plainly that
"UHF and SPINLOCK must be used to define a reasonable orbital
occupancy", an open-shell atom now gets `SYMMREMO` in the geometry
block, `UHF` at Hartree-Fock or `SPIN` inside the `DFT` block, and
`SPINLOCK <n_unpaired> 50`. A closed-shell atom gets none of them, since
a restricted symmetric solution is already correct there.

`emit_input_atom` gains `n_unpaired` and `spinlock_cycles`, exports
`GROUND_STATE_MULTIPLICITY`, and now **raises** for an element with no
tabulated ground state rather than guessing one. `Crystal23Engine`
reports `atom_reference` describing the occupancy
(`p1_box_aspherical_spin_polarised` / `p1_box_closed_shell`) instead of
just the box, so the convention can be audited against whatever
reference a number is compared to.

The `recipes.crystal_stage1` and `recipes.crystal_objective` atom paths
inherit the corrected deck. Both now also refuse an untabulated element
instead of silently emitting a spin-restricted deck for it.

Any CRYSTAL free-atom energy computed before this fix is wrong for
open-shell elements. Cache keys are unchanged, so delete stale
`EnergyCache` journals rather than resuming onto them.

vibe-basis moves to **0.5.0**.

### Fixed: a durable exit marker outlives an unfetchable workspace (2026-07-26)

A scheduler job that had left the queue could stay `running` forever. site_i
2026-07-26: jobs `04b5d4b0b46c` (rc 127) and `9e2f3dc15a78` (rc 0) had both
disappeared from `qstat` with durable `_vq/exit-code` markers already read and
authoritative, yet sat `running` / `scheduler_state=fetch_failed` indefinitely,
and `vq fetch` reported a missing `result.tar`.

The cause was that terminal state was gated on artifact retrieval.
`fetch_results` failed because `tar -cf {ws}.result.tar -C {ws} .` cannot
archive a workspace that no longer exists, and the handler parked the row and
`continue`d — discarding an exit code vq already held. The assumption is written
into `_stamp_scheduler_fetch_failed`'s own docstring, *"staging failed and will
retry"*: true for a transport hiccup, false forever once the workspace is gone.

The two facts are now independent. Consecutive post-scheduler fetch failures are
counted, and below `SCHEDULER_FETCH_FAILURE_LIMIT` (3) the row still parks and a
recovered transport re-fetches exactly as before. On exhausting the bound with a
known rc, the daemon reaps on the marker anyway — `completed` for 0, `failed`
for nonzero — after recording `scheduler_state="artifacts_unavailable"`, so a
terminal row whose outputs are unrecoverable stays distinguishable from one
whose outputs simply have not been fetched. No resubmission and no retry.

Both fetch sites were affected. The no-marker path wedged identically: a failing
final fetch `continue`d before the missing-marker abort could classify it. It
now shares the bound and falls through to the abort.

Nothing here fabricates a replacement archive. When the remote workspace is gone
there is nothing to package, and an empty `result.tar` would make an
unrecoverable run look fetchable; the row is terminal with a trustworthy exit
code and `vq fetch` reports the missing workspace honestly.

### Added: the vibe-qc engine computes periodic energies and relaxes geometries (2026-07-26)

`VibeQcEngine` — the primary engine of the basis-optimisation roadmap — now
implements the two stages a cohesive energy needs on the Gaussian route.
`crystal_energy` drives `run_periodic_job` for the bulk single point, and
`relax` drives `bipole_optimize.relax_full` for cell + internal coordinates,
so the engine declares the optional `relax` capability. Zero-point energy
stays undeclared until the Gaussian-route phonon driver lands, which means a
pipeline running on this engine records a *skipped* ZPE stage and reports a
static-lattice cohesive energy that says so, rather than a number that looks
ZPE-corrected.

Periodic runs default to the four-centre BIPOLE route. A *candidate* basis has
no density-fitting auxiliary basis — the GDF path has nothing registered for
one — and borrowing another basis's JKFIT set would lay a fitting error on top
of the basis-incompleteness signal a cohesive-energy objective exists to
measure. BIPOLE needs no auxiliary basis and is the same route the relaxation
drives, so the single point and the geometry are consistent by construction.

An SCF that ran and failed comes back as `ok=False` with a specific
`failure_mode`, never as an exception and never as a last-cycle energy dressed
up as converged: a basis optimiser walks into infeasible regions constantly,
and a days-long campaign must score the point and continue. The structure
classes the engine cannot express — a magnetic ordering, an ECP library — fail
closed for the same reason.

Three correctness fixes came with the wiring, each of which produced a
converging SCF and a wrong number:

* **Isolated atoms were being given the wrong element's basis.** The engine
  parsed the *first* element block of the candidate basis text and stamped the
  requested `Z` on it, so oxygen in MgO was computed with magnesium's
  exponents. `basis_crystal.parse_crystal_inline_basis` now splits a
  multi-element inline basis properly and the engine selects by element.
* **The DFT atom path silently ran at LDA.** `run_rks` / `run_uks` take the
  functional on their options object, not as a keyword, so every "DFT" free
  atom ran at the default while the bulk ran at the requested functional — an
  atomisation energy wrong by the difference between the two.
* **The free-atom multiplicity table was a hand-written copy** that put
  silicon in a singlet. The engine now shares `vibeqc.atomization`'s table, so
  the periodic cohesive energy and the molecular atomisation energy cannot
  disagree about an element's ground state.

`tests/basisset_dev/test_vibeqc_engine.py` (38 tests) pins the marshalling,
the failure contract and the conventions with the SCF stubbed out, plus two
Γ-point runs that prove the wiring reaches the native core. It asserts no
energy: agreement with CRYSTAL23 on a cohesive energy is a separate acceptance
gate that needs converged settings and reference geometries, and a wiring test
that pinned a number would become a regression lock on a value nobody has
certified.

### Fixed: CRYSTAL inline basis text did not survive a re-read (2026-07-26)

`basis_crystal.emit_crystal` writes `SCAL = 0.0` on every shell header, and
`parse_crystal_atom_basis` read that as a literal scale factor, multiplying
each exponent by `0.0²` and then reporting the resulting zero exponent as a
mis-parsed shell header. Per the CRYSTAL23 manual (*Basis set input*, p. 25,
note 2) `SCAL` is meaningful only for the standard Pople `ITYB=1` sets, where
`0.` selects the standard Pople factor; for a general user basis the exponents
are already scaled, which is why CRYSTAL's own GAUSS98 exporter writes `1.`
Both `0.0` and `1.0` now mean unscaled. Emit → parse is a round trip again,
which is what the basis-optimisation engines exchange candidate bases over.

### Fixed: vibe-view Save View stored the default camera, not your view (2026-07-26)

The viewer renders client-side, where the browser owns the camera, and nothing
reported that camera back to the server. Every feature that persisted "the
current view" therefore stored whatever the last server-side camera reset had
left behind. Rotating the structure until 18 percent of the viewport changed
and saving a bookmark either side of the rotation produced byte-identical
cameras, so a saved view always restored the default orientation; Save Session
and server-side renders read the same stale camera. The browser now reports its
camera once per interaction end and the server adopts it, which corrects all
three at once. Bookmark entries also now reach the browser at all: they were
appended to a list in place, which the framework cannot detect, so the names
list updated while the entries themselves did not.

## [v0.15.65] - 2026-07-26 - *Neese's Cheetah*
### Fixed: vibe-view tests no longer skip on gitignored example archives (2026-07-26)

Thirty-seven vibe-view tests were guarded on archives under
`examples/vibe_view/`, which is gitignored. CI never has those files, so
the tests **skipped** there and the gate read green, while a developer who
had generated the showcase saw them run. A regression shipped straight
through that hole on 2026-07-26: a change to the vq submit path broke
`test_vq_submit_job_uses_queue_with_name_and_tag`, and v0.15.65 was cut
over it.

The archives are now synthesized in-process. `tests/conftest.py` gains a
`build_qvf` helper (promoted from `test_renderers.py`, where it was
private) plus four session fixtures: `water_qvf` (molecular, with the
`scf_hist0` and `traj0` ids the watcher tests activate by name),
`showcase_qvf` (periodic NaCl-like, with a volume, atom properties and two
2-D panel kinds), `tables_qvf` (four atoms, vibrations, both charge
flavours and a wavefunction, for the table/CLI extractors), and
`reaction_qvf` (a five-frame H3 path with waypoints). Eight test modules
were rewired off the file-existence guards.

One assertion was generalized rather than pinned to a fixture:
`test_wf_density_integrates_to_n_electrons` hardcoded "10 electrons" from
the water example and now derives the expected count from the archive's
own occupations, so it states the invariant (integral equals the summed
occupations) instead of a number tied to one file.

The vibe-view suite is now **1222 passed, 0 skipped** with no generated
archive present -- the CI condition. Building these fixtures also
documented three reader contracts that a symbol-only payload silently
violates: `read_trajectory` and `read_reaction_path` index
`metadata["atoms"]` as objects, and `read_vibrations` additionally
requires a `position` on each.

### Added: terminal-mode docs, tutorial, examples and SDK entry point (2026-07-26)

Follow-up to the terminal-mode landing below, covering the surfaces a feature
needs before it counts as shipped.

`render_terminal` joins `capture_structure` / `capture_volume` on the public
SDK — the same renderers with text instead of a PNG, and no GL context
required. It takes a path, a file-like, or an already-open `QVFReader` (a
caller's reader stays open, matching every other api function), and returns a
short explanation instead of raising for a section with no graphical form, so
a caller sweeping an archive never has to pre-filter by kind.

`vibe-view/examples/terminal_mode.py` is a runnable script covering the whole
surface — representations, isosurfaces, supercells, charts, text panes, frame
animation, and the full sweep — branching on what the archive actually holds
so it is safe to point at any `.qvf`. Two tests run it, one for the render
paths and one for the missing-file path.

`docs/tutorial/vibe_view_terminal.md` is the worked tutorial: produce an
archive, then read every section of it from a login shell. Its sample output
is generated by the real formatters rather than hand-drawn, and its `run_job`
call was corrected against the actual signature (`write_density` /
`write_molden_file`; an earlier draft invented a `cube_mos` parameter that
does not exist).

The docs set now also answers the question a reader actually arrives with —
*which* terminal viewer. `docs/tutorial/moltui_terminal_viewer.md` and
`docs/installation.md` gain a comparison: MolTUI reads the formats the field
already uses, so it works with output from any code; terminal mode reads
`.qvf` only, but reaches every section of a self-describing archive rather
than the one file you opened.

Per the licensing rule, `docs/license.md` gains an inventory of vibe-view's
own Python dependencies, which had never been recorded there. Licenses are
taken from the distributions' declared metadata, not from memory — trame is
Apache 2.0, not the BSD an assumption would have written.

### Added: submit a QVF job container straight from vibe-view (2026-07-26)

The Job Manager's **Submit to vq cluster** dialog gained **Submit as QVF
container**, on by default. Instead of generating a Python script, the
viewer writes a single *pending* `.qvf` — the structure on screen plus a
`job.spec` (method, basis, functional, charge, multiplicity), stamped
`run_status = "pending"` — and submits that as the whole payload. `vq`
already treats a `.qvf` input as a first-class job, so it resolves the
pinned runtime and runs `vibeqc run job.qvf`, which settles the same
archive in place: one file out, the settled one back, openable directly in
the viewer with its Job Spec and Run Record panels intact. Container jobs
are tagged `qvf-container`; no interpreter is passed, since a container
resolves its own runtime from the program pin.

Writing a *pending* archive is a producer action and vibe-view is a
consumer that does not depend on vibeqc, so the switch is disabled — with
the reason shown — when vibeqc is not importable next to vibe-view, and
the previous generated-script path is used instead. The Å→bohr conversion
that `input_generator` documents applies here too (QVF stores Å,
`vibeqc.Atom` takes bohr, and PeriodicSystem wants lattice vectors as
columns); a round-trip test pins it, since skipping it silently shrinks
every geometry by 0.529×.

Ships with `docs/tutorial/qvf_job_containers.md` (the round trip from
Python, from `vq`, and from the viewer), a user-guide section in
`vibe-view/docs/user_guide/vq_jobs.md`, and a runnable
`examples/input-qvf-container-roundtrip.py` whose sample output is the
measured run.

### Added: MACE runtime health and comparison examples (2026-07-26)

The MACE documentation now separates source implementation, optional runtime
availability, molecular `method="mace"` dispatch, direct periodic support, and
landed scientific evidence. A dependency-only health example reports source
revision, package versions, public APIs, model registry provenance, license
state, cache files, and weight digests without loading a model.

The periodic Si example now starts with a reusable two-point strain probe and
requires an explicit `--relax` for cell optimization. A new MACE/PM6 H2O
stretch example normalizes each fixed-composition curve to its own sampled
minimum, so it demonstrates a valid curve-shape comparison without mixing
incompatible absolute energy references. The tutorial removes unvalidated
adsorption and general-accuracy claims and documents the registered model
scope, OFF23 ASL gate, cache behavior, citations, and EOS boundaries.
Follow-ups from screenshotting it for the docs, none of which a test would
have caught: the dialog blurb still promised a generated script in
container mode, the `.py` path field was shown for a payload that has no
script, the live-checkpoint switch was still active though a container
settles in place, and its dynamic label rendered its raw mustache because a
Vuetify `label` is an attribute and needs Trame's tuple binding rather than
`{{ }}`. Also fixed a regression this feature introduced in
`test_vq_submit_job_uses_queue_with_name_and_tag`: it pins the
generated-script contract (an interpreter is passed) and now opts out of
container mode explicitly, instead of passing or failing depending on
whether vibeqc happens to be importable. A new controller test pins the
container path itself, and the committed figures carry a sanitized host.

### Added: vibe-view terminal mode — `vibe-view tui` and `vibe-view show` (2026-07-26)

vibe-view gains a third front-end alongside the web viewer and the PNG capture
API: a full viewer that draws into a terminal with Unicode braille characters
and 24-bit colour. Structures, isosurfaces, band structures, DOS, spectra, SCF
traces, scan surfaces, trajectories and normal modes all render; the kinds that
are tables rather than pictures (citations, run records, job specs, charges,
bond orders, MO listings, NMR/EPR tensors, QTAIM) get text panes.

The motivation is where a QVF actually lands. `vibe-view open` and
`vibe-view capture` both drive VTK through an OpenGL context, and a compute node
reached over SSH generally has no display server, no GL and no X forwarding. So
terminal mode carries its own pure-NumPy rasterizer — analytically shaded
spheres, bond cylinders, barycentric triangle rasterization, all depth-buffered
— and packs the pixel buffer into braille glyphs (2x4 dots per cell, so an 80x24
terminal is a 160x96 canvas). Isosurfaces still come from VTK's `contour`
filter, which is pure computation and needs no render window. `vibe-view show`
runs on the core install; only the interactive `vibe-view tui` needs the new
`[tui]` extra (Textual).

Element colours and radii come from the same `cpk_color` / `cpk_radius` the
interactive viewer uses, so a terminal frame and a GUI screenshot of one archive
agree. Periodic handling follows the 3D renderer's rules: only `pbc`-flagged
axes are drawn as cell edges, and a bond crossing a cell face is drawn to its
nearest periodic image rather than stretched across the box — graphene's bond
list stores such pairs at 2.84 / 3.76 / 5.68 Å for what are 1.42 Å bonds, and
both the naive reading and a length cutoff get it visibly wrong. Camera framing
solves the projection for the fitting distance instead of using a bounding
sphere, whose radius includes the depth extent and leaves a slab or a polymer at
half the size it could render. Chart conventions match the Plotly renderers:
bands and DOS Fermi-reference only when E_F is inside the data window, and SCF
convergence plots |ΔE| on a log axis whose limits are taken after the transform
(taking them before inverts the axis and clips the converging tail).
### Added: vibe-view ribbon colouring by b-factor (2026-07-26)

The cartoon ribbon can be coloured by crystallographic temperature factor:
blue for the rigid low-B end, red for the mobile high-B end. The ramp is
normalised over the structure being viewed rather than an absolute scale,
because b-factors from different refinements are not comparable and a fixed
range flattens a well-ordered structure into a single colour; the status line
therefore states the observed range and atom count alongside the render. An
atom with no recorded b-factor is drawn in an off-scale grey rather than the
coldest colour, since absent is not the same as rigid, while a genuine 0.00
remains on the ramp as the datum it is. A file carrying no b-factors at all
falls back to chain colour and says so. Unlike the categorical schemes the
ramp interpolates, b-factor being a continuous quantity.

`StructureData.ca_residues()` is now public. It is the single alpha-carbon
ordering that `backbone_trace()` and `secondary_structure()` share, and any
per-residue array zipped against the trace must walk it rather than
re-deriving it.

### Changed: a scheduler runtime update no longer waits for running work (2026-07-26)

A release could not land on a cluster that was never idle. `vq admin update
<program> <scheduler-host>` drained the target and refused while any job was
active, so on a continuously-rolling fleet every release queued behind the
longest-running calculation — routinely `--drain-wait 4h`.

That wait protected nothing. A runtime deployment is *contractually required* to
"stage away from the active path and atomically switch it only after its own
build checks pass" (`config.SchedulerRuntimeDeployment`), and nothing reclaims a
published per-SHA bundle — which is why site_i has accumulated eleven. A running
job therefore keeps the exact bundle it started with for its whole life, and an
atomic pointer flip cannot reach it.

Runtime updates now proceed immediately with jobs running. `--drain-wait` is
accepted and ignored on that path (existing fleet invocations and the rollout
planner both still pass it), and the result carries `drain_skipped_reason` so a
transcript shows the skip was deliberate rather than silently dropped. The
contract stays enforced rather than assumed: verification already fails the
update unless the receipt reports `activation='atomic'` with an `active_path`
and `quiescent=true`, so a deployment command that mutates the active path in
place fails closed instead of corrupting a running job.

The **helper** update keeps its wait, and the reason is now written down at the
call site so it is not deleted later as symmetric cleanup: it replaces the vq
installation the scheduler side itself uses to poll, reconcile and dispatch,
which has no per-SHA bundle or atomic-flip contract behind it.

`test_update_scheduler_runtime_refuses_active_scheduler_job` pinned the old
contract and is replaced by
`test_update_scheduler_runtime_proceeds_with_an_active_scheduler_job`, which runs
a full update to success with a job still active on the target.

Venv hosts (`site_e`, `site_b`, `site_c`, `site_a`, `localhost`) are **not** covered
by this change — they still mutate in place and must still drain. Per-SHA runtime
slots for them are the next increment; see
`vibe-queue/docs/design_immutable_venv_runtimes.md`.

### Fixed: GFN2-D4 reference data is cached per process (2026-07-26)

Molecular `GFN2Model` now loads the immutable native-D4 reference dataset once
per Python process instead of reparsing `d4_reference_data.json` on every
energy call. This removes avoidable JSON parsing and transient allocations
from repeated GFN2 single points and finite-difference gradients while leaving
the D4 formula, supported-element warnings, and experimental GFN2 gate
unchanged. The broader external-xtb numerical, wall-time, and peak-RSS
discrepancies remain open.

### Fixed: periodic PM6 cancels diamond-Si image-shell monopoles (2026-07-26)

The periodic PM6 core baseline now uses the same two-center gamma kernel as
electron-core attraction. Silicon exposed the mismatch because its electronic
block uses the multi-term NDDO gamma expansion while core repulsion used the
separate `polvo` soft-Coulomb kernel. When the 15-bohr translation sphere lost
12 cells between lattice scales 1.02 and 1.04, those blocks changed by
`+26.12996` and `-27.14913 Ha`, leaving a spurious `-1.01917 Ha` step.

The core block now changes by `-26.12801 Ha` at that boundary, cancelling the
unchanged electronic monopole to a `0.00195 Ha` total step in line with its
neighbors. Conventional PM6 damping and Gaussian pair terms remain
short-range corrections, and the established graphene, Ice-Ih, dry-ice,
fcc-Ar, and explicit molecular-limit regressions are unchanged. Periodic PM6
remains experimental pending independent MOPAC parity; the separate h-BN
physics row also remains open.

### Fixed: an auto-generated build job is born admissible (2026-07-26)

`vq submit HOST --refresh ENV` and the auto-update timer generate a
`build-ENV` job, and it requested `os.cpu_count()` outright — the machine's
physical core count, ignoring the daemon's caps entirely. On any host whose
daemon caps CPUs below physical, that spec can never be admitted: site_b has 16
cores against an 8-CPU cap, so every generated build was born unadmittable and
self-service env refresh simply did not work there. It sat `PENDING` forever
before the daemon learned to terminal-fail such a spec, and fails immediately
after — unusable either way.

The request is now clamped to what the local daemon will actually admit, taking
the most authoritative source available: the daemon's advertised effective
budget (`daemon_capacity.json`, written at startup *after* CLI flags and config
are resolved, so it is the only source reflecting a CLI-only `--max-cpus`), then
the durable `[daemon] max_cpus` config section for a daemon that has not
advertised, then the physical count — which is what the daemon itself defaults
`max_cpus` to, so an uncapped host is unchanged. A cap above the machine never
inflates the request.

CPU count is a build-parallelism hint, not a correctness requirement, so
clamping costs build wall time and nothing else.

Not the whole site_b story: site_b currently advertises no capacity at all, so it
needs a daemon restart (or `[daemon]` caps in its config) before the clamp can
see its 8-CPU limit, and its memory dimension is untouched by this change. Both
are recorded in `handovers/HANDOVER_OPEN_BUGS_V015.md`.

### Fixed: molecular GFN2-xTB rejects nonconverged SCC before D4 (2026-07-26)

`GFN2Model.energy()` now fails closed when the native molecular GFN2-xTB SCC
driver returns `converged=False`. The wrapper records the native iteration
count/result for diagnostics, then raises before applying the post-SCF D4
correction or returning a scalar energy from a nonstationary density. This
closes a bounded finalization leak only; GFN2-xTB remains gated experimental
and the broader external-xtb parity, wall-time and memory discrepancies remain
open.
### Added: cohesive-energy pipeline for basis optimization (2026-07-26)

vibe-basis 0.4.0 adds `vibe_basis.pipeline`, which composes an
`EnergyEngine` into a cohesive (atomization) energy: relax, single
point, zero-point energy, isolated atoms, assemble. The result is
kJ/mol per formula unit with the sign convention of
`vibeqc.atomization.AtomizationResult` (positive for a bound solid).

There is **one concrete pipeline, not one per engine.** The engine
abstraction already absorbs every program difference, so the engine is
a constructor argument and no branch on it appears in the module. That
is what makes the milestone's acceptance gate meaningful: run the
identical orchestration on two engines, and a disagreement is provably
the engines' rather than the orchestration's.

Relaxation and zero-point energy are **optional engine capabilities**
(`EnergyEngine.supports`), not separate protocols. An engine that lacks
one produces a *recorded skipped stage naming the engine*, never a
defaulted value — returning the input geometry would look like a
converged relaxation, and returning zero would look like a solid with
no vibrations. `CohesiveResult.zero_point_applied` states whether the
number includes the correction, because a static-lattice cohesive
energy and a ZPE-corrected one differ by tens of kJ/mol, the same size
as the effects being measured. A failed ZPE therefore downgrades a
result and says so, while a failed relaxation stops the run before an
SCF is spent on a geometry that is not one.

`vibe_basis.cache` is a content-addressed cache over an append-only
JSONL journal, so a campaign killed mid-run resumes instead of
re-spending the queue. Free-atom entries carry **no system
identifier**, which makes the oxygen computed for MgO reusable for CaO
— the win that matters, since atoms are the expensive part (a single
free F atom cost 100–240 s in the plane-wave reference work while the
solid was quick). Keys derive from declared configuration only, never
from observed output: keying on a reported engine version would be
unstable, because the CRYSTAL engine cannot report one until its first
evaluation and the key would change halfway through a run.

This is the API half of the milestone. Its acceptance gate — the
pipeline reproducing published pob cohesive energies on CRYSTAL23, then
vibe-qc reproducing CRYSTAL23 — needs real runs and is tracked in
`handovers/HANDOVER_BASISOPT.md`.

### Added: vibe-view colours the cartoon ribbon by residue type (2026-07-26)

"Ribbon colour" gains a third option, Residue type, which colours each residue
by its own identity in the RasMol amino scheme (Sayle and Milner-White, *RASMOL:
biomolecular graphics for all*, Trends Biochem. Sci. 20, 374 (1995)). The
palette is transcribed from that scheme rather than invented, because the value
of colouring by residue type is that a reader already knows the mapping: acidic
red, basic blue, aromatic indigo, sulphur yellow, hydroxyl orange, amide cyan,
aliphatic green. Non-standard and unknown residues take the scheme's own
fallback colour, and a chain carrying residue numbers but no residue names falls
back to chain colour rather than rendering one flat fallback hue, which would
say nothing and read as a rendering fault. Colouring stays categorical and is
not smoothed, as for secondary structure; a residue selection still overrides
it. Verified live on DHFR at 9 distinct saturated hues in the viewport against 3
for secondary structure and 1 for chain, with the lit-pixel fraction unchanged.

### Added: vibe-view residue and chain selection on the cartoon ribbon (2026-07-26)

A "Select residues" field appears for the cartoon representation, and matching
residues render white over whichever ribbon colour mode is active — white being
the one value that cannot be mistaken for a chain hue or a secondary-structure
colour. The grammar is three forms and no operators: `A` for a whole chain,
`A/24-38` for a range, `A/24` for one residue, and `*` in the chain position for
every chain, with terms separated by commas or whitespace. A term with no slash
is always a chain id and never a residue number, because mmCIF chain ids can be
numeric and inferring from the shape of the token would make one selection mean
different things in different files; chain ids match case-sensitively, since in
a PDB chain a and chain A are two different chains. The field commits on Enter
or on leaving it rather than per keystroke, as each commit rebuilds the scene.

The summary line under the field is part of the feature, not decoration: a
selection that matches nothing is indistinguishable from a render bug unless it
says so. It reports the residue count and the chains touched, and calls out an
absent chain id and an unreadable term separately. It also covers the case a PDB
with blank chain columns creates, where every residue groups under an empty
chain id that no selection can name: naming a chain that does not exist on such
a file adds a pointer to the `*` wildcard rather than insisting the chain is
missing. A structure with nothing selected renders exactly as before, since the
per-sample colour array only materialises once something matches.

Selection is scoped to the cartoon representation, the same way the Ribbon
colour picker is; the control is hidden for the atom representations, which
would need a separate atom-level highlight path.

### Fixed: base release installs now include ASE for semiempirical optimization (2026-07-26)

`ase>=3.22` is now a base runtime dependency, with the `[ase]` extra kept as a
compatibility alias. The public `run_job(optimize=True)` route for DFTB0,
SCC-DFTB, PM6, MSINDO, GFN2-xTB, and MLIP methods deliberately uses ASE
because the native molecular optimizer owns only Gaussian-basis providers; site_i
release deployments install with `--extras none`, so declaring ASE only in
optional extras made those basis-free optimization jobs fail before any
semiempirical energy or force evaluation. A packaging metadata regression now
pins the base dependency.

### Fixed: periodic OMx cancels neutral lattice-image monopoles (2026-07-26)

Gamma-periodic OM1/OM2/OM3 now sum nonzero overlap, resonance, and exchange
blocks as directed image pairs, weight image core pairs by one half, and use
the overlap-decaying transition-density exchange kernel. More importantly,
their non-orthogonal image electrostatics now use the conserved Mulliken
population `Tr(P S)` and the overlap-weighted atomic potential instead of
mistaking `Tr(P)` for the electron count. The archived one-carbon chain made
that error visible: its nominally neutral four-electron cell was assigned a
2.678-electron image population, leaving a fictitious charged `1/R` tail and
a 1.398-Ha energy jump when the 15-bohr image sphere lost two cells.

The same 0.995 to 1.000 strain boundary now changes by 0.0560, 0.0495, and
0.0493 Ha for OM1, OM2, and OM3, in line with its neighboring strain steps.
At scale 1.0, increasing the cutoff from 15 to 30 bohr changes each result by
less than `0.7e-6 Ha`. The periodic solver now stays in the
Löwdin-orthonormal metric throughout and tests its physical commutator plus
energy, matching the molecular OMx solver architecture; the public wrapper
also uses the native `1e-5` overlap-eigenvalue floor instead of the stale 0.5
override. Periodic OMx remains experimental pending independent MOPAC parity
and broader polar/two-dimensional validation.

## [v0.15.64] - 2026-07-26 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Changed: vibe-view cartoon draws flat helix ribbons and sheet arrows (2026-07-26)

The cartoon representation no longer sweeps a circular tube of varying radius
along the alpha-carbon trace. Each spline sample now carries an orientation
frame plus its own half-width and half-thickness, and an elliptical
cross-section is swept along that, so a helix renders as a flat band 2.2 A
across and 0.4 A edge-on rather than a thick cord, and each beta-strand run
ends in an arrowhead pointing at its C-terminus. Loops keep equal width and
thickness, so they stay round. The frame is the standard alpha-carbon
construction from Carson and Bugg, *Algorithm for ribbon models of proteins*,
J. Mol. Graphics 4, 121-122 (1986); its sign is propagated along the chain,
without which a strand's zig-zagging alpha-carbons twist the ribbon a half
turn per residue. Runs shorter than three residues get no arrowhead, since the
secondary-structure detector reads those as bridges rather than sheets.

The wire payload is unchanged: 56,636 triangles and 0.60 MB on the
885-residue ClC benchmark, identical to the tube this replaces, with server
build at 0.07 s against 0.04 s. A payload regression test pins the three
properties that keep it there — triangle strips rather than polygons,
renderer-computed point normals, and float32 arrays — each of which roughly
doubled the payload when absent, with no visible difference in the render.

### Fixed: periodic MACE scans can reuse one loaded model (2026-07-26)

`PeriodicMACEEvaluator` retains the upstream calculator and model weights
across a sequential fixed-model scan while validating every new structure and
preserving the established lattice, unit, provenance and ASL-license
contracts. The one-shot `run_periodic_mace` API is unchanged. Construct one
evaluator per worker for parallel scans. Regression:
`tests/test_mlip_mace.py::test_periodic_mace_evaluator_reuses_one_loaded_model`.

### Added: vibe-view reads b-factors and prefers producer-supplied biomolecule metadata (2026-07-26)

`pdb_to_qvf` preserves the PDB temperature factor (cols 61-66) onto each atom,
and `Atom` carries it as `b_factor`. A missing column reads as `None` rather
than `0.0`, because a b-factor of 0.00 is a real measurement and conflating the
two would paint unmeasured atoms as the coldest. `read_structure` also reads a
producer-supplied section-level `b_factors` array, which fills in only where an
atom did not carry its own value; an array whose length disagrees with the atom
count is ignored whole rather than applied partially. This is the data path for
the colour-by-b-factor ribbon mode, not the mode itself.

Where an archive supplies `residues`, `chains`, or `secondary_structure`, the
reader now prefers those over its own inference, which is what the QVF spec
requires: the viewer's CA-only assignment cannot tell an alpha from a pi from a
3-10 helix, or a beta-bridge from a sheet, and a producer can. `chains()` uses
supplied residues when they resolve to in-range atoms and otherwise derives as
before, so the contiguous-run grouping that keeps wrapped PDB residue numbers
apart is untouched. `secondary_structure()` applies supplied ranges **per
chain**: a producer that annotates one chain and says nothing about another
leaves the second on geometry rather than flattening it to coil, and residues
an annotated chain's ranges do not cover are coil. `chain_ids()` is new and
returns the supplied chain order when there is one. `has_residues` is now true
from supplied residues alone. The edit overlay drops all of it, since supplied
atom indices refer to the file's atom list that the overlay replaced.

This closes cross-repo Ask B. Tests:
`vibe-view/tests/test_biomolecule_metadata.py`.
### Added: QVF biomolecule metadata is schema'd, and gains b-factors (2026-07-26)

The four optional biomolecule fields on a `structure` section object are now
named in the canonical manifest schema instead of merely riding an open Section
object: `chains`, `residues` (via the new `$defs/BiomoleculeResidue`),
`secondary_structure` (via `$defs/BiomoleculeSecondaryStructure`), and a new
`b_factors` array carrying one temperature factor per atom in payload order.
`$defs/StructureAtom` gains an optional per-atom `b_factor`, the carrier a
PDB-derived structure uses. The writer accepts `b_factors` through the existing
`biomolecule_data` context key, and drops a secondary-structure range whose
`type` is outside helix/sheet/coil rather than failing the whole archive at the
validate gate.

Spec section 5.1 gains a normative precedence rule, because vibe-view derives
residues, chains and secondary structure itself and needed to know which source
wins: a consumer must prefer producer-supplied values over its own inference,
since a producer knows what CA geometry cannot reveal, and a per-atom
`b_factor` beats the section-level array because it cannot desynchronize from
its own atom. An array whose length disagrees with the atom count is ignored
outright rather than applied partially.

Every field is optional, which is the additive case, so there is **no
`qvf_version` bump**: this closes vibe-view's cross-repo Ask 1 Ask B without the
`qvf_manifest_v3.schema.json` that ask proposed, per the versioning policy and
the 2026-07-10 withdrawal of `qvf_version: 2` recorded in
`qvf-writer/GOVERNANCE.md`. The reference writer toolkit passes the section
fields and the per-atom biomolecular fields through as well. Tests:
`tests/test_qvf_biomolecule.py` (including that a structure carrying none of the
fields still validates, and that malformed values are now actually rejected),
`qvf-writer/python/tests/test_reference_writer.py`.

### Fixed: the deploy side also refuses non-release-gate evidence (2026-07-26)

The deploy-side half of the evidence gate. `make_release_report.py` stopped
*generating* reports that rest on an ordinary `main` pipeline, but a report is
a committed JSON file, and `parse_report` — which is what
`vq admin rollout-latest` consults to decide a report is deployable — never
looked at `ci_evidence.ref`. So a report written by an older vq, hand-edited,
or simply already on disk stayed deployable. `parse_report` now refuses any pin
whose evidence ref is not a release-gate ref (a `vX.Y.Z` tag or
`release-candidate/*`), which is the same set the generator enforces; a drift
guard pins the two predicates to one behaviour, since the generator is
deliberately stdlib-only and cannot import `vq`.

This is a consistency gate, not an authenticity one: `ref` is the report's own
claim, and parsing stays deterministic and offline over immutable git objects
rather than re-querying GitLab. It catches legacy, stale, and mistaken
evidence, not a deliberate forgery.

Effect on the committed reports: `v0.15.63` (the one that deploys) and
`v0.15.61` are evidenced by their release-gate pipelines and are unaffected.
The consumer's own fixtures had built every pin with `"ref": "main"`, which is
exactly why nothing on the deploy side ever exercised evidence provenance.

`v0.15.60.json` is **retracted**, following the same precedent as `v0.15.62`.
Three of its four pins cited ordinary `main` pipelines (4598, 4602, 4608), so
it claimed `all_pins_accepted: true` on evidence that does not prove a release
tree, and it can never be regenerated: its release-candidate pipeline 4591 ran
no `test-vq` job at all, which makes the vq pin rule C. It was already
unreachable operationally — discovery is newest-first and stops at the newest
acceptable report — and since this release it was refused outright. Retracting
it removes the last way a future reader could mistake it for evidence. The
v0.15.60 tag, its release commit, and the file's own history are untouched in
git; only the deployable-report claim is withdrawn.
### Changed: one engine abstraction for basis optimization; CRYSTAL23 retarget (2026-07-26)

Basis optimization gains a single engine protocol, and the CRYSTAL
backend now targets **CRYSTAL23**. vibe-basis moves to **0.3.0**.

`vibe_basis.engine.EnergyEngine` is the one abstraction: implementers
override `crystal_energy` / `atom_energy`, which return an
`EngineEnergy` carrying the engine name, its version, a failure mode and
free-form detail alongside the number. The float-returning
`evaluate_crystal` / `evaluate_atom` are concrete methods **derived from**
those, so the two views cannot disagree and every existing call site
keeps working unchanged. Failed evaluations return `ok=False` rather than
raising — a derivative-free optimizer scores infeasible points `inf` and
routes around them, and a days-long campaign must not abort because one
exponent collapsed. `EngineEnergy.energy_if_ok()` refuses to hand out a
non-converged run's last-cycle energy, which is otherwise how such a
value gets silently consumed as converged.

The roster: `VibeQcEngine` (primary; the isolated-atom path works, the
periodic path is the next milestone), `Crystal23Engine` (Gaussian
fallback and the head-to-head baseline), and `GpawEngine` (plane-wave
fallback — declared and constructible, but raising until it is wired to
the existing validated PW-limit worker out-of-process).

`Crystal23Engine` and the `Calculator` ABC it descended from **moved out
of** `vibeqc.basis_optimization.calculators` into vibe-basis. Both
imported only from `vibe_basis` and needed nothing from vibe-qc, so they
were driver-tier code sitting on the vibe-qc side.
`calculators.py` now holds only `VibeQcEngine`, which genuinely needs the
native build. `vibeqc.basis_optimization.__init__` still imports no
third-party package, so `optimize_bdiis` and the analytic
`energy_gradient` remain usable on a plain `pip install vibe-qc` without
the `[basisopt]` extra.

The CRYSTAL retarget is naming plus provenance, not a parser rewrite:
the `.d12` surface vibe-basis emits is stable CRYSTAL09 through 23, the
`TOTAL ENERGY` / `SCF ENDED` lines are unchanged, and the one real
difference — CRYSTAL23's dated `EEEEEEEEEE TERMINATION` banner against
CRYSTAL14's bare rule of E's — was already handled. What is new is
`probe_version()`, which reads the major version off the start-up
banner, and `CrystalEnergyResult.crystal_version` /
`version_matches()`, so a result records *which* CRYSTAL produced it
instead of leaving that assumed. Version is provenance, not a gate: an
output with no visible banner still parses to a usable energy, and
`version_matches()` is three-valued (match / mismatch / unknowable).
`Crystal23Engine.strict_version` (off by default) turns a mismatch into
a failed evaluation for production campaigns, where a stray binary on
one host quietly contributing points is the real hazard.

Module paths `vibe_basis.backends.crystal14{,_atom}` are renamed to
`…crystal{,_atom}` — breaking, under the SemVer 0.x minor allowance.
`vb parse` takes `crystal` as the canonical backend name with
`crystal14` / `crystal17` / `crystal23` as aliases (one parser genuinely
reads all three, and now reports which it saw) and prints the detected
version. Emitted `.d12` titles say "CRYSTAL23 parity".

Two guards landed alongside: `vibe-basis/tests/test_no_vibeqc_dependency.py`
(an AST scan asserting no vibe-basis module imports vibe-qc at any
nesting depth — the dependency arrow must stay one-way, or the
ten-second collaborator install and the clean MPL-2.0 surface both go)
and `tests/basisset_dev/test_optresult_contract.py` (pins the two
`OptResult` dataclasses structurally; they are a deliberate duplication,
because collapsing them either reverses that arrow or makes the external
driver package a hard requirement for vibe-qc's own native optimizer).

Plan and rationale: `vibe-basis/ROADMAP.md`, tracked in
`handovers/HANDOVER_BASISOPT.md`.

### Added: `[basisopt]` extra installs the basis-set optimization driver (2026-07-26)

`uv pip install -e '.[basisopt]'` now installs the co-located
`vibe-basis` driver into the vibe-qc environment, wired the same way as
`[viewer-gpu]` — an ordinary `vibe-basis>=0.1` pin redirected to
`vibe-basis/` through `[tool.uv.sources]`, never a relative `file:`
direct-URL (which breaks even the base install, since uv reads every
extra's `Requires-Dist`). Under pip, install it as a second step:
`pip install -e . && pip install -e vibe-basis/`.

This closes a latent gap rather than adding a feature. Six modules
shipped inside the vibe-qc wheel — `vibeqc.basis_optimization.calculators`
and `recipes.{crystal_objective,crystal_stage1,crystal_stage2,crystal_stage3,production}`
— import `vibe_basis` at module top level, and `vibe_basis` was installed
in none of the 40 local vibeqc environments audited on 2026-07-26. No
test imported it, so nothing caught it. `tests/test_packaging_extras.py`
now pins the extra's wiring and imports all six wherever the extra is
present. The extra adds only Click and NumPy, both already vibe-qc
dependencies; vibe-basis's optimizers stay behind its own
`[nlopt]` / `[iminuit]` / `[scipy]` / `[all]` extras.

vibe-basis moves to **0.2.0** and adopts an independent version line
(`vibe-basis/VERSIONING.md`), as `vq` and `vibeview` have; its Python
floor drops from `>=3.12` to `>=3.11` to match vibe-qc's, so the extra
resolves across vibe-qc's whole supported range. vibe-basis remains a
**deliberate non-target** for fleet rollout — it is a client that submits
*to* the fleet through the `vq` CLI, not a payload that runs on it —
recorded in `handovers/HANDOVER_VIBE_BASIS_DEPLOYMENT.md`. No
`vibe-queue` change: `PROGRAM_PINS` keeps its four programs and the
release report's `sibling_versions_at_release.vibe_basis` string stays
correct as-is.

### Fixed: an unreachable host no longer disappears from a fleet rollout plan (2026-07-26)

`vq admin status --all --json` isolates a per-host failure as
`{"error": ...}` so one bad host cannot break the sweep. The rollout planner
discarded that sentinel: finding no `envs`/`deployments`, every lane-state
reader returned "not configured", so an unreachable host's lanes planned as
`skip` "no managed local venv lane" — indistinguishable from a host that
genuinely has no lane. `vq admin rollout-latest --dry-run` exited 0 without
ever naming the host. Worse on a scheduler host, whose helper lane takes
`configured` from config rather than from the payload: the planner proposed a
real helper *update* against a host it could not reach. Such lanes now defer
with the probe's own error, naming the host and the transport failure.
Deferral, not a block, so a single down host still cannot stop the independent
hosts. A real rollout already failed closed here (`doctor_failures` forces
`blocked`); that safety net is now pinned by a test. Found while diagnosing the
v0.15.62 fleet skew, which was itself an in-flight rollout and not a defect.

### Fixed: an admin-update marker is attributed to the host that holds it (2026-07-26)

A scheduler host has no daemon of its own, so its status payload carries the
*driver's* marker, while a local-scheduler host delegates remotely and returns
its own. The planner attributed every marker to the host whose payload carried
it, so a site_j update reported as "active update marker on site_i
(envs=scheduler-runtime:site_j:vibeqc-dev)" — which reads exactly like a scope
leak and costs real time to tell apart from one. The deferral itself was always
correct: the marker is a driver-global mutex, so `_guard_admin_update_marker`
refuses any `vq admin update` from that driver while it is held. The reason now
names the marker's own target, and says when a marker is stale, because the
recovery differs (wait vs. clear). The regression fixture that missed this put
the marker in a single host's payload, a shape `collect_snapshots` cannot
produce; it now carries the driver marker into every scheduler-host payload.

### Fixed: fleet release reports accept release-gate evidence only (2026-07-26)

`make_release_report.py` asked GitLab for every pipeline at a release SHA and
believed the first one carrying a green gate job, whatever ref it ran on. The
release-only CI policy says only the release-gate pipeline — a `vX.Y.Z` tag or
a `release-candidate/*` branch — proves a release tree, but nothing enforced
it, and pre-policy `main` pipelines are still returned by the API for older
commits. The gate is now enforced in `gating_evidence`, which discards any
pipeline whose ref is not a release-gate ref.

This was not theoretical: the committed v0.15.62 report claimed
`all_pins_accepted: true` with its release and dev pins evidenced by `main`
pipeline 4630, while release-gate pipeline 4631 had failed `build-test` on the
identical tree. Since `rollout-latest` deploys the newest accepted report, that
release was deployable to the fleet on evidence the policy forbids. The report
has been retracted; v0.15.62 cannot be regenerated and is unevidencable. The
v0.15.61 report is regenerated against its release-gate pipeline 4611, pinning
the same tag and SHAs on truthful evidence. Taking a green component gate from
a release-gate pipeline that failed a *different* component's gate stays
allowed, since each component is gated by its own job.

### Fixed: periodic GFN2-xTB honors the public SCC iteration budget (2026-07-26)

The Gamma-periodic GFN2-xTB runner now forwards `max_iter` and `conv_tol` to
the native SCC options, and the native automatic-stabilization path treats
`max_iter` as a hard total across all attempts. The exact h-BN scale-1.06
reproducer now fails honestly at 500 iterations instead of reporting success
after 2096, while an explicit 1000-iteration budget reaches the same stationary
branch in 557 iterations at the native default tolerance. This changes no
Hamiltonian, image sum, charge-response equation, or convergence threshold.
Periodic GFN2-xTB remains gated experimental.

## [v0.15.63] - 2026-07-26 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Fixed: periodic PM6 rejects cancellation-dominated Pulay histories (2026-07-26)

Gamma-periodic PM6 now uses the shared guarded fixed-depth DIIS
implementation instead of its private unchecked bordered solve. The exact
Pa-3 dry-ice scale-0.96 campaign point now converges in 290 iterations rather
than failing at 1200, and the neighboring scale-0.98 point drops from 474 to
399 iterations, without damping, level shifts, smearing, or threshold
relaxation. A three-point dry-ice regression pins the smooth solver branch.
Periodic-PM6 molecular-crystal accuracy and its direct-space cutoff sensitivity
remain explicitly experimental and are not claimed fixed.

### Added: vibe-view ribbon colour by chain or secondary structure (2026-07-26)

A "Ribbon colour" picker appears for the cartoon representation, offering
Chain, which gives one hue per chain so subunits stay tellable apart, and
Secondary structure, which colours helices red, sheets yellow and loops grey
following the convention the field reads without a legend. The picker is hidden
for every other representation, where it would do nothing. Structure mode falls
back to chain colour on any chain with no assignment to colour by. Colouring is
categorical by design and is not smoothed the way the radius profile is, since
a blended colour would imply a structure that was never assigned.

### Added: vibe-view secondary structure and architecture-aware ribbons (2026-07-26)

`StructureData.secondary_structure()` assigns helix, strand or coil per
alpha-carbon from the CA trace alone, using the distance and virtual
angle/dihedral descriptors P-SEA established rather than real DSSP's
hydrogen-bond energies, since a QVF is not guaranteed to carry backbone
oxygen. Assignment is per chain, so a window never spans a chain break.
Validated on two architectures: DHFR gives 4 helices and 11 strands against
its published 4 helices and 8-stranded sheet, and the ClC channel gives 77
percent helix in 36 helices, as an alpha-helical channel should. The cartoon
representation now uses this, thickening over helices and strands and thinning
over loops, which turns an undifferentiated tube into a ribbon that shows the
fold's architecture. It falls back to the uniform tube whenever the assignment
is unavailable or inconsistent.

### Changed: CI runs once per release, on the exact release tree (2026-07-26)

Maintainer policy: ordinary `main` pushes no longer create any GitLab
pipeline — the `workflow:` rules refuse pipeline creation, and day-to-day
test evidence is produced locally before landing. The single release-gate
pipeline (version tag or `release-candidate/*` branch) runs every component
gate exactly once on the exact release tree: `build-test` (clean native
build + blocking T0+T1 profile), `test-vq`, `ruff-vq`, `vibe-view-test`,
`docs-build`, and `ci-path-policy`. `make_release_report.py` now pins all
four components (release, dev, vq, vibe-view) to the release commit and
accepts only that pipeline's per-job evidence at the exact SHA; it never
walks main pipelines. Website deploys stay decoupled (`main` pushes touching
`website/**` still deploy), and on-demand docs/website publishing moves to
manually started pipelines. The tested path-policy classifier, its unit
tests, and the docs (`docs/release_process.md`, the fleet update runbook,
`CLAUDE.md` § 2/§ 9/§ 14, `AGENTS.md`) moved together.

### Changed: fleet rollouts are report-pinned end to end (vq 0.19.0, 2026-07-26)

The accepted release report is now the sole source of every deployed vq
identity. `vq admin update <scheduler-host> --expected-sha SHA` stages the
cluster-side helper from that exact commit of the managed runtime repository
via `git archive` (dirty/ahead driver worktrees can no longer leak into a
helper deployment), and `vq admin rollout-latest` always passes the report's
vq pin. A deployed vq lane (driver, helper, or venv `vibeqc-queue`) that is
*ahead* of the accepted pin is explicit release drift: the plan fails closed
naming both SHAs and the recovery (cut the next release so the report pins
the deployed vq, or redeploy the pin), instead of combining "no downgrade"
with helper staging from the ahead tree. Chemistry lanes keep the plain
no-downgrade skip.

### Fixed: helpers at the accepted pin are recognised canonically (2026-07-26)

Helper updates now persist a canonical LAST OK record (same store and shape
as the scheduler runtime lanes; surfaced as the `helper` block in
`vq admin status <scheduler-host> --json`), and the rollout planner proves
"already at the accepted pin" from that record plus the live provenance
probe — never by comparing the helper against the live driver checkout. The
doctor's `scheduler_remote_vq` check also reports the helper's SOURCE-SHA as
a structured field even when the tree digest differs from the driver. A
helper standing exactly at the accepted pin can no longer be reported as
"not deployed" because the driver tree moved, and an immediate second
rollout (or dry run) is a true no-op.

### Added: per-action deploy evidence and persistent compiler caching (2026-07-26)

The site_i and site_j runtime deployers emit machine-readable
`VQ-DEPLOY-METRIC` lines — dependency-cache decision with the exact
per-candidate incompatibility on a cold rebuild (build-stamp drift report,
toolchain fingerprint mismatch quoting both digests, incomplete dependency
set), compiler-cache hit/miss counts and hit rate, build/install and
verification durations, and whether any native dependency was rebuilt. vq
parses them into the canonical deployment records and
`vq.fleet.rollout_result/1` reports them per lane together with each
action's journalled wall-clock duration. Both deployers now configure a
persistent ccache across immutable releases, scoped by toolchain
fingerprint, Python ABI, architecture, CMake options, and dependency recipe
hashes (with `CCACHE_BASEDIR`/`CCACHE_NOHASHDIR` so per-SHA build paths
still hit), so a Python-only release gets near-total compiler-cache reuse;
a missing ccache on a build host is reported with its exact remediation.

### Changed: read-only fleet discovery fans out in bounded parallel probes (2026-07-26)

`vq admin status --all --json` and `vq doctor --all` probe hosts through
the bounded v0.7.6 fan-out pool (max 8 workers, `VQ_FANOUT_SERIAL` opt-out)
instead of serially, `rollout-latest` collects its three discovery sweeps
concurrently, and accepted-report discovery validates candidates
newest-first and stops at the newest accepted report. Dry-run discovery
drops from minutes to seconds; deployment itself remains strictly serial,
and running calculations and host-scoped holds are preserved exactly as
before.
## [v0.15.62] - 2026-07-26 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Fixed: periodic semiempirical helper energies reject nonconverged results (2026-07-26)

`make_periodic_energy_function(...)` now refuses nonconverged SCC-DFTB,
GFN2-xTB, PM6, and OMx periodic helper results instead of converting a failed
native result's energy field into an optimizer/scanner scalar.
`PeriodicOMxModel.energy()` gets the same guard. This closes the zero-energy
sentinel leak exposed by the still-open graphene OM2/OM3 periodic SCF gap; it
does not claim periodic OMx physics convergence or production parity.

### Added: vibe-view cartoon representation for biomolecules (2026-07-26)

Structures that carry residue and chain metadata can now be drawn as a
per-chain ribbon splined through the alpha-carbon trace, selectable from the
Representation picker and used as the default when a file has a splineable
backbone. Molecules are unaffected and still open ball-and-stick. Chains are
splined separately so a ribbon never leaps between them, and a chain with
fewer than four alpha-carbons is skipped rather than drawn as a stub.

### Fixed: vibe-view bond inference was quadratic (2026-07-26)

Covalent-radius bond inference ran as an all-pairs Python loop, which is
tolerable for a molecule and not for a biomolecule: 13,772 atoms is 94.8
million iterations, measured at 158.7 s, and 150,925 atoms did not finish.
Because the Trame server binds its port only after the first render, that
cost was paid before the page was reachable at all, so opening a real
protein looked like a hang. Inference now bins atoms into a uniform cell
list at the largest possible cutoff and tests only neighbouring bins. The
pair criterion is unchanged and the output is identical, verified against a
verbatim transcription of the superseded loop over six geometries including
a pathologically dense one. The same 13,772-atom protein now takes 0.23 s
and the 150,925-atom system 2.91 s.

Startup also no longer infers bonds purely to discover whether a structure
is periodic, which needs only the lattice.

### Fixed: periodic PM6 neutral-pair lattice cancellation (2026-07-26)

The periodic PM6 diatomic core-repulsion branch now includes the baseline
valence-charge repulsion already present in the ordinary atomic branch. The
periodic electronic decomposition retains the opposite attractive monopole
term, so omitting this baseline left a spurious long-range `-1/R` lattice
sum. Closed-shell fcc Ar exposed the defect without an SCF ambiguity: its
minimal basis is completely occupied, giving `D = 2I` at every geometry.
The corrected 0.94 through 1.06 scale sweep approaches dissociation under
expansion, strong compression is repulsive, and the scale-1 energy agrees
within `5e-11 Ha` between 15 and 40 bohr lattice cutoffs. Bare PM6 has no
validated rare-gas dispersion model, so this closes the monopole defect but
does not claim a physical argon equation of state or external MOPAC parity.

### Fixed: scheduler config invalidation on coarse filesystems (2026-07-26)

The daemon now fingerprints scheduler configuration by content rather than
mtime and size. Same-length rewrites inside one coarse or overlay filesystem
clock tick can no longer keep a stale scheduler dispatcher and continue
rendering jobs with superseded wrappers. The exact race was exposed by the
queue-fix CI pipeline and is pinned with a deterministic same-size,
same-mtime regression.

### Fixed: vq records multi-user update outcomes in canonical daemon state (2026-07-26)

`vq admin update` now carries its already-authenticated admin credential into
outcome persistence and writes `LAST OK` through the daemon RPC on multi-user
hosts. A canonical write failure is part of the update verdict and leaves the
update marker failed; it can no longer fall back silently to the invoking
user's XDG file while reporting a successful deployment. Single-user hosts
retain the daemon-down direct-file fallback. This closes the site_e
v0.15.61 rollout failure where vibe-view installed and verified successfully
but every fleet status sweep still saw the old daemon-owned record.

### Fixed: dev runtime verification at a release-tag commit (2026-07-26)

site_i now accepts a `vibeqc-dev` runtime whose generated build metadata names
an exact release tag when that tag resolves to the report's expected dev SHA.
Component-gated reports can legitimately select the release commit as the
newest build-test-green dev pin; the old verifier treated its truthful tag as
a lane mismatch after a successful build and activation. Release lanes still
require their exact requested tag, untagged dev commits remain valid, and a
stale or unrelated tag still fails verification.

## [v0.15.61] - 2026-07-26 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Fixed: fleet rollout keeps each host drained across lane handoffs (2026-07-25)

`vq admin rollout-latest` now acquires one outer, canonical-host dispatch hold
before a host's first pending action and keeps it through helper and runtime
updates. Clearing an individual update marker can no longer dispatch queued
chemistry in the gap before the next lane acquires its marker. Scheduler hosts
use scoped driver-side scheduler-target drains; ordinary venv hosts use a full
update drain. Existing administrator drains are borrowed and preserved.
Rollout-owned holds are persisted in the resume journal, bounded by a six-hour
safety expiry, and released after the host's final action, a terminal failure,
or an interruption. Re-entry reacquires the hold from live state. Regression
coverage includes interleaved site_i/site_j actions, interruption/re-entry,
failure cleanup, and preservation of an external scheduler hold.

### Fixed: Linux libecpint caches work with immutable legacy releases (2026-07-25)

site_i and site_j native-cache staging now supplies the `lib/cmake/ecpint`
compatibility path expected by vibe-qc releases through v0.15.60 when a
validated Linux cache installs that metadata under `lib64/cmake/ecpint`.
The bridge is a relocatable link inside the copied cache; it neither edits the
immutable source nor weakens build-stamp or toolchain validation. This avoids
an otherwise unnecessary libcerf, pugixml, and libecpint rebuild after every
release while preserving a cold-build fallback for incomplete caches.

### Fixed: vq local reaping during scheduler submission bursts (2026-07-25)

The driver daemon now reconciles local `Popen` children between blocking
SSH plus scheduler-submission attempts. A large batch of cluster jobs can no
longer keep an already-finished local payload defunct and reported as running
until every serial `qsub` or `sbatch` call returns. The local kill path also
persists the requested `KILLED` transition when an already-dead or otherwise
unreapable process group returns `PermissionError`, while reporting that no
signal landed instead of aborting before the terminal record is written.

### Fixed: periodic PM6 polar-crystal charge-transfer cycle (2026-07-25)

The exact six-atom proton-ordered Ice-Ih article cell exposed a genuine
period-two SCF orbit on current main: after seven direct Aufbau updates the
density alternated between two charge-localized states to machine precision,
with `max|D_n-D_(n-1)| = 1.9983`, while neither state commuted with its
