physical Fock matrix. Gamma-periodic PM6 omitted the Pulay commutator solve
already used by molecular PM6. The periodic solver now applies bounded
eight-vector DIIS without damping or level shifting and accepts convergence
only when both the density change and unextrapolated `[F,D]` residual meet the
requested tolerance. All seven archived 0.94--1.06 Ice-Ih lattice scales now
converge in 22--34 iterations to a smooth negative-energy branch, and the
scale-1 energy changes by `5.4e-5 Ha` between 30 and 40 bohr cutoffs.
Periodic PM6 remains experimental pending independent MOPAC energy
validation.

### Fixed: padded multi-k BIPOLE UHF analytic gradient (2026-07-25)

Corrected-gauge integer-occupation UHF analytic gradients now reproduce the
production padded radial M5 short-range domain on Monkhorst-Pack meshes. The
guard covered a real code defect: the analytic path formed
`D_alpha + D_beta` through a helper that intentionally narrowed the total
density onto the ordinary Fock-output cells, silently dropping the wider BvK
density blocks required by padded `J_SR`. Exchange already retained its
per-spin wide support. The fixed path preserves the full total-density
support, applies the total Coulomb and per-spin exchange density transposes,
corrects the occupied Lagrangian, and solves the coupled alpha/beta
real-linear orbital response. Fixed-density padded J and both spin-K
derivatives match displaced-geometry finite differences to
`6.0e-10 Ha/bohr`; asymmetric BeH/STO-3G `[2,1,1]` converged analytic parity
improves from `1.4417e-3` to `6.83e-8 Ha/bohr`. Padded multi-k KS,
pair-resolved, and fractional routes remain fail-closed; finite differences
remain the production force path.

### Added: vibe-view carries PDB residue/chain identity (2026-07-25)

`Atom` gains optional `atom_name` / `residue_name` / `residue_seq` /
`chain_id`, populated by `pdb_to_qvf` and read back by
`QVFReader.read_structure`. `StructureData` gains `has_residues`,
`chains()` (residues per chain, in file order) and `backbone_trace()`
(alpha-carbon spine, optionally per chain) — the foundation the
cartoon/ribbon work needs. Residues group by contiguous run rather than
by residue number, because PDB numbers are four columns wide and wrap at
9999: on a solvated membrane protein, keying by number merged a lipid
and a water sharing number 1001. All fields are optional, so XYZ/CIF and
computed structures are unaffected.

### Fixed: padded multi-k BIPOLE RHF analytic gradient (2026-07-25)

Corrected-gauge integer-occupation RHF analytic gradients now reproduce the
production padded radial M5 short-range domain on Monkhorst-Pack meshes. The
energy maps a wide BvK density support into a narrower Fock-output domain, so
the old forward-only treatment missed the cellwise J/K density transpose,
the corresponding occupied Lagrangian correction, and the coupled orbital
response. The native adjoint is directionally finite-difference pinned on
non-homogeneous lattice blocks; the completed real-linear k-coupled solve
brings asymmetric BeH2/STO-3G `[2,1,1]` analytic-vs-production-FD parity to
`2.58e-5 Ha/bohr`. The UHF radial route is closed in the entry above;
padded multi-k KS, pair-resolved, and fractional routes remain fail-closed.
Finite differences remain the production force path.

### Fixed: vibe-view mis-typed every element in PDBs without an element column (2026-07-25)

Columns 77-78 carry the element, but many real files omit them (older
entries, MD engine output). The fallback stripped digits from the atom
name, which read the protein backbone alpha-carbon `" CA "` as calcium
and minted symbols out of hydrogen names. On a 150k-atom membrane
protein that meant 885 spurious calciums (the file contains none), some
36,000 hydrogens typed as `Hr`/`Hs`/`Hb`/`Ha`/`Hd`/`Hg` — `Hg` being
mercury — and 166 atoms dropped outright. Wrong colours, radii and
bonding in the viewer, and wrong chemistry in anything exported from it.

The fallback now uses the convention that gives that field its meaning:
the element is right-justified in columns 13-14, so a blank column 13
marks a one-letter element — which is exactly what separates `" CA "`
(alpha-carbon) from `"CA  "` (calcium). Four-character hydrogen names
are recognised by their position suffix, so `HE1` stays hydrogen while a
real `HE` is still helium. Unknown symbols are preserved with
`atomic_number 0` as before, never dropped.

### Added: vq release-aware fleet rollout orchestration (2026-07-25)

`vq admin rollout-latest` is now the release operator's single fleet action:
it discovers the newest accepted component-gated report from the managed
driver checkout, updates driver vq first and re-enters through it, then
reconciles scheduler helpers, immutable scheduler runtimes, and local managed
venvs serially. Operators supply no version, tag, branch, or SHA; the report
retains exact internal pins and provenance. Explicit managed/vq-only/alias/
excluded topology prevents coordinator and scheduler-alias mis-targeting,
temporary admin or external scheduler holds defer only their host, no-downgrade
and dirty/divergent ancestry gates fail closed, and live `LAST OK` state makes
re-entry and repeated runs idempotent. `--dry-run` and `--json` expose the
exact plan and final per-host/module identity. No unattended timer is enabled.

### Fixed: scheduler runtimes reuse native dependency installs (2026-07-25)

site_i and site_j immutable runtime stages no longer rebuild Libint, Libxc,
spglib, FFTW, and libecpint for every release when a compatible healthy
runtime already exists. The deployers copy only installed dependency trees,
validate the target checkout's native build stamp, and record a
host/toolchain fingerprint; old source trees and compiled build objects are
never reused. site_i seeds from an active immutable runtime, while site_j seeds
from a checksum-verified artifact that already passed relocation testing.
Recipe or toolchain drift fails closed to the normal cold dependency build.
The vibe-qc extension itself is still rebuilt and passes every existing
health, relocation, and provenance gate. site_i now builds that extension once
at the final non-active immutable path instead of compiling once in staging
and again after the move; failed candidates are quarantined before activation.

### Fixed: per-host authentication for delegated admin writes (2026-07-25)

Delegated admin writes can use a per-host `admin_token_file`, allowing
multi-user hosts with distinct protected tokens to participate in single-host
and `--all-hosts` updates without sending bearer bytes through the fleet
driver.

### Fixed (EXPERIMENTAL): bounded-memory CCM CCSD Lambda solve (2026-07-25)

The experimental Gamma-CCM CCSD and UCCSD analytic-gradient drivers now offer
an opt-in `lambda_solver="matrix-free"` path. The original solver materializes
the full doubles-dominated amplitude Jacobian, requiring O(n_so^8) memory;
the new LSMR path evaluates exact complex-step `J*x` and `J.T*x` products while
retaining only O(n_so^4) amplitude-sized state. It fails closed when the
least-squares residual misses the requested tolerance and matches the dense
small-system gradient oracle to machine precision. The dense solver remains
the default while larger-system iteration cost and convergence are calibrated.

### Removed: vibe-view share.py (2026-07-25)

The sharing module minted `https://vibe-qc.com/share/<token>` URLs that
no route ever served, generated iframe embeds for them, and persisted
"share sessions" to the user's cache — imported by nothing but its own
tests since it was written. Shipping it as designed would have meant
hosting users' unpublished research geometries on a public server: a
service with a real privacy surface, not a viewer feature. Removed with
its tests and the tutorial section that documented an API which never
worked (maintainer decision).

### Added (EXPERIMENTAL): per-unit-cell adapter for the real-Γ direct route (2026-07-25)

`vibeqc.periodic_ccm_real_gamma` — step 1 of wiring
`jk_method='real-gamma'` into `run_periodic_job` (the FR-1 follow-up):
`run_real_gamma_scf` runs the direct-torus drivers (RHF/UHF/RKS/UKS,
global + screened hybrids) and constructs the runner-contract
per-unit-cell result — energy/N_c, circulant-folded per-unit-cell
`LatticeMatrixSet` densities (per spin open-shell), supercell-Γ MOs, and
the `CCMRealGammaConvention` record (`exchange_q0`,
`exchange_q0_applicability`, D86 executed values — structural 0.0 for
mixing/damping/level shift — `lattice_vector_convention="columns"`,
screened-exchange assembly triple for HSE-class). The runner surface
still fails closed (`validate_jk_method` pin unchanged); the dispatch
wiring is the next increment. Gates:
`tests/test_periodic_ccm_real_gamma_adapter.py` (T3 experimental;
adapter-vs-API parity exact per method, open-shell fold identities,
boundary pins).

### Fixed: periodic PM6 graphene image counting and exchange tail (2026-07-25)

The Gamma-periodic PM6 graphene robustness sweep now converges at all seven
0.94 through 1.06 lattice scales in 21--22 iterations. The lattice Fock build
previously mirrored every directed nonzero-cell resonance/exchange block even
though the opposite lattice cell supplies its transpose, doubling all image
terms; the final core-core energy likewise omitted the one-half weight for
directed image pairs. Nonzero-cell exchange also used an unscreened
`gamma_AB ~ 1/R` kernel with the home-cell density, leaving a spurious
long-range exchange monopole after neutral electrostatic cancellation.
Directed Gamma blocks are now summed once, image core pairs carry their
one-half weight, and image exchange follows the transition-density asymptotic
`S_mu,nu(R)^2 gamma_AB(R)`. The graphene energy changes by less than
`5e-6 Ha` when the image cutoff doubles from 15 to 30 bohr, instead of
diverging with the number of cells. Periodic PM6 remains experimental; the
h-BN PM6 and graphene OMx robustness rows remain open, while the diamond-Si
image-shell defect is addressed in the newer entry above.

### Fixed: periodic GFN2 h-BN expansion SCC holes (2026-07-25)

The Gamma-periodic GFN2-xTB h-BN robustness sweep no longer fails at
lattice scales 1.02, 1.04, and 1.06. Periodic AES image pairs now evaluate
the Klopman-Ohno screening kernel at the translated pair distance instead of
reusing the home-cell separation, and the matching analytic-gradient kernel
uses the same image physics. The third-order shell-charge solve uses bounded
vector Aitken relaxation and now honors `XTBSccOptions.auto_stabilize` with
one neutral, low-step retry after the ordinary solve fails. A regression pins
the smooth energy branch across all three formerly failing cells and verifies
that disabling the retry still fails closed. Periodic GFN2-xTB remains gated
experimental; periodic PM6/OMx robustness rows remain open.

### Fixed: bulk-Si periodic GFN2 screening regression coverage (2026-07-25)

The article diamond-Si Gamma GFN2-xTB seven-point scale scan now has
regression coverage proving all points converge within the original
200-iteration budget without the neutral retry. This reclassifies the old
bulk-Si 0/7 periodic-screening diagnostic as resolved on current main while
periodic PM6/OMx robustness remains open.

### Added: open-shell CCM DLPNO per-spin PAO pair domains (2026-07-25)

`ccm_dlpno_ump2` and `ccm_dlpno_uccsd` now accept an opt-in `tcut_mkn`
threshold that selects pair atoms from occupied-orbital Mulliken populations
and builds separate semicanonical alpha/beta projected atomic orbital spaces.
Pair densities and PNOs are built in those bounded spaces, with per-pair and
average PAO-size diagnostics reporting the reduced work. The zero threshold
bypasses PAO construction and preserves the canonical virtual correctness path
exactly.
### Fixed: ordinary runs now declare they finished (`run_status`) (2026-07-25)

Only container runs (`vibeqc run job.qvf`) stamped
`provenance.run_status`; archives written by the ordinary API —
`run_job`, `run_periodic_job` (basis-driven and semiempirical routes),
and the double-hybrid driver — left it absent. That is spec-conforming
but misleading in practice: QVF § 3.2 defines an absent status as "not
stated" and forbids a consumer from inferring one, so the majority of
runs produced archives that never declared they were done, and vibe-view
showed them no lifecycle status even though `scf_converged` sat right
beside it in the same provenance block. Every settled vibe-qc run now
stamps `"converged"` / `"failed"` through one shared
`terminal_run_status(result)` helper that applies the same rule as the
container finalizer, so a calculation settles to the same status whether
it was driven by the API or by a job container. Archives that are not a
settled run (reaction paths, relaxed scans, `qvf_bytes`) stay silent by
design.

The periodic basis-driven route stamps from the `_qvf_archive_result`
snapshot the rest of its archive is built from, not from the
post-optimization `result` — geometry optimization rebinds `result` to an
object whose `converged` means "geometry converged", which would have let
one provenance block describe two different results (`run_status` sits
beside `scf_converged`). A structural guard pins each periodic QVF
dispatch to stamp from the object it archives; the semiempirical route,
which archives the post-optimization result, legitimately stamps from it.
Verified on a periodic run with `optimize=True`: consistent status, and
the embedded log is byte-identical to the `.out` including the
geometry-optimization epilogue.

The `failed` half of the lifecycle is now pinned end-to-end too, and
documenting it turned up a behaviour worth stating: a non-converged SCF
makes `run_job` *raise* rather than publish, so no result archive is
written and the terminal-dispatch stamp is never reached. `failed`
reaches an archive via the checkpointer's terminal frame (and, for
containers, the container finalizer), which is what stops a consumer
watching a live job from seeing a `running` snapshot frozen forever. The
new test drives a real divergent SCF through the real runner
(`rhf_options.max_iter = 1` — `run_job` has no top-level iteration cap)
and asserts both halves: no `{stem}.qvf`, and a terminal checkpoint
archive stamped `failed`.

## [v0.15.60] - 2026-07-25 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Added: vq — site_j helper lane ships the maintenance scripts (2026-07-25)

`vq admin update site_j` now closes the last host-copy drift gap on site_j:
the helper updater `update-scheduler-vq-admin.sh` is repo-tracked at
`vibe-queue/contrib/site_j/` and, after its SLURM venv rebuild succeeds,
syncs `contrib/site_j/*` from the verified staged archive into
`~/.local/libexec/vq-site_j/bin/` by atomic rename, routing itself back to
its live location in the vq-site_j root — the same pattern as site_i's
`update-scheduler-vq-from-stage`. Previously the updater existed only as a
host copy and installing the deploy/verify scripts was a manual scp. The
updater also gained a `VQ_SCHEDULER_EXPECTED_SOURCE_SHA` cross-check on the
stage. One manual bootstrap copy of the updater onto site_j remains (the
script cannot install itself for the first time); pinned by four new tests
in `vibe-queue/tests/test_site_j_maintenance_scripts.py` and documented in
the fleet update runbook § "site_j: vibe-view".

### Added: vq — site_j vibe-view managed runtime lane (2026-07-25)

`vq admin update vibe-view site_j --expected-sha <40-hex>` now works like
any managed runtime: `deploy-site_j-runtime` gained a `vibe-view` program
(pure-Python viewer wheel in a cp312 venv with the site Mesa module,
producer QVF schemas packaged over the wheel's symlink stubs, headless
capture-backend probe baked into the bundle) and `verify-site_j-runtime`
gained a viewer probe (API surface, both packaged schemas, wrapper-carried
build SHA). Previously the deploy script rejected everything but the two
vibeqc programs with exit 64, so site_j's vibe-view ran as hand-built
per-SHA wrappers pinned by config edits instead of `--expected-sha`. Both
scripts are now repo-tracked at `vibe-queue/contrib/site_j/` and pinned by
`vibe-queue/tests/test_site_j_maintenance_scripts.py`; the vibeqc lanes'
wrapper and launcher templates are byte-identical to the validated
2026-07-21 script. The first managed vibe-view deploy (next release sweep)
creates the stable `vibe-view-python` wrapper, after which the per-SHA
wrappers are retired — see the fleet update runbook § "site_j: vibe-view".

### Fixed: periodic semiempirical Gamma route boundary is pinned (2026-07-25)

The release-era ArtVal periodic route-boundary failure now has current-main
regression coverage across the basis-free Gamma method set. `run_periodic_job`
accepts `basis=None` for DFTB0, SCC-DFTB, GFN2-xTB, PM6, OM2 and OM3 before
the RHF/RKS/UHF/UKS basis gate, while the remaining EOS article work stays
classified as input-generation and rerun plumbing.

### Added: vibe-view downloads run.record attachments (2026-07-25)

Binary attachments were listed by name with no way to get at them.
The Run Record panel now shows a download chip per attachment
(filename + size); the bytes are served as `application/octet-stream`
so the browser saves rather than renders, producer-supplied filenames
are reduced to a bare basename so a crafted archive cannot propose a
path, and a 64 MB ceiling is checked from the ZIP directory before any
read. Attachment payloads still never enter the panel DOM — the chips
sit outside the (script-free) iframe, which is the only way they could
be interactive at all.

### Fixed: `python -m vibeqc` exists — fleet QVF container jobs can dispatch (2026-07-25)

vq's first-class QVF dispatch runs `$VENV/bin/python -m vibeqc run
job.qvf` on the managed runtime it resolves, but the `vibeqc` package
had no `__main__.py` — the CLI existed only as the `vibeqc` console
script — so every fleet container job died at startup with "No module
named vibeqc.__main__" (observed live on site_b, job `a58b29390017`).
New `python/vibeqc/__main__.py` routes `python -m vibeqc` through the
same `vibeqc._cli.main` entry point. The regression test runs the
exact queue invocation as a subprocess on a real pending container and
asserts the settled, validator-clean result.

### Added: DFTB0 method-native Mulliken population sidecars (2026-07-25)

Molecular DFTB0 and UDFTB0 results now expose net atomic Mulliken charges
formed from the final one-shot total density and overlap,
`q_A = n_val(A) - sum_{mu in A} (D S)_{mu mu}`. The unrestricted route uses
`D_alpha + D_beta`, and both routes conserve the requested molecular charge.
`run_job(method="dftb0")` therefore emits the native `.population.txt` and
`.population.json` sidecars by default. Analyses requiring the Gaussian-AO
property stack remain explicit `unsupported:` entries; DFTB0 Molden output is
still unavailable because its minimal Slater basis is not a Gaussian GTO
serialization contract.

### Fixed: stale semiempirical population-sidecar diagnostic is pinned (2026-07-25)

Explicit population sidecar requests for basis-free PM6, OM2, OM3 and
MSINDO have regression coverage proving they fail before output planning,
manifest creation or engine entry. Auto sidecar mode omits those unsupported
population files. DFTB0 and SCC-DFTB keep their validated native Mulliken
population sidecars.

### Fixed: vibe-view details panel no longer runs untrusted archive content; NDJSON survives a killed run (2026-07-25)

Two follow-ups on the container-lifecycle viewer work. The details-panel
iframe was mounted with `sandbox="allow-scripts"` unconditionally while
displaying content straight out of a QVF (run logs, embedded
attachments, citation text); scripts are now denied by default, reset on
every section activation, and opted into only by the orbital energy
diagram, whose click-to-render bridge needs them. And a structured event
log whose run was killed mid-write no longer renders as raw text: the
records that did parse are shown, with the count of skipped lines stated
beneath the table — vibe-qc's NDJSON log is specified so that a partial
write leaves earlier records readable, and that is exactly when they
matter most.

### Added: vibe-view closes the container-lifecycle viewer gaps (2026-07-25)

vibe-view now renders the hardened v0.15.59 container lifecycle in
full. The Run Record panel renders all three embedded sidecars: the
`.perf` timing log as text and the structured `.scf.jsonl` event log as
an NDJSON event table — any line that fails to parse sends the whole
attachment through the raw-text fallback, and both paths are size-gated
(4 MB read cap; 300-row render cap with head/tail elision). "Done" is
now judged as the spec means it: a terminal `run_status`
(`converged`/`failed`) **plus** a complete latest `run.record`; a
terminal archive whose record lacks its `input` or `log` member gets an
explicit warning banner in the panel and a WARNING line in the Run Info
card (`QVFReader.lifecycle_warnings`). A zero-byte embedded log is
accepted as a complete record — a run that failed before output began
logged exactly zero bytes — and labels as "ended before output began".
Sequenced `run.record` sections display as run history: each panel
carries "Run #k of N — latest" / "(superseded by run #N)"
(`QVFReader.run_record_sections` / `run_record_position`), and the Run
Info card counts the runs. Arbitrary binary attachments stay strictly
non-executable: only the allowlisted text roles render; everything else
is listed by name with an extraction note and its bytes never enter the
DOM. The executed-input member now shows its files-index description
("Executed declarative job specification").

Verification: 16 new viewer tests build **real** containers via
`vibeqc.run_container` — success (all three attachments), pre-output
failure (empty log, no warning), forced rerun (two sequenced records),
tampered terminal archives (warnings fire), atomic
pending → running → terminal reload transitions through the change
tracker, and binary-attachment safety. Full vibe-view suite: 959
passed, 0 failed with the `[viewer]` stack installed (the historic
controller-smoke "env failures" were missing-trame artifacts). Live
GPU/trame QA: new `docs/qa_job_container.py` drives a real browser
with trusted events through the whole lifecycle — pending chip +
"not yet run" banner, real `vibeqc run`, chip settles converged via
auto-reload, run record renders system manifest / performance log /
structured events — 10/10 checks pass.

### Added: vq treats complete-calculation QVF as a first-class job (2026-07-25)

`vq submit HOST job.qvf --program NAME` now resolves the managed vibe-qc
runtime, snapshots its full git SHA automatically, and runs
`vibeqc run job.qvf`; a QVF can no longer fall through to
`python job.qvf`. `--expected-sha` remains an optional assertion for historical
reproduction. Scheduler targets use their configured program wrapper, and
stale/mismatched runtimes still fail before dispatch.
`vq fetch --name job.qvf` atomically retrieves only the updated container,
leaving queue logs, metadata, and redundant sidecars server-side. Status JSON
adds `qvf_lifecycle`, including run status, sequence, terminal completeness,
and distinct chemistry-failure versus queue-process-failure fields; a terminal
container without a complete sequenced run record is not reported done.
Regression coverage includes remote forwarding, scheduler wrapper resolution,
artifact-only fetch, a daemon round trip, forced-rerun sequences, and a
complete failed-run container.

### Fixed: QVF job containers settle atomically and completely (2026-07-25)

The in-place container path now enters `running` before execution and
always settles with a complete, sequenced `run.record`, including when
the runner raises. The executed `job.spec` section and member bytes are
preserved exactly; large archive members and logs are streamed during
the final atomic rewrite instead of loading the archive into memory.
The final record embeds available `.system`, `.perf`, and structured
event sidecars, and dotted output stems resolve to the same artefact
paths as `OutputPlan`. Ordinary molecular and periodic QVF writes are
atomic too. Periodic QVF assembly now occurs after the last
geometry-optimization log byte, removing the old truncated-log ordering
problem, and basis-free periodic semiempirical jobs now produce QVF
archives instead of silently skipping them. Regression coverage includes
success, runner exceptions, missing result archives, forced sequences,
dotted stems, all three attachment roles, and real molecular,
Gaussian-basis periodic, and basis-free periodic container runs.

## [v0.15.59] - 2026-07-25 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Verified: QVF containers round-trip through vq with no protocol extension (2026-07-25)

A QVF job container needs no queue-protocol extension: the container is
the whole payload (`vq submit HOST -d jobdir/ -- vibeqc run job.qvf`)
and the updated container is the whole result (`vq fetch`). Verified
live through a vq daemon: a pending H₂/STO-3G `job.qvf` went in, the
daemon executed it, and the fetched container came back
validator-clean and `converged` with the spec preserved, the embedded
log byte-equal to the streamed `.out`, the system manifest inside, and
all result sections present. Recipe documented in
`docs/design_qvf_format.md`. Fleet hosts pick this up as soon as their
`vibeqc-dev` env includes this release line (managed-env submits use
`"$VQ_PROGRAM_BIN/vibeqc" run job.qvf`).

### Added: vibe-view understands job containers (2026-07-25)

vibe-view now renders the QVF container lifecycle. The app-bar status
chip covers the full spec § 3.2 value set — a `pending` container shows
an amber "pending" chip (clock icon) next to the title, alongside the
existing running/converged/failed states — and the Run Info card leads
with a `Status` line (`pending — job not yet run`). The new `job.spec`
section kind gets a full registration (supported kinds, titles, icons,
dispatch, 2-D panel list) and a renderer showing the declarative
request — job type, method/functional/basis, charge, multiplicity,
k-mesh, tasks, options — with a banner distinguishing "not yet run"
from "the request this settled archive was run from". The Run Record
panel now renders the embedded `.system` manifest (`attachment.system`)
as text instead of listing it as an unrendered attachment, so a settled
container shows structure, results, log, references, system manifest,
and status with no sidecar file. Reader API: `QVFReader.read_job_spec`
+ `read_run_record_attachment` (size-capped, UTF-8-gated).

### Added: QVF containers embed the `.system` manifest (2026-07-25)

The container update now also folds the run's `.system` manifest into
the archive as the `run.record`'s `attachment.system` member (declared
in the `files` index with its original basename and
`application/toml` media type). With the log already embedded and
references carried by the `citations` section, a settled container
needs no sidecar file to understand the run: structure, results, log,
references, system manifest, and status travel in the one archive.
Sidecar files still land at the output stem — the container makes them
redundant, it does not suppress them; the existing per-artifact runner
switches (`write_xyz_file=False`, …) remain the opt-out surface, usable
as job.spec `options`. See `docs/design_qvf_format.md` § run.record /
job.spec.

### Added: QVF containers update in place — pending in, done out (2026-07-25)

`vibeqc run job.qvf` (and `vibeqc.run_container`) now completes the
container round trip: after the runner finishes, the *same* archive is
updated atomically (write-new + `os.replace`, the checkpointer pattern) —
result sections and the `run.record` are folded in, the original
`job.spec` section is preserved verbatim (spec § 5.9), and
`provenance.run_status` moves to `"converged"` / `"failed"`. The update
is the genuinely last act of the run, so the embedded log is re-read
from disk at that point: epilogues the runner appends after its own
archive write (the periodic `optimize=True` geometry summary) are now
inside the container, and the `files.log.truncated` flag is dropped.
If the runner raises, the container is stamped `failed` (its job.spec
intact, so it can be re-run); a `--force` re-run of a settled container
carries the earlier `run.record` sections over, ordered by `sequence`.
The final archive is schema-validated before it replaces the container;
a validation failure leaves the container untouched. Periodic containers
now resolve their basis name to a real `BasisSet` for
`run_periodic_job`. End-to-end tests: molecular H₂/STO-3G and periodic
He-in-a-box pending containers each run a real SCF and come back as
single validator-clean archives whose embedded log equals the streamed
`.out` byte-for-byte.

### Added: `vibeqc run job.qvf` — execute a pending QVF job container (2026-07-25)

`vibeqc run` now accepts a `.qvf` argument and executes the job the
container describes: the declarative `job.spec` payload is parsed
(sha256-verified), the `structure` section is reconstructed into a
`Molecule`/`PeriodicSystem` (Å→bohr, row→column lattice, prefix-`pbc`
masks only), and the job runs through the ordinary
`run_job`/`run_periodic_job` surface. Non-`pending` archives are refused
without `--force`; unknown tasks and unknown/reserved spec options are
refused rather than silently dropped (QVF spec § 5.9); no embedded
script is ever executed on this path. New public API in
`vibeqc.qvf_job`: `write_pending_qvf` (build a pending container from a
structure + spec), `load_job_container`, `run_container` — all exported
from `vibeqc`. Tests: `tests/test_qvf_job_container.py` (round trips,
refusals, kwarg mapping, CLI dispatch, and a real H₂/STO-3G end-to-end
run from a pending container). The in-place archive update (results +
run.record written back into the same container) is the next milestone;
for now results land at the output stem as usual.

### Added: QVF `job.spec` canonical kind + `pending` run status (2026-07-25)

A QVF archive can now *describe* a calculation before it has run. The new
canonical section kind `job.spec` (spec § 5.9, governance ruling 2026-07-25
in `qvf-writer/GOVERNANCE.md`) carries a declarative JobSpecPayload —
`job_type` (`molecular` | `periodic`, required) plus optional `method`,
`basis`, `functional`, `charge`, `multiplicity`, `kpoints`, `tasks`, and an
open `options` object — as a schema-validated JSON member. In the same
ruling, `provenance.run_status` is formalized in spec § 3.2 as
`pending | running | converged | failed`, adding `pending` for a container
(structure + job.spec) that has not yet run. The payload is data, never
code, and the spec explicitly forbids executing `run.record.input` as a
side effect of opening or running an archive. Additive under v1 — no
`qvf_version` bump. Touched surfaces follow the run.record recipe:
canonical schema (+ byte-copies + derived v2), `registry.json`, reference
Python writer (`add_job_spec`) / validator (JobSpecPayload check), C++
writer + C ABI + regenerated `qvf_single.hpp`, conformance corpus case
`job_spec.qvf` (additive), producer `_write_job_spec_section` via the
`job_spec` context key of `write_qvf` (which now also accepts
`run_status="pending"`), and docs. Groundwork for `vibeqc run job.qvf` —
the runners do not consume `job.spec` yet.
### Changed: CCM multi-k GDF reuses symmetry-equivalent pair fits (2026-07-25)

`run_ccm_rhf_gdf` and hybrid `run_ccm_rks_gdf` now reduce the production
RSGDF Lpq cache over exact cluster space-group and time-reversal stars while
retaining the full k-mesh for SCF. Non-representative factors are reconstructed
in the canonical auxiliary frame with the full AO, auxiliary, and Bloch-phase
action. On the `(3,1,1)` H2 chain gate this lowers native fit builds from 9 to
8 and changes the converged RHF energy by `8.9e-16 Ha`; low-symmetry and
non-RSGDF routes keep the existing full-build path. `CCMGDFResult` reports the
requested pair count, actual build count, and reduction factor.

### Fixed: BIPOLE pair-domain integer UKS no longer hits a stale safety gate (2026-07-25)

Integer-occupation Gamma UKS analytic gradients now accept the pair-resolved
padded erfc domain. The shared open-shell J/K adjoint already differentiates
the output and density shell-pair projectors, while the spin-polarised XC
gradient remains on the physical unmasked Bloch densities; only the
pre-adjoint fail-close guard was stale. Off-boundary triplet-H2/STO-3G LDA
and PBE0 analytic forces agree with converged production-energy finite
differences to `1.11e-7 Ha/bohr`. Fractional padded UKS and padded multi-k
remain fail-closed, and finite differences remain the production force path.

### Added: site_i runtime updates feed the mirror and prepare automatically (2026-07-25)

`vq admin update PROGRAM site_i --tag ... --expected-sha ...` now performs
the two formerly manual per-release steps itself when the deployment
profile opts in: `feed_source_mirror` pushes the exact pin
(`+SHA:refs/heads/main`, `+SHA:refs/remotes/origin/main`, all tags)
from the driver's `scheduler_runtime_source_repo` into the login host's
push-fed mirror, and `prepare_command` runs the login-host preparer with
the identity arguments under marker heartbeats, output teed into the
transcript. Both run after quiescence and before the build; any failure
(stale clone, push rejection, preparation error) fails closed with the
current runtime untouched. This closes fleet-automation gap 2: a release
rollout needs no per-release human commands on site_i. Guards:
`vibe-queue/tests/test_site_i_runtime_prepare_automation.py`.

### Fixed: scheduler runtime pins survive the daemon dispatch gate (2026-07-25)

Scheduler-target submissions carrying BUG 101's target-owned immutable runtime
pin no longer fail immediately before `qsub` because the driver daemon compared
that SHA with its unrelated local `[programs.NAME]` checkout. The daemon now
accepts a target-owned pin only when its recorded scheduler host matches the
job target; a cross-target pin fails closed. Local-daemon and legacy runtime
pin checks are unchanged. This is a pre-chemistry routing fix: no SCF or
electronic-structure result was involved.

### Changed: vibe-view QA harness covers the element picker and symmetrize (2026-07-24)

docs/interact_controls.py (trusted-event Playwright QA) grows two checks:
the periodic-table element picker (toolbar pencil → "New: C" → click
nitrogen → state changes, dialog closes) and symmetrize driven through the
command palette (Ctrl/Cmd+K → detect point group → Symmetrize button →
"Symmetrized C2v → C2v" on the showcase's already-symmetric water, max
shift 0.000 Å). 10/10 in a real Chromium. Keyboard shortcuts are avoided
mid-run — focus left on a form control by an earlier check swallows them —
and the toon check forces a fresh WebGL frame before each capture.

### Added: χ-CCM-B screened-exchange assembly attestation (2026-07-25)

The B exact-exchange descriptor now has the first formal nested schema,
`vibeqc.aiccm2026dev-b.exact-exchange-assembly/v1`, and records separate
screened-branch applicability plus the finite-N assembly convention. An
active four-center HSE RKS/UKS record is accepted only when the direct
`K_erfc` branch emits matching coefficient and physical-omega execution
evidence after its matrix fold and energy contraction; missing, stray, or
contradictory evidence fails before B diagnostics attach. The shared
corrected-gauge route may retain Ewald/exxdiv selector labels at `c_full=0`;
those labels do not override coefficient-derived D83 applicability or the
branch-emitted direct screened assembly. Current B HSE is therefore labelled
`short-range-direct`, never inferred from the functional name. RI and
RIJCOSX range-separated routes remain fail-closed, and HSE remains outside the
quantitative fleet.

Fleet JSON now requires the exact seven-key v1 object for successful and
non-converged rows. The independent route oracle requires every current route
to be screened `inactive` / `not-applicable`; legacy unversioned four-field
records and route-conflicting assembly labels fail before audit or comparison
rendering. Normal B `.system`, QVF vendor metadata v2, and band metadata
preserve the complete descriptor; `.out` reports its schema, screened
applicability, and assembly. This is provenance and executed-branch guarding,
not a Hamiltonian change, HSE validation, screened-exchange derivative, or
Γ-CCM/χ-CCM construction claim.

### Added: vibe-view symmetrize-to-group (2026-07-24)

The Symmetry card gains "Symmetrize to <group>" (also in the command
palette): it finds the symmetry operations the geometry supports around
the detected principal axis, closes them into a group, and iteratively
projects the coordinates onto the symmetry-invariant subspace. The result
is verified to be exactly invariant before it is applied — the action
refuses (with the reason) rather than delivering a half-symmetric
geometry — and it is undoable. The closed group can exceed the detected
label: a jittered benzene detected as D2h symmetrizes to the full D6h
(24 operations). Deliberately does not trigger live-optimize, which knows
nothing of symmetry and would re-break it.

### Fixed: build-as-job self-SIGSTOP wedge and impossible refresh-build sizing (2026-07-25)

A `vq submit --refresh` build job runs `vq build-env`, whose
`update_env` pause bracket swept up the build job's OWN spec:
`killpg(SIGSTOP)` froze the process before the SUSPENDED write, the
marker acquire, or any event, leaving the job "running"-but-stopped
forever (site_a `e4c32b654b03`, site_c `ca78bea5db13`, localhost
`8cd5ad2cd096`, each ~9 h past wall on 2026-07-25; latent since
v0.12.0 build-as-job). `pause_job` now refuses to SIGSTOP its own
process group, and `update_env` excludes the executing job (via
`VQ_JOB_ID`) from `pause_all` / `pause_provides_branches`. The
daemon also terminal-fails an auto-generated build job whose CPU or
memory request exceeds its configured caps, with a named reason —
site_b carried a 16-CPU refresh build against an 8-CPU daemon, pending
forever while reading as "queued". Deliberately scoped: operator
specs over the caps still stay pending (raising `--max-cpus` on
restart remains a supported path). Guards:
`vibe-queue/tests/test_build_job_self_pause.py`.

### Fixed: BIPOLE pair-domain UHF differentiates both density masks (2026-07-25)

The pair-resolved padded Gamma UHF analytic gradient now includes the
transpose action of both finite-domain projectors: the output shell-pair mask
and the independently wider density-support mask. The native J/K energy
derivative accepts both masks plus the unmasked physical Gamma density, and
the spin-resolved short-range exchange gradient now applies the same private
density mask as the SCF builder. On an off-boundary saturated-spin
H2/STO-3G discriminator, the analytic-vs-production-FD residual falls from
`2.31e-3` to `9.85e-8 Ha/bohr`; the saturated-spin pair-domain refusal is
removed. Pair-resolved UKS was retained behind a separate method-level
certification gate, resolved in the entry above; finite differences remain
the production force path.

### Changed: vibe-view comparison overlay honours the spectra Display selector (2026-07-24)

The multi-file spectrum overlay now follows the same Envelope + sticks /
Envelope only / Sticks only selector as the single-spectrum view, with
per-file colours on the sticks (sticks-only gets one legend entry per
file). The default stays the historical envelopes-only overlay — several
files' sticks read as a picket fence unless explicitly requested.

### Improved: multi-k RSGDF shares the exact q-dependent fit state (2026-07-25)

The multi-k RSGDF setup rebuilt the auxiliary Coulomb metric, its
eigendecomposition, and the Schwarz AO-pair mask for every ordered
`(k_i,k_j)` pair even though those objects depend only on
`q = k_j - k_i`. Full regular meshes now cache that state once per unique q,
reducing those exact setup operations from `n_k^2` to `n_k`. The
three-centre tensor is still evaluated separately for every pair because its
inter-cell AO product carries the ket momentum phase; no historically wrong
q-only cderi approximation is reintroduced. A skew-cell regression compares a
cached second-ket factor against a fresh build at `2e-12`.

### Fixed: scheduler-target `--expected-sha` pins the target's runtime, not the driver's (BUG 101, 2026-07-25)

`vq submit site_j INPUT --program vibeqc-release --expected-sha 820e718…`
failed with "expected git SHA 820e718…, got 63a80907a473" although site_j's
registered runtime WAS at `820e718…`: the submit rewrote its host to the
scheduler driver and then validated the pin against the driver-local
program of the same name (wave038 dispatch blocker). The pin now resolves
against the scheduler target's REGISTERED program (the immutable wrapper
a submitted job actually executes, identity parsed from its filename;
one read-only remote call), falling back to the verified deployment
record — the exact SHA,
tag, and immutable wrapper path that post-deploy verification receipted —
before the host rewrite, with subqueue aliases (`site_j-campaign`) sharing
their cluster's identity via the ssh endpoint. The resolved identity is
stored on the spec's `program_runtime_pin` (scheduler host, executable,
kind, version, full SHA, immutable artifact identity), reported in the
submission `--json` receipt, and named in mismatch errors. Fails closed
when no verified record exists; failures are atomic (no spec, no receipt);
a driver-local binary program of the same name no longer blocks pinned
scheduler submits; array submits validate before the first spec is
written. Guards: `vibe-queue/tests/test_bug101_scheduler_target_pin.py`.

### Added: vibe-view command palette reaches sections and exports (2026-07-24)

Ctrl/Cmd+K now lists one "Open section" entry per section of the loaded
file (rebuilt when another file is opened), so any panel is reachable by
typing its name, plus all eight geometry/scene export formats and the
vibe-qc input script — the same handlers the toolbar menus use.

### Fixed: BIPOLE RKS stops reapplying DIIS at a stationary physical Fock (2026-07-24)

The legacy-gauge Gamma RKS LiH analytic-gradient regression reached a
machine-zero physical commutator, but its lagging energy difference had not
yet passed on the same iteration. The driver therefore reapplied extrapolated
DIIS, Fock mixing, and level shift, kicked the density away from an Aufbau
fixed point, and cycled beyond the maintained 100-step cap. RKS now
diagonalizes the physical `F(D)` as soon as its commutator is stationary and
uses the following physical iteration to confirm the energy. The LiH
reference reaches the same lower stationary root in 94 iterations under an
explicit 100-step regression cap, and its analytic force still matches the
central finite difference.
Fractional occupations retain their separate density fixed-point check.

### Fixed: unrestricted χ-CCM level shifting fails closed (2026-07-24)

The experimental `aiccm2026dev-b` UHF and UKS routes now reject nonzero static
or scheduled level shifting before backend dispatch. The four-center loop
currently applies the restricted-density half coefficient to each
unit-occupation spin density, while fitted RI and RIJCOSX do not execute the
request. Accepting either behavior could silently misstate the SCF path and
select a different stationary basin.

The public periodic runner now forwards its resolved level-shift request into
the B options object before this gate. Zero and all-zero schedules remain
accepted, restricted RHF/RKS driver semantics are unchanged and now execute
through the public surface as declared, and the existing 1D/2D Hamiltonian
fail-close still takes priority.

### Fixed: self-update restart verification scales with the state dir (2026-07-25)

`vq admin update` on a vq self-update verifies the restarted daemon by
polling its RPC for the expected source SHA. That readiness window was a
flat 30 s, but a restarted daemon scans every `queue/*.json` before its
RPC socket answers, so on a driver carrying a large state dir the probe
timed out against a daemon that was coming up healthy. 2026-07-25 on
site_d (~12.6k job specs): two consecutive self-updates reported
"vq self-update detected — daemon restart FAILED ... daemon RPC did not
respond" while `rpc.ping()` returned the correct `source_sha` 10-30 s
later, and each false failure needed a manual `vq admin mark-ok`. The
window now scales as 30 s base + 10 ms per queued spec (capped at
600 s; ~156 s for that state dir), honors a `VQ_DAEMON_HEALTH_TIMEOUT`
env override read at call time like the other admin timeout knobs, and
the no-response failure message names the window it actually waited and
the override knob. Guards:
`vibe-queue/tests/test_admin_launchd_self_update.py`
(`test_daemon_health_window_scales_with_queued_specs`,
`test_daemon_health_window_env_override_and_cap`,
`test_restart_verification_survives_slow_state_scan`,
`test_no_response_failure_names_window_and_override_knob`).

## [v0.15.58] - 2026-07-24 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Added: vq doctor attributes scheduler dispatch stops (2026-07-25)

When a cluster stops starting queued jobs, `vq doctor HOST`'s
`scheduler_liveness` check now establishes WHO is holding dispatch instead
of only naming the stopped queues. It inspects the effective vq drain state
and any applicable (scoped, non-stale) admin-update marker for that
scheduler target and reports one of: a scheduler-side administrative stop
(`authority: scheduler_admin` — PBS queues `enabled` but not `started`, or
SLURM partitions not `up` via a new read-only `sinfo` probe), a vq hold, or
both at once (each named, neither claimed as sole cause). The verdict says
explicitly that running jobs continue, that queued jobs wait, and that
`qstart` / partition re-enablement belongs to the scheduler administrator —
`vq drain --release` cannot lift a scheduler-side stop. Doctor `--json`
carries the classification as a stable `scheduler_dispatch` object on the
check. When doctor runs away from the driver, the vq-side fields stay null
and the attribution is explicitly partial rather than guessed; when SLURM
partition state is unreadable, no attribution is claimed. Diagnostics only —
no dispatch behavior changes, and nothing ever mutates scheduler state.
Motivated by site_i 2026-07-25: all PBS queues sat `started = False` and
correlating "is this vq?" took three commands by hand. Guards:
`vibe-queue/tests/test_scheduler_dispatch_attribution.py`.

### Added: vibe-view periodic-table element picker (2026-07-24)

The Atom Editor's two element dropdowns (a dozen elements each) are
replaced by one periodic-table dialog covering H through Cm — all 96
elements the renderer's CPK palette knows. Cells are CPK-tinted with
contrast-aware labels, laid out in the standard 18-column form with
detached lanthanide/actinide rows. "New: <El>" picks the element used for
added atoms; "Change to…" (enabled with a selection) changes every
selected atom, undoable as before. Verified with trusted clicks in a real
browser.

### Changed: release flow reconciles release ancestry before tagging (2026-07-24)

The v0.15.57 cut left `release` HEAD one commit past the tag (the post-tag
`chore: absorb release ancestry` merge), which aborted the fleet's
`vq admin update vibeqc-release <host> --tag vX.Y.Z` verification
(`git describe --exact-match --tags HEAD`) on every venv host during the
2026-07-24 rollout. The documented flow now runs the tree-neutral
`merge -s ours origin/release` reconcile *before* the tag, in the minor cut
on `main` (step 1) and in the hotfix cut on the hotfix branch (step 6), so
the tag always lands on the final release-branch commit and `release` HEAD is
exactly the tag. `docs/release_process.md` carries the reordered steps and
the recovery path; `vibe-queue/docs/fleet_update_runbook.md` documents the
`--expected-sha <release-HEAD>` workaround for the already-cut
post-tag-absorb releases (v0.15.57 and earlier absorb-era tags). No history
or tags were rewritten.

### Added: vibe-view spectra stick-vs-envelope display selector (2026-07-24)

The spectra panel gains a Display selector — "Envelope + sticks" (the
historical rendering), "Envelope only", and "Sticks only" — completing the
last pending item in the design-refresh spectra controls. Sticks-only
promotes the stick spectrum to the primary trace: full width and hoverable
values, since there is no envelope to carry the hover. Applies to IR,
Raman, UV-Vis, ECD, VCD, and generic spectra; unknown values fall back to
the combined view.

### Fixed: MSINDO recovers the archived tetrazine DIIS cycle (2026-07-24)

The exact archived Thiel tetrazine frame cycles under the ordinary MSINDO
commutator-DIIS solve through 2000 iterations (and only happens to escape after
4516), so raising the public iteration cap was not a reliable fix. After DIIS
fails, MSINDO now uses its extended-Huckel/WICHT iteration only to cross that
basin, then restarts strict commutator DIIS from the recovered density. The
intermediate WICHT result is never accepted on its energy-only criterion: its
residual is about `2.2e-5`, whereas the final zero-temperature stationary
solution has energy `-50.737177619704 Ha`, residual `1.3e-10`, and the correct
30-electron density. Native and Python implementations follow the same
recovery route, the high-level job route retains a Python safety fallback, and
exact-geometry regressions pin the cold failure and strict result.

### Changed: vibe-view ambient-occlusion toggle moved to the Export menu (2026-07-24)

A renderer pass only shapes server-side renders (screenshots, video
frames), never the live viewport, so among the Display panel's viewport
toggles the switch read as broken. It now lives in the toolbar Export
menu as "Ambient occlusion: on/off (screenshots & video)". Three
consistency fixes ride along: scene rebuilds no longer silently re-enable
a switched-off SSAO; toggling re-renders immediately so the next
screenshot reflects the change instead of the previous frame; and the
occlusion radius returns to its long-standing 2.0 — the earlier "tuned"
0.5 was based on a measurement that does not reproduce (the visible
magnitude depends on camera distance, and the pixel-diff ranking of the
two radii inverts between sessions).

### Changed: archived SCC-DFTB imidazole occupation cycle is pinned (2026-07-24)

The v0.15.48 Thiel imidazole row remains noncontractive under a 500-iteration
zero-temperature SCC diagnostic. The current public molecular route converges
its existing bounded `0.001 Ha` Mermin retry to a stationary solution about
`0.065 Ha` lower, preserving the Hamiltonian, charge threshold, and neutral
total charge. An exact archived-geometry regression now pins the
zero-temperature failure, selected retry rung, converged energy, and
neutrality.

### Added: QVF canonical kind `run.record` — self-contained archives (2026-07-24)

A QVF archive can now carry the calculation itself, not just its results:
the new canonical section kind `run.record` (spec § 5.8) stores the
verbatim program input, the full log/output, and auxiliary attachments of
one program invocation. The kind is producer-neutral — a required
`program` field names the code the input/log belong to (`"vibe-qc"`,
`"orca"`, …), independent of the root `source.program`, so converters can
repack another code's finished run faithfully. Multiple run records with a
`sequence` index cover multi-step workflows. Added under v1 as the
additive case per the governance versioning policy (no `qvf_version`
bump); recorded as a maintainer decision in `qvf-writer/GOVERNANCE.md` and
`registry.json`. Ships with schema branch, reference Python + C++/C-ABI
writer support (`add_run_record`), validator semantics (UTF-8 checks on
`input`/`log`, files-index resolution), a conformance-corpus archive with
a new language-agnostic `decode: "utf8"` check form, and vibe-qc producer
+ vibe-view consumer support.

### Fixed: right-click targeting survives a pause; QA harness covers the new interactivity (2026-07-24)

The right-click menu discarded its hover-pick target when the pick was
older than 3 seconds — but while the pointer rests on the canvas nothing
changes, and users pause to read the tooltip before right-clicking (the
QA harness measured a valid target thrown away at 3.95 s on a busy
scene). The window is now 30 s, guarding only against truly ancient
state. The trusted-event QA harness (docs/interact_controls.py) gained
three checks — hover tooltip, right-click targeting, toon switch — and
passes 8/8 in a real Chromium.

### Fixed: site_i deploys gate on a login-host import; maintenance scripts repo-tracked (2026-07-24)

`deploy-site_i-runtime`'s health checks ran only on the build node, and every
site_i build/compute node is x86-64-v2-capable while the login node is not — so
the v0.15.57 deploy activated a runtime the login node could not import, and
the independent login-host verify failed only after the atomic switch. Every
health check now includes a login-host import gate (SSH from the build node
to `VQC_site_i_LOGIN_HOST`, default `site_i`; the runtime tree is shared NFS), so
a CPU-baseline-broken runtime is refused before activation, per the
scheduler-runtime deployment contract.

The five site_i maintenance scripts that lived only on the host
(`deploy-site_i-runtime`, `verify-site_i-runtime`, `finalize-site_i-runtime`,
`finalize-vibeqc-release-site_i`, `update-scheduler-vq-from-stage`) are now
tracked at `vibe-queue/contrib/site_i/` next to `prepare-site_i-runtime-source`,
and the helper lane installs them into the host bin directory on every
`vq admin update site_i` — a hand-edit on the host now lasts exactly one helper
update, which is the discipline that would have prevented the 2026-07-20 →
2026-07-24 numpy hand-patch/wipe/re-break cycle. The stage updater is pinned
to its parent `contrib/update-scheduler-vq.sh` by an ordered-subsequence
drift guard (`vibe-queue/tests/test_site_i_maintenance_scripts.py`), with two
documented site_i deltas: offline `pip install --no-build-isolation`, and the
maintenance-script sync itself.

The helper lane's driver entry point `vq-update-scheduler-buildhost` — the
`[hosts.site_i] scheduler_update_command` wrapper that builds an immutable
per-SHA helper root and atomically flips the stable symlink before
delegating to `update-scheduler-vq-from-stage` — is now repo-tracked at
`vibe-queue/contrib/site_i/` as well; it previously lived only in the login
host's `~/bin`. The maintenance-script sync routes it back there
(`VQC_site_i_ENTRY_BIN`, default `~/bin`, where the driver config points)
while every other script keeps installing into `VQC_site_i_BIN`.

### Fixed: vibe-view Toon switch works (2026-07-24)

The "Toon / NPR shading" switch never did anything: it sends its new value
as an argument, but the controller accepted none — every flip raised
TypeError server-side before doing any work. And had it run, it would have
flipped the state its own v_model had just written, cancelling the toggle.
Fixed with the set-don't-flip pattern; verified with a trusted click in a
real browser — the viewport now visibly switches to flat cel-shading with
outline edges, and switching it off restores each actor's original shading
(previously a blanket Phong reset that changed bonds and axes).

## [v0.15.57] - 2026-07-24 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Fixed: PM6 recovers symmetric fragment occupation cycles (2026-07-24)

The archived S22 formamide-dimer PM6 row remains nonconverged under the
ordinary hard-occupation SCF even at 2000 iterations. Different converged
seeds select stationary roots separated by more than `0.06 Ha`, confirming an
occupation/root problem rather than a short iteration budget. The high-level
closed-shell PM6 route now retains its zero-temperature fast path, then uses a
bounded `0.005 Ha` Mermin occupation homotopy only after failure and cools the
result back to the ordinary idempotent PM6 density. The finite-temperature
energy is never accepted as the result.

The exact archived geometry now converges to the lowest continuation root at

less than one nanohartree and the final density contains exactly 36 electrons.

### Fixed: recursive QVF listing is time-bounded (2026-07-24)

Clicking "All QVFs below here" from a huge browse root — the desktop app
launched from the dock serves the Electron process's working directory,
which is the home folder or even / — walked the entire tree and opened

"the button does not do anything". The walk and the manifest-reading pass
now each carry an 8-second budget; past it the page still lists every

### Fixed: vibe-view build tools no longer crash the scene on overlapping atoms (2026-07-23)

Driving the build-tool controllers for the first time surfaced a crash
family rooted in coincident atoms. "Add Hydrogens" on a partially
saturated atom placed two hydrogens on the same tetrahedral vertex (each
candidate direction was only checked against pre-existing atoms, never
against hydrogens placed earlier in the same call). Inserting any fragment
onto a selected atom was a guaranteed crash: every fragment's base atom
sits at the relative origin, so it landed exactly on the anchor. Both fed
a zero-length bond into the bond renderer, whose zero-direction cylinder
raised "matrix must have finite values" and killed the whole scene rebuild.

Hydrogen placement now consumes directions (fewer hydrogens beat
coincident ones when geometry blocks every vertex), fragments attach a
bond length outward from the anchor (or beside the structure when nothing
is selected), and the bond renderer skips coincident pairs outright so no
future overlap can take the viewport down.

## [v0.15.56] - 2026-07-23 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Fixed: vibe-view right-click menu actions now work; atom tooltips live (2026-07-23)

The viewport context menu was untargeted: the DOM right-click event only
carries screen coordinates, which the server cannot unproject (the client
owns the camera), so "Select Atom" was gated on an index that was hardcoded
to −1 and "Add Atom Here" was a stub that told the user to go click
elsewhere. The hover tooltip was equally dead — its text was never written —
yet its listener flushed a websocket state update on every mousemove over
the canvas.

The chain now runs off vtk.js hover picks, which are debounced client-side
(they fire when the pointer pauses — which it does right before a
right-click): the server remembers the last hovered world position, the
menu snapshots it on open, "Select Atom" toggles that atom's selection,
"Add Atom Here" places the current edit element there (undoable, refused on
top of an existing atom), and hovering an atom shows "O · atom 3". The
tooltip positioning listener is throttled to 80 ms.

### Changed: paper-core SCC-DFTB methanol optimizer is pinned (2026-07-23)

The archived CH3OH optimization failure was first recovered by the public
runner's bounded 500-iteration safety budget. With the molecular charge
relaxation fix below, the same starting geometry now converges inside the
native 100-iteration budget, while the complete optimization still reaches its
force threshold within the 80-step article budget. A production-shaped
regression pins a finite multi-frame trajectory so future SCF or routing
changes cannot silently restore the stale failure.

### Fixed: smeared BIPOLE RKS requires occupation self-consistency (2026-07-23)

Finite-temperature BIPOLE RKS convergence now requires the density produced by
the newly diagonalized physical Fock matrix to match the input density. The
energy and orbital-commutator tests alone can stop early when symmetry fixes
the orbitals: the commutator is zero even while the eigenvalue gap, Fermi
occupations, and density are still moving. That left the returned Mermin free
energy non-stationary with respect to occupations and shifted the Gamma
fractional-occupation analytic force by `4.833948e-6 Ha/bohr`.

The maintained historical-domain H2/STO-3G discriminator now leaves a
one-more-physical-Fock-update occupation residual below `1e-8` and restores
analytic-versus-free-energy-FD agreement to `1.2e-8 Ha/bohr`. Fractional
analytic gradients on the padded M5 Gamma domain now fail closed: its
finite-domain J/K forward map needs a variational density-transpose completion
before the Mermin no-occupation-response cancellation is valid. The exact
finite-difference gradient remains available on that production energy
surface.

### Fixed: molecular SCC-DFTB recovers from early charge sloshing (2026-07-23)

The molecular zero-temperature restricted and unrestricted SCC-DFTB loops now
use bounded vector Aitken relaxation for their Mulliken charge fixed points.
The previous one-way heuristic could permanently reduce the charge-mixing
fraction to 0.01 after an early anticorrelated residual, leaving an otherwise
contractive calculation too slow for the native 100-iteration limit. The
caller's requested mixing fraction remains a hard upper bound, and the charge
convergence criterion is unchanged.

The archived Thiel pyrrole row now converges in 88 native-default iterations
instead of failing at 100 and requiring 149 through the high-level safety
budget. The earlier paper-core CH3OH case now converges in 60 native-default
iterations. Geometry optimization carries the preceding geometry's converged
charges forward so Aitken history does not reselect a charge branch from a
zero-charge guess at every step. The separate finite-temperature occupation
retry ladder retains its validated damping path for molecular SCC cycles that
do not have a stable zero-temperature fixed point.

## [v0.15.55] - 2026-07-23 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Fixed: the full paper-core PM6/HCOOH optimizer now converges (2026-07-23)

Building on v0.15.54's PM6 finite-difference recovery: molecular PM6/OMx
finite-difference gradients now also refine the step when an *intermediate*
displaced SCF fails to converge, not only when the two displaced energies
land on different roots — a derivative is accepted only once both displaced
solves converge and the energy-continuity criterion is satisfied. Separately,
closed-shell PM6 geometry optimization now carries each converged density
forward to the next nuclear geometry (electronic-state continuation along the
Born-Oppenheimer surface) instead of restarting every line-search trial from
zero density, and retains the converged optimizer result for final reporting
instead of rerunning a cold-start single point that can select a different
stationary root.

Together, the two fixes resolve the archived PM6/HCOOH paper-core row
completely: it previously exhausted 200 iterations from a cold start despite a
chemically reasonable 0.950 Angstrom shortest distance, and now completes in
27 trajectory frames on a continuous lower-energy branch with a final energy
below `-24.50 Ha`.

### Fixed: `vq status`/`logs` name the host they searched on a bare not-found (2026-07-23)

`vq status JOBID` (no host given) resolves to `default_host` and searches only
there; a job living elsewhere returned a flat "no such job" that never said
the search was scoped to one host, so polling a healthy job on the wrong host
looked identical to polling a missing one. The error now names the host
searched and points at `vq status HOST JOBID` or `vq queue --all`. Scoped to
the read/poll verbs (`status`, `logs`) where an agent gets stuck; the mutating
verbs are a follow-up.

## [v0.15.54] - 2026-07-23 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Fixed: missing `vq` submit archives fail before queue mutation (2026-07-23)

The ArtVal27 article campaign exposed a generated command that referenced a
renamed payload archive. Code inspection confirmed that this was an external
planning error, not a queue implementation defect: `vq submit --compressed`
already requires the local archive to exist before the command body runs. A
regression now pins the fail-fast diagnostic and verifies that a missing
archive cannot create a queue.

### Fixed: PM6 finite differences refine across a local SCF basin boundary (2026-07-23)

Molecular PM6 and OMx finite-difference gradients now reduce an individual
central-difference step by a bounded factor of ten when the two displaced
energies initially land on different SCF roots. A derivative is accepted only
after the existing energy-continuity criterion is satisfied; after three
unsuccessful refinements the calculation still fails closed.

The archived PM6/HCOOH optimizer frame now returns a finite force on the lower
adiabatic root instead of pairing it with a metastable root 0.129 Ha higher.
The full optimizer remains fail-closed at a later line-search trial whose
displaced SCF does not converge even with the refined step, so this is a
controlled partial recovery rather than a claim that the paper-core row is
fully converged.

### Fixed: PM6 finite-difference displacements reuse the base density (2026-07-23)

Closed-shell PM6 finite-difference gradients now seed each displaced SCF from
the converged base density while retaining the bounded step refinement,
nonconvergence, nonfinite, and pair-jump guards. This keeps PM6 force
evaluation on the base stationary branch when nearby hard-occupation roots are
available. The full PM6/HCOOH optimizer row is still open because later
line-search trial geometries can fail the base SCF convergence gate.

### Added: `vq events JOBID` renders the per-job lifecycle timeline (2026-07-23)

The daemon has always written a structured event per lifecycle transition
(submitted, dispatched, every state change, kill requests, watchdog kills, and
cluster cancellations) to `<workspace>/_vq/events.jsonl`, but nothing rendered
it — `vq status` only printed the file path. `vq events JOBID` now renders
that timeline one line per event, with `--json` for the raw records, routed
the same way as `vq logs`. `vq status`'s former dead-end path pointer now
points at the verb instead.

### Added: `vq status` reports every reason a job is pending, not just the first (2026-07-23)

The pending-reason helper covered 5 of the daemon's 16 dispatch gates and
returned only the first blocker, so a job stuck behind several gates at once
showed just one of them. `pending_blockers()` now reports every gate
establishable from persisted state — drains, an in-flight admin-update
marker, unmet `--depends-on`, a running `--refresh` build, a scheduled
`not_before`, and the job/CPU/memory caps — since they stack and clearing one
can leave a job parked on the next. Conservative by construction: a gate that
cannot be proven from state files is omitted, never guessed.

Fixes a real bug found while here: the daemon charges an undeclared job its
`--default-job-mem-mb`, but that value was daemon-CLI-only and invisible to
readers, so the client under-counted the memory tally and silently dropped the
memory reason for exactly the jobs it applies to. The daemon now advertises
`default_job_mem_mb` in `daemon_capacity.json` and the client mirrors it.

## [v0.15.53] - 2026-07-23 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Fixed: OMx density recovery is iteration-cap invariant (2026-07-23)

The closed-shell OMx recovery phase added in v0.15.52 derived its damping
length from the caller's unused iteration allowance, so the same archived row
could take a different SCF path — and, in principle, land on a different
stationary point — depending only on the 200- vs 500-iteration cap passed in.
The recovery phase lengths are now fixed rather than allowance-derived, so a
row's path is invariant to the cap.

Re-measuring the archived Thiel thymine OM2 row under the corrected, cap-
invariant recovery: 146 of 200 iterations at `-66.0995572878289 Ha` (previously
148 iterations at `-66.0995573149495 Ha` under the allowance-derived recovery;
same stationary point, marginally different path). The archived Thiel adenine
OM3 row, which shares this density-recovery iteration, now converges in 131
iterations at `-65.5435854159920 Ha` under both 200- and 500-iteration caps.

### Fixed: SCC-DFTB recovers the HCOOH paper-core optimizer via a third retry rung (2026-07-23)

The v0.15.52 finite-temperature retry ladder (`0.001 Ha`, then `0.0012 Ha`)
left the paper-core HCOOH SCC-DFTB optimizer nonconverged: its compressed
line-search frames have slower charge tails than the archived single-point
rows the ladder was tuned against. A third, final `0.0015 Ha` low-mixing SCC
fallback rung now recovers it. Acetamide, cytosine, and the H2CO optimizer
diagnostic are unaffected and still finish on the first or second rung as
before.

### Changed: archived OM3 heterocycle convergence is pinned (2026-07-23)

The release-era Thiel imidazole OM3 nonconvergence row is stale after the
closed-shell OMx density-recovery fixes. A rebuilt current core converges the
exact archived geometry in 140 iterations at `-31.90345500509072 Ha` under
both 200- and 500-iteration caps. A dedicated regression now distinguishes
that cap-invariant stationary root from an older nominal-success artifact at a
materially different energy; no additional Hamiltonian or SCF mutation was
scientifically justified.

The sibling Thiel pyrrole OM3 row is likewise stale: the exact archive
converges in 138 iterations at `-28.79895432216395 Ha` with identical results
under 200-, 500-, and 1000-step caps. Its regression completes coverage of the
three named release-era OM3 failures.

### Fixed: `vq kill` cancels the scheduler job it claims to kill (2026-07-23)

Killing a scheduler-backed job the daemon was not currently tracking (the
routine window during `vq admin update`, a `systemctl restart`, or a failed
startup reattach) marked the spec `KILLED` locally without ever cancelling the
batch job — and, once `KILLED`, the spec is terminal, so the job could never
become tracked and cancelled later. `vq kill` now issues its own `qdel` for a
scheduler spec directly, in addition to the daemon's own reconciliation, and
degrades loudly: a failed cancel or a spec with no recorded scheduler job id
still marks the spec terminal but names the id to cancel by hand instead of
reporting plain success.

Two related fixes: retention's cleanup sweep gated only on terminality, so it
could `rm -rf` a leaked `KILLED` job's remote workspace out from under a
calculation that was, in fact, still running; a spec killed with no exit code
and no fetch is now skipped. And `vq status` no longer reports a workspace as
"staged locally" for a job that was killed rather than fetched — only
`last_fetched_at` counts as evidence of a fetch.

(vq 0.12.0 → 0.12.1; vq is versioned independently of vibe-qc and carries no
tag of its own — see the sibling-module note in this release's notes.)

## [v0.15.52] - 2026-07-23 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Added: `vq doctor` diagnoses the SSH chain locally before probing the host (2026-07-23)

Every `vq doctor` check was remote-side, so each one presupposed the SSH
session it was trying to diagnose. When SSH itself was what broke, doctor could
only report that everything failed, and a dead local link, a dead jump host, a
dead target, and a rejected key were indistinguishable. They look identical at
the OpenSSH level because a failure anywhere in a proxied chain is reported
against the final target as `Connection closed by UNKNOWN port 65535`; the line
naming the real cause is one row up in `ssh -v`.

A new module, `vq.ssh_probe`, adds three local primitives, and doctor now runs
them before any remote check:

* `resolve_route` asks `ssh -G` what the alias actually resolves to and whether
  a `ProxyJump` or `ProxyCommand` sits in front of it, walking a nested jump
  chain to the endpoint the local machine dials first. This alone makes an
  otherwise invisible bastion visible.
* `probe_tcp` opens a bare TCP connection to that first hop, below the SSH
  layer, so "no path to the host" is separated from "the host rejected my key"
  without offering a credential to anything.
* `classify` folds the probe result, ssh's stderr, and (only on an already
  failed path) one `ssh -v` re-run into a single named verdict:
  `first_hop_unreachable`, `first_hop_refused`, `proxy_failed`, `auth_rejected`,
  `host_key_changed`, `target_refused`, `target_closed`, `target_unreachable`,
  or `dns_failure`.

Human and `--json` output gain `ssh_route`, `ssh_first_hop`, and (on a
transport failure past a live first hop) `ssh_transport`, whose message
includes the `ssh -v` transcript lines that name the failing hop, including
anything a `ProxyCommand` wrote to its own stderr. A dead first hop short-circuits the remote checks, which would otherwise reproduce the same
failure more slowly and with less information, unless a live `ControlMaster` socket
(`ssh -O check`) means ssh can still reach the host over an established multiplexed
connection, in which case the hop is reported but the remote checks still run. `vq doctor --all` probes a
shared bastion once per invocation, and `localhost` skips the leg entirely.

Nothing in this is site-specific and none of it knows what a VPN is: any vq
user behind a bastion gets "first hop unreachable" as an actionable verdict.

### Fixed: PM6 recovers from persistent closed-shell DIIS cycles (2026-07-23)

The molecular closed-shell PM6 solver now clears a stalled Pulay history,
crosses the nonlinear hard-occupation region with a bounded density-damping
phase, and restarts DIIS from the stabilized basin. The ordinary DIIS fast
path is unchanged; the recovery changes only the route to the same
zero-temperature idempotent-density fixed point.

The archived Thiel adenine PM6 row, which did not converge even with 2000
iterations, now converges reproducibly in 150 of the public route's 200
iterations at `-51.2783009980128 Ha`. Runs with 200, 500, and 1000 iteration
caps follow the same recovery schedule and reach the identical root.

### Fixed: OM2 accelerates the post-cycle density tail (2026-07-23)

The closed-shell OMx solver now restarts Pulay DIIS with clean history after
its bounded density-damping recovery phase. Damping still carries
near-degenerate densities across the nonlinear hard-occupation cycle, while
the clean restart converges the remaining locally linear tail without changing
the zero-temperature idempotent-density target or OMx energy expression.

The archived Thiel thymine OM2 row now converges in 148 of the public route's
200 iterations at `-66.0995573149495 Ha`; damping alone required 393
iterations. The previously fixed Thiel furan row retains its stationary energy
and convergence within the same budget.

### Fixed: SCC-DFTB recovers from molecular occupation cycles (2026-07-23)

Restricted molecular SCC-DFTB now supports electron-conserving Fermi-Dirac
occupations and evaluates the corresponding variational electronic free
energy. The high-level runner preserves the existing zero-temperature
500-iteration path, then walks a bounded finite-temperature retry ladder
(`0.001 Ha`, then `0.0012 Ha` only if still nonconverged) when hard Aufbau
occupations do not admit a stable charge fixed point. Results expose the
temperature and cumulative iteration count rather than presenting the retry as
a zero-temperature solution.

The selected Thiel acetamide row now converges after its reproducible
zero-temperature failure, with neutral total Mulliken charge and a
finite-difference check of the free-energy gradient. The archived Thiel
cytosine SCC-DFTB row, whose `0.001 Ha` retry remains in an occupation/root
cycle, now converges on the second bounded rung; acetamide and the H2CO
optimizer diagnostic still finish on the first rung. Unrestricted and periodic
SCC-DFTB behavior is unchanged.

### Fixed: OM2 recovers from persistent closed-shell DIIS cycles (2026-07-22)

The molecular OMx SCF driver now switches stalled closed-shell calculations
from Pulay DIIS to a bounded density-damped fixed-point phase after clearing
the obsolete DIIS history. This preserves the ordinary fast path and the
zero-temperature OMx energy expression while giving cyclic occupation maps a
controlled route to a stable density within the existing iteration budget.

The Thiel ground-state furan OM2 row that failed repeatedly in v0.15.48 now
converges in 165 of the public runner's 200 allowed iterations. The regression
pins that archived geometry and stationary energy; this change does not claim
to resolve the separate OM2/thymine, OM3, PM6, or SCC-DFTB diagnostics in the
article-validation inventory.

### Fixed: scheduler workspace creation retries transient SSH failures (2026-07-22)

Scheduler-backed `vq` submissions now retry transient SSH transport failures
while creating the remote workspace with idempotent `mkdir -p`. A momentary
login-node banner-exchange timeout can therefore recover before submission
instead of failing the job with no scheduler id. The non-idempotent `qsub`
operation remains single-attempt to avoid duplicate batch jobs after an
ambiguous transport failure.

## [v0.15.51] - 2026-07-22 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Fixed: stale GAPW dry-run memory-estimate assumption in the test gate (2026-07-22)

`test_periodic_dry_run_estimate_writes_gpw_gapw_memory[gapw]` hardcoded
`augmentation_active=True` for every GAPW dry-run, but the hydrogen
valence-contraction fix (below) correctly makes an all-hydrogen system need no
augmentation at all. The test now derives `n_soft_basis` and
`augmentation_active` the same way `run_periodic_job`'s dry-run path does,
instead of assuming augmentation is always active for `jk_method="gapw"`.

### Fixed: SCC-DFTB paper-core optimizer uses robust SCC steps (2026-07-22)

The high-level semiempirical runner now gives molecular SCC-DFTB calculations
up to 500 SCC iterations while keeping the existing charge-convergence
threshold. `run_job(..., method="scc_dftb", optimize=True)` also bounds
ASE BFGSLineSearch trial steps to 0.08 Å for SCC-DFTB, keeping optimizer
geometries inside the converged charge branch instead of jumping into
nonconverged electronic steps.

This fixes current-main reproductions of the paper-core SiH4 optimizer row and
the CO2 optimizer-step failure, and it lets the paper-core CH3OH starting
geometry converge through the unified runner. H2CO and HCOOH remain honest
SCC-DFTB nonconvergence diagnostics; they still fail closed rather than being
reported as completed optimizations.

### Fixed: GAPW-HF retains hydrogen's full valence contraction (2026-07-21)

The GAPW hard/soft split no longer removes a tight primitive from hydrogen's
only contracted AO shell. The old element-blind 3.0 bohr⁻² cutoff pruned the
3.425 bohr⁻² STO-3G primitive even though H has no core, producing a
grid-independent approximately −108 mHa H₂ GAPW-HF error. Hydrogen is now
kept in the full soft basis while core-bearing atoms, including those in mixed
systems, retain the existing augmentation split. H₂/STO-3G agrees with an
out-of-process PySCF 2.13.1 molecular RHF reference within 0.0304 mHa on a
48³ grid. GAPW remains experimental, and the separate second-row atomic grid
residual is unchanged.

### Fixed: CCM RHF returns one consistent converged SCF state (2026-07-21)

The shared CCM RHF loop now checks its raw-Fock fixed point before constructing
the next DIIS trial. Previously a converged result combined the energy, residual,
and Fock from one iteration with the density and orbitals from a subsequent
extrapolated diagonalization. The mixed-boundary wire regression now pins both
the returned commutator and total-energy identity. Tight-core wire convergence
remains under investigation.

### Fixed: semiempirical finite-difference gradients fail closed on SCC root switches (2026-07-21)

Native PM6/UPM6 and OMx/UOMx finite-difference gradients now reject
non-converged displaced SCF solves, non-finite displaced energies, and
large energy jumps across the `+/-h` central-difference pair. The error names
the method, element list, atom, axis, step, energies, threshold, and iteration
