`runner._coerce_initial_guess`, which keeps its behaviour), so a value
assigned after construction is honoured. The Roothaan driver seeds from
densities only, so the overlap-dependent guesses (SAP / PATOM / HUECKEL /
MINAO) are rejected with a clear `ValueError` naming the supported set
(SAD / HCORE / AUTO) rather than being downgraded to SAD; unrecognised
values raise as well. No in-tree caller pinned a non-default guess on
these options, and `run_job(initial_guess=...)` already rejected
ROHF/ROKS, so shipped energies are unchanged. Regressions:
`tests/test_rohf.py::test_rohf_initial_guess_*` and
`::test_roks_initial_guess_normalisation_matches_rohf`.

## [v0.15.47] - 2026-07-19

### Fixed: retired the stale multi-k GDF +U regression guard (2026-07-18)

`test_run_periodic_job_multik_dft_plus_u_raises` expected
`run_periodic_job(method="RHF", kpoints=(2,1,1), dft_plus_u=[...])` to raise
`NotImplementedError("Increment 4c")`, but closed-shell multi-k +U has run
natively on the GDF drivers since 2026-07-04: auto `jk_method` resolves
RHF/RKS to GDF and the +U request is no longer intercepted by the legacy
Gamma-only route, so the node ran the full multi-k SCF and then failed on
the missing raise. Replaced with
`test_run_periodic_job_multik_dft_plus_u_runs_native_gdf`, which pins
convergence, `e_dft_plus_u > 0`, the `gdf_rhf_multi_k` route tag in the
`.out`, and the Dudarev + Cococcioni citations in the `.bibtex` on a small
H2/STO-3G cell. Also refreshed the stale section-13 comment and the
`run_rhf_periodic_gamma` docstring that still called multi-k +U "queued".

## [v0.15.46] - 2026-07-19

Patch release. Four fixes found by the release-paper validation campaign
running full matched-reference calculations against ORCA 6.1.1 on
immutable v0.15.45. All four are user-facing; none changes a published
numerical convention.

### Fixed: EDIIS/ADIIS anti-replay guard forked SCF onto a worse solution (2026-07-19)

The anti-replay guard added for the periodic SCF keyed on the previous
`extrapolate()` **return**, but `last_extrap_` was recorded on every cycle --
including cycles where the EDIIS_DIIS hybrid's switch metric selected the
DIIS branch and discarded the EDIIS Fock, and cycles before
`diis_start_iter` where the result is computed and dropped. The guard then
misread the next genuine use as a replay, erased live history and re-solved,
forking the trajectory onto a different SCF solution. `EDIIS`/`ADIIS` now
expose `discard_last_extrapolation()`, called at every site that drops a
produced Fock, so the guard keys on *consumed* returns.

Found by the release-paper validation campaign: n-octane RKS/PBE/def2-SVP
converged to -313.1525133850 Ha on v0.15.45 against -313.1624959631 Ha on
v0.15.21 from byte-identical input (identical options digest), with a clean
convergence report and no warning; ORCA 6.1.1 gives -313.1631401577 Ha.
Selecting `scf_accelerator="DIIS"` on the same build reproduced the older
value to 5e-11 Ha, isolating basin selection rather than the energy
functional. A deterministic 3x3 reproducer confirmed the guard destroying
history on a *first* use on the unmodified release. The original periodic
anti-replay protection stays armed and its kernel tests still pass.

### Added: closed-shell RHF/RKS slab GDF energies (2026-07-18)

An explicit `jk_method="gdf"` now runs genuine `dim=2` closed-shell RHF and
RKS on full Gamma-centered `(n1,n2,1)` meshes. The route uses a signed
slab-truncated auxiliary metric, the Born-von-Karman probe-charge exchange
correction, and rigorous Parry-gauge `V_ne(k)` / nuclear terms instead of
treating the layer as a 3D crystal of sheets. On compact H2/STO-3G
`(2,2,1)`, RHF agrees with PySCF 2.13.1 to 3.7 microHa; PBE and PBE0 agree
within 0.238 and 0.182 mHa, and doubling the bookkeeping normal length changes
all totals by less than 0.06 microHa. AUTO remains on the direct
`SLAB_EWALD_2D` route. Open shell, custom/IBZ meshes, smearing, restarts,
DFT+U, range-separated functionals, and gradients remain fail-closed.

### Added: HSE-type screened hybrids on the multi-k COSX backend (2026-07-19)

`run_krks_periodic_gdf(functional="hse06", k_exchange="cosx")` — and the
public `run_periodic_job(method="RKS", functional="hse06",
jk_method="rijcosx", kpoints=...)` route — now run HSE-type screened
hybrids (`c_full = 0` per the shared `resolve_periodic_exchange`
policy): the physical `erfc(ω_s r)/r` exchange composes as the bridge's
alias-safe real-space SR part plus a cusp-free reciprocal band kernel
`[erf(ω_p r) − erf(ω_s r)]/r` whose G=0 value is finite
(`π(1/ω_s² − 1/ω_p²)`), so no exxdiv Madelung shift applies. The G=0
convention includes the erfc kernel's finite `π/ω_s²` zero mode
(VASP/CRYSTAL convention, shared with the BIPOLE screened route).
Validated: ERI-exact vs the direct-ERI erfc reference (5.6e-4, COSX
quadrature floor) with split-omega invariance (2.3e-4); vacuum-box
molecular limit 5.1e-5 Ha; cross-backend vs BIPOLE screened 0.20 mHa;
out-of-process-pattern PySCF 2.13.1 KRKS hse06 agrees to 7.3e-5 Ha
after adding the analytic zero-mode term PySCF's `exxdiv=None`
convention drops. The Lpq GDF backend keeps rejecting screened hybrids,
full-range-arm RS functionals (ωB97X, CAM-B3LYP) keep failing closed on
every backend, and the open-shell multi-k driver keeps rejecting all RS
functionals (bounded follow-on).
### Fixed: periodic 52-dash .out blocks are content-sized (2026-07-19)

The final hand-guessed rules in the periodic runner are retired: the
periodic D3-BJ dispersion block and the vibrational-frequencies family
(skip / normal / failed) draw their title rule through `section_header`,
and the Mode/Freq/IR frequency table renders through `Table`, mirroring the
molecular frequency table (content-sized rule, policy-driven frequency
rendering). Both runners now contain zero hand-drawn dash rules; rows and
numeric values are unchanged.

### Added: vibe-view Structure Library pinned favourites (2026-07-17)

A star next to the library search box pins the selected molecule; pinned
structures appear as accented chips above the recents row and one click
re-selects them. Favourites are a deliberate choice, so unlike the implicit
recents they persist with a saved session (alongside bookmarks). Sessions
written before this load unchanged.

### Fixed: banner provenance API reachable from the package root (2026-07-18)

`vibeqc/__init__.py` exports a `banner()` *function*, which shadows the
`vibeqc.banner` *submodule* on the package root. `from vibeqc import banner`
therefore binds the function, so `getattr(banner, "build_info", None)`
returned `None` instead of the provenance helper -- a silent miss that cost
the release-paper validation campaign a production job when a runtime
identity probe fell through to a bogus fallback path. Every public name of
`vibeqc.banner` (`build_info`, `codename_for_version`,
`enforce_runtime_pin_from_env`, `RELEASE_CODENAMES`) is now re-exported on
the package root and listed in `vibeqc.__all__`, so callers no longer need
`importlib.import_module("vibeqc.banner")`. Purely additive: `vibeqc.banner`
remains the callable function with unchanged behaviour.

### Added: vibe-view SCF |ΔE| per-cycle bars (2026-07-17)

The SCF Convergence plot now shows each cycle's energy change as bars on the
log residual axis. vibe-qc's solvers record `delta_e` on every cycle but emit
no `diis_error`, so that axis had been permanently empty and the file's only
convergence signal went unplotted. Magnitudes are used (the sign flips as the
energy settles) and exact zeros are dropped; files without `delta_e` degrade
to no series rather than an empty axis.
### Fixed: molecular 52/60-dash .out blocks are content-sized (2026-07-18)

The remaining hand-guessed rules in the molecular runner are retired: the
implicit-solvation, MSINDO binding-energy, atomization, D3-BJ/D4 dispersion,
gCP, SRB, composite-total, vibrational-frequencies, and thermochemistry
titled blocks draw their rule through `section_header` (sized to the title);
the non-mean-field solver-result frame and the MLIP single-point header drop
their detached 60-dash rules for the same title-sized form; and the MACE
provenance card sizes its box rules to its widest content line. Rows and
numeric values are unchanged. The Hessian golden was regenerated with a
reviewed two-line diff (the two rules), and the format guard now pins the
dispersion/vibrational/thermochemistry rules with a real RKS-D3BJ+Hessian
run.

### Added: vibe-view Structure Library recents (2026-07-17)

The Structure Library keeps the last few molecules you inserted or opened and
offers them as one-click chips above the search box, so reaching for the same
handful no longer means retyping into an 83-entry autocomplete. Most-recent
first, de-duplicated, capped at six; session-scoped.

### Fixed: correlated-method .out blocks are content-sized (2026-07-18)

The molecular MP2, DLPNO-MP2/UMP2, DLPNO-CCSD/UCCSD, coupled-cluster, and
OVGF/GF2 blocks no longer draw hand-guessed 78-dash rules. Titled component
blocks render through `section_header` (rule sized to the title), the
CCSD/CCD/QCISD/BCCD-family iteration trace renders through `Table` with the
same column conventions as the CCSDT/CC3 blocks (policy-driven energies, a
signed-e `dE` column, content-sized rules), and both GF2 quasiparticle
tables render through `Table` with eV carried in the headers. Numeric values
are unchanged; a format guard (`tests/test_correlated_block_format.py`) pins
the content-sized shapes.

### Added: Gamma RIJCOSX UHF/UKS on vacuum-padded cells (2026-07-18)

`run_periodic_job(method="UHF"/"UKS", jk_method="rijcosx",
kpoints=(1,1,1))` now runs dedicated Gamma RIJCOSX open-shell drivers
(`run_periodic_rijcosx_uhf` / `run_periodic_rijcosx_uks`) on the same
vacuum-padded envelope as the RKS rung: molecular DF J from the total
density, per-spin periodic COSX K through the dedicated Gamma builder,
per-spin post-convergence one-center replacement, and (UKS) XC on the
molecular Becke grid, via the production C++ `run_uhf_scf_with_jk` /
`run_uks_scf_with_jk`. Spin counts follow the system multiplicity.
Validated on triplet H₂/STO-3G in a 50-bohr box: 2.0e-5 Ha vs the
molecular RIJCOSX oracle (the apples-to-apples comparison — the
1.1 mHa deviation from *exact* molecular UHF is the method-inherent
COSX quadrature error, reproduced by molecular RIJCOSX itself).
Tight/short-axis one-cell open-shell runs keep failing closed.

### Added: Gamma RIJCOSX RKS on vacuum-padded cells (2026-07-18)

`run_periodic_job(method="RKS", jk_method="rijcosx", kpoints=(1,1,1))`
now runs a dedicated Gamma RIJCOSX RKS driver
(`run_periodic_rijcosx_rks`) on vacuum-padded cells (every active
lattice length ≥ 12 bohr, not a tight cell): molecular DF J plus
periodic COSX K via the dedicated Gamma builder, XC on the molecular
Becke grid (exact in that envelope), SCF through the production C++
`run_rks_scf_with_jk` including the post-convergence COSX one-center
replacement. Hybrids route their exact-exchange fraction through COSX;
pure functionals never build K. Validated on H₂/STO-3G in a 50-bohr box
vs vibe-qc molecular RKS: pbe0 4.7e-5 Ha, pbe 4.8e-5 Ha (identical
scale with and without exact exchange — the residual is the shared
box-limit/DF piece, not COSX). Tight or short-axis cells and one-cell
UHF/UKS keep failing closed with narrowed messages.

### Fixed: GPAW PW-limit reference — K/Ca/Br free-atom convergence; reference set complete at 28 systems (2026-07-18)

The out-of-process GPAW atom worker
(`examples/regression/pw_limit_atomization/pw_reference.py`) could not
converge the K, Ca, or Br r2SCAN free atoms, blocking the last four
compounds (CaO, CaF2, KBr, KCl) of the plane-wave-limit atomization
reference set. Root cause was the SCF-fallback path: a hard
150-iteration cap plus the default 4e-8 eV^2/e eigenstates criterion,
on which K/Ca plateau near 1e-7 indefinitely while the energy is
stable to 1e-6 eV. The fallback now uses the full iteration budget
with an explicit 1e-6 eV^2/e eigenstates criterion; K gets a
damped-mixer branch (beta 0.02, nmaxold 8, density 1.5e-3) against
intermittent charge-sloshing excursions, and Br joins the SCF-fallback
list (its etdm direct minimisation does not converge). Validation:
two independent converged K runs agree to 0.04 kJ/mol; an Al control
reproduces its production energy unchanged; Ca matches the
criterion-starved long-grind energy to 2e-4 kJ/mol. The four new
systems land at GPAW-vs-VASP deltas of -7.2 (CaO), -8.2 (CaF2),
-2.1 (KCl), and -27.2 kJ/mol (KBr; three-way split, Br atom-reference
convention suspected - see `studies/pw_limit_atomization/CONSOLIDATED.md`).
Consolidated stats over the full 28-system set: GPAW-VASP MD -6.5 /
MAD 8.5 kJ/mol; GPAW-pob MD -24.6 / MAD 35.4 kJ/mol. Regression
coverage: `tests/test_pw_limit_atomization.py` pins the fallback
settings; the GPAW-gated end-to-end smoke test passes through the
modified worker.

### Added: weighted full-BZ k-meshes on the multi-k COSX backend + explicit-KPoints exxdiv fix (2026-07-18)

The multi-k COSX exchange bridge (`KPointCosxK`) now consumes BZ
quadrature weights: the D(g) inverse Bloch fold, the LR-erf complement
(per-source-k `w_j` factors), its G=0 finite-part term (now detected on
`q ≈ 0` pairs rather than index equality, so duplicated-k quadratures
are consistent), and the one-center D(g=0) fold all accept `weights`
(None = uniform, bit-identical to the historical behavior). Both multi-k
drivers pass their quadrature weights through, so `k_exchange="cosx"` on
a custom-weighted full-BZ `KPoints` mesh — previously silently wrong
(uniform 1/N_k fold regardless of weights) — is now exact: a weighted
{Γ 1/3, X 2/3} SCF equals the equivalent duplicated uniform [Γ, X, X]
run to machine precision, and matches the `k_exchange="gdf"` backend on
the same quadrature at the established COSX parity band (0.128 mHa).

In the same merge, a latent exxdiv defect on explicit `KPoints` inputs
was fixed for both exchange backends: the drivers took the Born-von-
Kármán mesh for the exxdiv Madelung constant from
`kmesh_bloch.mesh`, which is `(1,1,1)` after the explicit-KPoints
conversion, silently substituting the primitive-cell Madelung
(measured 78 mHa on the dimerized H₂ chain, identical uniform
[Γ, X] quadrature vs the tuple `(1,1,2)` mesh). The BvK mesh now comes
from the caller's `kmesh` argument; explicit `KPoints` without declared
`mesh` metadata fail closed on hybrid/HF runs instead of converging a
wrong exxdiv. Regressions: a bridge-level duplicated-k exactness oracle
and an SCF-level weighted/explicit/duplicated/backend-parity gate in
`tests/test_periodic_rijcosx.py`.

### Fixed: toroidal DLPNO wrappers use minimum-image pair distances (2026-07-18)

The toroidal-megacell DLPNO wrappers (`toroidal_dlpno_mp2` /
`toroidal_dlpno_ccsd` / `toroidal_dlpno_ccsd_t` in
`vibeqc.periodic_toroidal_mp2`) previously inherited the molecular
drivers' open-cluster Euclidean centroid distances, which overestimate
wrap-around separations on the torus — the distant-pair dipole screen
could falsely screen, and the CCSD coupling-radius sets silently
under-couple, pairs that are adjacent on the torus (measured on the
(1,1,4) H₂/STO-3G chain: the Euclidean screen's error vs the unscreened
reference is 1.6e-4 Ha, 8.6× the torus-aware 1.8e-5 Ha). The wrappers
now consume the toroidal pair geometry by default: a new exact
minimum-image pair-distance factory (`toroidal_pair_distance_fn`,
sharing the LLL/QR sphere-decode machinery of
`classify_toroidal_pairs`) feeds new additive, default-off
`pair_distance_fn` hooks on `DLPNOMP2Options` and `LocalCCSDOptions`
(None preserves the historical Euclidean behavior bit-identically), and
the `classify_toroidal_pairs` family view is attached to the wrapper
results. Regressions: minimum-image unit gate (orthorhombic + skew,
integer-oracle consistency), the wrap-around screening anchor above,
and a CCSD coupling-set gate. Representative-only pair-family
evaluation was re-scoped to the localized-basis BvK
translational-symmetry route (the named v0.17.0 gate) — canonical-MO
per-pair energies carry no translational structure, so it cannot be
landed honestly at the canonical layer
(handovers/HANDOVER_GATED_ITEMS.md G-PBC-008).
### Added: periodic Gamma GPW ROHF through the unified runner (2026-07-18)

The maintained-preview 3D Gamma GPW ROHF implementation is now reachable as
`run_periodic_job(method="ROHF", jk_method="gpw")`. The unified result retains
one restricted spatial-orbital set with integer 2/1/0 occupations, exact
spin-pure S-squared metadata, per-spin densities and Focks, normal manifest
backend provenance, and the existing ROHF citation. Unsupported dimensions,
k meshes, JK backends, electronic smearing, gradients, response properties,
and restart densities fail closed. Periodic ROKS, GDF/BIPOLE/GAPW ROHF,
multi-k GPW exact exchange, and metallic occupations remain gated.

### Added: multi-k COSX one-center replacement (2026-07-18)

The multi-k periodic RIJCOSX backend (`k_exchange="cosx"` in
`run_krhf_periodic_gdf` / `run_kuhf_periodic_gdf`, reached by
`run_periodic_job(jk_method="rijcosx")` at multi-k) now applies the
analytic one-center replacement after convergence, closing the gap with
the dedicated Gamma builders (2026-07-15) and the molecular RIJCOSX
lifecycle: the SCF iterates and reports its energy on the uncorrected
seminumerical exchange surface, and the returned Fock matrices and
orbitals are upgraded by the same-atom analytic-minus-quadrature
exchange correction. Because the bridge's real-space exchange is
range-separated, `OneCenterCorrection` gained an omega-aware variant
that evaluates BOTH sides of the replacement with the erfc short-range
kernel (libint `erfc_coulomb` analytic ERIs plus the attenuated
quadrature seeding); the smooth reciprocal-space LR complement carries
no same-atom cusp error and is untouched. New binding
`compute_cosx_one_center_correction`, bridge method
`KPointCosxK.one_center_correction`, four regressions in
`tests/test_periodic_rijcosx.py` (kernel-match with dense-grid
shrinkage and erfc/coulomb branch continuity, D(g=0) fold, RHF and
UHF driver lifecycle pins).

Also fixed in the same merge: public periodic RIJCOSX jobs
(`jk_method="rijcosx"`) now fire the COSX acceleration citations
(Neese 2009, Izsák-Neese 2011, Helmich-Paris 2021) into the
references surface — the runner previously passed
`acceleration=("rijcosx",)` only for the χ-CCM rijcosx backend,
silently dropping the attribution on the dedicated route. Pinned by
`test_rijcosx_periodic_job_cites_cosx`.

### Fixed: periodic optimization verdicts share one semantic block (2026-07-18)

Gaussian-basis and full-k semiempirical periodic optimizations now render
their final energy, iteration count, and convergence verdict through one
content-sized `HeaderlessBlock`. The energy retains the active output policy,
and the duplicated 56-character guessed rule is retired in both routes. The
covered periodic-geometry golden changes only that rule, to the 28-character
width of the rendered final-energy row.

### Fixed: periodic electronic summaries use semantic headerless blocks (2026-07-18)

The multi-k band-extrema and crystal-orbital `.out` summaries now use
content-sized `HeaderlessBlock` layouts. K-point locations and HOCO/LUCO
markers remain ragged annotations and therefore do not inflate the rule. The
band summary retains its deliberate parallel Ha/eV values through explicit
semantic energy rendering, while the crystal-orbital values and title follow
the active energy policy. The two covered periodic goldens change only the
formerly undersized crystal-orbital rule.

### Fixed: periodic metadata summaries use semantic headerless blocks (2026-07-18)

Periodic basis, primitive-cell reduction, and finite-temperature smearing
summaries now use content-sized `HeaderlessBlock` layouts. Smearing energies,
electronic temperature, and entropy also follow the active quantity policy,
including matching eV labels after energy conversion. The two covered periodic
goldens change only the formerly overlong basis rule.

### Fixed: molecular atom summary rule follows its coordinate rows (2026-07-18)

The molecular `.out` atom/geometry summary now uses `HeaderlessBlock`, matching
the periodic system summary. Atom and footer rows are byte-neutral; the rule
now spans the actual coordinate-row width instead of stopping six characters
short. The reviewed five molecular golden diffs change only that rule line.

### Fixed: runner timing summaries are content-sized and unit-truthful (2026-07-18)

Molecular and periodic `.out` timing summaries now share one
`HeaderlessBlock` formatter. Their rules size to the non-annotation content,
iteration-count annotations remain outside the rule, and a `time:ms` or
`time:min` output policy updates the title as well as converting the values.
The reviewed molecular and periodic golden diffs change only the seven timing
rule lines covered by the snapshot suite.

### Fixed: double-hybrid energy block uses the document primitive (2026-07-18)

Standalone double-hybrid `.out` files now render their RKS, MP2, optional
dispersion, and total energies through the same `HeaderlessBlock` and active
energy policy as the molecular SCF component blocks. The content-sized rule
is one character shorter than the former guessed 52-character rule; the
reviewed `double_hybrid.out` golden diff changes only the two rule lines.

### Added: fixed-cell full-k DFTB periodic optimization (2026-07-18)

`run_periodic_job(..., method="dftb0"|"scc-dftb", kpoints=..., optimize=True)`
now relaxes atomic positions at fixed cell for the public zero-temperature
full-k DFTB0/SCC-DFTB routes. The runner uses the same route-planned
native-batched finite-difference gradient facade as full-k semiempirical NEB,
forwards SCC iteration/convergence controls to displaced steps, writes an
optimized-geometry summary, and marks the manifest crashed if the optimizer
does not converge. Finite-temperature optimization and `optimize_cell=True`
remain fail-closed until their derivative and stress semantics are defined.

### Added: finite-temperature full-k DFTB derivative facades (2026-07-18)

The experimental full-k DFTB0/SCC-DFTB derivative facades now expose finite
Fermi-Dirac smearing explicitly. The structured
`evaluate_periodic_kpoint_energy_gradient_stress(...)` result keeps internal
energy and Mermin free energy separate and labels whether gradients/stress
differentiate `energy` or `free_energy`; the tuple
`evaluate_periodic_energy_gradient(..., kpoints=...)` facade returns the
differentiated potential, preserving zero-temperature behavior while making
finite-temperature calls follow the native Mermin free-energy FD batch.
Finite-temperature NEB and geometry optimization remain fail-closed.

### Changed: pure-RKS BIPOLE Hartree routes through the padded SR+LR composition (2026-07-18)

The pure semilocal periodic RKS (BIPOLE) Hartree J no longer defaults to the
exact analytic-FT Ewald builder. It now uses the same M5-padded,
QQR-screened SR+LR erfc composition as every other BIPOLE route (maintainer
ruling 2026-07-13; the M4b/M5 repair of the short-range ket-image truncation
was its precondition). This closes the exact-FT finite-ke reciprocal
core-tail undercount (~0.5-1 Ha in absolute totals on dense-core cells at
the default `VIBEQC_J_EWALD3D_KE=200`, cancelling in energy differences) and
restores absolute cross-code comparability for pure functionals on
MgO-class cells. Absolute pure-RKS BIPOLE energies move at the recovered
core-tail scale; affected regression pins were re-derived. The analytic-FT
builder remains available as an explicit `use_exact_ft_j=True` cross-check
oracle on `run_pbc_bipole_rks` (pure functionals on the corrected split
only; fails closed otherwise) and only that route still emits the
dense-core reciprocal-tail warning. This also removes the exact-FT
pair-resolved density-template cost from the symmetry-reduction default
path on pure functionals.

### Fixed: molecular workflow progress uses the live logger (2026-07-18)

Standalone molecular geometry optimization (L-BFGS-B and Brent), relaxed 1D
and 2D scans, dimer transition-state search, and MECI optimization no longer
call `print()`. Their opt-in progress now flows through `ProgressLogger` while
preserving the existing stdout text, blank lines, quiet behavior, and dimer's
caller-owned writable-stream contract. Molecular optimizers and scans also
accept a caller-supplied `ProgressLogger`, allowing one live sink to follow the
whole nested workflow. All four modules are pinned by the no-print guard. The
reviewed residual AST inventory contains only deliberate CLI, named-printer,
demo/smoke, fetch/build, benchmark, and data-generation output surfaces.

### Added: Γ compcell GDF UHF analytic gradient preview (2026-07-18)

`run_pbc_gdf_uhf(compute_gradient=True)` computes the open-shell analytic
gradient on the same narrow compcell preview envelope as the RHF route
(G-PBC-002 milestone 1): DF-J from the total density, per-spin DF-K at half
the closed-shell kernel weight, occupation-1 energy-weighted density, and
the per-spin exxdiv overlap term. In-driver only (cache built from the
SCF's retained fit state; no standalone re-derivation wrapper yet).
Fails closed on rsgdf/mdf, AFT-on, smearing, and the grid V_ne backend.
Gates: UHF(M=1) ≡ RHF gradient to 5e-7 (algebraic collapse onto the
FD-validated closed-shell route), H₂-triplet central FD to < 5e-3 Ha/bohr,
Newton's third law to 1e-10 (`tests/test_periodic_gdf_gradient.py`, 35
passed). **Scope caveat:** the gradient is validated against the driver's
own energy surface (FD); a matched-convention PySCF cross-check surfaced a
pre-existing ~52 mHa Γ *compcell* UHF triplet energy discrepancy
(vibe-qc −0.5877 vs PySCF pbc UHF −0.5358505 on H₂-triplet/12-bohr/
exxdiv='ewald'; the rsgdf and multi-k routes match PySCF) — recorded as an
open GDF bug in `HANDOVER_OPEN_BUGS_V015.md`; compcell open-shell absolute
energies and forces inherit that hold until it is resolved.

### Added: MS/XMS-CASPT2 state-pair nonadiabatic couplings (2026-07-18)

`CASPT2Options(nac_pair=(Q, P))` now requests the full symmetrized
MS/XMS-CASPT2 derivative-coupling vector from an exact, equal-weight
SA-CASSCF reference. The under-review route reoptimizes every central nuclear
displacement, includes the internally contracted first-order CASPT2
wavefunctions, tracks physical roots and phases by cross-geometry overlaps,
and retains AO-centre motion through native two-basis overlap integrals.
Unsupported shifts, open shells, selected references, unequal weights,
singular state gaps, and lost state tracking fail closed. Results surface as
`SolverResult.nonadiabatic_pair` and `.nonadiabatic_coupling` in bohr^-1; the
default remains unchanged when no pair is requested.

### Fixed: standalone periodic diagnostics use the progress logger (2026-07-18)

Opt-in density/Fock symmetry diagnostics and experimental periodic GAPW-OT
iteration messages no longer call `print()`. They now flow through
`ProgressLogger`, preserving their direct-call stdout and quiet-mode behavior
without confusing transient progress with the ambient `.out` channel. GAPW-OT
also now returns its real completed iteration count instead of zero on
convergence and preserves the final sub-threshold gradient norm instead of
replacing it with an invented `0.0`. Focused regressions pin both the live text
and the corrected metadata; the two emitters are covered by the no-print guard.

### Removed: vibe-view dead shadow-pass helper; rendering boundary documented (2026-07-17)

`setup_shadow_pass` is deleted. It was never called from anywhere, never
added its pass to the chain (`docs/audit_2026_07_02.md` finding 4), and — being
a `renderer.SetPass` effect — could not have reached the client's vtk.js
viewport even once fixed.

That last point is the general rule, now documented in `material_presets.py`:
the live viewport is drawn client-side from a serialised scene, so **actor
properties** (material presets, toon shading) are visible there, while
**renderer passes** (SSAO, OSPRay, shadows) only shape server-side output —
exported screenshots and the high-quality render. An audit of every optional
effect confirmed the remaining user-facing controls are honest.

### Fixed: vibe-view orbital opacity is now adjustable (2026-07-17)

Molecular-orbital lobes were pinned at 0.6 opacity: `_render_mo_volume`
hardcoded the value instead of reading the Opacity setting, and the Opacity
slider lived only in the volume panel — which is not shown while a
wavefunction section is selected, so an orbital could not be made opaque at
all. MO rendering now honours the setting, an **Orbital opacity** slider sits
next to Render MO, and dragging it retints the existing lobes in place rather
than re-evaluating the MO grid (~1 s).

Beyond being adjustable, this makes a fully opaque orbital possible — useful
for figures, and the way to test whether translucent-isosurface depth-peeling
is behind the client-side render freeze.

### Fixed: correlated-solver diagnostics use the output channel (2026-07-18)

Verbose CASSCF, selected-CI, DMRG, and v2RDM diagnostics no longer print
directly to process stdout. They now follow the ambient `vibeqc.output`
channel, so runner-owned diagnostics stay in `.out` and direct library calls
remain silent unless the caller explicitly installs a file, stream, or stdout
channel. All four emitters are covered by the output no-print guard and a
shared routing regression. Default calculation output is byte-neutral because
these messages remain gated by each solver's explicit `verbose` option.

### Added: native Mulliken population sidecars for SCC tight binding (2026-07-18)

Molecular SCC-DFTB and experimental GFN2-xTB runs now preserve their native
net atomic Mulliken charges and emit the default `.population.txt` / `.json`
sidecars. The files mark Loewdin, Hirshfeld, Mayer, Wiberg, NPA, and dipole
analyses explicitly unsupported instead of applying Gaussian-AO formulas to a
minimal Slater-orbital model. Molden remains fail-closed because the current
writer is GTO-specific. Citation routing now follows each successfully emitted
population section rather than treating any population file as proof that the
full analysis stack ran. DFTB0, NDDO, MSINDO, solver-only, and MLIP routes remain
capability-inapplicable until their producers expose a validated native
population contract. SCC-DFTB now also reports the native convergence flag and
iteration count that were previously flattened to `true` / `1` by the
high-level adapter.

### Fixed: output-sidecar I/O failures use structured warnings (2026-07-18)

Crash-dump attachments, performance logs, and structured NDJSON logs no longer
print ad hoc failure messages directly to stderr. Their optional I/O failures
now flow through the shared output-warning record with a stable category,
role, path, exception type, Python warning, and logger entry. The migration
also fixed nested `crash_dump=` paths: their parent directory is now created
before density/Fock/MO attachments, so a TOML dump cannot silently outlive
missing diagnostic siblings. These three non-CLI writers are now pinned by the
output no-print guard; QVF's validator remains an intentional CLI.

### Fixed: bounded GFN2-xTB SCC auto-stabilization (2026-07-18)

The experimental molecular GFN2-xTB driver replaces its cumulative six-stage
auto-stabilization ladder with one slow zero-temperature retry followed by one
short finite-temperature retry. The eleven BUG 45 article-validation outliers
now converge in 1,828--2,853 total SCC iterations instead of 9,828--20,853,
without changing their converged energies. The Python model delegates retry
ownership to the native driver instead of wrapping it in another retry ladder,
and failed stabilization now reports the total attempted iteration count.
Pyridine and cyclopropene regressions pin both retry classes and the public
model path. This is a convergence/performance fix; GFN2-xTB remains
experimental pending its separate physical-model parity milestones.

### Fixed: SCC-DFTB optimizers reject non-converged electronic steps (2026-07-18)

Molecular SCC-DFTB and unrestricted SCC-DFTB now propagate the native SCC
convergence verdict and real iteration count through their public models and
the unified semiempirical runner. ASE geometry optimization aborts with the
typed SCF-convergence error before using an energy or force from a
non-converged SCC state. This resolves the ArtVal25 H2CO failure: its submitted
geometry does not reach an integer-occupation SCC fixed point, but the adapter
previously reported `converged=True` in one iteration and fed the inconsistent
state to BFGSLineSearch, producing run-dependent 31-step convergence,
500-step caps, or `LineSearch failed!`. The same input now fails immediately
and leaves a crashed manifest plus trajectory for diagnosis.

### Fixed: BIPOLE RHF Gamma analytic preview follows the padded M5 domain (2026-07-18)

Corrected-gauge RHF Gamma analytic gradients now differentiate the production
M5 padded erfc short-range domain when pair-resolved SYM3b reduction is
inactive. The ERI derivative kernel independently follows the ordinary-cutoff
Fock-output cells, 2x-cutoff density support, and padded internal ket-image
ball used by the energy build. Fixed-density J/K and converged-SCF central
differences pin the result at unchanged tolerances. Pair-resolved output masks
and padded multi-k routes remain fail-closed; finite differences remain the
production force path.

### Added: padded M5 Gamma gradients for UHF and hybrid RKS (2026-07-18)

The same non-pair-resolved three-domain derivative contract now reaches
corrected-gauge UHF Gamma and hybrid-RKS Gamma. The maintained asymmetric BeH
UHF and PBE0 RKS central-difference gates run with the production
`sr_image_precision=1e-6` policy and pass at the unchanged 1e-5 Ha/bohr
tolerance. Padded UKS remains fail-closed after exposing an XC-specific
1.29e-2 Ha/bohr residual; pair-resolved and multi-k M5 derivatives remain
gated. Finite differences remain the production force path.

### Fixed: semiempirical logs no longer show an empty DIIS table (2026-07-18)

Basis-free semiempirical result adapters expose the final SCF iteration count
but not per-iteration energies or residuals. The shared text and Python-logging
renderers now omit the otherwise-empty `energy / dE / ||[F,DS]|| / DIIS` table
while retaining the real convergence verdict, iteration count, and final
energy. Native molecular and periodic traces remain unchanged, and periodic
dict-backed trace rendering now has direct regression coverage.

### Fixed: semiempirical periodic status docs no longer overclaim k-point routes (2026-07-18)

The semiempirical user guide now separates Gamma-point periodic support from
the narrower public full-k route surface. Full-k semiempirical jobs are
documented as closed-shell DFTB0/SCC-DFTB only, while GFN2 full-k, periodic
open-shell NDDO, and MSINDO through the Gamma/k-point runner remain gated or
inapplicable. A status-text regression pins the wording so the guide cannot
drift back to "all families" or "GFN2 Gamma + k" claims.

### Fixed: vibe-view ambient occlusion never applied (2026-07-17)

`ambient_occlusion_pass()` called `vtkSSAOPass.SetSamples()`, a method that
class has never had (its sample count is `SetKernelSize`), so it raised
AttributeError before attaching the pass — and its `except ImportError` could
not catch it. Callers swallow exceptions, so SSAO silently never applied while
the Display switch read "on". Fixed to use `SetKernelSize` and to fail
honestly.

Also clarified what the toggle does: SSAO is a **server-side** render pass, so
it shapes exported screenshots and the high-quality render, and cannot affect
the live vtk.js viewport (a scene serialised to the client is identical with
and without it). The switch is relabelled "Ambient occlusion (exported
images)". This also rules SSAO out as a cause of the client-side render
freeze.

### Added: vibe-view sidebar section icons + warning badges (2026-07-17)

Each section in the sidebar now carries a glyph for its kind — a molecule for
structures, an orbit for orbitals, a curve for spectra, a chart for DOS/SCF —
instead of eight identical status ticks, so the list is scannable at a glance.
Families deliberately share a glyph so the eye groups them. A section that
errored or is unsupported gains a trailing warning badge; the exact status
stays in the subtitle.

### Changed: vibe-view toolbar grouped into labelled menus (2026-07-17)

The app bar's loose icon strip is grouped further: camera views collapse into
a **Camera** menu (isometric / top / front / side / reset) and the
diagnostics-and-help cluster into an **Info** menu (keyboard shortcuts,
memory by section, performance profile, download manager, settings, about),
joining the existing **Export** menu. Nine unlabelled icons become three
labelled menus, which also fixes the overflow that pushed buttons off a
narrow window. Retires a duplicate: "Memory usage" and "Memory usage by
section" were two buttons firing the same action (and the former shared the
info icon with About).

### Added (EXPERIMENTAL): double hybrids on the real-Γ direct-torus route (2026-07-18)

`run_ccm_double_hybrid_direct` (closed shell): the standard two-step
double-hybrid composition on the direct route — hybrid-KS SCF half
(`run_ccm_rks_direct` with the DH functional, exchange-q=0 seam included)
plus a spin-component-scaled MP2 correction (`mp2_c_os`/`mp2_c_ss`) on the
converged KS orbitals, both halves on ONE neutral cderi `L` (the BvK-ewald
direct-reference composition; the `run_ccm_ri_mp2` default reference stays
`"neutral"` — that flip remains the pending maintainer decision of
`HANDOVER_D2_EXXDIV.md`). Open shells and dispersion composition fail
closed with pointers; RSH double hybrids fail closed through the shared
resolver. Gates (`tests/test_ccm_double_hybrid_direct.py`, manual research
lanes): vacuum limit vs molecular `run_double_hybrid` (−6.7e-4 total,
PT2 halves at the 3e-5 RI-vs-canonical floor), exact composition
identity, seam-moves-SCF-not-density identity (a_x·ξ_N·N_e/2 with the
eigenvalue-denominator PT2 response), fail-closed boundary.

### Added: vibe-view per-element colour overrides (2026-07-17)

The Display panel gains an element picker + colour swatch: choose any element
present in the structure, pick a colour, **Set**. "Reset element colours"
restores the CPK palette. Overrides are keyed by atomic number and applied
inside ``cpk_color()``, so every render path honours them — molecular
per-atom actors, glyph-batched large systems, replicated supercells and
compare mode alike.

### Fixed: scheduler helper updates wait for shared-filesystem readiness (2026-07-18)

After a scheduler helper is installed from a separate build host, `vq admin
update HOST` now requires two consecutive successful helper executions before
writing and verifying its exact source-SHA marker. The readiness check retries
only the bounded `ETXTBSY` (`Text file busy`) race seen when a shared NFS venv
has not settled on the scheduler login host. Exhaustion, unrelated execution
failures, malformed marker replies, and SHA mismatches remain fail-closed with
structured probe diagnostics and a retained admin marker.

### Fixed: requested sidecars cannot disappear behind a complete manifest (2026-07-17)

Molecular and periodic Molden/population requests are now capability-aware.
The default auto mode emits both sidecars on molecular Gaussian-basis SCF and
exact single-Gamma periodic Gaussian-basis routes, and omits inapplicable plan
rows for periodic non-Gamma/multi-k, basis-free semiempirical, solver-only, and
MACE routes. Explicit `True` on an unsupported route fails before calculation;
MACE remains explicitly wavefunction-inapplicable. At finalization,
`ManifestUpdater.finish()` refuses `status="complete"` while any `always=true`
plan row is unwritten, durably records the missing rows and `status="crashed"`,
then raises `IncompleteOutputError`. Conditional rows may remain pending. This
closes the requested/empty sidecar contract behind BUG 29/34/42 without
changing supported-route sidecar bytes. The optimizer `.traj` row is now
truthfully conditional because only the ASE backend writes that sibling;
native, Brent, and geomopt histories remain available through QVF.

### Fixed: multi-k GDF warns + tags dense-core parity-held cells (2026-07-18)

The multi-k GDF drivers returned dense-core (P01-class) absolute energies
with no flag: MgO primitive FCC / STO-3G at the untailed default measured
**−0.503 Ha** ((1,1,2)) / **−0.505 Ha** ((2,2,2), Γ-centered AND shifted
meshes) vs live PySCF 2.13.1 on identical meshes — while the Γ driver has
warned, tagged `+PARITY_HELD`, and auto-sized the high-|G| tail since the
P01 audit. `run_krhf/kuhf_periodic_gdf` (and the KS wrappers) now reuse
the Γ dense-core classifier: a loud warning + `+PARITY_HELD` backend tag
on the un-tailed hold class. The tail genuinely closes the gap at multi-k
— `rsgdf_tail_ke_cutoff = 1.1·10·ζ_max` lands (1,1,2) at **+0.16 mHa** vs
tight PySCF (the same shared-thresholds floor as the Γ ladder) — but at
~40× the untailed cderi build cost per (k_i,k_j) pair (611 s → 25240 s at
(1,1,2)), so multi-k does NOT auto-tail: at n_k² pair builds that default
would be a production-scale cost the caller must opt into (whether it
should auto-tail anyway is an open maintainer call, tracked with the
production-k-sampling audit findings in `HANDOVER_OPEN_BUGS_V015.md`).
Regression: `tests/test_periodic_k_gdf.py::
test_multik_dense_core_parity_hold_warns` (warn fires before the cderi
build; a parity-sized tail lifts it).

### Added: semantic convergence-criteria output (2026-07-17)

`CriteriaTable` renders value, configured threshold, display unit, and ASCII
`pass`/`fail` status through the active format policy. Native geometry
optimization traces use its compact form instead of hand-assembling Unicode
check/cross fragments, so measurements and thresholds convert together.

### Fixed: GAPW molecular-dynamics status uses the persistent output channel (2026-07-17)

GAPW NVE/NVT/NPT status callbacks now convert ASE-native eV energies to
Hartree at the boundary, render them through the active output policy, and
write them to the ambient job output channel when one is installed. Standalone
calls retain live progress output without duplicating channel-backed rows.

### Fixed: Γ-CCM CCSD/UCCSD gradient heteronuclear energy-weighted density (2026-07-17)

The experimental Γ-CCM CCSD and UCCSD analytic nuclear gradients omitted the
Z-vector constraint term's generalized Fock from the energy-weighted (Pulay)
density (`W^Δ`), producing an h-independent analytic error on heteronuclear
systems (1.77e-5 on LiH/STO-3G, confirmed against both the CCM energy FD and
the independent molecular C++ CCSD FD) while every homonuclear H₂-chain gate
stayed green (the term is ∝ z, small by symmetry there). With the term
(`¼C(Fz+Fzᵀ)Cᵀ`, `Fz = ∂⟨−z, F_ai(C(1+U))⟩/∂U`, Fock rebuilt) the total
Lagrangian is stationary under all orbital rotations (residual ~1e-13) and the
LiH gate closes to the 1.6e-7 O(h²) floor. Open-shell mirror carries the
cross-spin Coulomb coupling. New heteronuclear regression test; manuscript
§1.9.3 erratum (`docs/manuscripts/aiccm_a_forces.md`).

### Added: Γ-CCM CCSD(T)/UCCSD(T) analytic forces (2026-07-17)

`run_ccm_ccsd_gradient(..., compute_triples=True)` — the perturbative-triples
correction to the experimental Γ-CCM forces, via the non-canonical
(general-single-determinant) (T) functional (Watts, Gauss & Bartlett, J. Chem.
Phys. 98, 8718 (1993)): the connected triples solve the full off-diagonal
`A[f]t₃ = W` equation and the disconnected numerator carries the `f_ov·T₂`
term, making the functional holomorphic in the Fock matrix so the complex-step
Lagrangian densities include the previously missing off-diagonal (T) 1-PDM
blocks. Reduces bit-identically to the canonical (T) energy at the reference.
Heteronuclear LiH CCSD(T) FD gate at the O(h²) floor (9.5e-8–1.6e-7); H₂-chain
gate preserved. The open-shell mirror `run_ccm_uccsd_gradient(...,
compute_triples=True)` reuses the same spin-agnostic functional on the UHF
spin-orbital tensors: closed-shell reduction to the CCSD(T) gradient at
machine ε (1.6e-13); heteronuclear HeH doublet-chain FD gate at the O(h²)
floor (4.9e-6 → 1.2e-6). This completes the experimental Γ-CCM analytic-forces
method surface (RHF/UHF/RKS/UKS + MP2/UMP2 + CCSD/UCCSD + (T), all
FD-gated including heteronuclear); derivation in
`docs/manuscripts/aiccm_a_forces.md` §1.10.

### Changed: Γ-CCM (`aiccm2026dev-a`) is explicitly labeled experimental (2026-07-17)

The Γ-CCM line now carries the same experimental contract as its χ-CCM
sibling: every public SCF driver in `vibeqc.periodic.ccm` (four-center,
scalable, direct/real-Γ, GDF/RI/RIJCOSX controls, and the wire route) emits
`AICCM2026DevAExperimentalWarning` (exported from top-level `vibeqc`;
correlation, gradient, and property drivers inherit it through the SCF they
run). The `aiccm2026dev-a` and `aiccm2026dev-a-real-gamma` jk-method
descriptions say "experimental", the `periodic_jk_method` status table gains
the missing -a row, and the tutorial/feature-matrix/catalog pages state the
status. All Γ-CCM test files now carry a module-level
`pytestmark = pytest.mark.experimental` (marker already registered), with a
test-gate pin ensuring new -a test files keep it. No numerical behavior
changes.

### Added (EXPERIMENTAL): screened HSE-class hybrids on the real-Γ direct-torus route (2026-07-17)

The neutral fitted-torus real-Γ control (`run_ccm_rks_direct` /
`run_ccm_uks_direct`, route `"real-gamma"`) now runs short-range-only
screened hybrids (`hse06`-class) instead of failing closed. Experimental
research surface (manual test lanes only; not release-gating):

* `build_lpq_bloch_native_fft(..., omega_screen=)` — erfc-SR-attenuated
  fitted kernel (`FT[erfc(w r)/r](p) = (4π/p²)(1 − e^{−p²/4w²})`); the
  default `0.0` is bit-identical to the historical Coulomb build. Threaded
  through `ccm_neutral_cderi{,_fold}` (supercell, fold, and both symmetry
  reductions carry over unchanged — the attenuation is |G+q|-invariant).
* The screened kernel's finite `G+q=0` weight (`π/ω²`) is excluded from the
  fit and restored analytically as `σ₀·S·D·S`,
  `σ₀ = π/(ω²·V_sc)` (`ccm_sr_exchange_zero_mode_constant`). **No
  exchange-q=0 seam attaches** (finite kernel; runs are exxdiv-independent
  by construction, η = 0 in the aiccm2026dev-b binding contract);
  `CCMKSResult.exchange_q0_applicability` records `"active"`/`"inactive"`.
* RSH functionals resolve through the shared
  `resolve_periodic_exchange` policy: full-range-arm RSH (wb97x,
  cam-b3lyp, …) keeps failing closed.
* Gates (`tests/test_ccm_rsh_direct.py`): fitted-vs-direct-G-sum
  four-center identity (1.4e-4 RI floor), vacuum-box real-space erfc-K
  zero-mode pin, vacuum-limit vs molecular HSE06 (−2.1e-4), fold-vs-
  supercell parity (3e-11), UKS→RKS collapse (9e-16),
  exxdiv-independence, applicability records, fail-closed boundary.
  Cross-code caveat documented there: PySCF assembles HSE full-minus-LR
  with exxdiv coupling — a *different finite-size convention* (its own two
  exxdiv settings differ by 0.235 Ha on LiH (1,1,1), and its ewald value
  degenerates to PBE0 where the LR kernel has no reciprocal support); the
  direct route uses the SR-direct (CRYSTAL-style) assembly per the
  resolver policy.

### Changed: vibe-view measurement labels corrected (2026-07-16)

The toolbar ruler button auto-lists every bond distance & angle (no clicking),
so its "click two atoms" tooltip was wrong — relabelled "List all bond
distances & angles". The interactive measure-mode hint now states what it
actually does: click 2 atoms → distance, 3 → angle, 4 → dihedral (all three
were already computed; only the prompt undersold it).

### Added: vibe-view orthographic projection toggle (2026-07-16)

An "Orthographic projection" switch in the Display panel (and a command-
palette action) drops perspective foreshortening so parallel lattice edges
stay parallel — what crystallography and publication figures want. Pushes
the camera to the client so the change is visible immediately.

### Fixed: SAP initial guess unusable in any relocated build (2026-07-18)

The SAP atomic-potential table was located solely from libint's
*compile-time* `LIBINT_DATADIR` macro, which points at the **build** tree.
Wherever that directory no longer exists at run time -- relocatable
bundles, wheels installed elsewhere, multi-stage containers -- every job
using `initial_guess=SAP`, **and `AUTO`, which resolves to SAP for
molecular closed-shell**, died with `SAP: cannot open atomic-potential
file <build-path>/basis/sap_helfem_large.g94` even though the data
shipped correctly inside the install. Ordinary basis loading was never
affected because libint honours `$LIBINT_DATA_PATH`; SAP simply ignored
it. The table is now resolved at run time with the same precedence
libint uses for basis sets -- `$LIBINT_DATA_PATH` first (which vibe-qc's
Python package already points at its bundled `basis_library/` on import,
so relocated wheels need no user action), the compile-time value only as
a fallback -- and a genuinely missing table now names every location
searched instead of one dead build path. Regression:
`tests/test_sap_data_path.py`.

### Fixed: ROHF/ROKS `initial_guess` is no longer fail-open (2026-07-19)

`ROHFOptions.initial_guess` (and `ROKSOptions`, which inherits it) is a
plain Python field rather than the pybind11-typed slot RHF/UHF/RKS/UKS
carry, and its only consumer tested `isinstance(guess, str) and
guess.lower() == "core"`. Every other value -- including the
`InitialGuess` enum that the typed drivers accept -- was silently
accepted and ignored, and the Roothaan driver used SAD regardless. A user
who pinned a guess got a different one with no diagnostic. Verified on
release v0.15.45: `initial_guess = InitialGuess.HCORE` on OH/STO-3G built
the SAD density (`|D_alpha| = 2.2092820106`) instead of the Hcore one
(`2.5179097124`); `"sap"`, `"patom"` and even `"bogus"` all built SAD too.

Both spellings are now normalised at consumption time through the shared
`vibeqc._initial_guess.coerce_initial_guess` (extracted from
`runner._coerce_initial_guess`, which keeps its behaviour), so a value
assigned after construction is honoured. The Roothaan driver seeds from
densities only, so the overlap-dependent guesses (SAP / PATOM / HUECKEL /
MINAO) are rejected with a clear `ValueError` naming the supported set
(SAD / HCORE / AUTO) rather than being downgraded to SAD; unrecognised
values raise as well. No in-tree caller pinned a non-default guess on
these options, and `run_job(initial_guess=...)` already rejected
ROHF/ROKS, so shipped energies are unchanged. Regressions:
`tests/test_rohf.py::test_rohf_initial_guess_*` and
`::test_roks_initial_guess_normalisation_matches_rohf`.

## [v0.15.45] - 2026-07-18 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Fixed: RP209 population analysis definitions (2026-07-17)

Molecular Loewdin populations now use the global symmetric orthogonalization,
Mayer bond orders retain their standard overlap contraction without a
condition-number-triggered Wiberg substitution, and incomplete Natural
Population Analysis fails closed instead of relabeling Loewdin values as NPA.

### Fixed: geometry optimization fails closed at the step cap (2026-07-17)

ASE and semiempirical geometry optimizations no longer report success after
exhausting their configured step limit. Nonconverged runs raise a structured
process-control error, mark the output manifest crashed, and preserve the
trajectory and last geometry for diagnosis; genuine convergence still
finalizes normally.

### Fixed: multi-k GDF rejects symmetry-reduced (IBZ) k-meshes (2026-07-17)

`run_krhf/kuhf/krks/kuks_periodic_gdf` accepted a symmetry-reduced
`KPoints` (e.g. `KPoints.monkhorst_pack(..., symmetry=True)`) and silently
converged to a wrong energy. This is NOT a weight-bookkeeping issue -- the
J and K contractions both honour the supplied BZ weights -- but a physics
gap: HF exchange requires the `k_j` sum over the FULL BZ, and weighting
the irreducible representatives is not equivalent to summing their orbits
(the exchange integrand needs symmetry-unfolded cderi/density per orbit
member). Measured *with the weighted contractions in place* on MgO
primitive FCC / STO-3G: the (2,2,2) full mesh vs its 2-point IBZ
reduction (weights 1/4, 3/4) converged **1.389 Ha apart**, both
`converged=True`, no warning -- exactly the workflow a production-density
mesh (8x8x8-class) invites. Mesh normalisation now fails closed
(`NotImplementedError`) on reduction metadata (non-empty `ir_mapping`);
custom-weighted FULL-BZ quadratures remain supported. True IBZ support =
symmetry-unfolded exchange, tracked in the open-bug inventory. Regression:
`tests/test_periodic_k_gdf.py::test_ibz_reduced_kmesh_fails_closed`
(guard fires at entry, no SCF).

### Fixed: requested sidecars cannot disappear behind a complete manifest (2026-07-17)

Molecular and periodic Molden/population requests are now capability-aware.
The default auto mode emits both sidecars on Gaussian-basis SCF routes and
omits inapplicable plan rows for basis-free semiempirical, solver-only, and
MACE routes. Explicit `True` on an unsupported route fails before calculation;
MACE remains explicitly wavefunction-inapplicable. At finalization,
`ManifestUpdater.finish()` refuses `status="complete"` while any `always=true`
plan row is unwritten, durably records the missing rows and `status="crashed"`,
then raises `IncompleteOutputError`. Conditional rows may remain pending. This
closes the requested/empty sidecar contract behind BUG 29/34/42 without
changing supported-route sidecar bytes. The optimizer `.traj` row is now
truthfully conditional because only the ASE backend writes that sibling;
native, Brent, and geomopt histories remain available through QVF.

### Fixed: multi-k GDF warns + tags dense-core parity-held cells (2026-07-18)

The multi-k GDF drivers returned dense-core (P01-class) absolute energies
with no flag: MgO primitive FCC / STO-3G at the untailed default measured
**−0.503 Ha** ((1,1,2)) / **−0.505 Ha** ((2,2,2), Γ-centered AND shifted
meshes) vs live PySCF 2.13.1 on identical meshes — while the Γ driver has
warned, tagged `+PARITY_HELD`, and auto-sized the high-|G| tail since the
P01 audit. `run_krhf/kuhf_periodic_gdf` (and the KS wrappers) now reuse
the Γ dense-core classifier: a loud warning + `+PARITY_HELD` backend tag
on the un-tailed hold class. The tail genuinely closes the gap at multi-k
— `rsgdf_tail_ke_cutoff = 1.1·10·ζ_max` lands (1,1,2) at **+0.16 mHa** vs
tight PySCF (the same shared-thresholds floor as the Γ ladder) — but at
~40× the untailed cderi build cost per (k_i,k_j) pair (611 s → 25240 s at
(1,1,2)), so multi-k does NOT auto-tail: at n_k² pair builds that default
would be a production-scale cost the caller must opt into (whether it
should auto-tail anyway is an open maintainer call, tracked with the
production-k-sampling audit findings in `HANDOVER_OPEN_BUGS_V015.md`).
Regression: `tests/test_periodic_k_gdf.py::
test_multik_dense_core_parity_hold_warns` (warn fires before the cderi
build; a parity-sized tail lifts it).

### Fixed: GAPW molecular-dynamics status uses the persistent output channel (2026-07-17)

GAPW NVE/NVT/NPT status callbacks now convert ASE-native eV energies to
Hartree at the boundary, render them through the active output policy, and
write them to the ambient job output channel when one is installed. Standalone
calls retain live progress output without duplicating channel-backed rows.

## [v0.15.44] - 2026-07-17 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Fixed: native geometry-optimizer output ownership (2026-07-17)

Native molecular and periodic geometry optimizers now send persistent text
through the ambient output channel and optional live text through
`ProgressLogger`; runners no longer hand them a file-like `.out` channel.

### Added: gated DFTB0-SECCM analytic gradients and NEB (2026-07-17)

The experimental one-dimensional H/C DFTB0-SECCM adapter can now differentiate
its complete frozen-record energy closure analytically. The native kernel
contracts the electronic `D dH0 - W dS` term over the exact directed
Wigner-Seitz records, differentiates the matching weighted repulsive sum, and
normalizes both terms by the finite-group order. Odd groups, even Nyquist ties,
group-only defects, invalidated atom actions, and the molecular limit are pinned
against fixed-topology finite differences or the molecular DFTB0 gradient.

`run_neb(..., method="dftb0", seccm_topology=...)` now exposes this force for
periodic reaction paths and QVF output. Selection is explicit: the topology
must match the periodic cell, exact ties require a caller-provided trust bound,
and unsupported states fail before image evaluation. SCC-DFTB, charged cells,
stress, broader parameter sets, and every other non-MSINDO SECCM adapter remain
gated; no production or paper-facing claim is added.

### Fixed: multi-k GDF parity debug example uses the current API (2026-07-17)

`examples/debug/gdf_multik_pyscf_parity.py` no longer passes the removed
`exxdiv=` keyword to `run_krhf_periodic_gdf`; three-dimensional HF already
selects the validated Ewald exchange-divergence convention internally.

### Fixed: `vq fetch` is idempotent for an already-fetched job (2026-07-17)

Per-job workspace and workdir fetches now treat an existing destination as a
successful retry only when its terminal-diagnosis sidecar identifies the same
job. Remote fetch also handles the race where another fetch publishes that
complete destination between the tar pre-check and atomic promotion; macOS no
longer surfaces `OSError: [Errno 66] Directory not empty`. Unmarked, malformed,
symlinked, and different-job destinations still fail closed without overwrite.

## [v0.15.43] - 2026-07-17 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Fixed: vibe-view recovers from a hung/crashed 3D view (2026-07-16)

The 3D view renders client-side in WebGL; a heavy scene (a large orbital
isosurface or a big supercell) could hang or crash that render process and
leave the window frozen with no way out. The Electron shell now catches the
``unresponsive`` and ``render-process-gone`` events and offers a Reload prompt
(and auto-reloads on a crash), turning a dead window into a recoverable one.
Root-causing the underlying WebGL overload is tracked separately.

### Added: vibe-view working light/dark UI theme + cohesive accent (2026-07-16)

The UI theme toggle now actually works. Previously "Dark UI theme" only
flipped a state flag — the CSS class it needed was never bound, so the chrome
always rendered light. The toggle (Settings, or the command palette) now
switches every Vuetify component between light and a deep-navy dark theme that
matches the 3D viewport, and a single indigo accent (#4361EE) is applied
consistently across both. Defaults to light (the long-standing visible
default). Card headers are slightly denser/heavier for consistency.

### Added: first gated DFTB0-SECCM energy adapter (2026-07-17)

The direct `run_dftb0_seccm(...)` API now consumes the shared frozen SECCM
Wigner-Seitz records for neutral, closed-shell, insulating one-dimensional H/C
finite cyclic clusters. The native adapter assembles overlap, the in-house
STO-6G/Wolfsberg-Helmholtz DFTB0 screening Hamiltonian, and pair repulsion
without borrowing MSINDO Madelung equations or the ordinary Gamma-periodic
cutoff domain. It reports both the total cyclic energy and explicit
per-primitive-cell closure, including zero long-range, dispersion, and
method-specific terms.

Unsupported charge, spin, SCC, property, parameter, dimensionality, and stale
topology combinations fail before heavy kernel allocation. The first slice
uses full finite-cluster evaluation; no orbit reduction, gradient, stress,
SCC-DFTB, GFN2-xTB, PM6, OMx, generalized NDDO, or production-status claim is
added.

### Fixed: GAPW molecular-dynamics status follows the active energy unit (2026-07-16)

The ASE-driven GAPW NVE/NVT/NPT live status now represents ASE-native eV
values as semantic energy quantities and renders them through vibe-qc's active
output policy. Status rows therefore use Ha by default and move both values and
labels together when `VIBEQC_OUTPUT_UNITS` selects another energy unit. The
touched live diagnostics now emit through `ProgressLogger` instead of direct
`print()` calls.

### Fixed: multi-k GDF rejects symmetry-reduced (IBZ) k-meshes (2026-07-17)

`run_krhf/kuhf/krks/kuks_periodic_gdf` accepted a symmetry-reduced
`KPoints` (e.g. `KPoints.monkhorst_pack(..., symmetry=True)`) and silently
converged to a wrong energy. This is NOT a weight-bookkeeping issue -- the
J and K contractions both honour the supplied BZ weights -- but a physics
gap: HF exchange requires the `k_j` sum over the FULL BZ, and weighting
the irreducible representatives is not equivalent to summing their orbits
(the exchange integrand needs symmetry-unfolded cderi/density per orbit
member). Measured *with the weighted contractions in place* on MgO
primitive FCC / STO-3G: the (2,2,2) full mesh vs its 2-point IBZ
reduction (weights 1/4, 3/4) converged **1.389 Ha apart**, both
`converged=True`, no warning -- exactly the workflow a production-density
mesh (8×8×8-class) invites. Mesh normalisation now fails closed
(`NotImplementedError`) on reduction metadata (non-empty `ir_mapping`);
custom-weighted FULL-BZ quadratures remain supported. True IBZ support =
symmetry-unfolded exchange, tracked in the open-bug inventory. Regression:
`tests/test_periodic_k_gdf.py::test_ibz_reduced_kmesh_fails_closed`
(guard fires at entry, no SCF).

### Added: vibe-view SCF log-convergence view (2026-07-16)

The SCF Convergence panel gains a **"Log scale (|E − E_final|)"** checkbox
that plots the energy's distance from the converged value on a log axis, so
the last orders of magnitude of the convergence tail become visible (a linear
energy axis flattens everything after the first couple of cycles). Pairs with
the existing hide-initial-guess toggle.

### Added: job-scoped semantic output coalescing (2026-07-17)

* `record()`, `warn()`, and `note()` accept a semantic `once_key` whose
  first occurrence emits the human `.out` line and structured event together;
  repeats within the active job surfaces emit neither. Periodic BIPOLE
  geometry optimization uses severity-specific fold-guard keys, replacing 14
  repeated warnings with one without hiding a later note-to-warning escalation.

### Fixed: output ownership conformance (2026-07-17)

* Periodic BIPOLE optimization summaries now emit through the ambient
  `vibeqc.output` channel. The runner no longer threads a file handle into the
  optimizer, and direct optimizer calls no longer bypass the channel with
  `print()`.
* The deterministic TOML registry formatter now lives under
  `vibeqc.output.formats`; semiempirical and MACE registry exports no longer
  maintain a standalone file-writer module outside the owned output surface.

### Fixed: QVF population-property fidelity (2026-07-16)

* QVF `dipole_moment.origin` now preserves the explicit three-element bohr
  coordinate as numeric JSON instead of stringifying the list. The schema
  continues accepting named-string origins from legacy producers.
* QVF `atom_properties` now carries the Hirshfeld charges already present in
  `.population.json`; vibe-view reads and displays the new
  `hirshfeld_charge` member alongside Mulliken and Löwdin charges.

## [v0.15.42] - 2026-07-17 - *Neese's Cheetah*

### Fixed: vibe-view replication no longer fights a playing animation (2026-07-16)

Applying periodic replication (Nx/Ny/Nz supercell) while a trajectory or
vibration animation was playing was buggy: the animation loop kept pushing
single-cell frames on its timer, racing and overwriting the supercell
rebuild so it flickered or never appeared. `update_replication` now stops any
playing animation first, so the supercell rebuild wins. Apply Replication
also reports "Replication: N×N×N" so it's clear the action took effect. (The
tiling itself was already correct: exactly 4× geometry at 2×2, 9× at 3×3.)

### Fixed: vibe-view installs a discoverable /Applications app (2026-07-16)

`install-electron.py` now also installs `vibe-view.app` into an Applications
folder (`/Applications`, or `~/Applications` when the former isn't writable),
so Spotlight (Cmd+Space) finds it and it launches from the Dock like a normal
app. Previously the only bundle lived inside `node_modules/electron/dist`,
which Spotlight never indexes. The installed copy tracks live checkout edits
(its launcher shim requires the checkout's main.js); the step is idempotent
and skips the copy when already current. Re-run `python3 install-electron.py`
once to install it.

### Fixed: RP209 output telemetry, provenance, and manifest truthfulness (2026-07-16)

* Performance reports now cap the native OpenMP runtime by explicit scheduler
  and environment allocations. A one-CPU job on a 96-core host reports one
  thread and no longer fabricates 0.01x parallelism; host-wide available-core
  counts are never used as an allocation fallback.
* The `.system` manifest now marks its own output row with
  `checksum_status = "self-excluded"`, an empty SHA, and a zero byte-count
  sentinel. The lifecycle no longer records a pre-finalization self-hash, and
  `vibeqc-outputs` suppresses impossible stale self-digests in legacy files.
* Per-calculation manifests record the full immutable 40-character Git SHA
  when build provenance is available instead of only the abbreviated SHA.
* Population citation assembly now cites NPA only when non-empty NPA rows were
  actually emitted without an NPA error. A fail-closed NPA calculation no
  longer claims the Reed-Weinhold method merely because population output was
  requested.

### Fixed: vibe-view draggable splitter + working toolbar tooltips (2026-07-16)

Two issues reported from the running app:

* **The viewport/plots splitter now resizes** instead of rotating the
  molecule. The bar between the 3D view and the bottom panel is draggable;
  a full-window overlay during the drag keeps the VTK canvas from
  swallowing the gesture. (Previously the bar was decorative and the only
  resize grip was the easy-to-miss native corner handle.)
* **Toolbar icons now show tooltips on hover.** The native ``title``
  tooltip was unreliable/slow in the Electron shell; a lightweight instant
  tooltip is shown from the same labels (and the native ``title`` is
  removed so it can't double up).

### Added: vibe-view command palette (Ctrl/Cmd+K) (2026-07-16)

A command palette opens with **Ctrl/Cmd+K** from anywhere and fuzzy-searches
quick actions — camera views, view presets, render HOMO/LUMO, energy diagram,
toggle labels/background, screenshot, detect point group. Selecting one runs
it and closes the palette. Keyboard-first parity with the toolbar.

### Added: vibe-view click-to-render MO from the energy diagram (2026-07-16)

Clicking any level in the orbital energy diagram now renders that MO. Each
level carries its ``{spin}:{index}`` render key; a click in the sandboxed
diagram iframe posts the key to the app, which renders the orbital and syncs
the MO picker. Completes the frontier-orbital UX alongside the HOMO/LUMO
buttons.

### Added: semiempirical NEB energy-gradient routes (2026-07-16)

`run_neb(...)` now accepts every executable molecular semiempirical
energy-gradient route and the existing Gamma-periodic DFTB0/SCC-DFTB,
GFN2-xTB, PM6, and OM1/OM2/OM3 routes. Gamma DFTB0 uses its native analytic
gradient at the validated 15-bohr image domain; SCC-DFTB and GFN2-xTB use
central differences of converged total energies; periodic PM6/OMx use their
native finite-difference batches. Full k-point semiempirical paths remain
fail-closed.

The current closed-shell MSINDO-SECCM route also drives NEB through its
analytic fixed-topology gradient. Periodic endpoints require the explicit
cyclic translations to match the QVF lattice, and non-MSINDO SECCM adapters
remain unavailable. Semiempirical reaction-path QVFs carry method-specific
citations without a fallback Gaussian basis or XC functional. Periodic MACE
and SECCM QVFs no longer cite the unrelated periodic Gaussian-LCAO route.
All NEB routes reject endpoint charge or multiplicity mismatches before image
evaluation instead of rebuilding the product with the reactant's state.

### Changed: content-sized titled headerless output blocks (2026-07-16)

The document layer now provides `HeaderlessBlock`/`HeaderlessColumn` for
titled label/value and matrix-shaped bodies, optional footers/dividers, and
ragged right-hand annotations that do not widen the content rule. Energy
components, molecular orbital energies, and periodic system summaries use the
primitive instead of fixed 52/54/56-character rules. Orbital values retain
their deliberate parallel Hartree/eV columns through explicit-unit
`render_energy` calls.

The seven affected golden snapshots were deliberately regenerated. Reviewed
diffs change only the targeted rule lengths: molecular RHF/RKS/UHF/Hessian/
TD-DFT orbital or energy blocks and periodic RHF/geometry-optimization system
and energy blocks. The periodic label/value rows retain their historical
per-row minimum label width, so a runtime label such as `periodic length`
does not shift unrelated equals signs.

### Changed: periodic artefact writes use role dispatch (2026-07-16)

`run_periodic_job` now constructs its `OutputWriter` before compute, publishes
the complete plan with `status="running"`, and marks the manifest complete or
crashed at the public exit after any geometry optimization. This includes the
basis-free periodic semiempirical route. Molden, method-specific population
pairs, Extended XYZ, POSCAR, CIF, citation files, structure/density XSF, QVF,
and runtime `.opt.*` files all route through `dispatch_role`; the end-of-job
filesystem sweep is retired. Late-bound route provenance updates the original
manifest in place.

The population plan distinguishes standard, BIPOLE, and AICCM2026DEV-B
summary formats while the shared multi-output adapter still computes and
writes each `.txt`/`.json` pair once. A representative periodic RHF+BIPOLE
job with structure formats, QVF, and optimization matched a direct-writer
control byte-for-byte for every deterministic artefact it produced; every QVF
scientific member also matched, leaving only banner/timings, QVF wall-time
provenance, and the intentionally improved live manifest lifecycle dynamic.

### Added: vibe-view spectra X-unit toggle + CSV export (2026-07-16)

Spectrum panels gain an **X unit** selector (native / cm⁻¹ / eV / nm; e.g.
UV-Vis eV→nm) and an **Export CSV** button. Broadening stays in native units
(correct physics) and the axis is remapped for display; the CSV carries the
broadened envelope and the discrete peaks in the chosen unit.

### Changed: molecular artefact writes use role dispatch (2026-07-15)

The molecular `run_job` path now routes molden, population, density and
per-orbital cubes, citations, final XYZ, runtime NTO molden files, and QVF
through `OutputWriter.dispatch_role`. Existing progress stages and
`PerfScope` timings remain around the same writer operations, while successful
files are recorded in `.system` at dispatch time instead of by the end-of-job
plan sweep. Dispatch now supports strict runner error propagation, path/format
targeting, runtime-conditional files, and a per-call multi-output cache so the
population analysis runs once for its `.txt` and `.json` siblings.

The plan also preserves integer cube requests as `.mo_<index>.cube`, aligns
the QVF role with its dispatcher key, and declares the actual periodic XSF
paths without structure/density collisions. A representative RHF audit found
the molden, XYZ, population, cube, and citation payloads byte-identical before
and after; every scientific QVF entry was also byte-identical, with only its
recorded wall time changing.

### Added: vibe-view spectra display controls (2026-07-16)

Spectrum panels gain a **Broadening** slider (0.2-4x the per-kind default
width) and a **Normalize** checkbox (peak scaled to 1; sticks scaled with
it) -- both also apply to the multi-file comparison overlay.

### Fixed: vibe-view branded Electron launches from the Dock (2026-07-16)

The branded dev `Electron.app` had no default app baked in, so a Dock or
Finder double-click exited silently; only the `vibe-view desktop` spawn path
worked. `install-electron.py` now writes a two-file launcher shim into
`Contents/Resources/app` that loads the checkout's `main.js`, and ad-hoc
re-signs the bundle. Re-run `python3 install-electron.py` once per checkout
(or after moving it) to (re)generate the shim.

### Added: vibe-view one-click view presets (2026-07-16)

A "View preset" selector at the top of the Display panel applies a complete
look in one click: **Publication** (white background, publication-grade
material, no SSAO or labels), **Presentation** (dark, glossy, SSAO depth),
**Analysis** (flat material with atom labels). Each preset orchestrates the
existing representation, material, SSAO, and label controls in an order that
survives the scene rebuilds.

### Changed: marketing site at the root; docs move to /docs/ (2026-07-16)

vibe-qc.com now serves a new static marketing/landing site (Astro, in
`website/`) at the domain root; the Sphinx documentation moves under `/docs/`
(`html_baseurl`, robots/sitemap `CANONICAL`, and the CI deploy target all
updated). Docs remain the single source of truth and build unchanged. A
rolling preview of `main` is published at `vibe-qc.com/preview/` by the new
`website-staging` CI job (noindex; served from its own `/web/preview/`
subtree).

**Release-operations note:** the first `release` deploy carrying this change
relocates every documentation URL from the root to `/docs/`. Before that
deploy, apply the Apache legacy-URL redirects in
`deploy/htaccess-redirects.conf` to the server's root `/web/.htaccess` — the
CI deploy deliberately excludes `.htaccess` — or old doc URLs (`/quickstart.html`,
`/_static/…`) will 404 in the gap.

### Fixed: native molecular D3(BJ) is quantitative for H-Ar (2026-07-16)

The native molecular D3(BJ) backend now ships the complete H-Ar corner of
Grimme's coordination-dependent C6 reference grid (1,443 active references),
the corrected D3 covalent radii, all 156 simple-dftd3 BJ parameter sets, and
the full analytic C6(CN) chain rule for two-body and ATM gradients. The root
cause of the RP208 overbinding was the earlier one-reference-per-element
framework table, compounded by incorrect coordination radii; it was not pair
double-counting, geometry units, damping dispatch, periodic images, or an SCF
setting.

For the archived rounded methane-dimer geometry and printed B3LYP parameters,
the native component changes from `-0.0123798158 Ha` to
`-0.00517760871046 Ha`, agreeing with simple-dftd3 to `1.3e-15 Ha` and with
ORCA 6.1.1 (`-0.005177608303 Ha`) within the archived coordinate precision.
Native/reference analytic gradients agree within `8e-14 Ha/bohr`, including
the ATM term. `backend="auto"` now uses this self-contained quantitative path
for H-Ar and retains optional `dftd3` fallback for heavier elements. These are
geometry-only dispersion comparisons; no total B3LYP parity is claimed for
the unmatched SCF routes.

### Fixed: vibe-view desktop dodges stale servers on its port (2026-07-16)

A crashed or tray-forgotten session can leave an old `vibe-view serve`
holding the default port for days; a fresh dock launch then collided with it
and died silently (observed: a 6-day-old server on 8765 blocked every
launch). The Electron shell now probes its port before spawning the server
and, if the port is taken, transparently moves to an OS-assigned free one.

### Fixed: stale BIPOLE analytic-preview reconstruction gate (2026-07-16)

The internal Gamma RKS Fock-reconstruction regression now tests its stated
`1e-8` matrix identity from a converged plain-DIIS density instead of enabling
the unrelated FMIXING state machine with a numerically zero positive weight
and demanding SCF energy changes below the fixed-grid numerical floor. The
reconstructed and SCF Focks agree under the original `1e-8` acceptance bound;
no production convergence policy or analytic-gradient capability changed.

### Added: vibe-view design refresh M1+M2 — Export menu, SCF guess toggle, resizable panels, Structure Library, multi-file spectrum comparison (2026-07-16)

First two milestones of the design-refresh workstream
(`vibe-view/docs/design_refresh_2026.md`):

* **Toolbar**: the eight cryptic per-format export buttons (OBJ/glTF/XYZ/
  CIF/POV/Bldr/SVG/CML) are one labeled **Export** menu with per-format
  icons and full names.
* **SCF convergence**: a "Hide initial guess (first SCF point)" checkbox
  above the plot drops the guess energy, whose scale otherwise flattens
  the convergence tail (`SCFHistoryRenderer.render_to_html(skip_first=)`).
* **Resizable panels**: the Sections sidebar and the right control panel
  are user-resizable by dragging their inner edge (live drag preview,
  width committed to trame state on release so the layout reflows).
* **Structure Library** (editor): autocomplete over the curated
  `vibeqc_naming` structure DB (83 molecules today) with **Insert** (into
  the current structure, next to the selection, undo-able) and **Open as
  file** (new entry in the Files dropdown). Card hides when the package
  isn't installed.
* **Spectrum comparison across QVF files**: with several files open, a
  "Compare across open files" checkbox on any spectrum panel overlays the
  same-kind spectra from every open file with a per-file legend
  (`render_comparison_html`; envelopes only, sticks omitted).

Pinned by `vibe-view/tests/test_design_refresh.py`; Export menu, SCF
toggle, resize handles, and the library card also verified live in a
browser against a real QVF.

### Fixed: bounded BIPOLE NEB and relaxation diagnostics (2026-07-16)

Periodic `run_neb` and `relax_atoms` now expose `sr_image_precision`
explicitly and forward it to every BIPOLE reference, objective, and
finite-difference SCF. The production default remains the precision-derived
M5 padded domain at `1e-6`; no image radius is capped. Tiny-cutoff dispatch,
warm-start, and QVF tests that do not validate numerical accuracy now select
the documented historical-domain diagnostic with `None`, restoring bounded
runtime without weakening production correctness.

### Fixed: BIPOLE HSE06 uses the shared padded erfc domain (2026-07-16)

The dedicated restricted and unrestricted HSE screened-exchange traversal now
honors M5's padded ket-image domain, including the SYM3b-reduced build. The
longer-ranged of the Ewald-J and screened-K erfc kernels sets the shared
precision-derived radius. On the maintained H2 fixture, padded and unpadded
screened exchange already agree with the independent multi-k Ewald route to
machine precision; the reported post-M5 `6.8e-5 Ha` total-energy movement is
entirely Hartree J. Production `sr_image_precision=1e-6` agrees with `1e-9`
within `5e-15 Ha`. The screened-K cross-driver gate now selects the documented
historical unpadded diagnostic domain explicitly, with its tolerance unchanged;
no production energy was re-pinned.

### Fixed: duplicate BIPOLE M5 energy regression contract (2026-07-16)

The cross-backend H2/STO-3G/12-bohr test now records the independently
sanctioned M5 padded-domain BIPOLE energy already owned by the primary
integration regression. Both routes were rerun together against a freshly
rebuilt native extension and obtained `-1.122138533948132 Ha`. This is a stale
test-pin correction only; production domain selection, tolerances, and
numerical results are unchanged.
